## Answered (sixteenth round, 2026-10-30; settled in `decisions.md`)

#### D165 Copyright holder in LICENSE
Question: D75 decides MIT, and code-guidelines 9 and architecture 1 repeat it. No document names the copyright holder that the MIT notice's line `Copyright (c) <year> <holder>` needs. LICENSE on main reads "Copyright (c) 2026 the NCXchange authors", a placeholder chosen in P0-01. Who holds the copyright?
Recommendation: The maintainer's full name, as `Copyright (c) 2026 <full name>`. The holder should be someone who can grant the license, and the maintainer is the only author in the history so far; later contributors keep their own copyright under the same license. Alternative: keep "the NCXchange authors", a collective name used by projects with many contributors, usually together with an AUTHORS file.
Where: LICENSE; code-guidelines 9 (license line); optionally the D75 row.

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27: the library does not answer this (searched the whole cached library for 'MIT License', 'MIT-Lizenz', 'Open-Source-Lizenz', 'Open Source License', 'GNU General Public', 'Apache License' and 'BSD License': no file matches any of them. 'Urheberrechtsinhaber' / 'copyright holder' matches exactly three files, all three Philips MillPlus IT manuals, and in each it is the publisher's own reservation of rights beside '© Heidenhain Numeric B.V. Eindhoven, Niederlande 2008' ('Vervielfältigen ... ist lediglich zulässig mit schriftlicher Zustimmung des Urheberrechtsinhabers', page 18 of the V600 Programmierhandbuch). No manual discusses open-source licensing or how to name a copyright holder. Nothing in a CNC manual bears on who holds the copyright of NCXchange; this is the maintainer's to state). The recommendation above stands for the maintainer.
(Peter, 2026-10-30) The copyright holder is Peter Burgener: `Copyright (c) 2026 Peter Burgener`, and the same name for the package `Authors` (D347).

#### D389 A Fanuc tool change without a length offset (R1-13)
Question: `TOOL=1 RPM=6000` compiles for `fanuc-mill-30i` to `T1 M6` and `S6000 M3` and no `G43 H1`, so the control never applies the tool length and the tip runs one tool length below the programmed Z. Heidenhain (`TOOL CALL`) and Siemens (the active edge) apply the length either way. Should a Fanuc tool change without `OFFSET:LEN` (and without a point word that D373 maps) apply the length register of the tool's own number, or at least warn when a motion follows the change with no length offset active?
Recommendation: a WARNING, not a default. The Fanuc M-series `T` has no relation to `H` (the D373 audit: 30i-B Operator's Manual printed p. 219), so `H` = tool number is a guess at the shop's numbering; and some builders apply `G43` inside their change macro, which a written `G43` would duplicate. The Fanuc compiler reports a WARNING (next free code of the Fanuc band) at the first tool-axis motion after a `TOOL` while the holder has neither `OFFSET:LEN`, `OFFSET` nor a mapped point register, once per tool change, naming the tool. A machine file whose builder macro applies the length silences it with a `[tool_change]` flag (`length_offset_by_macro = true`). With D373's `registers` form and an explicit `TOOL_POINT` (D393) the CAM gets `G43 H` from the mapping, which replaces its present workaround (`OFFSET:LEN=n`).
Meanwhile: nothing changes; no diagnostic and no `G43`, so no existing program changes. The CAM keeps writing `OFFSET:LEN`, or writes `TOOL_POINT=1` on a machine with `[tool_points] form = "registers"` (D393).
Where: controllers/fanuc.md 5; machine-config 3; `src/Ncx.Compilers/Fanuc/FanucToolWords.cs`, `src/Ncx.Compilers/Fanuc/DiagnosticCodes.Fanuc.cs`.

ANSWER: (Peter, 2026-10-27) Accept the recommendation: a WARNING at the first tool-axis motion after a TOOL without a length offset, once per tool change, naming the tool; `[tool_change] length_offset_by_macro = true` silences it. No default G43 H.

#### D390 Brackets in a Fanuc comment (R1-14)
Question: `SECTION="PROFIL (D10)"` compiles for `fanuc-mill-30i` to `(PROFIL (D10))`: the first `)` ends the comment and the rest of the line is read as code, and neither `check --strict` nor `compile` says anything. Should the Fanuc compiler replace `(` and `)` inside comment text (for example by `[` and `]`), or refuse them with an ERROR? And does a machine file state a comment length limit that the compiler checks?
Recommendation: replace `(` by `[` and `)` by `]` with a WARNING per comment that names the replacement, because the text stays readable and the program stays runnable; `[` `]` are ordinary characters inside a Fanuc comment as far as the program format goes. Not verified against the manual library in this session: the connector (`mcp__cnc-manuals__search_manuals`) was refused, so whether a nested `(` is itself an alarm on the 30i-B (control-in inside a comment) must be checked before the answer. A comment length limit: no new key; the existing `max_line_length` with CMP021 (D263) covers the line, which is what the control limits.
Meanwhile: the Fanuc compiler refuses a comment text with `(` or `)` with an ERROR (CMP-code of the Fanuc band), because a silently broken line is worse than none and an ERROR is easy to relax later; the CAM already refuses those characters (SplinterCAM DEC-CL-005), so it never meets the ERROR.
Where: controllers/fanuc.md 10 rule 5; controller-mapping 1 (COMMENT); `src/Ncx.Compilers/Fanuc/FanucBlock.cs` (`CommentText`), `src/Ncx.Compilers/Fanuc/DiagnosticCodes.Fanuc.cs`.

ANSWER: (Peter, 2026-10-27) Accept the recommendation: replace ( by [ and ) by ] in Fanuc comment text with a WARNING per comment that names the replacement; check the 30i-B manual for an alarm on [ ] before release and note the page. No new length key.

#### D391 Which holder the point words address without a role
Question: D372 gives `TOOL_POINT` the holder role as an optional address and names no address for `TIP_OFFSET` and `POINT_RADIUS`. `TOOL` without a role addresses `default_holder`, `OFFSET` the holder of the last `TOOL` (virtual machine 3.8 rule 2). Which holder does a point word without a role address, and which holder do `TIP_OFFSET` and `POINT_RADIUS` follow?
Recommendation: as `OFFSET` does: the holder of the `TOOL` of the block, else of the `TOOL_POINT:r` of the block, else the holder of the last `TOOL`; `TIP_OFFSET` and `POINT_RADIUS` take no address and follow the same holder. A point change belongs to the tool that is cutting, which on a turret is the last called one, not the default holder. On a machine with one holder every reading gives `default_holder`.
Meanwhile: the recommendation is coded (`VirtualMachine.ResolvePointWords`), and an address on `TIP_OFFSET` or `POINT_RADIUS` is refused by the catalog (PAR150), so a later answer that adds one breaks no program.
Where: language 4.4; VM 2.3, 3.8 rule 2; `src/Ncx.Core/VirtualMachine/VirtualMachine.cs`, `src/Ncx.Core/Catalog/ToolWords.cs`.

ANSWER: (Peter, 2026-10-27) Accept the recommendation as coded.

#### D392 What "a block of their own" admits
Question: D372 makes the point words valid "in a TOOL block or in a block of their own". May such a block carry anything else: `SKIP`, a `COMMENT`, `OFFSET` words, `PRELOAD`, a motion verb?
Recommendation: nothing but the three point words, `SKIP` and a `COMMENT`; anything else beside them without `TOOL` is an ERROR (PAR017). The point takes effect with the next tool-axis motion, so a block that also moves would make it unclear whether its own motion is in the old or the new point; `OFFSET` beside a point word mixes the register numbers the point replaces with the point (D369 (b)); a `PRELOAD` belongs to the next tool, not to this point.
Meanwhile: the recommendation is coded (`BlockRules.CheckPointWords`, PAR017); it is the stricter reading and can be relaxed without breaking a program.
Where: language 4.4, 5 rule 5; VM 5; `src/Ncx.Core/Parsing/BlockRules.cs`, `src/Ncx.Core/Model/DiagnosticCodes.Parsing.cs`.

ANSWER: (Peter, 2026-10-27) Accept the recommendation as coded.

#### D393 Does an explicit point 1 write the mapped register?
Question: D375 says "point 1 with a = r = 0 writes nothing, so existing programs compile byte for byte as before", and D369 (b) says the CAM writes the point words and no `OFFSET:*` numbers, so the registers must come from the mapping. Read together they conflict for a CAM program that writes `TOOL=1 TOOL_POINT=1`: on a Fanuc `registers` machine it then gets no `G43 H` at all (the R1-13 failure), on Siemens no `D1`. Does an explicit `TOOL_POINT` of 1 write the register of the mapping, and what wins where a block carries `OFFSET:LEN` and the holder a point?
Recommendation: a tool whose program names its point (a `TOOL_POINT` word in its `TOOL` block or after it) writes the register the mapping gives, point 1 included; a tool without any point word compiles as before, which is the case D375's sentence protects (no program written before the words has one). Under a point the `OFFSET:*` words are the hand-written form and are not mixed with it: a block with both is refused by PAR017 (D392), and an `OFFSET` word on a holder whose tool named a point is a WARNING that the register of the mapping is replaced.
Meanwhile: the recommendation's first half is coded: the mapping is written for every tool whose holder carries an explicit `TOOL_POINT` word since its `TOOL`; without one nothing changes. An `OFFSET` word after the point keeps today's behaviour (it writes its register) with no WARNING.
Where: language 4.4; controller-mapping 3; `src/Ncx.Compilers/CompilerBase.Tools.cs` and the three family tool writers.

ANSWER: (Peter, 2026-10-27) Accept the recommendation as coded, including the WARNING when an OFFSET word follows a named point.

### Sixth round: needed now (phase 1 behaviour)

#### D108 InvariantGlobalization silences CA1305
Question: Code-guidelines 9 sets `<InvariantGlobalization>true</InvariantGlobalization>` in Directory.Build.props for every project, and code-guidelines 3.4 and 9 make CA1305 an error. The .NET analyzers receive this MSBuild property (a CompilerVisibleProperty in the SDK's Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.NetAnalyzers.targets) and do not report CA1305 while it is true, so the build does not enforce the culture rule of 3.4. Rechecked 2026-09-13 on a copy of main: a probe `decimal.Parse(text)` in Ncx.Core builds clean as configured and fails with `error CA1305` under `-p:InvariantGlobalization=false`. Every src project builds clean with the property removed, so main has no violation today. At run time the property acts only through the runtimeconfig.json of an executable (Ncx.Cli and the five test projects), where it becomes the runtime option `System.Globalization.Invariant`; in the library projects its only effect is to silence the analyzer. Which setting gives way?
Recommendation: Keep both rules and change how the first one is set. Replace the `InvariantGlobalization` property in Directory.Build.props with `<RuntimeHostConfigurationOption Include="System.Globalization.Invariant" Value="true" />`, and keep CA1305 an error. The runtimeconfig.json of ncx and of the test projects keeps `"System.Globalization.Invariant": true`, so ncx, the plugins it loads and the tests run culture-independent exactly as today. The analyzer reads only the MSBuild property, so it then checks every project, Ncx.Cli included. Checked on a copy of main: with the item in Ncx.Cli.csproj, a probe in Ncx.Cli is `error CA1305` and the runtimeconfig still carries the setting. Code-guidelines 9 then names the item instead of the property. Alternative: set the property in Ncx.Cli.csproj only. That brings CA1305 back for the libraries and tests, but leaves Ncx.Cli itself unchecked (checked: the probe in Ncx.Cli then builds clean), and the tests run under the machine's culture. Second alternative: keep both settings as written and amend 3.4 so that review, not the analyzer, holds the rule.
Where: code-guidelines 3.4 and 9 (Directory.Build.props line); implementation 00-method 3 and 10-phase-0 (P0-01 Directory.Build.props line); Directory.Build.props (TODO(question) above InvariantGlobalization); .editorconfig line 43.

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27: the library does not answer this (searched re-ran the search independently over the whole text cache (1643 .txt files): CA1305, InvariantGlobalization, MSBuild, Roslyn, dotnet, Directory.Build, System.Globalization and RuntimeHostConfiguration all give zero files. The only software-development document in the library is 01_Steuerungen/Fanuc/Allgemein/Schulung/Fanuc_CNC-Kommunikation_Schulung_DE.pdf (FOCAS training, 2012), which names Visual Studio and a sample C# .NET header file for the FOCAS library (cache pp. 11, 17) and nothing about analyzers, globalization or build properties; everything else is controller and machine-builder documentation. This is a pure .NET build question (Roslyn analyzer behaviour and runtimeconfig generation) that the maintainer must settle from the .NET side). The recommendation above stands for the maintainer.

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

Replace the `InvariantGlobalization` property in Directory.Build.props with `<RuntimeHostConfigurationOption Include="System.Globalization.Invariant" Value="true" />` and keep CA1305 an error; code-guidelines 9 names the item.
Basis: logical
Source: Pure .NET build question; the item keeps `System.Globalization.Invariant` in every runtimeconfig.json while the analyzer no longer sees the MSBuild property, so CA1305 checks every project (verified on a copy of main in the proposal).
Differs from the recommendation: no
Confidence: high
Code impact: Directory.Build.props, code-guidelines 9.

#### D109 Enforcing the 120-character line
Question: Code-guidelines 3.3 says the project "uses 120 and lets the formatter enforce it", and code-guidelines 9 lists 120-character lines among the .editorconfig additions. But dotnet format has no line-length rule, and max_line_length only guides editors. None of the CI steps checks the limit: code-guidelines 9 names format --verify-no-changes and test, and ci.yml (implementation 00-method 3) adds restore and build with -warnaserror. Main already has 53 lines over 120 characters (40 in src, 13 in tests, up to 126). A test that reads the source tree would break code-guidelines 8 (tests independent of the working directory, fixtures embedded).
Recommendation: Add one step to .github/workflows/ci.yml that fails on any `*.cs` line over 120 characters in src/ and tests/: a grep, no package, no test. Give it `shell: bash` or run it on the Linux job only, since the Windows job's default shell is PowerShell. Wrap the 53 lines in the same commit, and amend 3.3 to "lets CI enforce it". This keeps the limit enforced, as 3.3 intends, for one workflow step. Alternative: amend 3.3 to "editors show the limit, review holds it" and leave the 53 lines as they are.
Where: code-guidelines 3.3 and 9; .editorconfig line 145 (TODO(question) at max_line_length); .github/workflows/ci.yml; the 53 lines (e.g. src/Ncx.Config/Cycles/CycleCatalogLoader.cs:65, src/Ncx.Core/VirtualMachine/VirtualMachine.cs:56, tests/Ncx.Core.Tests/Writing/NcxWriterTests.cs:309).

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27: the library does not answer this (searched dotnet format, .editorconfig, max_line_length, Continuous Integration, Quellcode and stderr all give zero relevant files (the Quellcode hits are Brother manuals using the word for a light or signal source), and "Zeilenlänge" hits are Heidenhain display and PLC text-line limits. I confirmed the "120 Zeichen" hits an earlier pass cited and they are NC block length, not source lines: Sinumerik 810M Programmieranleitung GA3 (2003) cache p. 8, "Die Satzlänge kann maximal 120 Zeichen betragen" (also pp. 114, 115, 203); Sinumerik 840C Programmieranleitung (2001) cache p. 285, same limit; Sinumerik 840D sl NC-Programmierung 06/2019 p. 50, "Ein Satz kann maximal 512 Zeichen enthalten". Unrelated to code-guidelines 3.3; recorded so the search is not repeated. Nothing in the library bears on enforcing a 120-character line in C# source or on a CI step, so this stays a repository-tooling decision). The recommendation above stands for the maintainer.

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

Add one CI step (`shell: bash`) that fails on any `*.cs` line over 120 characters in src/ and tests/; wrap the 53 existing lines in the same commit; code-guidelines 3.3 reads "lets CI enforce it".
Basis: logical
Source: dotnet format has no line-length rule; a grep step is the cheapest real enforcement and keeps tests free of source-tree reads (code-guidelines 8).
Differs from the recommendation: no
Confidence: high
Code impact: .github/workflows/ci.yml; 53 source lines rewrapped.

#### D110 Rendering a diagnostic without a file
Question: D98 renders every diagnostic as `file(line): ERROR VM042: message`, and code-guidelines 6 says every diagnostic carries the line of an NCX or source block. D97 and architecture 10 give a usage error exit code 2 but do not say how a diagnostic about the command line, which has neither a file nor a line, is printed. Program.Run prints `ncx(1): ERROR CLI001: ...`, naming the tool as the file and inventing line 1. P1-07 adds the usage errors of check, trace and annotate.
Recommendation: Print `ncx: ERROR CLI001: message`, with the tool as the origin and no line. This is the form that the MSBuild canonical error format, which D98 follows, uses for tool-level errors (`MSBUILD : error MSB1009: ...`), and it invents no line number. `Diagnostic.Line` gets a "no line" value, null as `OriginLine` has it (code-guidelines 3.4: `?` states that null is valid), rendered without parentheses and used only for diagnostics about the command line; code-guidelines 6 names that exception. A diagnostic about a whole file (CLI002, the Ncx.Config loaders) keeps line 1 of that file. Alternative: keep `ncx(1)` as coded and add that form to D98.
Where: D98 row and rationale; code-guidelines 6; architecture 4 (Diagnostic); src/Ncx.Cli/Program.cs Run (TODO(question)); src/Ncx.Core/Model/Diagnostic.cs ToText.

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27: the library does not answer this (searched Kommandozeile, command line, Exit-Code, exit code, stderr, Konsole, Rückgabewert, Fehlercode and ERRORLEVEL over the cache. The only real command-line tool in the library is TNCcmd, documented in 01_Steuerungen/Heidenhain/Allgemein/Software_Tools/Heidenhain_TNCremoNT_Software-Tools_DE_1998.pdf (chapter 5, cache pp. 32-34, footer "Mai 2002"): its session transcripts show messages such as "Already connected" and "Kann die Schnittstelle nicht öffnen" with no file, line or code, and the manual documents no exit code — which neither supports nor refutes the MSBuild canonical form D98 follows. I also checked the Fanuc 30i/31i/32i-B alarm index and the Heidenhain TNC 640 error chapters; they are control alarm lists and PLC interfaces. Correction to an earlier search note: the Fanuc alarm index (Anhang H, VERZEICHNIS DER ALARMMELDUNGEN) begins at cache p. 2382, not p. 2380 — cache p. 2380 is Anhang G, the character-code table). The recommendation above stands for the maintainer.

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

Print `ncx: ERROR CLI001: message` (tool as origin, no line). `Diagnostic.Line` becomes nullable and null renders without parentheses, used only for command-line diagnostics; whole-file diagnostics (CLI002, config loaders) keep line 1 of that file. Code-guidelines 6 names the exception.
Basis: logical
Source: Follows the MSBuild canonical error format D98 already adopts (`MSBUILD : error MSB1009: ...`) and invents no line number; the manuals have nothing on it.
Differs from the recommendation: no
Confidence: high
Code impact: Ncx.Core Diagnostic (nullable Line, ToText); Ncx.Cli Program.Run.

#### D111 Byte order mark in an NCX file
Question: Language 3 (Encoding: "UTF-8, LF or CRLF line endings") does not say whether a UTF-8 byte order mark may begin an NCX file, nor whether format keeps it; Windows editors and postprocessors often write one. Parser.Parse does not skip the mark: checked on a copy of main, a mark before FILE=BEGIN gives PAR002 and three structural ERRORs. Only FormatCommand handles it: it strips the mark before parsing and writes it back, so a canonical file with a mark passes --check (FormatCommandTests.Format_CanonicalFileWithByteOrderMark_KeepsIt). The check, trace and annotate commands of P1-07 would reject such a file. No example has a mark.
Recommendation: A byte order mark at the start of a file is allowed and is not part of the text. The parser skips it and the program records it next to its line ending, so every command accepts it. Format writes it back as read, the same way the writer keeps the file's line ending (implementation 10, P0-06 NcxWriter line). A program built by a reader has none, just as it gets LF. Alternative: format drops the mark, so canonical text never carries one, and --check reports every file that has one.
Where: language 3 (Encoding row); architecture 4 (NcxProgram) and 4.1; src/Ncx.Core/Parsing/Parser.cs Parse; src/Ncx.Core/Model/NcxProgram.cs; src/Ncx.Cli/Commands/FormatCommand.cs Run (TODO(question)); P1-07 commands.

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, not confirmed by the maintainer: the manuals do not settle this. The only control statement about a byte order mark points the way the recommendation does: Heidenhain says a UTF-8 text file should begin with a BOM and that the control detects the encoding itself when there is none. That passage is about PLC text files, not NC programs, and no manual in the library says whether an NC program file may carry a mark, so "allowed, not part of the text, kept by format" remains an NCX choice. What the manuals add is only context: cell software expects the program-start marker in the first line of the file, and Siemens ends a block with LF. The Heidenhain BOM rule is about PLC text files read by module 9217 and shows only that a Heidenhain control both expects and tolerates a leading BOM in a UTF-8 file. I struck the earlier claim that a BOM "does not disturb" the first-line program-start marker: no page in the library says that, and a BOM would in fact sit in front of the % on that first line, so the Fastems statement is if anything a small argument against carrying one.
Evidence: `Heidenhain_TNC640_Technisches-Handbuch_NC-SW-34059x-10_DE_2019`, p. 1153 (In the boundary conditions of PLC module 9217 (overlay window for messages): text files may be UTF-8 or ISO/IEC 8859-1 coded; UTF-8 coded files "sollten am Anfang eine Byte-Order-Mark (BOM) enthalten", and when no BOM is present the control tries to recognise the coding automatically. The same sentence, word for word, is the only BOM passage anywhere in the library (TNC 640 technical handbooks of 2018, 2019 and 2021 and the TNC 620 handbook of 2015); it is never said of NC programs.); `Heidenhain_TNC640_Programmierung-Klartext_892903-18_NC-SW-34059x-10_DE_2019`, p. 293 (The only other encoding rule in the library, and it runs the other way: for the FN 16 log-file output, "Wenn Sie FN 16 verwenden, dann darf die Datei nicht UTF-8 kodiert sein." A file a Heidenhain NC function writes to must not be UTF-8.); `Fastems_NC-Program-Metadata-Format_Functional-Description_166651_EN_2021`, p. 4, 8, 10, 12, 16 (Page 4, NOTE 2: the MMS code viewer of the NC library and the CR/LF trimming in the DNC interface support only UTF-8 encoding; a file in another encoding is handled and transferred like a binary file with no trimming. The dialect tables say the program-start marker is "located always in the first line" — % for Fanuc (pp. 10, 12), %MPF6987 for Siemens 840D, carrying program number and type (p. 16). The Fanuc program number, ":" or the letter "O", is stated to be in the SECOND line (pp. 10, 12), and the Siemens `;%_N_<name>_<ext>` form of p. 8 is a comment line of the metadata header, not a raw program start. Nothing in the document mentions a byte order mark.); `Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl_Programmierhandbuch-NC-Programmierung_SW492_DE_2019`, p. 50 (Satzregeln: a block ends with the character LF, which need not be written because the line break produces it; a block holds at most 512 characters including comment and the LF.). (Citations re-paged to the cnc-manuals connector 2026-10-26.)

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

A UTF-8 BOM at file start is allowed and is not part of the text. The parser skips it, NcxProgram records it next to the line ending, every command accepts it, and format writes it back as read. Programs built by readers get none.
Basis: manual
Source: Heidenhain TNC 640 Technisches Handbuch 2019 p. 1153 (UTF-8 text files "sollten ... eine BOM enthalten", tolerated if absent; about PLC texts, not NC programs). The rest is an NCX choice; compilers write no BOM, since cell software expects `%` in the first line (Fastems metadata format p. 10-16).
Differs from the recommendation: no
Confidence: medium
Code impact: Ncx.Core Parser.Parse and NcxProgram (BOM flag); NcxWriter; FormatCommand simplifies.

#### D112 Canonical text inside braces: NOT, parentheses, case
Question: ncx format writes every expression as the print of its tree. The P0-05 phase and task files make that print the text 'used by ncx format', and P0-04 stores it in ExprValue.Text, so {$Q1+20} comes back as {$Q1 + 20} and {sin($a)} as {SIN($A)}. No section of the specification defines this text. Language 4.12 says only 'Whitespace inside {} is free'. D43 and language 2 rule 7 fix only the word order of a block. D92's 'nothing is normalized but the comment column' is about blank lines. Three points are open. (1) P0-05 writes NOT like the unary minus, directly before its operand. But NOT written directly before a name or a number reads back as one name (NOTSIN(30), NOT1 < 2). The NOT case among P0-05's own tests, {$Q1 < $Q2 AND NOT $Q3}, is written with the space. (2) No document says whether parentheses the grammar does not need are kept ({((1))}, {($Q1 < $Q2) AND ($Q3 > 0)}). The P0-05 node list has no parentheses node, so its printer would have to place parentheses by precedence, which drops the unneeded ones. The code keeps written parentheses as ParenthesesNode, and BinaryNode adds none of its own. A tree built in code without ParenthesesNode therefore prints with the wrong grouping: `Binary(*, Binary(+, a, b), c)` prints as `a + b * c`. The Fanuc reader of phase 3 builds such trees from '[ ]' (P3-02, FanucMacro). (3) Language 3, Case ('Parsers may accept lowercase and normalize') names keys, addresses and identifiers. It does not name the function names or the words AND, OR, NOT and MOD of 4.12 ({sin($a) mod 2}).
Recommendation: Keep what the code does, and make the printer safe. (1) NOT is followed by one space; the unary minus stands directly before its operand. (2) Written parentheses are kept and printed as written. This never changes the grouping, and it keeps the author's grouping just as design rule 5 keeps the author's numbers. Where a tree built in code has none, the printer adds the parentheses that precedence needs, so no tree can print as text that reads back differently. (3) Function names and the operator words are accepted in any case and written in uppercase, like variable names. Write the canonical expression text into language 4.12: format, the readers and annotate all produce it, and today only a phase-plan paragraph defines it. Alternative for (2): drop the parentheses the grammar does not need and print parentheses by precedence alone. The text then depends on the tree alone (language 2 rule 7), readers need no rule for source brackets, and a trip through a controller that needs extra brackets cannot add any. ParenthesesNode goes.
Where: Language 4.12 (a new paragraph on the canonical text); language 3 (the Case row); docs/implementation/10-phase-0-foundations.md P0-05 (the canonical-text sentence and the node list); P3-02 (how FanucMacro turns '[ ]' into a tree). Code: src/Ncx.Core/Expressions/UnaryNode.cs, ParenthesesNode.cs and ExprTokenizer.cs (the TODO(question) markers become comments); BinaryNode.cs and UnaryNode.cs (parentheses by precedence); the summary of ExprNode.ToCanonical; tests in tests/Ncx.Core.Tests/Expressions/.

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, not confirmed by the maintainer: the manuals do not settle this. Part (3) is informed but not settled: Fanuc writes NC programs in capitals, and bit 0 (ESL) of parameter 3459 either converts lowercase to the corresponding capitals or raises alarm 1090 — everything outside the comment, the program name and the folder name, the manual's own example turning `G90G01X100y50` into `G90G01X100Y50`. That is precedent for uppercase as the canonical spelling, not a rule about what NCX must accept. Part (1) is not a Fanuc question — Fanuc has no NOT at all (its operators are `+ - * /`, `MOD`, `AND`, `OR`, `XOR` and the EQ/NE/GT/GE/LT/LE comparisons) — but it is a Siemens one: the 840D has `NOT` and `B_NOT` and requires spaces between boolean operands and operators, so the recommendation's "NOT plus one space" matches the one control in scope that has the operator. For part (2) keep the parentheses, but write into the compilers that they must bracket from the tree and never copy the canonical text: Fanuc's precedence is functions, then `* / AND`, then `+ - OR XOR`, with brackets nesting at most five levels (a function's own counted, else alarm PS0118), while Siemens' is different again — NOT highest, then `* / DIV MOD`, then `+ -`, then the bit operators, AND, XOR, OR, with the comparisons lowest of all — so neither family reproduces the grouping of language 4.12 from unbracketed text.
Evidence: `Fanuc_30i-B_Bedienung-Drehen-Fraesen_B-64484EN_EN`, p. 2124-2125 (parameter 3459) (Bit 0 (ESL) of parameter 3459 decides how lowercase letters in an NC program are handled: 0 raises an alarm, 1 converts them to the corresponding capitals. The rule covers the whole program except the comment part, the program name and the folder name, and applies when the program is registered in or compared with CNC memory from an external device, and in M198/DNC operation. The example turns a lowercase axis word into the uppercase one; with ESL = 0 the control gives SR1090 on registration and PS1090 in operation); `Fanuc_30i-B_Bedienung-Drehen-Fraesen_B-64484EN_EN`, p. 2445 (alarm list) (Alarm 1090 "FEHLER PROGRAMMFORMAT" is raised when an NC program carries lowercase letters anywhere other than in a comment, a program name or a folder name); `Fanuc_30i-B_Bedienung-Drehen-Fraesen_B-64484EN_EN`, p. 508 (§16.5, table 16.5 (a)) (The table of arithmetic and logical operations lists addition and subtraction together with OR and XOR, multiplication and division together with AND and MOD, and the functions SIN through POW. No NOT operator appears, and the reserved-word lists elsewhere in the manual (AND, OR, XOR, MOD, EQ, NE, GT, LT, GE, LE and the function names) do not contain one either); `Fanuc_30i-B_Bedienung-Drehen-Fraesen_B-64484EN_EN`, p. 511-512 (Priority of operations: first functions, then the multiplication-type operations (*, /, AND), then the addition-type operations (+, -, OR, XOR). Brackets change the order and nest up to five levels, the brackets that delimit a function counted, beyond which the control raises alarm PS0118 "ZU VIELE KLAMMERN". The same page allows a function to be written with its first two letters (ROUND as RO, FIX as FI); POW cannot be abbreviated); `Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl_Programmierhandbuch-NC-Programmierung_SW492_DE_2019`, p. 451-452 (§3.1.3, operators and priority) (Siemens has the logical operators AND, OR, NOT, XOR and the bitwise B_AND, B_OR, B_NOT, B_XOR, and states that spaces must be written between boolean operands and operators. The priority list runs from NOT and B_NOT highest, through * / DIV MOD, then + -, then B_AND, B_XOR, B_OR, then AND, XOR, OR, then string concatenation, with the comparison operators ==, <>, >, <, >=, <= lowest of all). (Citations re-paged to the cnc-manuals connector 2026-10-26.)

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

(1) NOT is followed by one space; unary minus stands directly before its operand. (2) Written parentheses are kept as ParenthesesNode; where a code-built tree lacks them, the printer adds the parentheses precedence needs. (3) Function names and AND/OR/NOT/MOD are accepted in any case and written uppercase. Write this canonical text into language 4.12. Compilers must bracket from the tree, never copy the canonical text.
Basis: manual
Source: Siemens 840D sl NC-Programmierung 2019 p. 451-452 (NOT exists, spaces required, own precedence); Fanuc 30i-B B-64484EN p. 508, 511-512 (no NOT, different precedence, max 5 bracket levels, PS0118); p. 2124-2125 (lowercase converted to capitals).
Differs from the recommendation: no (adds the compiler bracketing note)
Confidence: high
Code impact: Ncx.Core Expressions (UnaryNode, BinaryNode precedence parens, tokenizer case); language 4.12.

#### D113 SPINDLE_MODE without a role address
Question: Language 4.5 writes the SPINDLE_MODE row as 'addr = spindle role'. In the same table, SPINDLE and RPM say 'optional addr' and ORIENT says 'addr optional'. VM 2.4 writes `SPINDLE_MODE:r` next to `SPINDLE[:r]`, `RPM[:r]`, `ORIENT[:r]` and `CSS[:r]`. VM 3.8 rule 2 lists SPINDLE, RPM, VC, CSS, RPM_MAX and ORIENT as the words that target default_spindle, and SPINDLE_MODE is not among them. VM 3.8 rule 4 writes `SPINDLE_MODE:r=AXIS`. On the other side stand two general sentences: language 4.10, 'A word without a role address targets the default resource of its kind', and machine-config 1, '`default_*` resolve NCX words without a role address'. Is a bare `SPINDLE_MODE=AXIS` an ERROR? If not, which spindle does it switch? On main the address is optional (SpindleWords.cs), and ResourceResolver.ResolveWorkSpindle sends a bare SPINDLE_MODE to default_spindle. When that spindle is not a work spindle, it reports the wrong-resource-type ERROR of 3.8 rule 1. On millturn1.toml (default_spindle S1 = MAIN), a bare SPINDLE_MODE=AXIS after WORKPIECE=SUB therefore switches MAIN. A bare C in the next block resolves to the axis of SUB (3.8 rule 3), and that is the rule 4 ERROR.
Recommendation: Required, as the 4.5 row, VM 2.4 and VM 3.8 rules 2 and 4 write it. A bare SPINDLE_MODE is the PAR ERROR of a missing address (PAR151). Reason: on a mill-turn the spindle to switch is the one that holds the part, and the program should name it. Both examples write the role (SPINDLE_MODE:SUB, SPINDLE_MODE:MAIN), and a reader takes the role from the [spindle_mode.ROLE] table it matched. Language 4.10 then reads 'A word whose row makes the role address optional targets the default resource of its kind'. Code changes: set IsAddrRequired on the SPINDLE_MODE entry and remove its TODO(question); the sample word in CanonicalOrderTests becomes SPINDLE_MODE:MAIN=AXIS. Alternative: optional. A bare SPINDLE_MODE then targets the current workpiece holder (WORKPIECE, initially default_workpiece), which must be a work spindle, because that is the spindle whose C axis a bare C drives (3.8 rule 3). The 4.5 row, VM 2.4 and 3.8 rule 2 are amended to match. Keeping default_spindle, as main does now, makes a bare SPINDLE_MODE and a bare C point at different spindles after WORKPIECE=SUB.
Where: language 4.5 (SPINDLE_MODE row), 4.10; VM 2.4, 3.8 rules 2 and 4; machine-config 1 (`default_*`); src/Ncx.Core/Catalog/SpindleWords.cs (TODO(question) at SPINDLE_MODE); src/Ncx.Core/VirtualMachine/VirtualMachine.cs ResolveResource and ResourceResolver.cs ResolveWorkSpindle; tests/Ncx.Core.Tests/Catalog/CanonicalOrderTests.cs; docs/spec/generated/word-catalog.md.

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, not confirmed by the maintainer: the manuals do not settle this. The manuals cannot decide the NCX rule, but the convention they show is uniform: on every mill-turn in the library the spindle whose mode changes is carried by the code itself — Mori M45 (spindle 1) / M245 (spindle 2), Nakamura M91 main / M441-M491 sub, Doosan M34/M35 for C1 and M134/M135 for C2, DMG L701, L703, L705, L707 one cycle per spindle. A compiler can therefore never pick the template without the role, which is the recommendation's case for requiring the address. Siemens is the counter-example: a bare M70 is legal and switches the master spindle into axis mode, and SETMS(n) moves the master to the spindle holding the part for the second side. So the manuals back "required" over main's behaviour; and where an un-addressed form does exist (Siemens M70, Doosan M35) it targets the master spindle or the main work spindle, never a configured default — the resource the controls model is the current workpiece holder, not a fixed default_spindle.
Evidence: `Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl-828D_Programmierhandbuch-Grundlagen_DE_2013`, p. 116-118 (section 7.4) (M<n>=70 switches a spindle into axis mode: the bare M70 (or M0=70) acts on the master spindle, M<n>=70 on spindle n. No defined position is approached and the block advances once the switch is done. Page 118 adds that the control detects the transition into axis mode from the programming sequence itself, so programming M70 explicitly is in principle no longer necessary.); `Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl-828D_Programmierhandbuch-Grundlagen_DE_2013`, p. 81-84 (section 6.1) (As a rule the main spindle is declared master spindle by machine data; bare S, M3, M4, M5 act on it and every other spindle needs S<n>= / M<n>=. SETMS(<n>) redeclares the master spindle and must stand in a block of its own. The worked lathe example machines the right side with the preset master, then SETMS(2) makes the second work spindle master so G95 applies to it for the left side, then SETMS returns.); `Mori-Seiki_NT-NTX-Serie_Programmierung_Programmieranleitung-NTX1000SZM_PX-NT_4-K0DEEN_2011`, p. 264-265 (section 1-14) (M45 connects the C axis of spindle 1 and M245 that of spindle 2, M46 and M246 cancel them. Page 265 adds that M05 must stop spindle 1 or 2 before M45 or M245 is given, otherwise alarm PS0197. The spindle is identified by the M code number, never implicitly.); `Nakamura-Tome_Super-NTJX_Programmierung_Liste-M-G-Codes_DE_2016`, p. 1-3 (M91 switches the main spindle C axis on and M41 off (page 1); M491 does the same for the sub spindle and M441 switches it off (page 3). Separate codes per spindle, with M427 for machining at the sub spindle and M428 at the main spindle.); `Nakamura-Tome_Fanuc_Programmierung_Programmierhandbuch-1_4810004ECL-1_DE_2013`, p. 136-137, chapter 7, item (68) (M491 (C-Achsenwahl an der rechten Einheit) switches the right-hand unit from spindle mode into C-axis mode, i.e. the code itself names which unit's spindle changes mode.); `Doosan_PUMA-Baureihe_Bedienungshandbuch_DE_2020`, p. 274 and 276 (no readable text in the cnc-manuals connector), Teil 5 Anhang M-code list; worked transfer example on p. 240 (no readable text in the cnc-manuals connector) (M35 is "C-Achsenwahl EIN" and M34 off; M135 is "C2-Achsenwahl EIN" and M134 off. The transfer example programs M135 with the comment "Umschaltung auf Zusatzspindel-C-Achsen-Modus" and then M35 for the main spindle. The un-numbered form exists but is bound to the main spindle by its code number.); `DMG-MORI_CTX-GMX_Technik-Programmierung-Sinumerik840Dsl_V2.1_DE_2015`, p. 29-36 (no readable text in the cnc-manuals connector; its index, p. 251-254, lists L701 to L708 at printed 2-15 to 2-22), section 2.3.1 (Four separate builder cycle pairs switch C-axis mode on and off, one per spindle: L701/L702 for tool spindle 1 (C1), L703/L704 for tool spindle 2 (C2), L705/L706 for the counter spindle (C3), L707/L708 for the main spindle (C4), each positioning to a given angle.). (Citations re-paged to the cnc-manuals connector 2026-10-26.)

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

The role address is required: a bare SPINDLE_MODE is PAR151 (missing address). Set IsAddrRequired on SPINDLE_MODE; language 4.10 reads "A word whose row makes the role address optional targets the default resource of its kind"; the CanonicalOrderTests sample becomes SPINDLE_MODE:MAIN=AXIS.
Basis: manual
Source: Every mill-turn names the spindle in the code itself: Mori NTX M45/M245 (Programmieranleitung NTX1000 p. 264-265), Nakamura M91/M491 (Liste M-G-Codes p. 1-3), DMG L701..L707 (CTX 840D sl p. 29-36). Siemens bare M70 targets the master spindle (Grundlagen 2013 p. 116-118), not a configured default.
Differs from the recommendation: no
Confidence: high
Code impact: Ncx.Core SpindleWords.cs; CanonicalOrderTests; word-catalog.md.

#### D114 Parameter names of a catalog cycle in the parser
Question: Language 4.7.1 lets a program use any catalog name with that entry's parameter names ('CYCLE=RECT_POCKET LENGTH=60 WIDTH=40 DEPTH=-10 ...'). cycles/heidenhain.toml maps LENGTH to Q218 and WIDTH to Q219 for cycle 251, as machine-config 6 does. Architecture 4, however, lets the parser pass 'no unknown key other than the two provisional forms': the machine axis word of D93 and the native parameter of a `CYCLE:<controller>=n` block of D94. Language 3 (KEY) and VM 3 step 1 name the same two. The cycle catalogs are data (D76), and ncx format reads without a machine file (D91), so the parser cannot look LENGTH up. On main, LENGTH and WIDTH are the unknown-key ERROR PAR010. The legal 4.7.1 program therefore does not parse, and a reader cannot write CYCL DEF 251 under its catalog name.
Recommendation: Add a third provisional form, after the pattern of D93 and D94. In a block whose CYCLE value is a name other than the seven built-in names and OFF, every key the word catalog does not know is a cycle parameter with a number or expression value. It is kept in source order after the cycle words (the D94 rank), so the canonical text does not depend on a machine file. A key of the machine-axis form stays a machine axis word (D93). A catalog may not name a parameter in that form, and the cycle catalog loader reports it, so the block reads the same with or without a machine file. The VM checks the cycle name and the parameter names against the machine's cycle catalog. With a machine file, an unknown name is an ERROR. Without one, it is the WARNING 'not checked: no machine file'; this extends the D103 list (role, function, machine axis) by the cycle name and its parameters, which D103 does not name today. Alternative: a word that carries the parameter name as its address (CYCLE=RECT_POCKET PARAM:LENGTH=60). That keeps the parser closed, but it rewrites the 4.7.1 example and the params keys of machine-config 6.
Where: language 3 (KEY row), 4.7.1; architecture 4 and 4.1 (the 'two provisional forms' sentence and the flowchart); VM 3 step 1, 3.3, 3.8 (default machine), 5; D93, D94, D103; src/Ncx.Core/Catalog/WordCatalog.cs IsNativeParameterAllowed (TODO(question)); src/Ncx.Core/Parsing/Parser.cs CheckWords; src/Ncx.Core/Catalog/CanonicalRanks.cs (native-parameter rank); src/Ncx.Config/Cycles/CycleCatalogLoader (parameter-name check); docs/spec/generated/word-catalog.md (rank 940 row); the cycle handling of P1-03.

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, not confirmed by the maintainer: the manuals do not settle this. No manual settles this: whether the parser takes a third provisional form is an NCX grammar question. What the manuals do settle is that there is no native name=value cycle form to imitate — Heidenhain writes numbered Q parameters and carries the name only as the dialogue text (CYCL DEF 251: Q218 = 1. Seiten-Länge, Q219 = 2. Seiten-Länge, exactly as cycles/heidenhain.toml maps them), Siemens calls a cycle with positional parameters, Fanuc with address letters. The one place a control does attach names to cycle parameters confirms the same split: Siemens' uc.com user-cycle description file gives each parameter a display text while the call itself stays positional. So the catalog parameter name is NCX's own layer in all three families, which argues for the recommendation (let the machine's catalog, not the word catalog, know the name) rather than for the PARAM:LENGTH alternative, which would have no native counterpart either.
Evidence: `Heidenhain_iTNC530_Zyklen_670_388-12_NC-SW-340490-07_DE_2011`, p. 147 (cycle 251 RECHTECKTASCHE, parameter list) (Verified. The pocket's two side lengths are the numbered parameters Q218 ("1. Seiten-Länge", parallel to the main axis) and Q219 (parallel to the secondary axis); the name exists only as the dialogue text, the program carries the number); `Index_Sinumerik-840D_Zyklen_Sinumerik-840D-Zyklen_LY4401.10092_DE_2004`, p. 51 (CYCLE81) (Verified. A Siemens cycle is called with a positional parameter list, CYCLE81 (RTP, RFP, SDIS, DP, DPR); the names appear only in the manual's Datentyp/Bedeutung table, not in the call); `Fanuc_30i-B_Bedienung-Fraesen_B-64484EN-2_EN`, p. 60, G73 format (Verified. A Fanuc canned cycle takes its parameters as address letters in the block (G73 X_ Y_ Z_ R_ Q_ F_ K_); there are no parameter names at all); `Siemens_Sinumerik-840D-810D_Programmierhandbuch-Arbeitsvorbereitung_DE_2006`, p. 129-132, section 2.17 Anwenderzyklen parametrieren (Added by me. The files cov.com and uc.com parameterise a shop's own cycles. Each parameter gets a line whose last field is a comment text of at most 50 characters shown in front of the input field, while the cycle itself is still called positionally — the name is a layer the description file adds, not part of the call). (Citations re-paged to the cnc-manuals connector 2026-10-26.)

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

Add a third provisional form: in a block whose CYCLE value is not a built-in name or OFF, every key unknown to the word catalog is a cycle parameter (number or expression), kept in source order at the D94 rank. Machine-axis-form keys stay D93 words, and the catalog loader rejects a parameter name of that form. The VM checks names against the machine's cycle catalog: ERROR with a machine file, the D103 WARNING "not checked: no machine file" without one (D103 list extended).
Basis: manual
Source: No control has a name=value cycle form (Heidenhain iTNC 530 Zyklen p. 147 Q218/Q219; Sinumerik 840D Zyklen LY4401 p. 51 positional; Fanuc B-64484EN-2 p. 60 letters), so the name is NCX's own catalog layer, which argues against PARAM:LENGTH.
Differs from the recommendation: no
Confidence: medium
Code impact: Ncx.Core WordCatalog.IsNativeParameterAllowed, Parser.CheckWords, CanonicalRanks; Ncx.Config CycleCatalogLoader.

#### D115 Kind of a catalog parameter
Question: 12-phase-2 P2-03 asks for CycleEntry 'Params with their kinds', and the P2-03 task asks for 'parameter names and kinds'. machine-config 6 has no kind key, and architecture 6 draws Params as `Dictionary<string,string>`. The kind matters when a program writes a catalog parameter that is not a word of language 4.7, for example CYCLE=RECT_POCKET LENGTH=60 WIDTH=40 (language 4.7.1). D94 gives a value type only to the native parameters of a `CYCLE:<controller>=n` block, and ncx format has no machine file (D91). Is a kind key needed, and what value does such a parameter take?
Recommendation: No kind key. A catalog parameter that is not a word of language 4.7 takes a number or an expression, as D94 gives native parameters. The words of 4.7 keep the kinds of the Value column of language 4.7: AXIS is an axis name, CYCLE_RETRACT is CLEARANCE or SAFE, CONTOUR is a sub name (D65). Every shipped entry fits this, and the code already records no kind. Strike 'with their kinds' in the phase file and the task, and add that sentence to machine-config 6. Answer this together with D114 (how the parser accepts LENGTH in a CYCLE=RECT_POCKET block): the value type decided here is the one the parser gives it. Alternative: a per-entry kinds table for a future string parameter such as CYCLE952 _PRG. Without a machine file the parser could not read it anyway.
Where: machine-config 6; 12-phase-2-configuration.md P2-03; docs/plan/tasks/done/P2-03-cycle-catalogs.md (scope); src/Ncx.Core/Machine/CycleEntry.cs (header TODO); header TODOs of cycles/fanuc.toml, heidenhain.toml, siemens.toml; with D114: src/Ncx.Core/Catalog/WordCatalog.cs IsNativeParameterAllowed.

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, not confirmed by the maintainer: the manuals do not settle this. The draft's reasoning does not survive the pages. Heidenhain cycle parameters are not all numeric: the same cycle-251 page that carries Q218/Q219 offers "alternativ FAUTO, FU, FZ" for the milling feed Q207 and "alternativ PREDEF" for Q200, Q204 and the climb/conventional selector Q351, and Q208 of cycles 201 and 203 takes FMAX, FAUTO or PREDEF — so a catalog parameter mapped to one of those positions can legitimately carry a control literal, which is exactly what D164's own Q208=MAX default writes. And the one native cycle-catalog description format in the library does carry a kind: Siemens' uc.com, the file with which a shop parameterises its own cycles, gives every parameter a line (type / min max / default / comment) whose type letter is R, I, C or S. The recommendation can still stand for the entries the shipped catalogs contain, since those are all numeric, but "a number or an expression" has to be widened to admit the family's literals, and the draft's alternative (a per-entry kinds table) is precisely what the one control that ships such a format does.
Evidence: `Heidenhain_iTNC530_Zyklen_670_388-12_NC-SW-340490-07_DE_2011`, p. 147 (cycle 251) (Corrected. The selectors are numeric (Q215 = 0/1/2, Q367 = 0..4, Q351 = +1/-1), but the same page ends several entries with "alternativ FAUTO, FU, FZ" (Q207) and "alternativ PREDEF" (Q200, Q204, Q351) — named literals, not numbers); `Heidenhain_iTNC530_Zyklen_670_388-12_NC-SW-340490-07_DE_2011`, p. 90 (cycle 203, Q208) (Added by me. Q208 "Vorschub Rückzug" has input range 0 to 99999,999 "alternativ FMAX, FAUTO, PREDEF" — the position NCX fills with the literal MAX); `Siemens_Sinumerik-840D-810D_Programmierhandbuch-Arbeitsvorbereitung_DE_2006`, p. 131-132, Syntaxbeschreibung für die Datei uc.com (Added by me. A parameter line is (<Datentypkennung> / <Minimalwert> <Maximalwert> / <Vorbelegungswert> / <Kommentar>) with the type letters R for Real, I for Integer, C for Charakter and S for String; min/max may be omitted, enumerated values are listed after "*", and String and Charakter have no limits); `Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl_Programmierhandbuch-NC-Programmierung_SW492_DE_2019`, p. 1096-1097 (CYCLE95 parameter table) (Verified. Each cycle parameter has a Datentyp: NPP is string (Name des Konturunterprogramms), MID/FALZ/FALX/FAL real. machine-config 6 does route NPP through the `contour` key, as the answer claims); `Siemens_Sinumerik-840D-sl_Programmierung_BS.000504-DE-000-00_DE`, p. 776-777 (CYCLE800 parameter table) (Verified. _TC is typed String[20], the name of the swivel data set; _FR and _ST are integers with enumerated values). (Citations re-paged to the cnc-manuals connector 2026-10-26.)

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

No kind key in 1.0, as recommended. An NCX catalog parameter that is not a word of language 4.7 takes a number or an expression. Words of 4.7 keep their 4.7 kinds. Native control literals (Heidenhain FMAX, FAUTO, FU, FZ, PREDEF) are allowed only on the native side: in a catalog's native `defaults` text (as D164's Q208=MAX already is). When the Heidenhain reader finds such a literal in a position that is mapped to an NCX catalog parameter, it keeps the block RAW (D5). It does not invent a number for it. machine-config 6 says this in one sentence. Reserve an optional per-entry `kinds` table (R/I/C/S, after Siemens uc.com) for later string parameters. It is not a 1.0 key.
Basis: manual + logical
Source: iTNC 530 Zyklen 670388-12 p. 147 (cycle 251), p. 90 (Q208); Siemens 840D/810D Arbeitsvorbereitung 2006 p. 131-132 (uc.com type letters). Logical: every shipped entry is numeric. Mapping a literal like FAUTO onto an NCX number would be a silent guess, and RAW is the safe fallback.
Differs from the recommendation: yes: adds the RAW rule for native literals in mapped positions, and names `kinds` as the future extension point instead of rejecting it.
Confidence: medium
Code impact: Heidenhain reader (P3) keeps such a block RAW. Doc sentence only in Ncx.Core/CycleEntry.

#### D116 Words whose Scope column names a partner
Question: Language 5 rule 5 and VM 5 name IF, ARG, TIMES, WITH, FRAME, MOVE, ROT, POINT and PHASE as words that need their partner in the block. The Scope column of language 4 names partners for more words. NAME is 'with PROGRAM=BEGIN, SUB=BEGIN or START_CHANNEL', NUMBER is 'with PROGRAM=BEGIN', and CHANNEL is a 'header' word; section 4.1 says 'NAME, NUMBER and CHANNEL may follow in the same block', and the EBNF puts the header words on the PROGRAM=BEGIN line. The cycle words AXIS to CONTOUR are 'with CYCLE', and 4.7 says 'its parameters follow in the same block'. Is CHANNEL=2 on a block of its own an ERROR? Is DEPTH=-5 without CYCLE? On main the parser checks only the rule-5 words. StructurePass refuses any other word in the PROGRAM=BEGIN block, but not a header word outside it, and the VM reads NAME, NUMBER and CHANNEL from the PROGRAM=BEGIN or SUB=BEGIN block only. A misplaced CHANNEL=2 is therefore ignored silently, and the program runs on channel 1. TOLERANCE:ROTARY needs no decision: VM 5 makes 'TOLERANCE:ROTARY or TOLERANCE_MODE without an active TOLERANCE' an ERROR of the modal state, not of the block. That rule is not on main yet (FrameHandlers.ApplyTolerance sets a rotary tolerance with none active); it belongs to the validation of P1-04.
Recommendation: Add these words to rule 5, with the existing PAR ERROR PartnerWordMissing (PAR016): NAME needs PROGRAM=BEGIN, SUB=BEGIN or START_CHANNEL; NUMBER and CHANNEL need PROGRAM=BEGIN; AXIS, SURFACE, CLEARANCE, DEPTH, SAFE, CYCLE_RETRACT, PECK, CYCLE_F, CYCLE_DWELL, PITCH and CONTOUR need CYCLE. List them in VM 5 as well. Reasons: the rows already say so, the catalog on main records these words as WithPartner or Header, and a silently ignored CHANNEL changes where the program runs. Alternative: keep rule 5 closed and report these words as a WARNING 'ignored outside its partner's block'.
Where: language 5 rule 5, VM 5; src/Ncx.Core/Parsing/BlockRules.cs s_partners (TODO(question) above it; its list also names TOLERANCE:ROTARY, which then drops out); the P0-04 block-rule tests; src/Ncx.Core/VirtualMachine/Handlers/FrameHandlers.cs ApplyTolerance (the VM 5 rule, for P1-04).

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, not confirmed by the maintainer: the manuals do not settle this. The manuals support the recommendation rather than contradict it, on both halves. Header words: Heidenhain puts the program name and the unit in the program-start block itself (BEGIN PGM), so NAME belonging to PROGRAM=BEGIN matches the source. Cycle words: on Heidenhain a CYCL DEF is one numbered NC block that carries all its Q parameters, and on Siemens a cycle is a call whose whole parameter list stands in the block (CYCLE81(RTP, RFP, SDIS, DP, DPR)), repeated in full at every position — both are exactly "its parameters follow in the same block". Only Fanuc differs, and there the drilling data is modal: the G8x stays active and a following block commands only what changes, so a Fanuc reader must re-emit the whole cycle definition wherever the source changes one datum. Language 4.7.1 already accepts that cost for the modal G90/G92/G94 turning cycles, where it says the following X blocks read as CYCLE plus one CYCLE_CALL each. The severity is still an NCX choice the manuals do not touch. No manual bears on CHANNEL: the channel of a Siemens multi-channel program is an assignment outside the program text, not a word. On NUMBER the sources disagree in form — Fastems (p. 16) puts the Siemens program number in the program-start line itself (%MPF6987), while for Fanuc (pp. 10, 12) the number stands alone in the second line, after the % of the first; both are compatible with NCX putting NUMBER on the PROGRAM=BEGIN block, but neither states a rule. Correction to an earlier citation: the Fanuc sentence on p. 71 about the modal G code staying effective "so that for identical drilling operations the drilling data need not be specified in every block" stands in the section on the small-hole peck-drilling cycle G83, not in the general canned-cycle chapter; the general statement is the one on p. 58.
Evidence: `Heidenhain_TNC640_Programmierung-Klartext_892903-18_NC-SW-34059x-10_DE_2019`, p. 90 ("Der erste NC-Satz eines NC-Programms ist mit BEGIN PGM, dem Programmnamen und der gültigen Maßeinheit gekennzeichnet"; the last block with END PGM and the same two. The name is part of the program-start block, never a block of its own.); `Heidenhain_TNC640_Zyklen_892905-18_NC-SW-34059x-10_DE_2019`, p. 63 ("Zyklus definieren über Softkeys": the control opens a dialog and asks for all input values, and ends the dialog only after every required datum has been entered. The worked example is one numbered NC block, "7 CYCL DEF 200 BOHREN" followed by Q200, Q201, Q206, Q202, Q210, Q203, Q204, Q211, Q395 — all nine parameters inside block 7. The programming example on p. 168 shows the same: block 14 is the whole CYCL DEF 200 with its parameters and block 15 is the CYCL CALL.); `Index_Sinumerik-840D_Zyklen_Sinumerik-840D-Zyklen_LY4401.10092_DE_2004`, p. 51-53 (Section 2.1.2, CYCLE81: "Programmierung: CYCLE81 (RTP, RFP, SDIS, DP, DPR)" — the whole parameter list stands inside the call. The example calls it three times, N40 CYCLE81 (110, 100, 2, 35), N60 CYCLE81 (110, 102, , 35) and N90 CYCLE81 (110, 100, 2, , 65), each with the full list (an omitted parameter is an empty place between commas). A Siemens cycle parameter never stands in a block of its own.); `Fanuc_30i-B_Bedienung-Fraesen_B-64484EN-2_EN`, p. 58 (Bohrmodus: G73, G74, G76 and G81 to G89 are modal G codes and stay effective until switched off; drilling data commanded in the drilling mode is retained until it is changed or cleared; all data needed for drilling is specified at the start of the canned cycle, and while cycles run only the changes are commanded. The cycle G code remains modally active throughout, so such a block is not a parameter block without a cycle.); `Fanuc_0i-D_Bedienung-Drehen-Fraesen_B-64304EN_EN`, p. 1231, appendix K "Unterschiede zur Serie 0i-C" (K.46.1: with K0 for the repeat count in a G80 to G89 canned cycle, on the M series "findet kein Bohrvorgang statt und es werden nur die Bohrdaten gespeichert"; on the T series the behaviour is chosen by parameter 5102 bit 5 (0i-C) and by 5105 bit 4 on the 0i-D for both series. A definition-only cycle block therefore exists, but it still carries the cycle G code.); `Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl-828D_Programmierhandbuch-Grundlagen_DE_2013`, p. 82 and 84 (SETMS), 110 (WAITP), 342 (frames), 387 (G4) ("SETMS muss in einem eigenen Satz stehen" (pp. 82, 84); "WAITP(<Achse>) ; Programmierung im eigenen NC-Satz!" (p. 110); "Frame-Anweisungen werden jeweils in einem eigenen NC-Satz programmiert" (p. 342); "G4 muss im eigenen NC-Satz programmiert werden" (p. 387). Siemens' per-word block rules are all of the "alone in the block" kind, not of the "needs its partner" kind.). (Citations re-paged to the cnc-manuals connector 2026-10-26.)

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

Extend language 5 rule 5 and VM 5 with PAR016 PartnerWordMissing: NAME needs PROGRAM=BEGIN, SUB=BEGIN or START_CHANNEL; NUMBER and CHANNEL need PROGRAM=BEGIN; AXIS, SURFACE, CLEARANCE, DEPTH, SAFE, CYCLE_RETRACT, PECK, CYCLE_F, CYCLE_DWELL, PITCH and CONTOUR need CYCLE. TOLERANCE:ROTARY drops out of s_partners (its rule is the VM 5 modal ERROR, P1-04).
Basis: manual
Source: Heidenhain TNC 640 Klartext 2019 p. 90 (name in BEGIN PGM block); TNC 640 Zyklen p. 63 and Sinumerik 840D Zyklen LY4401 p. 51-53 (all cycle parameters in the cycle block). Fanuc modal drilling data (B-64484EN-2 p. 58) means its reader re-emits the full CYCLE block.
Differs from the recommendation: no
Confidence: high
Code impact: Ncx.Core BlockRules.s_partners; P0-04 block-rule tests.

#### D120 Indexed SYS_ registers in the vars file (machine-config 8)
Question: VM 2.7 says $SYS_WEAR_Z[99] 'reads register 99 of the wear table, which the VM does not hold: UNKNOWN in STATIC mode, from the vars file or an ERROR in INTERPRETED mode'. VM 3.6 names only the ERROR, both for a name the configuration does not map and for a state that is unknown. The phase 4 risks name the vars file as the way out for unknown SYS_ state. Machine-config 8 shows only plain keys (Q1 = 10, QS1 = "TEXT") and says nothing about SYS_ names or an index, and a bare TOML key cannot contain brackets. How does part.vars.toml give register 99 of SYS_WEAR_Z its value? And does a vars-file value also count for a SYS_ name the configuration does not map? Without a machine file that is every SYS_ name, because the built-in default machine of D103 maps none.
Recommendation: The key is the name as the program writes it, without the $, quoted in TOML, with the index as a plain whole number: "SYS_WEAR_Z[99]" = 0.012. A SYS_ name without an index stays a bare key (SYS_POS_X = 12.5). The evaluator uses the vars-file value wherever the VM has no value of its own, including a name the configuration does not map, and VM 3.6 says so as 2.7 does. Without a vars-file value it reports VM903, and the message names the vars file. Reason: the user copies the name from the program, and analyze without a machine file can still run a program that reads a register. VarsFile already loads any top-level key, and VariableStore already keeps SYS_ start values apart by name, so only the lookup is new. Alternatives: one table per name, [SYS_WEAR_Z] with 99 = 0.012, which groups the rows of a table but needs tables in the vars file loader; the vars file supplies only names the configuration maps.
Where: machine-config 8 (vars file example); VM 2.7, 3.6 (the `$SYS_*` bullet); src/Ncx.Config/VarsFile.cs; src/Ncx.Core/VirtualMachine/State/VariableStore.cs (constructor with the SYS_ start values, GetSystem); src/Ncx.Core/Expressions/Evaluator.cs EvaluateSystemVariable (TODO for P4-01 part two).

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, not confirmed by the maintainer: the manuals do not settle this. No manual can decide a TOML key, but they support the NAME[index] spelling: Fanuc's own named system variable for the Z wear register is #_OFSZW[n] with n the compensation number, numerically #11001-#11999, so "SYS_WEAR_Z[99]" = #11099 is exactly how the programmer writes it — and register 99 only exists on a machine with more than 64 offset pairs (without the extended memory the range is #2101-#2164, n = 1..64). One index is a Fanuc shape, though: Siemens wear length 1 is $TC_DP12[t,d] with a T number and a D number, and Heidenhain FN 18 selects system data by group number (ID), data number (NR) and an optional index (IDX). Whatever key form is chosen, the SYS_ index will have to carry more than one number once Siemens and Heidenhain tool data are mapped.
Evidence: `Fanuc_30i-B_Bedienung-Drehen-Fraesen_B-64484EN_EN`, p. 455-456, ch. 16 Kundenmakro (The tool compensation system variables of series T are listed with a named form carrying a bracketed index: the Z wear value is #_OFSZW[n], numerically #2101-#2164 for n = 1..64 and #11001-#11999 for n = 1..999 when more than 64 pairs are fitted; X wear is #_OFSXW[n], nose radius #_OFSRW[n].); `Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl_Listenhandbuch-Systemvariable_SW45_DE_2012`, p. 264-265 (section 1.8 Werkzeugparameter) ($TC_DP12[t,d] is wear length 1, with index 1 the T number (1..32000) and index 2 the cutting-edge / D number (1..32000); only with the 'flache D-Nummernverwaltung' function active does it collapse to $TC_DP12[d]. $TC_DP13[t,d] is wear length 2.); `Heidenhain_TNC640_Programmierung-Klartext_892903-18_NC-SW-34059x-10_DE_2019`, p. 295 (FN 18: SYSREAD selects a system datum by group number (ID-Nr.), system data number and optionally an index, as in the example reading the active Z scaling factor with ID210 NR4 IDX3. The values read are always returned metric, independent of the NC program's unit.). (Citations re-paged to the cnc-manuals connector 2026-10-26.)

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

Key = the name as the program writes it, without `$`, quoted, with the index as plain whole numbers: `"SYS_WEAR_Z[99]" = 0.012`; unindexed names stay bare keys. Allow a comma-separated multi-index (`"SYS_X[3,1]"`) in the key grammar from the start. The evaluator uses a vars-file value wherever the VM has none, including names the configuration does not map; otherwise VM903, whose message names the vars file. VM 3.6 says so as 2.7 does.
Basis: manual
Source: Fanuc B-64484EN p. 455-456 (#_OFSZW[n], one index); Siemens Systemvariable SW45 p. 264-265 ($TC_DP12[t,d], two indices); Heidenhain TNC 640 Klartext p. 295 (FN 18 ID/NR/IDX). Siemens and Heidenhain need more than one index.
Differs from the recommendation: yes: the key grammar admits more than one index.
Confidence: medium
Code impact: Ncx.Config VarsFile (key parse); VariableStore and Evaluator.EvaluateSystemVariable lookup.

#### D121 Precision of coordinates the VM computes
Question: The phase 1 risk in 11-phase-1 says a double reaches the position store only as "a rounded decimal with the units' decimals (D62)", but no document says how many decimals that is. D62 and architecture 4.2 only separate decimal storage from double geometry. The [format] decimals of machine-config 2 belong to the compiler, are set per address and per machine, and do not exist without a machine file (D103). The VM computes coordinates in double only in arc geometry. VM 3.2 keeps the center of an R arc ("The VM keeps the computed center, so the compiler can write either form") and the end of an ANGLE arc ("The VM stores start, center, sweep and end"). Retract, cycle and diameter positions stay decimal arithmetic. The computed digits reach trace, annotate, the Before/After snapshots, $SYS_POS_X and the start of the next block. How many decimals does a computed ANGLE end such as 69.025870876999 keep?
Recommendation: Use one fixed VM precision that does not depend on the machine: 6 decimals, rounded half away from zero (language 4.12, ROUND), in MM and INCH alike. Reasons: every example machine file uses 3 axis decimals, so 6 decimals leave the compiler's [format] rounding to decide the written digit. Trace stays readable (69.025871). It is one constant and needs no machine file. It also makes a computed point that should equal a written one compare equal (6.9999999999997 becomes 7), and the exact start = end comparison of D122 relies on that. Alternative: 4 decimals in MM and 5 in INCH. Trace is shorter, but rounding twice changes the last written digit more often (1.23449 becomes 1.2345, then 1.235 instead of 1.234).
Where: VM 3.2 (one sentence on stored computed coordinates); 11-phase-1 Risks (replace "the units' decimals"); architecture 4.2. Code: src/Ncx.Core/Geometry/Vec3.cs RoundToDecimal (TODO line 42) and its P1-03 callers (arc resolution in VirtualMachine.ExecuteMotion).

ANSWER: (Peter, 2026-10-07, drafted by Claude in project_spike) Accept as recommended: one fixed VM precision of 6 decimals, rounded half away from zero, in MM and INCH. It matches the resolution the CAM writes (opencam D-149) and D364's centre.
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, not confirmed by the maintainer: the manuals do not settle this. Six decimals in MM is the right constant: it is exactly the finest least input increment documented anywhere in the library (Fanuc IS-E, 0,000001 mm), and finer than Siemens' default Rechenfeinheit of 1000 increments per mm and than Heidenhain's finest input resolution of 0,01 µm. Rounding twice is also what the controls themselves do — Siemens rounds the programmed value multiplied by the Rechenfeinheit to a whole number, so 97,3786 mm becomes 97,379 mm at 1000 Inkr./mm — so the alternative's objection is the normal behaviour of a machine, not a defect. The one gap is INCH: Fanuc IS-E is 0,0000001 inch, one digit finer than six decimals; the ordinary IS-B (0,0001 inch) is four.
Evidence: Fanuc Serie 30i/31i/32i-B, Betriebshandbuch Drehen/Fräsen (B-64484GE/02), p. printed 30-31 (PDF 64-65), sections 2.3 and 2.4 (Table 2.3 (a) of the five increment systems IS-A to IS-E: least input and command increment 0,01 / 0,001 / 0,0001 / 0,00001 / 0,000001 mm, and 0,001 / 0,0001 / 0,00001 / 0,000001 / 0,0000001 inch, set per axis by bits 0 to 3 of parameter 1013, with IS-C, IS-D and IS-E named as optional functions. Section 2.4: maximum travel = least command increment × 999999999 (99999999 for IS-A).); SINUMERIK 840D sl / 828D Grundfunktionen, Funktionshandbuch 07/2012 (6FC5397-0BP40-3AA0), p. 335-336 (section 6.2.4, heading on 335, text and example on 336); default value on 333-334; PDF page = printed page (Distinguishes Eingabe-, Anzeige- and Rechenfeinheit. The Rechenfeinheit is set by MD10200 INT_INCR_PER_MM and MD10210 INT_INCR_PER_DEG (standard pre-assignment 1000 increments per mm and per degree) and fixes the number of effective decimals for positions, tool offsets and zero offsets; the programmed value times the Rechenfeinheit is rounded to a whole number, with the worked example 97,3786 mm becoming 97,379 mm.); HEIDENHAIN Funktionsübersicht Bahnsteuerungen TNC 320/620/640/iTNC 530, 11/2015 (785107-15), p. 47 (section 2.2 Technische Daten); option 23 listed on 42-43 (Eingabefeinheit und Anzeigeschritt: linear axes down to 0,1 µm on both TNC 640 and iTNC 530, 0,01 µm on the TNC 640 with software option 23 ("Display step"); rotary axes to 0,0001°, 0,00001° with the same option.).

#### D123 ORIGIN and positions known in the workpiece frame
Question: VM 2.1 and 4 let ORIGIN empty the chain, and VM 3.4 lets it clear the setpos shifts. But VM 3.4 does not list ORIGIN among the frame changes that mark the position unknown (TILT, TILT_AXIS, ROTATE, MIRROR, WORKPIECE, POLAR=OFF, CYLINDER=OFF). D35 keeps an axis moved in the machine frame unknown in the workpiece frame unless a datum table is configured. machine-config defines no datum table, so the VM does not know how two datums relate either. Yet VM 3.4 keeps a WORKPIECE change unknown "until the next ORIGIN or motion with known coordinates". Example: ORIGIN=1, RAPID X=10 Y=10 Z=5, ORIGIN=2, LINE IX=5 F=100. FrameRules.SelectOrigin folds the chain back as a RESET does and keeps the position. Once P1-03 executes the motions, X=10 therefore stays known in datum 2, the IX passes, and trace shows X 10 under G55. That is true only if G54 and G55 coincide. VM 3.4 and D101 already settle an axis known through SETPOS. MILLTURN_TRANSFER (WORKPIECE=SUB, ORIGIN=2, then absolute motions) checks clean under either rule.
Recommendation: ORIGIN=n that selects a datum other than the active one is a frame change of VM 3.4: every axis known in the workpiece, polar or cylinder frame becomes unknown there. Axes known in the MACHINE frame stay known, and the setpos handling stays as implemented. ORIGIN=n that repeats the active datum empties the chain as a RESET does (shifts folded back; a removed rotation, mirror or tilt marks the position unknown) and keeps the rest. Reasons: D35, since there is no datum table. A repeated datum changes nothing on the machine, so the coordinates stay true. Posts repeat the active datum at every operation (G54 per tool). They mostly write absolute X Y in the same block, which makes the position known again under either rule, but an incremental word after a repeated datum must not become an ERROR. The WORKPIECE sentence of VM 3.4 then reads "until the next motion with known coordinates". Alternative: every ORIGIN marks those positions unknown, the active datum included. That is one rule, but a repeated G54 loses the position until the next absolute motion.
Where: VM 3.4 (add ORIGIN to the list of frame changes; reword the WORKPIECE sentence); VM 2.1 origin row; language 4.2 ORIGIN row. Code: src/Ncx.Core/VirtualMachine/FrameRules.cs SelectOrigin (TODO line 71); FrameChainTests and SetposTests.

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, corrected 2026-10-26 after the manual audit, not confirmed by the maintainer: the manuals do not settle this. The manuals do not model a position "unknown in the workpiece frame", so the rule stays an NCX choice, but they support the recommendation on the point that matters. None of the three manuals makes an incremental word after a datum selection an error. Siemens defines the case through setting datum SD42440 $SC_FRAME_OFFSET_INCR_PROG, which decides whether an incremental move also traverses the active zero offset (0: only the programmed path, 1: the offset as well). No manual in the library states its delivered value: the programming manual's example sets it to 0 explicitly, and the function manual's wording reads as if 1 were the standard behaviour, so the default may be the reverse of what this answer first said. Fanuc requires absolute motion only after a G52 local-coordinate block, not after G54..G59. The alternative in the draft would therefore reject programs that run on the machine. The manuals also show the gap D35 rests on: every control holds a work zero offset memory for its six datums, which is exactly the datum table machine-config does not define. No manual in the library models an axis whose coordinate is unknown in a frame; that concept is NCX's own, so the exact rule for a repeated ORIGIN cannot be settled from the manuals. The SD42440 behaviour is about whether the offset is traversed, not about whether the coordinate is known; the parallel is by analogy. The Fanuc page does not say that the control always knows how any two datums relate, and the answer does not claim it. The negative claim is limited to the Fanuc 30i-B, Siemens 840D sl and Heidenhain TNC 640 manuals read, not to every control in the library. The correction does not change the agreement with the recommendation.
Evidence: SINUMERIK 840D sl NC-Programmierung, Programmierhandbuch 06/2019 (SW 4.92), p. 158 and 160 (SD42440 $SC_FRAME_OFFSET_INCR_PROG and SD42442 $SC_TOOL_OFFSET_INCR_PROG: 0 = an incremental axis command does not traverse the active zero offset or tool length compensation, 1 = it does. Example 3 on p. 160 sets SD42440 = 0 explicitly, with G54 holding an offset of 25 in X: N20 G1 G91 X10 travels 10 mm without the offset, and N30 G90 X50 then travels to X75, traversing it. No default is given.); SINUMERIK 840D sl/828D Funktionshandbuch Grundfunktionen (2012), p. 1704 (17.8.1 G91-Erweiterung: SD42440 decides whether the zero offset is traversed with "Wert = 1 standardmäßig" or only the programmed value with 0, without a default value; if the offset stays active over RESET (MD20110 bit 6 = 1) and the first part-program block is incremental, the offset is always traversed, and the note advises starting part programs absolute.); SINUMERIK 840D sl NC-Programmierung, Programmierhandbuch 06/2019, p. 731 (Frame change under G91 with an active transformation is not handled specially; the increment is evaluated in the workpiece coordinate system of the new frame.); FANUC Series 30i/31i/32i-MODEL B Operator's Manual B-64484EN, p. 217 (G52 caution 6: a move command right after the G52 block must be absolute.); FANUC Series 30i/31i/32i-MODEL B Operator's Manual B-64484EN, p. 206-207 (G54 to G59 select workpiece coordinate systems 1 to 6, changed through EXOFS and ZOFS1..ZOFS6; no requirement that motion after a G54..G59 block be absolute.).
Corrected: Withdrew "default: it does not" for SD42440, because no manual in the connector states the default and Grundfunktionen p. 1704 reads as if 1 (offset traversed) were the standard. The Fanuc pages now cite the English B-64484EN, which the connector holds; the conclusion is unchanged.

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

ORIGIN=n selecting a datum other than the active one is a VM 3.4 frame change: every axis known in the workpiece, polar or cylinder frame becomes unknown; MACHINE-frame knowledge and setpos handling stay. ORIGIN=n repeating the active datum empties the chain as RESET does and keeps the rest. The WORKPIECE sentence of VM 3.4 reads "until the next motion with known coordinates".
Basis: manual
Source: No control makes an incremental word after G54..G59 an error (Fanuc B-64484EN p. 206-207, only G52 needs absolute motion p. 217; Siemens SD42440, 840D sl NC-Programmierung 2019 p. 158-160, default not stated per audit). There is no datum table (D35), so a new datum gives unknown coordinates.
Differs from the recommendation: no
Confidence: high
Code impact: Ncx.Core FrameRules.SelectOrigin; FrameChainTests, SetposTests.
