#### D124 MIRROR=OFF as the reset form of the mirror
Question: VM 2.1 gives the chain words SHIFT, ROTATE, MIRROR, TILT and TILT_AXIS RESET forms that "cut the chain at the last entry of that kind" (D31). Language 4.2 writes SHIFT=RESET, ROTATE=RESET, TILT=RESET and TILT_AXIS=RESET. The MIRROR row gives the value "axis list or OFF", has no RESET, and does not say what OFF does. D31 and VM 2.1 already fix what a reset form does. What is open is whether MIRROR=OFF is that form, and whether it keeps the spelling OFF. Example: after MIRROR=X, ROTATE=30, MIRROR=OFF, the reset form removes the rotation together with the mirror, because the chain is cut at the mirror. An OFF that only ended mirroring would keep the rotation, as resetting Heidenhain cycle 8 keeps cycle 10.
Recommendation: MIRROR=OFF is the reset form of the mirror: it cuts the chain at the last MIRROR entry and removes everything after it, as the code does (FrameHandlers.ApplyMirror, FrameChainTests). A rotation programmed after the mirror goes with it. So a reader whose control resets the mirror alone (Heidenhain cycle 8 without axes, Fanuc G50.1) writes MIRROR=OFF followed by the words that should stay, for example ROTATE=30 again. A reader that cancels one of several mirrored axes (G50.1 X with X and Y mirrored) writes MIRROR=OFF followed by MIRROR=Y. OFF stays the spelling, which the parser, writer and catalog tests already use. Alternative: rename it MIRROR=RESET like the other chain words; the catalog, parser and writer tests would change.
Where: Language 4.2 MIRROR row; VM 2.1 transform chain row. Code: src/Ncx.Core/VirtualMachine/Handlers/FrameHandlers.cs ApplyMirror (TODO line 126); the MIRROR description in src/Ncx.Core/Catalog/FrameWords.cs (rank 680 of docs/spec/generated/word-catalog.md).

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, not confirmed by the maintainer: the manuals do not settle this. The manuals confirm both control facts the draft rests on and leave only the NCX naming open. On the iTNC 530 a coordinate transformation acts from its definition until it is reset or redefined, and each one is reset on its own — cycle 8 SPIEGELN by re-programming it with NO ENT, cycle 10 DREHUNG with 0 degrees — so cancelling the mirror there really does leave a later rotation standing, and the Heidenhain reader must re-emit ROTATE after MIRROR=OFF exactly as the recommendation says. Fanuc is the mirror image of that: mirror, scaling and rotation are processed in that order, the manual says to program them in that order and cancel them in reverse, and G50.1/G51.1 may not be given while scaling or coordinate rotation is active — so a legal Fanuc program can never cancel a mirror under a rotation programmed after it, which is exactly the chain cut. Whether the reset form keeps the spelling OFF or becomes MIRROR=RESET is not a control question.
Evidence: `Heidenhain_iTNC530_Zyklen_670_388-12_NC-SW-340490-07_DE_2011`, p. 278 (11.1 Grundlagen), 287 (cycle 8), 289 (cycle 10) (Verified. "Eine Koordinaten-Umrechnung wird ab ihrer Definition wirksam ... Sie wirkt so lange, bis sie rückgesetzt oder neu definiert wird", and resetting means redefining that cycle with its base value. Cycle 8 is reset by programming it again with NO ENT, cycle 10 by a rotation angle of 0 — each with its own reset instruction); `Fanuc_30i-B_Bedienung-Drehen-Fraesen_B-64484EN_EN`, p. 367-368, 15.3 programmierbare Achsenspiegelung (Verified. G51.1 IP_ starts the programmable mirror and G50.1 IP_ ends it, G50.1 naming only the axis ("Ein Symmetriepunkt ist nicht spezifiziert"). "Die Verarbeitung erfolgt in der Reihenfolge Achsenspiegelung, Skalierung, Koordinatensystemdrehung", the commands are to be given in that order and cancelled in reverse, and G50.1/G51.1 must not be programmed while scaling or coordinate rotation is active). (Citations re-paged to the cnc-manuals connector 2026-10-26.)

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

MIRROR=OFF is the reset form: it cuts the chain at the last MIRROR entry and removes everything after it. Readers whose control resets the mirror alone (Heidenhain cycle 8 with NO ENT) re-emit the words that stay (e.g. ROTATE=30) after MIRROR=OFF; cancelling one of several axes is MIRROR=OFF then MIRROR=<remaining>. Spelling stays OFF.
Basis: manual
Source: iTNC 530 Zyklen p. 278, 287, 289 (each transformation reset on its own); Fanuc B-64484EN p. 367-368 (mirror, scale, rotate in that order, cancel in reverse; G50.1 not allowed under rotation), so a legal Fanuc program never needs anything else.
Differs from the recommendation: no
Confidence: high
Code impact: none (FrameHandlers.ApplyMirror TODO becomes a comment; language 4.2 row text).

#### D125 X of SHIFT under DIAMETER=ON
Question: D60 and the DIAMETER row of language 4.2 halve "exactly the absolute and incremental X words of the workpiece (X, IX, the absolute CENTER:X)" and the X words of an AXIS=X cycle, and keep "every other radial distance" a radius; VM 3.1 repeats the list. The X of a SETPOS is such a word: the SETPOS row declares "these coordinates in the active workpiece frame", and the code halves it (VirtualMachine.cs ApplySetpos). The X of a SHIFT is an X word by its key, but a displacement of the frame, and so a radial distance by its meaning. The code keeps it as written, like CENTER:IX (ApplyShift). Example: under DIAMETER=ON, does SHIFT X=20 move the datum by 20 or by 10 in the radius store?
Recommendation: Every word with the key X or IX is a diameter under DIAMETER=ON, whatever the verb: SHIFT X=20 shifts by radius 10, just as SETPOS X=40 declares radius 20. Reasons: the row names the X words by key; a shift is written in the same program coordinates as the motions it moves; and IX, also a distance, is halved. How a control writes its shift under diameter programming (Fanuc G52 X, Siemens TRANS X under DIAMON) stays with the readers and compilers through the programming setting (D60). Alternative: SHIFT X is a radius distance like CENTER:IX, and a sentence in the DIAMETER row says so.
Where: Language 4.2 DIAMETER and SHIFT rows; VM 3.1 halving sentence and 3.4; D60 log line. Code: src/Ncx.Core/VirtualMachine/VirtualMachine.cs ApplyShift (TODO line 363); DiameterRules.

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, corrected 2026-10-26 after the manual audit, not confirmed by the maintainer: the manuals do not settle the NCX rule, but they now settle the convention of both controls, and the two differ. Fanuc backs the recommendation: on a Fanuc lathe the work coordinate system shift and the work zero offset both follow diameter or radius programming, with a worked example in which a reference point that should stand at ø120 but stands at ø121 is corrected with a shift of X=1.0, the diameter difference. The Siemens half is newly settled by a positive statement: the function manual lists the data that stay radius values on a facing axis whatever DIAMON says, and programmable and settable frames, the external zero offset and the DRF and preset offsets are on that list, so TRANS X under DIAMON is a radius by default. It is a machine setting, not a fixed rule: MD20360 $MC_TOOL_PARAMETER_DEF_MASK bit 3 = 1 makes zero offsets in frames diameter values for all facing axes, and bit 5 does the same for the external zero offset. What follows for the readers: a Fanuc reader halves the X of a lathe work shift or work zero offset; a Siemens reader keeps a TRANS X as a radius unless the machine sets MD20360 bit 3, so the reader needs that bit as a machine setting rather than a constant. The NCX rule itself stays a choice; the proposal agrees with the recommendation for Fanuc and records Siemens as the counter-case, now with its switch. The Fanuc statements are about the lathe work shift and the work zero offset, not about G52: that a G52 X is a diameter follows by inference, not from a page. Nothing was found in the Nakamura-Tome, Doosan, Muratec or Mori Seiki manuals: the Nakamura G354 work-shift description (NT-Nurse, cache p. 84) gives X only as "Verschiebungsbetrag der X-Achse" with no diameter note.
Evidence: FANUC Series 30i/31i/32i-MODEL B Operator's Manual B-64484EN, p. 215 (Diameter and radius values: the work coordinate system shift amount depends on diameter or radius programming. Example: the reference point should be at X = 120.0 (diameter) and Z = 70.0 but stands at X = 121.0 and Z = 69.0; the shift to set is X=1.0, Z=-1.0.); FANUC B-64484EN, p. 206-207 (Caution on selecting a workpiece coordinate system: the work origin offset value depends on diameter or radius programming.); FANUC B-64484EN, p. 230-231, Table 8.4 (a) (Under diameter programming the X command, the incremental command and the G50 coordinate are diameters; canned-cycle X depth, arc R, I, K and feed are radii; the position display is a diameter. G52 is not in the table.); SINUMERIK 840D sl/828D Funktionshandbuch Grundfunktionen (2012), p. 900 ("Durchmesser-bezogene Daten" under DIAMON/DIAM90: display of the facing axis in the WCS, JOG increments, programmed end positions, I, J, K with AC, and actual values read in the WCS: $AA_MW, $P_EP, $AA_IW.); same manual, p. 901-902 ("Fest Radius-bezogene Daten": for facing axes always radius values are tool offsets, programmable and settable frames, the external zero offset, DRF and preset offset, the working-area limitation, the software limit switches, the feed and the display data in the machine coordinate system.); same manual, p. 902-903 (MD20360 $MC_TOOL_PARAMETER_DEF_MASK: bit 3 = 1 computes zero offsets in frames of all facing axes as diameter values, stored internally as radius; bit 5 = 1 the same for the external zero offset.); SINUMERIK 840D sl NC-Programmierung, Programmierhandbuch 06/2019, p. 168-169 (DIAMON, DIAM90, DIAMOF, DIAMCYCOF; the list of data the diameter values apply to has no frames, TRANS or zero offsets.).
Corrected: The Siemens half is now settled: Grundfunktionen p. 901-903 states that frames on a facing axis are radius values by default and that MD20360 bit 3 switches them to diameter, where the earlier answer inferred the radius from an omission and treated it as fixed. The Fanuc pages now cite the English B-64484EN.

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

Every word with key X or IX is a diameter under DIAMETER=ON, whatever the verb: SHIFT X=20 shifts by radius 10. Readers translate: a Fanuc reader treats the lathe work shift / work offset X as a diameter; a Siemens reader keeps TRANS X as a radius (doubles it into the NCX word) unless the machine file sets the MD20360 bit 3 equivalent, which becomes a machine setting.
Basis: manual
Source: Fanuc B-64484EN lathe work shift follows diameter programming (worked ø120/ø121 example); Siemens Funktionshandbuch Grundfunktionen 2012 p. 901-903 (frames on a facing axis are radii unless MD20360 bit 3 / bit 5).
Differs from the recommendation: no (adds the Siemens reader setting)
Confidence: medium
Code impact: none in Ncx.Core (ApplyShift halves X); Siemens reader/compiler and a machine-file key for MD20360 bit 3 later.

#### D126 Frame of the rotary positions after TILT_AXIS with MOVE=TURN or MOVE
Question: VM 3.4 says MOVE=TURN or MOVE=MOVE "marks the rotary axes as moved to the plane (their positions are known only from TILT_AXIS words, ...)" without naming the frame they are known in. Language 4.2 calls the TILT_AXIS values "the rotary axis positions of this machine", and D82 says nothing about the frame. The frame decides three things: whether an IA or IC afterwards has a current value (VM 3.1), whether the limit check applies (MACHINE frame only, D100), and what the tool-vector analytics read (VM 8). Example: TILT_AXIS A=-90 C=180 MOVE=TURN, then RAPID IC=10. The code keeps A and C known in the MACHINE frame (VirtualMachine.cs ApplyTilt; FrameChainTests).
Recommendation: Use the MACHINE frame, as the code does. TILT_AXIS names the plane by physical axis positions, from which the kinematics module computes it (VM 10), and limits are machine coordinates (D100). The workpiece coordinate of those axes stays unknown until a motion with known coordinates (D35), so the IC above is the ERROR of VM 3.1. Whether a control applies a rotary datum offset to PLANE AXIAL, cycle 19 or the CYCLE800 axis mode stays with readers and compilers. Alternative: the workpiece frame of the active datum (the values a RAPID A= C= would write). That allows IA and IC afterwards, but skips the limit check until the machine position is known.
Where: VM 3.4 (name the frame); language 4.2 TILT_AXIS row. Code: src/Ncx.Core/VirtualMachine/VirtualMachine.cs ApplyTilt (TODO line 454); FrameChainTests.TiltAxisWithMoveTurn_NamedRotaryAxes_AreKnownAtTheirAngles.

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, corrected 2026-10-26 after the manual audit, not confirmed by the maintainer: the manuals do not settle this. The earlier answer said the manuals contradict the recommendation; after the audit that verdict is withdrawn, and the proposal neither confirms nor contradicts the MACHINE frame. The Siemens sentence it rested on, that CYCLE800 in the swivel mode "Rundachsen direkt" takes the WCS positions of the rotary axes, stands in the 840D Zyklen manuals of 2006 and 2008, whose text the connector cannot read, so it is unverified. The 840D sl manuals in the library point the other way or at least name no work frame: they tie only axis-wise swivelling to the workpiece coordinate system, and describe direct swivelling as programming the machine's swivel axes directly, giving the desired rotary-axis positions from which the control computes a matching coordinate system. A 2015 cycle-package note adds that direct swivelling positions differently when the rotary axes of the swivel data set carry zero offsets, switchable by SD55221 bit 8, so a rotary datum offset is a real case on Siemens and its handling is a setting. Heidenhain names no frame either: PLANE AXIAL defines the plane and the setpoint coordinates of the rotary axes, its axis angles must match the rotary axes present on the machine, an incremental axis angle adds to the currently effective one, and the function computes in no basic rotation, which concerns a basic rotation of the plane and does not by itself point at machine angles. After MOVE or TURN the rotary axes stand at the calculated axis values. So the manuals speak of axis positions of the machine, which fits the recommendation better than the earlier quote did, but no page says in which frame a control records them. The maintainer decides, and VM 3.4 should name the frame either way. On both controls a rotary axis normally carries no datum offset, so its workpiece and machine reading coincide and the two readings of the draft differ only on a machine that offsets a rotary axis. Separately, worth a line in language 4.2: CYCLE800's axis-wise mode rotates about the coordinate axes and is NCX TILT, not TILT_AXIS; only direct swivelling is TILT_AXIS, which matches the D82 mapping already recorded in decisions.md.
Evidence: SINUMERIK 840D sl/828D Bedienhandbuch Fräsen (2013), p. 138-140 (3.5 Schwenken: the WCS rotations about X, Y, Z are converted into positions of the machine kinematics, or the machine's swivel axes are programmed "direkt" and a matching workpiece coordinate system is generated; axis-wise swivelling refers to the workpiece coordinate system, direct swivelling gives the desired rotary-axis positions and computes a new coordinate system from them, with no frame named for those positions.); same manual, p. 484 (CYCLE800 "direkt": the desired rotary-axis positions are given and a new coordinate system is computed.); SINUMERIK 840D sl/828D Bedienhandbuch Drehen (2013), p. 482 (the same wording); SINUMERIK 840D sl Anhang Zyklenpakete SW4.7 SP2 HF1 (2015), p. 15 (CYCLE800 direct swivelling with values in the zero offsets of the rotary axes of the swivel data set: new positioning behaviour, switched on by SD55221 $SCS_FUNCTION_MASK_SWIVEL_SET bit 8, bit 8 = 0 for compatibility.); HEIDENHAIN TNC 640 Benutzerhandbuch Klartextprogrammierung (10/2019), p. 426-427 (PLANE AXIAL defines the plane and the setpoint coordinates of the rotary axes; axis angles must match the machine's rotary axes; incremental angles add to the effective one; no basic rotation is computed; no frame is named.); same manual, p. 429-430 (MOVE and TURN swivel the rotary axes onto the calculated axis values, MOVE with a compensating motion of the linear axes; STAY needs a separate positioning block.); SINUMERIK 840D Zyklen Programmierhandbuch 01/2008 p. 217-219 and 2006 p. 214 (cited by the earlier answer for "WKS-Positionen der Rundachsen" and "maschinenabhängig"; listed in the connector, but their text cannot be read there).
Corrected: Withdrew "this contradicts the recommendation" and softened it to not settled, because the Siemens WCS quote cannot be read in the connector and the 840D sl manuals of 2013 describe direct swivelling by the machine's rotary-axis positions without naming a work frame. Added the SD55221 bit 8 note on rotary-axis zero offsets.

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

Follow the recommendation. After TILT_AXIS with MOVE=TURN|MOVE, the named rotary axes are known in the MACHINE frame at the TILT_AXIS values, and the limit check applies (D100). Their workpiece-frame value stays unknown until a motion with known coordinates (D35), so `RAPID IC=10` right after is the VM 3.1 ERROR. VM 3.4 names the MACHINE frame. If a control applies a rotary datum offset to direct swivelling (Siemens SD55221 bit 8), the reader or compiler handles it, not the VM. Language 4.2 adds one line: CYCLE800 axis-wise is TILT and only direct swivelling is TILT_AXIS (D82).
Basis: manual + logical
Source: 840D sl/828D Bedienhandbuch Fräsen 2013 p. 138-140, 484 (direct swivelling gives the machine's rotary-axis positions); TNC 640 Klartext 2019 p. 426-430 (PLANE AXIAL sets the rotary axes' setpoints). The audit withdrew the contradiction (manual-audit-2026-10-26 sec. 4).
Differs from the recommendation: no
Confidence: high
Code impact: none (ApplyTilt already does this; remove the TODO, doc edit to VM 3.4 and language 4.2)

#### D128 Role TOOL names the tool spindle, not the holder
Question: D103 gives the role TOOL to two resources. The decisions.md row says "spindle MAIN, holder TOOL"; the rationale and the closing paragraph of VM 3.8 say "one tool holder TOOL with the tool spindle TOOL". VM 3.8 rule 1, however, resolves a role to one resource id and makes a wrong resource type an ERROR. Language 4.10 recommends TOOL for the "milling spindle on a mill-turn, the only spindle on a mill" and names no role for a mill's holder. D104 gives millturn1.toml TOOL = S3, a tool spindle, and TURRET1 = H1, the holder. The examples write SPINDLE:TOOL (POLAR_FACE lines 12, 37 and 44; MILLTURN_TRANSFER lines 30 and 36) and never TOOL:TOOL. Concrete case: TOOL:TOOL=3 without a machine file, or with the three mill files in machines/, is today the ERROR 'wrong resource type', while the D103 row reads as if it were accepted.
Recommendation: Keep what the code does. TOOL is the role of the tool spindle (S2 on the default machine, S1 on the mills), as D104 already has it for millturn1.toml. The holder has no role; it is default_holder, which TOOL and PRELOAD without an address reach (VM 3.8 rule 2). A machine with one holder needs no holder role, and TOOL:TOOL=n stays the wrong-type ERROR. Reason: this is the only reading under which the examples' SPINDLE:TOOL words check clean against the default machine, which is D103's own acceptance, and rule 1 stays unchanged. Alternative 1: a spindle word addressed to a holder role reaches that holder's spindle, so TOOL could name the holder and serve both words. That changes rule 1 and breaks with D104 (millturn1.toml: TOOL = "S3", TURRET1 = "H1"). Alternative 2: give the default machine's holder the recommended holder role TURRET1, as D104 does on millturn1.toml. Then TOOL:TURRET1 in MILLTURN_TRANSFER reaches that holder, and the 'not checked' WARNING for TURRET1 that P1-02 raises and P1-04 expects goes away. The spindle-OFF rule then checks the holder's spindle TOOL whatever the default spindle is.
Where: decisions.md D103 row and rationale.md D103 ("holder TOOL" becomes "one tool holder, the default holder, without a role, carrying the tool spindle TOOL"); VM 3.8 closing paragraph; language 4.10 (one sentence: a machine with one holder needs no holder role); src/Ncx.Config/DefaultMachine.cs TODO; the [roles] TODO comments in machines/fanuc-mill-30i.toml, machines/heidenhain-itnc530.toml and machines/siemens-840dsl-mill.toml.

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, not confirmed by the maintainer: the manuals do not settle this. No manual names NCX roles, but the machine manuals back what the code does. On the Mori Seiki NTX1000 the tool spindle is a spindle of its own that M13/M14 start and M319 orients, and the tool sits in that spindle — the T function calls a tool to the change position and G361 exchanges "the tool presently set in the tool-spindle" with the magazine, and a CAUTION forbids turning the tool spindle without a tool clamped in it — so the tool spindle and whatever stores tools are different resources, and on the milling side the store is a magazine, not a turret. On a mill there is only one spindle and it is the tool spindle: Hermle's M-function list for the C series calls M3/M4/M5 "Werkzeugspindel Rechtslauf / Linkslauf / ausschalten" and M16 "Werkzeugspindel ins Magazin fahren". That fits TOOL = the tool spindle with the single holder carrying no role, and gives no support for a holder that a spindle word could be addressed to.
Evidence: `Mori-Seiki_NT-NTX-Serie_Programmierung_Programmieranleitung-NTX1000SZM_PX-NT_4-K0DEEN_2011`, p. 313 (1-1 T-Funktion (Werkzeugspindel)) (Verified. The T function brings a tool to the change position and the magazine rotates; G361 then exchanges the tool currently in the tool spindle ("Austauschen des derzeit in der Werkzeugspindel eingesetzten Werkzeugs"). T0 with G361 empties the tool spindle back into the magazine); `Mori-Seiki_NT-NTX-Serie_Programmierung_Programmieranleitung-NTX1000SZM_PX-NT_4-K0DEEN_2011`, p. 258 (entry 1-8), 259 (entry 1-9), 286 (entry 1-28) — the original citation "p. 233 ff." pointed at the table of contents (Corrected. Entry 1-8: M13/M14 start the tool spindle or the driven tool spindle of turret 2 normal and reverse, M05 stops it, with a CAUTION not to rotate the tool spindle unless a tool is clamped in it. Entry 1-9: M319 orients the tool spindle. Entry 1-28: M314/M315 make the FEEDRATE OVERRIDE clamp valid or invalid on the tool-spindle side — and that text names the tool spindle "Revolver 1: KOPF1" against "Revolver 2: KOPF2", i.e. the tool spindle is its own head with its own feedrate); `Hermle_Allgemein_Programmierung_M-Funktionen-C400-C12-C60_DE_2015`, p. 1-3 (Verified with one correction: the wording sits in a single "Aktionsbeschreibung" column that covers every C-series column, not in the C 12 / C 22 column (the per-machine columns only mark standard or option). M3, M4 and M5 are "Werkzeugspindel" clockwise, counter-clockwise and off; M16 moves the tool spindle into the magazine; M19 orients it. The machine's only spindle is the tool spindle and the magazine is the store). (Citations re-paged to the cnc-manuals connector 2026-10-26.)

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

TOOL is the role of the tool spindle; the holder has no role and is default_holder, reached by unaddressed TOOL and PRELOAD. TOOL:TOOL=n stays the wrong-resource-type ERROR. Fix the D103 decisions.md row ("holder TOOL") to match.
Basis: manual
Source: Mori NTX1000 manual: tool spindle is its own spindle (M13/M14, M319) and the magazine is a separate resource (G361); Hermle C-series M list calls M3/M4/M5 "Werkzeugspindel". Matches D104 millturn1.toml (TOOL = S3, TURRET1 = H1).
Differs from the recommendation: no
Confidence: high
Code impact: none (docs: D103 row, VM 3.8 closing paragraph).

#### D129 Default spindle of the default machine
Question: D103 and VM 3.8 give the default machine two spindles (MAIN and TOOL) but no default_spindle, and rule 2 needs one. The P1-04 tests in implementation 11 assume MAIN: for MILLTURN_TRANSFER, "the holder TURRET1 created on the spot has no spindle, so the default spindle MAIN is checked", which puts 'spindle OFF before a LINE' (VM 5, F30) at LINE C=90 (line 34). The same paragraph expects no such WARNING in 2.5D_FRAESEN, INCREMENTAL_SUB and PATTERN_LOOP. Those three need their bare SPINDLE=CW and RPM to reach the tool spindle, because the rule checks the default holder's spindle, TOOL. The code takes TOOL (DefaultMachine sets DefaultSpindle = "S2"). The rule itself is not on main yet. Once P1-04 builds it the way F30 words it, MILLTURN_TRANSFER gets the WARNING at lines 13 and 14 (LINE X=40 and LINE Z=-60, while TOOL is still off) and not at line 34. With millturn1.toml it also falls at lines 13 and 14, because TURRET1 is H1 there and carries the tool spindle S3 (D104).
Recommendation: Keep what the code does: default_spindle is the tool spindle TOOL. Amend the P1-04 expectation for MILLTURN_TRANSFER: 'spindle OFF before a LINE' at lines 13 and 14 instead of at LINE C=90. Reason: the three mill examples then check as implementation 11 expects, and MILLTURN_TRANSFER gives the same WARNINGs without a machine file as with millturn1.toml. The cost: every lathe and mill-turn file in docs/spec/examples/machines names the main spindle as default_spindle, so a lathe program with bare spindle words drives TOOL when it is checked without a machine file. Among the examples only POLAR_FACE line 11 does that, with CSS=OFF, which changes nothing because CSS starts OFF. Alternative: MAIN, as implementation 11 reads. Then the three mill examples each get the WARNING, because their bare SPINDLE=CW starts MAIN while the holder's spindle TOOL stays off, which contradicts the same paragraph. Option, whichever way this is answered: the WARNINGs at lines 13 and 14 are false alarms (MAIN turns the part at 1500 rpm), and F30 was written to keep exactly that out of MILLTURN_TRANSFER. VM 5 could let the rule pass while the spindle of the workpiece holder runs as well. With default_spindle TOOL, MILLTURN_TRANSFER then has no such WARNING with or without millturn1.toml, and without a machine file it keeps only its five 'not checked' WARNINGs. With MAIN, line 34 keeps the WARNING, because SUB is in AXIS mode there. The mill examples and POLAR_FACE do not change.
Where: VM 3.8 closing paragraph and the D103 rationale (name the default spindle); implementation/11-phase-1-virtual-machine.md, P1-04 tests paragraph (the MILLTURN_TRANSFER expectation); src/Ncx.Config/DefaultMachine.cs TODO; for the option only, the VM 5 WARNING 'spindle OFF before a LINE' and the F30 row of implementation/01-findings.md.

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, corrected 2026-10-26 after the manual audit, not confirmed by the maintainer: the manuals do not settle this. They split by machine family, so they do not point at MAIN, and for the mill examples the recommendation stands. On lathe-based mill-turns the bare spindle words are the work spindle's. Siemens declares the main spindle master spindle by machine data, gives it thread cutting, tapping, revolution feed and dwell, and its lathe example moves the master to the counter spindle with SETMS(2) for the second side of the part. Nakamura does the same by M-code convention: bare M3/M4/M5 turn the main work spindle while the milling spindle needs M88/M89/M90, and S is modal and belongs to the spindle of the M code in the same block, so the wrong order hands a later S to the previous spindle. On mill-based mill-turns it is the reverse: Hermle's M-function list gives M3, M4 and M5 to the tool spindle on every model and the work spindle of its MT machines its own M303, M304 and M305, and on the TNC 640 the work spindle is switched on in turning mode by a builder-specific M function such as M303 or M304. Burkhardt+Weber's "Masterspindel 1" is a neutral case, a machine with one spindle. So the D103 default machine, which has both spindles, matches neither family by itself. The mill examples behave as on a mill-based machine, which supports TOOL, and a lathe program checked without a machine file is the cost the recommendation already names. The manuals say nothing about where the F30 WARNING should fall, which is the real question behind the draft. With this correction the proposal no longer goes against the recommendation.
Evidence: SINUMERIK 840D sl/828D Grundlagen, Programmierhandbuch 03/2013 (6FC5398-1BP40-3AA1), p. 81-84 (section 6.1: the main spindle is declared master spindle by machine data, changeable by NC command; bare S, M3, M4, M5 act on the master spindle; the master owns thread cutting, tapping, revolution feed and dwell; the two-side turning example makes S2 master with SETMS(2) and switches back.); Nakamura-Tome Programmierhandbuch Band 1 (4810004ECL-1, 2013), p. 58-60 (chapter 5: M03 main spindle, M88/M89/M90 milling spindle; S modal and in the same block as the spindle M code; milling spindle first (M88 S1000), work spindle after (M03 S100).); Liste M- und G-Codes Nakamura NTJX (Walter Meier / KOST, 26.04.2016), p. 1 and 2 of 6 (M3, M4, M5 main spindle; M53, M54, M55 sub spindle; M88, M89, M90 milling spindle.); Hermle M-Funktionen C 400 / C 12 / C 22 / C 32 / C 42 / C 52 / C 60 (2015), p. 1-3 (M3, M4, M5 "Werkzeugspindel", standard on every model; M16 tool spindle to magazine; M19 tool spindle orientation.); same list, p. 4-7 (M303, M304, M305, M319 "Werkstückspindel (nur MT-Maschinen)", standard on C 32 to C 60.); Hermle Technische Information Postprozessor-Heidenhain V2 (2016), p. 7 (M303/M304/M305 workpiece spindle clockwise, anticlockwise, stop.); HEIDENHAIN TNC 640 Benutzerhandbuch Zyklenprogrammierung (892905-18, NC-SW 34059x-10, 2019), p. 415 (in turning mode the work spindle is switched on as master spindle with a builder-specific M function, M303, M304, ...); BURKHARDT+WEBER MCX 800 HVP Betriebsanleitung Band 1 (2019), p. printed 6-10 to 6-14 (one spindle, "Masterspindel 1" in every home state; the document is listed in the connector but cannot be searched there).
Corrected: Dropped "wherever a machine has both a work spindle and a tool spindle, the bare spindle words are the work spindle's" and "that points at MAIN", because Hermle MT machines and the TNC 640 in turning mode give bare M3/M5 to the tool spindle and the work spindle its own M303 to M305. The proposal now agrees with the recommendation for the mill examples instead of going against it.

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

`default_spindle` of the D103 default machine is TOOL, as the code has it. Also take the draft's option: the VM 5 WARNING "spindle OFF before a LINE" fires only when neither the active holder's spindle nor the spindle of the current workpiece holder is running. Turning against a running work spindle with a stationary tool is a normal cut. With this, MILLTURN_TRANSFER gives no such WARNING with or without millturn1.toml. The three mill examples and POLAR_FACE do not change. Amend the P1-04 expectation and the F30 row to match.
Basis: manual + logical
Source: Hermle M-Funktionen 2015 p. 1-7 (M3/M5 = tool spindle; work spindle M303-M305); TNC 640 Zyklen 892905-18 p. 415; Siemens Grundlagen 03/2013 p. 81-84 (master spindle on lathes). Logical: the manuals split by machine family, and TOOL fits mill-based use without a machine file. A material-removal check has to accept either spindle as the cutting motion, or it raises false alarms on every turning op.
Differs from the recommendation: yes: adopts the recommendation's "option" (pass when the workpiece holder's spindle runs) as part of the decision.
Confidence: medium
Code impact: DefaultMachine TODO removed; the P1-04 VM 5 rule checks holder spindle OR workpiece-holder spindle.

#### D130 Coolant channel the machine file does not name
Question: Language 4.6 lets COOLANT address "a named channel from the machine configuration" (COOLANT:AIR), and VM 2.5 makes STANDARD the default channel (F29). No list names an unknown channel: not VM 3.8, not the VM 5 ERROR list ("unknown role, function or machine axis word"), and not D103's WARNING ("an unknown role, function or machine axis"). Case: COOLANT:MIST=ON with a machine file whose [coolant] has no MIST, and the same word without a machine file.
Recommendation: Keep what the code does and treat it like an unknown function. With a machine file it is an ERROR, because the compiler has no template to write (machine-config 5). Without one it is the D103 WARNING 'not checked: no machine file', once per name. STANDARD is always accepted. Add 'coolant channel' next to 'function' in the VM 5 ERROR list, in VM 3.8 and in the D103 WARNING wording. One gap in that reason: the code also accepts STANDARD when a machine file's [coolant] lacks it, and then the compiler has no template for it either. All eight machine files name STANDARD, so nothing shows today; the loader could require it.
Where: VM 3.8 (rule 1 or 2a); VM 5 ERROR and WARNING lists; language 4.6 (COOLANT row); decisions.md D103 row; src/Ncx.Core/VirtualMachine/ResourceResolver.cs ResolveCoolantChannel TODO.

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, not confirmed by the maintainer: the manuals do not settle this. The manuals support the compile-time ERROR, though not through the reason the draft answer gave. M7/M8/M9 themselves are generic across all three builders; what is machine-specific is every channel beyond them and whether each one is fitted at all. Hermle's table marks M8 external coolant as standard on every machine group while M7 external blast air, M12 internal blast air, M10/M11 mist extraction and M51/M52 internal coolant are options; the NTJX has a closed list (M7 low pressure with M708 medium, M8 high pressure, M9 off, M20/M21 main-spindle air, M48/M49 through the right spindle, M56/M57 tool-spindle air, M420/M421 sub-spindle air, M424-M426 tool-spindle flushing, M720/M721 tool-spindle internal and external cooling, M742/M743 through the right spindle); and Doosan blocks the cool-jet outright when holding relay K6.4 is 0. So for a channel the machine file does not name, the compiler has nothing to write. STANDARD is present on all of them, which supports accepting it always — but no page obliges a machine to have it, so requiring STANDARD in the loader is the safer reading of the gap the draft names.
Evidence: `Hermle_Allgemein_Programmierung_M-Funktionen-C400-C12-C60_DE_2015`, p. 2 and 4 (The M-function table has one column per machine group (C 400, C 12/C 22, C 32/C 42, C 52/C 60) with a filled marker for standard and a hollow one for option. M8 (äußere Kühlschmierstoffzufuhr) is standard in all four columns; M7 (äußere Blasluft), M12 (innere Blasluft), M10/M11 (Emulsionsnebelabsauganlage) and, on p. 4, M51/M52 (innere Kühlschmierstoffzufuhr) are options. M9 switches external coolant, external air and internal air off together.); `Nakamura-Tome_Super-NTJX_Programmierung_Liste-M-G-Codes_DE_2016`, p. 1-4 (Gives the machine's coolant and air channels as a fixed list of M codes: M7 coolant low pressure (M708 medium), M8 coolant high pressure, M9 off, M20/M21 main-spindle outside air, M48/M49 air blast through the right spindle, M56/M57 tool-spindle air, M420/M421 sub-spindle outside air, M424/M425/M426 tool-spindle flushing air and water, M706/M707 chip-flush cover, M720/M721 tool-spindle internal and external cooling, M742/M743 coolant through the right spindle.); `Doosan_PUMA-Baureihe_Bedienungshandbuch_DE_2020`, p. 138-139 (no readable text in the cnc-manuals connector), ch. 12.4 to 12.6 (Optional coolant / cool-jet is M07 on and M09 off, and holding relay K4.2 decides whether standard and optional supply can run together. The cool-jet needs holding relay K6.4 set to 1; with it at 0 the cool-jet motor must not be used at all, and a Vorsicht adds that the cool-jet normally works only while the standard coolant supply runs. Through-spindle coolant (TSC) is M108/M109 for the Zusatzspindel and M128/M129 for the main spindle.). (Citations re-paged to the cnc-manuals connector 2026-10-26.)

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

With a machine file, an unnamed coolant channel is an ERROR; without one it is the D103 WARNING "not checked: no machine file", once per name. Add "coolant channel" to the VM 5 ERROR list, VM 3.8 and the D103 WARNING wording. STANDARD is always accepted by the VM, and the machine-file loader requires `[coolant] STANDARD` (ERROR when missing) so the compiler always has a template for it.
Basis: manual
Source: Channels beyond M8 are options or machine-specific (Hermle M-function table; Nakamura NTJX M-code list; Doosan K6.4 interlock); no page obliges a machine to have STANDARD, hence the loader check.
Differs from the recommendation: yes: the loader requires STANDARD (closing the gap the recommendation names).
Confidence: medium
Code impact: Ncx.Core coolant resolution diagnostics; Ncx.Config machine loader (STANDARD required).

#### D132 Preload after TOOL=k with another tool preloaded
Question: Two readings exist. VM 3.5 (row TOOL=n) clears the preload only 'if preloaded == n'. The code-guidelines 2 sample (line 51) keeps a preload of another tool, and so does the comment rule in the same section (line 19: 'Consume the preload only when it names the tool that arrives'). Architecture 5.2 drops it: the diagram goes from Pending to Loaded on TOOL=k, and the text says 'TOOL=k with another tool changes too'. VM 2.3 ('consumed by TOOL'), VM 4 ('preload consumed by TOOL') and language 4.4 ('modal until consumed') read most naturally the same way, but they do not name TOOL=k. Case: PRELOAD=5, TOOL=4, then a bare TOOL. If the preload is kept, the bare TOOL changes to 5 and the Fanuc compiler writes M6 alone (VM 3.5: 'M6 alone when preloaded'). If it is dropped, the bare TOOL is the ERROR 'nothing preloaded'. The tool list of VM 8 also reports differently whether tool 5 was preloaded before its change.
Recommendation: TOOL=k consumes any preload, and the WARNING stays (D42). Fanuc 5 says T4 M6 'changes to 4 directly (the control preloads and changes)', so after it the control's preselection is 4. A later M6 alone does not bring tool 5. A reader whose source-side VM kept 5 would read that M6 as TOOL=5 (VM 3.5: 'M6 alone gives TOOL=n from the source-side VM'). The reason given for the WARNING, the magazine cycling twice, is the control putting tool 5 back. A block may carry both words, as the Nakamura G340 T0101. A02. does (TOOL=1 OFFSET=1 PRELOAD=2, language 4.4). There the change comes first and the preload after it. The code already applies TOOL before PRELOAD (VirtualMachine.ApplyStateWords), and VM 3 step 3, which says the state words of a block do not depend on each other, gets that exception written in. The VM 3.5 row TOOL=n becomes 'spindleTool = n; preloaded = none'. The code-guidelines 2 sample and its line 19 comment rule change with it, and so does ToolChangeRules.ApplyTool (its comment and line 54). Alternative: keep the preload, leaving VM 3.5 and the code as they are. The Fanuc compiler must then write T5 M6, not M6 alone, for the later bare TOOL, and readers must not use the VM for Fanuc M6.
Where: VM 3.5 (row TOOL=n), VM 3 step 3 (order within a block), code-guidelines 2 (line 19 comment rule, sample line 51); VM 2.3, VM 4, language 4.4, architecture 5.2; src/Ncx.Core/VirtualMachine/ToolChangeRules.cs ApplyTool (comment at 37-39, TODO at 50-52, line 54); src/Ncx.Core/VirtualMachine/VirtualMachine.cs ApplyStateWords (TOOL before PRELOAD).

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, not confirmed by the maintainer: the manuals do not settle this. The recommendation is well supported but no page states it: take it as the reading the machines force, not as a quoted rule. On the Fanuc machines of the corpus a preload is a physical magazine position, not a register — on the Mori Seiki NTX1000 the T word makes the magazine rotate the named tool into the tool change position, and G361 exchanges the tool in the tool spindle with the one standing there, so naming another tool for the change moves that other tool into the same single position and the earlier preselection is physically gone. Nakamura shows the block form of language 4.4 from the other side: G341 T18 is the preselect alone (the next tool is brought to the ATC waiting position while the program runs) and G340 T_ A_ is the change with the next tool in A, so change first and preload after. On that basis TOOL=k consuming any preload (VM 3.5 row TOOL=n becoming `spindleTool = n; preloaded = none`) and the D42 WARNING staying are the right call.
Evidence: `Mori-Seiki_NT-NTX-Serie_Programmierung_Programmieranleitung-NTX1000SZM_PX-NT_4-K0DEEN_2011`, p. 313 (§1-1 T-Funktion, Werkzeugspindel) (The T function calls the tool named by a four-digit number to the tool change position: in response to the T word the magazine rotates to bring that tool there. The example shows T9001 followed by G361 B0 D1., described as exchanging the tool currently in the tool spindle for T9001; T0 then G361 empties the spindle); `Nakamura-Tome_Fanuc_Programmierung_Programmierhandbuch_DE_2019`, p. 160-162 (G340 is the tool change cycle: T is the tool with its offset number (mandatory), A the tool number of the next tool, and M, S, B what runs after the change. G341 T_ is the separate preselect cycle that brings the next tool into the ATC waiting position while the program continues, and the page notes it is rarely used because G340 can name the follow-up tool itself); `Fanuc_30i-B_Bedienung-Drehen-Fraesen_B-64484EN_EN`, p. 286 (table 10.5.3) (Tool-life management knows four tool change types A to D, chosen by M6T (parameter 6800#7) and M6E (6801#7); which one a machine uses is the builder's business. Under type A the tool group number in the same block as M06 is the group already used, under B, C and D the group to be used next. The remarks column gives alarm PS0155 "UNZUL. T-CODE IN M06" when the T after M06 is not the group currently in use (with bit 6 (IGI) of 6800 = 0), and alarm PS0153 "T-CODE N GEFUND" when M06 stands alone); `Burkhardt-Weber_MCX800-HVP_Betriebsanleitung-Band1_DE_2019`, p. 395 (no readable text in the cnc-manuals connector) (§6.12.4) (The normal pattern is T for the tool, L796 for the change, then a new T, which the next L796 consumes. Preparing a second tool ahead needs its own address, T2=xxx, which puts the tool after next into the magazine gripper; the plain T selection and the advance one are separate stages); `Stama_Sinumerik-840D_Programmierung_Programmieranleitung-MC-Baureihe_MC3xx-5xx-S840D-PRG-DEU_DE_2004`, p. 25-27 (§2.3) (Calling the address T preselects the tool, and the magazine thereby switches that tool to the tool change position; the change itself is a separate program (L6). The rules that follow require the tool to have been preselected with T before L6 is called). (Citations re-paged to the cnc-manuals connector 2026-10-26.)

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

TOOL=k consumes any preload (VM 3.5 row: `spindleTool = n; preloaded = none`), and the D42 WARNING stays. In a block with both words, TOOL applies before PRELOAD (exception written into VM 3 step 3). Update code-guidelines 2 sample and its comment rule, and ToolChangeRules.ApplyTool.
Basis: manual
Source: On the Fanuc machines the preload is a physical magazine position (Mori NTX1000: T rotates the tool to the change position, G361 exchanges); Nakamura G340 T_ A_ changes first and preselects after.
Differs from the recommendation: no
Confidence: high
Code impact: Ncx.Core ToolChangeRules.ApplyTool; code-guidelines 2 sample.

#### D134 Start state of a later program of the file in STATIC mode
Question: In STATIC mode, VM 1 walks 'every program of the file' but does not say which state the second and later programs start from. Most sentences point to a fresh channel state. VM 3.7 says 'A job runs one VM per channel program'. VM 3.9 says the other programs of the file 'are not executed unless the job runs them on their channels'. Language 4.13 says 'programs are entered from the job only'. D15 and machine-config 8 have a job entry run one program of a file, and architecture 13 on D48 says 'the VM runs one program per channel'. D100 says 'At program start an axis with home is known in the MACHINE frame'. Two others read as if a later program continued. D11 says 'UNITS is required before the first motion of an NCX file' and was written before D48 allowed several programs per file. The 'Reset by' column of VM 4 says what PROGRAM=END keeps. Case: a file with two programs on channel 1, where only the first sets UNITS=MM. With a fresh state, the first motion of the second program is the ERROR 'motion before UNITS'. If the state continues, it checks clean and starts with the first program's tool, origin and position.
Recommendation: Every program starts from the initial state of its channel, the Initial column of VM 2 with positions per D100, as the job enters it. This is what the code does. D11 then applies to every program, and the complete header of D34 already puts UNITS into the output of every writer and into every example program. The D11 row may say 'of every program'. Alternative: a program continues on its channel from the state that the previous program of the file left at its PROGRAM=END.
Where: VM 1 (STATIC), 3.7 and 3.9; D11 in decisions.md and language 4.1 (row UNITS); src/Ncx.Core/VirtualMachine/VirtualMachine.Static.cs Run (TODO at 51-53).

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, corrected 2026-10-26 after the manual audit, not confirmed by the maintainer: the manuals do not settle this. No manual has NCX's case (several programs in one file walked in turn), but both control families make the start state a machine setting rather than a language rule, and neither resets everything. Fanuc's appendix F shows that after a reset the modal G codes return to their initial value and F to 0 only in the clear state, which parameter 3402 bit 6 selects, while S, T and M are kept in both the clear state and the reset state; only power-on clears them, and the initial value of the modal G code is itself set by parameters. Siemens fixes the basic state at part-program start with MD20112 START_MODE_MASK, where a bit at 0 keeps the current setting of its function and a bit at 1 puts it into its reset position. Not every bit is delivered at 0: the default of MD20112 is 400H, so bit 10 resets its function at program start on a delivered control; the function manual comments the value 'H400' as switching off a synchronous spindle coupling, and the tool is not among what it resets. So the manuals back the fresh-state recommendation for units, plane, origin and feed as a configurable option, but they contradict it for the tool: on a real control the T the previous program left is still active, whereas VM 2.3 starts spindleTool at 0. Caveats: This proposal contradicts the recommendation. The analogy is the operator selecting and starting a second program, which is not literally NCX's STATIC walk of a file, although language 4.13 itself names 'Fanuc files with several O programs' as the real-world shape, so the Fanuc side of the analogy is the closer one. Both controls parameterise the behaviour (Fanuc 3402 bit 6 and 3406-3409; Siemens MD20110/20112/20150/20152), so the manuals cannot settle the question, only show what machines actually do. That bit 10 is the synchronous spindle is read from the example's comment, not from a bit table. One page of the Siemens manual states the two machine data the wrong way round; see the corrections.
Evidence: FANUC Series 30i/31i/32i-MODEL B Operator's Manual B-64484EN, Appendix F, p. 2409-2411 (Settings at power-on, in the clear state or in the reset state: modal G codes take their initial value at power-on and in the clear state and are kept in the reset state; F becomes 0 at power-on and in the clear state; S, T and M are cleared only at power-on and kept otherwise; bit 6 (CLR) of parameter 3402 selects clear or reset state; a note gives the initial modal G codes by 3402 bits 0, 1, 2, 3, 7 and parameters 3406 to 3409.); SINUMERIK 840D sl/828D Funktionshandbuch Grundfunktionen (2012), p. 575 (MD20112 $MC_START_MODE_MASK fixes the basic state at part-program start for G codes (current plane, settable zero offset), tool length compensation, transformation and axis couplings; the example sets $MC_START_MODE_MASK = 'H400' with the comment that a synchronous spindle coupling not configured is switched off.); same manual, p. 658 and 661 (section 8.14 event table: Hochlauf, RESET/part-program end, part-program start with their machine data; p. 661 gives MD20110 RESET_MODE_MASK after power-up and reset and MD20112 START_MODE_MASK after part-program start, MD20150/MD20152 and MD20120.); same manual, p. 659-661, figure 8-15 (the bit meanings of MD20112, bit = 0 keep, bit = 1 reset position, with the functions G codes, tool length compensation, transformation, coupled motion, synchronous spindle, basic frame, master spindle, master tool holder, reference axis; the figure has no text in the connector, so this reading from the earlier proposal cannot be checked there.); SINUMERIK 840D Programming Manual Measuring Cycles HMIsl (EN, 2009), p. 452 (machine data table: 20112 START_MODE_MASK, maximum 07FFFH, default value 400H.); Index SINUMERIK 840D Zyklen (LY4401.10092, 2004), p. 232-233 (machine data list: 20112 $MC_START_MODE_MASK 'H400').
Corrected: Replaced "the default setting of every one of its bits is to keep the current settings": MD20112 defaults to 400H (Measuring Cycles HMIsl 2009 p. 452), so one function, by the example on Grundfunktionen p. 575 the synchronous spindle coupling, resets at program start. The conclusion about the tool is unchanged; the Fanuc pages now cite the English B-64484EN.

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

Every program starts from the initial state of its channel (VM 2 Initial column, positions per D100), as the job enters it. This includes the tool: spindleTool starts at its VM 2.3 initial value. Nothing is carried over from the previous program's PROGRAM=END. D11 reads "before the first motion of every program".
Basis: logical
Source: Fanuc B-64484EN App. F p. 2409-2411 and Siemens Grundfunktionen 2012 p. 575, 659-661 show that the start state is a machine setting (3402#6, MD20112) and that T survives on a real control. Logical: a job may start any program of the file on its own (language 4.13, D15). The checker can't know which program ran before, so relying on the previous program's tool is the same unchecked assumption as relying on its UNITS. A fresh state makes a missing tool call show up as a diagnostic instead of a silent inheritance.
Differs from the recommendation: no
Confidence: medium
Code impact: none (VirtualMachine.Static.cs already does this; remove the TODO, doc edit to D11 row and VM 1)

#### D135 D99 entry state when the first program has no verb
Question: D99 and VM 1 give a subprogram that nothing calls 'units, workplane, diameter and feed mode as at the first verb of the file's first program'. A first program without a verb has no such point. One example is a library file whose first program is only a header and PROGRAM=END. Another is a program that sets the header and only CALLs, because the code records only verbs in the program's own blocks. Case: a lathe file whose first program sets FEED_MODE=PER_REV UNITS=MM WORKPLANE=ZX DIAMETER=ON and only calls. A subprogram that nothing calls is then checked in XY, with X as a radius and the units unknown.
Recommendation: When the first program has no verb, take the four values as they stand at its first CALL, before the subprogram is entered. When it has no CALL either, take them as they stand when its walk reaches PROGRAM=END, before that block resets the feed mode (VM 4). In both cases these are the settings of its header, which D34 has every writer emit and which D99 is after. A program that only calls has them in place at its first CALL. PROGRAM=END could instead hand the uncalled subprogram a WORKPLANE or DIAMETER that the program changed between two calls. D99 keeps the first verb wherever the program has one. The code change is small: WalkSection records the state at the first CALL and at PROGRAM=END as fallbacks, and a verb in the program's own blocks still wins. Alternative: the initial values, as the code does now, or PROGRAM=END for every first program without a verb.
Where: VM 1 and 3.9 (default entry state), D99 in decisions.md; src/Ncx.Core/VirtualMachine/VirtualMachine.Static.cs EntryStateOfUncalledSub (TODO at 102-104) and WalkSection (_firstVerbState).

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, not confirmed by the maintainer: the manuals do not settle this. No manual knows a static check of an uncalled subprogram, and the one near-analogue in the library does not carry as far as the draft needs. Heidenhain states only this: subprograms are to be programmed after the block with M2 or M30, and if they stand before it in the NC program they are worked through at least once without a call. That is a warning against misplacing a subprogram, not a definition of an entry state — a correctly placed Heidenhain subprogram stands after M2/M30 and is never executed uncalled at all. The 'with the state the program has reached there' step is linear-execution reasoning, not on the page, and it cannot be transferred to NCX in any case, because language 4.13 lets programs and SUB sections stand in the file in any order, so there is no fixed physical point to read a state off. Nothing in the library speaks for the initial values the code uses today either, nor for the first-CALL and PROGRAM=END fallbacks the recommendation proposes. Caveats: Fanuc and Siemens keep uncalled subprograms in separate programs or files, where they are simply never run, so they say nothing. I found no manual passage on the specific case of a first program that has no verb. The earlier reading of this draft took the Heidenhain rule to favour the PROGRAM=END fallback over the first-CALL branch; that conclusion does not survive, because it depends on SUB sections following the program, which NCX does not require.
Evidence: `Heidenhain_TNC640_Programmierung-Klartext_892903-18_NC-SW-34059x-10_DE_2019`, p. 247 (Programmierhinweise for subprograms: 'Unterprogramme hinter dem NC-Satz mit M2 bzw. M30 programmieren' and 'Wenn Unterprogramme im NC-Programm vor dem NC-Satz mit M2 oder M30 stehen, dann werden sie ohne Aufruf mindestens einmal abgearbeitet.' The page describes execution and warns against the misplacement; it says nothing about the state such a run starts from.); `Heidenhain_TNC640_Programmierung-Klartext_892903-18_NC-SW-34059x-10_DE_2019`, p. 246 (Section 8.1: subprograms and program-part repetitions are marked only by the LBL label inside the same NC program, with numbers 1 to 65535 or a name, each used once. The page gives no header or declaration for a subprogram — but it does not state, as the earlier reading claimed, that a subprogram therefore has no entry state of its own.). (Citations re-paged to the cnc-manuals connector 2026-10-26.)

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

If the first program has no verb, take units, workplane, diameter and feed mode as they stand at its first CALL (before entering the callee); if it has no CALL either, as they stand when the walk reaches PROGRAM=END, before that block resets the feed mode. A verb in the program's own blocks still wins.
Basis: logical
Source: Manuals have no static check of an uncalled subprogram. These points carry the header settings D34 makes every writer emit, which is what D99 is after; first CALL avoids picking up later mid-program changes.
Differs from the recommendation: no
Confidence: medium
Code impact: Ncx.Core VM WalkSection (record state at first CALL and PROGRAM=END as fallbacks).

#### D136 CALL with TIMES from an expression in STATIC mode
Question: VM 1, VM 3.9 and D99 walk a CALL with TIMES=n n times in sequence, and STATIC mode does not evaluate expressions (VM 1). Nothing says what CALL=100 TIMES={$Q5} does, where n may be 0, 1 or many. Case: INCREMENTAL_SUB with TIMES={$Q5}. The code walks the subprogram once and continues at Y=15, while the machine stands at Y = 15 times n (60 for the example's TIMES=4).
Recommendation: Walk the subprogram once, so that check validates its blocks with the caller's state. Then continue with the state of that pass, except that every axis whose position the pass changed becomes unknown, because its position after n passes depends on n, 0 included. An axis the subprogram leaves where it found it stays known, so a later incremental word on it in the caller does not raise a false 'IX from an unknown position' ERROR. In INCREMENTAL_SUB, X (net 0) and Z (back at 2) stay known and Y becomes unknown. The TIMES expression counts toward the VM 5 WARNING 'unresolved expression in STATIC mode'. This follows the rule of VM 1 that whatever depends on an unevaluated expression is UNKNOWN, and no example is affected. Alternatives: walk once and keep the position that pass leaves, as the code does, which is right only for n = 1. Or make every axis unknown, as after a CALL of an external program (VM 1); this also blocks incremental words on axes the subprogram never touches.
Where: VM 1 and 3.9 (TIMES sentences), VM 5 (unresolved expression WARNING), D99 in decisions.md; src/Ncx.Core/VirtualMachine/VirtualMachine.Static.cs PassesOf (TODO at 368-370) and FollowCall (the axes the pass moved made unknown after it).

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, not confirmed by the maintainer: the manuals do not settle this. The manuals do not rule on a static walk, but they confirm the premise the recommendation rests on and narrow it. On Fanuc a variable may stand at almost any address (a variable may be used as the value of an address; only /, :, O and N may not take one, and neither may the n of a block-skip /n), so M98 P1000 L#100 is legal, and an undefined (null) variable makes the address itself be ignored, which is one pass. One call command can repeat a subprogram up to 99999999 times, and with the count omitted it runs once. Siemens is the opposite: the repetition address P is an INT from 1 to 9999 without sign, so no Siemens program can ask for zero passes, and Siemens warns that call parameters are handed over only on the first pass. A repetition count of zero is documented on Fanuc, but for a canned cycle, not for M98: the rigid-tapping restriction page explains K0 and L0 as setting the repetition count to 0 and preventing the G84 block from being executed. So n = 1 or many is documented for M98 and n = 0 is documented for the canned-cycle repetition address; 'walk once and keep the position of that pass' is right for one case only. Caveats: Whether the axes a pass moved should become unknown is an NCX checking decision that no manual addresses. Two inferential steps remain: the Fanuc rule on variables at addresses is general, not specific to L on M98, so the conclusion for M98 L#n is drawn from that general rule; and no page in the library says what M98 ... L0 does — the L0 = no execution statement is about the G84 canned cycle. I did not find a statement that Siemens P or Heidenhain REP may be a parameter.
Evidence: `Fanuc_30i-B_Bedienung-Drehen-Fraesen_B-64484EN_EN`, 16. Kundenmakro, p. 449-450 ('Variablenaufruf': the value after an address may be replaced by a variable (F#33 is F1.5 when #33 = 1.5); 'Eine Variable kann nicht mit Adresse /, :, oder O und N abgerufen werden', and the n of a block-skip /n may not be a variable either. 'Nicht definierte Variable': 'Wenn eine nicht definierte Variable aufgerufen wird, wird die Adresse selbst auch ignoriert' — G90 X100 Y#1 becomes G90 X100 for null and G90 X100 Y0 for 0.); `Fanuc_30i-B_Bedienung-Drehen-Fraesen_B-64484EN_EN`, 13.3 Unterprogramm, p. 329-330 (M98 Pxxxx Lxxxxxxxx, or the count folded into P (P100100 calls subprogram 100 ten times); note 2: if the count is not given the subprogram is called once; note 3: with a 4-digit number folded into P, L may not be in the same block; 'Ein einziger Aufrufbefehl kann ein Unterprogramm bis zu 99999999-mal aufrufen.'); `Fanuc_30i-B_Bedienung-Drehen-Fraesen_B-64484EN_EN`, 3. Handbetrieb, p. 1103 (A restriction on manual (handwheel) rigid tapping under the heading 'Anzahl Wiederholungen': in MDI programming K0 and L0 may not be used — and the parenthesis is where their meaning is given, 'mit denen die Anzahl der Wiederholungen auf 0 festgesetzt und die Ausführung eines G84-Satzes verhindert wird'. A repetition count of zero is therefore a documented value, but of the G84 canned cycle, not of M98.); `Siemens_Sinumerik-840D-sl_Programmierung_BS.000504-DE-000-00_DE`, p. 195-196 (Section 2.24.3.3 'Anzahl der Programmwiederholungen (P)': syntax <Programmname> P<Wert>, Typ INT, Wertebereich 1 … 9999 (ohne Vorzeichen). A VORSICHT adds that with parameter passing 'Parameter werden nur beim Programmaufruf bzw. ersten Durchlauf übergeben. Für die weiteren Wiederholungen bleiben die Parameter unverändert.'); `Heidenhain_TNC640_Programmierung-Klartext_892903-18_NC-SW-34059x-10_DE_2019`, p. 249 (Section 8.3: a program part may be repeated with CALL LBL n REPn up to 65 534 times, and 'Programmteile führt die Steuerung immer einmal häufiger aus, als Wiederholungen programmiert sind, da die erste Wiederholung nach der ersten Bearbeitung beginnt.'). (Citations re-paged to the cnc-manuals connector 2026-10-26.)

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

Walk the subprogram once with the caller's state; afterwards every axis whose position that pass changed becomes unknown, axes it left where it found them stay known. The TIMES expression counts toward the VM 5 WARNING "unresolved expression in STATIC mode".
Basis: manual
Source: Fanuc B-64484EN allows a variable at any address (so M98 P_ L#100 is legal) and L/K0 means no execution (canned cycle page); Siemens P is 1..9999. So n may be 0, 1 or many, and only "unknown after the pass" is safe.
Differs from the recommendation: no
Confidence: high
Code impact: Ncx.Core VM CALL walk (mark changed axes unknown when TIMES is unresolved).

#### D137 X values of home, limits and [positions] on a diameter axis
Question: Machine-config 4 and D100 put `home`, `home2`, `limits` and `[positions]` in machine coordinates (the G53 / M91 frame). D28 says the VM stores radii, and D60 lets `programming` decide how the program's X words are read and written. No document says whether a machine-frame X value on an axis with `programming = "diameter"` or `"switchable"` is a diameter or a radius. The four builder files write their X values as diameters, as their TODO(question) comments say. dmg-ctx-840d.toml, for example, has X `home = 450` and `tool_change` X = 450. millturn1.toml came with the documents: it has X `home = 300` and `limits = [-20, 300]` and does not say which. MotionState.cs:32 takes `home` unchanged, and so does HOME through ResourceResolver.ReferencePoint, so the VM holds a radius of 300 on millturn1. P1-04 compares targets with `limits` in the MACHINE frame. `{position:tool_change}` becomes an X word that D60 halves under `DIAMETER=ON`.
Recommendation: The file writes these values the way the axis is programmed: diameters for `programming = "diameter"` and `"switchable"`, radii for `"radius"` or when `programming` is absent. `home`, `home2` and `limits` of such an axis are halved once, where the VM takes them, into the radii it stores (D28). HOME, the start position and the limit check then all work in radii. `[positions]` stays as the file writes it: `{position:NAME}` copies the value into an X word, which the VM halves under `DIAMETER=ON` (D60). The expander never sees the state (architecture 5.5). On a switchable machine milling often runs under `DIAMETER=OFF`, so there a rule with `{position:NAME}` carries `requires = { DIAMETER = "ON" }` and `restore = ["DIAMETER"]` (machine-config 5a). The compiler writes DIAMON only when the state changes, and a Fanuc lathe without a `[diameter]` table writes nothing for it. Reason: the D100 answer asks for values 'based on the machine frame / G53', which a diameter-programmed Fanuc lathe gives as diameters. The four builder files are already written that way. millturn1.toml keeps its numbers, and they become diameters. Alternative: radii everywhere, the VM's unit. Then the far X limits and the X home of the four builder files halve (dmg-ctx-840d X home 225). `{position:NAME}` would also need `DIAMETER=OFF` around every rule, which a Fanuc lathe with fixed diameter programming cannot write. docs/ does not say whether a Sinumerik shows the machine-frame X as a diameter under DIAMON; the rule does not depend on it.
Where: machine-config 4 (a sentence after the home/limits paragraph) and 5a ({position:NAME}, requires). Code: src/Ncx.Config/MachineConfigLoader.Resources.cs (ReadAxes, ReadPositions); src/Ncx.Core/VirtualMachine/State/MotionState.cs:32; src/Ncx.Core/VirtualMachine/ResourceResolver.cs:227 (ReferencePoint, used by HomeRules.cs); the P1-04 limit check; the P1-06 expander. TODO(question) markers: docs/spec/examples/machines/doosan-puma-2600sy.toml:55, mori-ntx1000-mapps.toml:63, nakamura-ntjx.toml:63, dmg-ctx-840d.toml:67 (millturn1.toml has none).

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, corrected 2026-10-26 after the manual audit, not confirmed by the maintainer: Diameters, as the recommendation says, as NCX's convention for the file. The manuals prove it for Fanuc; for Siemens they show that positions written as program words are diameters but that limits and machine-frame data are radii, so values copied from Siemens machine data must be doubled when written into the file. Fanuc is consistently diameter for machine-frame limit data: parameters 1320/1321 (and 1322 to 1325) are stroke-check coordinates in the machine coordinate system, given as diameter values on a diameter axis, and the position-switch ranges 6930ff and 6950ff carry the same note. A G53 block's coordinates follow the diameter/radius switching unless parameter 11222 bit 7 (PDM) pins them, the axis position display is a diameter, and the Mori NTX displays machine coordinates as diameters by default even in radius mode (parameter 3194 #3). Siemens goes the other way for machine data: on a facing axis the software limit switches, the working-area limitation, frames and offsets and all display data in the machine coordinate system are always radius values, whatever DIAMON says; only MD20360 bits 6 and 7 turn actual values and their display into diameters. Programmed end positions under DIAMON are diameters, though, and DMG's own tool-change cycle L710 writes DIAMON before G0 G153 X=R690 Z=R691, doubles a radial term into X only, and restores the mode through PROC ... SAVE, which is the requires/restore pair the recommendation asks for around {position:NAME}. So [positions] used as X words fit the recommendation on both controls, while limits and a home read in the Siemens machine frame are radii. "All four builder files can keep their numbers" therefore has to be checked for every Siemens-based builder file whose limits or home come from machine data rather than from a G153 program. The proposal still agrees with the recommendation, with that check added.
Evidence: FANUC Series 30i/31i/32i-MODEL B Parameter Manual B-64490EN-05, p. 74 (1320/1321 stored stroke check 1 coordinates in the machine coordinate system, 1322 to 1325 likewise; note: specify diameter values for axes with diameter programming.); same manual, p. 397-398 (6930 to 6945 and 6950ff, operating ranges of the position switches; note: for a diameter-specified axis use diameter values.); FANUC Operator's Manual B-64484EN, p. 2195 (the same position-switch note) and p. 2069-2071 (1320ff); FANUC B-64484EN, p. 230-231, Table 8.4 (a) (X command, incremental command and G50 are diameters, the position display a diameter; arc R, I, K, canned-cycle depth and feed radii.); FANUC B-64484EN, p. 232 (with diameter/radius switching, G53 coordinates switch when bit 7 (PDM) of parameter 11222 is 0 and follow the parameter setting when it is 1.); MORI SEIKI NT/NTX-Serie Programmieranleitung NTX1000 SZM (PX-NT_4-K0DEEN, 2011), p. 116-117 (G10.9 X0/X1; parameter 1006 #3; parameter 3194 #3 displays machine coordinates as diameter in radius mode by default.); SINUMERIK 840D sl/828D Funktionshandbuch Grundfunktionen (2012), p. 900 (under DIAMON the programmed end positions, the WCS display and WCS actual values are diameters.); same manual, p. 901-902 ("Fest Radius-bezogene Daten": for facing axes always radius are offsets and frames, the working-area limitation, the software limit switches, the feed and the display data in the machine coordinate system.); same manual, p. 902-903 (MD20360 bit 6 actual values of the facing axis as diameter, bit 7 their display.); SINUMERIK 840D sl NC-Programmierung, Programmierhandbuch 06/2019, p. 168-169 (DIAMON) and 511 (SAVE restores the modal G commands at the end of the subprogram.); SINUMERIK 840D sl/828D Grundlagen, Programmierhandbuch 03/2013, p. 150 (G153 acts like G53 and also suppresses the total base frame.); DMG GMX 400 linear, builder cycle L710.SPF, lines 14, 20, 31 and 101 of the cycle source (PROC L710(REAL VARI) SAVE; DIAMON; G0 G153 X=R690 Z=R691; X with 2*GM_PARAM[1,2]*cos, Y with GM_PARAM[1,2]*sin; a cycle from the project's documents, not in the connector); DOOSAN PUMA 2600 LSY II Benutzerhandbuch Spezifikation und Wartung (2020), p. 242 (X travel 301,500 against a span of -137,000 to 466,000, twice the range; Z without doubling; present in the connector, not re-read in the audit).
Corrected: Deleted the Fanuc "counter-case": position switches 6930ff and 6950ff are diameter values too (Parameter Manual B-64490EN-05 p. 397-398). Reversed the Siemens inference for limits and home, which Grundfunktionen p. 901-902 makes radius values on a facing axis, while program words under DIAMON stay diameters.

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

The machine file writes X values the way the axis is programmed: diameters for `programming = "diameter"` or `"switchable"`, radii for `"radius"` or absent. The VM halves `home`, `home2` and `limits` once on load; `[positions]` stays as written and `{position:NAME}` becomes an X word that the VM halves under DIAMETER=ON, so such rules carry `requires = { DIAMETER = "ON" }` and `restore = ["DIAMETER"]` on switchable machines. Document that values copied from Siemens machine data (limit switches, machine-frame display) are radii and must be doubled; recheck the Siemens-based builder files.
Basis: manual
Source: Fanuc Parameter Manual B-64490EN-05 p. 397-398 and 1320ff (diameter values); Siemens Funktionshandbuch Grundfunktionen p. 901-902 (machine data radius on a facing axis); DMG L710 writes DIAMON before G153 X and restores it.
Differs from the recommendation: no (adds the Siemens doubling note and builder-file check)
Confidence: medium
Code impact: Ncx.Core MotionState / ResourceResolver.ReferencePoint (halve home/limits); P1-04 limit check; builder TOML review.

#### D138 Required keys of the machine file and the job manifest
Question: P2-01 (implementation 12) makes a missing required key an ERROR on the line of its table, but machine-config 1 to 9 name no required key. They only mark some keys as optional or to be left out: `tool_table` (D10), `home2`, `change_preloaded`, `preload` ('omit on machines without a magazine'), `channel` of a resource, `PHASE` of `[spindle_sync]` ('omit when the machine has none'), `start_mark`, `program_end` in `[positions]`, the kinematics of section 9, and `program` of a channel (D48). Which keys must a machine file and a job manifest contain? The case: a `[[axis]]` without `kind`, or a `[machine]` without `controller`.
Recommendation: Keep what the loader does now. Required are `[machine]` with `name` and `controller`; `id` and `type` of every `[[resource]]`; `id`, `ncx` and `kind` of every `[[axis]]`; and `id` of every `[[node]]`. In a job manifest, `[job] machine` and `id` and `file` of every `[[channel]]` are required. Every other key is optional, and leaving it out has the effect written where the key is described: no `home` gives the D100 WARNING, a missing template gives the compiler's ERROR. The conditional defaults of VM 3.8 rule 2 stay. Reason: these are the keys without which a record cannot exist or be referenced. `controller` is the one exception: the record allows none, for the default machine of D103, but the loader takes the cycle catalog family and the reading of the decimal comma from it. Anything a compiler needs is checked by that compiler, since the schema is a sketch until the compilers exist (machine-config status line). Alternative: also require at load time what compiling needs (`[format]`, `[tool_change] change`, `letter`); that would stop `check` on files that only a compiler should reject.
Where: machine-config 1 (one paragraph) and 8; src/Ncx.Config/MachineConfigLoader.cs:60; src/Ncx.Config/JobManifestLoader.cs.

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, not confirmed by the maintainer: the manuals do not settle this. No manual can decide which keys an NCXchange machine file or job manifest must contain — that is a property of NCX's own TOML schema, and the control manuals describe individual machine data, not a required set for an external description file. What the library does have, which the first pass missed, is the builders' own machine-description forms for CAM postprocessors: they are the nearest real-world analogue of a machine file, and the set they treat as indispensable matches the loader's list closely. DMG MORI's "Technisches Formular für Postprozessoren" opens with Grunddaten in which Maschinentyp, Steuerung (with software version), the axis count and the kinematics stand before anything else, then gives each rotary axis its arrangement (Dreh-Tisch / Schwenk-Kopf) and its limits, then a coolant channel table and a cycle list. Grob's Postprozessorinformation devotes section 1.3 to "Beschreibung der Achsen" and says for each axis whether it moves the workpiece or the tool. Controller and a per-axis kind are therefore not arbitrary choices — they are what a code generator is asked for first.
Evidence: `DMG-MORI_DMU160duoBLOCK_Postprozessor-Anforderung_V2.02_DE_2019`, p. 1-3 (A three-page form a customer fills in so a postprocessor can be built. Page 1 Grunddaten: Maschinentyp, Steuerung, Software Version, Achsen, Kinematik, Verfahrweg per axis, WZW-Position, WZ-Achse. Page 2 asks per rotary axis for Bauart, which axes the 4th and 5th are, the arrangement (Dreh-Tisch / Schwenk-Kopf) and the swivel limits, then the control functions (TCPM, TRAORI, CYCLE800), the clamping M codes, and a coolant table naming the on and off code of each channel. Page 3 lists the available drilling cycles against their native CYCLE numbers, with a blank line for further ones.); `Grob_G550_Technische-Information_Postprozessorbeschreibung_G552-2183_DE`, p. 4, section 1.3 with the contents on p. 2 (The machine description for the postprocessor begins with Werkzeugachse and then "1.3 Beschreibung der Achsen", whose whole content is which axes move what: "Die Achsen Y', A' und B' bewegen das Werkstück! Die Achsen X und Z bewegen das Werkzeug!" — the kind of an axis is the first thing recorded about it, before travels and speeds in section 3.). (Citations re-paged to the cnc-manuals connector 2026-10-26.)

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

Keep the loader: required are `[machine] name` and `controller`; `id` and `type` of every `[[resource]]`; `id`, `ncx`, `kind` of every `[[axis]]`; `id` of every `[[node]]`; in a job manifest `[job] machine` and `id`, `file` of every `[[channel]]`. Everything else is optional with its documented effect; compiler needs are checked by the compiler.
Basis: manual
Source: Builder postprocessor forms ask first for machine type, control and per-axis kind (DMG MORI "Technisches Formular für Postprozessoren", Grob Postprozessorinformation 1.3), the same set the loader requires.
Differs from the recommendation: no
Confidence: high
Code impact: none (machine-config text).
