#### D139 Machine key for the arc tolerance (D36)
Question: D36 and VM 3.2 take the arc tolerance 'from the machine configuration', with defaults of 0.01 mm and 0.0005 in, and architecture 5 gives it a place in `VmOptions`. Machine-config 1 to 9 name no key for it, and part two of P1-03 is to read the tolerance from the configuration. What is the key, and in which unit?
Recommendation: `[machine] arc_tolerance = 0.01`, in millimetres like `rapid`, `max_feed` and `acceleration` (machine-config 4), converted for an `INCH` program. When the key is absent, the D36 defaults per unit apply, which is what `VmOptions.ArcTolerance = null` and the default machine already do. Alternative: one value per unit, `arc_tolerance = { MM = 0.01, INCH = 0.0005 }`, mirroring the two defaults of D36.
Where: machine-config 1; VM 3.2; src/Ncx.Core/Machine/MachineIdentity.cs; src/Ncx.Config/MachineConfigLoader.Identity.cs; src/Ncx.Core/VirtualMachine/VmOptions.cs:52 (ForMachine); src/Ncx.Config/DefaultMachine.cs:24; P1-03.

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, not confirmed by the maintainer: the manuals do not settle this. The manuals cannot name an NCX key, but they settle the shape and back the recommendation's single key in millimetres. Heidenhain's counterpart is exactly that: one machine parameter circleDeviation (200901, iTNC 530 MP 7431), 'Zulässige Abweichung des Kreisradius', entered in mm, input range 0.0001 to 0.016 mm with at most four decimals, default 0.005 mm — one length, not one value per unit system, and NCX's 0.01 mm default sits inside that range. Fanuc has one parameter too, No. 3410 'Toleranz des Bogenradius', but its data unit is mm or inch in the input unit, so the same number is read in whichever units the control is set to — a third convention, and the one a Fanuc-shaped key would copy. Siemens does not use a single constant: alarm 14040 is raised against MD21000 CIRCLE_ERROR_CONST for small radii and against the programmed radius times MD21010 CIRCLE_ERROR_FACTOR for large ones. Caveats: No manual can decide the TOML key name or the table it belongs in; that stays the maintainer's. Worth noting for the compilers: if NCX ever wants to write its tolerance out to a target, Siemens needs a constant and a radius factor, so a single arc_tolerance cannot round-trip a Siemens setting. Fanuc's 'Eingabeeinheit' is the control's active input unit system, which is not quite the same thing as the NCX program's UNITS word.
Evidence: `Heidenhain_TNC640_Technisches-Handbuch_892899-18_NC-SW-34059x-09_DE_2018`, p. 2636 (Section 'Kreisendpunkt-Toleranz': the control computes the deviation of the arc radius between arc start and arc end and reports KREISENDPUNKT FALSCH when the entered tolerance is exceeded. circleDeviation (200901), 'Zulässige Abweichung des Kreisradius', Format Numerischer Wert, Eingabe 0.0001 bis 0.016 [mm] with max. 4 Nachkommastellen, Default 0.005 mm; the entry notes 'iTNC 530: 7431'.); `Fanuc_30i-B_Parameterhandbuch_B-64490EN-05_EN`, p. 196 (Parameter 3410 'Toleranz des Bogenradius': Eingabetyp Einrichteingabe, Datentyp Real Kanal, Dateneinheit 'mm, Zoll (Eingabeeinheit)', smallest unit depending on the increment system of the reference axis, value 0 or a positive 9-digit value. One value, read in whichever unit the control is set to.); `Fanuc_30i-B_Bedienung-Drehen-Fraesen_B-64484EN_EN`, p. 80-81 (section 4 Interpolationsfunktionen) (Under 'Radiusdifferenz zwischen Start- und Endpunkt': if the difference between the radius at the start point and at the end point of the arc is greater than the value in parameter 3410, alarm PS0020 is raised; and 'Um Spiralinterpolation zu verwenden, geben Sie in Parameter Nr. 3410 ... einen großen Wert an.' This is the same start-versus-end radius check the VM does in 3.2.); `Siemens_Sinumerik-840D-sl_Parameter_Alarme_BS.000503-DE-000-00_DE`, p. 216 (alarm 14040) (Alarm 14040 Kreisendpunktfehler: the alarm comes when the difference of the two radii is greater than MD21000 $MC_CIRCLE_ERROR_CONST (small radii, when the programmed radius is below the quotient of MD21000 and MD21010) or greater than the programmed radius times MD21010 $MC_CIRCLE_ERROR_FACTOR (large radii). Siemens uses an absolute constant plus a proportional factor, not one tolerance.). (Citations re-paged to the cnc-manuals connector 2026-10-26.)

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

`[machine] arc_tolerance = 0.01`, in millimetres like `rapid` and `max_feed`, converted for an INCH program; absent means the D36 defaults per unit (0.01 mm, 0.0005 in).
Basis: manual
Source: Heidenhain circleDeviation 200901 (iTNC MP 7431): one value in mm, range 0.0001-0.016, default 0.005. Fanuc 3410 is one value in input units; Siemens MD21000/21010 is constant plus factor (cannot round-trip, compilers note).
Differs from the recommendation: no
Confidence: high
Code impact: Ncx.Config machine loader (key into VmOptions.ArcTolerance).

#### D140 Override of a catalog entry: key by key
Question: machine-config 6 says the built-in family 'can be overridden per machine', and 5a lets every catalog cycle carry pre, post, requires and restore. Neither says whether a later [[cycle]] of the same name replaces the whole earlier entry or only the keys it writes. This applies to a catalog file over the built-in family and to a machine file over the catalog. The 5a example writes only name, native and pre for PECK on G83. The commented entries of doosan-puma-2600sy.toml do the same for PECK and for CHIP_BREAK, both on G83. If the whole entry were replaced, they would lose DEPTH, CLEARANCE, PECK, CYCLE_F and CYCLE_DWELL.
Recommendation: Key by key, as the code does it (CycleEntry.OverriddenBy, CycleCatalog.Override). A key the later entry writes replaces the earlier value, and a table key such as params is replaced as a whole. A key the later entry leaves out stays, and each of the four rule keys counts as a key of its own. An entry with a new name is added at the end. native stays required on every entry. This is one sentence in machine-config 6. Alternative: the later entry replaces the whole earlier one, and the 5a example then has to write every parameter again.
Where: machine-config 6, 5a; src/Ncx.Core/Machine/CycleEntry.cs (OverriddenBy); src/Ncx.Core/Machine/CycleCatalog.cs (Override); docs/spec/examples/machines/doosan-puma-2600sy.toml ([cycles] comments).

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27: the library does not answer this (searched grep over 01_Steuerungen and 02_Maschinenhersteller for Anwenderzyklus/Anwenderzyklen, Herstellerzyklus, 'Zyklus überschreiben/überschrieben', Zyklensuchpfad, Suchreihenfolge Zyklen, CUS.DIR / CMA.DIR / CST.DIR; checked the Siemens 840D sl Zyklen-Programmierhandbuch (2008), the Anhang Zyklenpakete SW47, the 840D sl Arbeitsvorbereitung chapter 'Zyklen extern programmieren' and the Heidenhain TNC 640 Zyklen manual. The DMG MORI postprocessor form's cycle list (Bohren CYCLE81 ... plus a blank line for further cycles) is an add-to list, not a merge. #### D141 Severities of the cycle catalog checks
Question: machine-config 6 names no mistake of a catalog entry. The P2-01 line in 12-phase-2 settles only unknown keys (WARNING), missing required keys and wrong types (ERROR). The code makes an unusable entry an ERROR: a name written twice in one file (CFG150), a name or params word that is not an NCX identifier (CFG151), a contour of more than two words (CFG154). It makes an inconsistent entry a WARNING: an absolute_from_surface word that params does not map (CFG152), absolute_from_surface without SURFACE (CFG153), modal on Heidenhain or Siemens, or a signature on Fanuc (CFG155). An ERROR stops the catalog or machine file from loading (the loaders return null; exit 1, D97).
Recommendation: Keep the severities as implemented. They follow P2-01: strict on what makes an entry unusable, lenient on the rest, as for unknown keys until the schema is final (12-phase-2 risks). List the six checks and their severities in machine-config 6 after the key list.
Where: machine-config 6; src/Ncx.Config/Cycles/DiagnosticCodes.Cycles.cs; src/Ncx.Config/Cycles/CycleCatalogLoader.Entries.cs; docs/spec/generated/diagnostics.md.

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, not confirmed by the maintainer: the manuals do not settle this. The severities are still NCXchange's own to set — no manual describes a TOML catalog with per-check severities — so keep them as implemented and list the six checks in machine-config 6 as the recommendation says. But the library is not silent on the shape of the split, and the earlier "nothing bears on this" was too strong: Siemens' own cycle-description files carry exactly this two-tier treatment. A line of the description that cannot be interpreted raises alarm 105052 and the offending line is displayed, while a parameter that cannot be interpreted raises 105054 and "Die Initialisierung der Zyklen wird abgebrochen". That is the same rule NCX implements — strict where the entry becomes unusable, lenient where it is merely inconsistent — and is worth citing in machine-config 6 as the precedent.
Evidence: SINUMERIK 840D sl/840D/840Di/810D Diagnoseanleitung, 08/2005, p. PDF 599 (alarm 105052) and 600 (alarm 105054); 596 for 105001 (no readable text in the cnc-manuals connector, which lists the manual as `Siemens_Sinumerik840D_Diagnosehandbuch_DE_2005`) (Added by me. 105052 "Fehler in der Zyklenbeschreibung": sc.com or uc.com contains a line that cannot be interpreted, and that line is output — nothing is aborted. 105054 "Fehler beim Aufruf der Zyklenbeschreibung": one of the files sc.com, cov.com contains a parameter that cannot be interpreted, and "Die Initialisierung der Zyklen wird abgebrochen". 105001 reports the description file as simply not found). (Citations re-paged to the cnc-manuals connector 2026-10-26.)

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

Basis: manual

#### D142 Anchoring trivia in a reader's program
Question: D92's recommendation gives the model `NcxProgram.Trivia (line number, text)`, architecture 4 draws Trivia with Line and Text, and implementation 10 (P0-02) says "the writer interleaves them with the blocks by line number". A reader begins each block with its source line, which that block's diagnostics cite (architecture 7, `Begin(int sourceLine)`). Language 4.13 has the reader move code kept after M30 in front of PROGRAM=END, so block lines decrease; two NCX blocks read from one source line can also stand around a trivia line. In these cases a line number cannot keep trivia "in place" (D92). The builder's workaround gives a trivia line the line of the block begun last. With it, a comment line added after the moved section's last block (source line 40) and before PROGRAM=END (source line 31) is written after PROGRAM=END. P3-01 meets this.
Recommendation: Trivia also records the block it stands before: the index of that block, set by the parser and by NcxBuilder.Trivia at the call, and the writer places it there. Trivia after FILE=END stand after the last block. The anchor must survive every step that inserts blocks. The expander and IProgramRewriter plugins insert generated blocks into the program (architecture 5.5, 9), so they shift the index, or the trivia travel with their block. The line stays, as the file line for a parsed program. NcxBuilder.Trivia(text), which ISourceRule plugins reach through the builder (implementation 13), keeps its signature, and a parsed file still formats byte for byte. Alternative: keep placement by line number and document the limit: in a reader's output, a trivia line inside reordered blocks may move to the next block with a greater line.
Where: architecture 4 (Trivia class and the sentence after the diagram) and 5.5; D92 rationale (model sentence); implementation 10 P0-02 (NcxProgram line); src/Ncx.Core/Model/Trivia.cs; src/Ncx.Core/Parsing/Parser.cs:38; src/Ncx.Core/Writing/NcxBuilder.cs Trivia (TODO(question)); src/Ncx.Core/Writing/NcxWriter.cs Write.

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, not confirmed by the maintainer: the manuals do not settle this. Less than the draft answer claimed. What the controls show is that a comment belongs to a block, not to a line number: on a Fanuc the comment lives inside the block, between the control-out and control-in characters, and is read in, displayed and written out with the program; on a Heidenhain a comment is either appended to an NC block with a semicolon or is an NC block of its own, and the block numbers are generated by the control, so a number is a position that renumbers, not an identity. But the manuals do not back the DIRECTION the recommendation picks. The Heidenhain dialog for a free comment block asks the operator to "select the NC block BEHIND which you want to insert the comment" — anchored to the preceding block, the opposite of "the block it stands before" — and a Fanuc comment is inside a block, so it is neither before nor after one. Which end of the gap the anchor holds, and how NCXchange keeps it valid when the expander or a plugin inserts blocks, stays the maintainer's call.
Evidence: `Heidenhain_TNC640_Programmierung-Klartext_892903-18_NC-SW-34059x-10_DE_2019`, p. 192-193 (section 6.3) (Three ways to enter a comment: appended while the block is being written, added afterwards to a chosen block, or as a comment in its own NC block — and for that third case the instruction is "NC-Satz wählen, hinter dem Sie den Kommentar einfügen wollen", i.e. select the block BEHIND which it goes. A whole block can be turned into a comment by putting a semicolon at its start and turned back by removing it.); `Heidenhain_TNC640_Programmierung-Klartext_892903-18_NC-SW-34059x-10_DE_2019`, p. 94 ("Die Steuerung erzeugt die Satznummern sowie den BEGIN- und END-Satz automatisch", with the example program numbered 0 to 3 in sequence.); `Fanuc_30i-B_Bedienung-Drehen-Fraesen_B-64484EN_EN`, p. 322, ch. 13 Programmkonfiguration (Everything between the control-out and control-in codes, the opening and closing parenthesis, is treated by the CNC as a comment section. Comment sections are read into memory with the program, shown on the screen with it, and output again when the program is sent to an external device; in memory or DNC operation they are skipped.). (Citations re-paged to the cnc-manuals connector 2026-10-26.)

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

Trivia records the index of the block it stands before (set by the parser and by NcxBuilder.Trivia at the call); the writer places it there, trivia after FILE=END after the last block. Block-inserting steps (expander, IProgramRewriter) keep the anchor valid by shifting indices. The line stays as data; NcxBuilder.Trivia(text) keeps its signature.
Basis: logical
Source: Manuals show comments belong to blocks, not line numbers (Fanuc in-block comments; Heidenhain renumbered blocks). Heidenhain's dialog anchors to the preceding block, but "before the next block" is equivalent for a writer and handles leading header comments without a predecessor, so the recommendation stands.
Differs from the recommendation: no
Confidence: medium
Code impact: Ncx.Core Trivia model, Parser, NcxBuilder, NcxWriter; expander/rewriter index shift.

#### D143 Canonical rank of CENTER:C and CENTER:IC
Question: Under POLAR and CYLINDER the arc plane is the X word (or the cylinder axis) and the C word, and R and CENTER keep their meaning there (VM 3.1 and 3.2, D102). Language 4.3 makes the CENTER address a plane axis, so CENTER:C and CENTER:IC are valid words. Language 5 rule 6, bucket 5 (D90) ranks only CENTER:X, CENTER:Y and CENTER:Z, then the incremental forms. ARC=CCW X=0 C=17.32 CENTER:X=0 CENTER:C=0 therefore has no canonical order. Under the closing sentence of the rule (words of one key sort by the address text), CENTER:C would come first. The same sentence would also put CENTER:IX before CENTER:X, against the explicit list of bucket 5, and D90 approved both. The list is the more specific rule, and the catalog follows it: each CENTER address has a rank of its own (WordDefinition.AddrRanks, which P0-03 added). The plan does not follow it. The P0-03 phase file gives each word one CanonicalRank, and P0-06 sorts 'by CanonicalRank and then by address text', which puts CENTER:IX first. CENTER is the only key where the two rules disagree; OFFSET:LEN, OFFSET:RAD and TOLERANCE:ROTARY agree with the address text.
Recommendation: Rank CENTER:C after CENTER:Z and CENTER:IC after CENTER:IZ, as the catalog already does (ranks 330 and 370). This follows bucket 3 (X Y Z A B C, absolute before incremental), and it writes the plane axes in the order of D102: X or the cylinder axis first, C second. Change bucket 5 to read 'CENTER:X, CENTER:Y, CENTER:Z, CENTER:C, then the incremental forms in the same order'. Limit the closing sentence to the words of one key whose address has no rank of its own (a role, a channel, a variable), as the header of generated/word-catalog.md already says. Give the P0-06 sort sentence the same limit.
Where: Language 5 rule 6 (bucket 5 and the closing sentence); D90 row (a Clarified line); docs/implementation/10-phase-0-foundations.md P0-03 (a rank per address for the fixed address sets) and P0-06 (the sort sentence). Code: src/Ncx.Core/Catalog/CanonicalRanks.cs, bucket 5 (the TODO(question) becomes a comment), and the AddrRanks of CENTER in MotionWords.cs. docs/spec/generated/word-catalog.md stays as it is.

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, not confirmed by the maintainer: the manuals do not settle this. No manual ranks words — canonical order is an NCX invention, and Siemens' own order N G X Y Z F S T D M H is explicitly only a recommendation for legibility — but the manuals do back the reason the recommendation gives. Fanuc states that under G12.1 the linear axis is the first axis of the polar plane and the hypothetical (rotary) axis the second, and that the arc-centre addresses in that plane follow the first axis of the plane: I and J in the Xp-Yp plane, J and K in Yp-Zp, K and I in Zp-Xp, with R as the alternative. The pairing runs first-axis address then second-axis address, which is the order CENTER:X before CENTER:C reproduces. One hard fact the draft does not mention: under cylindrical interpolation G07.1 Fanuc forbids I, J and K altogether — an arc there can only be given with R, whose unit is mm or inch rather than degrees — so a CENTER form under CYLINDER=n has no Fanuc output at all. Caveats: The rank of CENTER:C against CENTER:IX, and the scope of the closing sentence of rule 6, are purely internal to NCX. The Fanuc page pairs each centre address with a plane axis but prescribes no writing order at all, so the plane-axis-order argument is an inference from that pairing, not a rule the manual states. The G07.1 restriction is a compiler concern rather than a ranking one, but controller-mapping does not currently record it.
Evidence: `Fanuc_30i-B_Bedienung-Drehen-Fraesen_B-64484EN_EN`, 4.8 Polarkoordinaten-Interpolation, p. 91 (G12.1 selects a plane formed by a linear axis and a hypothetical axis perpendicular to it: 'Die lineare Achse ist die "erste Achse" der Ebene, die hypothetische Achse die "zweite Achse" der Ebene.'); `Fanuc_30i-B_Bedienung-Drehen-Fraesen_B-64484EN_EN`, p. 93 ('Kreisinterpolation in der Polarkoordinatenebene': the addresses for the arc in that plane 'richten sich nach der ersten Achse der Ebene (der linearen Achse)' — I and J in the Xp-Yp plane, J and K in Yp-Zp, K and I in Zp-Xp, each pair naming the first axis's address before the second's; 'Der Bogenradius kann auch mit einem R-Befehl spezifiziert werden.' The page says which addresses apply, not in what order they must be written.); `Fanuc_30i-B_Bedienung-Drehen-Fraesen_B-64484EN_EN`, 4.9.1 Zylindrische Interpolation, p. 99-100 (Page 100, under Beschränkungen: 'Im Modus "Zylindrische Interpolation" kann ein Bogenradius nicht mit der Wortadresse I, J oder K spezifiziert werden.' Pages 99-100, under Kreisinterpolation (G02, G03): R is used as usual and 'Die Radiuseinheit ist nicht Grad, sondern Millimeter (bei metrischer Eingabe) oder Zoll (bei Zoll-Eingabe).'); `Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl_Programmierhandbuch-NC-Programmierung_SW492_DE_2019`, p. 50 ('Reihenfolge der Anweisungen': 'Um den Satzaufbau übersichtlich zu gestalten, sollten die Anweisungen in einem Satz in folgender Reihenfolge angeordnet werden: N… G… X… Y… Z… F… S… T… D… M… H…'. It is phrased as a recommendation for legibility, not a rule the control enforces.). (Citations re-paged to the cnc-manuals connector 2026-10-26.)

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

Rank CENTER:C after CENTER:Z and CENTER:IC after CENTER:IZ (catalog ranks 330, 370). Bucket 5 reads "CENTER:X, CENTER:Y, CENTER:Z, CENTER:C, then the incremental forms in the same order"; the address-text sort applies only to addresses without their own rank, in rule 6 and the P0-06 sort. Record in controller-mapping that Fanuc G07.1 forbids I/J/K (R only), so CENTER under CYLINDER has no Fanuc output.
Basis: manual
Source: Fanuc B-64484EN G12.1 section: linear axis first, rotary second, centre addresses follow plane-axis order; G07.1 allows only R. Ranking itself is NCX's own.
Differs from the recommendation: no (adds the G07.1 compiler note)
Confidence: high
Code impact: P0-06 writer sort (address rank before text); docs only otherwise.

#### D145 The index of a variable (language 4.12)
Question: The grammar variable = "$" addr [ "[" expr "]" ] allows an index on every variable. 4.12 gives the index a meaning only for SYS_ names: 'The index selects a register or table row and may itself be an expression' (D51). An ADDR cannot contain brackets (language 3), so VAR can never assign Q1[2], and controller-mapping 6 reads the Siemens indirect R[R1] as RAW. Nothing says what $Q1[2] means. Nothing says either what an index that is not a whole number selects ($SYS_WEAR_Z[99.5]). A native template such as SYS_WEAR_Z = "#11{index:03}" (machine-config 7) cannot write such an index, and STATIC mode, which the compilers use, does not evaluate the index (VM 1).
Recommendation: Only a SYS_ name takes an index. An index on any other variable is an ERROR of the expression parser (a PAR code): the text shows it, and STATIC mode never evaluates expressions (VM 1). The index must be a whole number of 0 or more; a negative number cannot fill #11{index:03} or RG{index}. An index written as a number that breaks this rule ($SYS_WEAR_Z[99.5], $SYS_WEAR_Z[-1]) is a PAR ERROR for the same reason. A computed index that breaks it is the ERROR VM908 in INTERPRETED mode. Code changes: VM907 moves from Evaluator.EvaluateVariable into ExprParser.ParseVariable, which also checks an index written as a number. RegisterOf keeps VM908 and adds the negative case. Alternatives: both checks stay at evaluation, so only analyze reports them (as implemented); a non-whole index is rounded half away from zero, like ROUND.
Where: language 4.12 (system variables paragraph); src/Ncx.Core/Expressions/ExprParser.cs ParseVariable; src/Ncx.Core/Expressions/Evaluator.cs EvaluateVariable (VM907), RegisterOf (VM908); src/Ncx.Core/Model/DiagnosticCodes.Expressions.cs (new PAR codes).

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, not confirmed by the maintainer: Two parts of the recommendation hold and one must change. Only a SYS_ name takes an index — that is exactly Fanuc's model: the [n] suffix exists only on named system variables (a name is an underscore plus up to seven capitals, digits or underscores, and the index is for axis-specific or table-like data such as tool compensation, `[#_OFSW[n]]` with n = 1..999 standing for #10001..#10999); a local #1..#33 has no index form at all, indirection there is `#[<Ausdruck>]` on the variable number itself, and `##30` is explicitly illegal. A negative or otherwise invalid index is an error on the control too (alarm PS1099 "UNZUL. SUFFIX [ ]"), so the ERROR for `$SYS_WEAR_Z[-1]` is right. But an index that is not a whole number is not an error on Fanuc: the places after the decimal point are rounded, `[#_ABSIO[1.4999999]]` being #5001 and `[#_ABSIO[1.5000000]]` #5002 — so take the alternative and round half away from zero like ROUND (which language 4.12 already defines that way) instead of making `$SYS_WEAR_Z[99.5]` a PAR ERROR.
Evidence: `Fanuc_30i-B_Bedienung-Drehen-Fraesen_B-64484EN_EN`, p. 450-451 (§16.1) (A system variable may be addressed by its name, which begins with an underscore and has up to seven capitals, digits or underscores; for axis-specific variables and variables with many similar entries (tool compensation is the example given) an index [n] may be used, and n may be written as an expression (`[#_ABSKP[#500*2]]`). If n is not a whole number the places after the decimal point are rounded, 1.4999999 giving register 1 and 1.5000000 register 2. Note 2 says a negative or otherwise invalid index raises alarm PS1099 "UNZUL. SUFFIX [ ]"); `Fanuc_30i-B_Bedienung-Drehen-Fraesen_B-64484EN_EN`, p. 449 (§16.1) (A variable number may not be written with a variable directly: to reach #5 through #30 one writes #[#30], not ##30. The indirection therefore replaces the whole variable number, which is what corresponds on Fanuc to an index on a name); `Fanuc_30i-B_Bedienung-Drehen-Fraesen_B-64484EN_EN`, p. 453 (§16.2) (The tool-compensation system variables are given twice: as the named form [#_OFSW[n]] / [#_OFSG[n]] with the note that the index n is a compensation number from 1 to 999, and as the plain numbers #10001-#10999 and #11001-#11999 that may be used instead). (Citations re-paged to the cnc-manuals connector 2026-10-26.)

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

Only a SYS_ name takes an index. An index on any other variable is a PAR ERROR (the check moves from Evaluator into ExprParser.ParseVariable, as recommended). An index written as a literal number must be a whole number of 0 or more. `$SYS_WEAR_Z[-1]` and `$SYS_WEAR_Z[99.5]` are PAR ERRORs: no writer emits them, and they are plainly wrong text. A computed index (INTERPRETED mode) is rounded half away from zero, like ROUND, as Fanuc does. If it is negative after rounding, or has no register, it is VM908.
Basis: manual + logical
Source: Fanuc B-64484EN p. 450-451 §16.1 (non-whole index rounded, 1.5 -> 2; negative or invalid -> PS1099), p. 449, 453. Logical: rounding a computed value matches the control and absorbs float noise from arithmetic. A literal 99.5 is an authoring error and gets the ERROR.
Differs from the recommendation: yes: a computed non-whole index is rounded, not VM908. Literal non-whole and negative indexes stay PAR ERRORs.
Confidence: medium
Code impact: ExprParser.ParseVariable (VM907 to PAR, literal index check); Evaluator.RegisterOf rounds and checks the negative case.

#### D146 Cylinder plane when the workpiece's rotary axis does not turn about Z
Question: D102, VM 3.1 and 3.4 define the CYLINDER plane by the cylinder axis ("the linear axis along the cylinder's own axis, Z on a lathe", VM 3.4) and "the C word as a length on the circumference". Language 4.2 and controller-mapping 1 map CYLINDER to Heidenhain cycle 27 and Siemens TRACYL, which also run on mills whose workpiece turns on an A or B axis (about X or Y). The VM cannot tell the plane on such a machine: no key of a rotary [[axis]] in machine-config 4 says which linear axis it turns about (owner is described only as the rotary axis of a work spindle); machine-config 9 says only the kinematics module reads the [[node]] direction; and the three mill files in machines/ model the table as a table resource with no rotary axis at all. On a mill with an A table axis, which plane does CYLINDER=40 use, and does the program write A or C? The code builds only the lathe plane (Plane.Cylinder: Z, C, tool axis X).
Recommendation: The cylinder axis is the linear axis parallel to the rotary axis of the current workpiece holder. For a rotary axis owned by a work spindle that is Z (every lathe, and the D103 default machine). Otherwise a new optional key on the rotary [[axis]] names it (for example parallel = "X", default Z). owner may name a table resource as well as a work spindle, so that a mill table is a workpiece holder with its rotary axis. CYLINDER while the workpiece holder has no rotary axis is an ERROR at check. The rotary word is that axis, written as C or by its own name, since VM 3.8 rule 3 already resolves A, B and C to the holder's rotary axis. The direction stays cylinder axis first, rotary axis second. The tool axis is X on a lathe and the spindle axis (Z) on a mill. Reason: VM 3.4 already defines the cylinder axis in general terms, and controller-mapping 1 maps cycle 27, which on mills usually turns about X or Y. Alternative: 1.0 supports only the Z/C cylinder. CYLINDER on a holder whose rotary axis does not turn about Z is then an ERROR at check, and readers keep such sources as RAW (D5).
Where: D102 log line; VM 3.1, 3.2, 3.4, 3.8; language 4.2 CYLINDER row; machine-config 4 (the new [[axis]] key, owner for a table). Code: src/Ncx.Core/Geometry/Plane.cs Plane.Cylinder (TODO line 37) becomes per machine; the axis record in MachineConfig and MachineConfigLoader; P1-03 motion rules; readers and compilers of cycle 27 and TRACYL (P3-04, P3-05, P5).

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, not confirmed by the maintainer: The cylinder axis is the linear axis parallel to the rotary axis of the current workpiece holder, as the recommendation has it — both families define it that way and neither ties it to Z. Siemens names TRACYL's three machine axes purely by their relation to the rotation (rotary axis, infeed axis perpendicular to it, longitudinal axis parallel to it); the Heidenhain contour subprogram holds an angular axis and the linear axis running parallel to it. Add one rule the draft is missing: at the cycle call the spindle axis has to stand perpendicular to the rotary-table axis, or the Heidenhain control issues an error. That is a condition on the actual tool orientation, not on the axis letter — the same page runs the cycle with a tilted working plane and mentions a kinematics switch — so it does not by itself turn a C table into an ERROR, and NCX cannot decide it from an axis letter in machine-config 4. On the compile side the rotary letter is not fixed: the TNC 640 always writes the contour in X and Y whatever rotary axes the machine has, Siemens after TRACYL writes the circumference as a length on the transformation's Y axis with Z along the cylinder, and only the iTNC 530 writes the machine's own rotary-axis letter. So NCX may keep one C word as a length (VM 3.4, D102), but the letter a compiler emits is per family and must not be passed through.
Evidence: `Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl-828D_Programmierhandbuch-Arbeitsvorbereitung_DE_2013`, p. 353 (TRACYL without slot-wall correction maps the programmed cylinder coordinates onto three machine axes named only by their relation to the rotation: the rotary axis (Y/CM), the infeed axis "senkrecht zur Drehachse" (XM) and the longitudinal axis "parallel zur Drehachse" (ZM), with the note that the linear axes stand perpendicular to one another. The infeed axis being perpendicular to the rotary axis is the Siemens counterpart of the Heidenhain perpendicularity requirement.); `Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl-828D_Programmierhandbuch-Arbeitsvorbereitung_DE_2013`, p. 352 (The worked TRACYL(40) example runs in G19 and writes the section along the cylinder as Z ("Nutabschnitt parallel zur Zylinderachse") and the section around the circumference as Y ("Nutabschnitt parallel zum Umfang"), with X the radial infeed. C appears only as CC=200 in the positioning blocks before TRACYL and after TRAFOOF, never inside the transformed blocks.); `Heidenhain_TNC640_Zyklen_892905-18_NC-SW-34059x-10_DE_2019`, p. 333 (For cycle 27 the contour subprogram is described "immer mit den Koordinaten X und Y", independent of which rotary axes the machine has, so the contour description does not depend on the machine configuration. The figure marks Y (Z) as the axis along the cylinder and X (C) as the angular axis, and the angular coordinate may be given in degrees or mm, chosen by Q17.); `Heidenhain_TNC640_Zyklen_892905-18_NC-SW-34059x-10_DE_2019`, p. 334 (Requirements for cycle 27: the cylinder must be clamped centred on the rotary table with the preset set at the table centre, and at the cycle call the spindle axis must stand perpendicular to the rotary-table axis, otherwise the control issues an error and a kinematics switch may be needed. The same list states that the cycle may also be run with a tilted working plane, so the condition is on the actual spindle orientation, not on which rotary axis the table has.); `Heidenhain_iTNC530_Zyklen_670_388-12_NC-SW-340490-07_DE_2011`, p. 227-228 (Page 227: the contour subprogram of cycle 27 holds coordinates in an angular axis ("z.B. C-Achse") and in the axis that runs parallel to it ("z.B. Spindelachse") — the machine's own rotary letter, not a fixed X/Y pair. Page 228: the cylinder must be clamped centred on the rotary table and the spindle axis must run perpendicular to the rotary-table axis, otherwise the TNC issues an error message; this older manual prints no preset-at-table-centre sentence and no kinematics-switch note, and it may likewise be run with a tilted plane.). (Citations re-paged to the cnc-manuals connector 2026-10-26.)

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

Follow the recommendation. The cylinder axis is the linear axis parallel to the rotary axis of the current workpiece holder: Z for an axis owned by a work spindle, otherwise the new optional `[[axis]] parallel = "X"|"Y"|"Z"` (default "Z"). `owner` may name a table resource. CYLINDER without a rotary axis on the workpiece holder is an ERROR at check. In NCX the rotary word stays one C word, a length on the circumference (D102). Compilers choose the native letters per family: TNC 640 cycle 27 contour in X/Y, Siemens TRACYL Y around the circumference and Z along it, and iTNC 530 the machine's rotary letter. A compiler never passes the NCX letter through. The VM does not check that the spindle axis is perpendicular to the table axis. That is the kinematics module's job and the control's own error.
Basis: manual
Source: Siemens Arbeitsvorbereitung 2013 p. 352-353 (TRACYL axes defined by relation to the rotation); TNC 640 Zyklen 892905-18 p. 333-334; iTNC 530 Zyklen 670388-12 p. 227-228.
Differs from the recommendation: yes: adds the per-family compile letters and states that perpendicularity is not checked from the axis letter.
Confidence: high
Code impact: Plane.Cylinder per machine; `parallel` key in MachineConfigLoader; the cycle 27/TRACYL compilers (P5) map the letters.

#### D149 An ARG named outside V1..V33
Question: Language 4.9 describes ARG as an 'Argument of the CALL in the same block (G65 P9010 A1). The callee sees it as a local variable.' VM 3.6 assigns ARG words 'to the callee's locals', and the locals a CALL pushes are V1..V33 (VM 3.6, VM 4). Several sources write names outside V1..V33. One is the ARG:A=1 row of language 4.9. Another is controller-mapping 6, row CALL + ARG, where Siemens ARG names come from the callee's PROC line, else ARG:P1.. by position. Nothing says where such a name lives, and the code assigns it as a program variable. Case: CALL=ROW ARG:DEPTH=5. DEPTH is still 5 in the caller after SUB=END, and a caller variable named DEPTH is overwritten. This shows in trace and in the After snapshots. In INTERPRETED mode a later $DEPTH in the caller reads 5 instead of raising the D38 ERROR.
Recommendation: Every name an ARG of a CALL assigns is a local of that call, like V1..V33. It hides a caller variable of the same name until SUB=END or RETURN restores the caller's (VM 4). This keeps 'the callee sees it as a local variable' of language 4.9 true for every name. It also matches the Siemens call-by-value PROC parameters that controller-mapping 6 turns into ARG names, which are local to the PROC on the control. The row's example becomes ARG:V1=1 (G65 P9010 A1), because the last paragraph of language 4.9 maps G65 A to V1 (fanuc 7: A = #1). Consequences: a Siemens VAR (call-by-reference) parameter writes back to the caller (controller-mapping 1, row SUB; siemens), so it is not an ARG, and the Siemens reader (P5-01) keeps it RAW or reports it. On Heidenhain the compiler sets the Q parameters before CALL PGM (controller-mapping 6), and the control keeps them after the return, where the VM has restored the caller's values. A caller that reads such a name after the call therefore behaves differently on the control, and the Heidenhain compiler (P3-04) reports that case. Alternative: a name outside V1..V33 is a program variable assigned before the call, as the code does and as a Heidenhain control does. Siemens PROC parameters then stay set in the caller, where the control has dropped them.
Where: language 4.9 (row ARG and its example), VM 3.6 (CALL sentence), VM 4 (row variables), controller-mapping 6 (row CALL + ARG) and 1 (row SUB, VAR parameters); src/Ncx.Core/VirtualMachine/VirtualMachine.Static.cs AssignArguments (TODO at 251-253); src/Ncx.Core/VirtualMachine/State/VariableStore.cs TableOf, IsLocal, PushLocals; Siemens reader (P5-01), Heidenhain compiler (P3-04).

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, not confirmed by the maintainer: the manuals do not settle this. The manuals confirm both premises the recommendation rests on. Siemens: a PROC call-by-value parameter is a value the caller hands over, the callee gets no access to the caller's variable, and a change has no effect on the caller after the return — exactly the hiding-and-restoring the recommendation asks of every ARG name; a parameter declared VAR is passed by reference and does write back, which is why a VAR parameter cannot be an ARG. Heidenhain is the opposite, which the earlier answer left unverified: a plain Q parameter acts on all NC programs in the control's memory, so a value the compiler sets before CALL PGM, or one the called program changes, is still there after the return — only QL is local to one NC program (and Q0-99 act locally inside macros and manufacturer cycles, where changes are not given back). That is precisely the divergence the recommendation's consequence paragraph describes, so the Heidenhain compiler's report is warranted. Two Siemens details for the reader: a parameter left out of the call takes 0, or the init value on the PROC line, and a call-by-reference or AXIS parameter may not be left out at all. Where such a name lives in the NCX VM stays an NCX choice; the manuals only show that the recommendation, not the alternative, matches Siemens.
Evidence: `Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl_Programmierhandbuch-NC-Programmierung_SW492_DE_2019`, p. 507 (Call-by-value with PROC: the caller passes only the value, the subprogram gets no direct access to the variable, a change alters only the value visible inside the subprogram, the caller's variable stays unchanged, and the transfer has "keine Rückwirkungen" on the calling program.); `Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl_Programmierhandbuch-NC-Programmierung_SW492_DE_2019`, p. 509 (Call-by-reference with PROC and the keyword VAR passes a reference (pointer), the subprogram writes the caller's variable directly, and the effect persists after the subprogram ends.); `Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl_Programmierhandbuch-NC-Programmierung_SW492_DE_2019`, p. 505-506 (Page 505: an omitted parameter of a PROC call takes the default "0", the separating commas must still be written (only a trailing one may be dropped), and parameters passed by reference or of type AXIS may not be omitted. Page 506 adds $P_SUBPAR[n], with which the callee can ask whether a parameter was actually passed.); `Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl_Programmierhandbuch-NC-Programmierung_SW492_DE_2019`, p. 404, 407-408 (Page 404: a local user variable (LUD) is one defined in an NC program that is not the main program; it is created when that program is called and can be accessed only inside the program that defines it. Pages 407-408 carry the worked example: SUB2 defines LUD VAR2, and one level deeper SUB3's line VAR2=1 is commented "Fehler: LUD aus SUB2 nicht bekannt".); `Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl_Programmierhandbuch-NC-Programmierung_SW492_DE_2019`, p. 508 (A PROC line may give each parameter an initialisation value, which the parameter takes when the call supplies none, and up to 127 parameters may be passed.); `Heidenhain_TNC640_Programmierung-Klartext_892903-18_NC-SW-34059x-10_DE_2019`, p. 266-267 (The Q-parameter table: plain Q parameters "wirken auf alle NC-Programme im Speicher der Steuerung"; QL parameters "wirken nur lokal innerhalb eines NC-Programms" (0-499); QR parameters are retained across a power failure. A note on the Q0-99 row says those act locally inside macros and manufacturer cycles, so changes there are not given back to the NC program.). (Citations re-paged to the cnc-manuals connector 2026-10-26.)

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

Every name an ARG of a CALL assigns is a local of that call, hiding a caller variable until SUB=END/RETURN. The language 4.9 example becomes ARG:V1=1. A Siemens VAR parameter is not an ARG (reader keeps it RAW or reports). The Heidenhain compiler reports a caller that reads such a name after the call, since Q parameters survive CALL PGM on the control.
Basis: manual
Source: Siemens PROC call-by-value parameters are local, VAR writes back (840D sl programming manual); Heidenhain TNC 640 Klartext: Q parameters act on all programs, only QL local.
Differs from the recommendation: no
Confidence: high
Code impact: Ncx.Core VM CALL/ARG handling (push all ARG names as locals); Heidenhain compiler diagnostic (P3-04).

#### D150 Placeholder of the preload template
Question: The introduction of machine-config defines `{tool}` as 'the tool in the spindle after the block' and `{next}` as 'the preloaded next tool'. In a `PRELOAD=5` block, `{tool}` is therefore the old tool and `{next}` is 5. The table in machine-config 3 writes the preload with `{tool}` for Fanuc, Heidenhain, Siemens and Mori Seiki (`T{tool}`, `TOOL DEF {tool}`, `T{tool:04}`), but with `{next}` in both Nakamura rows (`G341 T{next:02}.`). The six machine files with a preload template follow the table; doosan-puma-2600sy.toml and millturn1.toml have none. Which placeholder carries n of `PRELOAD=n`?
Recommendation: In the `preload` template both placeholders mean n: `{tool}` is the tool the block preloads, and `{next}` is the preloaded tool as already defined. This needs one sentence in the introduction and no change to any template, file or test. The manual table, the six files with a preload and the P2-02 tests are already written this way. Alternative: follow the definitions strictly, so `preload` uses `{next}` only. Then the Fanuc, Heidenhain, Siemens and Mori Seiki cells of the table change, and so do the preload lines of fanuc-mill-30i, heidenhain-itnc530, siemens-840dsl-mill and mori-ntx1000-mapps.
Where: machine-config introduction (placeholder list) and 3; TODO(question) in machines/fanuc-mill-30i.toml:41, heidenhain-itnc530.toml:39, siemens-840dsl-mill.toml:40; P3-03 (the compiler fills the values).

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, not confirmed by the maintainer: the manuals do not settle this. The manuals settle the meaning, not the name: in every builder's preload command the number written is n, the tool being preselected. Nakamura `G341 T18` puts T18 in the ATC wait position while the program runs, and in the Nakamura change command `G340 T… A…` it is the separate A word that carries the next tool; Heidenhain's `TOOL DEF` block, when tool tables are used, preselects the next tool. So the Recommendation is right on substance (both placeholders resolve to n in the `preload` template) and `{next}` is the name the manuals' own wording matches; which of the two NCX writes is a naming choice no manual touches.
Evidence: `Nakamura-Tome_Fanuc_Programmierung_Programmierhandbuch_DE_2019`, p. 162 (G341 takes one T word, a 2- or 3-digit tool number; the machine prepares that tool while the program continues. The example G341 T18 brings T18 into the ATC wait position, so the T of the preload command is the tool being preselected. The page adds that the cycle is seldom used because G340 can define the follow-on tool too.); `Nakamura-Tome_Fanuc_Programmierung_Programmierhandbuch_DE_2019`, p. 161 (Syntax of the tool-change cycle G340 T_ A_ M_ S_ B_ (W_): T is the tool number with its offset number, A is the "Werkzeugnummer des nächsten Werkzeuges". In the change command the current tool and the next tool are two different words.); `Heidenhain_iTNC530_Programmierung-Klartext_NC-SW-340490-05_DE_2008`, p. 177 (Under "Vorauswahl bei Werkzeug-Tabellen": when tool tables are used, a TOOL DEF block makes the preselection for the next tool to be used, given by tool number, Q parameter or a name in quotation marks. The number in the Heidenhain preload line is therefore the preloaded tool.). (Citations re-paged to the cnc-manuals connector 2026-10-26.)

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

In the `preload` template both `{tool}` and `{next}` mean n of PRELOAD=n; one sentence in the machine-config introduction. No template, file or test changes; `{next}` is the preferred spelling in new files.
Basis: manual
Source: In every builder's preselect the number written is the tool being preselected (Nakamura G341 T18; Heidenhain TOOL DEF preselects the next tool). The name is an NCX choice.
Differs from the recommendation: no
Confidence: high
Code impact: none.

#### D151 Tolerance template without a rotary tolerance
Question: D85 and language 4.1 make `TOLERANCE:ROTARY` optional, and VM 2.1 starts it at none. Yet the `[tolerance] ON` templates in machine-config 5 for Heidenhain (`... HSC-MODE:{mode} TA{rotary}`) and Siemens (`CYCLE832({tol},{mode},{rotary})`) need `{rotary}`. The machine-config introduction says a missing placeholder value leaves the template unusable. So `TOLERANCE=0.02` on its own cannot compile for either family. The three-axis mills heidenhain-itnc530.toml and siemens-840dsl-mill.toml have no rotary tolerance at all, and millturn1.toml (D104) writes the same Siemens template. On Siemens there is a second gap: the orientation tolerance also needs the tens digit 1 in the mode (controller-mapping 1), which `mode = { FINISH = 1, ROUGH = 3 }` cannot produce.
Recommendation: Add an optional `ON_ROTARY` template to `[tolerance]`, written instead of `ON` while `TOLERANCE:ROTARY` is set, and drop `{rotary}` from `ON`. Heidenhain: `ON` ends with `HSC-MODE:{mode}`, and `ON_ROTARY` adds ` TA{rotary}`. Siemens: `ON = "CYCLE832({tol},{mode})"` and `ON_ROTARY = "CYCLE832({tol},1{mode},{rotary})"`, where the literal 1 is the tens digit. A machine without `ON_ROTARY`, such as the three-axis mills, writes `ON` and reports `TOLERANCE:ROTARY` as a WARNING that it was not written. Reason: this keeps D85's optional word compilable with templates alone. Alternative: a `[tolerance] rotary = <value>` written for `{rotary}` when the program sets none; it does not fix the Siemens tens digit. Whether the iTNC 530 accepts cycle 32.2 without TA still has to be checked on the control.
Where: machine-config 5 ([tolerance]); controller-mapping 1 (TOLERANCE row); machines/heidenhain-itnc530.toml:130, machines/siemens-840dsl-mill.toml:136 and docs/spec/examples/machines/millturn1.toml:237; src/Ncx.Core/Machine/ToleranceTable.cs and its loader; tests/Ncx.Config.Tests/Templates/TemplateSetMachinesTests.cs (Render_HeidenhainTolerance_WritesTheCommaOfItsFormat); P3-04, P5-02.

ANSWER: (Peter, 2026-10-07, drafted by Claude in project_spike) Accept as recommended: an optional `ON_ROTARY` template, `{rotary}` dropped from `ON`, and a machine without `ON_ROTARY` reports `TOLERANCE:ROTARY` as a WARNING that it was not written (one diagnostic per distinct value, as in D367). Whether the iTNC 530 accepts cycle 32.2 without TA stays a fact to check on the control before release 1.0; release 1 of the CAM writes no rotary tolerance.
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, not confirmed by the maintainer: The proposed Siemens `ON = "CYCLE832({tol},{mode})"` does not compile: the manual says the third parameter must always be programmed, including on three-axis machines running programs without tool orientation, where it is written as 1. So use `ON = "CYCLE832({tol},{mode},1)"` and `ON_ROTARY = "CYCLE832({tol},1{mode},{rotary})"` — the tens digit 1 of the machining type is confirmed (_ORI_FINISH = 11, _ORI_ROUGH = 13 against _FINISH = 1, _ROUGH = 3). The shipped `OFF = "CYCLE832(0,0,1)"` is the manual's own deselection example and needs no change, though the manual also allows the bare `CYCLE832()` for deselection, so nothing forces three arguments there. On Heidenhain the split works as proposed: TA may be given as 0, which makes the control fall back on the manufacturer's configured tolerance, so a machine without a rotary tolerance loses nothing. Write TA0 rather than dropping TA altogether — the zero/NO-ENT fallback is stated for the TNC 640, not for the iTNC 530.
Evidence: SINUMERIK 840D sl NC-Programmierung, Programmierhandbuch 06/2019 (CNC-SW 4.92), p. 1125-1126 (The syntax line is CYCLE832(<S_TOL>, <S_TOLM>, <S_OTOL>) — contour tolerance, machining type, orientation tolerance. Of S_OTOL: "Der Parameter <S_OTOL> muss programmiert werden. Dies gilt auch für Anwendungen auf 3-Achs-Maschinen bei Programmen ohne Orientierung des Werkzeugs (<S_OTOL> = 1)." The tens digit of the machining type selects 0 = compatibility / no orientation tolerance, 1 = orientation tolerance in the third parameter.); SINUMERIK 840D sl NC-Programmierung, Programmierhandbuch 06/2019 (CNC-SW 4.92), p. 1127-1128 (The plain-text names confirm the digits: _OFF = 0, _FINISH = 1, _SEMIFIN = 2, _ROUGH = 3, _PRECISION = 4, and with an orientation tolerance _ORI_FINISH = 11, _ORI_SEMIFIN = 12, _ORI_ROUGH = 13, _ORI_PRECISION = 14. The three-axis examples are CYCLE832(0.004,_FINISH,1) and CYCLE832(0.004,1,1), the five-axis ones CYCLE832(0.3,_ORI_ROUGH,0.8) / CYCLE832(0.3,13,0.8), the deselection CYCLE832(0,_OFF,1) / CYCLE832(0,0,1). For deselection S_TOL must be passed as zero, and the manual adds that "Die Syntax CYCLE832() ist für die Abwahl von CYCLE832 ebenfalls erlaubt".); HEIDENHAIN TNC 640 Benutzerhandbuch Zyklenprogrammierung, NC-SW 34059x-10, 10/2019, p. 373 (Cycle 32 parameter TA, the tolerance for rotary axes, input range 0.0000 to 10.0000: an entry greater than zero is used as the maximum permitted deviation, and an entry of zero, or pressing NO ENT while programming, makes the control use a value configured by the machine manufacturer. HSC-MODE is 0 finish, 1 rough. The example block is CYCL DEF 32.2 HSC-MODE:1 TA5.); HEIDENHAIN iTNC 530 Benutzerhandbuch Zyklen-Programmierung, NC-SW 340490-07, 2011, p. 316 (The older control gives TA an input range from 0 to 179.9999 and prints only the full example CYCL DEF 32.2 HSC-MODE:1 TA5; it states no zero/NO-ENT fallback and shows no 32.2 block without TA.).

#### D152 Placeholder names outside the introduction's list
Question: The machine-config introduction lists the placeholders but does not say whether the list is closed. The documents use six names that are not on it: in machine-config 3, {point} (G30 P{point} {axes}) and {order} (DMG L711({order})); in machine-config 5, {channel} (START({channel}), WAITE({channel})) and {radius} (FGREF[{axis}]={radius}); in dmg-ctx-840d.toml, {pair} and {ratio} (L725({pair},{ratio},{angle})). Main accepts any well-formed name, reads it as a number and reports nothing. A name that nothing fills shows up only as CFG100, when a compiler renders the template.
Recommendation: Make the introduction the complete list. Add {point} (the POINT of HOME, language 4.3) and {channel} (the value of START_CHANNEL or WAIT_CHANNEL, an integer, language 4.8), both numbers. Add {radius}, {order}, {pair} and {ratio} as numbers that have no NCX source in 1.0: the reader keeps the FGREF radius as RAW (controller-mapping 1, the ROTARY_PATH, ROTARY_FEED row, D86), and the L7xx cycles are DMG structure programming (D68), so a compiler that meets one of these names reports CFG100. A well-formed name outside the list becomes a WARNING with a CFG code of its own and is still read as a number, just as unknown keys are WARNINGs until P5-02 (implementation 12, P2-01 and Risks). The introduction says so, which code-guidelines 6 requires before a mistake may be a WARNING. With the six names added, the example files stay free of WARNINGs, as P2-04 requires. Alternative: keep the list open, as on main.
Where: machine-config introduction; implementation 12 P2-02; src/Ncx.Config/Templates/Placeholder.cs (the second TODO(question) at the top, Placeholder.Read); src/Ncx.Config/Templates/DiagnosticCodes.Templates.cs (one new code for an unlisted name); tests/Ncx.Config.Tests/Templates/TemplateParseTests.cs (Constructor_EveryPlaceholderOfTheIntroduction_IsReadByItsName).

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, not confirmed by the maintainer: the manuals do not settle this. The manuals confirm all four native meanings the draft assigns and that each is a number: Fanuc `G30 P2/P3/P4` selects the 2nd, 3rd or 4th reference point, so `{point}` is 2–4; Siemens `FGREF[<Rundachse>]=<Bezugsradius>` is an effective radius per rotary axis in the G70/G71 unit (default 360 mm / 2π = 57.296 mm), so `{radius}` is a length; DMG `L711(P1)` parameter 1 is the "Reihenfolge" 0–4 in which the axes reach the tool-change point; DMG `L725(P1,P2,P3)` parameter 1 is the "Paarung" (31, 32, 41, 42), parameter 2 the gear ratio i (−99…99) and parameter 3 the angular offset ANG (0–359.999). Nothing in the library bears on whether NCX's placeholder list should be closed — that part of the Recommendation is an NCX decision.
Evidence: `Fanuc_16i-210is-B_Beschreibungen_B-63522GE-02_DE`, p. 116 (Section 6.5 "Anfahren des 2., 3. und 4. Referenzpunkts (G30)": the format is G30 P2/P3/P4 IP_, with "P2, P3, P4: Auswahl des 2., 3. oder 4. Referenzpunkts" and, with no P given, the second reference point. The same page states that the 2nd, 3rd and 4th reference points are each set in a parameter. So the P value is an integer 2 to 4.); `Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl-828D_Funktionshandbuch-Grundfunktionen_DE_2012`, p. 352 (Section 6.3.3 FGROUP and FGREF: for each participating rotary axis an effective radius (Bezugsradius) must be given, programmed as the modal NC address FGREF[<Rundachse>]=<Bezugsradius>; its unit depends on the G70/G71/G700/G710 setting, and after system power-up and RESET the default is FGREF = 360 mm / 2π = 57.296 mm.); `DMG-MORI_CTX-GMX_Technik-Programmierung-ShopTurn3G_V1.0_DE_2013`, p. 32 (no readable text in the cnc-manuals connector) (Cycle L711 is called as L711(P1); parameter 1 is named "Reihenfolge", a number 0 to 4, deciding the order in which the tool-change point is reached. In this X/Z/Y variant: 0 = X, Z and Y together, 1 = X then Z and Y, 2 = Z then X and Y, 3 = X then Y, 4 = Z then Y. (The plain X/Z variant on cache page 36 uses the same 0–4 with 3 = X only and 4 = Z only.)); `DMG-MORI_CTX-GMX_Technik-Programmierung-ShopTurn3G_V1.0_DE_2013`, p. 36-37 (no readable text in the cnc-manuals connector) (Section 2.3.3.1: cycle L725(P1,P2,P3) switches on angular synchronism between spindle 4/3 and a tool spindle 1/2 with a gear ratio, and is switched off by L729 (page 36). The parameter table (page 37) gives parameter 1 "Paarung", the combination of spindles to be synchronised, with values 31, 32, 41, 42; parameter 2 the "Übersetzungsverhältnis der Spindeln zueinander", range −99 to 99 (example 1.2); parameter 3 ANG, the angular offset, range 0 to 359.999 (example 113.5).); `Siemens_Sinumerik-840D-sl_Programmierung_BS.000504-DE-000-00_DE`, p. 121 (Section 2.13 gives the syntax of the coordination commands: START(<ChanNr>, <ChanNr>, ...) and WAITE(<ChanNr>, <ChanNr>, ...) — each takes one or more channels, WAITE waiting for program end in one or more other channels; channel names configured in MD20000 $MC_CHAN_NAME may be used instead of numbers once MD10280 bit 1 is set.). (Citations re-paged to the cnc-manuals connector 2026-10-26.)

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

The introduction becomes the complete list. Add `{point}` (POINT of HOME) and `{channel}` (START_CHANNEL/WAIT_CHANNEL value), and `{radius}`, `{order}`, `{pair}`, `{ratio}` as numbers with no NCX source in 1.0 (a compiler meeting one reports CFG100). A well-formed name outside the list is a WARNING with its own CFG code and is still read as a number.
Basis: manual
Source: Native meanings all numeric: Fanuc G30 P2..P4; Siemens FGREF[axis]=radius; DMG L711 order 0-4, L725 pairing/ratio/angle (DMG CTX 840D sl manual). Closing the list is an NCX choice.
Differs from the recommendation: no
Confidence: high
Code impact: Ncx.Config template placeholder validation (new CFG WARNING).

#### D154 Function-table states as NCX words, and the pair of [spindle_sync]
Question: Architecture 7 has FindFunctionByCode("M88") answer SPINDLE:TOOL=CW. Machine-config 5 says the states of the tables other than [func] 'are the values of their word'. It lists CW, CCW, OFF, ORIENT, RPM, VC, CSS_OFF and RPM_MAX in [spindle.ROLE], and ON, OFF and PHASE in [spindle_sync]. The language disagrees: only CW, CCW and OFF are values of SPINDLE; ORIENT and RPM (4.5) and CSS, VC and RPM_MAX (4.11) are words of their own; SPINDLE_SYNC takes two roles or OFF, and PHASE is its own angle word (4.5). A reader must write the language words, and some of them need what the tables do not give. ORIENT and PHASE take a number (word catalog: 'number, expression'), while most templates write no angle: M19, M419, M219 and M319 for ORIENT; M92 (Nakamura), M213 (Doosan) and M34 (Mori Seiki) for PHASE. SPINDLE_SYNC needs its pair for M96 (Nakamura), M35 (Mori Seiki) or M203 (Doosan), and [spindle_sync] does not name it. VM 2.5 settles the default coolant channel ('the channel STANDARD is the default channel that a bare COOLANT addresses'), and VM 3.8 rule 2 settles the default spindle. Main answers in table form (SPINDLE:MAIN=ORIENT, SPINDLE_SYNC=ON, COOLANT:STANDARD=ON) and leaves the words to P3.
Recommendation: Keep the table form of architecture 7 as the answer of FindFunctionByCode, as on main. In machine-config 5, replace 'the values of their word' with a mapping that readers and compilers both follow: [spindle.R] CW, CCW, OFF give SPINDLE:R=state; ORIENT gives ORIENT:R={angle}, or ORIENT:R=0 where the template has no angle (M19 stops at the orientation position; controller-mapping 4: Biglia M19 at 0 degrees); RPM gives RPM:R={rpm}; VC gives CSS:R=ON VC:R={value} (G96 S, controller-mapping 4); CSS_OFF gives CSS:R=OFF; RPM_MAX gives RPM_MAX:R={value}; [spindle_mode.R] gives SPINDLE_MODE:R=state; [coolant] C gives COOLANT:C=state. The reader writes the address as the examples do. On a machine with more than one spindle, a spindle word carries its role: controller-mapping 4 says the Siemens reader 'writes the role', and MILLTURN_TRANSFER writes SPINDLE:MAIN=CW RPM:MAIN=1500 for S1500 M3 on millturn1. On a machine with one spindle, it carries none: 2.5D_FRAESEN writes SPINDLE=CW, and P3-02 and P3-05 compare it block for block. The channel STANDARD is written as a bare COOLANT (VM 2.5), as POLAR_FACE writes COOLANT=ON for M8 on the Nakamura. [spindle_sync] couples the default spindle with the other work spindle, the default spindle leading. Language 4.5 says 'the second follows the first', and the comments of nakamura-ntjx.toml and millturn1.toml say the sub follows the main. So ON gives SPINDLE_SYNC=default,other (MAIN,SUB in the example files); PHASE gives the same plus PHASE={angle}, and where the template has no angle (M92, M213, M34), the machine keeps the offset (Nakamura M93), and the reader writes PHASE=0 with a WARNING that names the code; OFF gives SPINDLE_SYNC=OFF. A machine with more than two work spindles, or whose default spindle is not a work spindle, names its pair with a new key, pair = ["MAIN", "SUB"]. Alternative: make pair a required key of every [spindle_sync].
Where: machine-config 5 (the paragraph after [raw], and [spindle_sync]); architecture 7; src/Ncx.Config/Templates/TemplateSet.cs FunctionStates and FindFunctionByCode (TODO(question)); src/Ncx.Config/MachineConfigLoader.Functions.cs (pair); P3-01, P3-02 (FanucBuilder), P3-03.

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, not confirmed by the maintainer: the manuals do not settle this. For the pair the manuals decide it and the Recommendation is right: the sync codes are defined for the machine's first and second work spindle — Nakamura M96 makes the 1st and 2nd spindle run together as soon as a rotation command is executed for the first spindle (on the NTJX these are the L-unit and R-unit spindles), and Mori M34 synchronises speed and phase "zwischen Spindel 1 und Spindel 2". So `SPINDLE_SYNC=default,other` is right and a `pair` key is only needed beyond two work spindles — which is a real case: the DMG L725 cycle names its pair explicitly (31/32/41/42, counter- or main spindle with tool spindle 1 or 2). PHASE genuinely carries no angle — Nakamura fixes the phase by parameter or M93 — so PHASE=0 plus a WARNING is harmless. ORIENT=0 is the weak spot: the Mori manual says the spindle stops "an der spezifizierten Ausrichtung (Winkel)" without the M code carrying one, the Nakamura code sheet gives M19/M419 as orientation on/off with no angle, and Nakamura needs a separate `G419 A_` (0–360°, 30° steps) for any other angle. No page says that angle is zero, so writing ORIENT:R=0 asserts a value the manuals do not give.
Evidence: `Nakamura-Tome_Fanuc_Programmierung_Programmierhandbuch-1_4810004ECL-1_DE_2013`, p. 254 (Chapter 15 "Synchronisierungssteuerung der ersten und zweiten Spindel" defines what first and second spindle mean per series — on the WTW/WTS/STW/STS/NTX(W)/NTX(S)/NTXL/NTJX/NTMX/MX5 machines they are the spindles of the L and R unit. M96 is speed synchronisation: in that mode the 1st and 2nd spindle turn synchronously when a rotation command is executed for the first spindle. M97 cancels it. M92 is phase synchronisation, and the phases are fixed "über Parameter oder M93"; M93 sets the phase-synchronous position.); `Nakamura-Tome_Fanuc_Programmierung_Programmierhandbuch-1_4810004ECL-1_DE_2013`, p. 255 (The note continuing from p. 254: on the TW series these commands must come from the right unit, while on the TW/WT/WY/WTS/STW/STS/NTX(W)/NTX(S)/NTXL/NTJX/NTMX/MX5 and NTJ/NTJ-100/NTM3/NTY3 machines they may be issued "von jeder der beiden Seiten" (M96, M97, M92).); `Nakamura-Tome_Super-NTJX_Programmierung_Liste-M-G-Codes_DE_2016`, p. 1-3 (sync codes and orientation codes) (On page 2 the NTJX code sheet names the pair in the code's own description: M96 "RECHTE SPINDEL LÄUFT SYNCHRON MIT SPINDEL LINKS", M97 "LOESCHEN VON M96", M92 "PHASENSYNCHRONER SPINDELLAUF EIN", M93 "PHASENVERSCHIEBUNG SETZEN". The orientation codes are on other pages: page 1 has M18/M19 spindle orientation off/on, page 3 has M418/M419 the same for the right spindle. None of the four carries an angle.); `Nakamura-Tome_Fanuc_Programmierung_Programmierhandbuch-1_4810004ECL-1_DE_2013`, p. 340-341 (Section 23-1-3 "Ausrichtung der Werkzeugspindel: Befehl für Eingabe eines beliebigen Winkels": orienting the tool spindle to an arbitrary angle is a separate G code, `G419 A_.` with A the orientation angle, range 0 to 360 in 30° steps; the note names the NTJX explicitly among the supported machines. It is to be used for positions other than those defined by M785/M786/M787/M788. So the plain orientation codes carry no angle.); `Mori-Seiki_NT-NTX-Serie_Programmierung_Programmieranleitung-NT-NTX_DE_2017`, p. 556 (Section 2-1 M34/M35/M36: M34 calls the phase-synchronised operation mode and synchronises both the speeds and the phases "zwischen Spindel 1 und Spindel 2"; M35 is speed synchronisation, M36 switches synchronisation off. The pair is fixed by the machine and neither code takes an angle. A note restricts M34/M35/M36 to the NT-S, NT-SZ and NT-SZM series.); `Mori-Seiki_NT-NTX-Serie_Programmierung_Programmieranleitung-NT-NTX_DE_2017`, p. 267-268 (Section 1-9: M19 orients spindle 1, M219 spindle 2, M319 the tool spindle / rotary tool spindle, M2073 cancels orientation. The spindle, tool spindle and rotary tool spindle stop "an der spezifizierten Ausrichtung (Winkel)" — the M code itself carries no angle word, and the page does not say where the angle is set or what its value is.); `Doosan_Puma-2600SY_M-Funktionen_DE`, p. 1, 3-4 (The machine's own list gives M19 "SPINDELORIENTIERUNG HAUPTSPINDEL (OPTION)" on page 1 and M119 "SPINDELORIENTIERUNG SUBSPINDEL (OPTION)" on page 3, both without an angle; page 4 gives M203 "SYNCHRONISATION VORWÄRTS", M204 rückwärts, M205 stop, M206 ausschalten, and M213/M214 "SPINDEL VORWÄRTS/RÜCKWÄRTS SPINDELDREHZAHL & PHASENSYNCHRON". The phase code names no angle and no pair.); `DMG-MORI_CTX-GMX_Technik-Programmierung-ShopTurn3G_V1.0_DE_2013`, p. 36-37 (no readable text in the cnc-manuals connector) (On a machine with four spindles the pair is not implicit: L725's first parameter is the "Paarung", the combination of spindles to be synchronised, 31 = spindle 3 (counter spindle) with tool spindle 1, 32 = spindle 3 with tool spindle 2, 41 = spindle 4 (main spindle) with tool spindle 1, 42 = spindle 4 with tool spindle 2. This is the case the Recommendation reserves the `pair` key for.). (Citations re-paged to the cnc-manuals connector 2026-10-26.)

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

Follow the recommendation's mapping table, with one change for ORIENT. ORIENT gives ORIENT:R={angle} when the template carries an angle. When the template has none (M19, M219, M319, M419), the reader writes ORIENT:R=0 plus a WARNING naming the code: "orientation angle set by the machine". This is the same treatment as PHASE without an angle (M92, M213, M34). A compiler writes such a template only for ORIENT:R=0. For any other angle it needs a template with {angle} (for example Nakamura G419 A), and without one it reports a CMP ERROR. [spindle_sync] ON couples the default spindle (leader) with the other work spindle: SPINDLE_SYNC=default,other. The `pair = ["MAIN","SUB"]` key is optional and required only with more than two work spindles, or when the default spindle is not a work spindle (DMG L725 case). FindFunctionByCode keeps the table form.
Basis: manual + logical
Source: Nakamura Programmierhandbuch 1 4810004ECL-1 p. 254-255, 340-341; Nakamura NTJX code list 2016 p. 1-3; Mori NT/NTX 2017 p. 267-268, 556; Doosan Puma 2600SY M list p. 1-4. Logical: the plain orientation codes carry no angle and the manuals give no value. The WARNING makes the 0 visible instead of asserting it silently.
Differs from the recommendation: yes: ORIENT=0 without a template angle now gets a WARNING, and the compiler refuses non-zero ORIENT without an angle template.
Confidence: medium
Code impact: TemplateSet.FindFunctionByCode consumers in readers P3-01..03 (WARNING); MachineConfigLoader.Functions reads the optional `pair`.

#### D155 A native code that several states write
Question: Machine-config 5 says only 'Readers map M codes back to names', yet one code often belongs to several states of a machine. M9 is OFF for STANDARD, LOW_PRESSURE, MEDIUM_PRESSURE and TOOL_SPINDLE_INTERNAL on nakamura-ntjx.toml, and M109 is OFF for three channels on dmg-ctx-840d.toml. M3 P11 is CW of both MAIN and SUB on the Doosan, and M34/M134 ([workpiece]) select which one. On the Doosan, M34 and M134 are also SPINDLE of [spindle_mode.MAIN] and [spindle_mode.SUB]; [workpiece] is not a function table, so FindFunctionByCode never names it. M3 is CW of both MAIN and TOOL on the Mori Seiki, which the file marks 'verify on the machine'. On millturn1.toml, M5 is both SPINDLE:MAIN=OFF and SPINDLE_MODE:MAIN=SPINDLE, and G97 is CSS_OFF of both MAIN and SUB. Architecture 7 gives the reader a source-side state that 'resolves what the controller leaves implicit'. Controller-mapping 4 uses it for S and for the Siemens M3 (the master spindle of SETMS). No document says how the reader chooses among states. Main returns only the first state in file order, which leaves the reader nothing to choose from.
Recommendation: FindFunctionByCode returns every state that writes the code, in the order of machine-config 5 and of the file, with the captured values. The reader drops the states its source state rules out: a state of a table bound to another channel (D56); a spindle that the source state does not address, that is the work spindle on the side that [workpiece] did not select (Doosan P11 after M34 or M134), or on Siemens a spindle other than the master spindle of SETMS (controller-mapping 4); an OFF for a resource that is not on. It writes every remaining state that does not already hold: M9 gives COOLANT=OFF for each channel that was on; M5 on millturn1 adds SPINDLE_MODE:MAIN=SPINDLE only when that spindle was in AXIS mode; a code that is also a [workpiece] template gives the WORKPIECE word as well, so the Doosan M34 gives WORKPIECE=MAIN, plus SPINDLE_MODE:MAIN=SPINDLE when the C axis was on (the [workpiece] table first, as D40 says). The reader falls back to the first state in file order when nothing remains, and when two resources of one word would be switched on (M3 for MAIN and TOOL on the Mori Seiki); in the second case it also reports a WARNING that names the others. Alternative: keep the first state in file order, as on main, and leave every other case to a reader rule from a plugin (D40, D66).
Where: machine-config 5 ('Readers map M codes back to names'; also a document fix whatever this decides: the example's DOOR = { OPEN = "M68", CLOSE = "M69", channel = 1 } repeats the codes of SUB_CHUCK in the same listing, and its comment names Biglia); architecture 6 and 7 (the FindFunctionByCode signature); src/Ncx.Config/Templates/TemplateSet.cs FindFunctionByCode (TODO(question)); tests/Ncx.Config.Tests/Templates/TemplateSetTests.cs FindFunctionByCode_CodeOfTwoEntries_IsTheFirstInTheOrderOfMachineConfig5 (it uses the DOOR/SUB_CHUCK pair); P3-01 SourceState (master spindle), P3-02 FanucBuilder.

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, not confirmed by the maintainer: the manuals do not settle this. The manuals confirm that one native code really does carry several states, and they support the mechanism the Recommendation proposes on all three machines the draft names — including the two the draft was least sure of. Nakamura M09 switches the coolant off at high and low pressure together, so "OFF for each channel that was on" is the right reading. On the DMG CTX/GMX, M109 stands twice in the builder's own M list, as "Kühlschmierstoffkreis 1 aus" and "Kühlschmierstoffkreis 2 aus", and its own text says it switches the inner and the outer coolant off — one code, several channels. On the Mori NTX1000 the M-code list gives M03 as spindle 1 alone and M13/M14 as the tool-spindle start, but section 1-23 defines M90 "Simultanbetrieb Spindel 1 / Werkzeugspindel", and the manual's own example writes `M90 S3000;` then `G97 S2000 M03;` annotated as starting spindle 1 at 2000 min-1 *and* the tool spindle at 3000 min-1. So M3 is CW of MAIN always and of TOOL while M90 is active: a modal source state decides which of two states the code writes, exactly the mechanism the Recommendation names, and the file's "verify on the machine" comment is right. The one premise the manuals do not support is the Doosan one.
Evidence: `Nakamura-Tome_Fanuc_Programmierung_Programmierhandbuch-1_4810004ECL-1_DE_2013`, p. 114 (M07 supplies coolant at low pressure where the supply pressure can be switched between HIGH and LOW, M08 at high pressure, and for M09 the manual states that where the supply pressure can be switched between high and low, M09 switches the coolant supply off at high and low pressure together. One OFF code therefore ends several coolant states.); `DMG-MORI_CTX-GMX_Programmierung-M-Funktionsliste-Siemens_DE`, p. 12-13 (Section 2.8.5.2 "Kühlschmierstoff Schlitten 1" lists for circuit 1 (inner, through the tool) M108 minimal-quantity lubrication on, M154/M150/M871 pressure stages 2/3/4, M122 blast air on, then "M109 Kühlschmierstoffkreis 1 aus"; for circuit 2 (outer) M107 pressure stage 1 normal, M156/M152, M127 blast air, then "M109 Kühlschmierstoffkreis 2 aus". Both M109 entries carry the same description: "Die Funktion schaltet den inneren / äußeren Kühlschmierstoff für den Werkzeugwechsler 1 aus." One code, two circuits.); `DMG-MORI_CTX-GMX_Programmierung-M-Funktionsliste-Siemens_DE`, p. 11 (Section 2.8.5.1 "Kühlschmierstoff allgemein": "M9 Alle Kühlschmierstoffe aus — Die Funktion schaltet alle Kühlschmierstoffe aus und die Vorwahlen zurück auf niedrigen Druck." This is the ALL_OFF entry of dmg-ctx-840d.toml, and it ends every coolant state at once.); `Mori-Seiki_NT-NTX-Serie_Programmierung_Programmieranleitung-NTX1000SZM_PX-NT_4-K0DEEN_2011`, p. 243 (The M-code list reads M03 "Spindle 1 start (normal)", M04 "Spindle 1 start (reverse)", M05 "Spindle 1/spindle 2/tool-spindle/rotary tool spindle (turret 2) stop", M13/M14 "Tool-spindle/rotary tool spindle (turret 2) start (normal/reverse)" and M25/M26 tailstock forward/backward. M05 is the code that ends the state of four resources; M13/M14 are each shared by two.); `Mori-Seiki_NT-NTX-Serie_Programmierung_Programmieranleitung-NTX1000SZM_PX-NT_4-K0DEEN_2011`, p. 275-277 (Section 1-23 M90/M91/M290/M291 "Modus für Simultanbetrieb von Spindel 1 / (Angetriebene) Werkzeugspindel EIN/AUS": M90 and M290 are used to rotate the spindle and the tool spindle simultaneously, and the block with M90 must always contain the tool-spindle speed. The worked example on page 277 reads `M90 S3000;` (tool-spindle speed 3000) then `G97 S2000 M03;`, annotated "Starten der Spindel 1 in normaler Richtung mit 2000 min-1 / Starten der Werkzeugspindel in normaler Richtung mit 3000 min-1". Under M90 one M03 starts two spindles.); `Mori-Seiki_NT-NTX-Serie_Programmierung_Programmieranleitung-NT-NTX_DE_2017`, p. 267 (Section 1-8 gives M13 as start (normal) and M14 as start (reverse) of the tool spindle and of the rotary tool spindle of turret 2, with M05 as the stop, and notes that the M05 command is also used to stop spindle 1 or spindle 2.); `Doosan_Puma-2600SY_M-Funktionen_DE`, p. 1-3 (M03 is "SPINDEL VORWÄRTS (DREHSPINDEL M03P11 FRÄSSPINDEL M03P12)", M05 the same with P11/P12 (page 1); M34 "DREHMODUS LINKS" and M35 "C1-ACHSE ANWAHL" (page 2); M134 "DREHMODUS RECHTS" and M135 "C2-ACHSE ANWAHL EIN" (page 3). The P suffix distinguishes the turning from the milling spindle; the list names no code that says which physical spindle the turning P11 drives.); `Doosan_MX-Series_CNC-Programmierbuch_DE`, p. 21 (Section 4.3 "Spindle command by address P-code": M35/M34 = C1-axis ON/OFF, M135/M134 = C2-axis ON/OFF; the P code itself selects the spindle — 11 left spindle, 12 milling spindle, 21 right spindle, 22 revolving spindle — with M03 S1000 P11 / P21 given as "Left Spindle CW / Right Spindle CW". On this Doosan the side is in the P code, not in M34/M134.). (Citations re-paged to the cnc-manuals connector 2026-10-26.)

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

FindFunctionByCode returns every state that writes the code (file order, captured values). The reader drops states its source state rules out (other channel, non-addressed spindle, OFF of a resource not on) and writes every remaining state that does not already hold; a [workpiece] template code also gives the WORKPIECE word first. Fallback: first state in file order when nothing remains, or when two resources would be switched on (plus a WARNING naming the others). Recheck doosan-puma-2600sy.toml: on Doosan the spindle side may be in the P code (MX: P11 left, P21 right), not in M34/M134.
Basis: manual
Source: Nakamura M09 covers several coolant pressures; DMG M109 is "Kreis 1 aus" and "Kreis 2 aus"; Mori NTX M3 also starts the tool spindle under M90 (section 1-23); Doosan MX Programmierbuch p. 21 (P-code spindle select).
Differs from the recommendation: no (adds the Doosan file check)
Confidence: medium
Code impact: Ncx.Config FindFunctionByCode (all matches); reader state filtering in Ncx.Readers.
