#### D156 File names of the shipped cycle catalogs
Question: Machine-config 6 writes `catalog = "heidenhain-cycles.toml"` for the catalog 'shipped with NCXchange', and section 10 lays out `cycles/heidenhain-cycles.toml`. P2-03 ships `cycles/fanuc.toml`, `heidenhain.toml` and `siemens.toml`. The example millturn1.toml (D104) and the three mills in `machines/` write `catalog = "<family>.toml"`. Which name does a machine file write for the shipped catalog?
Recommendation: `<family>.toml`, as shipped and as every machine file already writes it. Machine-config 6 and 10 and the comment in CyclesConfig.cs change to `heidenhain.toml`. A shop's own catalog may have any file name. Only documents change.
Where: machine-config 6 and 10; src/Ncx.Core/Machine/CyclesConfig.cs:9 (comment).

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, not confirmed by the maintainer: the manuals do not settle this. What a shipped NCXchange catalog file is called stays internal to NCXchange, so keep <family>.toml as shipped and as every machine file writes it. The one native precedent in the library does bear on the shape of the answer, though, and the earlier flat "nothing bears on this" was too strong: Siemens ships cov.com with the standard cycles and expects the shop to extend it, while uc.com — also a fixed name — is the file the user creates for their own cycles. So the convention a control actually uses is a single fixed, family-wide name for the shipped catalog, which is what <family>.toml is and what heidenhain-cycles.toml would also be; the precedent favours the shorter shipped name over a second spelling in the documents, but it cannot choose between them.
Evidence: `Siemens_Sinumerik-840D-810D_Programmierhandbuch-Arbeitsvorbereitung_DE_2006`, p. 129, section 2.17 (Added by me. "Mit den Dateien cov.com und uc.com können eigene Zyklen parametriert werden. Die Datei cov.com wird mit den Standardzyklen geliefert und ist entsprechend zu erweitern. Die Datei uc.com ist vom Anwender selbst zu erstellen." Both are fixed names loaded into the Anwenderzyklen directory; cov.com is the overview of the cycles, uc.com the call description). (Citations re-paged to the cnc-manuals connector 2026-10-26.)

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

`<family>.toml` (fanuc.toml, heidenhain.toml, siemens.toml), as shipped; machine-config 6 and 10 and the CyclesConfig.cs comment change to `heidenhain.toml`. A shop catalog may have any name.
Basis: logical
Source: Internal naming; matches what every machine file already writes. Siemens' fixed shipped name cov.com is the only precedent and favours one short fixed name.
Differs from the recommendation: no
Confidence: high
Code impact: none (one comment).

#### D157 Words a family rule carries instead of a native parameter
Question: In controller-mapping 5, several cycle words come from a rule of the reader and compiler instead of a native parameter. On Fanuc these are SURFACE ('R minus TOML clearance or 0'), SAFE (the G98 initial level), CYCLE_RETRACT (G98/G99) and the PITCH of G84 (F/S). On Heidenhain, CYCLE_RETRACT is 'with or without Q204' (controller-mapping 5; heidenhain 8 rule 7: 'CYCLE_RETRACT=SAFE becomes Q204'). On Siemens the cycle 'always returns to RTP'. AXIS is a rule wherever no _AXN carries it. machine-config 6 has no key for these words, so the code names them in DrillingFamily (CycleEntry.RuleWords) for the built-in family only. A catalog entry of a built-in name keeps them through CycleEntry.OverriddenBy, and the P2-03 test 'G81, CYCLE81 and CYCL DEF 200 map the same NCX words' passes only through them. An entry of a name of its own gets none: a Heidenhain RECT_POCKET with Q204, or a cycle that a machine file adds. Do the rules apply to catalog entries, and how does an entry say so?
Recommendation: The rule words follow from the entry's params, with no new key: one sentence per family under the table of controller-mapping 5. Fanuc: an entry that maps CLEARANCE = "R" carries SURFACE, SAFE and CYCLE_RETRACT, and the tapping entry (TAP on G84) also carries PITCH. Heidenhain: an entry that maps SAFE = "Q204" carries CYCLE_RETRACT. Siemens: an entry that maps SAFE = "RTP" carries CYCLE_RETRACT. Every family: AXIS, unless params maps it. CycleEntry.RuleWords is then computed for every entry, the built-in family included, which makes the built-in family 'defined in the same way' (machine-config 6). Alternative: a 'rule_words' list key in machine-config 6, set by the file. It could claim a rule the family's code does not have.
Where: controller-mapping 5; machine-config 6; src/Ncx.Core/Machine/CycleEntry.cs (RuleWords, OverriddenBy); `DrillingFamily.*.cs`; header comments of `cycles/*.toml`; tests/Ncx.Config.Tests/Cycles/ShippedCatalogsTests.cs.

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, not confirmed by the maintainer: the manuals do not settle this. The Fanuc rules are confirmed: G98 returns to the initial level and G99 to the R plane, the block carries only X Y Z R Q P F K so there is no workpiece-surface word, and the tapping pitch is feed divided by spindle speed in feed-per-minute mode and equal to the feed in feed-per-revolution mode — write the rule with the feed mode, as the controller-mapping 5 TAP row already does, not as the bare F/S of this draft. Siemens is confirmed too: CYCLE81 ends with "Rückzug auf die Rückzugsebene mit G0", so the cycle always returns to RTP. The Heidenhain rule as written is wrong: Q204 is a fixed position of every CYCL DEF 200/201/203 block, so "with or without Q204" distinguishes nothing; the TNC 640 states on each of the drilling cycles that the 2nd clearance takes effect only when it is programmed larger than Q200, so the rule is CYCLE_RETRACT=SAFE when SAFE > CLEARANCE (Q204 > Q200) and CLEARANCE otherwise. Deriving the rule words from params is safe for SURFACE, SAFE and CYCLE_RETRACT, but AXIS is not as clean as the draft assumes — the cited page says the axis address in the G73..G89 block decides which base or parallel axis is used, and bit 0 (FXY) of parameter 5101 can make Z the drilling axis always.
Evidence: `Fanuc_30i-B_Bedienung-Fraesen_B-64484EN-2_EN`, p. 56-58, general canned-cycle explanation (Verified with a qualification. Abb. 5.1 (a) shows the six steps from the initial level over the R plane and back; G98 returns to the initial level, G99 to the R plane. Table 5.1 (b) fixes the positioning plane and drilling axis from G17/G18/G19, but the text adds that the axis address in the block selects the base or parallel axis and only "Ist keine Achsenadresse für die Bohrachse spezifiziert, wird die Grundachse als Bohrachse verwendet"; the note on p. 64 says bit 0 (FXY) of parameter 5101 can force Z as the drilling axis always); `Fanuc_30i-B_Bedienung-Fraesen_B-64484EN-2_EN`, p. 103, 5.3.1 rigid tapping (Verified verbatim. "Im Modus 'Vorschub pro Minute' ergibt sich die Gewindesteigung aus dem Ausdruck Vorschubgeschwindigkeit ÷ Spindeldrehzahl. Im Modus 'Vorschub pro Umdrehung' ist die Gewindesteigung gleich der Vorschubgeschwindigkeit."); `Heidenhain_TNC640_Zyklen_892905-18_NC-SW-34059x-10_DE_2019`, p. 87 (cycle 200) and 96, 97, 98 (cycle 203) — the original citation gave 96 and 98 only (Verified and widened. The sentence "Der 2. SICHERHEITS-ABST. Q204 wirkt erst, wenn dieser größer programmiert ist als der SICHERHEITS-ABST. Q200" closes the last step of cycle 200 (p. 87) and of all three cycle-203 behaviours (pp. 96, 97, 98), so the rule is general across the drilling cycles, not particular to 203); `Heidenhain_iTNC530_Zyklen_670_388-12_NC-SW-340490-07_DE_2011`, p. 79-80 (cycle 200), 89-90 (cycle 203) (Verified. Q204 is one of the fixed parameters the control writes into every CYCL DEF 200/203 block, and the sequence says the tool retracts to the clearance or, "falls eingegeben", to the 2nd clearance. The older manual does not state the Q204 > Q200 condition); `Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl-828D_Bedienhandbuch-Fraesen_DE_2013`, p. 304 (CYCLE81, Ablauf) (Verified verbatim. The cycle approaches the reference plane advanced by the safety distance with G0, drills at the programmed feed (G1) and then "Rückzug auf die Rückzugsebene mit G0" — there is no choice of return level). (Citations re-paged to the cnc-manuals connector 2026-10-26.)

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

Follow the recommendation: the rule words follow from the entry's params, with no new key, and CycleEntry.RuleWords is computed for every entry. Corrected rules for controller-mapping 5: - Fanuc: an entry that maps CLEARANCE="R" carries SURFACE, SAFE and CYCLE_RETRACT (G98 = SAFE at the initial level, G99 = CLEARANCE). TAP carries PITCH = F/S under G94 and F under G95. - Heidenhain: an entry that maps SAFE="Q204" carries CYCLE_RETRACT = SAFE when Q204 > Q200, otherwise CLEARANCE. The compiler writes Q204=0 for CLEARANCE. For SAFE at or below the clearance height, it reports a CMP WARNING because the control would retract only to Q200. - Siemens: an entry that maps SAFE="RTP" carries CYCLE_RETRACT=SAFE always. - AXIS: Z under G17. Outside G17, the Fanuc drilling axis depends on parameter 5101#0 FXY (0 = always Z, 1 = by plane and axis address). The Fanuc reader then derives AXIS from the plane but adds a WARNING naming 5101#0.
Basis: manual
Source: Fanuc B-64484EN-2 p. 56-58, 64, 103; Fanuc 30i-B Parameter Manual B-64490EN-05 p. 282 (5101#0 FXY: 0 always Z, 1 axis selected by program); TNC 640 Zyklen 892905-18 p. 87, 96-98; Siemens Bedienhandbuch Fräsen 2013 p. 304.
Differs from the recommendation: yes: the Heidenhain rule compares Q204 with Q200 instead of "with or without Q204", PITCH depends on the feed mode, and AXIS outside G17 gets a WARNING.
Confidence: high
Code impact: DrillingFamily.*.cs and CycleEntry.RuleWords (computed for all entries); Heidenhain/Fanuc readers and compilers (P3/P5).

#### D158 Fanuc SURFACE from R: a clearance key
Question: Controller-mapping 5 (row DEPTH, CLEARANCE, SURFACE, SAFE) reads the Fanuc SURFACE as "R minus TOML clearance or 0", and per the status line of controller-mapping "TOML" means a value of the machine configuration. Machine-config names no such key: [cycles] has only `catalog` (machine-config 6), and CyclesConfig.cs holds only that. A Fanuc cycle block has no surface address, so without the key the reader can only write SURFACE=0. PATTERN_LOOP.ncx needs exactly that: note 2 says the Fanuc reader gives the same file, with G81 R2. read as SURFACE=0 CLEARANCE=2. So does BOHREN, where R5. matches Q203=0 Q200=5. The two files use R distances of 2 and 5, so no single clearance value fits both.
Recommendation: Add the optional key `[cycles] surface_clearance`, which controller-mapping 5 already assumes. The Fanuc reader writes SURFACE = R - surface_clearance, and SURFACE=0 when the key is absent. fanuc-mill-30i.toml leaves the key out, so that BOHREN and PATTERN_LOOP read as their expected files. The key affects reading only; the Fanuc compiler has no surface address and writes R from CLEARANCE. For an NC programmer the value is a per-machine guess. CAM sets the R distance per operation, so the SURFACE the key gives is right only for programs that use that distance. The motion is the same either way, because the Heidenhain compiler writes a Q203 and Q200 that reach the same R. Alternative: no key; controller-mapping 5 reads "surface = 0" on Fanuc.
Where: machine-config 6 ([cycles]); controller-mapping 5 (SURFACE row); src/Ncx.Core/Machine/CyclesConfig.cs and `src/Ncx.Config/MachineConfigLoader*.cs`; cycles/fanuc.toml lines 14-15 (TODO(question)); the rule-word comment in src/Ncx.Core/Machine/DrillingFamily.Fanuc.cs; P3-02 FanucCycles.

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, not confirmed by the maintainer: the manuals do not settle this. The manuals confirm the premise and leave the key itself to the maintainer. A Fanuc canned cycle knows only three levels — Ausgangsebene, R-Ebene and the hole bottom — and its block has no address for the workpiece surface: G82 X Y Z R P F K, with R the R plane and Z the bottom, absolute coordinates under G90 and the two distances under G91. Heidenhain splits the same geometry into two values, Q203 "Koord. Werkstück-Oberfläche" (absolute) and Q200 "Sicherheits-Abstand" (incremental, tool tip to workpiece surface), so the Fanuc R is Q203 + Q200 and the split back cannot be recovered from a Fanuc block — which also bears out the note that the motion is the same either way, since only the sum reaches the machine. Whether the reader guesses the split per machine with `[cycles] surface_clearance` or always writes SURFACE=0 is an NCX choice no manual settles.
Evidence: `Fanuc_30i-B_Bedienung-Fraesen_B-64484EN-2_EN`, p. 66-67 (§5.1.5 G82) (The format of the drilling/counterboring cycle is G82 X_ Y_ Z_ R_ P_ F_ K_, where X Y is the hole position, Z the distance from point R to the hole bottom, R the distance between the initial level and the R plane, P the dwell at the bottom, F the feed and K the repeat count. There is no address for a workpiece surface); `Fanuc_30i-B_Bedienung-Fraesen_B-64484EN-2_EN`, p. 56-58 (§5.1) (A canned cycle is six operations between three levels only — positioning in X and Y, rapid to the R plane, drilling, an action at the bottom, retract to the R plane, rapid to the initial point. The paragraph on the drilling axis under G90/G91 shows R and Z as absolute coordinates in absolute mode and as the two distances in incremental mode, and G98/G99 choose the return level); `Heidenhain_TNC640_Zyklen_892905-18_NC-SW-34059x-10_DE_2019`, p. 89 (Zyklus 200 BOHREN, Zyklusparameter) (Cycle 200 carries the two values separately: Q200 is the incremental safety clearance, the distance from tool tip to workpiece surface, entered positive, and Q203 is the absolute coordinate of the workpiece surface; Q201 is the depth measured from that surface). (Citations re-paged to the cnc-manuals connector 2026-10-26.)

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

Add optional `[cycles] surface_clearance`. The Fanuc reader writes SURFACE = R - surface_clearance, SURFACE=0 when absent; fanuc-mill-30i.toml omits it. Reading only; the Fanuc compiler writes R from CLEARANCE.
Basis: manual
Source: Fanuc canned cycles know only initial level, R plane and bottom (B-64484EN-2 G82 format); Heidenhain splits R into Q203 + Q200, so the split is unrecoverable and only the sum moves the machine.
Differs from the recommendation: no
Confidence: high
Code impact: Ncx.Config CyclesConfig (new key); Fanuc reader SURFACE computation.

#### D159 Unit of the Fanuc G4 P
Question: Controller-mapping 1 (DWELL) gives Fanuc G4 P as "ms or s per TOML", and G4 X/G4 U as seconds on lathes; fanuc 4 says "milliseconds or seconds by parameter". Machine-config 1 and 2 name no key for the unit. So the Fanuc reader cannot convert G4 P1 on a control set to seconds, and the compiler cannot know which P to write. The P of a cycle block is a separate case: fanuc 6 gives it in milliseconds without a parameter ("G82 adds a dwell P (milliseconds)"). DWELL and CYCLE_DWELL are seconds (language 4.1, 4.7), and lines 19-20 of cycles/fanuc.toml take the cycle P as milliseconds.
Recommendation: Add `[machine] dwell_p = "ms" | "s"` for Fanuc, default "ms": the unit of G4 P for reading and writing. G4 X and G4 U stay seconds. The P of a cycle block stays milliseconds, as fanuc 6 says. If the Fanuc manual shows that the same parameter also switches the cycle P, the key covers it too and fanuc 6 says so. Alternative: no key. Controller-mapping 1 and fanuc 4 read "G4 P in milliseconds", and the compiler writes the dwell as G4 X in seconds, which does not depend on the parameter. Fanuc 4 names G4 X for lathes only, so the maintainer confirms it for the machining centers.
Where: machine-config 1 ([machine]); controller-mapping 1 (DWELL); fanuc 4 (G4) and 6; src/Ncx.Core/Machine/MachineIdentity.cs and src/Ncx.Config/MachineConfigLoader.Identity.cs; cycles/fanuc.toml lines 19-20; P3-02 and P3-06.

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, corrected 2026-10-26 after the manual audit, not confirmed by the maintainer: On the 30i-B, G4 P takes no decimal point and counts least input increments of time, so the key cannot be `"ms" | "s"`: with the usual IS-B one P unit is 0.001 s (P1000 = 1 s), with IS-A 0.01 s, IS-C 0.0001 s, IS-D 0.00001 s and IS-E 0.000001 s, and bit 7 (DWT) of parameter 1015 fixes it at 1 ms independently of the increment system. In feed-per-revolution mode bit 1 (DWL) of parameter 3405 can make the dwell count spindle revolutions instead. If a key is kept it should carry that time increment (a factor, default 0.001 s). The alternative, writing the dwell as G4 X in seconds, is safe only with a decimal point: X and U written without one count the same increments as P (at IS-B `G4 X1` is 0.001 s), so the compiler always writes X or U with a decimal point. `G04 X_` is the documented machining-centre form too, not lathe-only. The two corpus machines take P in plain milliseconds (Mori Seiki NTX: P in units of 0.001 s, P1500 = 1.5 s; Nakamura: P0-P9999999 = 0-9999.999 s, no decimal point), but a builder can differ: the Mori Seiki NL series accepts P with a decimal point, P1.0 being 1 s and P1 0.001 s. Whether the P of a canned cycle follows the same increment system and DWT is not found; the only example (G82 ... P1000 = 1 s) is at IS-B. The proposal still disagrees with the Recommendation's `"ms" | "s"` key.
Evidence: FANUC Series 30i/31i/32i-B Operator's Manual (B-64484EN), p. 188 (§5.6 Dwell: the M format is G04 X_ or G04 P_, the T format adds U; X and U take a decimal point, P does not. Table 5.6 (b) gives the P unit per increment system, from 0.01 s (IS-A) to 0.000001 s (IS-E); bit 7 (DWT) of parameter 1015 fixes the P unit at 0.001 s; Note 1: X, U or P without a decimal point follow the increment system of the X axis or of the reference axis); FANUC 30i-B Parameter Manual (B-64490EN-05), p. 59 (1015#7 DWT: P in the increment system, or 1 ms) and p. 195 (3405#1 DWL: always dwell per second, or per revolution under G95); FANUC 30i-B Operator's Manual Milling (B-64484EN-2), p. 68 (G82 example with P1000, a dwell of 1 s at the hole bottom); Mori Seiki NT/NTX-Serie Programmieranleitung NTX1000 SZM (PX-NT_4-K0DEEN), p. 106 (§2-9 G04: X and U in seconds with a decimal point, X1 = 0.001 s; P in units of 0.001 s without a decimal point, P1500 = 1.5 s); Nakamura-Tome Programmierhandbuch 1 (4810004ECL-1), p. 54 (§4-6 Verweilzeit: U and X 0 to 9999.999 s, P0-P9999999 for the same range, P without a decimal point); Mori Seiki NL-Serie Programmierhandbuch (PX-NL-A0DEEN, 2007), p. 75 (§1-8 G04: the dwell is given in seconds with a decimal point; X1.0, U1.0 and P1.0 are 1 s, X1, U1 and P1 are 0.001 s).
Corrected: added from Note 1 of the same page that X and U without a decimal point also count increments, so the compiler writes them with one, and added the Mori NL page on which P takes a decimal point, so "P is never seconds as written" holds for the 30i-B manual and the corpus machines, not for every builder. The German citations are replaced by the English editions the connector holds.

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

No `"ms"|"s"` key. Instead, add `[machine] dwell_increment` (seconds per unit of G4 P, default 0.001). It also applies to G4 X/U written without a decimal point and to the P of canned cycles (until a manual shows otherwise). Reader: G4 X/U with a decimal point is seconds. P, and X/U without a decimal point, are multiplied by dwell_increment. Compiler: always writes the dwell as G4 X<seconds> with a decimal point (documented for both mill and lathe formats), which is independent of the increment system and of 1015#7. A cycle P is written as round(seconds / dwell_increment), an integer. Parameter 3405#1 DWL (dwell in revolutions under G95) is not modelled. machine-config 1 notes that NCX assumes DWL=0.
Basis: manual + logical
Source: Fanuc B-64484EN p. 188 §5.6 and Note 1; Parameter Manual B-64490EN-05 p. 59 (1015#7 DWT), p. 195 (3405#1 DWL); Mori NTX p. 106, Nakamura p. 54, Mori NL p. 75. CAM posts emit P as integer milliseconds and G82 when a dwell is set (https://www.emastercam.com/forums/topic/11380-backplot-cycle-time-calculation/, https://www.mcadcentral.com/threads/dwell-format-in-canned-cycles.19887/). Logical: G4 X with a decimal point is the one form whose unit no parameter changes.
Differs from the recommendation: yes: the key is a time increment rather than ms/s, the compiler writes G4 X with a decimal point, and the key also covers cycle P.
Confidence: medium
Code impact: MachineIdentity/MachineConfigLoader.Identity (`dwell_increment`); Fanuc reader and compiler (P3-02, P3-06); fanuc 4 and 6 docs.

#### D162 Catalog cycle names beyond the documents
Question: The documents name catalog cycles only as examples: RECT_POCKET (machine-config 6), and TURN_OD, ROUGH_TURN, ROUGH_FACE, FINISH, GROOVE and THREAD (language 4.7.1). The phase file (12-phase-2 P2-03) added TURN_ID, FACE and COMPOUND_THREAD. P2-03a named the rest: BACK_BORE 204, UNIVERSAL_PECK 205, TAP_COMPENSATING (206 and CYCLE840), BORE_MILL 208, TAP_CHIP_BREAK 209, CENTERING 240, SINGLE_LIP_DRILL 241, DEEP_HOLE CYCLE830, CIRC_POCKET 252, SLOT 253, CIRC_SLOT 254, RECT_STUD 256, CIRC_STUD 257. Programs write these names ('A program may use any catalog name', 4.7.1). A name that two catalogs share converts a cycle between families only if both entries carry the same words. One shipped name already disagrees with the language: THREAD, which D161 settles. Are the other names accepted, and is 241 the same NCX cycle as CYCLE830?
Recommendation: Accept the names. List every shipped catalog name once in cycles/README.md (name, meaning, native per family), with the rule that one name means one cycle with one word set in every catalog. THREAD and the name of G92 follow D161. Keep SINGLE_LIP_DRILL and DEEP_HOLE apart until the parameter lists (D178, D181) show the same words; joining them later is a rename by decision. The two TAP_COMPENSATING entries differ today: Heidenhain 206 maps neither PITCH nor CYCLE_F, while Siemens CYCLE840 maps PITCH. They must be aligned from the same facts. Alternative for the deep hole: DEEP_HOLE for both 241 and CYCLE830 now.
Where: cycles/README.md (or machine-config 6); language 4.7.1; 12-phase-2-configuration.md P2-03; cycles/heidenhain.toml; cycles/siemens.toml; for THREAD, D161.

ANSWER: (Peter, 2026-10-07, drafted by Claude in project_spike) Accept as recommended: every shipped catalog name once in cycles/README.md, one name one cycle with one word set in every catalog, THREAD and G92 per D161, SINGLE_LIP_DRILL and DEEP_HOLE kept apart for now, and the two TAP_COMPENSATING entries aligned from the same manual facts.
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, not confirmed by the maintainer: the manuals do not settle this. The shipped names are faithful to the controls: 204 is RUECKWAERTS-SENKEN, 205 UNIVERSAL-TIEFBOHREN, 206/207/209 the three GEWINDEBOHREN variants, 208 BOHRFRAESEN, 240 ZENTRIEREN, 241 EINLIPPEN-TIEFBOHREN, 251-257 the pockets, slots and studs, and the Siemens counterparts POCKET3/POCKET4 and CYCLE76/CYCLE77 carry the same meanings. On the deep hole: 241 and CYCLE830 are the same cycle in substance — both add entry/exit spindle direction and speed, a separate drilling speed, coolant-on and coolant-off M functions and a pilot or recessed start to a plain peck — so DEEP_HOLE for both is defensible, while 205 pairs with CYCLE83 (Tieflochbohren 1), not CYCLE830 (Tieflochbohren 2). Two warnings before the list is frozen. CYCLE830 is a strict superset: its VARI also chooses 'in one cut', chip-break, peck or both, plus soft entry and break-through, and it has a pilot bore S_ZP that cycle 241 has no counterpart for. And SLOT would not mean one cycle in both families: Heidenhain 253 NUTENFRAESEN is a single slot, whereas the Siemens SLOT1 is 'Nuten auf einem Kreis', a pattern of slots on a pitch circle, and SLOT2 'Kreisnut' is the circular slot that answers 254; Siemens has no cycle for a single slot at the current position. Also align the two TAP_COMPENSATING entries from the facts: cycle 206 does have a feed word (Q206), and CYCLE840 takes the pitch only in its encoder or ENC=11 forms.
Evidence: HEIDENHAIN TNC 640 Benutzerhandbuch Zyklenprogrammierung, NC-SW 34059x-10, 10/2019, p. contents, 87-125, 133-141 and 173-206 (The cycle titles are 200 BOHREN, 201 REIBEN, 202 AUSDREHEN, 203 UNIVERSAL-BOHREN, 204 RUECKWAERTS-SENKEN, 205 UNIVERSAL-TIEFBOHREN, 208 BOHRFRAESEN, 241 EINLIPPEN-TIEFBOHREN, 240 ZENTRIEREN, 206 GEWINDEBOHREN mit Ausgleichsfutter, 207 GEWINDEBOHREN ohne Ausgleichsfutter GS, 209 GEWINDEBOHREN SPANBRUCH, and 251 RECHTECKTASCHE, 252 KREISTASCHE, 253 NUTENFRAESEN, 254 RUNDE NUT, 256 RECHTECKZAPFEN, 257 KREISZAPFEN, 258 VIELECKZAPFEN.); HEIDENHAIN TNC 640 Benutzerhandbuch Zyklenprogrammierung, NC-SW 34059x-10, 10/2019, p. 119-120 (Cycle 241 carries Q426 spindle direction on entry and exit (3/4/5), Q427 speed on entry and exit, Q428 drilling speed, Q429 and Q430 the M function that switches coolant on and off, Q379 a recessed start point, Q202 max infeed, Q212 decrement, Q205 min infeed, Q211 dwell at the bottom, Q435/Q401 a dwell depth with feed reduction, and Q208 retract feed.); SINUMERIK 840D sl NC-Programmierung, Programmierhandbuch 06/2019 (CNC-SW 4.92), p. 1119-1122 (CYCLE830 'Tieflochbohren 2' has the matching set: S_SDAC2 spindle direction on approach (3/4/5), S_SV2 approach speed, _SDAC and _SV1 direction and speed while drilling, S_SDAC3 and S_SV3 on retract, S_FB drilling feed, S_ZP pilot bore, S_FR retract feed, and S_CON / S_COFF coolant on and off as an M command or subprogram call. Its VARI ones digit offers 0 in one cut, 1 chip-break, 2 peck, 3 both; further digits give soft entry (Hunderter) and break-through (Tausender).); SINUMERIK 840D sl/840D/840Di sl Zyklen, Programmierhandbuch 01/2008, p. 8 (contents ch. 3), 111-179 (The Siemens milling cycles are LONGHOLE 'Langlöcher auf einem Kreis' (p.111), SLOT1 'Nuten auf einem Kreis' (p.117), SLOT2 'Kreisnut' (p.125), POCKET1/POCKET3 rectangular pocket (p.132, 142), POCKET2/POCKET4 circular pocket (p.137, 150), CYCLE76 rectangular stud (p.173), CYCLE77 circular stud (p.179) — so the two slot cycles are a pitch-circle pattern and a circular slot, not a single slot at the current position.); HEIDENHAIN TNC 640 Benutzerhandbuch Zyklenprogrammierung, NC-SW 34059x-10, 10/2019, p. 134-135 (Cycle 206 (tapping with a compensating chuck) has no pitch parameter; p.134 states the control computes the pitch from the programmed spindle speed and the feed defined in the cycle, and p.135 prints the rule F = S x p beside the parameter Q206 'Vorschub Tiefenzustellung'. So the cycle does have a feed word, contrary to the shipped entry.); SINUMERIK 840D sl/840D/840Di sl Zyklen, Programmierhandbuch 01/2008, p. 66, 69 (CYCLE840 covers both forms through ENC: 1 = no encoder, feed programmed before the cycle (the pitch then follows from F and S), 11 = no encoder with the pitch entered in MPIT or PIT and the feed computed in the cycle, 0 / 20 = with encoder, where the cycle likewise derives the feed from spindle speed and pitch. So TAP_COMPENSATING needs a feed word on both families and a pitch word only Siemens can take.).

#### D164 Values for Q parameters that no NCX word carries
Question: machine-config 6 'signature' lists every native parameter 'also those without an NCX word', and heidenhain 8 rule 7 writes the Q parameters in the control's order. No document gives the value for a position that neither params nor fixed fills. For Siemens the position simply stays empty (machine-config 6, siemens 7). The cases are Q202 and Q210 of 200; Q210, Q212, Q205, Q208 and Q256 of 203; and Q208 of 201. Q213 is D163. BOHREN.h writes Q202=|Q201|, Q210=0, Q212=0, Q205=Q202, Q208=MAX, Q256=0,6, and Q208=Q206 on 201. P3-04 requires the compiled BOHREN.ncx to be equivalent to BOHREN.h.
Recommendation: Add an optional key 'defaults' to machine-config 6. It maps a native name to the value the compiler writes at a signature position that no NCX word and no fixed value fills: a number, or the control's literal such as MAX. The shipped heidenhain.toml takes BOHREN.h's values: Q210=0, Q212=0, Q208=MAX on 203, Q256=0.6. Three values depend on the block and become compiler rules in heidenhain 8 rule 7, all as BOHREN.h writes them. Q202 of 200 is the full depth (one infeed; a source Q202 of at least the depth reads as one infeed). Q205 of 203 equals Q202. Q208 of 201 equals Q206. The reader takes the named entry only when the unmapped source values equal what the compiler would write. It does not compare a value the cycle does not use in that form: Q256 when Q213=0, Q205 when Q212=0. So CAM output that differs only there still converts. Otherwise the reader keeps the cycle natively as CYCLE:HEIDENHAIN=n (D94), as D5 requires. On Siemens the key records the control's own default of a position, which the reader assumes for an empty position (VARI; see D181). The Siemens compiler still leaves that position empty, as machine-config 6 and siemens 7 say. Alternative: the reader drops differing values with a WARNING. That conversion is more lenient, but it needs an exception to D5.
Where: machine-config 6 (new key); heidenhain.md 7 rule 7, 8 rule 7; cycles/heidenhain.toml (header TODO); src/Ncx.Core/Machine/CycleEntry.cs; src/Ncx.Config/Cycles/CycleCatalogLoader.Entries.cs (s_entryKeys); P3-04, P3-05.

ANSWER: (Peter, 2026-10-07, drafted by Claude in project_spike) Accept as recommended, with one change: Q256 is not a `defaults` entry. It is the chip-break lift the control holds, and D358 makes the machine key of D357 (`[cycles] chip_break_lift`) its one source, so the compiler writes Q256 from that key. The other values (Q210=0, Q212=0, Q208=MAX on 203) and the three block rules stay as recommended. Answer together with D190.
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, not confirmed by the maintainer: The manuals give a value, or a provably inert value, for every position in question, so the defaults key can be filled from them rather than from BOHREN.h. Q210 and Q212 are the off values of their own functions (no dwell above, no degression), Q211=0 no dwell below; Q202 of cycle 200 as the full depth is right because the control drills in one pass when the infeed equals or exceeds the depth, which the manual states outright; and Q205 needs no compiler rule at all, since it limits the infeed only when a degression Q212 is programmed, so with Q212=0 any value is inert. Q208 is where the recommendation must change: Q208=0 is not "no value" but "retract with Q206", so on cycle 201 Q208=0 and Q208=Q206 are the same program and the reader must accept both (BOHREN.h writes 420 = Q206, ordinary CAM writes 0), while on 203 MAX is the right default because it makes the Heidenhain cycle retract in rapid like the Fanuc G83/G73 it comes from. Q256 has no neutral value (iTNC input range starts at 0.1), so a catalog default such as 0.6 is the only way to fill it; the control's own way is a GLOBAL DEF BOHREN block with PREDEF, which NCX would have to emit — and Siemens' uc.com shows the same idea as an explicit per-parameter Vorbelegungswert in the catalog file itself, which is the closest native precedent the library holds for the proposed defaults key.
Evidence: HEIDENHAIN iTNC 530 Benutzer-Handbuch Zyklenprogrammierung (NC-SW 340490-07, 2011), p. 80 (cycle 200) and 89 (cycle 203) (Verified with a qualification. P. 80: "Die TNC fährt in einem Arbeitsgang auf die Tiefe wenn: Zustell-Tiefe und Tiefe gleich sind / die Zustell-Tiefe größer als die Tiefe ist" — unconditional for cycle 200. P. 89 states the same for cycle 203 but adds "und gleichzeitig kein Spanbruch definiert ist". Q210 is the dwell at the clearance after the tool has been pulled out for chip removal, range 0 to 3600; Q212 is the amount by which the infeed is reduced after each infeed, range from 0); HEIDENHAIN iTNC 530 Benutzer-Handbuch Zyklenprogrammierung (NC-SW 340490-07, 2011), p. 82 (cycle 201) and 90 (cycle 203) (Verified verbatim. Cycle 201: "Wenn Sie Q208 = 0 eingeben, dann gilt Vorschub Reiben." Cycle 203: "Wenn Sie Q208=0 eingeben, dann fährt die TNC das Werkzeug mit Vorschub Q206 heraus. Eingabebereich 0 bis 99999,999 alternativ FMAX, FAUTO, PREDEF." Q205: "Falls Sie einen Abnahmebetrag eingegeben haben, begrenzt die TNC die Zustellung auf den mit Q205 eingegeben Wert." Q256 range 0,1000 to 99999,9999); HEIDENHAIN TNC 640 Benutzerhandbuch Zyklenprogrammierung (NC-SW 34059x-10, 10/2019), p. 101 (cycle 203 parameters) (Added by me, to carry the caveat the answer asserted without a citation. The current control repeats "Wenn Sie Q208=0 eingeben, dann fährt die Steuerung das Werkzeug mit Vorschub Q206 heraus", and gives Q256 the input range 0,000 to 99999,999 — wider at the bottom than the iTNC 530's 0,1); HEIDENHAIN iTNC 530 Benutzer-Handbuch Zyklenprogrammierung (NC-SW 340490-07, 2011), p. 57-59 (2.2 Programmvorgaben für Zyklen, GLOBAL DEF) (Verified exactly. GLOBAL DEF defines cycle parameters centrally at the start of the program and the control writes the word PREDEF into the cycle definition as the link. "Globale Daten für Bohrbearbeitungen" is exactly Rückzug Spanbruch, Verweilzeit unten and Verweilzeit oben, and applies to cycles 200 to 209, 240 and 262 to 267. A fixed value entered in a cycle is not changed by GLOBAL DEF); FANUC Series 30i/31i/32i-MODEL B Bedienungshandbuch Fräsen (B-64484GE-2/02), p. PDF 66 (printed 50), G73 (Verified. "Der Abstand d wird in Parameter 5114 festgelegt. Das Werkzeug wird im Eilgang zurückgezogen." The retract is in rapid and its amount is a machine parameter, not a program word — the reason a Heidenhain Q208 of MAX, not a feed, reproduces the Fanuc cycle, and the reason the chip-break retract has no NCX word); SINUMERIK 840D sl / 840D / 840Di sl Zyklen, Programmierhandbuch 01/2008, p. 45, 51 and 62 (Verified verbatim, including the sentence the answer paraphrased: p. 62 "Der jeweils nicht benötigte Parameter wird im Aufruf weggelassen bzw. erhält den Wert Null." P. 45 shows the empty position (N60 CYCLE81 (110, 102, , 35)). P. 51: _VRT = 0 means a retract of 1 mm, _DTD = 0 means the value of DTB, _DIS1 = 0 means automatic calculation, DAM = 0 means no degression); SINUMERIK 840D/810D Arbeitsvorbereitung, Programmierhandbuch 11/2006, p. PDF 130-131 (printed 2-40 to 2-41), uc.com (Added by me. The user-cycle description file carries a Vorbelegungswert per parameter — "Wert, der bei Aufruf des Zyklus in der entsprechenden Maske vorbesetzt ist" — in the same line as the type and the range, and it may be omitted. That is a native cycle-catalog file with exactly the defaults key D164 proposes).

### Sixth round: later

#### D166 What a column is in the canonical layout
Question: Language 5 rule 7 and D92 put the semicolon of a trailing comment in column 57, or three spaces after words that reach column 54, but do not define a column. Language 3 allows UTF-8, and strings of any characters (NAME, COMMENT, RAW text), so the count matters for a block whose string words hold non-ASCII text before a comment. NcxWriter.WriteBlock and the lexer's "at column n" PAR messages count UTF-16 units of the .NET string. These differ from Unicode code points only for characters outside the Basic Multilingual Plane (emoji), and from display cells also for combining marks and wide East Asian characters. The five examples are pure ASCII (checked), so none of them is affected.
Recommendation: A column is one Unicode code point of the line, the first being column 1. The writer and the lexer count with string.EnumerateRunes. The definition does not depend on .NET's string encoding, so a CAM postprocessor written in another language produces the same text (language 2 rule 7). It also equals today's count for every character NC programs use (umlauts, Ø, °), so no realistic program changes. The writer changes by one line (it counts the runes of the words instead of the string length); the lexer converts the string indices it reports into code-point columns. Alternative: keep UTF-16 units as coded (identical for all BMP text) and write that into rule 7. Display width is not recommended, because it depends on the font and the terminal.
Where: language 5 rule 7 (one sentence); src/Ncx.Core/Writing/NcxWriter.cs WriteBlock (TODO(question)); src/Ncx.Core/Parsing/Lexer.cs and WordLexer.cs (columns in PAR messages).

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, not confirmed by the maintainer: the manuals do not settle this. No manual defines a comment column, so the definition stays the maintainer's, but the manuals show that the distinction the draft worries about cannot arise in anything the compilers write. Siemens lists the characters available for NC programs as A-Z, a-z, 0-9 and a fixed table of special characters, and adds that non-displayable special characters are treated as blanks; a block may hold at most 512 characters including the comment. Heidenhain restricts drive, directory and file names to letters, digits, minus, dot and underscore, and lists Unicode support in cycle texts as a recent addition. Counting code points, UTF-16 units or display cells therefore differs only inside NCX's own NAME, COMMENT and RAW strings, never in output a control will accept — and a compiler that passes a non-ASCII COMMENT through to a Siemens program is on thin ice regardless of how the column is counted. Caveats: This is corroboration of the draft's own remark that no realistic program is affected, not an answer to which of the three definitions rule 7 should name. Siemens' character list is for the NC program as a whole; I did not find a statement that a comment may not contain other characters, and no manual in the library uses the notion of a column at all (searched Siemens and Heidenhain for comment-length and column rules).
Evidence: `Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl_Programmierhandbuch-NC-Programmierung_SW492_DE_2019`, p. 55-56 (Section 2.3.2 'Verfügbare Zeichen' lists everything an NC program may contain: capitals A-Z (O parenthesised), lower case a-z, digits, and a table of special characters (%, round and square brackets, <, >, :, =, /, *, +, -, double quote, apostrophe, $, underscore, dot, comma, semicolon, ampersand, LF, tab, blank, with ? and ! marked reserved). A note adds 'Nicht darstellbare Sonderzeichen werden wie Leerzeichen behandelt.'); `Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl_Programmierhandbuch-NC-Programmierung_SW492_DE_2019`, p. 50 ('Satzlänge': 'Ein Satz kann maximal 512 Zeichen enthalten (inklusive Kommentar und Satzende-Zeichen LF)'; the note adds that the current-block display shows three blocks of at most 66 characters each. Block length is counted in characters, and the comment counts toward it.); `Heidenhain_TNC640_Technisches-Handbuch_892899-18_NC-SW-34059x-09_DE_2018`, p. 3157 (Section 8.5.3 Pfadangaben, in the PLC-programming chapter: the control's file system supports letters A…Z and a…z, digits 0…9, minus, dot and underscore for drive, directory and file names; other characters risk file-access errors, and a path may be 240 characters. The rule is about path names, not about the content of an NC block.); `Heidenhain_TNC640_Technisches-Handbuch_892899-18_NC-SW-34059x-09_DE_2018`, p. 255 (The list of new features of this software level (Einführung | Software) includes 'Unterstützung des Unicode-Zeichensatzes in Zyklentexten' — Unicode arrived late and only for cycle texts, not for the NC program in general.). (Citations re-paged to the cnc-manuals connector 2026-10-26.)

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

A column is one Unicode code point of the line, first is column 1. Writer and lexer count with `string.EnumerateRunes`; lexer converts its string indices to code-point columns in PAR messages. Language 5 rule 7 says so.
Basis: logical
Source: Encoding-independent, so a postprocessor in another language produces the same text; identical to today for all BMP text. Siemens/Heidenhain character sets (840D sl NC-Programmierung) mean compiled output is unaffected either way.
Differs from the recommendation: no
Confidence: high
Code impact: Ncx.Core NcxWriter.WriteBlock (one line), lexer column reporting.

#### D167 Canonical rank of @SAVE and @RESTORE
Question: Language 5 rule 6 says the catalog carries the rank of every word, but the buckets of D90 do not place the pseudo-words @SAVE and @RESTORE (D95, language 4.15). A pseudo-word takes no address (its value is the state key), so rule 4 allows one @SAVE and one @RESTORE per block. Their rank shows only when a generated block that holds a pseudo-word together with other words is written as text. ncx format never writes generated blocks (4.15). annotate shows them (VM 3.10) and writes through the canonical writer (VM 6). P1-07 requires the annotate output, comments stripped, to format back to the original. Written as blocks, generated blocks would add blocks, and their pseudo-words would be the ERROR 'pseudo-word in a user file' (D95). So annotate can show them only as comment lines, and that is where the rank would be seen. The documented expansions list each pseudo-word as an item of its own (architecture 5.5 and P1-06: '@SAVE=SPINDLE:MAIN', 'SPINDLE:MAIN=OFF', the coolant block, '@RESTORE=SPINDLE:MAIN'), but a plugin rewriter does not have to keep them apart. Where do they rank? A related point that the rank does not settle: no document says which value @SAVE pushes when its own block also sets that variable, or whether @RESTORE acts before or after a state word in its own block. VM 3 step 3 applies state words in any order, and VM 3.10 says only 'the current value'.
Recommendation: Add a bucket 18 after COMMENT or SECTION: @SAVE, then @RESTORE, as the catalog already does (ranks 1130 and 1140). ncx format never writes them, so ranking them last leaves every user word where rule 6 puts it and leaves the generated table unchanged above them. Keep pseudo-words in blocks of their own. The expander writes them that way (P1-06, now in wave 2), and a rewriter's block that mixes a pseudo-word with other words is reported as an ERROR on the plugin, so the related point needs no VM rule. Alternative: @SAVE first in its block and @RESTORE last, with a VM 3.10 sentence that @SAVE takes the value before the state words of its block and @RESTORE applies after them, so that a mixed block reads in the order it acts.
Where: Language 5 rule 6 (bucket 18); language 4.15 or VM 3.10 (pseudo-words in blocks of their own, or the order of the alternative); D95 row (a Clarified line); P1-06 (the expander and rewriter blocks); P1-07 (annotate shows generated blocks as comment lines). Code: src/Ncx.Core/Catalog/CanonicalRanks.cs, Save and Restore (the TODO(question) becomes a comment), and PseudoWords.cs; docs/spec/generated/word-catalog.md.

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, not confirmed by the maintainer: the manuals do not settle this. No manual can rank NCX pseudo-words, and I found no control in the library with a word that saves and restores modal state block by block, so the bucket-18 choice is the maintainer's. The one real analogue is Siemens' SAVE attribute, and its semantics back the recommendation's side point: SAVE saves the modal G commands active before the subprogram call and reactivates them after the subprogram end, and it is written on the PROC line, PROC <name> SAVE, not as a word inside a block — the save point is the boundary, and the mechanism never shares a block with the state words it protects. Keeping @SAVE and @RESTORE in blocks of their own therefore matches the only prior art in the library, and the ordering question the draft leaves open does not arise there. Caveats: SAVE is an attribute of a subprogram, not a word, and it covers only the modal G commands (frame behaviour under SAVE depends on the frame type and is set by machine data), so it is an analogue rather than a counterpart to @SAVE=SPINDLE:MAIN. Fanuc and Heidenhain have nothing comparable in the library: searching the 30i-B set for 'Modalinformationen', 'modalen Zustand' and 'Modaldaten ... speichern', and the TNC 640 set for 'Zustand sichern', 'Zustand wiederherstellen' and 'Bearbeitungszustand', turned up only data backup, restart-after-alarm and operator recovery, nothing programmable.
Evidence: `Siemens_Sinumerik-840D-sl_Programmierung_BS.000504-DE-000-00_DE`, p. 168 (section 2.24.2.4) ('Modale G-Funktionen sichern (SAVE)': 'Das Attribut SAVE bewirkt, dass die vor dem Unterprogrammaufruf aktiven modalen G-Befehle gesichert und nach dem Unterprogrammende wieder reaktiviert werden.' Syntax: PROC <Unterprogrammname> SAVE — it stands on the definition line, not in a block with other words. An ACHTUNG adds that with Bahnsteuerbetrieb active the path mode is interrupted at the return.); `Siemens_Sinumerik-ONE_Programmierhandbuch-NC-Programmierung_SW614_DE_2020`, p. 500-501 (Worked example of SAVE: the subprogram KONTUR works in G91, the main program in G90, and after the subprogram end G90 is active again because of SAVE. Under Randbedingungen: 'Das Verhalten von Frames bezüglich Unterprogrammen mit dem Attribut SAVE ist abhängig vom Typ des Frames und kann über Maschinendaten eingestellt werden.'); `Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl_Programmierhandbuch-NC-Programmierung_SW492_DE_2019`, p. 50 (Under 'Reihenfolge der Anweisungen' the recommended order N G X Y Z F S T D M H is given expressly so that the block reads clearly ('Um den Satzaufbau übersichtlich zu gestalten'). The page says nothing about an order of effect, in either direction.). (Citations re-paged to the cnc-manuals connector 2026-10-26.)

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

Add bucket 18 after COMMENT/SECTION: @SAVE, then @RESTORE (ranks 1130, 1140). Pseudo-words stand in blocks of their own; a rewriter block mixing a pseudo-word with other words is an ERROR on the plugin.
Basis: manual
Source: Only analogue is Siemens PROC ... SAVE, which saves/restores at the subprogram boundary and never shares a block with the state it protects (840D sl programming manual).
Differs from the recommendation: no
Confidence: high
Code impact: Expander/rewriter output check (ERROR on mixed block).

#### D169 Strings in comparisons (language 4.12)
Question: A variable may hold a string: VAR:QS1="TEXT" (language 4.9), QS1 = "TEXT" in the vars file (machine-config 8), and in the code $SYS_TOOL when the tool in the spindle has a name (language 4.4 lets TOOL take a string; VariableStore.ActiveTool). VM 5 makes 'string where a number is required' an ERROR, but 4.12 does not say whether == and != require numbers. The grammar has no string literal, so a string comparison is always between two variables, {$QS1 == $QS2}. {$SYS_TOOL == 5} with a named tool in the spindle is VM902 under either answer.
Recommendation: Numbers only, as implemented. A string operand of any operator is the ERROR VM902, and a string passes through an expression only as its whole value, {$QS1}. Reason: without string literals, comparing strings has little use, and controller-mapping 6 keeps the Siemens string functions RAW. String comparison belongs in one later extension together with string literals. Alternative: == and != compare two strings by exact text and yield 1 or 0; every other operator, and a string compared with a number, stay VM902.
Where: language 4.12; VM 5; src/Ncx.Core/Expressions/Evaluator.cs EvaluateBinary, RequireNumber (TODO(question)).

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, not confirmed by the maintainer: the manuals do not settle this. The manuals argue for the Alternative, not for the recommendation's reasoning. Siemens allows exactly == and <> on variables of type STRING (all six comparison operators are reserved for CHAR/INT/REAL/BOOL), and the TNC 640 accepts numbers, texts and QS string parameters in an IF condition, with FN 9 (equal) and FN 10 (not equal) usable on QS parameters and text literals while FN 11/FN 12 (greater/less) stay numeric. Both controls also write a string literal directly into the comparison (Siemens IF STRG=="Index:"<<IDX GOTOF, IF STRG[0] == "E" GOTO), which the NCX grammar does not have. Fanuc has no string variables at all, so it contributes nothing; the premise that a tool can be a name is confirmed (Siemens T="Bohrer", Heidenhain shows tool number and name). What is left for the maintainer: keeping numbers only is a defensible NCX-1.0 choice, but its stated reason — that comparing strings has little use — does not hold on two of the three families. Caveats: This proposal contradicts the recommendation's reasoning. The manuals cannot settle what NCX's own expression language does; they contradict the recommendation's reasoning, not its feasibility. Note that both controls restrict string comparison to equal/not-equal, exactly the Alternative's wording, and that Siemens explicitly extends it to synchronous actions. The further claim that a Siemens or Heidenhain source with a string comparison then has to go RAW is an NCX consequence of controller-mapping 6, not something a manual says.
Evidence: `Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl-828D_Programmierhandbuch-Arbeitsvorbereitung_DE_2013`, p. 71 (section 1.4) (Comparison operations apply to CHAR, INT, REAL and BOOL; for the types STRING, AXIS and FRAME only == and <> are possible, and for STRING these also work in synchronous actions. The result of a comparison is always BOOL.); `Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl-828D_Programmierhandbuch-Arbeitsvorbereitung_DE_2013`, p. 81-82 and 86 (section 1.9 Stringoperationen) (The worked examples compare a STRING variable with a literal inside a jump condition: IF STRG=="Index:"<<IDX GOTOF NO_MSG, and IF STRG[0] == "E" GOTO ... for a single character of a system variable.); `Heidenhain_TNC640_Programmierung-Klartext_892903-18_NC-SW-34059x-10_DE_2019`, p. 279 (section 9.6) (The inputs allowed in an IF condition are listed as numbers, texts, Q/QL/QR and QS (string parameters); FN 9 is the equal jump, FN 10 the not-equal jump, FN 11/FN 12 the greater/less jumps.); `Heidenhain_TNC640_Programmierung-Klartext_892903-18_NC-SW-34059x-10_DE_2019`, p. 46 (changed functions of NC-SW 34059x-10) (Besides FN 9, the comparison for inequality FN 10 is now possible with QS parameters and texts as well.); `Heidenhain_TNC640_Programmierung-Klartext_892903-18_NC-SW-34059x-10_DE_2019`, p. 336-337 (section 9.11, String-Parameter) (Alphabetical order of strings is compared with STRCOMP(SRC_QSn SEA_QSm), which writes 0, -1 or +1 into a numeric Q parameter - an ordering, not a boolean result.); `Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl-828D_Programmierhandbuch-Grundlagen_DE_2013`, p. 56 (section 4.2) (With active tool management, tools must carry a name as well as a number (e.g. "Bohrer", "3") and the tool call can be made by name, T="Bohrer", T=<Name>; so the active tool is a string on this control.); `Heidenhain_iTNC530_Benutzerhandbuch-Klartext_NC-SW-340422_DE_2004`, p. 47 (section 1.4, Status-Anzeigen) (The tool status display shows 'Anzeige T: Werkzeug-Nummer und -Name', i.e. the control itself identifies the tool in the spindle by number and by name.). (Citations re-paged to the cnc-manuals connector 2026-10-26.)

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

Take the alternative. `==` and `!=` compare two strings by exact, case-sensitive text and yield 1 or 0. Every other operator, and a string against a number, stay VM902. There are still no string literals; they remain a later extension. Compilers: Siemens writes `==`/`<>` on STRING. Heidenhain writes FN 9/FN 10 (or IF) on QS where the control supports it, otherwise a CMP ERROR. Fanuc has no strings, so it is a CMP ERROR.
Basis: manual
Source: Siemens Arbeitsvorbereitung 2013 p. 71 (STRING allows only == and <>), p. 81-82, 86; TNC 640 Klartext 892903-18 p. 46, 279. Both controls restrict string comparison to exactly the alternative's two operators, so NCX matches them and adding literals later stays additive.
Differs from the recommendation: yes: string == / != are allowed instead of VM902.
Confidence: medium
Code impact: Evaluator.EvaluateBinary / RequireNumber (string equality branch); language 4.12 and VM 5 text.

#### D170 Resources created on the spot without a machine file
Question: D103 (clarified 2026-09-13) and the closing paragraph of VM 3.8 say that a word with an unknown role runs against a resource created on the spot, and that a work spindle created this way gets its own rotary axis. They do not say which type a spindle word creates, nor the id of the resource or of its axis. The P1-04 tests in implementation 11 settle two points: "the holder TURRET1 created on the spot has no spindle" and "the SUB created on the spot has its own C axis". The type decides later ERRORs: SPINDLE_MODE, SPINDLE_SYNC (rule 5) and WORKPIECE need a work spindle, and rule 1 rejects a wrong type. The id and the axis name show up in ncx trace rows (RPM:SUB, the position of C_SUB).
Recommendation: Keep what the code does (ResourceResolver.CreateOnTheSpot). Every spindle word (SPINDLE, RPM, VC, CSS, RPM_MAX, ORIENT, SPINDLE_MODE, SPINDLE_SYNC) and WORKPIECE create a work spindle. That is the one type all of them accept, so the guess never causes a wrong-type ERROR later. TOOL and PRELOAD create a holder without a spindle. The resource's id is its role, and the axis of a created work spindle is `C_<role>` (C_SUB). No program can write that name as an axis word (it is not of the D93 form), so the axis can never collide with a machine axis. The id can collide, though: a role spelled like one of the default machine's own ids (S1, S2, H1) creates a resource that shares that resource's state, so SPINDLE:S2=CW without a machine file drives the tool spindle. A prefix on the created id closes that gap.
Where: VM 3.8 closing paragraph (one sentence); the 'Clarified' line of D103 in rationale.md; src/Ncx.Core/VirtualMachine/ResourceResolver.cs (the TODOs in ResolveSpindle and CreateOnTheSpot).

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27: the library does not answer this (searched the alarm side ("ILLEGAL AXIS", "nicht vorhandene Achse") across the Fanuc 0i-D, 16i/18i/21i and 30i-B manuals, which yields only alarms about misusing existing axes; and, across the whole cache, "nicht projektierte Achse", "Achse nicht projektiert", "nicht vorhandene Spindel", "unbekannte Achse", "Defaultmaschine" — no hits anywhere in 01_Steuerungen or 02_Maschinenhersteller. "virtuelle Achse" hits only Siemens/Mazak/Grob transformation and postprocessor contexts, not resource creation. Nothing on default machines, synthesised resources, resource ids or generated rotary-axis names in the Fanuc, Heidenhain or Siemens manuals, nor in the Nakamura, Doosan, Mori Seiki, DMG, Hermle or Burkhardt+Weber builder manuals). The recommendation above stands for the maintainer.

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

Keep ResourceResolver.CreateOnTheSpot: every spindle word and WORKPIECE create a work spindle with axis `C_<role>`; TOOL and PRELOAD create a holder without a spindle. Close the id collision the recommendation names: a created resource's id is `ROLE_<role>` (never equal to a default-machine id such as S2), the axis stays `C_<role>`.
Basis: logical
Source: Manuals have no synthesised resources. Without the prefix, SPINDLE:S2=CW silently drives the default machine's tool spindle; a prefix makes the guess never alias real state.
Differs from the recommendation: yes: adopts the id prefix the recommendation only mentions.
Confidence: medium
Code impact: Ncx.Core ResourceResolver.CreateOnTheSpot (id prefix); P1-04 tests.

#### D172 Templates for named tools
Question: Language 4.4 lets `TOOL` and `PRELOAD` take a string. Machine-config 3 accepts one under `tool_name_allowed` and lists the Siemens change as `"T{tool}"` or `"T=\"{name}\" M6"`, but `[tool_change]` has only one `change` and one `preload` template. siemens-840dsl-mill.toml and millturn1.toml set `tool_name_allowed = true` with numeric templates only (`T{tool} M6`, `T{tool} D{offset}`). dmg-ctx-840d.toml has `{name}` templates only. Which template writes `TOOL="DRILL_D8"` on a machine that takes both numbers and names?
Recommendation: Add optional `change_named` and `preload_named` templates with `{name}`. They are written when the block's tool is a string: the value of `TOOL` or `PRELOAD`, or the preloaded tool of a bare `TOOL`. `change` and `preload` stay numeric. On a machine with `tool_name_allowed = true` and no named template, a named tool is an ERROR at compile time. For the Siemens mill: `change_named = "T=\"{name}\" M6"` and `preload_named = "T=\"{name}\""`. The DMG file moves its `{name}` templates to these keys (documentation only, D68). Alternative: `{tool}` renders a name in double quotes and the Siemens templates become `T={tool} M6`. That is valid for both forms but writes `T=4` where the corpus writes `T4`.
Where: machine-config 3 ([tool_change] keys and the table); language 4.4; machines/siemens-840dsl-mill.toml:39; docs/spec/examples/machines/millturn1.toml and dmg-ctx-840d.toml; src/Ncx.Core/Machine/ToolChangeConfig.cs, the loader, TemplateSet; P5-02.

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, not confirmed by the maintainer: the manuals do not settle this. The manuals show why one template cannot do the job, and they weaken the objection to the alternative. On a SINUMERIK a tool is selected as T<number> or T=<number> without tool management, and as T=<place> or T="<name>" with tool management active, so T=4 is a documented Siemens spelling and not a defect — but a named tool needs the tool-management option, which is what tool_name_allowed really asserts about a machine. Two constraints belong in the answer: tool names are the one place in the language where upper and lower case are distinguished, and they may hold no special characters. The change/preload split comes from the manual too: on a turret lathe the T command searches and changes in one step, on a mill with a chain, disc or flat magazine T only selects and M6 changes — and the worked example prints exactly the pair the recommendation proposes, T="Bohrer" to preselect and a later bare M6 to change, which is change_named = 'T="{name}" M6' and preload_named = 'T="{name}"' for the Siemens mill.
Evidence: `Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl-828D_Programmierhandbuch-Grundlagen_DE_2013`, p. 53-55 (Page 53: with chain, disc and flat magazines the change happens in two steps, T searches the tool in the magazine and an M command swaps it into the spindle, while with turret magazines on lathes searching and changing are done by the T command alone; which form applies is a machine datum. Pages 54-55 give the syntax without tool management: T<Nummer>, T=<Nummer>, T<n>=<Nummer>, number range 0 to 32000, with M6 making the selected tool and its D offset active on the magazine machines.); `Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl-828D_Programmierhandbuch-Grundlagen_DE_2013`, p. 56-60 (With the optional tool management the select syntax is T=<Platz>, T=<Name>, T<n>=<Platz> or T<n>=<Name>; tools are identified by name and number, the name is written in quotes as in T="Bohrer", it may contain no special characters, and the manual warns that upper and lower case must be written correctly. The worked example on p.59 is N10 T=1 M6 ... N70 T="Bohrer" (preselect) ... N100 M6 (change) — the named preload and the named change as two separate blocks.); `Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl-828D_Programmierhandbuch-Grundlagen_DE_2013`, p. 45, 88-89 (Page 45: "Klein- und Großbuchstaben werden nicht unterschieden (Ausnahme: Werkzeugaufruf)" — case is ignored across the whole language with the tool call as the single exception. Page 88 shows the mill form in full: N110 T="WZ2" M6 D1, commented as changing tool T2 in and activating offset D1.); BURKHARDT+WEBER MCX 800 HVP Betriebsanleitung Band 1, 2019, p. 392 (no readable text in the cnc-manuals connector) (The builder's own examples for the 840D sl machine mix all three spellings on the same control: T1244 selects a tool from magazine 1, T="WIKO" selects the angle head by name, T=TOOL selects through a name that is not a literal — and the change in every example is the builder subprogram L706, not M6.). (Citations re-paged to the cnc-manuals connector 2026-10-26.)

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

Add optional `change_named` and `preload_named` templates with `{name}`, used when the tool is a string (TOOL/PRELOAD value or the preloaded tool of a bare TOOL); `change`/`preload` stay numeric. Named tool with `tool_name_allowed = true` but no named template: compile ERROR. Siemens mill: `change_named = "T=\"{name}\" M6"`, `preload_named = "T=\"{name}\""`; DMG moves its `{name}` templates to these keys. Tool names are case-sensitive and without special characters on Siemens; the compiler reports a name that violates this.
Basis: manual
Source: Sinumerik 840D sl Grundlagen: T<n>/T=<n> without, T="<name>" with tool management; worked example T="Bohrer" then M6; names case-sensitive, no special characters.
Differs from the recommendation: no (adds the name-character check)
Confidence: high
Code impact: Ncx.Config [tool_change] keys; compiler template selection.

### Sixth round: controller and machine facts to confirm

#### D177 Fanuc dwell P outside G82 and G84
Question: Controller-mapping 5 (CYCLE_F, CYCLE_DWELL row) puts "F and P on the G8x block". Phase 2 P2-03 requires G81, CYCLE81 and CYCL DEF 200 to map the same words, CYCLE_DWELL included. Fanuc 6 names the dwell only for G82 ("G82 adds a dwell P (milliseconds)"), and BOHREN.fanuc.nc writes P only on G84 (P0). Controller-mapping 5 is the specification and wins over fanuc 6 (controllers/README.md line 14), so main follows the documents: CYCLE_DWELL = "P" stands on every Fanuc drilling entry (DrillingFamily.Fanuc.cs, cycles/fanuc.toml). The open point is what the control does. The Fanuc machining-center manuals list P in the formats of G82, G84 and G89 (also G74, G76, G87 and G88), but not of G73, G81, G83, G85 and G86, where the control stores P without dwelling. If so, CYCLE=DRILL CYCLE_DWELL=0.5 compiles to G81 ... P500, and a dwell read from Heidenhain Q211 or Siemens DTB, which VM 3.3 executes, is silently lost on the machine.
Recommendation: Confirm from the Fanuc 30i manual (controller-mapping 10). If it confirms: CYCLE_DWELL = P only on DRILL_DWELL (G82) and TAP (G84) (DrillingFamily.Fanuc.cs, cycles/fanuc.toml), and controller-mapping 5 reads "F on the G8x block, P on G82 and G84". The Fanuc compiler writes a DRILL with a CYCLE_DWELL other than 0 as G82, the code of DRILL_DWELL (controller-mapping 5). A REAM with a dwell goes out as G89 (G85 with a dwell), which the reader reads back as REAM with CYCLE_DWELL; the alternative for REAM is a CMP WARNING. The compiler reports that WARNING when PECK, CHIP_BREAK or BORE drop a dwell other than 0. The P2-03 sentence and its test read "the same words, CYCLE_DWELL through G82 on Fanuc". The same DRILL-to-G82 rule serves Siemens if CYCLE81 has no DTB (see D181). Reason: the compiled program then does what the VM executed. Alternative: keep P on every entry, as main does since the P2-03a review fix, and accept that the control ignores it.
Where: controller-mapping 5 (CYCLE_F, CYCLE_DWELL row) and 10; fanuc 6; 12-phase-2-configuration.md P2-03 (test sentence); src/Ncx.Core/Machine/DrillingFamily.Fanuc.cs (FanucEntry, TODO line 39); cycles/fanuc.toml lines 28-74 (TODO at line 30); tests/Ncx.Config.Tests/Cycles/ShippedCatalogsTests.cs (s_drillWords, Drill_G81Cycle81AndCyclDef200_MapTheSameNcxWords); P3-02, P3-06 FanucCycles.

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, corrected 2026-10-26 after the manual audit, not confirmed by the maintainer: Confirmed for the mill; on the lathe it depends on the command format. On a machining centre the Fanuc formats carry a dwell P only on G74, G76, G82, G84, G87, G88 and G89; G73, G81, G83, G85 and G86 have none (only the optional small-hole peck drilling G83, selected by an M code, takes P), and each cycle's restrictions name only the addresses its format carries. For the seven built-in entries that is exactly the recommendation: keep CYCLE_DWELL = P on DRILL_DWELL (G82) and TAP (G84) and drop it from DRILL (G81), PECK (G83), CHIP_BREAK (G73), REAM (G85) and BORE (G86). Routing a REAM with a dwell to G89 is right too: G89 is G85 plus a dwell at the hole bottom. But the proposed sentence for controller-mapping 5, "F on the G8x block, P on G82 and G84", does not fit a lathe. In the standard (Series 16/18) lathe format, G83, G84, G85, G87, G88 and G89 all take P as the dwell at the hole bottom and the group has no G82, so a lathe DRILL with a dwell stays G83 with P and the lathe catalog of D160 keeps CYCLE_DWELL on every entry. In the optional Series 15 format the lathe group is G81, G82, G83, G83.1, G84, G85 and G89, with G82 as the drilling cycle with a dwell, and G83 and G84 dwell only when P stands in the block (Series 15-T: G83 never dwells). Only there does the Recommendation's DRILL-to-G82 rule apply to a lathe. So the sentence is written per machine kind and, on a lathe, per command format.
Evidence: FANUC 30i-B Operator's Manual Milling (B-64484EN-2), p. 56 (Table 5.1 (a): at the hole bottom a dwell for G74, G82, G84, G88 and G89, spindle orientation for G76, spindle stop for G86, spindle CW for G87, nothing for G73, G81, G83 and G85); p. 61, 63, 64, 66, 67, 69, 75, 76-78, 80, 82 and 83 (the restrictions of each cycle: a Q paragraph for G73 (61) and G83 (69), a P paragraph for G74 (63), G82 (67), G84 (75), G88 (82) and G89 (83), a P and Q paragraph for G76 (64) and G87 (80), and none for G81 (66), G85 (76-77) and G86 (78)); p. 68 (G82 example with P1000, 1 s at the hole bottom); p. 70 (small-hole peck drilling G83 X Y Z R Q F I K P, selected by the M code of parameter 5163); p. 83-84 (G89 is almost the same as G85, plus a dwell at the hole bottom; example with P1000); FANUC 30i-B Operator's Manual Turning (B-64484EN-1), p. 92 (Table 4.3 (a): G83, G84, G85, G87, G88 and G89, each with a dwell at the hole bottom; no G82); p. 95-99 (the G83/G87 and G84/G88 formats list P as the dwell at the hole bottom; examples G83 Z-40.0 R-5.0 P500 F5.0, G84 ... P500 and G85 ... P500); p. 245 (Series 15 program format, selected by setting parameter 0001#1, an option); p. 297-299 (§6.5 in the Series 15 format: Table 6.5 (a) lists G81, G82 with a dwell, G83, G83.1, G84, G85 and G89; in G83, G83.1, G84 and G84.2 a dwell only when P is in the block; on Series 15-T, G83 and G83.1 do not dwell).
Corrected: "the lathe canned-cycle group has no G82" holds for the standard Series 16/18 format only; the Series 15 format gives a lathe G82 (EN-1 p. 297-299), so the per-machine sentence also depends on the command format. The German citations are replaced by the English editions.

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

Mill catalog (cycles/fanuc.toml): CYCLE_DWELL = "P" only on DRILL_DWELL (G82) and TAP (G84), plus REAM with a dwell, which goes out as G89 (read back as REAM with CYCLE_DWELL). The compiler writes a DRILL with CYCLE_DWELL != 0 as G82. PECK, CHIP_BREAK and BORE with a dwell other than 0 get a CMP WARNING ("dwell dropped"). Lathe catalog (cycles/fanuc-lathe.toml, D160, standard format): CYCLE_DWELL = P stays on every entry (G83/G87, G84/G88, G85/G89 all take P). The Series 15 command format (parameter 0001#1) is not a shipped catalog and needs its own catalog file. Controller-mapping 5 says "P per catalog: mill G82, G84, G89; lathe all entries". The P2-03 test reads "CYCLE_DWELL through G82 on the Fanuc mill".
Basis: manual
Source: Fanuc B-64484EN-2 p. 56, 61-84 (dwell only on G74, G76, G82, G84, G87, G88, G89); B-64484EN-1 p. 92, 95-99, 245, 297-299; consistent with D160. Web: CAM posts switch G81 to G82 to output a dwell (https://www.emastercam.com/forums/topic/111216-ive-no-idea-on-this-dwelling-debacle/).
Differs from the recommendation: yes: the lathe catalog keeps P on every entry, and the controller-mapping sentence is per catalog.
Confidence: high
Code impact: DrillingFamily.Fanuc.cs and cycles/fanuc.toml (P only on G82/G84/G89); ShippedCatalogsTests; Fanuc compiler P3-06 (DRILL->G82, REAM->G89, WARNING).

#### D179 Sub spindle C axis address on the NTJX and the Puma 2600SY
Question: D30 and the `letter` comment of machine-config 4 give the extended form `C2=` for the Fanuc 30i/31i (and for Siemens), and plain `C` per path for the Mori Seiki. Controller-mapping 2 (IX row), controller-mapping 8 (C axis mode row) and machine-builders 1 give `C2=`/`H2=` for the Nakamura NTX II and `A` for the SC series. No document gives the address of the sub spindle C axis on two machines. The first is the Nakamura NTJX (Fanuc 18i-TB, two paths). Its [spindle_sync] comment says path 2 owns the second spindle, but in the file the only tool spindle (S3) sits on turret 1, path 1. Controller-mapping 8 and the file's C_MIX function also list M432/M433 and M442/M443 as a C-axis command mix. The second is the Doosan Puma 2600SY (Fanuc 0i-TD, one path; M35 and M135 switch C1 and C2). Which address does each manual show: plain `C`/`H`, `C2=`/`H2=`, or another letter such as `A`? If plain `C`: on the NTJX, in which path's program, and with or without the command mix? On the Doosan, after M135?
Recommendation: Confirm `letter = "C"` and `incremental_letter = "H"` for both machines, as both files already have. Neither control is a 30i/31i, so the D30 extended form does not apply. With plain C the files follow mori-ntx1000-mapps.toml, whose C2 also has letter "C", "valid after M304 selects spindle 2". A source C then reads as the NCX C. VM 3.8 rule 3 resolves it to C2 while the sub spindle holds the workpiece (Doosan M134, Nakamura M427), and M135 or M491 puts the sub spindle in AXIS mode (rule 4). The compiler writes C for either axis. If a manual shows `C2=` or `A`, only `letter` and `incremental_letter` of that file change. Either way, turn both TODO(question) lines into comments that cite the manual page.
Where: docs/spec/examples/machines/nakamura-ntjx.toml [[axis]] C2 (TODO at line 130) and doosan-puma-2600sy.toml [[axis]] C2 (TODO at line 122), copied to machines/ in P2-04 part two. Also the Nakamura and Doosan paragraphs of machine-builders.md 1 and the C axis mode row of controller-mapping 8, plus the `letter` comment of machine-config 4 if a new form turns up. On main, only the loader stores `letter` (MachineConfigLoader.Resources.cs) and no code reads it. The Fanuc reader and compiler (P3-02, P3-06) are the first to read it. No phase-3 acceptance program depends on the answer: the WY-250L pair has no C axis words (only G411 C1.), POLAR_FACE mills on the main spindle, and check resolves NCX names, not letters.

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, not confirmed by the maintainer: Confirm `letter = "C"` and `incremental_letter = "H"` in both files. On the NTJX the manual's own worked pair settles it: the lower-turret program writes `M491` (sub-spindle C axis on) and then `G28 H0` when it mills at the sub spindle, and `M91` and `G28 H0` when it mills at the main spindle — only the M code and the datum (G59 versus G54) differ, the address stays C/H. Nakamura's own criterion for the extended form is the path count and which side already owns the plain C, not the control family: single-path SC on the 18i-TB uses `A`, two-path SC on the 0i-TD uses `C`/`H`, single-path NTX(II) R-side uses `C2=`/`H2=`, and the NTJX is listed as a two-path lathe. On the Doosan, the MX 31i manual writes `G28 H0`, `G50 C0` and plain `C` after `M135` (C2 select) exactly as after `M35` (C1 select), and the Puma operating manual says that on machines with a sub spindle the sub spindle serves as the C2 axis while the axis itself is moved with the C key. The C-axis command mix does not change the address: M432/M442 redirect the unit's own C word to the other unit's C axis.
Evidence: `Nakamura-Tome_Fanuc_Programmierung_Programmierhandbuch_DE_2019`, "Beispiele Arbeitskombinationen NTJX", p. 174 (Example 5 for the NTJX, "Revolver Unten bohrt/fräst an Gegenspindel": the lower-turret column reads G411 R1 I~, G18 G59, G0 T0151, M491, G28 H0, G97 S2500 M489, and after the cut G28 U0 V0 M490, M441. The sub-spindle C axis is referenced with the plain incremental letter H, with no extended axis name.); `Nakamura-Tome_Fanuc_Programmierung_Programmierhandbuch_DE_2019`, "Beispiele Arbeitskombinationen NTJX", p. 175 (Example 6, "Revolver Unten bohrt/fräst an Hauptspindel": the same turret column reads G411 L1 I~, G18 G54, G0 T0101, M91, G28 H0, and closes with M41. Main-spindle and sub-spindle milling differ only in the M code (M91 versus M491, M41 versus M441) and in the datum (G54 versus G59); the axis address stays C/H.); `Nakamura-Tome_Fanuc_Programmierung_Programmierhandbuch-1_4810004ECL-1_DE_2013`, p. 235-236 (Three cases side by side, each headed by the number of paths. §14-5-7, SC as a single-path lathe (18i-TB): because the C axis is used on the main-spindle side, the sub-spindle C axis is controlled as an A axis, absolute A___, incremental A[#5006+___]. §14-5-8, SC as a two-path lathe (0i-TD): the same axis is the C2 axis but is commanded absolute C___ and incremental H___. §14-5-9, NTX(II) R-side as a single-path lathe: because the C axis is used on the L-spindle side, it is the C2 axis and is commanded C2=___ and H2=___. No control is named in §14-5-9.); `Nakamura-Tome_Fanuc-16-21i_Bedienung_NT-Nurse-Bedienungsanleitung_4800001EBG_DE_2013`, p. 347 (The machine-model table lists "56 NTJX Drehmaschine mit 2 Bahnen" — a two-path lathe, so the case of §14-5-8, not the single-path cases of §14-5-7 and §14-5-9.); `Nakamura-Tome_Fanuc_Programmierung_Programmierhandbuch-1_4810004ECL-1_DE_2013`, p. 133-134 (Items (36) to (42): M432 lets the C-axis motion command of the lower unit move the left unit's C axis, while that unit's own C command is disabled; M442 does the same for the right unit; M433/M443 cancel it. The command mix changes which axis a C word drives, not how the C word is written. The series named are WTS, NTM3, NTY3 (and WTW for M442).); Doosan MX series programming manual, Fanuc 31i (MX31iPGE8A, 2008), p. 93 (no readable text in the cnc-manuals connector; the same M35/M135 examples are in `Doosan_MX-Series_CNC-Programmierbuch_DE`, p. 25-26, section 2.3) (Section 4.3.8 lists M35 "C1-AXIS SELECT ON" and M135 "C2-AXIS SELECT ON", and the two worked examples then read the same lines: M35 or M135, then M90 or M190, G28 H0, G50 C0, M101 G98(G99), G97 M3 S100 P12. The C axis is addressed with plain C and plain H whichever of the two the M code has selected.); Doosan PUMA-Baureihe Bedienungshandbuch (2020), p. 55 (no readable text in the cnc-manuals connector) ("Bei Maschinen mit Zusatzspindel wird die Zusatzspindel bei Bedarf als C2-Achse verwendet. In diesem Fall muss zwischen C (C1)- und C2-Achse gewählt werden." The sub-spindle axis is named C2, but after the selection it is moved with the machine's C keys — the same select-then-plain-C idiom as the MX programming manual.); `Doosan_Puma-2600SY_M-Funktionen_DE`, p. 2-3 (The 2600SY's own list gives M35 "C1-ACHSE ANWAHL" (page 2) and M135 "C2-ACHSE ANWAHL EIN" (page 3), plus M89/M90 clamp and release of the left C axis and M189/M190 of the sub-spindle C2 axis — the same selection scheme as the MX series, so the same plain C/H addressing follows.). (Citations re-paged to the cnc-manuals connector 2026-10-26.)

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

Confirm `letter = "C"`, `incremental_letter = "H"` for both nakamura-ntjx.toml and doosan-puma-2600sy.toml; turn both TODO(question) lines into comments citing the manual pages. The command mix (M432/M442) does not change the address.
Basis: manual
Source: Nakamura programming manual worked pair: M491 + G28 H0 at sub spindle, M91 + G28 H0 at main; extended C2= only for single-path NTX R-side. Doosan MX 31i manual: plain C/H after M135 as after M35; Puma manual: sub spindle is C2 moved with the C key.
Differs from the recommendation: no
Confidence: high
Code impact: none (comments in two machine files).
