#### D181 SINUMERIK drilling cycle facts
Question: siemens 7 gives CYCLE81 in full, but the signatures of CYCLE82 to 86, 830 and 840 only up to '...'. siemens 12 rule 5 wants 'the full sl signature from the catalog'. The documents also do not say how NCX's constant PECK is written with FDEP, FDPR and _DAM of CYCLE83, or which pitch a metric size MPIT (3 to 48) stands for. For _DP of CYCLE830, siemens 7 says only that _AMODE decides whether a depth is absolute or incremental, and the documented CYCLE830 signature does not reach _AMODE. Nor do they give the value of an omitted VARI of CYCLE83, which decides between PECK and CHIP_BREAK; the code then matches no entry (CycleCatalog.FindNative). The leading part needs a check as well. siemens 7 and controller-mapping 5 put DTB sixth in CYCLE81. The older form that siemens 7 quotes, CYCLE81(RTP, RFP, SDIS, DP, DPR), has no dwell; the dwell is what CYCLE82 adds. If the sl CYCLE81 has no DTB either, the compiler writes CYCLE_DWELL where the control reads _GMODE, and the P2-03 same-words test relies on DTB there. The feeds are answered for every cycle but CYCLE84: siemens 7 says 'The cycle feed is the modal F ... CYCLE85 has its own FFR'.
Recommendation: Take these from the 840D sl programming manual 3.25 (controller-mapping 10) into siemens.md 7: the full signatures, with the leading part checked (DTB in CYCLE81); the default of every position that a fixed value uses (VARI); the depth mode of CYCLE830; and whether CYCLE84 (rigid tapping, feed from PIT and SST) and CYCLE840 with an encoder (ENC) ignore the modal F. Proposed mappings to confirm there: constant PECK = FDPR with _DAM = 0 and FDEP left empty; PITCH = the ISO 261 coarse pitch of MPIT (M3 0.5 ... M48 5), with the compiler writing PIT. An omitted VARI takes the manual's default, recorded as a 'defaults' value that the reader assumes (see D164). Until then a CYCLE83 without VARI is read natively (D94). If CYCLE81 has no DTB, DRILL maps no CYCLE_DWELL on Siemens. A DRILL with a dwell then compiles as CYCLE82, the same rule D177 proposes for G82, and the same-words test reaches CYCLE_DWELL through that rule. CYCLE_F = "F" on CYCLE86, CYCLE830 and CYCLE840 follows siemens 7 now. CYCLE84 stays without it until the manual confirms.
Where: siemens.md 7, 12 rule 5; controller-mapping 5 (DRILL, PECK, TAP, CYCLE_F rows); cycles/siemens.toml; src/Ncx.Core/Machine/DrillingFamily.Siemens.cs; CycleCatalog.FindNative; tests/Ncx.Config.Tests/Cycles/ShippedCatalogsTests.cs (CYCLE_DWELL on CYCLE81); P5-01, P5-02.

ANSWER: (Peter, 2026-10-07, drafted by Claude in project_spike) Accept the method and the proposed mappings: the signatures, the defaults of every position a fixed value uses (VARI), the depth mode of CYCLE830 and the feed behaviour of CYCLE84 and CYCLE840 are taken from the 840D sl programming manual with page references; constant PECK is FDPR with _DAM = 0, consistent with D356. Nothing about the control is guessed: whatever the manual does not state stays native (D94) until it is checked.
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, not confirmed by the maintainer: Take the facts from the sl manual's chapter 3.25. CYCLE81 in the sl package does have DTB sixth — CYCLE81(RTP, RFP, SDIS, DP, DPR, DTB, _GMODE, _DMODE, _AMODE) — so the DRILL/CYCLE_DWELL mapping and the P2-03 same-words test stand as they are, and the dwell-free form the draft quotes is only the older 840D signature. An omitted parameter is a general rule, not a per-cycle default: it takes the value zero, so a CYCLE83 without VARI is VARI=0, chip-break. The draft's PECK proposal is right as written: the first depth is given by FDEP (absolute) or FDPR (relative) — they are alternatives for one value — and _DAM = 0 is 'keine Degression', so FDPR with _DAM = 0 and FDEP left empty is the constant peck. MPIT is the ISO metric thread size M3 to M48 whose pitch the cycle computes internally at run time, with the sign giving the hand, so having the compiler write PIT is right. CYCLE830's depth _DP is absolute or incremental by the ones digit of _AMODE. The feeds contradict the draft: of the three cycles it names for CYCLE_F = "F", only CYCLE86 is right — CYCLE84 taps with G331/G332 at SST and SST1 and its motion sequence uses no programmed feed, CYCLE840 uses the modal F only with ENC=1 and otherwise computes the feed from pitch and speed, and CYCLE830 has its own drilling feed S_FB. The modal F is also right for CYCLE81, CYCLE82, CYCLE87, CYCLE88 and CYCLE89, while CYCLE85 has FFR and RFF of its own. One more thing for siemens.md 12 rule 5: the sl CYCLE840 is not the 2008 signature — it is CYCLE840(RTP, RFP, SDIS, DP, DPR, DTB, SDR, SDAC, ENC, MPIT, PIT, _AXN, _PITA, _TECHNO, _PITM, _PTAB, _PTABA, _GMODE, _DMODE, _AMODE), with _PITA inserted at 13 and _PTAB moved to 16.
Evidence: SINUMERIK 840D sl NC-Programmierung, Programmierhandbuch 06/2019 (CNC-SW 4.92), p. 1082-1094 (The sl signatures in full: CYCLE81(RTP, RFP, SDIS, DP, DPR, DTB, _GMODE, _DMODE, _AMODE), with DTB described as 'Verweilzeit auf Endbohrtiefe'; CYCLE82 the same plus _VARI, S_ZA, S_FA, S_ZD, S_FD; CYCLE83(..., FDEP, FDPR, _DAM, DTB, DTS, FRF, VARI, _AXN, _MDEP, _VRT, _DTD, _DIS1, _GMODE, _DMODE, _AMODE); CYCLE84(RTP, RFP, SDIS, DP, DPR, DTB, SDAC, MPIT, PIT, POSS, SST, SST1, _AXN, _PITA, _TECHNO, _VARI, _DAM, _VRT, _PITM, _PTAB, _PTABA, _GMODE, _DMODE, _AMODE); CYCLE85(..., DTB, FFR, RFF, _GMODE, _DMODE, _AMODE); CYCLE86(..., DTB, SDIR, RPA, RPO, RPAP, POSS, _GMODE, _DMODE, _AMODE). MPIT is 'Gewindegröße nur für "ISO metrisch" (Steigung wird intern während der Laufzeit berechnet)'.); SINUMERIK 840D sl NC-Programmierung, Programmierhandbuch 06/2019 (CNC-SW 4.92), p. 1129 (The sl CYCLE840 signature is CYCLE840(<RTP>, <RFP>, <SDIS>, <DP>, <DPR>, <DTB>, <SDR>, <SDAC>, <ENC>, <MPIT>, <PIT>, <_AXN>, <_PITA>, <_TECHNO>, <_PITM>, <_PTAB>, <_PTABA>, <_GMODE>, <_DMODE>, <_AMODE>) — six positions longer than the 2008 form and with _PITA and _PTAB in different places; MPIT is again the ISO metric thread size whose pitch the cycle computes at run time.); SINUMERIK 840D sl/840D/840Di sl Zyklen, Programmierhandbuch 01/2008, p. 18 (General rule for every cycle: a supply parameter that is not needed, or that should be zero, may be left out of the parameter list, writing only the comma, or the list may be closed early; the examples comment the omitted positions as 'd.h. Wert Null'.); SINUMERIK 840D sl/840D/840Di sl Zyklen, Programmierhandbuch 01/2008, p. 50-55 (CYCLE83's VARI is 0 for Spänebrechen (chip-break) and 1 for Entspänen (peck); FDEP and FDPR give the first drilling depth absolute or relative and p.54 states the first depth is programmed through one or the other of the two; the degression parameter DAM is 0 for no degression, greater than zero as an amount and less than zero as a factor, and p.55 works through the strokes for the two non-zero cases only.); SINUMERIK 840D sl/840D/840Di sl Zyklen, Programmierhandbuch 01/2008, p. 58-62 (CYCLE84 tapping without a compensating chuck: the motion sequence is an oriented spindle stop with SPOS at POSS, tapping to depth with G331 at speed SST, dwell DTB, retraction with G332 at SST1 with reversed direction, then G0 — no programmed feed appears in it. MPIT is the thread size, range 3 for M3 to 48 for M48, PIT the pitch as a value 0.001 to 2000 mm; whichever is not needed is omitted or set to zero, a positive sign means right-hand and a negative one left-hand, and contradicting values raise alarm 61001.); SINUMERIK 840D sl/840D/840Di sl Zyklen, Programmierhandbuch 01/2008, p. 65-69 (CYCLE840(RTP, RFP, SDIS, DP, DPR, DTB, SDR, SDAC, ENC, MPIT, PIT, _AXN, _PTAB, _TECHNO) in the 2008 form. ENC selects 0 with encoder without dwell, 20 with encoder with dwell, 11 without encoder with the pitch entered and the feed computed in the cycle, 1 without encoder with the feed programmed before the cycle (the worked ENC=1 example writes N30 G1 F200 ahead of the call). Where the pitch is given the cycle derives the feed from spindle speed and pitch, and 'Nach Zyklusende wirkt wieder der letzte programmierte Vorschub'.); SINUMERIK 840D sl NC-Programmierung, Programmierhandbuch 06/2019 (CNC-SW 4.92), p. 1119-1122 (CYCLE830 has 41 parameters beginning CYCLE830(RTP, RFP, SDIS, _DP, FDEP, _DAM, DTB, DTS, FRF, VARI, _MDEP, _VRT, _DTD, _DIS1, S_FP, S_SDAC2, S_SV2, S_FB, _SDAC, _SV1, ...). Its final depth _DP is 'abs/ink (siehe <_AMODE> EINER)', and parameter 18, S_FB, is 'Bohrvorschub', the drilling feed of the cycle itself.); SINUMERIK 840D sl/840D/840Di sl Zyklen, Programmierhandbuch 01/2008, p. 46, 49, 72, 77, 80, 83, 86 (The motion sequences of CYCLE81 (p.46), CYCLE82 (p.49), CYCLE86 (p.77), CYCLE87 (p.80), CYCLE88 (p.83) and CYCLE89 (p.86) each state that the move to final depth uses the feed programmed in the calling program or before the cycle call, while CYCLE85 (p.72) has FFR for the drilling feed and RFF for the retraction feed of its own.).

They cover 85 of the 93 questions those tasks recorded; three of the other eight repeat an open entry of the sixth round (D129, D154, D164), and five are answered by the documents. Of the seventy-three, 28 were settled on 2026-10-01 from the manual library and stand in "Answered (ninth round, 2026-10-01)" below; 45 are still open here. As in the sixth round, the code keeps its workaround, marked `TODO(question)` where it applies, until an entry is answered, and the answer replaces workaround and marker in the commit that changes the specification. `../implementation/03-open-questions.md` (section "Wave 2") maps every question and its code location to its entry here, to the open entry it repeats, or to the section that already answers it. ### Seventh round: needed now

#### D183 IX on an axis known only in the MACHINE frame
Question: VM 3.1 says 'IX= adds to the current value (ERROR when the current value is unknown)' but does not name the frame of that value. VM 2.2 keeps one position frame per axis. After HOME or a FRAME=MACHINE move the axis is known in the MACHINE frame and unknown in the workpiece frame (VM 3 step 5, 3.4, D35, D100), while D101 lets SETPOS use an axis known 'in some frame'. Case: HOME Z on a machine whose Z has home, then LINE IZ=-5 F=100. The workpiece coordinate of Z is unknown, but with only shifts in the chain the machine position (home minus 5) is known. Main takes the current value in the frame the block programs in and reports VM202 (MotionRules.MoveAxis and CoordinateIn; MotionTargetTests.Line_IncrementalWordAfterHome_IsAnErrorInTheWorkpieceFrame). Under FRAME=MACHINE it adds in the MACHINE frame (Rapid_FrameMachine_MovesInMachineCoordinates). Without a machine file, HOME finds no reference point and the axis is unknown in every frame (D100, D103), so there the case is VM202 whatever is decided. The answer matters with a machine file, which convert always has (D77).
Recommendation: IX adds to the position in the frame the axis is known in, when that frame and the frame the block programs in differ on this axis by shifts alone. That means the default workpiece holder, no ROTATE turning a plane that holds the axis, no MIRROR naming it, and no TILT or TILT_AXIS in the chain. FrameRules.MovesAsItsWorkpieceCoordinate already makes this test for D101. The axis stays known in that frame (after HOME Z, LINE IZ=-5 leaves Z known in the MACHINE frame at home minus 5) and stays unknown in the workpiece frame, as D35 says. Every other case is VM202 as today, and in a subprogram nothing calls the axis becomes unknown instead (D99). VM 3.1 says so in one sentence. Reasons: the VM 3.1 ERROR is there because the target is unknown, and here the VM knows the target. Every control runs Fanuc G91 G28 Z0 followed by G91 G0 Z-50, and Klartext L Z+0 FMAX M91 followed by L IZ-50 FMAX. The readers write these as HOME Z or RAPID Z=0 FRAME=MACHINE followed by RAPID IZ=-50 (controller-mapping 2: incremental words as written). Today check stops there with an ERROR on a correct program, and convert exits 1. D100 and D101 already made the HOME idioms of real programs check clean. The limit check also still sees the axis after the step (VM 5, D100). D126's case (IC after TILT_AXIS ... MOVE=TURN) stays VM202 because a tilt stands in the chain, as long as D230 keeps a tilt out of the relation; the two are answered together. Alternative: keep what the code does. IX adds only to the coordinate in the frame the block programs in: the workpiece frame read through the setpos shift, the MACHINE frame under FRAME=MACHINE, or the polar or cylinder frame of D102. That is one rule, and no example writes an increment after HOME (in INCREMENTAL_SUB, HOME Z and HOME X Y are followed only by JUMP). A hand-written program can put FRAME=MACHINE on the step, but a reader cannot, because the source does not say it.
Where: VM 3.1 (the IX sentence) and 5 (IX from an unknown position); language 4.3 (IX row). Code: src/Ncx.Core/VirtualMachine/MotionRules.cs MoveAxis (TODO(question) at line 159) and CoordinateIn; src/Ncx.Core/VirtualMachine/FrameRules.cs MovesAsItsWorkpieceCoordinate and Turns (the relation test, shared with D230); tests/Ncx.Core.Tests/VirtualMachine/MotionTargetTests.cs.

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, not confirmed by the maintainer: the manuals do not settle this. The controls treat an incremental word as a distance from the position the machine is actually at, so the idiom the draft names has a defined target and nothing in the manuals supports the present VM202. Fanuc states for G00 that absolute programming gives the end-point coordinates while incremental programming gives "die Entfernung, um die das Werkzeug bewegt wird", and the manual's own retract idiom is `G91 G28 Z0.` before a tool change. Heidenhain goes further and states a frame rule outright: incremental coordinates programmed in an M91 block refer to the last programmed M91 position, and where the active program has no M91 position, to the current tool position. That is the same shape as the Recommendation — the increment resolves against whatever position the control has, machine-frame first — and the manuals back the Recommendation over the alternative. Which frame NCX keeps the axis known in afterwards remains an NCX decision.
Evidence: `Heidenhain_TNC640_Programmierung-Klartext_892903-18_NC-SW-34059x-10_DE_2019`, p. 226 (Section 7.3, "Verhalten mit M91 – Maschinen-Nullpunkt": incremental coordinates programmed in an M91 block refer to the last programmed M91 position; if the active NC program contains no M91 position, they refer to the current tool position. The control then shows the coordinates relative to the machine datum (REF display).); `Fanuc_30i-B_Bedienung-Drehen-Fraesen_B-64484EN_EN`, p. 72 (Section 4.1 Positioning (G00): with absolute programming the coordinate values of the end point are programmed, with incremental programming "die Entfernung, um die das Werkzeug bewegt wird". The incremental word is a travel distance, so it needs no known coordinate in any frame.); `Fanuc_30i-B_Bedienung-Drehen-Fraesen_B-64484EN_EN`, p. 1201 (Worked example under 4.10.1: N100 G91G28Z0.; N110 G28X0.Y0.; N120 T01M6; N130 G90G00X-50.Y0; N140 Z-10.; N150 G41G01X-50.F1000.D1. The G91 G28 Z0 retract before the tool change is the manual's own idiom and the program continues from it with no re-setting of the coordinate system — but the approach blocks are G90 absolute, so the page does not show an incremental after the retract.). (Citations re-paged to the cnc-manuals connector 2026-10-26.)

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

IX adds to the position in the frame the axis is known in when that frame and the block's frame differ on this axis by shifts alone (default workpiece holder, no ROTATE in a plane holding it, no MIRROR of it, no TILT/TILT_AXIS), the test FrameRules.MovesAsItsWorkpieceCoordinate makes. The axis stays known in that frame and unknown in the workpiece frame; every other case is VM202 (unknown in an uncalled subprogram). One sentence in VM 3.1.
Basis: manual
Source: Heidenhain TNC 640 Klartext: incremental coordinates in an M91 block refer to the last M91 position, else the current tool position; Fanuc B-64484EN G00: incremental is the distance moved, and G91 G28 Z0 is the documented idiom.
Differs from the recommendation: no
Confidence: high
Code impact: Ncx.Core MotionRules.MoveAxis/CoordinateIn; MotionTargetTests.

#### D185 Vector words under RAPID, ARC and CYCLE_CALL
Question: D81, the TX and NX rows of language 4.3, the TCPM row of 4.2, and VM 2.2 and 3.1 give the vector form to 'a LINE under TCPM=ON'. But language 5 rule 2 lets TX TY TZ and NX NY NZ stand with every verb that takes axis words: RAPID, LINE, ARC and CYCLE_CALL (HOME takes bare axis names, and RETRACT none). VM 5 has no ERROR for them under a verb other than LINE. The sources have rapid moves with a tool vector. heidenhain.md 2 gives FMAX as the rapid of a straight block and writes LN with F, and the Heidenhain reader accepts FMAX on LN before it keeps the block RAW. The tool-vector row of controller-mapping 2 gives the Fanuc words (G43.5 I J K) and the Siemens words (A3= B3= C3=) without tying them to a verb. Main is split. The VM checks and stores vector words under RAPID, ARC and CYCLE_CALL as on a LINE (ToolVectorRules.Apply, called after every motion verb). The Heidenhain reader keeps LN with FMAX as RAW (HeidenhainMotion.ReadVectorLine), and the Fanuc reader reads I J K as TX TY TZ only on a G1 under G43.5 (FanucMotion.ReadMotion).
Recommendation: RAPID and LINE carry the vector form, with one meaning: the tool direction at the end point, NX NY NZ optional, only under TCPM=ON, stored unresolved. Vector words under ARC or CYCLE_CALL are an ERROR with a new code after VM213, and VM 5 names it. Reasons: D81's own reason, that vector programs survive convert and compile to controllers that accept vectors, holds for the rapid moves of the same programs, and the VM already treats RAPID and LINE alike. No document shows an arc or a cycle with a vector: the I J K of a Fanuc arc are its centre, Heidenhain has only LN, and the Siemens corpus has no A3= at all (controller-mapping 11.1). A Siemens G2 or G3 with A3= B3= C3= stays RAW until a further vector form is decided, as D81 and language 4.3 expect. The readers then change as follow-ups to the finished P3-02 and P3-05: LN with FMAX, and G0 with I J K under G43.5, read as RAPID with TX TY TZ. Alternative: LINE only, as D81 is worded and as both readers read today. Vector words under RAPID, ARC and CYCLE_CALL then all get the new ERROR, and LN with FMAX stays RAW.
Where: Language 4.2 (TCPM row), 4.3 (TX and NX rows), 5 rule 2; VM 2.2 (tool vector row), 3.1 (vector form paragraph), 5; D81 (a Clarified line); the TX to NZ meanings in src/Ncx.Core/Catalog, which generate docs/spec/generated/word-catalog.md (ranks 240 to 290). Code: src/Ncx.Core/VirtualMachine/ToolVectorRules.cs Apply (TODO(question) at line 44); src/Ncx.Readers/Heidenhain/HeidenhainMotion.cs ReadVectorLine; src/Ncx.Readers/Fanuc/FanucMotion.cs ReadMotion and ReadToolVector.

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, not confirmed by the maintainer: the manuals do not settle this. The manuals confirm the RAPID half of the recommendation and refute the ARC half for Fanuc. Fanuc documents the tool-direction words I J K under the heading "Positionierung und Lineare Interpolation für Tool Center Point-Steuerung (Typ 2)", so a positioning block with a vector is the documented form, not an invention — the reader follow-up for G0 with I J K under G43.5 is right. But the very next section is "Kreisinterpolation für Tool Center Point-Steuerung (Typ 2)": under G43.5 a G02/G03 block carries I J K as the tool-axis direction at the block end and the arc is given by R, because I J K are no longer free to be the centre. So the draft's reason "the I J K of a Fanuc arc are its centre" holds only for TCP type 1 (G43.4), and an ERROR for vector words under ARC would make NCX unable to carry a real Fanuc G43.5 arc. Heidenhain has no such form (LN is a straight-line block only) and Siemens documents A3= B3= C3= with G1; no manual in the library shows a vector on a cycle-call block, so an ERROR under CYCLE_CALL is safe.
Evidence: `Fanuc_30i-B_Bedienung-Drehen-Fraesen_B-64484EN_EN`, p. 783-784 (Chapter 22, under the heading for positioning and linear interpolation with tool centre point control type 2: after the starting block `G43.5 IP_ H_ Q_`, the following blocks have the form `IP_ I_ J_ K_`, where I, J, K are the tool axis direction at the block end in the programming coordinate system. Caution 2 adds that a block in which none of I, J, K is defined takes over the compensation vector of the previous block); `Fanuc_30i-B_Bedienung-Drehen-Fraesen_B-64484EN_EN`, p. 786-787 (The section for circular interpolation under tool centre point control type 2 gives the block as G17/G18/G19 with G02 or G03, the end point, I J K, R and F, and says I, J, K are the tool axis direction at the block end. Caution 1 adds that only the arc radius R can be given, because the distance from start point to arc centre cannot be specified with I, J and K); `Fanuc_30i-B_Bedienung-Drehen-Fraesen_B-64484EN_EN`, p. 785 (The corresponding section for type 1 (G43.4) defines I, J, K in a circular block as the distance from the start point to the arc centre, and the rotary axes are named separately as α and β. The two TCP types therefore give I J K two different meanings on an arc); `Heidenhain_iTNC530_Benutzerhandbuch-Klartext_NC-SW-340490_DE_2005`, p. 184, 187 (Section 5.4 says the three-dimensional tool compensation is carried out for straight-line blocks (Geraden-Sätze); the block format is `LN X Y Z NX NY NZ F M`, with F the feed and M an auxiliary function. No arc form of LN appears anywhere in the manual. The TNC 640 manual repeats the same opening sentence on page 456 of its Klartext manual); `Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl_Programmierhandbuch-NC-Programmierung_SW492_DE_2019`, p. 682, 684, 686 (Page 684 gives the orientation-programming syntax as `G1 X Y Z A3= B3= C3=` (with the A2/A4/A5 variants), G1 being linear interpolation and A3/B3/C3 the direction vector in the coordinates of the workpiece coordinate system. Pages 682 and 686 add that the vector points from the tool tip towards the tool holder, that its length does not matter, and that unprogrammed vector components are set to zero). (Citations re-paged to the cnc-manuals connector 2026-10-26.)

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

RAPID and LINE carry TX TY TZ (NX NY NZ optional) only under TCPM=ON, with one meaning: the tool direction at the end point, stored unresolved. ARC may carry TX TY TZ under TCPM=ON too, with the same meaning, because Fanuc G43.5 (TCP type 2) documents arcs with a tool vector. Vector words under CYCLE_CALL are a new ERROR code after VM213, which VM 5 names. Readers: Fanuc G0 with I J K under G43.5 reads as RAPID with TX TY TZ. G02/G03 with I J K and R under G43.5 reads as an ARC in its radius form with TX TY TZ, or stays RAW where NCX ARC has no radius form. Heidenhain LN with FMAX reads as RAPID with vector. A Siemens G2/G3 with A3= B3= C3= stays RAW until a Siemens vector arc is checked. Compilers: an ARC with a vector to Heidenhain (LN has no arc form), and for now to Siemens, is a compile ERROR like RAW.
Basis: manual
Source: FANUC 30i-B Operator's Manual B-64484EN, connector p. 783-784 (G43.5 positioning and linear: `IP_ I_ J_ K_`) and p. 786-787 (G43.5 circular: I J K is the tool direction at the block end, radius only by R). Heidenhain iTNC 530 Klartext p. 184/187 (LN is for straight lines only). The web check found nothing beyond a Mastercam post that lists "Type 2 Vector output (G43.5)" (https://mastercam.com/?p=519).
Differs from the recommendation: yes: ARC is allowed (no ERROR), and only CYCLE_CALL gets the new ERROR.
Confidence: medium
Code impact: ToolVectorRules (ERROR only under CYCLE_CALL); FanucMotion (G0 and G02/G03 under G43.5); HeidenhainMotion.ReadVectorLine (FMAX); compilers reject vector arcs where the family has none.

#### D186 ARC with both CENTER and R
Question: Language 4.3 gives ARC its target 'with CENTER or R, or over a sweep ANGLE around CENTER', and VM 3.2 describes the CENTER form and the R form separately. Neither says what a block with both is, and VM 5 lists 'ANGLE with R' but not CENTER with R. Case, starting from X=0 Y=0: ARC=CW X=5 Y=5 CENTER:X=5 CENTER:Y=0 R=5, where both words describe the same arc. A Fanuc control runs G2 X5. Y5. I5. R5.; the Fanuc manuals give R precedence and ignore I J K, which the documents do not record. Main reports VM223 (ArcRules.CheckWords; ArcTests), and the Fanuc reader keeps such a source block RAW ('an arc carries its centre or its radius, not both', FanucMotion.ReadArc).
Recommendation: Keep it an ERROR, as coded (VM223). VM 5 lists 'CENTER with R' next to 'ANGLE with R', and the ARC row of 4.3 reads 'with CENTER or with R, not both'. Reasons: the row and VM 3.2 give two alternative forms, and VM 3.2 keeps the center an R arc computes 'so the compiler can write either form', so one form carries the whole arc. The ANGLE rule is the parallel case, and this is the smallest change, matching both the VM and the Fanuc reader. How the Fanuc reader reads G2 with R and I J K is a follow-up to the finished P3-02: RAW as today, or the R form with a WARNING once fanuc.md 4 records the control's precedence. Alternative: accept both words and check them against each other. |start - center| must equal |R| within the arc tolerance, and the center must lie on the side that the sign of R and the direction give. A disagreement is an ERROR.
Where: Language 4.3 (ARC row); VM 3.2, 5; docs/spec/generated/diagnostics.md (VM223 row). Code: src/Ncx.Core/VirtualMachine/ArcRules.cs CheckWords (TODO(question) at line 222); src/Ncx.Readers/Fanuc/FanucMotion.cs ReadArc; controllers/fanuc.md 4 (G2/G3 paragraph) if the precedence is confirmed.

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, not confirmed by the maintainer: the manuals do not settle this. The manuals do not settle whether NCX should reject an ARC with both CENTER and R — that stays an NCX choice and VM223 as coded is defensible — but they do settle the control fact the draft left open: on Fanuc, if I, J, K and R stand in the same G02/G03 block, the arc defined by R takes precedence and the remaining addresses are ignored. That can now be recorded in fanuc.md 4, and it makes the follow-up for the Fanuc reader a real choice: read such a source block as the R form with a WARNING rather than keeping it RAW. On the other two controls the case cannot arise in a single block at all: Siemens keeps the two forms in separate sections, with a note that the centre need not be given when CR= is used, and Heidenhain programs the circle centre in a block of its own (CC in Klartext, I/J in DIN/ISO) that stays modal, while the arc block is either the centre form (C, G02 without R) or the radius form (CR, G02 with R).
Evidence: `Fanuc_30i-B_Bedienung-Drehen-Fraesen_B-64484EN_EN`, p. 80 (Under the restrictions of circular interpolation, a paragraph headed "Gleichzeitige Spezifikation von R und I, J, und K" states that when I, J, K and R are given together the arc defined by address R has precedence and the other addresses are ignored); `Fanuc_30i-B_Bedienung-Drehen-Fraesen_B-64484EN_EN`, p. 79 (The same section introduces R as an alternative to I, J, K for defining the arc, with a negative R for an arc greater than 180 degrees, and notes that a full circle can only be programmed with I, J, K); `Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl-828D_Programmierhandbuch-Grundlagen_DE_2013`, p. 199 and 200 (Section 9.6.3 gives G2/G3 with CR= and the end point as its own form, with a note that the centre need not be given this way and that full circles must be programmed over the end point and the interpolation parameters instead. The centre form is a separate section; no rule for both together is given); `Heidenhain_TNC640_Programmierung-Klartext_892903-18_NC-SW-34059x-10_DE_2019`, p. 159 and 160 ("Kreisbahn C um Kreismittelpunkt CC" requires the centre CC to be set in a block before the arc; "Kreisbahn CR mit festgelegtem Radius" lists only the end-point coordinates, the radius R, the direction DR, M and F. The two are different block types, so one block never carries a centre and a radius); `Heidenhain_TNC640_Programmierung-DIN-ISO_892909-18_NC-SW-34059x-10_DE_2019`, p. 160, 161 and 162 (In Heidenhain DIN/ISO the circle centre is its own block ("N50 I+25 J+25*"), set before the arc and modal until a new centre is programmed; the arc is then either G02/G03 around that centre or, in the following section, G02/G03 with R. The G02 block itself never carries I and J). (Citations re-paged to the cnc-manuals connector 2026-10-26.)

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

Keep VM223: an ARC with both CENTER and R is an ERROR; VM 5 lists "CENTER with R" next to "ANGLE with R", and the 4.3 row reads "with CENTER or with R, not both". Record in fanuc.md 4 that R takes precedence and I/J/K are ignored; the Fanuc reader then reads such a G2/G3 as the R form with a WARNING instead of RAW (P3-02 follow-up).
Basis: manual
Source: Fanuc B-64484EN G02/G03: with I, J, K and R in one block the R arc wins, the rest is ignored. Siemens and Heidenhain cannot write both in one block.
Differs from the recommendation: no (fixes the follow-up choice to R form + WARNING)
Confidence: high
Code impact: Fanuc reader FanucMotion.ReadArc (R form + WARNING); docs.

#### D188 Cycle planes without a known value
Question: VM 3.3 requires 'known DEPTH and CLEARANCE' for the built-in family, VM 5 names the ERROR 'without DEPTH/CLEARANCE', and VM 1 makes a value from an expression UNKNOWN in STATIC mode. Language 4.7 makes SAFE optional, yet CYCLE_RETRACT=SAFE retracts to it, and no sentence says where the tool ends without SAFE. The Fanuc reader writes exactly that for G98 when the initial level is unknown (FanucCycles.WriteDefinition, WARNING FanucInitialLevelUnknown). Two cases: CYCLE=DRILL CLEARANCE={$Q2} DEPTH=-15 checked in STATIC mode, and CYCLE=DRILL CLEARANCE=5 DEPTH=-20 CYCLE_RETRACT=SAFE without SAFE. Main raises VM251 only for a missing word. A plane from an expression and a missing SAFE both leave the drilling axis unknown after the call, with no diagnostic.
Recommendation: Keep main's behaviour: 'known' in VM 3.3 means 'written'. In STATIC mode a plane written as an expression is no ERROR. It counts toward the VM 5 WARNING 'unresolved expression in STATIC mode', and INTERPRETED mode evaluates it. This is the same treatment as the expression position X={$Q1} of PATTERN_LOOP line 17, which STATIC mode cannot know (note 1). A plane without a value (from an expression, or SAFE missing under CYCLE_RETRACT=SAFE) makes the motions to that plane unknown, and the drilling axis after the call as well. The ERROR falls to a compiler that must write the value: SAFE as Heidenhain Q204 or Siemens RTP. The Fanuc compiler needs no value, since it writes G98. This follows D100, where HOME without a reference point is an ERROR only for a compiler. VM 3.3 gets this sentence, and VM 5 reads 'without DEPTH or CLEARANCE written'. Alternative for the second case only: CYCLE_RETRACT=SAFE without SAFE is an ERROR at check (VM 5), and the Fanuc reader keeps a G98 cycle with an unknown initial level as RAW.
Where: VM 3.3, 5 (ERROR list, VM251); language 4.7 (SAFE and CYCLE_RETRACT rows); src/Ncx.Core/VirtualMachine/CycleRules.cs Call (TODO(question) at lines 64-66), Drill (TODO(question) at lines 109-110), PlaneAt; src/Ncx.Readers/Fanuc/FanucCycles.cs WriteDefinition; P3-04 and P5-02 cycle compilers.

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, not confirmed by the maintainer: the manuals do not settle this. Nothing in the manuals speaks to STATIC checking or to a plane written as an expression, so that part stays an NCX choice and main's behaviour is not contradicted. What the manuals do settle is the asymmetry the recommendation rests on: on Fanuc the return level is never a programmed value — on a mill G98 returns to the initial level, which is simply where the tool stood, and G99 to the R level, and no address names it; on a lathe in G-code system A there is not even a G98/G99 for canned cycles, the tool always returns to the initial level. So a Fanuc compiler genuinely needs no SAFE. On Siemens, CYCLE81's retract plane RTP is the first positional parameter of the call and is filled in every example (SDIS may be left empty, RTP is not), and on Heidenhain the second set-up clearance Q204 is a parameter of CYCL DEF 200 itself. So putting the ERROR on the Siemens and Heidenhain compilers and not on the check is consistent with what those controls require.
Evidence: `Fanuc_30i-B_Bedienung-Fraesen_B-64484EN-2_EN`, p. 58 (Paragraph "Rückkehrebene G98/G99": after the hole bottom the tool goes either to point R or to the initial level, chosen by G98 and G99; the initial level stays unchanged even when drilling runs in G99. The same page says drilling data commanded in drilling mode are retained until changed or cleared); `Fanuc_30i-B_Bedienung-Drehen_B-64484EN-1_EN`, p. 25 and 93 (Note 6 of the G-code chapter: under G-code system A only the initial level is given as the canned cycle's return point. Page 93 repeats it: in system A the tool returns from the hole bottom to the initial level, and only in systems B and C do G98 and G99 choose between initial level and R level); Programmierhandbuch Zyklen SINUMERIK 840D sl/840D/840Di sl, p. 44 and 45 (no readable text in the cnc-manuals connector; the CYCLE81 signature with RTP as parameter 1 is in `Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl_Programmierhandbuch-NC-Programmierung_SW492_DE_2019`, p. 1082, and the call CYCLE81 (110, 100, 2, 35) in `Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl_HMI-Advanced-Bedienhandbuch_DE_2008`, p. 58-59) (CYCLE81 (RTP, RFP, SDIS, DP, DPR) with RTP the retract plane as an absolute value; the worked example calls CYCLE81 (110, 100, 2, 35), CYCLE81 (110, 102, , 35) and CYCLE81 (110, 100, 2, , 65), i.e. the safety distance or the depth form may be left out but the retract plane is always given as a number); `Heidenhain_TNC640_Zyklen_892905-18_NC-SW-34059x-10_DE_2019`, p. 89 (The cycle parameters of cycle 200 BOHREN include Q204 "2. Sicherheits-Abstand" alongside Q200, Q201, Q203 and the rest, and the sample CYCL DEF 200 block writes Q204=100, so the value is part of the cycle definition the compiler must emit). (Citations re-paged to the cnc-manuals connector 2026-10-26.)

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

"Known" in VM 3.3 means "written". A plane from an expression in STATIC mode counts toward the VM 5 "unresolved expression" WARNING; a plane without a value (expression, or SAFE missing under CYCLE_RETRACT=SAFE) makes the motions to it and the drilling axis after the call unknown. The ERROR falls to the compiler that must write it (Heidenhain Q204, Siemens RTP); the Fanuc compiler writes G98 and needs none. VM 5 reads "without DEPTH or CLEARANCE written".
Basis: manual
Source: Fanuc return level is never programmed (G98 = initial level; lathe system A has no G98/G99); Siemens CYCLE81 RTP is always filled (840D Zyklen LY4401 p. 51); Heidenhain Q204 is a CYCL DEF 200 parameter.
Differs from the recommendation: no
Confidence: high
Code impact: Siemens/Heidenhain compilers (ERROR on missing SAFE); VM unknown-axis marking.

#### D190 Motions of an expanded cycle call (ExpandCycles)
Question: VM 3.3 names the pecking with PECK, the dwell with CYCLE_DWELL, the spindle reversal for TAP, and the retract to CLEARANCE or SAFE. Under the option ExpandCycles (D37) it raises the call as individual MOTION events, which feed the runtime estimate and the segment analytics of VM 8. No document says how each motion moves. Main works as follows (CycleRules.Drill, Pecks). A known PECK above 0 splits the feed on any cycle of the family. Between the pecks the tool goes at rapid to CLEARANCE and at rapid back to the depth reached, except CHIP_BREAK, which feeds on without leaving the hole. The final retract is a rapid, except TAP, which feeds out at CYCLE_F all the way to the retract plane, SAFE included under CYCLE_RETRACT=SAFE. The dwell moves nothing. For REAM the documents point to a retract at feed, which main does not do. CYCLE85 has the retract feed RFF (controller-mapping 5, siemens 7), heidenhain 5 names Q208 the retraction feed, and BOHREN.h writes Q208=Q206 on cycle 201 (D164).
Recommendation: Write main's model into VM 3.3 with two changes. The model: a rapid in the plane to the call point, then a rapid to CLEARANCE. A known PECK above 0 splits the feed into steps of PECK, on any cycle of the family as main does; only PECK and CHIP_BREAK carry PECK from a reader. Between the steps the tool returns at rapid to CLEARANCE and back to the depth reached. The control's re-approach distance has no NCX word, so 0 is taken. CHIP_BREAK feeds on without leaving the hole, because its lift is a control setting. CYCLE_DWELL is time at DEPTH with no motion (VM 8 adds it). The retract is a rapid, for BORE after the spindle stop. Change 1: REAM feeds out at CYCLE_F, like TAP. D160, still open, also describes mill G85 as feed in and feed out, and D164 writes Q208 = Q206 for cycle 201. Change 2: TAP and REAM feed out only to CLEARANCE, and under CYCLE_RETRACT=SAFE the rest of the way to SAFE is a rapid. That is what Fanuc G84 and G85 do under G98, and Heidenhain 201 and 207 do with Q204 (our reading of the manuals, not in the documents). Main instead feeds TAP all the way to SAFE. Alternative: keep REAM's rapid retract and TAP's feed to SAFE as on main.
Where: VM 3.3 (ExpandCycles sentence), VM 8 (runtime estimate); src/Ncx.Core/VirtualMachine/CycleRules.cs Drill (TODO(question) at lines 126-132; the final retract line) and Pecks; CycleMotion.cs; the ExpandCycles tests; related: D160, D164.

ANSWER: (Peter, 2026-10-07, drafted by Claude in project_spike) Accept main's model with both changes (REAM feeds out at CYCLE_F; TAP and REAM feed out only to CLEARANCE, the rest to SAFE as a rapid), updated by the later answers: the first peck counts from SURFACE (D355); the re-approach distance between pecks and the CHIP_BREAK lift come from `[cycles] peck_clearance` and `chip_break_lift` when the machine file sets them, and are 0 or the family's behaviour when absent (D357). The CAM's simulation reads the same keys with the same defaults (opencam D-061), so the expanded motions and the CAM's picture agree.
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, not confirmed by the maintainer: Both changes are right and are documented on all three controls, but the re-approach distance is not 0. Change 1 (REAM feeds out): Heidenhain cycle 201 has Q208 "Vorschub Rückzug", the speed at which the tool leaves the hole, and falls back to the reaming feed when Q208 = 0; Fanuc's canned-cycle table gives G85 the retract column "Vorschub"; Siemens CYCLE85 retracts with G1 at RFF. Change 2 (feed out only to CLEARANCE, then rapid to SAFE): Heidenhain 201, 202, 203, 206 and 207 all retract to the Sicherheits-Abstand and go from there to the 2. Sicherheits-Abstand with FMAX; the Fanuc cycle sequence is "Vorgang 5 Rückzug bis Punkt R, Vorgang 6 Eilgang bis Ausgangspunkt"; Siemens CYCLE84 and CYCLE85 retract to the reference plane at the thread or RFF feed and then to the retract plane with G0. The one clause to drop is "the control's re-approach distance ... so 0 is taken": Fanuc rapids back to a distance d short of the previous depth (parameter 5115 for G83, 5114 for G73) and the TNC comes back at FMAX only as far as the Sicherheits-Abstand above the depth reached, so taking 0 makes the ExpandCycles rapid longer than any control's and biases the runtime estimate.
Evidence: HEIDENHAIN iTNC 530, Benutzer-Handbuch Zyklenprogrammierung (670 388-12, NC-SW 340490-07), p. 81, 82 (Cycle 201 REIBEN, step 4: the TNC moves the tool back to the safety clearance at the feed F and from there, if one was entered, to the second safety clearance with FMAX. The parameter page explains Q208 as the speed for leaving the hole and says the reaming feed applies when Q208 = 0); HEIDENHAIN iTNC 530, Benutzer-Handbuch Zyklenprogrammierung (670 388-12, NC-SW 340490-07), p. 111, 113 (Cycles 206 and 207 both say that after the dwell the spindle direction is reversed and the tool is pulled back to the safety clearance, and that the TNC goes from there to the second safety clearance with FMAX. At the safety clearance 206 reverses the spindle again and 207 stops it); HEIDENHAIN iTNC 530, Benutzer-Handbuch Zyklenprogrammierung (670 388-12, NC-SW 340490-07), p. 79, 83, 87 (Cycle 200, step 3: between pecks the TNC pulls back at FMAX to the safety clearance, dwells there if programmed, and then goes at FMAX back down to the safety clearance above the previous infeed depth; step 6 leaves the hole bottom with FMAX. Cycle 202 (page 83) orients the spindle to Q336, clears by a fixed 0.2 mm if a direction was chosen, and only then retracts at the Vorschub Rückzug to the clearance. Cycle 203 (page 87) differs again: without chip breaking it retracts at the Vorschub Rückzug, and with chip breaking it only pulls back by the programmed retract value and carries on inside the hole); FANUC Series 30i/31i/32i-MODEL B, Bedienungshandbuch Fräsen (B-64484GE-2), p. 62, 75, 84 (PDF; printed 46, 59, 68) (Table 5.1 (a) has a retract column: G73, G76, G81, G82, G83, G86 and G87 retract at Eilgang, G74, G84, G85 and G89 at Vorschub. The same page 62 also lists the six operations of a canned cycle, ending "Vorgang 6 Verfahren im Eilgang bis zum Ausgangspunkt". G85's text says the tool goes back to point R at feed speed. G83's text says that from the second peck the tool rapids to a point d short of the previous end point, d being parameter 5115; the parameter list names 5114 as the corresponding retract value for the G73 high-speed peck cycle); FANUC Series 30i/31i/32i-MODEL B, Betriebshandbuch Drehen/Fräsen (B-64484GE/02), p. 1185 (PDF; printed 1151) (The same six operations are repeated in the operating part, in the section on the tool-retract switch: 1 positioning, 2 rapid to point R, 3 drilling, 4 operation at the hole bottom, 5 retract to point R, 6 rapid to the initial point); SINUMERIK 840D sl / 840D / 840Di sl, Programmierhandbuch Zyklen (01/2008), p. 61 (CYCLE84), 73 (CYCLE85) (CYCLE84's sequence ends with a retract to the reference plane advanced by the safety distance with G332 at SST1 and reversed direction, then to the retract plane with G0. CYCLE85's ends with a retract to that same reference plane with G1 at the retract feed RFF, then to the retract plane with G0).

#### D191 What table kinematics is for the ROT WARNING
Question: Language 4.2 says ROT applies 'On table kinematics', and a target 'that has no such option ignores it with a WARNING'. The MOVE, ROT row of controller-mapping 1 makes the option a matter of the controller family: the Fanuc cell says 'ROT not available (WARNING on compile)' and the Siemens cell 'ROT not available'. VM 5 instead warns for 'ROT on a target without table kinematics'. That is a property of the machine, which neither machine-config 4 nor 9 defines, and no document says whether the rule runs without a machine file (D103). On main (FrameValidation.CheckRot, VM422), table kinematics means a rotary [[axis]] owned by a resource of type table, and nothing is checked without a machine file. No file in machines/ has such an axis: the three mills have TABLE1 but no rotary axis, and the five lathes and mill-turns have their C axes on work spindles. So on main every ROT gets VM422 against every machine file. Case: TILT B=45 MOVE=TURN ROT=COORD against mori-ntx1000-mapps.toml gets VM422, although its C axis carries the workpiece as a C table would (B head without owner; C and C2 on the work spindles S1 and S2). On that Fanuc target ROT is ignored anyway, and the compiler says so. The kinematics reading decides the outcome on a Heidenhain mill-turn whose C table is a work spindle; no such file is in machines/.
Recommendation: Keep two WARNINGs with two owners. VM422 is the machine side: table kinematics means a rotary [[axis]] whose owner is a resource that holds the workpiece, of type table or work_spindle (machine-config 4, D41). A spindle's C axis carries the part as a table axis does, and the VM needs no [[node]] tree for this (machine-config 9 is read by the kinematics module only). Without a machine file the rule is not checked, as coded: the D103 default machine is no target (D77), and its C on MAIN would count anyway. The family side stays with the compilers, as controller-mapping 1 already writes it. Code: HasRotaryTable also accepts ResourceType.WorkSpindle, and VM 5, language 4.2 and the VM422 text state the definition. Alternative 1: table owners only, as coded, so a mill-turn's spindle C never counts. Alternative 2: VM422 also fires when the family has no ROT option (controller-mapping 1: Fanuc, Siemens), which the VM knows from [machine] controller. Then check shows what compile will ignore, at the cost of a second WARNING at compile time.
Where: VM 5 WARNING list; language 4.2 ROT row; machine-config 4 (one sentence at the owner key); controller-mapping 1 MOVE, ROT row (cited, unchanged); src/Ncx.Core/VirtualMachine/Validation/FrameValidation.cs CheckRot and HasRotaryTable (TODO(question) at line 97); docs/spec/generated/diagnostics.md (VM422 row).

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, not confirmed by the maintainer: the manuals do not settle this. Heidenhain's current generation does not make ROT a property of "table kinematics", so VM422 as coded and as recommended both mis-fire against a TNC 640. On the older iTNC 530 the choice is still offered "für Maschinen die einen C-Rundtisch haben", but on the TNC 640 the criterion is a free rotary axis in the current swivel situation — one whose rotation axis is parallel to the tool axis there and which is the first rotary axis in the kinematic chain from the workpiece — and the manual says outright that for the positioning behaviour it is irrelevant whether that axis is a table or a head axis, that the effect depends on the programmed spatial angles and the kinematics, that both transformation types have no effect when no free rotary axis arises, and no effect at all with PLANE AXIAL. Two consequences for NCX: a Heidenhain target should always warn for ROT written with TILT_AXIS, since the control ignores it there whatever the machine; and language 4.2's "Default TABLE" differs from Heidenhain's own default, which is COORD ROT when nothing is chosen.
Evidence: `Heidenhain_TNC640_Programmierung-Klartext_892903-18_NC-SW-34059x-10_DE_2019`, p. 435 ("Auswahl der Transformationsart": COORD ROT and TABLE ROT influence the orientation of the working-plane coordinate system through the axis position of a so-called free rotary axis; entering either is optional. An axis becomes free when it has no effect on the tool attitude because rotation axis and tool axis are parallel in this swivel situation, and when it is the first rotary axis in the kinematic chain starting from the workpiece. The effect therefore depends on the programmed spatial angles and on the machine kinematics; if no free rotary axis arises the two types have no effect, and with PLANE AXIAL they have no effect at all.); `Heidenhain_TNC640_Programmierung-Klartext_892903-18_NC-SW-34059x-10_DE_2019`, p. 436 ("Wirkung mit einer freien Drehachse": for the positioning behaviour of COORD ROT and TABLE ROT it is irrelevant whether the free rotary axis is a table axis or a head axis. The resulting axis position also depends on an active basic rotation, and the orientation of the working-plane system additionally on a programmed rotation such as cycle 10. The softkey table gives COORD ROT = free rotary axis to 0 plus working-plane system to the programmed spatial angle, and the page closes: "Wenn keine Transformationsart gewählt wurde, verwendet die Steuerung für die PLANE-Funktionen die Transformationsart COORD ROT."); `Heidenhain_TNC640_Programmierung-DIN-ISO_892909-18_NC-SW-34059x-10_DE_2019`, p. 401-402 (The same section in the DIN/ISO twin, word for word, including the softkey table and the same closing default sentence: with no transformation type chosen the control uses COORD ROT for the PLANE functions.); `Heidenhain_iTNC530_Programmierung-DIN-ISO_737_760-11_NC-SW-606420-02_DE_2011`, p. 432 (On the older generation the wording is the machine one: the function is available "für Maschinen die einen C-Rundtisch haben". COORD ROT means the PLANE function rotates only the coordinate system, the rotary table is not moved and the compensation is computed; TABLE ROT means the PLANE function positions the rotary table and the compensation happens by turning the workpiece. With PLANE AXIS both have no function.); `Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl_Programmierhandbuch-NC-Programmierung_SW492_DE_2019`, p. 1111-1113 (Section 3.25.1.34 gives the full CYCLE800 parameter list: _FR, _TC, _ST, _MODE, _X0, _Y0, _Z0, _A, _B, _C, _X1, _Y1, _Z1, _DIR, _FR_I. The nearest thing to a rotation option is the tens digit of _ST, "Werkzeugspitze nachführen", and _DIR for the swivel direction; there is no COORD/TABLE rotation choice, which is what controller-mapping 1 already records for Siemens.). (Citations re-paged to the cnc-manuals connector 2026-10-26.)

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

VM422 no longer tests for "table kinematics". With a machine file it fires for ROT when the machine has no rotary [[axis]] at all, whatever the owner (table, work_spindle or head), because no free rotary axis can then arise. Without a machine file, the machine-side test is skipped. A second WARNING (new code, or a second VM422 text) fires for ROT written with TILT_AXIS on any target, because the control ignores ROT there. Whether ROT takes effect depends on the spatial angles and the kinematics, so that question belongs to the kinematics module (D24) and is not checked by the VM. The family side (Fanuc and Siemens have no ROT) stays with the compilers, as controller-mapping 1 says. The Heidenhain compiler always writes the transformation type explicitly (COORD ROT or TABLE ROT), because the TNC 640 defaults to COORD ROT while NCX defaults to TABLE.
Basis: manual
Source: Heidenhain TNC 640 Klartext 892903-18, connector p. 435-436: a free rotary axis is the criterion, table or head does not matter, and ROT has no effect under PLANE AXIAL. The default is COORD ROT (DIN/ISO twin p. 401-402). Siemens 840D sl PGH p. 1111-1113 (CYCLE800 has no ROT option).
Differs from the recommendation: yes: the criterion is "has a rotary axis" (owner type does not matter), plus a TILT_AXIS warning and an explicit transformation type in the Heidenhain output.
Confidence: medium
Code impact: FrameValidation.CheckRot and HasRotaryTable (any rotary axis; ROT with TILT_AXIS warns); Heidenhain compiler always emits COORD ROT or TABLE ROT.

#### D192 F against max_feed: axes, units and feed mode (VM441 and the clamp)
Question: VM 5 lists 'F above an axis max_feed' (VM441) without saying which axes count, or how UNITS=INCH and FEED_MODE=PER_REV compare with max_feed, which machine-config 4 gives in mm/min (the example files write deg/min on rotary axes). Only VM 8 gives a rule, and only for the runtime estimate: the commanded feed 'per minute, or per revolution times rpm' is 'limited by the max_feed of every axis that moves'. It does not say whether the path feed or each moving axis's share of it is limited. No document names the plunge feed CYCLE_F, which VM 3.3 moves the drilling axis with ('feed to DEPTH with CYCLE_F'; D29). The VM on main compares F on the block that writes it, a block without motion included, with every linear axis of the machine, and skips PER_REV. So on doosan-puma-2600sy `LINE X=50 Z=-20 F=6000` warns about Y (max_feed 5000), although Y does not move. An F written earlier that later moves Y is never compared, and CYCLE_F is compared nowhere. Under limits = "clamp" the expander, which never sees VM state (architecture 5.5), compares F as written with the smallest max_feed of the axes its own block names, rotary ones included. So the VM and the expander use different rules.
Recommendation: VM441 takes the VM 8 rule, read as a limit on the path feed. At every LINE and ARC the VM compares the feed per minute with the max_feed of each linear axis the block moves. A rotary axis counts only in a block that moves rotary axes alone under ROTARY_FEED=DEG_MIN, where F is in deg/min (language 4.2). The feed per minute is F under PER_MIN, and F times the rpm under PER_REV (the rpm as VM 8 computes it; not compared while the rpm is unknown). Under UNITS=INCH it is also multiplied by 25.4. At each CYCLE_CALL of a built-in drilling cycle, CYCLE_F is compared the same way with the max_feed of the drilling axis (VM 3.3). Other cycles are not compared, because the VM does not know their motions (D94). One WARNING per F or CYCLE_F word, on the first block where it exceeds a limit. Under "clamp" the expander compares F as written with the smallest max_feed of the linear axes its own block names. That is the code on main without the rotary axes, and this literal comparison never lowers a feed that is within the limit. The VM keeps VM441 under both policies for the feeds the expander cannot judge: INCH, PER_REV, a block that moves only rotary axes, a modal F that later moves a slower axis, CYCLE_F (its drilling axis comes from WORKPLANE, which is VM state) and an expression. Reason: VM441 and VM 8 then read max_feed the same way, no WARNING names an axis that does not move, and the expander needs no state. Alternative 1: VM441 stays on the block that writes F but compares only the axes that block names, as the expander does. It is simpler, but a modal F that later moves a slower axis is never reported. Alternative 2: compare each moving axis's share of the feed (F times that axis's travel over the path length). A control's per-axis clamp limits that share, so a diagonal move with a short travel on a slow axis gets no WARNING. But the share needs the start point, VM 8 would have to read max_feed the same way, and the expander's literal comparison would then lower feeds that are within the limit.
Where: VM 5 (the VM441 item and its clamp clause); VM 8 (runtime estimate, the shared rule); VM 3.3 and language 4.7 (CYCLE_F); machine-config 4 (max_feed comment). Code: src/Ncx.Core/VirtualMachine/Validation/MotionValidation.cs CheckFeedAboveMaxFeed (TODO(question) at line 72), called from RunValidation.AfterBlock; src/Ncx.Core/Expander/LimitClamp.cs ClampFeed and AxisNameOf (TODO(question) at line 121); tests MotionValidationTests Feed_AboveTheMaxFeedOfTwoAxes_WarnsNamingBoth, Feed_AboveTheMaxFeedOfOneAxis_NamesThatAxis, Feed_InInchesAboveTheMaxFeed_Warns, Feed_PerRevolution_IsNotCompared, and LimitClampTests.D64_FeedAboveTheMaxFeedOfAMovingAxis_IsClamped.

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, corrected 2026-10-26 after the manual audit, not confirmed by the maintainer: The manuals do not settle this for every control. Fanuc limits each axis's share: parameter 1430 is the maximum cutting feedrate of each axis, and when the feedrate along an axis that results from the interpolation exceeds it, the cutting feedrate is clamped. Its unit follows the axis (mm/min, inch/min or deg/min), so a rotary axis carries its limit in deg/min as the example files write it. In normal direction control the control lowers the feedrate of the other axes to keep the inserted C-axis motion within its 1430 value. Parameter 1422, one maximum cutting feedrate common to all axes, belongs to the 16i/18i, where 1430 applies only to linear and circular interpolation; the 30i-B parameter manual shows no 1422 and uses 1430, or 1432 under acceleration/deceleration before interpolation such as AI contour control. That per-axis share is the draft's alternative 2. Siemens does what the Recommendation reads: the maximum path speed follows from the maximum speeds (MD32000) of the axes that take part in the path, the axis with the lowest one setting it, and by default the path feed counts only the programmed geometry axes (others only with FGROUP), which supports "rotary axes count only in rotary-only blocks". Heidenhain keeps minFeed, maxFeed, maxWorkFeed and rapidFeed per axis. No page compares F with an axis the block does not move, so main's behaviour is unsupported on every reading. The Recommendation's path-feed reading therefore agrees with Siemens and not with Fanuc, which clamps each axis's component.
Evidence: FANUC 30i-B Operator's Manual (B-64484EN), p. 178 (Cutting feedrate clamp: parameter 1430 sets the maximum cutting feedrate for each axis; when the feedrate along an axis exceeds it as a result of interpolation, the cutting feedrate is clamped to it); p. 371 (normal direction control: if the C-axis feedrate exceeds its 1430 value, the feedrate of each of the other axes is clamped to keep the C axis within it); FANUC 30i-B Parameter Manual (B-64490EN-05), p. 88-89 (1430 maximum cutting feedrate for each axis, unit mm/min, inch/min or degree/min; 1432 the per-axis maximum under acceleration/deceleration before interpolation, 1430 otherwise); FANUC 16i/18i-B Parameter Manual (B-63530EN-03), p. 102-103 (1430 valid only in linear and circular interpolation; the 1422 clamp applies in polar coordinate, cylindrical and involute interpolation); FANUC 16i/18i-MB Operator's Manual (B-63534EN-02), p. 518 (table: maximum cutting feedrate common to all axes 1422, for each axis 1430); Siemens SINUMERIK 840D sl/828D Funktionshandbuch Grundfunktionen (07/2012), p. 273 (path dynamics from the axial maxima of the axes taking part in the path: MD32000, MD32300, MD32431), p. 1509 (the path feed is the geometric sum of the participating axes; by default the programmed geometry axes, others with FGROUP) and p. 1510 (maximum path speed: the axis with the lowest maximum speed sets it); Heidenhain TNC 640 Technisches Handbuch (892899-18, NC-SW 34059x-09), p. 1951-1952 (CfgFeedLimits per axis: maxWorkFeed in mm/min or °/min).
Corrected: the clause "the path-feed reading is not the one the controls use either" held for Fanuc only; the Siemens Funktionshandbuch (p. 1510) bounds the path speed by the slowest participating axis, so the Recommendation's reading fits Siemens. Parameter 1422 is marked as 16i/18i, the 30i-B using 1430 or 1432; the German Fanuc citations and the TNC 640 pages are moved to what the connector shows.

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

As recommended. VM441 compares the per-minute path feed at every LINE and ARC with the max_feed of each linear axis the block moves. Rotary axes count only in a rotary-only block under ROTARY_FEED=DEG_MIN. PER_REV is converted with the known rpm, or skipped while the rpm is unknown. INCH is multiplied by 25.4. CYCLE_F of the built-in drilling cycles is compared with the drilling axis. There is one WARNING per F or CYCLE_F word, on its first exceeding block, and no axis is named that does not move. The WARNING text says the control "may clamp", because on Fanuc (per-axis share, parameter 1430) the clamp can be smaller or absent on a diagonal move. The expander's literal clamp compares F with the smallest max_feed of the linear axes its block names. That clamp is exact for Siemens and errs to the slow side for Fanuc, which is safe.
Basis: manual + logical
Source: Siemens Funktionshandbuch Grundfunktionen 07/2012 p. 1509-1510 (the slowest participating axis bounds the path speed). FANUC B-64484EN p. 178 and B-64490EN p. 88-89 (1430 per-axis share). Logical: a WARNING should be conservative and should not need the start point. The path reading is a superset of the Fanuc clamp and equal to the Siemens one.
Differs from the recommendation: no (adds only "may clamp" to the WARNING text)
Confidence: medium
Code impact: MotionValidation.CheckFeedAboveMaxFeed (moving axes only, PER_REV/INCH/CYCLE_F); LimitClamp drops rotary axes.

#### D195 Unreachable blocks inside a subprogram
Question: VM 3.9 ('Inside a program, a block after an unconditional JUMP that no LABEL makes reachable is unreachable: WARNING') and language 4.13 ('A block of a program that no LABEL makes reachable ...') name programs only. VM 5 lists 'unreachable block after an unconditional JUMP' without that restriction, and VM 3.9 keeps 'everything structural' even in a subprogram nothing calls. Case: SUB=BEGIN NAME=100 ... RETURN, then LINE X=5 with no LABEL, then SUB=END. The LINE is dead text. On main FlowValidation.CheckSection runs CheckReachable (VM523) for program sections only, so the subprogram reports nothing.
Recommendation: Check subprograms as well. The rule is structural (it runs in the pre-pass and needs no state), and VM 3.9 keeps structural rules in every subprogram. VM 5 already words it generally, and 'inside a program' comes from the D89 case that the sentence goes on to explain, not from an exclusion. In a subprogram, JUMP, RETURN and JUMP=END are the unconditional exits (CheckReachable already counts RETURN). SUB=END is never unreachable, just as PROGRAM=END is not. Code: drop the section-kind guard in CheckSection. VM 3.9 and language 4.13 then read 'program or subprogram', and the VM523 text changes with them. Alternative: programs only, as coded, with VM 5 reading 'unreachable block of a program'.
Where: VM 3.9 (last paragraph) and VM 5 WARNING list; language 4.13 (last sentence of the D89 paragraph); src/Ncx.Core/VirtualMachine/Validation/FlowValidation.cs CheckSection and CheckReachable (TODO(question) at line 153); docs/spec/generated/diagnostics.md (VM523 row).

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27: the library does not answer this (searched, with a whole-cache grep, for 'nicht erreichbar', 'unerreichbar', 'nie erreicht', 'nie ausgeführt', 'toter Code', 'unreachable', 'dead code' — every hit is about a position or orientation the kinematics cannot reach ($P_ORI_STAT, Festanschlag, Antastpunkt, Kreuzungspunkt), never about program flow. Three further searches of my own: 'wird nie durchlaufen', 'niemals erreicht/ausgeführt', 'Satz wird nicht erreicht' (no hits about flow); 'Syntaxprüfung', 'Programmprüfung', 'syntax check' (only Brother's delete screen, Nakamura's fixed-format field check and single-block dry runs — no static analysis); 'Label nicht vorhanden', 'LBL nicht definiert', 'Sprungziel nicht' (only the runtime alarm 14080 in the Siemens 840D sl, Sinumerik ONE/MC and High-Level-Language manuals). Manuals covered include the Fanuc 30i-B and 0i-D Betriebshandbücher, the TNC 640 Klartext and DIN/ISO manuals, the 840D sl Grundlagen, Arbeitsvorbereitung and NC-Programmierung manuals, and the machine-builder folder. The controls have no static reachability check at all, in a program or in a subprogram, and no manual describes a warning for a block after an unconditional jump; the only thing they report about program flow is a jump whose target does not exist, and only when the jump executes (Siemens alarm 14080 'Sprungziel nicht gefunden', which GOTOC exists specifically to suppress), so the choice is NCX's own static analysis and should be decided on the spec's own logic (VM 3.9 keeps everything structural in every subprogram, and VM 5 already words the rule without the restriction)). The recommendation above stands for the maintainer.

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

Check subprograms too: drop the section-kind guard in FlowValidation.CheckSection. JUMP, RETURN and JUMP=END are unconditional exits; SUB=END is never unreachable. VM 3.9, language 4.13 and the VM523 text read "program or subprogram".
Basis: logical
Source: Structural rule with no state; VM 3.9 keeps structural rules in every subprogram and VM 5 already words it generally. No control has static reachability checks.
Differs from the recommendation: no
Confidence: high
Code impact: Ncx.Core FlowValidation.CheckSection.

#### D196 Single-channel job without a job manifest
Question: VM 3.7 and 5 make 'SYNC in a single-channel job' a WARNING, but they do not say what the job is when a file is checked without a manifest (D15, machine-config 8). Language 4.8 defaults WITH to 'all channels of the job', and 4.14 lets the channel programs of a job stand in one file or in one file each. Case: the path-1 file of a Nakamura job (controller-mapping 7: O1000 is path 1, O1000.P-2 path 2) becomes an NCX file whose one program has CHANNEL=1. It is checked alone with --machine nakamura-ntjx ([machine] channels = [1, 2]). On main (ChannelValidation.IsSingleChannelJob, VM570) only the file decides: all its programs run on one channel, so every SYNC warns, although the machine has two paths and the marks are real. The loader reads [machine] channels into MachineIdentity.Channels, but the rule does not use it.
Recommendation: Without a manifest, a run is a single-channel job when the machine has one channel and the programs of the file all run on one channel, as coded. The machine has one channel when [machine] channels names one (machine-config 1), or when the file has no channels key. A file for one path of a machine with several channels belongs to a job that the manifest describes: its SYNC blocks are not warned, and check --job (P6-01) checks the marks. Without a machine file, the default machine has one channel. DefaultMachine.cs already sets Channels = [1], but VM 3.8 and D103 do not say so yet and should. The coded rule then applies unchanged there. Reason: the key already names the machine's paths, and the file-only rule turns the one-file-per-path layout of 4.14 and controller-mapping 7 into a false WARNING at every mark. Code: IsSingleChannelJob also reads MachineIdentity.Channels, which RunValidation.CheckFile passes in. Alternative: the file alone decides, as coded.
Where: VM 3.7 (the SYNC sentence) and VM 5; VM 3.8 closing paragraph and the D103 row (the default machine's one channel); machine-config 1 (channels key); src/Ncx.Core/VirtualMachine/Validation/ChannelValidation.cs IsSingleChannelJob (TODO(question) at line 37) and Validation/RunValidation.cs CheckFile; implementation 11 P1-04 and implementation 16 P6-01 ('SYNC in a single-channel run').

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, not confirmed by the maintainer: the manuals do not settle this. The manuals settle the machine side of the question, not the NCX rule. On a multi-channel Fanuc each channel has its own program folder and its own selected program; the selected programs run simultaneously but independently of one another, and the wait M code is the only thing that couples them — and Fanuc states outright that a wait M code need not be deleted from a program when only one channel is active, because the NOWT/NMWT signal makes the control ignore it. For the NTJX, Nakamura says the upper and the lower unit are programmed and operated separately, stored in separate unit memories, and synchronised at a given block by M100 to M199. So the path-1 file of an NTJX job is by construction one path of a two-path job and its marks are real; warning at every SYNC because that one file happens to hold one channel is wrong, which supports reading [machine] channels in IsSingleChannelJob. What the manuals cannot settle is the NCX definition itself — whether a run without a manifest is a job by the machine's channel count or only by what the file holds, and what the default machine's one channel means in VM 3.8 and D103.
Evidence: `Fanuc_30i-B_Bedienung-Drehen-Fraesen_B-64484EN_EN`, p. 1032–1033, ch. 23.1 (Verified. The machining programs for simultaneous multi-channel machining are stored in their own folders in program memory; for automatic operation one program per channel is selected from those folders, and the selected programs are then executed "gleichzeitig, aber unabhängig voneinander". When tool carrier 1 and tool carrier 2 have to wait for each other during machining, the wait function is used. Figure 23.1 (a) shows one program folder per channel for a four-channel system); `Fanuc_30i-B_Bedienung-Drehen-Fraesen_B-64484EN_EN`, p. 1037, ch. 23.2, VORSICHT 1–4 (Verified. A wait M code must stand alone in its block; unlike other M codes it is not output to the PMC; and — CAUTION 3 — if only one channel is active the wait M code does not have to be deleted: the signal NOWT (two-channel system) or NMWT (three or more) can be used to make the control ignore wait M codes in a machining program); `Fanuc_30i-B_Bedienung-Drehen-Fraesen_B-64484EN_EN`, p. 1033–1034, ch. 23.2 (Verified, and this is the page the previous answer attributed to 997: "Ohne Adresse P warten die Kanäle 1 und 2 aufeinander" — without the address P, channels 1 and 2 wait for each other. P is named either as the sum of the channels' binary values (bit 1 MWP of parameter 8103 = 0, table 23.2 (a): channel 1 = 1, channel 2 = 2, channel 3 = 4 …) or as a combination of channel numbers); `Nakamura-Tome_Fanuc_Programmierung_Programmierhandbuch-1_4810004ECL-1_DE_2013`, p. 25, §2-4-6 (Verified (the content is on p. 25 alone; p. 26 already starts chapter 3). For the STS/NTX(S)/NTJX/NTMX/MX5 series, designed for two spindles, a lower turret and an ATC tool, the upper and the lower machine unit can be programmed and operated separately. Special M codes M100 to M199 synchronise the upper and lower unit programs at a given block; the programs are stored separately in each unit's memory, and after the cycle start signal the programs loaded in each unit's memory are executed at the same time). (Citations re-paged to the cnc-manuals connector 2026-10-26.)

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

Without a manifest, a run is a single-channel job when the machine has one channel ([machine] channels names one, or the key is absent) and all programs of the file run on one channel. A file for one path of a multi-channel machine gets no SYNC WARNING; check --job (P6-01) checks the marks. VM 3.8 and D103 state that the default machine has one channel.
Basis: manual
Source: Fanuc multi-path: each path has its own program, coupled only by wait M codes, which need not be removed when one path runs; Nakamura NTJX upper/lower units programmed separately, synchronised by M100-M199.
Differs from the recommendation: no
Confidence: high
Code impact: Ncx.Core ChannelValidation.IsSingleChannelJob reads MachineIdentity.Channels (passed by RunValidation.CheckFile).

#### D197 Variables that STATE_CHANGE and trace report
Question: VM 7 raises STATE_CHANGE on 'any modal change', VM 6 has trace write 'one row per changed state variable per executed block', and architecture 5.1 raises STATE_CHANGE 'for every changed variable'. None of them gives the list or the names, which are what trace prints, what annotate appends and what a listener plugin reads. The VM 6 example ('X 33.22 -> 55.44') shows a position, which is not a row of VM 4. VM 3.10 names a variable by the key that sets it, with a role in its examples (SPINDLE:MAIN). Main reports the modal items of VM 4, the setpos shift per axis, the position per axis, and the tool vector and surface normal. It names each by its VM 3.10 state key with the resource id as address (X, F, CHAIN, SETPOS:X, TOOL:H1, PRELOAD:H1, OFFSET:LEN:H1, SPINDLE:S2, RPM:S2, COOLANT:STANDARD, FUNC:name, WORKPIECE, CYCLE), so the bare SPINDLE=CW of 2.5D_FRAESEN traces as SPINDLE:S2 on the default machine. It writes values as NCX writes them, empty when unknown or none. It leaves out the variables (VAR_CHANGE covers them, and P1-07's trace writes them as VAR:Q1), the program, flow and channel rows, the block items, and lastHolder.
Recommendation: Keep what main does and write the list into VM 7. STATE_CHANGE covers every VM 2 variable that a word sets and that outlives its block. Two groups are left out because they have events of their own: the variables (VAR_CHANGE), and the program, flow and channel rows (the program rows of 2.1, 2.7, 2.8). STATE_CHANGE covers the frame rows of 2.1 (units, workplane, origin, transform chain, setpos shift per axis, cylinder, polar, tcpm, rotary path and feed, the three tolerance rows, diameter, workpiece holder); feed, feed mode, compensation, position per axis, tool vector and surface normal (2.2); tool, preload and offsets per holder (2.3); the spindle rows per spindle (2.4); coolant channels and named functions (2.5); and the cycle (2.6). Each is named by its VM 3.10 state key with the resource id as address, and a position by its axis. lastHolder stays out because no key of its own sets it. Trace and annotate read STATE_CHANGE and VAR_CHANGE, and the architecture 9 row names both. Alternative: report lastHolder under a name of its own. It decides where a bare OFFSET goes, and TOOL:r naming the tool already in that spindle changes it without raising any event. Alternative for the address: the role, as the examples of VM 3.10 write it (SPINDLE:MAIN), and the id only for a resource without a role. The id is unambiguous and every resource has one, while a resource may have no role (the holder H1 of the mill files, D128), but the id does not stand in the program.
Where: VM 6; VM 7 (STATE_CHANGE row); VM 3.10 (state keys); architecture 5.1 (step L) and 9 (Trace, annotate row: STATE_CHANGE and VAR_CHANGE); src/Ncx.Core/VirtualMachine/Events/StateChanges.cs Between (TODO(question) at line 38); src/Ncx.Cli/History/TraceRow.cs; tests/Ncx.Acceptance/Expected/2.5D_FRAESEN.trace.txt.

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, not confirmed by the maintainer: the manuals do not settle this. No manual defines an event list for NCX, but the controls' own status displays show which state they consider reportable, and it matches the recommendation's list closely. The iTNC 530 splits its additional status displays into: general program information (main program, called programs, active machining cycle, pole CC, machining time, dwell counter), positions and coordinates (position and its type, swivel angle of the working plane, basic-rotation angle), tool (T number and name, RT sister tool, tool axis, length and radii, delta values from TOOL CALL and the tool table, tool life), coordinate conversions (datum table and number, active datum shift over up to 8 axes, mirrored axes, rotation angle, scaling factors in up to 6 axes, centre of the scaling), program-part repeats and subprograms, tool measuring, and active M functions with the machine builder's M functions in a list of their own; the general display carries the axis positions with F, S and M. Two things are left for the maintainer: the controls do report the program and flow items (called programs, repeat and subprogram level) that the recommendation moves to other events, and nothing in the manuals corresponds to lastHolder or decides between the resource id and the role as the address. Caveats: This is an analogy from an operator display to an event stream, not a rule a page states; treat it as a cross-check of the list, not as a decision. The split of the builder's M functions into their own list is the control's counterpart of the NCX FUNC:name / MFUNC distinction, which supports keeping FUNC:name in STATE_CHANGE.
Evidence: `Heidenhain_iTNC530_Benutzerhandbuch-Klartext_NC-SW-340422_DE_2004`, p. 46-48 (section 1.4 Status-Anzeigen) (Lists the additional status displays one by one: general program information, positions and coordinates with swivel and basic-rotation angle, tool data with number and name, coordinate conversions with datum shift, mirrored axes, rotation and scaling, program-part repeats and subprograms, tool measuring, and the active M functions with the builder's own ones in a separate list.); `Heidenhain_iTNC530_Benutzerhandbuch-Klartext_NC-SW-340422_DE_2004`, p. 45 (allgemeine Status-Anzeige) (The general status display shows the actual or nominal coordinates of the current position per machine axis together with spindle speed S, feed F and the effective miscellaneous function M.). (Citations re-paged to the cnc-manuals connector 2026-10-26.)
Confidence: low.

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

Keep main and write the list into VM 7: STATE_CHANGE covers every VM 2 variable a word sets that outlives its block (frame rows of 2.1, feed/mode/comp/position per axis/tool vector/normal of 2.2, tool/preload/offsets per holder, spindle rows per spindle, coolant channels and functions, cycle); variables go to VAR_CHANGE, program/flow/channel rows are out, lastHolder is out. Names are VM 3.10 state keys with the resource id as address, positions by axis.
Basis: logical
Source: Resource id is unambiguous and every resource has one (D128 holders have no role). iTNC 530 status displays list essentially the same set (analogy only).
Differs from the recommendation: no
Confidence: medium
Code impact: none (docs: VM 7, architecture 9).
