#### D239 Klartext TOOL CALL by name
Question: heidenhain.md 4 gives TOOL CALL "NAME" on the TNC 640, and language 4.4 lets TOOL take a string. heidenhain 7 rule 2 writes both offset words with the tool number, because the length and radius come from the tool table with the call. Language 2 rule 4 says NCX always states the offsets. But OFFSET:LEN and OFFSET:RAD take an integer register (language 4.4), and a tool called by name has none. Offsets are modal, and only an explicit word resets them (VM 4). So TOOL="NAME" alone would keep the previous tool's registers active, and a Fanuc or Siemens compile would write them for the new tool. machine-config 3 says a target with tool_name_allowed = false maps names to numbers, without a rule for how. D172 (templates for named tools) is open. Today HeidenhainToolCall.ReadCall keeps a TOOL CALL by name RAW.
Recommendation: Keep TOOL CALL "NAME" as RAW:HEIDENHAIN with a WARNING in 1.0 (D5), as coded, with one sentence in heidenhain 7 rule 2. Take it up again with D172 and the name-to-number mapping of machine-config 3. Reason: no NCX form available today states the offsets such a call loads, and a TOOL without them compiles with the wrong offsets. Alternative: OFFSET:LEN and OFFSET:RAD also take a string, the tool name, which means the offsets of that tool's table entry (language 4.4). The reader then writes TOOL="NAME" OFFSET:LEN="NAME" OFFSET:RAD="NAME". A Heidenhain target writes nothing for these words (offsets_with_change), and a target without names needs the mapping of machine-config 3.
Where: heidenhain.md 4, 7 rule 2; language 4.4 (OFFSET rows); machine-config 3 (tool_name_allowed); D172; src/Ncx.Readers/Heidenhain/HeidenhainToolCall.cs ReadCall (TODO(question) at line 35).

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, not confirmed by the maintainer: The manuals do not decide the NCX form, but they correct two premises and hand over the mapping rule that machine-config 3 leaves open. First, TOOL CALL "NAME" is not a TNC 640 function: the iTNC 530 of NC-SW 606420 has it too (softkey WERKZEUG-NAME, and the control puts the name in quotation marks itself), so heidenhain.md 4 needs correcting. Second, a name is only a second key into the same tool-table row as the number: the row carries T, "die Nummer, mit der das Werkzeug im Programm aufgerufen wird", and NAME, "der Name, mit dem Sie das Werkzeug im Programm aufrufen", beside L, R and R2. A named call therefore loads exactly that row's length and radius — the offsets are well defined, not unknown — and the name-to-number mapping is the tool table's own row. Whether 1.0 keeps the block RAW or lets OFFSET:LEN/OFFSET:RAD take the name stays the maintainer's call with D172.
Evidence: Heidenhain iTNC 530 — Benutzer-Handbuch HEIDENHAIN-Klartext-Dialog (NC-SW 606420-01, 2010), p. 180 (The TOOL CALL dialog's first field takes "Nummer oder Name des Werkzeugs"; the softkey WERKZEUG-NAME switches to name entry, the control puts a tool name in quotation marks automatically, and names refer to an entry in the active tool table TOOL.T. An index after a decimal point calls the same tool with other correction values. So the iTNC 530, not only the TNC 640, calls by name. Verified); Heidenhain iTNC 530 — Benutzer-Handbuch HEIDENHAIN-Klartext-Dialog (NC-SW 606420-01, 2010), p. 166 (The tool table's standard columns: T is the number the tool is called with in the program, NAME is the name it is called with (max 16 characters, capitals, no space), and L, R and R2 stand in the same row. Number and name are two keys into one row of correction data. Verified); Heidenhain iTNC 530 — Benutzer-Handbuch HEIDENHAIN-Klartext-Dialog (NC-SW 606420-01, 2010), p. 181 (TOOL DEF preselection takes the tool number, a Q parameter, or a tool name in quotation marks — the preload word accepts the same two keys. Verified).

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

Keep TOOL CALL "NAME" as RAW:HEIDENHAIN with a WARNING in 1.0, and revisit it with D172. Correct heidenhain.md 4: the iTNC 530 (606420) also calls by name. Record in machine-config 3 that the tool table row is the name-to-number mapping (T and NAME are keys of one row).
Basis: manual
Source: iTNC 530 Klartext 606420-01 p. 166, 180, 181 (cnc-manuals).
Differs from the recommendation: no
Confidence: high
Code impact: none (docs: heidenhain.md 4, 7 rule 2; machine-config 3).

#### D240 Position variables of a diameter-programmed X axis
Question: Machine-config 7 maps SYS_POS_X to Fanuc #5041 and SYS_MPOS_X to #5021, and language 4.12 names Siemens $AA_IW[X]; siemens.md 8 adds $AA_IM[X]. No document says whether these variables read a diameter or a radius on an X axis programmed in diameters (Fanuc diameter programming, Siemens DIAMON), and machine-config 7 has no factor. The Fanuc reader of P3-02, already merged, maps #5041 and #5021 to $SYS_POS_X and $SYS_MPOS_X unchanged. Whichever unit D216 picks for the NCX names, a variable that reads the other unit needs a factor in its reader and compiler.
Recommendation: Confirm from the Fanuc manual (system variables for position information) and the Sinumerik manual ($AA_IW and $AA_IM under DIAMON), or on the machines. If they read diameters, the unit D216 recommends for the NCX names, the mappings stay one to one and the merged Fanuc reader does not change. A variable that reads radii gets the factor 2 in its reader and 1/2 in its compiler under DIAMETER=ON on an axis with programming = "diameter" or "switchable". The factor is fixed per controller family, since machine-config 7 carries none. The Heidenhain FN 18 ids wait for D182.
Where: Machine-config 7 ([system_variables]); language 4.12 (system variables paragraph); siemens.md 8 (system variables); fanuc.md 7. Code: src/Ncx.Readers/Fanuc/FanucExpression.cs (the [system_variables] mapping, P3-02, merged); P3-06 (Fanuc compiler); P5-01 and P5-02 (Siemens); D182 (Heidenhain FN 18).

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, corrected 2026-10-26 after the manual audit, not confirmed by the maintainer: the manuals settle the Siemens half for the work frame and in large part for the machine frame; the Fanuc half is not settled. Under DIAMON or DIAM90 the facing-axis actual values are diameters, and the manual says this expressly covers reading actual values in the workpiece coordinate system with MEAS, MEAW, $P_EP[X] and $AA_IW[X], so $AA_IW reads a diameter and its mapping stays one to one. For $AA_IM the function manual now gives the answer the earlier proposal lacked: machine-frame data of a facing axis are radius values by default, and only MD20360 bits 6 and 7 switch actual values and their display to diameter. So $AA_IM[X] very likely reads a radius and, with the unit D216 recommends, gets the factor 2 in the Siemens reader and 1/2 in the compiler under DIAMETER=ON. That is an inference from the display data the page names, not a sentence about the variable, and PRESETONS, a machine-frame value, takes an active DIAMON into account, so it should be confirmed on a machine before the factor is fixed. For Fanuc, no manual in the library says whether #5041/#5021 read a diameter: the diameter-programming table lists the X command, the incremental value, the G50 coordinate setting and the position display as diameters, and arc R/I/K and feeds as radii, but never names the macro position variables, and parameter 1006 bit 3 is named there only for the travel command. Measure it on the machine before fixing the factor, as the recommendation already proposes. The proposal agrees with the recommendation.
Evidence: SINUMERIK 840D sl/828D Programmierhandbuch Grundlagen (03/2013), p. 169-170, section 8.3.6 (actual values of the facing axis under DIAMON or DIAM90 shown as diameters, also when read in the WCS with MEAS, MEAW, $P_EP[x] and $AA_IW[x].); SINUMERIK 840D sl/828D Funktionshandbuch Grundfunktionen (2012), p. 901-902 ("Fest Radius-bezogene Daten": for facing axes the display data in the machine coordinate system, offsets, frames, limits and feed are always radius values.); same manual, p. 902-903 (MD20360 bit 6 actual values, bit 7 their display, as diameter.); SINUMERIK 840D sl Programmierung BS.000504, p. 310-311 (PRESETONS: new actual value in the machine coordinate system; an active DIAMON is taken into account.); SINUMERIK 840D sl Listenhandbuch Systemvariable (SW 4.5, 2012), p. 477 and 479 ($AA_IW[ax] setpoint in the WCS, $AA_IM[ax] setpoint in the MCS; neither mentions diameter or radius.); FANUC Series 30i/31i/32i-MODEL B Operator's Manual B-64484EN, p. 488-489 (#5021ff [#_ABSMT] current position in the machine coordinate system, #5041ff [#_ABSOT] in the workpiece coordinate system, tool offset included, no diameter or radius column.); FANUC B-64484EN, p. 230-231, Table 8.4 (a) (diameter values under diameter programming, bit 3 (DIA) of parameter 1006; the macro position variables are not listed; the parameter-manual page for 1006 was not checked in the connector.).
Corrected: Replaced "$AA_IM is not in that list" with the positive statement of Grundfunktionen p. 901-902 that machine-frame data of a facing axis are radius values by default, which points to a factor 2 for $AA_IM[X], with the PRESETONS counter-hint of BS.000504 p. 310-311. The Fanuc pages now cite the English B-64484EN; the Fanuc half stays open.

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

Siemens: $AA_IW[X] reads a diameter under DIAMON, so it maps one to one. $AA_IM[X] reads a radius by default (MD20360 bits 6/7 off), so it gets factor 2 in the reader and 1/2 in the compiler under DIAMETER=ON, after one check on a machine. Fanuc: keep the merged 1:1 mapping of #5041/#5021. Until it is measured, the reader adds a WARNING when it maps one of these on an axis with programming = "diameter"/"switchable", so the guess is never silent. Heidenhain waits for D182.
Basis: manual (Siemens), web inconclusive (Fanuc)
Source: 840D sl Grundlagen 03/2013 p. 169-170; Grundfunktionen 2012 p. 901-903 (cnc-manuals). Fanuc unresolved: a VERICUT demo shows radius for a local X variable, https://forum.cgtech.com/viewtopic.php?id=371, which is not authoritative.
Differs from the recommendation: yes: adds the interim WARNING on the Fanuc mapping.
Confidence: medium (Siemens), low (Fanuc)
Code impact: Siemens reader/compiler factor for $AA_IM; FanucExpression warning on diameter axes.

#### D244 Fanuc G52 across G54..G59 and G92, with incremental words, and under G68, G68.2 or G51.1
Question: Fanuc 4 gives only 'G52 X Y Z local coordinate system (a shift inside the active G54); a new G52 replaces the old one, G52 X0 Y0 Z0 cancels'. Controller-mapping 2 (IX row) cites G52 U2.75 W1.25 of system A, whose meaning D117 left to P3-02, and language 4.2 lets ORIGIN empty the chain (D31). (a) After G52 X5., does a G55 keep the local shift, and may G54..G59 stand while G68, G68.2 or G51.1 is active? Main writes ORIGIN=2 and drops the shift with the chain (FanucFrames.ReadOrigin, FanucChain.Clear). (b) Is G52 U2.75 measured from the active local origin or from the workpiece origin? Main adds it to the active G52 on that axis and writes SHIFT=RESET, then SHIFT with the sum (ReadShift). (c) A G52 while G68, G68.2 or G51.1 is active: the earlier G52's SHIFT stands in front of their entries, so a replacing SHIFT=RESET would remove them. Main keeps such a G52 RAW with a WARNING (tests G52_WhileAG682IsActive_IsKeptAsRaw, G52_ReplacedWhileAG68Rotates_IsKeptAsRawAndTheRotationStays). (d) Two neighbouring cases that the same manual sections settle and that main handles without a marker. A G92 (SETPOS on a mill) while a G52 is active leaves the G52 SHIFT in the chain (ReadSetpos). A G28 or G30 while G68 or G51.1 is active reads as HOME (ReadHome).
Recommendation: Confirm in the Fanuc 30i manual (local coordinate system, and the limitations listed for coordinate system rotation, programmable mirror image and the tilted working plane). Our reading, which is not in the documents: G52 sets the local system 'in all the workpiece coordinate systems (G54 to G59)', with its origin given in workpiece coordinates. A G92 cancels the local system of the axes it names. G52, G54..G59, G92 and the reference position returns G27 to G30 must not be commanded in G68 or G51.1 mode, and G52, G54..G59 and G92 must not be commanded in G68.2 mode. If that is confirmed: (a) After an ORIGIN the reader writes the active G52 SHIFT again (FanucChain keeps Local through ORIGIN), and a G54..G59 in those modes stays RAW with a WARNING that names the limitation. (b) An incremental word moves the local origin from the active one, as main does. D117 takes 'RESET plus SHIFT' for the Fanuc fold, and the IX row of controller-mapping 2 drops G52. (c) The G52 stays RAW with that WARNING, as main does, and fanuc 4 names the limitation, so no chain rule is needed. (d) A G92 writes SHIFT=RESET before its SETPOS, then the G52 SHIFT of the axes it does not name, so that a later G52 X0 does not fold back a shift the control no longer holds. A G28 or G30 in G68 or G51.1 mode stays RAW with the limitation's WARNING. If the manual says a datum change cancels G52, ReadOrigin stays as it is.
Where: controllers/fanuc.md 4 (G52, G92 and G68 bullets), 9 rule 6; controller-mapping 1 (ORIGIN, SHIFT, SETPOS and HOME rows) and 2 (IX row); D117; language 4.2 (unchanged); src/Ncx.Readers/Fanuc/FanucFrames.cs ReadOrigin and ReadShift (TODO(question) at lines 76, 219 and 221), ReadSetpos and ReadHome; src/Ncx.Readers/Fanuc/FanucChain.cs Clear; tests/Ncx.Readers.Tests/Fanuc/FanucFrameTests.cs (the G52, G92 and G28 tests).

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, corrected 2026-10-26 after the manual audit, not confirmed by the maintainer: (a) A G52 sets the local system in all the workpiece systems G54 to G59, its origin given in workpiece coordinates, so a G55 after a G52 X5. keeps the shift: FanucChain must carry Local through ORIGIN and write the SHIFT again, as the recommendation says; main's dropping it with the chain is wrong. (b) The manuals contradict main and the recommendation: the local origin lies at the given value measured from the active G54..G59 zero whether it is written U/W or X/Z, and `G52 U0. W0.` cancels the local system rather than adding zero to it. Fanuc's own caution that a `G52 α0` puts that axis's local origin on the workpiece zero says the same, and so does the spec's existing fanuc 9 rule 6. (c) In two-dimensional G68 rotation mode and in G51.1 mirror mode no reference-position code (G27..G30) and no coordinate-system code (G52 to G59, G92) may be specified; the 0i-D names the alarm, PS0412, the 30i-B pages name none. In G68.2 tilted-working-plane mode the current English 30i-B edition lists G52, G53, G28/G29/G30 and G54..G59/G54.1 among the allowed codes and leaves out G92 (any code not listed raises PS5462), while the German G68.2 chapter excerpt leaves G52 out too; so whether G52 is legal there depends on the edition. A G54..G59 in G68.2 mode is possible with parameter 1205#6 (3TW) = 1, which keeps the tilted plane's zero shift. Keeping a G52 under G68.2 RAW stays safe, but its WARNING must say that NCX keeps the block native, not that the control forbids it, and fanuc 4 names the edition dependence; the limit the Recommendation states holds for G68 and G51.1, not as a fixed G68.2 rule. G51.1 may itself stand nested inside G68.2 and inside 3D conversion, so a G52 while G51.1 is active follows the G51.1 prohibition. (d) A G92 clears the local system of the axes it names and leaves the others untouched, exactly as the recommendation says; but a G28 or G30 under a two-dimensional G68 or under G51.1 is forbidden, so main's reading it as HOME there is wrong. In three-dimensional G68 (with I J K) G28/G29/G30 and G53 are allowed and main's reading holds, while G52, G54..G59 and G92 are not.
Evidence: FANUC 30i-B Operator's Manual (B-64484EN), p. 216-217 (§7.3: G52 sets a local system in all workpiece systems G54 to G59, its origin at the position given in the workpiece system; a new G52 names the new origin; cancelled by matching the two origins; caution 1 G52 α0; caution 4: a G92 (G50 in system A) cancels the local system except on the axes the block does not name; cautions 5 and 6: radius compensation cancelled for a moment, next move absolute); Nakamura-Tome Programmieranleitung NC-Wort-Adresse Fanuc 31i Model A (WY series, 2008), p. 51-52 (G52 U2.75 W1.75 puts a local shift on the active program zero, measured from the active G54..G59 whether written U/W or X/Z; U0./W0. or X0./Z0. clears it; G50 overwrites active G52 values; G52 cancels nose-radius compensation; next block absolute); Nakamura-Tome Programmierhandbuch Fanuc (2019), p. 52-53 (the same text); FANUC 30i-B Operator's Manual Milling (B-64484EN-2), p. 267 (coordinate system rotation: no G27..G30 and no G52 to G59 or G92 until the mode is cancelled); FANUC 0i-D Operator's Manual Milling (B-64304EN-2-01), p. 191 (the same, with alarm PS0412); FANUC 30i-B Operator's Manual (B-64484EN), p. 368 (programmable mirror image: the same prohibition); p. 948-949 (tilted working plane indexing: the specifiable G codes include G28, G29, G30, G52, G53, G54 to G59 and G54.1, and G51.1 on M, but not G92; any other raises PS5462; G51.1/G50.1 nest inside G68.2); p. 890-891 (G54 to G59 in tilted working plane indexing with 1205#6 (3TW) = 1; the zero shift of the tilted plane is kept); p. 344-345 (3D coordinate conversion: G28, G29, G30, G53 and G51.1 among the specifiable codes; G52, G54..G59 and G92 not); p. 202 (G53 not in one block with G50/G51, G50.1/G51.1 or G68/G69); FANUC 30i-B Programmierung Kapitel 5-Achsen G68.2 (B-64484GE excerpt), p. 55-56 (the German list of specifiable G codes, without G52 and G92).
Corrected: the claim that G52 raises PS5462 in G68.2 mode holds only for the edition behind the German excerpt; the current English 30i-B edition allows G52 there (EN p. 948-949), so the WARNING may not name a control limit and the proposal now departs from the Recommendation on G52 in G68.2 mode. Noted that PS0412 is named only in the 0i-D manual and that G51.1 may nest inside G68.2; the German citations are replaced by the English editions, and the Nakamura example reads W1.75.

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

(a) G52 holds in all of G54..G59. FanucChain keeps Local through ORIGIN, and after ORIGIN the reader writes the active G52 SHIFT again. (b) `G52 U W` is measured from the active G54..G59 zero, like X/Z, not added to the active G52. The reader writes SHIFT=RESET then SHIFT with the given values, and `G52 U0 W0` cancels like X0 Z0. This follows settled D117. (c) A G52, G54..G59 or G92 under 2D G68 or G51.1 stays RAW with a WARNING naming the control prohibition (PS0412 on 0i-D). The same codes under G68.2 stay RAW with a WARNING that says NCX keeps the block native, not that the control forbids it (allowed depending on the edition and on 1205#6). (d) A G92 writes SHIFT=RESET, its SETPOS, then the G52 SHIFT of the axes it does not name. A G28/G30 under 2D G68 or G51.1 stays RAW with the prohibition WARNING. Under 3D G68 (I J K) and G68.2 it reads as HOME, as main does.
Basis: manual
Source: FANUC B-64484EN p. 216-217 (G52 in all workpiece systems; caution 4 on G92), B-64484EN-2 p. 267, 0i-D B-64304EN-2 p. 191 (PS0412), B-64484EN p. 368, 948-949, 890-891, 344-345. Nakamura 31i-A p. 51-52 (U/W from the active zero). The web hits (e.g. https://www.machiningdoctor.com/gcodes/g52/) claim that a G54..G59 ends G52, but that contradicts the Fanuc manual and was not used.
Differs from the recommendation: yes: (b) is absolute, not incremental, and the G68.2 WARNING wording changes. (a), (c) for G68/G51.1 and (d) for G92 are as recommended.
Confidence: high
Code impact: FanucFrames.ReadOrigin/ReadShift/ReadSetpos/ReadHome and FanucChain.Clear; fanuc.md 4.

#### D245 Fanuc G68: centre without X Y, and a G68 or G68.2 while one is active
Question: Fanuc 4 gives 'G68 X Y R30 rotates the coordinate system about a point' and 'G68.2 X Y Z I J K tilted working plane'. Language 4.2 turns ROTATE 'around the current origin' and appends TILT in the frame where it stands. The documents do not say (a) what G68 R without X Y turns about, or (b) what a G68 or G68.2 does while one is already active: whether it replaces the active one or adds to it in the active frame. Main writes ROTATE for G68 R without a centre or with X0 Y0, and keeps any other centre RAW (FanucFrames.ReadRotation). A second G68 while a G68 is active, or a second G68.2 while a G68.2 is active, stays RAW, and the G69 resets the one the chain holds (FanucTilt.ReadTilt; tests G68_AboutAnotherPoint_IsKeptAsRaw, G682AndG68_WhileOneIsActive_AreKeptAsRaw). A G68 while a G68.2 is active, and a G68.2 while a G68 is active, are appended to the chain without a marker (ReadRotation checks only for a G68, ReadTilt only for a G68.2), and one G69 then removes both (ReadCancel).
Recommendation: Confirm in the Fanuc 30i manual (coordinate system rotation; tilted working plane). Our reading, which is not in the documents: without X Y the centre is the tool position at the G68 block. A G68 in G68 mode sets the new centre and angle, and R is absolute unless parameter 5400#0 lets G91 add it to the active angle. A G68.2 in G68.2 mode defines its plane in the workpiece frame and replaces the active one; the form that adds to it is the separate G68.4. Also confirm whether G68 may stand in G68.2 mode and G68.2 in G68 mode, and what one G69 cancels then. If that is confirmed: (a) G68 R without X Y is ROTATE only where the reader knows the tool stands at X0 Y0 of the plane. Elsewhere it stays RAW with a WARNING, like a G68 about another point. (b) A second G68 is ROTATE=RESET followed by ROTATE with the new angle. Under G91 it stays RAW, because the reader does not know parameter 5400#0. A second G68.2 cuts the chain at the SHIFT of the old origin (SHIFT=RESET, which cuts at the last shift, as wave-1 question 95 answered), or at its TILT (TILT=RESET) when the old G68.2 had no origin, and the new SHIFT and TILT follow. A TILT=RESET alone would leave the old origin in the chain. FanucChain.TryChange writes both changes and the entries the control keeps, as it does for the G69 (D31: the reader translates a replacing function into reset plus word). A cross form that the manual forbids stays RAW with a WARNING instead of being appended. Alternative: keep main as it is (ROTATE for a missing centre, RAW for a second G68 or G68.2). Alternative for a centre away from the origin, in (a) and in G68 X Y R alike: SHIFT to the centre, ROTATE, then SHIFT back. The G69 removes these with ROTATE=RESET, then SHIFT=RESET. This keeps the rotation in the chain, where the RAW block of main leaves every following motion read without the rotation.
Where: controllers/fanuc.md 4 (G68 and G68.2 bullets); controller-mapping 1 (ROTATE and TILT rows); language 4.2 (unchanged); src/Ncx.Readers/Fanuc/FanucFrames.cs ReadRotation (TODO(question) at lines 294 and 297) and ReadCancel; src/Ncx.Readers/Fanuc/FanucTilt.cs ReadTilt (TODO(question) at line 57); src/Ncx.Readers/Fanuc/FanucChain.cs TryChange and CutsAt; tests/Ncx.Readers.Tests/Fanuc/FanucFrameTests.cs G68R30_IsRotate_AndG69Resets, G68_AboutAnotherPoint_IsKeptAsRaw, G682AndG68_WhileOneIsActive_AreKeptAsRaw.

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, not confirmed by the maintainer: (a) Confirmed: if the centre α β is not programmed, the tool position at the G68 block is taken as the centre of rotation, so `G68 R30` alone is a rotation about wherever the tool stands — the reader may write plain ROTATE only where it knows that point is the plane origin. R is absolute unless parameter 5400#0 (RIN) lets G90/G91 decide, and an omitted R falls back to parameter 5410. (b) For the two-dimensional rotation a second G68 in rotation mode is legal and is the documented idiom: with RIN=1 it adds under G91 (Fanuc's own example calls `G68 X0 Y0 G91 R45.0` seven times), so absolute R replaces and G91 must stay RAW, as recommended. For G68.2 the recommendation is confirmed exactly: a further G68.2 in tilted-working-plane mode ("Mehrfacher Absolutbefehl", parameter 11221#0 MTW) sets up a new feature system from an additional conversion of the workpiece coordinate system and replaces the active one, while the additive form is the separate G68.4. But a second G68 **with I J K** is three-dimensional coordinate conversion, and there the second G68 is measured in the system the first created, i.e. it accumulates, and a third raises PS5043 — the recommendation's "replaces" is wrong for that form; cross forms are indeed illegal (PS5462), so RAW with a WARNING is right.
Evidence: FANUC 0i-D Operator's Manual Milling (B-64304EN-2/01), p. 190-191, section 6.10 (The format is G17/G18/G19 G68 α_ β_ R_ with α β the centre in absolute coordinates and R the angle; parameter RIN (5400#0) decides whether R is always absolute or absolute/incremental per G90/G91. Under "Drehungsmittelpunkt" it says that if α β is not programmed the tool position at the time G68 is programmed is taken as the centre of rotation, and if R is missing the value in parameter 5410 is used); FANUC 0i-D Operator's Manual Milling (B-64304EN-2/01), p. 196-197 ("Sich wiederholende Befehle für Koordinatensystemdrehung": a subprogram O2200 containing G68 X0 Y0 G91 R45.0 is called seven times (M98 P072200) with parameter RIN (5400#0) set to 1, so each repeat adds 45 degrees; the text notes the angle is treated as absolute or incremental according to G90/G91 only with that parameter set); FANUC 30i-B Operator's Manual (B-64484EN), p. 347 (Three-dimensional and two-dimensional coordinate conversion use the same codes G68 and G69; a block with I, J and K counts as the three-dimensional command, one without them as the two-dimensional one); FANUC 30i-B Operator's Manual (B-64484EN), p. 342-344, section 14.2; PS5044 on p. 343, PS5043 on p. 344 (Three-dimensional coordinate conversion may be done twice: the second G68's Xp Yp Zp, I J K and R refer to the coordinate system produced by the first, and if Xp Yp Zp are left out the first block's centre is reused. Attempting more than two raises alarm PS5043 "ZUVIELE G68 VERSCHA."; a missing I/J/K or all of I J K zero raises PS5044 "G68 FORMATFEHLER"); FANUC 30i-B Operator's Manual (B-64484EN), p. 916-918, sections 22.6.3.5 and 22.6.3.6 ("Mehrfacher Absolutbefehl": a further G68.2 inside tilted-working-plane mode sets up a feature coordinate system produced by an additional conversion of the workpiece coordinate system, its origin specified in the workpiece coordinate system, and G69 returns to the workpiece system; the worked example comments the second G68.2 block (N6) as setting up a new feature system. "Mehrfacher Inkrementalbefehl": G68.4 applies the conversion to the currently established feature system instead. Both need parameter 11221 bit 0 (MTW)); FANUC 30i-B Operator's Manual (B-64484EN), p. 948-950 (Of the rotation group only G69 (and G69.1 on lathes) appears among the codes specifiable in tilted-working-plane mode, and the modal codes under which a tilted-working-plane command may be given are the same list, so a G68 inside G68.2 and a G68.2 under an active G68 both give PS5462; the restrictions also say that trying to set up a new system by a three-dimensional coordinate conversion of a feature coordinate system raises an alarm); FANUC 30i-B Operator's Manual (B-64484EN), p. 66 (The machining-centre G list names G68.4 as the tilted-working-plane command in its incremental multiple form, beside G68.2 and G68.3). (Citations re-paged to the cnc-manuals connector 2026-10-26.)

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

(a) G68 R without X Y turns about the tool position. The reader writes ROTATE only where it knows the tool stands at X0 Y0 of the plane. Otherwise the block stays RAW with a WARNING, as does a centre away from the origin. A missing R (parameter 5410) also stays RAW. (b) A second 2D G68 under absolute R is ROTATE=RESET plus ROTATE. Under G91 it stays RAW, because 5400#0 is unknown. A second G68.2 replaces the first: SHIFT=RESET (or TILT=RESET when the old one had no origin), then the new SHIFT and TILT. G68.4 is the additive form. A second 3D G68 (with I J K) accumulates: it is appended in the frame of the first, with no reset. A third stays RAW with a WARNING naming PS5043, and one G69 removes both. Cross forms (G68 under G68.2, G68.2 under G68) stay RAW with a WARNING naming PS5462 instead of being appended.
Basis: manual + web
Source: FANUC 0i-D B-64304EN-2 p. 190-191, 196-197. FANUC 30i-B B-64484EN p. 342-344, 347, 916-918, 948-950. Web: Haas G68 reference, where the current location is the centre when none is given (https://haascnc.com/ar/service/codes-settings.type=gcode.machine=mill.value=G68.html).
Differs from the recommendation: yes: a second 3D G68 accumulates instead of replacing, and a third is RAW (PS5043).
Confidence: high
Code impact: FanucFrames.ReadRotation/ReadCancel, FanucTilt.ReadTilt, FanucChain.TryChange.

#### D248 R of a Fanuc lathe drilling cycle
Question: fanuc 6 and controller-mapping 5 describe R only for the mill, and only as the level the reader converts to the absolute CLEARANCE (Z absolute under G90). What R means under G91 is in main's code, not in the documents: FanucCycles.ReadDrilling and Level count it from the initial level, and the code comment cites fanuc 6 and controller-mapping 5, which do not say so. For the lathe drilling cycles G83..G89, no document says whether R is a level or a distance from the initial level, or whether it is a radius or a diameter on X. System A has no G91, and main reads R as the absolute level, as on a mill under G90. POLAR_FACE.ncx line 39 contradicts that. It reads 'G87 R2. X30.' after RAPID X=60 as CLEARANCE=54 (SURFACE=50), where main would write CLEARANCE=2, a clearance inside DEPTH=30. The 54 is SURFACE 50 plus R2 as a radius on the diameter axis, so the example reads R as a distance above the surface. No Fanuc document gives that reading, and the reader cannot compute it, because Fanuc has no surface address (D158). A distance from the initial level X60 would need R-3.
Recommendation: Confirm from the Fanuc lathe manual and the Nakamura manual. Our reading, which is not in the documents: R is the signed distance from the initial level to the R level, as a radius value, and parameters (RAB and RDI on the 0i/30i) can make it absolute or a diameter. If confirmed, the reader writes CLEARANCE = initial level + R, adding twice R on an X diameter under DIAMETER=ON. When the initial level is unknown, it keeps the block RAW, as Level already does for G91. A machine key covers the parameters only if a machine of the corpus sets them. fanuc 6 gets the rule, together with the mill rule main already follows (under G91, R counts from the initial level and Z from the R level). POLAR_FACE line 39 gets source words that give CLEARANCE=54 (for example R-3. from X60). No acceptance source has a lathe drilling cycle; the WY-250L pair has none.
Where: fanuc 6 (lathe R, and R under G91 on a mill); controller-mapping 5 (DEPTH, CLEARANCE, SURFACE, SAFE row); docs/spec/examples/POLAR_FACE.ncx line 39; src/Ncx.Readers/Fanuc/FanucCycles.cs ReadDrilling (TODO(question) at lines 526-527, and the comment above it) and Level; machine-config 1 only if a key is needed; related: D158, D160.

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, not confirmed by the maintainer: The R half of the draft's reading is confirmed and contradicts main: on a Fanuc lathe R of G83..G89 is the signed distance from the initial level to the R level, always a radius value, and in the default Series-16 format it is always incremental, so the reader writes CLEARANCE = initial level + R (twice R on an X diameter axis under DIAMETER=ON) and keeps the block RAW when the initial level is unknown. In G-code system A the tool always returns from the hole bottom to the initial level; G98/G99 choose the return level only in systems B and C. The parameters the draft names exist and are exactly RAB (5102#6, R absolute) and RDI (5102#7, R as a diameter value), but both act only in the Series-15 program format (0001#1 FCV = 1 and 5102#3 F16 = 0), so no machine key is needed for the corpus. The depth word is a separate question the manuals do not settle in one place: Fanuc's format table calls Z_ (G83/G84/G85) or X_ (G87/G88/G89) "the distance from point R to the bottom of the hole", but the same table writes the word as Z(W)_ / X(U)_, and in system A absolute or incremental is chosen by the address, not by G90/G91 — Nakamura's own manual accordingly says the word may be "an incremental value or an absolute value". So `X30.` written with the absolute address most likely is the absolute hole-bottom diameter.
Evidence: FANUC 30i-B Operator's Manual Turning (B-64484EN-1), p. 94, VORSICHT 1 to 3 (In every canned cycle R is "immer als Radius" and Z/X follow diameter or radius programming; only in G-code systems B and C do G90/G91 choose absolute or incremental for the hole position, the R-to-bottom distance and R; in the Series-16 format R point data is always incremental, and only in the Series-15 format does 5102#6 RAB make R absolute); FANUC 30i-B Operator's Manual Turning (B-64484EN-1), p. 95-96, format of G83/G87; the same table on 97 to 99 for G84/G88 and G85/G89 (`G83 X(U)_ C(H)_ Z(W)_ R_ P_ Q_ F_ K_ M_ ;` / `G87 Z(W)_ C(H)_ X(U)_ R_ ...` with "Z_ oder X_ : Entfernung zwischen Punkt R und Bohrungsgrund" and "R_ : Entfernung zwischen Ausgangsebene und R-Ebene". Table 4.3(b) on page 93 fixes the drilling axis: Z for G83/G84/G85, X for G87/G88/G89); Fanuc Series 30i/31i/32i-B, Operator's Manual Turning, B-64484EN-1/05, p. 94 (CAUTION) and 95 (format) (The English original says the same: "R_ : Always handled as a radius", "Z_ or X_ : The distance from point R to the bottom of the hole", "R_ : The distance from the initial level to point R level"); FANUC 30i-B Operator's Manual Turning (B-64484EN-1), p. 93, "Rückkehrebene" (With G-code system A the tool returns from the hole bottom to the initial level; only in systems B and C do G98 and G99 choose the initial level or the R level. The lathe G-code list of the master manual (page 71) confirms this by leaving the group 11 rows G98/G99 empty for system A); FANUC 30i-B Operator's Manual (B-64484EN), p. 63, note 8 (marked T) ("Wenn das G-Code-System A verwendet wird, wird Absolut- oder Inkrementalmaßprogrammierung nicht mit einem G-Code (G90/G91), sondern einem Adresswort (X/U, Z/W, C/H, Y/V) spezifiziert. Am Rückfahrpunkt des Bohr-Festzyklus wird nur die Ausgangsebene angegeben." This is why the depth word, written X or Z rather than U or W, is not automatically an R-relative distance); FANUC 30i-B Operator's Manual Milling (B-64484EN-2), p. 58, "Verfahrweg entlang der Bohrachse G90/G91", figure 5.1 (b) (The mill manual shows the same two readings side by side: under G90 both R and the depth word are absolute levels measured from Z = 0, under G91 R counts from the initial level and the depth word from point R. So the format table's wording describes only the incremental case; the mill's own example on page 66 writes `G90 G99 G81 ... Z-150. R-100.` as absolute levels); Nakamura-Tome Programming Manual (WY-250L), 4810004EEE, 2020, p. 283 (chapter 14-7) (The corpus machine's own manual: "R: Designate the distance from the initial level to the point R level in an incremental value"; "Z (X): Designate the distance from the point R level to the hole bottom in an incremental value or an absolute value"; "Q: ... should always be designated in an incremental value in radius". R is unambiguously an incremental distance, the depth word explicitly is not); Fanuc Series 30i-A, Parameter Manual, B-63950EN/03, p. 316 (printed 302), parameter 5102 (Bit 6 RAB: with a Series-15-format canned drilling cycle, R is an increment command (0) or an absolute command in G-code system A (1). Bit 7 RDI: R is based on radius specification (0) or on the diameter/radius specification of the drilling axis (1). Both apply only when 0001#1 (FCV) is 1 and 5102#3 (F16) is 0); FANUC 0i-D Operator's Manual Turning (B-64304EN-1/01), p. 98 and 99 (The same CAUTION 1 and 2 and the same address table on the 0i-D, so the rule is not new with the 30i. The 0i-D page prints only CAUTION 1 and 2; the Series-15/16 caution is the 30i's addition). (Citations re-paged to the cnc-manuals connector 2026-10-26.)

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

On a lathe G83..G89, R is the signed incremental distance from the initial level, always as a radius. The reader writes CLEARANCE = initial level + R, adding 2·R on an X axis under DIAMETER=ON. When the initial level is unknown, the block stays RAW. The depth word follows its address in system A: Z/X is the absolute bottom and W/U is incremental from R. In systems B/C it follows G90/G91. No machine key: RAB/RDI apply only to the Series-15 format. Fix POLAR_FACE line 39 to R-3. from X60 (CLEARANCE=54). Fanuc 6 also records the mill rule: under G91, R counts from the initial level and Z from R.
Basis: manual
Source: FANUC B-64484EN-1 p. 93-99; B-64484EN p. 63 note 8; Nakamura WY-250L 4810004EEE p. 283; Parameter Manual B-63950EN/03 p. 316 (5102) (cnc-manuals).
Differs from the recommendation: no (adds the depth-word rule)
Confidence: high
Code impact: FanucCycles.ReadDrilling/Level for lathe R; POLAR_FACE.ncx line 39.

#### D249 Fanuc M98 P with more than four digits on a 30i
Question: Controller-mapping 6 (CALL, TIMES row) reads the older form M98 P51002 as program 1002 called five times. Fanuc 1 gives the same form (M98 P30100) but also says O numbers have 'four digits, eight on 30i'. With eight-digit program numbers, P51002 may be program 51002 called once. Neither document says which reading a 30i applies, or whether the eight digits are standard or selected by an option or parameter. FanucMacro.CalledProgram applies the older form whenever P has more than four digits and no L, also for fanuc-mill-30i.toml. The Fanuc compiler writes M98 P L (P3-06), so only reading is affected.
Recommendation: The maintainer confirms from the 30i manual. Our reading of the Fanuc manuals, which is not in the documents: eight-digit program numbers are an option. With the option, P holds the program number and L the count, and the older form holds only on controls with four-digit numbers. If confirmed, add [machine] program_number_digits = 4 or 8 for Fanuc, default 4. With 8 the reader takes P as the whole program number and L as the count. Fanuc 1 and controller-mapping 6 then name the older form 'on controls with four-digit program numbers'. If the 30i always reads the older form, only fanuc 1 changes: 'eight on 30i' gets that qualification. The compiler writes M98 P L either way. Alternative: derive the rule from dialect = "30i" instead of adding a key.
Where: fanuc 1 (Oxxxx and subprogram bullets); controller-mapping 6 (CALL, TIMES row); machine-config 1 ([machine]); src/Ncx.Readers/Fanuc/FanucMacro.cs CalledProgram (TODO(question) at line 146) and Repeats; if the key comes, src/Ncx.Core/Machine/MachineIdentity.cs, src/Ncx.Config/MachineConfigLoader.Identity.cs and machines/fanuc-mill-30i.toml.

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, corrected 2026-10-26 after the manual audit, not confirmed by the maintainer: In the 30i program format the 30i tells the two forms of M98 P apart by syntax, not by the control's program-number length, so no [machine] program_number_digits key is needed for it. For a subprogram number of at most four digits the repeat count is prefixed into P (`M98 P51002` is program 1002 called five times) and L must not stand in the same block; for a number of five digits or more the repeat count must not be omitted. Eight-digit program numbers are the option "8-digit number function", so fanuc 1 keeps "eight on 30i" with that qualification. There is one exception: a 30i set to the optional Series 15 program format (setting parameter 0001#1) takes P as the subprogram number, uses the last four digits of a longer P, and counts with L, once when L is missing; there `M98 P51002` calls program 1002 once. So main's coded rule (the older form when P has more than four digits and no L) holds for the 30i program format only, and controller-mapping 6 gets the L rule with that limit. A machine whose programs use the Series 15 format would need its own reading, bound to the program format rather than to a digit count; that is closer to the Recommendation's alternative (a rule bound to the dialect) than to its key.
Evidence: FANUC 30i-B Operator's Manual (B-64484EN), p. 330 (Notes 1-5: a number of four digits or fewer called repeatedly is padded to four digits, P100100 = program 100 ten times, P50001 = program 1 five times; without a count it is called once; no L in the same block with that form; with a number of five digits or more the repeat count must not be omitted); p. 331 (example: M98 P51002 calls subprogram 1002 five times in succession); p. 323 (program number O plus four digits, eight with the 8-digit number function); FANUC 30i-B Operator's Manual Turning (B-64484EN-1), p. 245-246 (§6: Series 15 program format by setting parameter 0001#1, an option; §6.2 M98 Pxxxx Lyyyy: L not usable in the 30i program format unless the custom macro option is present; a P of more than four digits takes its last four digits as the subprogram number; without L the count is 1); FANUC 30i-B Operator's Manual Milling (B-64484EN-2), p. 298 (the same Series 15 subprogram-call rule on the mill).
Corrected: added the Series 15 program-format exception (EN-1 p. 245-246), under which P51002 calls program 1002 once, so main's rule is limited to the 30i program format; the German citations, including the three-format table the connector cannot show as text, are replaced by the English pages.

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

No `program_number_digits` key. The reader keeps main's 30i-format rule. M98 P with more than four digits and no L means the leading digits are the count and the last four are the program (P51002 = O1002 five times). M98 P L means P is the program and L is the count. Fanuc 1 says "four digits, eight with the 8-digit number option", and controller-mapping 6 states the rule as "in the 30i program format". The optional Series 15 program format (0001#1), where P51002 calls O1002 once, is not supported for now. Fanuc 1 names it as a known limitation. If a machine needs it later, it becomes a dialect value, not a digit-count key. The compiler writes M98 P L.
Basis: manual
Source: FANUC B-64484EN p. 323, 330-331; B-64484EN-1 p. 245-246; B-64484EN-2 p. 298. Web: a Fanuc manual excerpt with "M98 P51002 ;" = O1002 five times (https://industrialmonitordirect.com/blogs/knowledgebase/fanuc-0t-m98-troubleshooting-subprogram-repeat-counts).
Differs from the recommendation: yes: no machine key. The syntax decides, and the Series 15 format is left for a later dialect.
Confidence: medium
Code impact: none in FanucMacro.CalledProgram (keep it, and resolve the TODO); docs only (fanuc 1, controller-mapping 6).

#### D250 System variables and G10 of the Nakamura pair
Question: P3-02 expects the Nakamura pair to convert with RAW:NAKAMURA only for G411, G300, G10, G333, G131 and the [raw] codes. But G10 is a Fanuc control code (fanuc 4, fanuc 9 rule 7), and controller-mapping 9 lists it apart from the builder macros. The RAW address is the 'controller or builder dialect id' (language 4.1), [raw] names the builder codes (machine-config 5), and nakamura-ntjx.toml's [raw] does not list G10. Controller-mapping 8 lists G10 L2 P and G10 P10012 R Q in the Nakamura row 'Builder macros and flow', which is probably where the P3-02 sentence comes from. Path 2 reads #11099, #5024 and #5025, which stay RAW while unmapped (controller-mapping 9). nakamura-ntjx.toml has no [system_variables]. Machine-config 7's example maps SYS_WEAR_Z = "#11{index:03}" and SYS_MPOS_B = "#5024" for this program. It says the program reads #5024 and #5025 'for the sub spindle slide' without naming #5025. Fanuc 7 names #5021..#5025 only as 'current machine position'. Under the usual Fanuc numbering these are five different axes. The reader writes G10 as RAW:FANUC and keeps the three B blocks of path 2 as RAW:FANUC, and the test allows exactly those.
Recommendation: The specification answers G10, and it wins over a phase file (implementation/README.md, as D161 cites). G10 is RAW:FANUC as coded, and P3-02 drops G10 from its RAW:NAKAMURA list. Controller-mapping 8 lists what the builder manuals show, not the RAW address. For the variables, the maintainer confirms which axes #5024 and #5025 read on path 2 of the WY-250L; the program moves B relative to both of them. Add SYS_WEAR_Z = "#11{index:03}" to nakamura-ntjx.toml now, as machine-config 7 gives it. Add SYS_MPOS_B = "#5024" and the name of the #5025 axis once confirmed. The three blocks then read as expressions, and the P3-02 test allows no RAW:FANUC except G10. Until then the unmapped blocks stay RAW:FANUC (D5), and the P3-02 sentence names them.
Where: 13-phase-3-readers-compilers.md P3-02 acceptance (the RAW:NAKAMURA list); controller-mapping 8 (Nakamura row 'Builder macros and flow'); docs/spec/examples/machines/nakamura-ntjx.toml (new [system_variables], owned by P2-04); machine-config 7 (the #5024/#5025 comment); tests/Ncx.Acceptance/Examples/FanucReaderTests.cs Convert_NakamuraPath_KeepsOnlyTheNamedCodesAsRaw (UnmappedSystemVariable).

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, not confirmed by the maintainer: the manuals do not settle this. G10 is settled: `G10 L2 Pp IP_` is Fanuc's own programmable work-offset write, documented in the 30i coordinate-system chapter, so it is RAW:FANUC as coded and P3-02 drops it from the RAW:NAKAMURA list. SYS_WEAR_Z is now settled too, from the Fanuc manual and not only from the program's own comment: on a lathe with tool geometry/wear compensation memory, #10001-#10999 is the X-axis wear offset and #11001-#11999 the Z-axis wear offset, so #11099 is the Z wear register of offset number 99 and `SYS_WEAR_Z = "#11{index:03}"` can go into nakamura-ntjx.toml on the manual's authority. For the B axis the manuals now give a rule but not the number: Fanuc defines #5021+(n-1) as the machine position of the n-th axis of the path, and the WY-250L's own manual states that the index of the B-axis position variable is the B-axis number ("3rd axis: #5003, 4th axis: #5004, 5th axis: #5005") and uses the 5th in its worked example, while its parameter examples put Y as the 4th axis and Z as the 2nd — which, with the WY address order X, Z, C, Y, B, leaves B as the 5th axis and makes #5025 the B machine position and #5024 the Y one. That is consistent with the edition split in the builder's own transfer program (#5024 in the 2008 and 2009 Walter Meier guides, #5025 in the 2019 handbook, whose page 244 line is our path-2 sample verbatim). The mixed #5024/#5025 in NAKAMURA_WY250L_O1000.path2.nc is therefore very probably a stale line from an older edition rather than a second axis, but no page states the axis order of path 2 of a WY-250L, so SYS_MPOS_B should still be confirmed on the machine.
Evidence: FANUC 30i-B Operator's Manual (B-64484EN), p. 207, section 7.2.3 (`G10 L2 Pp IP_;` writes the external work offset (p=0) or the offsets of the workpiece coordinate systems 1 to 6 (p=1..6), absolute or added when the values are incremental. It is a standard Fanuc function of the coordinate-system chapter, not a builder macro); FANUC 30i-B Operator's Manual (B-64484EN), p. 488, "Positionsdaten #5001-#5080" (#5021 to #5040, macro name #_ABSMT[1] to [20], are the current position of the 1st to the 20th axis in the machine coordinate system, tool offset included, not readable while an axis moves. So the index counts controlled axes of the path, and #5024 and #5025 are the 4th and the 5th axis); Fanuc Series 30i/31i/32i-B, Operator's Manual Turning and Milling, B-64484EN/05, p. 455 (printed 423), tool compensation system variables, "With tool geometry/wear compensation memory" (For a lathe with more than 64 offset pairs: #10001-#10999 [#_OFSXW[n]] X-axis compensation value (wear), #11001-#11999 [#_OFSZW[n]] Z-axis compensation value (wear), #12001 nose radius wear, #15001 X geometry, #16001 Z geometry. So #11099 is the Z wear of offset number 99. (The German edition of the same table, PDF pages 458 to 460 (not in the connector), has the variable names and descriptions mis-paired and should not be used.)); Nakamura-Tome Programming Manual (WY-250L), 4810004EEE, 2020, p. 836 and 837 (Appendix 4-2 to 4-4) (Page 836 reads #5021 as "X-axis machine coordinate" and #10001 as "X-axis wear offset value of No.1". Page 837 gives the B-axis incremental command as `G53` then `G00B[#5005+50.0]`, and notes: "#5005: B-axis block end position (work coordinate system). The last digit indicates the B-axis number. When the B-axis number is the 3rd axis: #5003 / 4th axis: #5004 / 5th axis: #5005." The same page's parameter examples name "P1620 Y (4th axis)" and "P12#0 Z (2nd axis)"); Programmieranleitung Nakamura WY-Maschinen / Fanuc 31i-Model A (Walter Meier, 2008), p. 2 (address table) and 106 (transfer program) (The absolute axis addresses of the WY machines are X, Z, C, Y, B, the incremental ones U, W, H, V — four incremental addresses for five axes, which matches the WY-250L note that B has no incremental address. Page 106 writes all three B moves of the transfer against the same variable: `B[#5024+[ABS[#503]]]`, `B[#5024+[ABS[#504]]]`, `G300B[#5024+1.]A40.F199`); Nakamura-Tome Programmieranleitung NC-Wort und Adresse, Fanuc 18i-TB (Walter Meier, 2009), p. 114 (The same three moves, again all with #5024); Nakamura-Tome Programmierhandbuch (Walter Meier, 2019), Fanuc 0iTF/31iB/32iA, p. 183 and 244 (The same transfer written with #5025 throughout (`G1G98B[#5025+#503]`, `B[#5025+#504]`, `G300B[#5025+1.5]`), including `G300B[#5025+1.5] A40.F180(CUT-CHECK)` on page 244 — the line our path-2 sample carries verbatim). (Citations re-paged to the cnc-manuals connector 2026-10-26.)

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

G10 is RAW:FANUC, and P3-02 drops it from the RAW:NAKAMURA list. Add `SYS_WEAR_Z = "#11{index:03}"` to nakamura-ntjx.toml now. Add `SYS_MPOS_B = "#5025"`: the WY address order X,Z,C,Y,B makes B the 5th axis. Leave #5024 unmapped, so its block stays RAW:FANUC with a WARNING; it is likely a stale line from an older edition. The P3-02 test then allows RAW:FANUC only for G10 and that block. Confirm the B axis number on the machine when possible.
Basis: manual
Source: FANUC B-64484EN p. 207 (G10 L2), p. 488 (#5021+n-1); B-64484EN/05 p. 455 (#11001-); Nakamura 4810004EEE p. 836-837; Walter Meier 2008 p. 2/106, 2019 p. 183/244 (cnc-manuals).
Differs from the recommendation: no (names #5025 as B instead of #5024)
Confidence: medium
Code impact: nakamura-ntjx.toml [system_variables]; FanucReaderTests allowed RAW list.

#### D253 Replacing a Klartext transform that others follow; cycle 247 over active transforms
Question: heidenhain.md 3 and 7 rule 6 say that a new cycle 7 replaces the previous one. They say it for cycle 7 only. The reader treats 8, 10 and PLANE the same way (HeidenhainChain.TryReplace), and the manual should confirm that too. Language 4.2 and D31 turn a replacing controller into RESET plus the new word. A RESET removes its entry and everything after it (language 4.2, VM 2.1). Nothing says where the new transform acts when another was programmed after the old one. Take CYCL DEF 7 X+10, CYCL DEF 10 ROT+30, CYCL DEF 7 X+20. Does the frame shift by 20 and then rotate by 30? Or does it rotate by 30 and then shift by 20 along the rotated axes? heidenhain 3 also does not say whether cycle 247 ends an active cycle 7, 8 or 10, or a tilted plane, on the control. The reader writes 247 as ORIGIN, which empties the NCX chain. Today HeidenhainChain.TryReplace writes RESET plus the new entry only when the replaced entry is the last of the chain, and keeps the block RAW otherwise. HeidenhainFrameCycles.ReadOrigin writes ORIGIN alone.
Recommendation: The maintainer confirms on the iTNC 530 or from its manual. If the new cycle acts in the place of the old one, the reader writes the RESET, the new entry, and then the entries that followed the old one again, in their order (the pattern D124 recommends for MIRROR=OFF). If it acts at the end, the reader writes the RESET, the following entries, then the new one. For cycle 247, our reading of the cycle manual (not in the documents) is that activating a preset resets datum shift, mirror, rotation and scaling, which is ORIGIN as coded. If a tilted plane (PLANE, cycle 19) stays active, the reader writes it again after ORIGIN with MOVE=STAY. heidenhain 3 records both facts, and which cycles replace their own kind. Until then the code stays: RAW, and ORIGIN alone. The Fanuc counterparts (G52 over G68, a second G68, G54 over G52) are D244 and D245.
Where: heidenhain.md 3, 7 rule 6; language 4.2 (chain paragraph); controller-mapping 1 (SHIFT, ROTATE, MIRROR, ORIGIN rows); src/Ncx.Readers/Heidenhain/HeidenhainChain.cs TryReplace (TODO(question) at line 94) and HeidenhainFrameCycles.cs ReadOrigin (TODO(question) at line 92); HeidenhainPlane.cs Read.

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, not confirmed by the maintainer: Point by point, with the third point struck. (a) Replacement is a general rule, not a cycle-7 rule: a coordinate transformation is effective from its definition and acts "so lange, bis sie rückgesetzt oder neu definiert wird", and the cycles that rule covers are 7, 247, 8, 10, 11, 26 and 19. Cycle 19 is said again explicitly — a new cycle 19 with other angles needs no reset first — so HeidenhainChain.TryReplace may treat 8, 10 and cycle 19 like cycle 7. (b) The manual states NCX's own chain model: a datum shift before cycle 19 shifts the machine-fixed system, a datum shift after it shifts the tilted system, and "Gehen Sie beim Rücksetzen der Zyklen in der umgekehrten Reihenfolge wie beim Definieren vor" — reset in the reverse order of definition, which is language 4.2's rule that a RESET removes its entry and everything after it. (c) The 7-10-7 case is not in the library and I do not think the manual points to the in-place reading; see the caveats. (d) Cycle 247 on the TNC 640 resets exactly Nullpunktverschiebung, Spiegeln, Drehung, Maßfaktor and achsspezifischer Maßfaktor; the tilted plane is not in that list. On the iTNC 530 the cycle manual says only that activating a preset resets an active Nullpunkt-Verschiebung.
Evidence: Heidenhain iTNC 530 — Benutzer-Handbuch Zyklenprogrammierung (670 388-12, NC-SW 340490-07, 2011), p. 278 (Chapter head "Wirksamkeit der Koordinaten-Umrechnungen": a coordinate transformation is effective from its definition and is not called; it acts until it is reset or newly defined. The overview table on the same page lists the cycles covered: 7, 247, 8, 10, 11, 26 and 19. Resetting also happens by redefining with the basic values, at M2, M30 or END PGM, on selecting a new program, or with M142. Verified); Heidenhain iTNC 530 — Benutzer-Handbuch Zyklenprogrammierung (670 388-12, NC-SW 340490-07, 2011), p. 301 ("Kombination mit anderen Koordinaten-Umrechnungszyklen": the swivel always happens about the active datum; a datum shift before cycle 19 shifts the machine-fixed system, a datum shift after it shifts the tilted system; and "Wichtig: Gehen Sie beim Rücksetzen der Zyklen in der umgekehrten Reihenfolge wie beim Definieren vor", with a worked order (shift, tilt, rotation — then rotation, tilt, shift). The order-sensitive chain and the unwind-from-the-end rule, from the control's own book. Verified); Heidenhain TNC 640 — Benutzerhandbuch Zyklenprogrammierung (892905-18, 10/2019), p. 245 (The TNC 640's twin of that paragraph, word for word, including the numbered define-and-reset order. The chain model is not a quirk of the 2011 book. This is the page that bears against the in-place reading of point (c)); Heidenhain iTNC 530 — Benutzer-Handbuch Zyklenprogrammierung (670 388-12, NC-SW 340490-07, 2011), p. 302 (In the cycle 19 guide: to machine at another axis position you simply define cycle 19 again with the new angles — "Es ist in diesem Fall nicht erforderlich Zyklus 19 zurückzusetzen, Sie können direkt die neuen Winkelstellungen definieren." A new definition of the same kind replaces the old one. Verified); Heidenhain iTNC 530 — Benutzer-Handbuch Zyklenprogrammierung (670 388-12, NC-SW 340490-07, 2011), p. 289 (Cycle 10: the control rotates the coordinate system in the working plane about the active datum; the rotation is effective from its definition; it is reset by programming cycle 10 again with angle 0. It also cancels an active radius compensation. Verified); Heidenhain iTNC 530 — Benutzer-Handbuch Zyklenprogrammierung (670 388-12, NC-SW 340490-07, 2011), p. 279 (Cycle 7: absolute values refer to the workpiece datum fixed by Bezugspunkt-Setzen, incremental values to the last valid datum, which may already be shifted; it is reset by a new definition with 0 in every axis, by TRANS DATUM RESET, or from a datum table. Cycle 8 (page 287) is reset by defining SPIEGELN again with NO ENT. Verified); Heidenhain TNC 640 — Benutzerhandbuch Zyklenprogrammierung (892905-18, 10/2019), p. 247 (Cycle 247: when a preset from the Bezugspunkttabelle is activated the control resets Nullpunktverschiebung, Spiegeln, Drehung, Maßfaktor and achsspezifischer Maßfaktor. The tilted working plane is not named. After the cycle all coordinate entries and datum shifts, absolute and incremental, refer to the new preset. Verified); Heidenhain iTNC 530 — Benutzer-Handbuch Zyklenprogrammierung (670 388-12, NC-SW 340490-07, 2011), p. 286 (Cycle 247 on the older control: "Beim Aktivieren eines Bezugspunktes aus der Preset-Tabelle, setzt die TNC eine aktive Nullpunkt-Verschiebung zurück." Only the datum shift is named — no mirror, rotation or scaling, and no plane. Verified); Heidenhain iTNC 530 — Benutzer-Handbuch HEIDENHAIN-Klartext-Dialog (NC-SW 606420-01, 2010), p. 459 (PLANE RELATIV is the one additive form: its angle always acts relative to the active working plane, whichever function activated that plane, and you may chain as many as you like. Page 446 adds that PLANE functions must always be cancelled with PLANE RESET — entering 0 everywhere does not fully reset them. Neither page says in so many words that a new absolute PLANE replaces the active one. Verified).

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

(a) HeidenhainChain.TryReplace treats cycles 7, 8, 10, 11, 26 and 19 (and absolute PLANE) like cycle 7: a new definition of the same kind replaces the old one. Where the replaced entry is the last in the chain, write RESET plus the new entry (as coded). Where other entries follow it, keep the block RAW:HEIDENHAIN with a WARNING, as coded. The in-place reading versus the at-end reading (the 7-10-7 case) stays unresolved until someone tests it on a machine. (b) Heidenhain 3 records the "reset in reverse order of definition" rule as the control's own form of language 4.2. (d) Cycle 247 is read as ORIGIN only when the active chain holds nothing but SHIFT entries and, optionally, a tilt. An active tilt (PLANE or cycle 19) is then written again after ORIGIN with MOVE=STAY. If MIRROR, ROTATE or scaling is active, the 247 block stays RAW with a WARNING, because the TNC 640 resets them and the iTNC 530 manual names only the datum shift.
Basis: manual + logical
Source: iTNC 530 Zyklen 670388-12 p.278, 286, 301-302 and TNC 640 Zyklen 892905-18 p.245, 247 (connector pages, as cited in rationale D253). The audit (manual-audit-2026-10-26 section 5) leaves (c) open. Choosing RAW over a guess about the frame order follows the brief's safety rule.
Differs from the recommendation: yes. 247 does not always become ORIGIN. It becomes ORIGIN only where the two control generations agree, and is RAW otherwise. Part (c) is not decided.
Confidence: medium
Code impact: HeidenhainChain.TryReplace widened to 8/10/11/26/19; HeidenhainFrameCycles.ReadOrigin adds the tilt re-write and the RAW case.

### Eighth round: needed now

#### D257 O number of a program without NUMBER
Question: Language 4.1 makes NUMBER optional ('NAME, NUMBER and CHANNEL may follow'). Controller-mapping 1 maps PROGRAM=BEGIN NAME NUMBER to Oxxxx (name), and fanuc 1 names a program by its O number. No document says what the Fanuc compiler writes when NUMBER is missing. Klartext has no program number (controller-mapping 1; D217), so no program read from Heidenhain has one. PATTERN_LOOP.ncx has none either, although its line comment gives F: O0002, and MILLTURN_TRANSFER.ncx has none. Main reports CMP300 and writes no O line, so every such program fails to compile to Fanuc. D217's alternative 2 (drop NUMBER=1 from 2.5D_FRAESEN.ncx) would make the example itself fail to compile to Fanuc under this rule.
Recommendation: Without NUMBER, the compiler takes a NAME of digits as the number, as it already does for a SUB (controller-mapping 6). The digit limit is eight today and follows D249. Otherwise it takes the lowest number from 1 that no other program or subprogram of the output file uses, with a WARNING that names the number. The name stands in parentheses as usual. Reasons: compiling from another controller is the main path, and the O number is only the slot the control stores the program under. The WARNING matters because another program may already be stored in that slot. Alternative: keep the ERROR, so that the user adds NUMBER, or add a compile option --number n.
Where: language 4.1 (NUMBER row); controller-mapping 1 (PROGRAM=BEGIN row); fanuc 10 rule 3; D217, D249; src/Ncx.Compilers/Fanuc/FanucProgramFrame.cs:94 WriteProgramBegin; DiagnosticCodes.Fanuc.cs CMP300; tests/Ncx.Compilers.Tests/Fanuc/FanucWriterRulesTests.cs:171.

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, not confirmed by the maintainer: the manuals do not settle this. No manual says what a translator should write, so the choice stays NCX's. What the manuals do fix is the control's own fallback chain and two hard limits. Fallback chain: without an O number the control registers the first N number as the program number (of a five-digit N, the last four digits; if those are all zeros, the last registered number plus one), and with neither an O nor an N the operator has to type a number when the program is stored — which makes the generated-number branch of the recommendation a close match to the control's own behaviour. Limits: the program number 0 must not be used, so counting from 1 is right; and the numbers 8000 to 9999 are "sometimes" reserved by the machine builder and are protected against editing by parameter 3202 NE8/NE9 — on the Nakamura the C-axis subprogram is O9000, so a generated number in that range can collide with a builder program on a real machine.
Evidence: FANUC 30i-B Operator's Manual (B-64484EN), p. 323, "Programmnummer" (Every program is identified by O plus a four-digit number (eight with the 8-digit option). If the program number is missing at the start, the first sequence number N is used as the program number; with five-digit N numbers the last four digits are registered; if these are all zeros the last registered number plus one is taken; N0 cannot be a program number. If neither a program number nor a sequence number is present, a number must be typed in when the program is stored. A note adds: "Manchmal sind die Programmnummern 8000 bis 9999 vom Maschinenhersteller reserviert. Sie können dann nicht verwendet werden."); FANUC 30i-B Operator's Manual (B-64484EN), p. 324, ANMERKUNG ("Die Programmnummer 0 darf nicht benutzt werden. 0 darf demnach nicht für eine Satznummer verwendet werden, die als Programmnummer gilt."); FANUC 30i-B Operator's Manual (B-64484EN), p. 560, section 16.14 BESCHRÄNKUNGEN, "Betrieb im Editiermodus" (Setting bit 0 (NE8) and bit 4 (NE9) of parameter 3202 to 1 disables deleting and editing of custom-macro programs and subprograms with the numbers 8000 to 8999 and 9000 to 9999, to protect the registered builder programs); Nakamura-Tome Programmierhandbuch (Walter Meier, 2019), p. 76 (The builder's own machining examples call the C-axis subprogram with `M98 P9000 (C-ACHSE EIN)`, i.e. the 9000 range on this machine holds builder programs); FANUC 30i-B Operator's Manual (B-64484EN), p. 323-324, "Dateiname" (Instead of a program number a file name may be assigned, coded in `<` and `>` at the start of the program (`<PARTS_1> ;`), and a coded file name is allowed only at the start of a program or directly after M98, G65, G66, G66.1, M96, G72.1 or G72.2). (Citations re-paged to the cnc-manuals connector 2026-10-26.)

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

Without NUMBER, a NAME of digits is the O number (limit per D249). Otherwise the compiler takes the lowest number from 1 that the output file does not use, skipping 8000-9999 (builder-reserved), with a WARNING that names the number. The name stays in parentheses. CMP300 goes.
Basis: manual + logical
Source: FANUC B-64484EN p. 323-324 (the control's own fallback chain; O0 is forbidden; 8000-9999 are often reserved), p. 560 (NE8/NE9); Nakamura 2019 p. 76 (O9000) (cnc-manuals).
Differs from the recommendation: yes: the generated range skips 8000-9999.
Confidence: high
Code impact: FanucProgramFrame.WriteProgramBegin; CMP300 becomes a WARNING code.

#### D258 CSS codes of a spindle whose table has no VC or CSS_OFF
Question: Machine-config 5 gives VC = "G96 S{value}", CSS_OFF = "G97" and RPM_MAX only in [spindle.MAIN]. Its [spindle.SUB] gives none of them, and neither does [spindle.SUB] of any Fanuc-family machine file (nakamura-ntjx, mori-ntx1000-mapps, doosan-puma-2600sy). Controller-mapping 4 (CSS, VC, RPM_MAX row) gives G96 S{vc}, G97 and G50 S (G92 S in B and C) for the whole family, and fanuc 5 says Fanuc has one S address. The Fanuc reader therefore reads G96 and G97 for any spindle, and the compiler falls back to S where a table has no RPM (FanucToolWords.SpeedOf). But it writes CSS only from the role's table and reports CMP010 otherwise. Case: G97G99S1785M54 of the Nakamura pair (path 1 line 50, path 2 lines 64 and 83) reads as CSS:SUB=OFF and does not compile back with the shipped nakamura-ntjx.toml. NakamuraJobCompileTests adds CSS_OFF to the file to make it compile.
Recommendation: For the Fanuc family, the compiler falls back to the codes of controller-mapping 4 where the role's table lacks the key, as RPM already falls back to S. VC becomes G96 S{value} and CSS_OFF becomes G97. RPM_MAX becomes G50 S{value} in system A, and G92 S{value} in B and C and on a mill, which has no gcode_system (as fanuc-mill-30i.toml writes it). Each is written as the role's own template would be, and a table key overrides the fallback. Machine-config 5 says so after the [spindle.SUB] example. Reason: this matches the reader, the RPM fallback and the single S address of fanuc 5, and no machine file changes. Alternative: the keys are required per role for CSS. The Fanuc machine files (both nakamura-ntjx.toml copies included) then get VC and CSS_OFF under [spindle.SUB], the compiler keeps CMP010, and the reader reads G96 and G97 only for a spindle whose table has them. G97 then stands in two tables of one file, the case of D155.
Where: machine-config 5 ([spindle.SUB] example and the paragraph after [raw]); controller-mapping 4 (CSS, VC, RPM_MAX row); controllers fanuc.md 4 (G96 bullet), 5, 10 rule 2; machines/*.toml and docs/spec/examples/machines/nakamura-ntjx.toml ([spindle.SUB], alternative only); D155 (alternative only); src/Ncx.Compilers/Fanuc/FanucToolWords.cs WriteSpindleLines (TODO(question) at line 173) and Line; tests/Ncx.Acceptance/Jobs/NakamuraJobCompileTests.cs (marker at line 24, the filled machine at line 120; wave-3 question 175).

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, not confirmed by the maintainer: the manuals do not settle this. The manuals support the fallback and make the alternative look wrong: G96/G97 are one modal G-code group of the control, not codes of a spindle. The 30i lathe G-code list puts G96 and G97 in group 02, so exactly one of the two is active per path at any time, and there is no room for a second pair for a second spindle; the multi-spindle case is handled by the spindle-selection address P or the spindle-name extension and by the spindle's own M codes, not by a second G96. The Nakamura NTJX code list likewise carries a single G96 and a single G97 for the whole machine beside its M3/M4/M5 and M53/M54/M55 direction codes, which is exactly what `G97G99S1785M54` of the WY-250L pair is, and the builder's own format is `G96 S M;` with `G50 S;` and `G97 S;`. Requiring VC and CSS_OFF in every [spindle.*] table would mean writing one control code into two tables of one machine file. What the manuals cannot settle is whether NCX models this as a compiler fallback or as required keys — but the fallback is the one that matches the controls.
Evidence: FANUC 30i-B Operator's Manual (B-64484EN), p. 71, table 3.2 (b) G-code list for lathes (G96 "Konstante Schnittgeschwindigkeits-Steuerung" and G97 "... Ende" are one modal group, group 02, in all three G-code systems A, B and C. A modal group holds one active code per path, so the pair belongs to the path and not to a spindle); FANUC 30i-B Operator's Manual (B-64484EN), p. 234-235, section 9.3 format (`G96Sxxxxx;` for constant surface speed, `G97Sxxxxx;` to end it with S as rpm, `G92 S_;` for the maximum spindle speed and, marked T, `G50 S_;` for the same, with the note that G50 goes with G-code system A. `G96Pα;` selects the axis (P0 = the axis of parameter 3770, P1..P8 = the 1st..8th axis); a note says that under multi-spindle control — spindle selection based on address P or on the spindle-name extension — that axis selection by P is disabled and parameter 3770 must be used instead); FANUC 30i-B Operator's Manual (B-64484EN), p. 235-236 (G96 is one modal G code that puts the control into the constant-surface-speed mode, in which S values count as cutting speed; G97 ends it; the speed is capped by whatever `G92S_;` or `G50S_;` last set, and that cap is not active at power-on); Nakamura-Tome Super NTJX, Liste M- und G-Codes (Walter Meier, 2016), p. 6 (G-code list) and 1 to 2 (M-code list) (The machine's G-code list has exactly one "G96 =KONSTANTE SCHNITTGESCHWINDIGKEIT" and one "G97 =KONSTANTE DREHZAHL" for the whole machine, while the M list carries M3/M4/M5 for the main spindle and M53/M54/M55 for the sub spindle. So the sub spindle has its own M codes but no G codes of its own in the list); Nakamura-Tome Precision Turning Center Programmierhandbuch 1, 4810004ECL-1, p. 61 to 62, section 5-2 (The builder's own format for constant surface speed is `G96 S    M   ;` with the speed limit `G50 S   ;` and cancellation with `G97 S   ;`, and the worked example writes `G50 S`, `G96 T S M`, then `G50 S` again to change the limit and `G97 S` to cancel. The spindle comes from the M code written in the G96 block; the section gives no second set of codes). (Citations re-paged to the cnc-manuals connector 2026-10-26.)

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

The Fanuc compiler falls back to the family codes where a role's table lacks the key: VC becomes G96 S{value} and CSS_OFF becomes G97. RPM_MAX becomes G50 S in system A, and G92 S in B/C and on a mill. A table key overrides the fallback. Machine-config 5 says so after [spindle.SUB]. No machine file changes, and the NakamuraJobCompileTests patch is removed.
Basis: manual
Source: FANUC B-64484EN p. 71 (G96/G97 are group 02, per path), p. 234-236; Nakamura NTJX code list 2016 p. 1-2, 6; 4810004ECL-1 p. 61-62 (cnc-manuals).
Differs from the recommendation: no
Confidence: high
Code impact: FanucToolWords.WriteSpindleLines; NakamuraJobCompileTests.
