#### D278 Fanuc G70..G76: where the CONTOUR section stands and which N numbers P and Q take
Question: Fanuc 6 and language 4.7.1 have P and Q name 'the block range of the contour that follows' the G70..G76 block. D65 makes the contour a SUB section named by CONTOUR=, and machine-config 6 (contour) says 'the compiler writes the block numbers of that section'. Language 4.13 places a Fanuc subprogram as an O program after the caller's M30, and P and Q cannot name blocks there. No document says where the section's blocks stand when two cycles name it (G71 and then G70, the usual pair, which the reader gives one section in StructurePass.Contours.cs). None says which N numbers its first and last block take. The reader writes the section without labels, and numeric labels and block_numbers already take N numbers (wave-3 questions 49 and 69, D277). None says from which target state the blocks are written either. The cycle call does not enter the section, because VM 3.3 knows no sequence outside the drilling family (D94, D187). So the VM walks it once as a subprogram nothing calls, from the default entry state (VM 3.9, D99). CompilerBase writes it after the last program as an O program under one_file, and under file_per_program in no file, with a WARNING (wave-3 questions 4 and 5, D264). On main every G70..G76 entry is CMP384, so CYCLE=FINISH CONTOUR=C1 does not compile (no acceptance source has one).
Recommendation: Write the inverse of the reader so that the round trip holds. The section's blocks stand directly after the first cycle block of the program that names it, the only place the reader recognizes (FollowingRange), and are not written again as an O program. Every later cycle of that program that names it (G70 after G71) writes the same P and Q. A section named from two programs is written in each, as VM 3.9 allows where the target needs a section per program. Its first and last block take N numbers the way identifier labels do (D277: after the greatest numeric label, in order); under block_numbers they keep those numbers, as a label does (FanucCompiler.OwnBlockNumber). The blocks are written from an unknown target state, as a subprogram is (D99). After them the program goes on with every code they write unknown, since the control does not run them as blocks of the program. A section that a CALL also names, or that holds a LABEL, JUMP, CALL or cycle, is a CMP ERROR. This rests on a fact the reader already assumes, which the maintainer confirms from the Fanuc lathe manual: after G70..G73 the control goes on after the Q block, and P and Q name blocks of the same program. Fanuc 6, language 4.13 (the Fanuc placement) and machine-config 6 each get one sentence. The comparison rules of 13-phase-3 compare P and Q of a contour cycle as references. Alternative: keep CMP384 for 1.0. The reader writes a contour cycle only for a bare G7x P Q whose range follows it, because the other words of G71..G76 stay RAW until D175.
Where: fanuc 6; machine-config 6 (contour); language 4.7.1 and 4.13 (Fanuc placement of a subprogram); VM 3.9; D99; 13-phase-3 (P3-06, comparison rules); src/Ncx.Compilers/Fanuc/FanucCycles.cs:202 (CodeOf, CMP384); src/Ncx.Compilers/Fanuc/FanucLabels.cs Number; src/Ncx.Compilers/Fanuc/FanucCompiler.cs:67 (OwnBlockNumber); src/Ncx.Compilers/CompilerBase.Layout.cs:26 and :67 (a SUB no program calls, D264); reader side src/Ncx.Readers/StructurePass.Contours.cs; related D65, D175, D176, D187, D224, D277.

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, corrected 2026-10-26 after the manual audit, not confirmed by the maintainer: Write the contour blocks inline, directly after the cycle block that names them, and never again as an O program: a later G70 of the same program repeats only P and Q. The sequence numbers at P and Q may appear only once in the same program, so a section two cycles name is written once; the rule is per program, so a second PROGRAM that names the section gets its own copy, and the manuals say nothing about which numbers that copy must take. After the roughing pass the control goes on with the block after the Q block, so the section is never run as ordinary blocks of the program. The first block (ns) is not free, though. It must carry G00 or G01 (otherwise alarm PS0065), and for G71 its axis words select the cycle type: X alone selects type I; X and Z together (W0 if Z does not move) select type II, which needs the option "multiple repetitive canned cycle II"; a start block in which X does not move raises PS0325. The manual describes G72 as the same cycle cutting parallel to the X axis. So, unlike the Recommendation, the first block cannot be written from an unknown target state: a compiler that writes every axis there silently selects type II, and it must write X alone there unless type II is meant. The later blocks of the section may be written from an unknown state. Between P and Q the control allows only G04, G00..G03, a custom-macro branch or repeat whose target lies inside the range, and direct-dimension / chamfer-and-rounding blocks; custom macro calls are allowed neither there nor in the G70..G73 block itself, and the Nakamura manual adds that no subprogram may be called from the blocks between ns and nf.
Evidence: FANUC 30i-B Operator's Manual Turning (B-64484EN-1), p. 53 (G71 format: the two G71 blocks, then N(ns) ... N(nf); F, S and T inside ns..nf are ignored; type II needs the multiple repetitive canned cycle II option); p. 54 (after rough cutting as finishing, the block after the Q block runs); p. 55 (start block: G00 or G01, otherwise PS0065; the type is selected in this block; if X does not move, PS0325); p. 56-57 (type I: only the second plane axis in block ns; type II: both plane axes, W0 if Z does not move; type II needs the option); p. 68 (G72 is the same as G71 except that it cuts parallel to the second plane axis); p. 76 (G70 example: G71 P100 Q200 with N100..N200, G71 P300 Q400 with N300..N400, later G70 P100 Q200 and G70 P300 Q400 without the blocks again; up to three P/Q addresses are stored, then memory is searched); p. 89-90 (§4.2.8: no custom macro calls in a G70-G73 block; the P block must command G00 or G01, otherwise PS0065; between P and Q only G04, G00-G03, macro branch and repeat inside the range and direct drawing dimension / chamfer and corner R blocks; the sequence numbers at P and Q not twice in the same program); Nakamura-Tome Programmierhandbuch 1 (4810004ECL-1), p. 174-175 (§9-2-4: G71 P101 Q109 with the contour blocks after it, later G70 P101 Q109 without repeating them; no subprogram call from the blocks between ns and nf).
Corrected: added the G71 type rule (EN-1 p. 55-57): the axis words of the first contour block select type I or type II, type II needs an option and PS0325 follows if X does not move, so that block may not be written from an unknown state; on this point the proposal now departs from the Recommendation. The German citations are replaced by the English pages.

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

Use the audit-corrected manual answer. The section's blocks are written inline, directly after the first G70..G73 block of the program that names them, and never as an O program. A later G70 repeats only P and Q. A second PROGRAM that names the section gets its own copy, numbered fresh in that program. The P/Q block numbers are unique per program and follow D277 (after the greatest numeric label), and block_numbers keeps them. The first block always writes G00 or G01 explicitly. For G71/G72 it writes exactly the plane axes that the NCX contour's first block moves: X only for type I (Z only for G72). Both axes (W0 when Z does not move) make type II, which is written only where the machine file declares the type II option; otherwise it is a CMP ERROR. A first block in which X does not move is a CMP ERROR (PS0325). The later blocks are written from an unknown state. After the section, every code they write is unknown. A section holding anything but G04, G00..G03 motion, or a LABEL/JUMP whose target is inside the range is a CMP ERROR. That includes any CALL, a cycle, or a macro call.
Basis: manual
Source: FANUC 30i-B Turning B-64484EN-1 p.53-57, 68, 76, 89-90; Nakamura 4810004ECL-1 p.174-175 (connector).
Differs from the recommendation: yes. The first contour block is not written from an unknown state: its motion code and axis words are fixed by the type I/II rule.
Confidence: high
Code impact: FanucCycles (drop CMP384, inline section writer, type rule); CompilerBase.Layout skips the O program for a contour SUB.

#### D279 Cycle words and native parameters of a CYCLE:<controller>=n block (Fanuc and Siemens)
Question: D144 settles only n. It leaves the parameters of a native Fanuc or Siemens cycle to a question of their own before P3-06 and P5-02. By D94 and language 4.7.1 a native parameter is a key the word catalog does not know. So the Fanuc addresses X Y Z A B C R F of a native cycle are NCX words (axis words, arc radius, feed), while U, W, P, Q, K and also Q215 are native parameters. In the verb-less CYCLE block, X, Z and R are axis words without a verb, which is an ERROR (language 5 rule 2). No document says what the cycle words of language 4.7 (DEPTH, CLEARANCE, CYCLE_F, CYCLE_RETRACT, PECK, CYCLE_DWELL) write in such a block, or how a native parameter is written. The comment above CycleCatalog.PassesThrough states a rule: the cycle words go through the entry of n (FindNative), and the native parameters follow in source order. Neither compiler follows it. Fanuc main writes the G code, the positions of CYCLE_CALL and every native parameter as its key followed by its value in source order, so Q215=1 becomes 'Q2151.'. FanucCompiler.WriteNative marks every word of the definition block as written, so its cycle words, and any other word it carries, are dropped without a diagnostic. The D189 check (FanucCycles.cs:135) skips a native cycle. So a drilling-axis word of its CYCLE_CALL goes into the G8x block, where the control takes it as the depth, while D189 has a call outside the family move that axis (D187). The Siemens compiler (NativeCallOf) reports a cycle word as SiemensCycleWordNotWritable where the catalog has an entry of n with a signature. Where it has none, it writes every parameter, cycle words included, positionally in source order.
Recommendation: Both compilers apply the rule that the comment above CycleCatalog.PassesThrough states. Where the catalog has an entry of n, the cycle words go through it. On Fanuc they become G98/G99, Z, R, Q, P and F, as FanucCycles.AddDefinition writes them for a catalog cycle. On Siemens they take the positions of the signature, as Fill writes them. Where the Fanuc catalog has no entry of n, the cycle words take the addresses of the Fanuc drilling entries, so that such a cycle can still carry its R. These are the mill codes G74, G76 and G87..G89 that fanuc 6 names and the catalog leaves out, the cycles a native block is for. A cycle word that nothing maps is a CMP ERROR and is never dropped (language 2 rule 8). The native parameters follow in source order. On Fanuc each key must be one address letter, otherwise it is a CMP ERROR, and its value takes the decimal point of fanuc 10 rule 5. A drilling-axis word on the CYCLE_CALL follows D189. Language 4.7.1 gets that sentence for every family. Reason: D94 keeps the native parameters in source order, and the addresses that are NCX keys reach the control through the words that mean them. Alternative: a native block carries native parameters only, and any cycle word in it is an ERROR. A Fanuc cycle that needs R, Z or F then stays RAW:FANUC.
Where: language 4.7.1, 5 rule 2; machine-config 6; D94, D144; related D157 (rule words such as G98/G99), D187, D189; src/Ncx.Compilers/Fanuc/FanucCycles.cs:458 (NativeCode, AddNativeParameters), :135 (the D189 check) and WriteCall; src/Ncx.Compilers/Fanuc/FanucCompiler.cs WriteNative; src/Ncx.Compilers/Siemens/SiemensCycles.cs NativeCallOf (:375, wave-3 question 135); src/Ncx.Core/Machine/CycleCatalog.cs PassesThrough.

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, corrected 2026-10-26 after the manual audit, not confirmed by the maintainer: Take the recommendation, with corrections from the manual. The five mill codes the recommendation names (G74, G76, G87, G88, G89) carry the addresses of the catalog drilling cycles, so CLEARANCE writes R, DEPTH writes Z, CYCLE_F writes F, CYCLE_DWELL writes P and CYCLE_RETRACT writes G98/G99 for all of them. PECK must not fall through to Q blindly: Q is the depth of cut per feed in G73 and G83, and also in G74 (and G84) under peck rigid tapping; it is the shift at the hole bottom in G76 and G87; and G88 and G89 have no Q. So PECK on G74 writes Q on a control with peck rigid tapping, as the Recommendation's fall-through gives, and is a CMP ERROR otherwise; PECK on G76, G87, G88 or G89 is a CMP ERROR. Q is moreover one modal value that the cycles share: the shift of G76/G87 is also used as the depth of cut of G73 and G83, so a native cycle that writes Q changes the Q a later G73 or G83 would inherit, and the compiler must not rely on an inherited Q across it. A native parameter key must be one address letter A..Z, because a Fanuc word is one address letter plus a number; Q215=1 has no meaning on the control and the CMP ERROR is right. On Siemens the parameters of a call are positional: an omitted one is passed as 0 and its comma must still be written, a subprogram call stands in a block of its own, more parameters than defined raise alarm 12340 and a type that cannot be converted alarm 12330. A same-typed list in the wrong order therefore runs; the 2008 cycles manual adds that cycles check no values for plausibility, which the connector cannot show. Writing a native Siemens cycle whose signature is unknown positionally in source order is therefore unsafe and should be an ERROR too.
Evidence: FANUC 30i-B Operator's Manual Milling (B-64484EN-2), p. 56 (Table 5.1 (a): G73, G74, G76 and G81 to G89, among them G74 left-hand tapping, G76 fine boring, G87 back boring, G88 and G89 boring); p. 61 (G73: Q in drilling blocks) and p. 68-69 (G83: Q the depth of cut for each cutting feed); p. 62-63 (G74: the restrictions name only P; example without Q); p. 63-65 (G76 X Y Z R Q P F K: Q the shift at the hole bottom, P the dwell, F the cutting feedrate; caution: Q is a modal value also used as the depth of cut for G73 and G83); p. 79-80 (G87: P and Q paragraph and the same caution); p. 82 and 83 (G88 and G89: P paragraph only); p. 110 (peck rigid tapping: G84 (or G74) X Y Z R P Q F K, Q the depth of cut for each cutting feed); p. 57 (the drilling axis is chosen by the axis address in the G73..G89 block); p. 58 (drilling data retained until modified or cancelled; G98 initial level, G99 point R); FANUC 30i-B Operator's Manual (B-64484EN), p. 324-325 (a word is an address, one of the letters A to Z, followed by a number); Siemens SINUMERIK 840D sl Programmierhandbuch NC-Programmierung SW 4.92 (2019), p. 505 (an omitted parameter is passed as 0; the commas must still be written) and p. 536 (a subprogram call is programmed in its own NC block); Siemens SINUMERIK 840D sl Parameter Alarme (BS.000503), p. 181-182 (alarm 12330, actual parameter type not convertible) and p. 182 (alarm 12340, more parameters than defined); Siemens Programmierhandbuch Zyklen 840D sl/840D/840Di sl (01/2008), p. 15-18 (no plausibility check of parameter values; listed in the connector, but its text cannot be read, so not re-checked).
Corrected: dropped "G74 has no Q": under peck rigid tapping G74 takes Q as the depth of cut (EN-2 p. 110), so PECK on G74 maps to Q there, as the Recommendation would have it; added that Q is one modal value shared by G76/G87 and G73/G83 (EN-2 p. 64-65). The Siemens facts are cited from the sl manuals the connector holds, the 2008 cycles manual only for the plausibility point it cannot show.

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

Use the recommendation with the audit-corrected manual refinements. Fanuc G74/G76/G87/G88/G89 map CLEARANCE to R, DEPTH to Z, CYCLE_F to F, CYCLE_DWELL to P, and CYCLE_RETRACT to G98/G99. PECK maps to Q only on G73/G83, and on G74/G84 where the machine declares peck rigid tapping. On G76, G87, G88 and G89 PECK is a CMP ERROR. The compiler treats Q as shared modal data: after a native cycle that wrote Q, it does not rely on an inherited Q for G73/G83. A native Fanuc parameter key must be one letter A..Z; Q215=1 is a CMP ERROR. On Siemens, cycle words go through the signature. A native call whose signature is unknown is a CMP ERROR instead of being written positionally. An unmapped cycle word is always a CMP ERROR, never dropped. A drilling-axis word on the CYCLE_CALL follows D189.
Basis: manual
Source: FANUC 30i-B Milling B-64484EN-2 p.56-58, 61-65, 68-69, 79-83, 110; B-64484EN p.324-325; SINUMERIK 840D sl NC-Programmierung SW4.92 p.505, 536; Parameter-Alarme p.181-182 (connector).
Differs from the recommendation: yes. PECK is restricted per code, Q is handled as shared modal data, and a Siemens native call without a signature becomes an ERROR.
Confidence: high
Code impact: FanucCycles.AddNativeParameters/WriteNative (map, no silent drop); SiemensCycles.NativeCallOf (ERROR without signature).

#### D280 Counter variable of a Fanuc REPEAT
Question: Controller-mapping 6 (REPEAT + TIMES row) writes a REPEAT for Fanuc as 'counter variable and IF GOTO (compiler)'. D213's recommendation starts that counter at the REPEAT block and clears it on every JUMP that leaves the section. No document names the variable, and every custom macro B range of fanuc 7 may be taken already. #1..#33 are the program's V1..V33 (D33, language 4.9); the QL names of machine-config 7 also land there (QL = "#"), and an M98 subprogram shares them. #100..#199 and #500..#999 hold the mapped Q and QR names (machine-config 7: Q1 -> #101, QR1 -> #501) and the set-up data of builder programs (the Nakamura pair reads #501 to #529). Case: a Heidenhain CALL LBL 1 REP 3 (REPEAT=1 TIMES=3) compiled for fanuc-mill-30i.toml. Main reports an ERROR (CMP304) for every REPEAT (FanucFlow.Write).
Recommendation: Add a [variables] key to machine-config 7, for example repeat_counters = ["#199", "#198"]: the variables the compiler may use, one per nesting depth of REPEAT sections. The compiler writes the count from TIMES (1 without it, D212), the IF GOTO, and the clearing that D213 asks for. It reports an ERROR when the key is missing, when it is too short for the nesting, or when it names a variable the program itself uses. Reason: which variables are free is a fact of the machine and its builder macros, like [variables] map, and machines without the key keep main's ERROR. Alternative: no key; the compiler takes the highest local variables, #33 downward, that the program does not name. These are cleared at the program end, but a subprogram called with M98 shares them.
Where: machine-config 7; controller-mapping 6 (REPEAT + TIMES row); controllers fanuc.md 7; machines/fanuc-mill-30i.toml and the Fanuc example machine files; the [variables] loader in Ncx.Config; src/Ncx.Compilers/Fanuc/FanucFlow.cs Write (TODO(question) at line 106); D212, D213.

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, not confirmed by the maintainer: the manuals do not settle this. The manuals cannot name a free variable, and they show why no constant can be right, which is the case for the [variables] key of the recommendation. Which globals exist at all is an option: with plain custom macro only #100..#149 and #500..#549 exist, so a hard-coded #199 or #198 would not exist on such a control; parameters 6036/6037 make part of #100..#199 and #500..#999 shared between channels, so a variable free on one path is written by another; parameters 6031/6032 can write-protect #500..#999 with alarm PS0116. The Nakamura side confirms the other half: on that machine #500..#549 are the P-CODE macro common variables, the builder's own macro-executor range, and the NTJX set-up programs in the library write #501..#529, #543..#549, #550..#581 and #590 for tool-change points, bar data, parting and clamping lengths. The fallback of taking #33 downwards is also unsafe by the manual: the main program is local level 0, a macro call changes the local-variable level but a subprogram call does not, so an M98 subprogram sees and can overwrite the counter, while a G65/G66/Ggg/Mmm macro call would save and restore it.
Evidence: FANUC 30i-B Operator's Manual (B-64484EN), p. 447-448 (Local variables #1..#33 are local to a macro and start as <Null> when no argument was passed; global variables #100..#199 and #500..#999 are shared by the main program, called subprograms and macros; with only the custom-macro option just #100..#149 and #500..#549 exist (the first group cleared at power-off, the second retained), the full 600 need the extended-global-variables option; #500..#999 can be write-protected through parameters 6031/6032, and a write into the protected range raises PS0116 "SCHREIBGESCHUETZTE VARIAB"); FANUC 30i-B Operator's Manual (B-64484EN), p. 448 (Parameters 6036 and 6037 (with parameter 6020 bits NC1/NC2 per channel) decide how many of #100..#199 and #500..#999 all channels share; the worked table shows #100..#119 common to every channel while the rest stay per channel); FANUC 30i-B Operator's Manual (B-64484EN), p. 524 (Restrictions on the macro call, stated directly: "Bei einem Makroaufruf aendert sich die Ebene lokaler Variablen. Bei einem Unterprogrammaufruf aendert sich die Ebene lokaler Variablen nicht." The same wording stands in the 0i-D Operator's Manual (B-64304EN) on page 246); FANUC 30i-B Operator's Manual (B-64484EN), p. 529 (Local variables have levels 0 to 5, the main program is level 0, and each macro call raises the level by one and saves the previous values, which M99 restores; the figure on the page shows the levels being raised by G65 calls, and global #100- and #500- variables written and read by macros at different levels); FANUC 30i-B Operator's Manual (B-64484EN), p. 560 (Reset: "Bei einem Reset werden lokale Variablen und die globalen Variablen #100 bis #199 auf den Wert Null zurueckgesetzt. Mit Bit 6 (CCV) von Parameter Nr. 6001 kann dies verhindert werden." A reset also clears all called states of macro and subprograms and returns control to the main program); Programmieranleitung NTJX-Maschinen (NC-Wort und Adresse), Nakamura-Tome Super NTJX, Fanuc 18i-TB, p. 19, 21 (The machine's own set-up program head on page 19 writes #526..#529 as tool-change points ("WZW. *X/L/O*", "*Z/L/O*", "*X/R/O*", "*Z/R/O*") and then a long block of #501..#529 for bar data, parting, facing allowance and clamping; page 21 adds #543, #548, #549, #550..#561, #570, #580, #581 and #590 for chuck and clamping lengths. Pages 24, 25 and 27 use #100, #101, #109 and #121..#126 in the body of the programs); Liste der Warn- und Alarmmeldungen (4830001EEJ), Nakamura-Tome, p. 320 (Alarm 2052 "#500-#549 P-CODE MACRO COMMON SELECT (CANNOT USE SETVN)": the SETVN command cannot be used with the P-CODE macro common variables #500 to #549, so on this machine that range is the macro executor's own); NT Nurse / NT Work Navigator Bedienungsanleitung (4800001EBG), Nakamura-Tome, Fanuc 16i/21i, p. 306, 307 (On a multi-path Nakamura, NC parameter P6037 set to 2 makes #500 and #501 common between the upper and the lower turret so the probing result can be handed over; the parameter list on the next page gives P6036 for #100..#199 and P6037 for #500..#599). (Citations re-paged to the cnc-manuals connector 2026-10-26.)

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

Add `[variables] repeat_counters = ["#199", "#198"]` (one per REPEAT nesting depth) to machine-config 7. The compiler writes the count from TIMES, the IF GOTO and the D213 clearing. It reports an ERROR when the key is missing, too short, or names a variable the program uses. No fallback to #33 downward. The fanuc-mill-30i.toml example gives values from #100..#149, which exist even without the extended-variables option.
Basis: manual
Source: FANUC B-64484EN p. 447-448 (#150-#199 need an option; 6036/6037 sharing), p. 524, 529 (M98 shares locals), p. 560; Nakamura NTJX p. 19, 21; alarm list 4830001EEJ p. 320 (cnc-manuals).
Differs from the recommendation: yes: the example values lie in #100..#149, since #198/#199 need an option.
Confidence: high
Code impact: [variables] loader; FanucFlow.Write replaces CMP304 with the counter form.

#### D282 The settings of Fanuc writer rule 1
Question: Fanuc 10 rule 1 writes G0/G1 only when the verb changes ('a [format] option may ask for the G on every block'). It writes G90 in the header 'and use absolute values, or write G91 blocks where the NCX block had incremental words (a machine setting)'. Machine-config names neither setting. (a) The rule names G0 and G1 only. Fanuc 3 says 'The compiler writes a G only when the group changes, unless the configuration asks for the G on every block', and 13-phase-3 (Risks) asks for a [format] option, not a special case, for the habits of the sources. The sources repeat G3 and G2 on every arc (2.5D_FRAESEN N300 to N330, 3D_FRAESEN N330 to N350), and the comparison rules of code-guidelines 8 require that. Main writes G2 or G3 on every arc block, with no key. (b) Main writes G91 blocks for incremental words. It writes absolute values from the point the VM reached for a block that mixes both forms, a block under G53, and the incremental positions of a canned-cycle call (FanucCycles.AddPositions, because the cycle planes are absolute). Where that point is unknown, this is an ERROR. In a subprogram called at several positions the walks write different lines, which is the ERROR of D99. No key selects absolute output.
Recommendation: Add no keys. Write main's behaviour into fanuc 10 rule 1: 'G0/G1 only when the verb changes, G2/G3 on every arc block; G90 in the header; G91 blocks where the NCX block had incremental words; absolute values from the reached point where a block mixes both forms, stands under G53 or positions a canned cycle'. The last sentence of fanuc 3 names the arc exception. Reasons: a subprogram called at several positions cannot be written in absolute form, because the compiler writes it once from an unknown state (D99; the header comment of INCREMENTAL_SUB.ncx). So an 'absolute' setting could only ever apply in part. G2/G3 on every arc is what the sources write, and it is valid whatever group 01 holds. No machine needs it switched off, so it is a rule of the writer and not a special case of these sources in the sense of 13-phase-3. Alternative: a [format] key for each, as 13-phase-3 and fanuc 3 foresee: arc code on every block, and incremental = "G91" | "absolute", where absolute is used where the VM knows the point and G91 elsewhere. Answer (a) together with D299, which recommends one [format] key for the motion code on every block, read by every compiler, and would settle the arc code with it.
Where: fanuc 3 (modality paragraph, last sentence); fanuc 10 rule 1; 13-phase-3 Risks; machine-config 2 (only for the alternative); src/Ncx.Compilers/Fanuc/FanucMotion.cs:176 AddAxisWords, AbsoluteWord, :263 WriteMotionCode; FanucCycles.AddPositions; related D299.

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, not confirmed by the maintainer: the manuals do not settle this. The manuals back main on both halves of (a) but leave the choice to NCX. G0, G1, G2 and G3 are all modal codes of group 01 and stay effective until another code of the group appears, so writing G2/G3 on every arc block is redundant but always correct; and it is Fanuc's own habit — its examples drop G01 on continuation blocks yet write G02/G03 on each arc block, including two consecutive G03 blocks in a row. For (b) the manual removes one of the reasons given: canned-cycle positions are not absolute by nature — under G90 the drilling-axis word is the absolute hole bottom, under G91 R is the distance from the initial plane to the R plane and Z the distance from the R plane to the hole bottom — so writing them absolute is an NCX simplification (its CLEARANCE and DEPTH are absolute by language 4.7) and not a rule of the control. Writing G90 in the header is, however, required rather than optional wherever the control has the code at all: which of G90/G91 is active after power-on or reset is set by bit 3 of parameter 3402, so the compiler may not assume G90.
Evidence: FANUC 30i-B Operator's Manual (B-64484EN), p. 62-63, 64 (Page 62-63: G codes are one-shot or modal; a modal code stays effective until another code of the same group is programmed, and the worked example shows G01 written once with the following blocks carrying only coordinates; note (4) adds that a block may hold several codes of different groups, and item 1(5) that the power-on state of G90/G91 comes from bit 3 of parameter 3402. Page 64, Table 3.1(a): G00, G01, G02 and G03 all stand in group 01); FANUC 30i-B Operator's Manual Milling (B-64484EN-2), p. 195 (Cutter-compensation example: N2 G01 Y900.0 F150, then N3 X450.0 with no code, then N4 G03, N5 G02, N6 G03 each carrying their arc code, then N7 G01 X1150.0 and N8 Y550.0 again without one — the verb is written only on change, but every arc block has its G02 or G03); FANUC 30i/31i/32i-B Bedienerhandbuch Fraesen (B-64484GE-2/02), p. 123 (not in the connector) (The chamfer/rounding figure prints two consecutive arc blocks that both carry G03 (G03 X7.5 Y16.0 R37.0 ,C28.0 ; then G03 X67.0 Y-27.0 R55.0 ;) although the direction has not changed, so repeating the arc code on an unchanged block is normal manual style); FANUC 30i-B Operator's Manual Milling (B-64484EN-2), p. 58 (Figure 5.1(b) and its text: "Der Verfahrweg entlang der Bohrachse variiert fuer G90 und G91" — absolute Z in the one and, in the other, R from the initial plane and Z from the R point — so the control accepts canned-cycle positions in either form). (Citations re-paged to the cnc-manuals connector 2026-10-26.)

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

(a) The motion code follows the one [format] key of D299 (`motion_code`). The Fanuc default is "arcs": G0/G1 on change and G2/G3 on every arc block, which is main's output. (b) No key. G90 in the header is required, since 3402#3 sets the power-on state. G91 blocks are written for incremental words. Absolute values from the reached point are written for mixed blocks, G53 blocks and canned-cycle positions. Fanuc 10 rule 1 records that canned-cycle absolutes are an NCX simplification, not a control rule.
Basis: manual
Source: FANUC B-64484EN p. 62-64; B-64484EN-2 p. 58, 195 (cnc-manuals).
Differs from the recommendation: yes: (a) uses D299's key, with a Fanuc family default equal to main, instead of a fixed rule.
Confidence: medium
Code impact: FanucMotion.WriteMotionCode reads motion_code.

#### D283 Fanuc G20/G21 when UNITS equals units_default
Question: Controller-mapping 1 (UNITS) reads Fanuc units from 'G20/G21, else TOML', meaning units_default. D34 has the writers of NCX emit a complete header, and D11 and D34 say that configuration defaults apply 'to source readers only'. No document says whether the Fanuc compiler writes G21 for UNITS=MM on a machine whose units_default is MM. The three Fanuc sources have no G20/G21. Their round trips compare the header words as a set and every other line as written (code-guidelines 8), so an added G21 fails them. Main takes units_default as the control's units at the start. It writes G20/G21 only where UNITS differs, or where the [format] header wrote the other code. The Fanuc compiler is the only one that takes a configuration default into its start state. The Siemens compiler starts unknown and writes G71 (Expected/MILLTURN_TRANSFER.millturn1.mpf, N10). The Heidenhain compiler starts unknown and writes M137 for the header's FEED_MODE, which its sources lack (wave-3 question 34, D337; P3-04 log).
Recommendation: Keep main and state it in fanuc 10 and in the UNITS row of controller-mapping 1. The compiler writes G20/G21 where UNITS differs from the units the control has active. At the start those are units_default, unless the [format] header writes a code. A machine whose control needs the code in every program puts it into its header (D276). The D11 row then says that its 'source readers only' concerns the state the VM assumes for an NCX file, and that a compiler takes units_default as the control's units at the start. Answer D337 (wave-3 question 34, M137) together with this one. If the rule is to hold for every compiler, the Siemens compiler stops writing G71 where units_default is MM, which changes Expected/MILLTURN_TRANSFER.millturn1.mpf. Reasons: this mirrors the reader rule, round-trips the sources, and needs no new key. Alternative: always write G20/G21 in the first block after the header, as the Siemens compiler writes G71. Our reading of the manual, which is not in the documents, is that the control keeps the last units through power-off. The comparison rules then have to accept a units code that the source leaves out.
Where: controller-mapping 1 (UNITS row); fanuc 10; the D11 row of decisions.md; src/Ncx.Compilers/Fanuc/FanucProgramFrame.cs:122 WriteHeader; src/Ncx.Compilers/Heidenhain/HeidenhainFunctions.cs WriteFeedMode (D337); src/Ncx.Compilers/Siemens/SiemensMotion.cs WriteModalWords; related D292 (the Siemens pair of UNITS).

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, not confirmed by the maintainer: The manual contradicts the premise of main and of the recommendation: the Fanuc control does not start a program in the machine's default units, it starts in the units that were active when it was last switched off ("Beim Einschalten ist der G-Code wirksam, der beim Ausschalten aktiv war"), and G20/G21 are explicitly left unchanged by the power-on and reset clear state. So units_default is a promise of the configuration, not a state of the control, and the compiler cannot decide from it whether the code may be left out. The same page gives the form the code must take when it is written: its own block at the start of the program, before the coordinate system is set up, with the warning that G20 and G21 must never be switched inside a running program — which also makes main's mid-program G20/G21 wrong (FanucMotion.WriteModalWords writes the units code on any block that carries UNITS, and FanucCompiler calls it for every block, not only the header).
Evidence: FANUC 30i-B Operator's Manual (B-64484EN), p. 226 (Section 8.2, inch/metric switchover: the G code must stand in a separate block at the beginning of the program before the coordinate system is set up; it changes the unit of feed F, position commands, work offsets, tool compensation, handwheel scale, incremental feed and some parameters; "Beim Einschalten ist der G-Code wirksam, der beim Ausschalten aktiv war"; and a WARNUNG states "G20 und G21 duerfen nicht im laufenden Programm umgeschaltet werden"); FANUC 30i-B Operator's Manual (B-64484EN), p. 62-63 (Item 1(2) of the G-code list: unlike the other modal codes, "G20 und G21 bleiben unveraendert, wenn beim Einschalten oder Ruecksetzen der Loeschzustand hergestellt wird"); FANUC 30i-B Operator's Manual (B-64484EN), p. 2409 (Appendix F, the power-on / clear / reset table repeats it in the "Modaler G-Code" row: at power-on the modal codes take their initial value but G20 and G21 are put into the state they were in at the last switch-off; in the clear state they stay unchanged; in the reset state the row is unchanged throughout); FANUC 0i-D Operator's Manual Turning/Milling (B-64304EN), p. 121 (The 0i-D says the same word for word, so the rule is not particular to the 30i: separate block at the start of the program before the coordinate system is set up, power-on state taken from the last power-off, and the same WARNUNG against switching inside a running program). (Citations re-paged to the cnc-manuals connector 2026-10-26.)

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

The Fanuc compiler always writes the units code (G20/G21) in a block of its own at the start of each program, before any coordinate-system or offset setup, whatever units_default says. units_default stays a reader-side assumption only (D11/D34). A UNITS change after the first motion is a CMP ERROR on Fanuc, since switching inside a running program is forbidden, so main's mid-program G20/G21 goes. The 13-phase-3 comparison rules accept a units block that the source lacks. The Siemens compiler's G71 is consistent with this and stays (D292 governs G70/G71 against G700/G710).
Basis: manual + web
Source: FANUC 30i-B B-64484EN p.62-63, 226, 2409; 0i-D B-64304EN p.121 (connector): G20/G21 survive power-off and reset, and must stand in their own block at the start. Fusion's Fanuc post writes the unit code at program start through its gUnitModal (https://forums.autodesk.com/t5/fusion-manufacture/how-do-i-get-fusion-to-make-quot-m06-t8-quot-instead-of-quot-t8/m-p/7655034).
Differs from the recommendation: yes. This takes its alternative (always write) and adds the mid-program ERROR.
Confidence: high
Code impact: FanucProgramFrame.WriteHeader (always emit); FanucMotion.WriteModalWords (no mid-program units, CMP ERROR); comparison rules.

#### D284 Which files a batch converts, and whether the plugins read along
Question: Implementation 13 P3-07 converts 'every file of the folder' with one machine. Architecture 10's batch row reads 'every file of a folder and of its folders' and 'per file as convert', both written by P3-07 together with its marker. No document says whether a file that is no program of the machine's controller counts (README.md, or a Heidenhain .h under a Fanuc machine). No document says either whether the plugins of the working directory load, as they do for convert (RunPlugins, since P7-01). Main converts every file of the folder and its subfolders, hidden files included, whatever the name, in ordinal order of the path. It loads no plugins (BatchCommand.ConvertFile passes null), because a plugin reports on the file it was loaded with (P3-07 log). Case: the committed example reports convert README.md and the .h sources with the Fanuc reader.
Recommendation: Files: keep main. A corpus mixes extensions and extensionless Fanuc O files, and a name filter would silently drop programs. A file of another family still tests the reader for crashes (sample-corpus 2: convert must never crash on any program). Option: leave out hidden files and folders, whose names start with a dot, since they hold no program. A corpus folder on the maintainer's Mac holds .DS_Store, which main converts and lists in the committed report. Plugins: load them once per batch as convert does. A plugin's diagnostics go to the file being converted, and a plugin that fails is left out for the rest of the batch. Reason: the batch is to report what convert does with each file (architecture 10: 'per file as convert'). convert reads with the plugins of the working directory, and a shop's reader rules belong to the machine the batch reads for (D231). Nothing changes without a plugins/ folder or plugin list, as in the maintainer's run from the repository root. Alternative: no plugins, as on main, so that the report measures ncx's own readers only.
Where: Architecture 10 (batch row); implementation 13 P3-07; tests/corpus-reports/README.md. Code: src/Ncx.Cli/Commands/BatchCommand.cs Run (TODO(question) at line 67), ConvertFile, FilesOf; src/Ncx.Cli/RunPlugins.cs; tests/Ncx.Acceptance/Cli/BatchCommandTests.cs.

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27: the library does not answer this (searched Stapelverarbeitung / Stapelbetrieb / Batchverarbeitung / 'batch process', Postprozessor, Konverter and Konvertierungsbericht, and konvertieren|Umwandlung|umwandeln near Ordner|Verzeichnis|Datei over the whole text cache; the only batch material is Heidenhain's on-control Batch Process Manager (TNC 640 Bedienung, chapter 8.4), the only conversion material the Fanuc Data Server card's 8.3 file-name rules and the FAPT Ladder III converter). The recommendation above stands for the maintainer.

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

Convert every file of the folder and its subfolders in ordinal path order, but skip hidden files and folders (names starting with '.'). Load the plugins once per batch, as convert does. A plugin's diagnostics go to the file being converted, and a plugin that fails is dropped for the rest of the batch.
Basis: logical
Source: The batch reports what convert does ('per file as convert'). .DS_Store holds no program. Without a plugins folder or list, nothing changes.

Confidence: high

Question: Implementation 13 P3-07 asks for 'a summary per file with blocks, RAW blocks per word, diagnostics per code, and totals' without a form. It starts with a head: the machine, then the files converted, unreadable and crashed. One table follows with a row per file, then a table of totals with the number of files each key stands in. #### D286 Where the path comes to rest under path_mode = "continuous"
Question: VM 8 and machine-config 4 ([dynamics]) say that "continuous" carries the speed through corners up to corner_speed. D64 (architecture 13) models no look-ahead beyond path_mode and corner_speed. No document says where the path comes to rest. Main (RuntimeEstimator) stops at a DWELL, a spindle start or stop, TOOL_BEGIN and TOOL_END, STOP, the program and file events, and around a motion it cannot time. Every other junction is a corner. That covers a block without motion between two motions (COOLANT=ON, FUNC, and a SYNC at which the channel waits, since the estimator ignores SyncEvent) and a reversal of direction. It also covers the CYCLE_DWELL at the depth of an expanded cycle, which ChargeCycleDwell adds after the call's motions without a stop, and a catalog or CYCLE:<controller>=n call that is not timed. Case: an expanded DRILL with CYCLE_DWELL on a continuous machine leaves the depth and starts its retract at corner_speed, and the dwell is added beside that.
Recommendation: Keep the code's rest points and write them into VM 8, with four additions. The path also comes to rest in four places. The first is where the direction reverses (a motion opposite to the one before it), as at the depth of a drilling cycle and between its pecks. The second is at the CYCLE_DWELL of an expanded cycle. The third is at a cycle call the estimate cannot time. The fourth is at a SYNC where the channel waits (SYNC_WAIT, VM 3.7). Every other junction, a block without motion included, is a corner. Reason: a reversal passes through speed zero on every control, a dwell and a wait hold the tool still, and an untimed cycle moves the tool, so none of them can carry corner_speed. Everything else is the tested code. Alternative: also rest after every block that writes a machine function (COOLANT, FUNC and MFUNC wait for their acknowledgement) and at the end of every RAPID (the in-position check of positioning), which is closer to Fanuc's defaults. Or keep the code unchanged.
Where: VM 8 (runtime estimate, after the path_mode sentence); src/Ncx.Analytics/Runtime/RuntimeEstimator.cs class marker (line 14), On (CycleCallEvent case; SyncEvent, not handled today), CloseCycleCall, ChargeCycleDwell, CornerSpeed; tests RuntimeAnalyticTests.PathModeContinuous_TwoLinesInARow_CarryTheCornerSpeedThroughTheCorner, CycleCall_ExpandedDrillingCycle_AddsItsRapidsPlungeAndDwell, plus new tests for the reversal, the cycle dwell, the untimed cycle and a job SYNC; related D190 (the motions and the dwell of an expanded cycle).

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, not confirmed by the maintainer: Keep the four rest points, add a fifth and drop the sentence that a block without motion is a corner: a block that commands a machine function and no motion (COOLANT, FUNC, MFUNC) is a rest point. Siemens brakes the path to zero before an auxiliary-function output and before any executable block that carries no path motion — with the one exception of auxiliary functions declared fast — while blocks holding only a comment, a computation or a CALL do not disturb continuous mode; that is the line NCX should draw. Record too that the end of a RAPID is a rest point on Fanuc, where G00 always ends with an in-position check, but a corner on Siemens, where G0 obeys G64/G641, so path_mode alone cannot decide it. On the SYNC the manuals go further than the draft: Siemens WAITM ends the preceding block with Genauhalt whether or not the channel has to wait, and a Fanuc waiting M code must stand in a block of its own (a block without path motion), so a mark costs a stop in general; only the conditional WAITMC brakes just when the partners are not yet at the mark. A rest point at every SYNC, not only at a SYNC_WAIT, is what the machines show. Caveats: The reversal rest point is not stated outright anywhere; it follows from the Siemens overload-factor formula (velocity jump = axis acceleration x (factor - 1) x IPO cycle, and factor 1.0 means every non-tangential transition brakes to zero), so for a 180 degree reversal the carried speed is essentially zero. The CYCLE_DWELL rest point is supported indirectly (Fanuc: a dwell serves as an exact check in G64 mode, a statement marked M, the milling system) rather than by a rule about cycles. Nothing was found on an untimed cycle call as a rest point. The Heidenhain page is the iTNC 530: M90 does not exist on the TNC 640, where cycle 32 TOLERANCE replaces it, and M90 needs following-error mode selected — so "Heidenhain means exact_stop" holds for that control generation, not as a rule. One item of the Siemens speed-zero list, "eine Synchronisation", is about preprocessing synchronisation inside the channel, not about channel coordination; the SYNC case rests on the WAITM page and on the Fanuc waiting-M-code block instead.
Evidence: Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl-828D_Funktionshandbuch-Grundfunktionen_DE_2012.pdf, chapter B1 Bahnsteuerbetrieb, Genauhalt, LookAhead, p. 177 (Lists the "impliziter Genauhalt" cases in continuous mode: an auxiliary function output before the motion ends the previous block at the exact-stop criterion; an executable block with no traverse information for the path axes does the same; likewise a positioning axis declared a geometry axis, a transformation change, a BRISK/SOFT switch and a buffer flush. A second list gives the cases where the path speed is braked to zero, among them a positioning axis or SPOS that takes longer than the path axes, a geometry/synchronous axis swap, and "eine Synchronisation" becoming necessary); Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl-828D_Funktionshandbuch-Grundfunktionen_DE_2012.pdf, chapter B1, p. 178-179 (A corner is passed at finite speed only by allowing an axial velocity jump; the jump equals axis acceleration times (overload factor minus 1) times the interpolator cycle, and at factor 1.0 only tangential transitions survive while all others brake to zero on the setpoint side. This is the mechanism behind corner_speed and it makes a direction reversal effectively a stop); Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl-828D_Programmierhandbuch-Grundlagen_DE_2013.pdf, 11.2 Bahnsteuerbetrieb, p. 312-313, 316-317 (Auxiliary functions switched after the end of a motion or before the next one interrupt continuous mode, "Ausnahme: Schnelle Hilfsfunktionen", and positioning axes always move to the fine exact-stop window. Intermediate blocks holding only comments, computations or subprogram calls do not disturb it. Page 316 lists the cases where the control halts between two blocks, among them an auxiliary function output before the motion of the following block and a following block containing no path motion. Page 317 notes that rapid traverse too needs G60/G9 or G64/G641-G645, otherwise the machine-data default applies); Fanuc_30i-B_Bedienung-Drehen-Fraesen_B-64484EN_EN.pdf, 5.4, p. 180-181 (G61 decelerates at the block end and makes a position check, G64 does not decelerate and runs the next block straight away; the figure contrasts the tool path in exact-stop mode with the one in machining mode. A caution says G64 is the mode after power-on and after reset. No list of exceptions is given, so Fanuc documents far less than Siemens about where the path still stops); Fanuc_30i-B_Bedienung-Drehen-Fraesen_B-64484EN_EN.pdf, 5.2 and 5.6, p. 171 and 189-190 (For G00 the next block is executed only once the commanded feed rate is zero and the servo has entered the maker-set in-position range, so a rapid always ends at rest. The dwell section (under the M marker) says a dwell can be used as an exact check in G64 mode and that G04 without P or X produces an exact stop, which is why a CYCLE_DWELL cannot carry corner speed); Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl_Programmierhandbuch-NC-Programmierung_SW492_DE_2019.pdf, 3.1.8 Kanalübergreifende Programmkoordinierung, p. 490-491 (WAITM sets the wait mark in its own channel and "der vorhergehende Satz wird mit Genauhalt beendet" — unconditionally, with no proviso about the partners. WAITMC is defined by the contrast: there the braking to exact stop is started only when the other channels have not yet reached the mark. So a mark costs a stop on Siemens unless the program uses the conditional form); Fanuc_30i-B_Bedienung-Drehen-Fraesen_B-64484EN_EN.pdf, 23.2, p. 1037 (Caution 1: a waiting M code must be specified in a block of its own; caution 2: unlike other M codes it is not output to the PMC. A block of its own with no path motion is exactly the Siemens case that ends the previous block at the exact-stop criterion, so a mark is a rest point on this control too); Heidenhain_iTNC530_Benutzerhandbuch-Klartext_NC-SW-340490_DE_2005.pdf, p. 267 (Default behaviour is a brief stop (Genau-Halt) at corners in positioning blocks without radius compensation; with RR/RL the control inserts a transition arc at outside corners; M90 gives constant path speed through corners, block by block, and needs following-error mode selected). (Citations re-paged to the cnc-manuals connector 2026-10-26.)

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

Since D349/D350 (settled 2026-10-07), the rest points apply while the programmed PATH_MODE state is CONTINUOUS. Under EXACT_STOP every block rests. The path rests at: DWELL, a spindle start or stop, TOOL_BEGIN/END, STOP, program and file events, untimed motion (as coded), a direction reversal, CYCLE_DWELL, an untimed cycle call, and every SYNC, not only SYNC_WAIT. It also rests at every block without path motion that the control executes: COOLANT, FUNC, MFUNC, PATH_MODE, TOLERANCE and other machine-function or state blocks. Only comments, variable/parameter computations, LABEL, JUMP and CALL blocks are transparent corners. The end of a RAPID is a rest point on a Fanuc-family machine (G00 in-position check) and a corner otherwise. A new optional key `[dynamics] rapid_exact_stop` overrides that family default. The report names these rules.
Basis: manual
Source: SINUMERIK FH Grundfunktionen 2012 B1 p.177-179; Grundlagen 2013 p.312-317; NC-Programmierung SW4.92 p.490-491; FANUC 30i-B B-64484EN p.171, 180-181, 189-190, 1037 (connector). Treating Siemens "fast" auxiliary functions as rest points too errs toward the longer, safer estimate.
Differs from the recommendation: yes. Machine-function blocks without motion and every SYNC become rest points, and the RAPID end is decided per family or key.
Confidence: medium
Code impact: RuntimeEstimator (motionless-block rest, SyncEvent, reversal, CycleDwell, rapid rule read against the PATH_MODE state); MachineDynamics `rapid_exact_stop`.

#### D290 Units of a rotary axis's rapid, max_feed and acceleration in the polar and cylinder plane
Question: Machine-config 4 writes mm/min and mm/s^2 in the comments of rapid, max_feed and acceleration on its linear example axis X1. Its rotary example C1 has none of the three keys. Every rotary axis in the example machine files writes deg/min and deg/s^2. VM 8 limits a motion by the max_feed and acceleration of every moving axis. In the polar and cylinder plane the C word is a length (VM 3.1, D102). Main takes the rotary values as they stand, as mm/min and mm/s^2, in those planes only, and the report says so. Case: LINE C=10 F=6000 under POLAR=ON on nakamura-ntjx.toml takes C's 18000 deg/min as 18000 mm/min, which is right only at a radius of 57.3 mm. D192 asks which axes and units count for max_feed but names neither plane, nor rapid or acceleration.
Recommendation: Machine-config 4 names the units per kind: mm/min and mm/s^2 for a linear axis, deg/min and deg/s^2 for a rotary axis. In the cylinder plane the estimate converts the rotary values at the reference radius of CYLINDER=r (D96), 1 degree = pi*r/180 mm. This is exact because the C word is a length on that circumference. In the polar plane the length per degree changes with the radius along the motion. There the rotary axis sets no limit, and the values of the linear plane axis X limit every motion of the plane, a motion with C alone included. The report says so. Answer it with D192. Alternative 1: convert in the polar plane too, at the larger X radius of the motion's two ends. Alternative 2: keep the numbers as they stand.
Where: machine-config 4 ([[axis]] rapid, max_feed, acceleration comments); VM 8 (runtime estimate); src/Ncx.Analytics/Runtime/MovingAxes.cs Of (marker at line 58), MachineDynamics (RotaryAxisLine) and RuntimeAnalytic.Report (rotary table and its line); test RuntimeAnalyticTests.Report_MotionInThePolarPlane_NamesTheValuesOfTheRotaryAxisItUsed; related D192.

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, not confirmed by the maintainer: This contradicts the recommendation in part. Name the units per axis kind, as Fanuc does: rapid (parameter 1420), permitted cutting feedrate (1430) and acceleration (1660/1671) all carry "mm/min, Zoll/min, Grad/min" and "mm/s2, Zoll/s2, Grad/s2" per axis, so a rotary axis's values are degrees whatever plane is active. The cylinder half of the recommendation is right: under G07.1 the programmed feed refers to the speed on the circumference at the radius r given with the cycle, and Siemens does the same through FGREF, a reference radius per rotary axis (default 57.296 mm = 1 mm per degree). The polar half is wrong: Fanuc says that in polar coordinate interpolation the C component of the feed grows as the tool nears the centre, and that when the C axis's permitted cutting feedrate of parameter 1430 is exceeded the automatic feed override and automatic speed clamp take over — and it gives the limit in closed form, F < L x R x pi/180 mm/min, with R the C axis's permitted feedrate in deg/min and L the distance between tool centre and workpiece centre at the motion's closest approach. So in the polar plane the rotary axis does limit the motion, and NCX should convert its deg/min at the smallest radius of the block rather than drop the axis. Rapid needs no rule in either plane on Fanuc: G00 is not among the G codes permitted under G12.1, and under G07.1 positioning including G00 is explicitly forbidden. Reading the formula needs care: the text cache renders the stacked fraction upside down as "L x R x 180 / pi" in every Fanuc manual in the library; in the PDF itself the pi glyph sits above the 180 (verified by the glyph coordinates on page 101 of B-64484GE/02 (not in the connector): pi at y=314.9, 180 at y=300.8, main line at y=308.7), so the factor is pi/180, which is also the only dimensionally correct reading. What the formula does not give is how to average the C component over a block whose radius changes; it gives the worst case, which is the conservative bound an estimate wants. Note that the draft's Alternative 1 has the radius the wrong way round — it proposes the larger X radius of the two ends, and the manual's L is the closest approach. The acceleration limit inside G12.1 is not documented anywhere I found; the unit statement is general and per axis.
Evidence: Fanuc_30i-B_Parameterhandbuch_B-64490EN-05_EN.pdf, p. 85-86 and 88 (Parameter 1420 (rapid traverse rate of an axis), 1421, 1423, 1424 and 1430 (permitted cutting feedrate of an axis) are all "Datentyp Real Achse" with the unit line "mm/min, Zoll/min, Grad/min" — degrees per minute for a rotary axis.); Fanuc_30i-B_Parameterhandbuch_B-64490EN-05_EN.pdf, p. 100-101 (Parameters 1660 and 1671, the maximum permitted acceleration of an axis for acceleration/deceleration before interpolation, are axis data with the unit "mm/s2, Zoll/s2, Grad/s2"; for 1671 the value 0 means 1000.0 mm/s2, 100.0 Zoll/s2 or 100.0 Grad/s2.); Fanuc_30i-B_Bedienung-Drehen-Fraesen_B-64484EN_EN.pdf, p. 95 (Under "Schnittvorschubgeschwindigkeit für die Rotationsachse": the Cartesian contour is converted into C-axis and X-axis motion, the C component of the feed grows as the tool approaches the workpiece centre, and when the permitted cutting feedrate set for the C axis in parameter 1430 is exceeded the automatic feed override and automatic speed clamp become active; the same applies for the X axis.); Fanuc_30i-B_Bedienung-Drehen-Fraesen_B-64484EN_EN.pdf, p. 96-97 (The warning defines L as the distance in mm between tool centre and workpiece centre when the tool centre is nearest to the workpiece centre and R as the C axis's permitted cutting feedrate in deg/min, and gives the programmable speed as F < L x R x pi/180 (mm/min); it then describes the automatic speed control, the automatic override (permitted speed divided by the rotary axis's velocity component, with the permission factor of parameter 5463) and the automatic clamp.); Fanuc_30i-B_Bedienung-Drehen-Fraesen_B-64484EN_EN.pdf, p. 92-93 (In polar coordinate interpolation the feedrate unit is mm/min and F is the speed tangential to the Cartesian interpolation plane; the list of G codes permitted in that mode is G01, G02, G03, G02.2, G03.2, G04, G40/41/42, G65/66/67, G90/91 and G94/95 — G00 is not among them.); Fanuc_30i-B_Bedienung-Drehen-Fraesen_B-64484EN_EN.pdf, p. 99-100 ("G07.1 IP r" turns the rotary axis's angular path into the path along the circumference at the workpiece radius r, a feedrate specified in that mode refers to the speed on the circumference, and arc radii there are millimetres, not degrees; page 105 adds that no positioning operation may be specified in the mode (including G28, G53 and the rapid cycles G73, G74, G76, G80 to G89) and that G07.1 cannot be commanded in G00.); Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl-828D_Programmierhandbuch-Grundlagen_DE_2013.pdf, p. 107-108 (FGREF gives each rotary axis an effective reference radius so that F acts as a path feed; after power-up and reset the rating 1 degree = 1 mm applies, a reference radius of 360/(2*pi) = 57.296 mm, and F is read as degrees per minute only when the radius reference is that default.). (Citations re-paged to the cnc-manuals connector 2026-10-26.)

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

Machine-config 4 names the units per axis kind: mm/min and mm/s^2 for linear axes, deg/min and deg/s^2 for rotary axes, in every plane. Under CYLINDER=r the rotary values convert at r (1 deg = pi*r/180 mm). Under POLAR=ON the rotary axis does limit the motion: the C limit converts at L, the closest approach of the tool centre to the centre of rotation along the block (the perpendicular distance of the segment from the centre, or the nearer end when the foot lies outside it), giving F <= L*R*pi/180. The linear X limits apply as well. Acceleration converts the same way. That part is logical, since no manual documents it. Where L is 0 (a motion through the centre), the estimate does not divide by zero. It uses the X limit alone for that block and the report lines it as "C clamp near centre not estimated". RAPID needs no rule: G00 is not allowed under G12.1/G07.1, so a RAPID under POLAR or CYLINDER compiles as before and is estimated with the linear rapids. Answer it together with D192.
Basis: manual
Source: FANUC 30i-B Parameterhandbuch B-64490EN-05 p.85-88, 100-101; Bedienung B-64484EN p.92-97, 99-100, 105; Siemens Grundlagen 2013 p.107-108 (FGREF) (connector).
Differs from the recommendation: yes. In the polar plane the C axis limits at the closest-approach radius instead of setting no limit.
Confidence: medium
Code impact: MovingAxes.Of and MachineDynamics (convert per plane, closest-approach radius); RuntimeAnalytic.Report line.

#### D291 Siemens lines without an NC action: GROUP_END and the DEFINE line
Question: Controller-mapping 5 (catalog cycles row) reads GROUP_BEGIN/GROUP_END as 'structure only, read as SECTION'. Section 9 lists both among the RAW constructs with the same parenthesis. GROUP_END(0,0) carries no text for a SECTION. Controller-mapping 6 (macros row) has the reader expand DEFINE name AS text in the blocks after it, but does not say what the DEFINE line itself becomes. Today SiemensChannels.Read keeps GROUP_END as RAW with a WARNING, so an INDEX archive (GROUP_BEGIN(0,"Kanal-1 ",0,0) ... GROUP_END) does not compile to another family. SiemensFlow.ReadDefine writes the DEFINE line as a comment-only line.
Recommendation: Both become a comment-only line that holds the source text (trivia, D92). Neither changes anything on the machine, so the text stays in the file and no RAW blocks a compile to another family (D5 keeps RAW for what NCX cannot express). GROUP_BEGIN stays SECTION with its text. Controller-mapping 5 and 6 say so, and section 9 drops GROUP_BEGIN/GROUP_END from its RAW list. Code: GROUP_END gets the CommentLine that ReadDefine already writes. Alternative for GROUP_END: RAW as coded, with section 5 reading 'GROUP_BEGIN as SECTION, GROUP_END RAW'.
Where: controller-mapping 5 (catalog cycles row), 6 (macros, messages, stops row), 9 (Siemens RAW list); controllers/siemens.md 11 rules 6 and 8. Code: src/Ncx.Readers/Siemens/SiemensChannels.cs Read (TODO at 47); SiemensFlow.cs ReadDefine (TODO at 315). Tests: tests/Ncx.Readers.Tests/Siemens/SiemensChannelTests.cs (GROUP_END expected RAW) and tests/Ncx.Acceptance/Examples/SiemensReaderTests.cs (the DEFINE comment line).

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, not confirmed by the maintainer: the manuals do not settle this. For GROUP_END and the DEFINE line the manuals back the recommendation, but "neither changes anything on the machine" is wrong for GROUP_BEGIN. GROUP_END(<_LEVEL>,<_SP>) carries only a nesting level and a spindle assignment (0 none, 1 main, 2 counter), so nothing is lost by turning it into a comment line; DEFINE ... AS is a definition whose instructions are executed only when the macro name is called, so a comment line there is right too. GROUP_BEGIN, however, also carries a _MODE whose bit 1 is documented as "ShopTurn: automatischer Rückzug (auf Werkzeugwechselpunkt fahren)": with that bit set the block carries a retract to the tool-change point, and neither a SECTION nor a comment expresses it. The INDEX archive's GROUP_BEGIN(0,"Kanal-1 ",0,0) has _MODE 0 and is harmless, so the rule should be: GROUP_BEGIN with _MODE bit 1 clear is a SECTION, with bit 1 set it must stay RAW.
Evidence: Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl_Programmierhandbuch-NC-Programmierung_SW492_DE_2019.pdf, 3.25.1.53, p. 1170 (GROUP_BEGIN(<_LEVEL>,<_NAME>,<_SP>,<_MODE>,<S_ICON>): level 0 main or 1 first sublevel, a block name, a spindle (0 none, 1 main spindle, 2 counter spindle), a bit-coded mode whose bit 0 says a GROUP_ADDEND exists and whose bit 1 is "ShopTurn: automatischer Rückzug (auf Werkzeugwechselpunkt fahren)", bits 12 and 13 reserved, and an icon name that is for the operator interface only. The same table stands in the Sinumerik ONE manual (SW 6.14) on page 1162.); Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl_Programmierhandbuch-NC-Programmierung_SW492_DE_2019.pdf, 3.25.1.54-55, p. 1170-1171 (GROUP_END(<_LEVEL>,<_SP>) takes only the level and the spindle - there is no mode parameter and nothing that can move an axis. GROUP_ADDEND(<_LEVEL>,<_SP>), "Ende Einfahrzusatz", has the same two parameters.); Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl_Programmierhandbuch-NC-Programmierung_SW492_DE_2019.pdf, 3.25.1.2, p. 1043-1044 (The technology-specific overview of all externally programmable technological cycles lists GROUP_BEGIN, GROUP_END and GROUP_ADDEND under "Alle", beside the drilling, turning and milling cycles - they are ordinary cycle calls of the same package, not language keywords.); Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl_Programmierhandbuch-NC-Programmierung_SW492_DE_2019.pdf, 3.1.9 Makrotechnik (DEFINE ... AS), p. 496-498 (A macro collects single instructions under a new name; "bei Aufruf des Makros im Programmablauf werden die unter dem Makronamen programmierten Anweisungen nacheinander abgearbeitet" - the instructions run on the call, not on the definition. The syntax is DEFINE <Name> AS <Operation_1> <Operation_2> ..., the call is the bare name, and the examples include DEFINE LINIE AS G1 G94 F300 and DEFINE M6 AS L6.); Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl_Programmierhandbuch-NC-Programmierung_SW492_DE_2019.pdf, 3.1.9, p. 497-498 (Macro scope mirrors the variable scope: a macro defined at the start of a subprogram is local to it, one defined at the start of the main program reaches the subprograms only with MD11120 = 1, and only a macro file gives a macro global life. Any identifier and G, M, H functions and L subprogram names may be defined, but G-command macros only as global macros; keywords, reserved names and jump targets may not be overwritten by a macro.). (Citations re-paged to the cnc-manuals connector 2026-10-26.)

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

GROUP_END(...) and GROUP_ADDEND(...) become a comment-only line holding the source text (trivia, D92); the DEFINE ... AS line stays the comment-only line ReadDefine writes. GROUP_BEGIN(<_LEVEL>,<_NAME>,<_SP>,<_MODE>,...) is a SECTION with its name only when _MODE is a literal with bit 1 clear; with bit 1 set ("automatic retract to the tool-change point"), or with a _MODE that is not a literal number, the block stays RAW with the existing RAW WARNING (D5). Section 9 lists "GROUP_BEGIN with _MODE bit 1" as RAW and drops GROUP_END. The INDEX archive (GROUP_BEGIN(0,"Kanal-1 ",0,0)) then compiles to other families.
Basis: manual
Source: Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl_Programmierhandbuch-NC-Programmierung_SW492_DE_2019.pdf, 3.25.1.53-55, connector p. 1170-1171 (_MODE bit 1 retract; GROUP_END only level and spindle); 3.1.9, p. 496-498 (DEFINE runs on call, not on definition). Web check found nothing more specific.
Differs from the recommendation: yes: GROUP_BEGIN with _MODE bit 1 set (or non-literal) stays RAW instead of becoming a SECTION.
Confidence: high
Code impact: SiemensChannels.Read (GROUP_END/GROUP_ADDEND to CommentLine, GROUP_BEGIN _MODE check); test expecting GROUP_END RAW changes.

#### D292 G70/G71 against G700/G710 for UNITS
Question: Controller-mapping 1 (UNITS row) and siemens 2 (group 13) tell G70/G71 from G700/G710. G70/G71 switch the geometry only, so feeds and offsets stay in the machine's base system; G700/G710 switch everything. The same row says 'the reader reports which pair the source used so the compiler can keep it', and implementation 15 expected this draft ('a [format] key is the likely home'). No word, key or rule carries the pair: the Siemens reader reads all four codes as UNITS, and the compiler always writes G71/G70. Case 1: UNITS=INCH compiled for siemens-840dsl-mill (units_default MM) writes G70, so the control reads F, which the program gives in inches, as mm. Case 2: a source with G70 ... F500 on that machine reads as UNITS=INCH F=500, while the control feeds 500 mm/min.
Recommendation: Derive the pair instead of storing it, and replace the UNITS row's 'the reader reports which pair the source used so the compiler can keep it' with this rule. Compiler: G71/G70 where UNITS equals units_default, because on such a machine they mean the same as G710/G700; G710/G700 where UNITS differs, so that the feeds follow UNITS as NCX reads them. Reader: G700/G710, and the pair that matches units_default, become UNITS. G70 or G71 against units_default also becomes UNITS, and the reader converts each feed under it from the base system into the NCX unit, with a WARNING that names the code. So F500 under G70 on a metric machine becomes F=19.685. This is an exception to siemens 11 rule 9 ('numbers as written'). Without it, the compiler's G700 F500 would feed 25.4 times faster than the source. Reasons: no new key or word; a source that uses the machine's own pair round-trips as written, and G700/G710 are absent from the corpus (controller-mapping 11.1); feeds keep their meaning in both directions. Alternative: a [format] key that names the pair the compiler writes (implementation 15), with a reader WARNING where a source uses the other pair. That keeps the source text, but an inch program on a metric machine then needs the key set to G700.
Where: controller-mapping 1 (UNITS row); siemens.md 2 (group 13), 11 rules 2 and 9, 12; machine-config 1 (units_default); implementation 15 (Decisions needed first, exit checklist); src/Ncx.Readers/Siemens/SiemensGroups.cs ReadUnits (TODO at 206); src/Ncx.Compilers/Siemens/SiemensMotion.cs WriteModalWords (TODO at 38); related D283 (Fanuc G20/G21 against units_default).

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, not confirmed by the maintainer: The manual confirms the reason for the rule and refutes "no new key". It confirms it exactly: under G70/G71 only length-bearing geometric data are read and written in the programmed system while feeds, tool offsets, settable frames and base frames stay in the parameterized base system ("Durch G70/G71 werden Vorschubangaben nicht beeinflusst"), and the worked example prints X=2.75 inch under G70 with the comment "F=500 mm/min" unchanged — D292's case 2, word for word — while G700 F100 on a metric machine is 2540 mm/min, the 25.4 factor of case 1. But G700/G710 are not always programmable: they need the extended measuring-system functionality, MD10260 $MN_CONVERT_SCALING_SYSTEM = 1, so on a machine without it the derived pair cannot be written at all; and the base system (MD10240) and the reset value of group 13 (MD20150) are two separate machine data, so a single units_default cannot stand for both. Derive the pair as recommended, but the machine configuration must say whether G700/G710 exist and what the base system is.
Evidence: Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl_Programmierhandbuch-NC-Programmierung_SW492_DE_2019.pdf, p. 164, 165 (Section 2.8.4.5: G70/G71 read and write length-bearing geometric data in the programmed system while length-bearing technological data — feeds, tool offsets, settable zero offsets, machine data, system variables — stay in the parameterized base system; G700/G710 put all of them in the programmed system; "Damit die Befehle G700 und G710 zur Verfuegung stehen, muss die erweiterte Massystem-Funktionalitaet eingeschaltet werden (MD10260 $MN_CONVERT_SCALING_SYSTEM = 1)"; the Grundstellung of the group is settable via MD20150 $MC_GCODE_RESET_VALUES; and an ACHTUNG adds that axis-specific data of rotary axes are always read and written in the base system); Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl_Programmierhandbuch-NC-Programmierung_SW492_DE_2019.pdf, p. 165, 166 (Worked example on a metric base system (MD10240 $MN_SCALING_SYSTEM_IS_METRIC = 1): N20 G1 Z-5 F500 is 500 mm/min, N40 G70 X2.75 Y3.22 switches the geometry to inch and the comment still reads F=500 mm/min, N50 likewise, N60 G71 returns to mm — the feed never follows G70. The table below it marks feeds, settable and base frames, external offsets, tool offsets and length-bearing machine and setting data as G (base system) under G70/G71 and P (programmed system) under G700/G710); Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl_Programmierhandbuch-NC-Programmierung_SW492_DE_2019.pdf, p. 115 ("Masseinheiten fuer den Vorschub F": G700 and G710 define the measuring system for F as well, inch/min and mm/min respectively, with the explicit Hinweis "Durch G70/G71 werden Vorschubangaben nicht beeinflusst"; the same unit then applies to FL); Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl_Programmierhandbuch-NC-Programmierung_SW492_DE_2019.pdf, p. 110-111 (FGROUP example: N120 G91 G1 G710 F100 is commented "Vorschub= 100mm/min", and N210 G700 F100 "Vorschub= 2540mm/min" — the same F number means a feed 25.4 times larger once the extended code is written). (Citations re-paged to the cnc-manuals connector 2026-10-26.)

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

Derive the pair as recommended, but on two new machine-config keys for Siemens: `base_units` ("mm" | "inch", MD10240; default = units_default) and `extended_units` (bool, MD10260 = 1, G700/G710 available; default false). units_default stays the reset value of group 13 (MD20150). Compiler: where UNITS equals base_units write G71/G70; where it differs and extended_units = true write G710/G700; where it differs and extended_units = false write G70/G71 and convert every feed (and FL) it writes into base_units, with an INFO naming the conversion. Reader: G700/G710 become UNITS as written; G70/G71 become UNITS, and where the pair differs from base_units each feed under it is converted from base_units into the NCX unit with a WARNING naming the code (exception to siemens 11 rule 9, as recommended).
Basis: manual
Source: Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl_Programmierhandbuch-NC-Programmierung_SW492_DE_2019.pdf, connector p. 164-166 (G70/G71 leave feeds in the base system; G700/G710 need MD10260 = 1; MD10240 and MD20150 separate), p. 110-111 and 115 (G700 F100 = 2540 mm/min). Web: Siemens 840de G-code list, https://manualslib.com/manual/1663517/Siemens-Sinumerik-840de.html?page=440 (G700/G710 = length plus velocity).
Differs from the recommendation: yes: two machine-config keys (base_units, extended_units) instead of "no new key"; feeds compared against base_units, not units_default; a fallback that converts feeds when G700/G710 are unavailable.
Confidence: high
Code impact: machine-config schema (two keys); SiemensGroups.ReadUnits feed conversion; SiemensMotion.WriteModalWords pair choice and feed conversion.
