#### D294 Control number of a spindle whose templates carry none
Question: SETMS(n), S{n}= and M{n}= address a spindle by its number on the control (siemens 1 and 5; controller-mapping 4, SPINDLE:role row). Machine-config 5 gives that number only through a role's templates (the comment 'Siemens: spindle number', as in S2= and M2=3). The spindle whose templates write the plain S and M3, the configured master spindle, has no number there, and machine-config 4 does not say that a resource id carries one. Case: a source for millturn1 with SETMS(1) or S1=1500, where MAIN writes M3 and S{rpm}. The reader must know that MAIN is spindle 1, and the compiler needs n to write SETMS(n) for any role whose templates carry no extension. Main takes the number from the resource id: the reader looks for the resource S{n}, and the compiler takes the digits of the id (S1 is spindle 1 in both). This is how the example files name their spindles, and how the MILLTURN_TRANSFER comment reads them ('S1=1500 M1=3 on a machine with another master').
Recommendation: Write main's rule into machine-config 5 as a Siemens rule: a spindle's number is the extension its templates write, else the digits of its resource id. The reader then matches the digits as the compiler does, not only the id S{n}. A spindle with neither cannot be addressed by number: the reader keeps SETMS(n) as RAW and the compiler reports its ERROR, as coded. Reason: the Siemens example files already follow this (millturn1 S1 to S3, where S2 writes M2=3; dmg-ctx-840d S1 to S4, where S4 writes M4=3), so nothing changes beyond the markers and the reader's lookup. Alternative: an explicit key on a spindle's [[resource]] (number = 1), required on Siemens where no template carries an extension. The ids would then be free names.
Where: machine-config 4 ([[resource]] id), 5 (the [spindle.SUB] comment 'Siemens: spindle number'); controller-mapping 4 (SPINDLE:role row, Siemens cell); src/Ncx.Readers/Siemens/SiemensSpindles.cs RoleOf (TODO at 34); src/Ncx.Compilers/Siemens/SiemensSpindles.cs NumberOf (TODO at 63).

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, not confirmed by the maintainer: the manuals do not settle this. The manuals settle what the number means but not where NCX takes it from. On the control a spindle is addressed only by its number: S alone and S0= are the master spindle, every other spindle needs its number in the address extension (S2=, M2=3, T2=), and SETMS(<Spindelnummer>) makes another spindle the master and must stand in its own block. Which spindle is the main spindle follows from the kinematics and is declared master by machine data, and the numbers themselves are machine data too - nothing in the program carries them, which is why the machine file must. The manuals neither bless nor forbid deriving the number from the resource id; they do say the address extension on T is only available where the machine is configured for it, so a role without a numbered template is genuinely unaddressable, as coded.
Evidence: Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl-828D_Programmierhandbuch-Grundlagen_DE_2013.pdf, 6.1, p. 82 (S… is the speed for the master spindle and S<n>= for spindle n, with the explicit note that a speed given as S0= applies to the master spindle; M3/M4/M5 act on the master and M<n>=3/4/5 on spindle n; SETMS(<n>) makes spindle n the master and SETMS alone returns to the configured one. At most three S values per block, and SETMS must stand in its own block.); Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl-828D_Programmierhandbuch-Grundlagen_DE_2013.pdf, 6.1, p. 84 (A channel may hold five spindles at once, the master plus four. One spindle is defined as master by machine data and gets the special functions (threading, tapping, revolutional feed, dwell); for all the others the corresponding numbers must be given with the speed and the direction or stop. The example block is N10 S300 M3 S2=780 M2=4.); Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl-828D_Programmierhandbuch-Grundlagen_DE_2013.pdf, 15.1.3, p. 392 (Which spindle is the main spindle is determined by the machine kinematics, and that spindle is as a rule declared master spindle by machine data; SETMS(<Spindelnummer>) changes the assignment and SETMS without a number returns to it. The spindle designator is given as "S oder S0".); Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl-828D_Programmierhandbuch-Grundlagen_DE_2013.pdf, 4.1.1 and 4.1.2, p. 54-55 (In the T syntax T<n>=<Nummer> the extension <n> is named as the spindle number, with the note that whether a spindle number may be programmed as an address extension at all depends on how the machine is configured - the builder's data, not the program's. The same note is repeated for the tool-management forms on pages 57 and 59.); DMG-MORI_GMX-CTX-TC_Trainingshandbuch-Sinumerik840D_DE_2010.pdf, p. 24 (The builder's own rule: before the technology commands are programmed the spindle to be programmed must be selected, with SETMS(n); the worked example is N80 SETMS(4) "Anwahl der Masterspindel 4" followed by N90 G96 with S4=200 and M4=4 and LIMS=3500. (Which physical spindle 3 and 4 are is not on this page; the chuck data on page 25 and the RG703 "GEGENSPINDEL" / RG704 "HAUPTSPINDEL" flags on page 126 identify 3 as the counter and 4 as the main spindle.)). (Citations re-paged to the cnc-manuals connector 2026-10-26.)

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

Siemens rule in machine-config 5: a spindle's number is the address extension its templates write, else the digits of its resource id. The reader matches by those digits, as the compiler does. A spindle with neither keeps SETMS(n) RAW in the reader and is an ERROR in the compiler.
Basis: manual + logical
Source: 840D sl Grundlagen 2013 p. 54-55, 82, 84, 392 (spindle numbers are machine data); DMG CTX training 2010 p. 24 (cnc-manuals).
Differs from the recommendation: no
Confidence: high
Code impact: Siemens reader SiemensSpindles.RoleOf matches digits.

#### D295 Siemens structure whose condition has no NCX form
Question: The JUMP + IF row of controller-mapping 6 reads the corpus form IF $P_SEARCH OR $P_SIM GOTOF BEGINN by keeping that jump block RAW, so the blocks it skips stay NCX blocks. The structured-loops row lowers IF/ELSE/ENDIF, WHILE, FOR, LOOP and REPEAT/UNTIL to LABEL, JUMP and IF, but no document says what happens when the condition, or the bounds of a FOR, have no NCX form. Case: IF $P_SEARCH ... ELSE ... ENDIF, or WHILE $A_DBB[1]==0 ... ENDWHILE. Since the P5-01 review fixes, SiemensStructures keeps the whole structure RAW with a WARNING: its blocks, its ELSE and its end. What those blocks may change then becomes unknown.
Recommendation: Keep what the code does, and write it into the structured-loops row and siemens 11 rule 6. A structure whose condition has no NCX form stays RAW as a whole. Reason: with only the condition RAW, the VM and every compiler would run the IF branch and then skip the ELSE branch whatever the condition. A lowered WHILE, whose back jump stays an NCX JUMP, would loop in INTERPRETED mode until the block cap. The GOTOF form stays the documented exception: in the corpus it skips only $P_UIFR datum writes, which are RAW anyway. Alternative: an IF without ELSE is lowered like the GOTOF form, with only the conditional jump RAW and its blocks as NCX; loops and IF with ELSE stay RAW as a whole.
Where: controller-mapping 6 (JUMP + IF and structured-loops rows); controllers/siemens.md 8, 11 rule 6. Code: src/Ncx.Readers/Siemens/SiemensStructures.cs OpenRaw (TODO at 289) and UntilProblem; tests/Ncx.Readers.Tests/Siemens/SiemensFlowTests.cs If_OnAnUnmappedSystemVariable_KeepsTheWholeStructureRaw, WhileAndRepeatUntil_OnAnUnmappedSystemVariable_AreKeptRawAsAWhole.

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, not confirmed by the maintainer: the manuals do not settle this. The manuals show that this is the normal Siemens idiom rather than an edge case, and they support keeping the structure whole, but the RAW-as-a-whole choice itself is NCX's. The manual's own nested-control-structure example is exactly the case in question: LOOP, then IF NOT $P_SEARCH with real motion blocks and a WHILE $AA_IM[X] <= 100 drilling pattern inside it, ELSE only a MSG - so the guarded blocks are genuine NC motion and lowering the structure with only the condition RAW would run the IF branch and skip the ELSE. The manuals also treat a control structure as one indivisible unit: it cannot be used across programs, labels are not allowed in blocks that carry control-structure elements, and such blocks cannot be skipped - all of which argue against splitting one up. What is left for the maintainer is the alternative, lowering an IF without ELSE like the GOTOF form; no manual bears on that.
Evidence: Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl_Programmierhandbuch-NC-Programmierung_SW492_DE_2019.pdf, 3.1.7.6, p. 489 (the code body is not in its text layer; it is readable in Siemens_Sinumerik-ONE_Programmierhandbuch-NC-Programmierung_SW614_DE_2020.pdf, p. 480-481) (The manual's example of nested control structures is a LOOP containing IF NOT $P_SEARCH with G1 G90 X0 Z10 F1000 and a WHILE $AA_IM[X] <= 100 loop of G1 G91 motion blocks, an ELSE branch that only issues MSG("Im Suchlauf wird nicht gebohrt"), then $A_OUT[1] = 1 and G4 F2 before ENDLOOP. Both conditions are system variables, and the branches carry real motion.); Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl_Programmierhandbuch-NC-Programmierung_SW492_DE_2019.pdf, 3.1.7, p. 482-483 (Control structures are possible only inside the statement part of a program, definitions in the program header cannot be executed conditionally or repeatedly, "eine Kontrollstruktur kann nicht programmübergreifend verwendet werden", and the nesting depth is at most 16 control structures per subprogram level.); Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl_Programmierhandbuch-NC-Programmierung_SW492_DE_2019.pdf, 3.1.7, p. 484 (Constraints on control-structure blocks: they cannot be skipped, jump labels are not allowed in them, and control structures are processed interpretively so that the block structure of a program is not completely checked in interpreter mode. Mixing control structures and jumps is discouraged.); Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl_Listenhandbuch-Systemvariable_SW45_DE_2012.pdf, p. 44-45 ($P_SEARCH is a channel-specific BOOL, "Suchlauf aktiv", TRUE while a block search is active, readable in the part program and not writable. $P_SEARCH1 is "Suchlauf mit Berechnung aktiv"; $P_SEARCH2 is "Satzsuchlauf ohne Berechnung war aktiv", TRUE when the last selected search type was the one without calculation, and $P_SEARCHL gives that last type as an INT. All of it is control state with no counterpart in a program's own data, which is why a condition on it cannot be expressed in NCX.). (Citations re-paged to the cnc-manuals connector 2026-10-26.)

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

Keep main. A structure (IF/ELSE/ENDIF, WHILE, FOR, LOOP, REPEAT/UNTIL) whose condition or bounds have no NCX form stays RAW as a whole, with a WARNING. The GOTOF form stays the documented exception. Write this into the structured-loops row and siemens 11 rule 6.
Basis: manual
Source: 840D sl SW 4.92 p. 482-484, 489 (IF NOT $P_SEARCH with real motion; a structure is indivisible); System variables SW 4.5 p. 44-45 (cnc-manuals).
Differs from the recommendation: no

#### D297 A lone Siemens T0 on a machine that changes with M6
Question: Siemens 5 says that on mills M6 performs the change, so a T before it is a preload. It also says 'T0 unloads', without a context. Controller-mapping 3 reads a T alone on a machine that changes with M6 as PRELOAD (PRELOAD=5 row), and T0 M6 and a turret's T0 as TOOL=0 (TOOL=0 row). The same row also reads the Hermle's T=0 before M30, a lone T0 on a mill that changes with M6, as TOOL=0. Language 4.4 says PRELOAD=0 clears a pending preload. No document says which reading applies to a lone T0 that no program end follows. Main (SiemensTools.Preload, EndsBeforeAChange) writes TOOL=0 where the unit is a main program and M30, M2 or M17 follows before any M6 or T, and PRELOAD=0 otherwise. Case: a subprogram that ends with T0 and RET, or a T0 followed by T5 and then M6. As PRELOAD=0 the spindle keeps its tool. As TOOL=0 the VM empties the spindle, and a compile for siemens-840dsl-mill writes its unload template T0 M6 instead of T0.
Recommendation: Keep main's reading and write it down. A lone T0 on a machine that changes with M6 is PRELOAD=0, as any lone T is (PRELOAD=5 row, language 4.4). It is TOOL=0 only where the main program ends after it without an M6 or another T, the Hermle form of the TOOL=0 row. Siemens 5 then reads 'T0 M6 unloads, T0 alone on a turret'. Reason: on such a control T0 only selects the empty place, and the program end is the one place where the documents read that selection as the unload. A RET is not an end, because the caller may still write the M6. With either reading, a caller's M6 after such a subprogram stays D225's case (a bare TOOL). Alternative: a lone T0 is TOOL=0 wherever no M6 follows it in its unit, as siemens 5's 'T0 unloads' reads. The Hermle form is then the rule, and a subprogram that ends with T0 empties the spindle in the NCX reading.
Where: controller-mapping 3 (PRELOAD=5 and TOOL=0 rows, Siemens cells); siemens.md 5 ('T0 unloads'); language 4.4 (PRELOAD row); D225; src/Ncx.Readers/Siemens/SiemensTools.cs Preload, EndsBeforeAChange (TODO at 131).

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, not confirmed by the maintainer: Keep main's reading and write it down: a lone T0 on a machine that changes with M6 is PRELOAD=0. The manual's M6 section separates the three things - T selects, M6 changes ("Aktiv wird das Werkzeug erst mit M6"), T0 deselects - and with tool management it glosses T0 as the deselection command for an unoccupied magazine place and adds that selecting an unoccupied place can be used to position the empty place. That is a selection, not an unload; the spindle keeps its tool until an M6 follows. Only on a turret, where "das Suchen und Wechseln, nur mit dem T-Befehl ausgeführt" wird, is a T0 by itself the unload, which is exactly the TOOL=0 row's turret case. So siemens 5 should read "T0 M6 unloads; T0 alone unloads on a turret".
Evidence: Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl-828D_Programmierhandbuch-Grundlagen_DE_2013.pdf, ch. 4, p. 53 (On chain, disc and surface magazines a tool change normally happens in two steps: the T command searches the tool in the magazine and the M command then swaps it into the spindle. On turret magazines of lathes the change, that is search and swap, is carried out with the T command alone. Which kind applies is set by a machine datum.); Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl-828D_Programmierhandbuch-Grundlagen_DE_2013.pdf, 4.1.1, p. 54 (Section 4.1.1 "Werkzeugwechsel mit T-Befehl", whose stated application is lathes with a turret magazine: T is "Befehl zur Werkzeug-Anwahl inklusive Werkzeugwechsel und Aktivierung der Werkzeugkorrektur" and T0 "Befehl zum Abwählen des aktiven Werkzeugs"; the example writes N10 T1 D1 to swap tool 1 in and N70 T0 to deselect it.); Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl-828D_Programmierhandbuch-Grundlagen_DE_2013.pdf, 4.1.2, p. 54-56 (Section 4.1.2 "Werkzeugwechsel mit M6", for milling machines with chain, disc or surface magazines: "Mit der Programmierung des T-Befehls wird das Werkzeug angewählt. Aktiv wird das Werkzeug erst mit M6 (inklusive Werkzeugkorrektur)." The syntax block lists selection (T), change (M6) and deselection (T0) as three separate things, and the example shows N70 T5 as a preselection with the change happening only at N100 M6, so a T between two M6 blocks changes nothing in the spindle.); Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl-828D_Programmierhandbuch-Grundlagen_DE_2013.pdf, 4.2.1 and 4.2.2, p. 57 and 59 (With tool management T0 is glossed "Befehl zur Werkzeug-Abwahl (Magazinplatz nicht besetzt)", and the note adds that if the selected place is not occupied the tool command acts like T0 and that selecting an unoccupied place can be used to position the empty place. The same note stands on both pages, that is for the turret case and for the M6 case, and on page 59 it sits beside the statement that the tool becomes active only with M6.); Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl-828D_Programmierhandbuch-Grundlagen_DE_2013.pdf, 3.3 Programmkopf, p. 46 (the text layer there shows only the heading; the code is readable in Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl_Programmierhandbuch-NC-Programmierung_SW492_DE_2019.pdf, p. 57) (The typical lathe program header writes N10 G0 G153 X200 Z500 T0 D0 with the comment "Werkzeugträger zurückziehen, bevor Werkzeugrevolver geschwenkt wird", and only then N20 T5 to swing tool 5 in. The milling header by contrast is N10 T="SF12", N20 M6, N30 D1 - the two idioms the reader has to separate.); Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl_PLC-Alarmliste_DE.pdf, p. 126 (The counter-indication, from a builder's PLC alarm texts on a mill with an additional magazine. Alarm 701051 "Zusatzmagazin beladen über Spindel: Spindel nicht leer" gives as its remedy "Die Werkzeugspindel mit T0 leer fahren, anschließend das Beladen wiederholen", and 701052 says a tool put into the spindle "kann mit T0 im Zusatzmagazin abgelegt werden". Neither mentions an M6, so on that machine a lone T0 is spoken of as emptying the spindle.). (Citations re-paged to the cnc-manuals connector 2026-10-26.)

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

Keep main. A lone T0 on an M6 machine is PRELOAD=0. It is TOOL=0 only when the main program ends after it (M30/M2/M17) with no M6 or other T in between; a RET is not an end. Siemens 5 reads: 'T0 M6 unloads; T0 alone unloads on a turret'.
Basis: manual
Source: 840D sl Grundlagen 2013 p. 53-57, 59 (T selects, M6 changes, T0 deselects) (cnc-manuals). A builder PLC text (PLC alarm list p. 126) is machine-specific and can be handled by that machine's plugin.
Differs from the recommendation: no
Confidence: high

#### D299 G0 to G3 on every motion block
Question: Implementation 13 (P3-03, TargetState) writes a modal word "only on change". Fanuc 10 rule 1 writes G0/G1 only when the verb changes and adds "a [format] option may ask for the G on every block", without naming the key. Siemens 12 has no rule on it, and siemens 2 makes group 1 modal. The phase 5 acceptance (15-phase-5, P5-02) asks for "the generic words of the example's own comments", among them `G0 Z2=-58`. That line follows `G0 X45` with only COUPON(S2,S1) and M68 between them. The Siemens compiler writes G0 to G3 on every motion block without an option, and so does the expected output file. The Fanuc compiler writes G0/G1 on change and G2/G3 on every arc (wave-3 question 75, D282). The comparison rules (implementation 13, P3-07; SiemensEquivalence) compare every line after the header in order. Whichever form the compiler writes, a corpus program that writes the other form fails the round trip of the phase 5 acceptance (M8).
Recommendation: Use one [format] key, the option fanuc 10 rule 1 foresees, read by every compiler, for example `motion_code = "change" | "every_block"`, with "change" as the default (implementation 13, fanuc 10 rule 1). millturn1.toml sets "every_block", so the phase 5 acceptance and the expected file stay as they are. siemens-840dsl-mill.toml takes the form its two corpus programs write. Siemens 12 rule 2 and fanuc 10 rule 1 name the key, and the answer also settles the G2/G3 of Fanuc arcs, which D282 recommends as a fixed rule of the writer; answer the two together. Reason: implementation 13 (P3-07 risks) says an output habit gets a [format] option, "not a special case", and the [format] keys of D276 (wave-3 questions 48, 81 and 82) already hold the Fanuc habits this way. Alternative: a family rule. Siemens always writes the code on every motion block (the code on main), siemens 12 rule 2 says so, and a corpus source that writes it on change does not round-trip line by line.
Where: Siemens 12 rule 2; fanuc 10 rule 1; machine-config 2 ([format]); implementation 13 (P3-03 TargetState; P3-07 comparison rules and risks) and 15-phase-5 (P5-02 acceptance). Code: src/Ncx.Compilers/Siemens/SiemensMotion.cs Write (TODO(question) at line 215); src/Ncx.Compilers/Fanuc/FanucMotion.cs WriteMotionCode (TODO(question) at line 263, wave-3 question 75); src/Ncx.Core/Machine/OutputFormat.cs (TODO(question) at line 73, wave-3 questions 81 and 82); machines/millturn1.toml; tests/Ncx.Acceptance/Expected/MILLTURN_TRANSFER.millturn1.mpf; tests/Ncx.Acceptance/Examples/SiemensEquivalence.cs; related D276, D282.

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, not confirmed by the maintainer: the manuals do not settle this. Holds after checking. The manuals do not settle which form NCX should write, because G0/G1/G2/G3 are modal ("Die Fahrbefehle sind modal wirksam") and only one G of a group may stand in a block, so both forms run identically and this is an NCX output habit. But they do refute the draft's Alternative: Siemens' own turning example writes the verb only where it changes (N70, N75 and N90 carry no G1), and a real 840D post output in the library does the same, including arcs (a second arc block with no G3). Take the [format] key of the Recommendation, `motion_code = "change" | "every_block"`, with millturn1.toml on "every_block"; "Siemens always writes the code on every motion block" is not a family rule.
Evidence: Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl-828D_Programmierhandbuch-Grundlagen_DE_2013.pdf, p. 177 (Lists G0, G1, G2 and G3 as the Fahrbefehle and closes the list with "Die Fahrbefehle sind modal wirksam", so the control needs the verb only where it changes. Verified verbatim.); Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl-828D_Programmierhandbuch-Grundlagen_DE_2013.pdf, p. 458 (Legend of the statement list, entry "G-Funktion": only one G function of a group may be written in a block, and a G function is either modal until another of its group revokes it or effective only for the block it stands in. Verified verbatim.); Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl-828D_Programmierhandbuch-Grundlagen_DE_2013.pdf, p. 48-49 (Section 3.4, turning example 2. G1 is rewritten after each arc (N45, N55, N65, N85) but omitted on the blocks that only continue a line: N70 X35 Z-40, N75 Z-57, N90 X52 Z-63. Both of the consecutive rapid blocks N125 and N130 carry G0, and N130 is the G53 retract.); Eigene Notizen: Reiden, Muster_PGM.MPF (840D post output, not a manual), p. file lines 77-78 and 81-83 (blocks N74/N75 and N78/N79/N80) (not in the connector) (A real Sinumerik post writes the motion verb only on change: the second arc of a pair, N75, carries no G3, and after N78 G0 Z211. the blocks N79 Z217. and N80 X-54.392 Y-199.131 carry no G0. (The answer under review located these at "lines 74-80, 137-140"; the N numbers it quotes are right, the file line numbers were not.)). (Citations re-paged to the cnc-manuals connector 2026-10-26.)

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

One [format] key, read by every compiler: `motion_code = "change" | "arcs" | "every_block"`. "change" writes the verb only on change, arcs included. "arcs" writes G0/G1 on change and G2/G3 on every arc block. "every_block" writes the verb on every motion block. A key left out takes the family value main writes today: Fanuc "arcs", Siemens "every_block" (D263 pattern). millturn1.toml keeps "every_block". siemens-840dsl-mill.toml takes the form of its corpus programs.
Basis: manual
Source: 840D sl Grundlagen 2013 p. 48-49, 177, 458 (verbs are modal; the Siemens example writes them on change) (cnc-manuals). Both forms run the same, so this is an output habit.
Differs from the recommendation: yes: adds a third value "arcs" and uses family defaults instead of a global "change" default, so no current output changes.
Confidence: medium
Code impact: OutputFormat/loader key; SiemensMotion.Write, FanucMotion.WriteMotionCode.

#### D303 Where the machine file of a job manifest is looked for
Question: Machine-config 8 writes [job] machine = "nakamura-ntjx.toml". Architecture 10 runs the job 'on the machine the manifest names unless --machine names another'. No document says where that value is looked for. Language 4.8 puts the manifest 'next to the files', and machine-config 10 puts machine files in machines/. Its layout shows no manifest. D206 (open) covers only --machine and the machine key of ncx.toml. D207 (open) asks the same question for the cycle catalog that a machine file names. It recommends the cycle folders alone. Its alternative is to look first in the folder of the machine file, 'so that a machine file and its own catalog travel together'. On main, JobPipeline.MachineOf first takes a file of that name next to the manifest. Otherwise it takes the value the way --machine does: a path from the working directory, then a name in the machine folders. ncx compile --job uses the same function.
Recommendation: Keep what the code does. The value is looked up first in the folder of the manifest, where the channel files stand, and otherwise resolves as --machine does (D206). Write this into machine-config 8 and the --job sentence of architecture 10. Answer with D206 and D207, so that the three lookups read alike, or state why a manifest's machine is looked up differently from a machine's catalog. Reason: a manifest and its machine file can travel together. A project that keeps its manifests next to the channel files in programs/ (language 4.8, machine-config 10) still finds the machine in machines/ through the machine folders. Alternative: resolve [job] machine exactly as --machine, so that a value names the same machine on the command line and in a manifest. That is the rule D207 recommends for the catalog.
Where: Machine-config 8 (machine key comment) and 10; architecture 10 (the --job sentence); D206; D207. Code: src/Ncx.Cli/JobPipeline.cs:142 MachineOf; src/Ncx.Cli/Commands/CompileJob.cs:57; src/Ncx.Cli/ProjectFolders.cs FindMachine.

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, not confirmed by the maintainer: the manuals do not settle this. No manual settles an NCXchange lookup, but the control the project mirrors resolves a name the way main does and gives a reason to make the three lookups read alike. Siemens resolves a subprogram call without a path through one fixed order: the current directory — the workpiece or standard directory in which the program was selected — then its _SPF and _MPF variants, then the subprogram directory in the NC and in the global store, then a CALLPATH extension, and last the user, manufacturer and standard cycle directories; that order is walked for every single call, so where the calling program sits is irrelevant, and nested directories are not searched. That is main's manifest-folder-first rule with the shared folders behind it, and it is one order used everywhere rather than a different one per kind of file, so answering D206, D207 and D303 with the same order has a precedent. This is an analogy from a control's program store, not a statement about NCXchange; Siemens' first entry is the directory in which the program was selected, which corresponds to the manifest's own folder rather than to the working directory, so it supports the manifest-first half and says nothing about the --machine fallback.
Evidence: Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl_Programmierhandbuch-NC-Programmierung_SW492_DE_2019.pdf, p. 572-573 (Section 3.4.1.4 gives the eight-step search path for a subprogram call without a path — current directory/name, name_SPF, name_MPF, the _N_SPF_DIR of the NC and of the global part-program store, a CALLPATH extension, then _N_CUS_DIR, _N_CMA_DIR and _N_CST_DIR — and adds that the path is walked for every single call, "es ist irrelevant, wo sich das übergeordnete Programm befindet", and that nested directories are not searched.); Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl_Programmierhandbuch-NC-Programmierung_SW492_DE_2019.pdf, p. 545-546 (CALLPATH extends that search path by one named workpiece directory, inserted as step 5 before the user cycle directory, must be programmed in a part-program line of its own, and aborts with correction-block alarm 14009 if the directory does not exist.). (Citations re-paged to the cnc-manuals connector 2026-10-26.)

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

Keep main. [job] machine is looked up first in the manifest's folder, then resolved as --machine does (working directory path, then the machine folders). Answer D206 and D207 with the same order.
Basis: manual (analogy) + logical
Source: 840D sl SW 4.92 p. 545-546, 572-573 (one fixed search order: the selection directory first, then the shared folders) (cnc-manuals).
Differs from the recommendation: no
Confidence: high
Code impact: none.

#### D304 Channels at one mark with different WITH
Question: VM 3.7 releases a mark 'when all participants (WITH, default all) wait at m', and language 4.8 gives WITH per SYNC block. Neither says whose WITH counts when the channels waiting at one mark name different participants. Language 4.8 can be read both ways. 'The channel waits until every participating channel has reached SYNC=100' counts each channel's own participants, and 'then all continue' describes a shared release. Case: a three-channel job where channel 1 writes SYNC=100 WITH=1,2 and channel 2 writes SYNC=100 (all, so 1,2,3). The compiler writes the participants on the wait code of every path (controller-mapping 7: Fanuc P lists). Siemens WAITM lists, for each channel, the channels it waits for (siemens 9). On main (JobRunner.MarkReleasable) a mark is released only when every participant waits there with the same set. Otherwise the channels keep waiting, and the job ends in the deadlock VM571, which names each channel's mark and WITH.
Recommendation: Keep what the code does and say it in VM 3.7: the channels waiting at one mark must name the same participants. Channels whose participants differ are not released, and the job ends in the deadlock ERROR naming each channel's mark and WITH. Reason: VM 3.7 releases the participants together ('all are released'), and the path programs of a compile carry one participant list per wait, so differing lists are a mismatch between the programs. Alternative: the per-channel reading of language 4.8's first clause and of Siemens WAITM. Each channel continues once every channel of its own WITH has reached m. In the case above that releases channel 1 alone, and a Fanuc compile would then need a check of its own.
Where: VM 3.7 (SYNC sentence), 5 (deadlock at SYNC); language 4.8 (SYNC and WITH rows). Code: src/Ncx.Core/Jobs/JobRunner.Waits.cs:36 MarkReleasable.

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, not confirmed by the maintainer: The requirement is right, the consequence is not — but the correction has to be stated more narrowly than the answer under review did. Siemens WAITM releases each channel by its own participant list, and the control has a dedicated alarm for exactly the draft's case: alarm 16949 takes Ch3 WAITM(99,3,5), Ch5 WAITM(99,3,5), Ch7 WAITM(99,5,7) and says channel 7 may continue as soon as 5 and 7 are at the mark although channel 3 is still far away, after which the behaviour on reaching the mark again can no longer be determined; the remedy it gives is to name in every wait mark all the channels one wants to synchronise with. So keep the rule in VM 3.7 that the channels waiting at one mark must name the same participants, but report a mismatch with a diagnostic of its own modelled on 16949 instead of letting the job fall into the deadlock VM571. In the draft's own case (ch1 WITH=1,2; ch2 WITH=all) the control releases channel 1 as soon as 1 and 2 are at the mark, while channel 2 goes on waiting for channel 3 — so VM571 is wrong for the channel whose list is satisfied, not for every channel.
Evidence: Siemens_Sinumerik-840D-sl_Parameter_Alarme_BS.000503-DE-000-00_DE.pdf, p. 345-346 (Alarm 16949 "Korrespondenz zwischen Marke von Kanal %1 und Kanal %2 ist ungueltig": a channel defines a wait mark with channels that have no corresponding mark, so the channels do not wait for each other. The worked example has Ch3 and Ch5 waiting mutually while Ch7 waits only for Ch5, so Ch7 may continue as soon as 5 and 7 are at the mark, and once the mark is reached again the behaviour can no longer be determined precisely. Remedy: name in every wait mark all channels to synchronise with, or suppress the alarm with $MN_SUPPRESS_ALARM_MASK bit 23; three worked solutions follow. Unlike 16946 to 16948 on the same pages, this alarm is not restricted to "Group-Serupro". Verified verbatim.); Siemens_Sinumerik-840D-sl_Parameter_Alarme_BS.000503-DE-000-00_DE.pdf, p. 346 (Added in review as a current-edition corroboration: the 2018 alarm manual carries 16949 with the same explanation, the same Ch3/Ch5/Ch7 example and the same remedy, citing MD11410 $MN_SUPPRESS_ALARM_MASK bit 23 — so the behaviour is not an artefact of the 2005 edition.); Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl-828D_Programmierhandbuch-Arbeitsvorbereitung_DE_2013.pdf, p. 117-118 (Section 1.13, Bedeutung: WAITM waits for a mark to be reached in the channels it names; the mark is set in the channel's own program by the WAITM itself, the own channel need not be listed, the mark is deleted after synchronisation, and at most ten marks per channel may be set at a time — i.e. the participant list is per channel. Verified verbatim.); DMG-MORI_CTX-NTX_Schulung-Strukturprogrammierung-Teil1_DE_2016.pdf, p. 114-119 (The two-channel example X_FUTTER_GAMMA writes the identical participant list WAITM(n, WAIT_K1, WAIT_K2) in both channel programs at every mark (10, 15, 20, 25, 1, 80, 90, 0) — the shop convention is exactly the remedy alarm 16949 prescribes. (The answer under review gave the printed pages as 5-48/5-49; the page footers read 5-49 and 5-50.)). (Citations re-paged to the cnc-manuals connector 2026-10-26.)

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

Keep the rule that the channels waiting at one mark must name the same participants, but report a mismatch with an ERROR of its own (next free VM57x code, "channels at mark m name different participants: ch1 WITH=1,2; ch2 WITH=1,2,3"), raised as soon as a channel reaches mark m while another participant of either list waits there with a different set; the job stops there instead of running into the deadlock VM571. The job compiler checks the same statically (CMP diagnostic, ERROR) where it can pair the marks, because the Fanuc P lists it writes would raise alarm 160 on the control. NCX does not model the Siemens per-channel release, since the control itself calls the behaviour after it undeterminable.
Basis: manual
Source: Siemens_Sinumerik-840D-sl_Parameter_Alarme_BS.000503-DE-000-00_DE.pdf, connector p. 345-346 (alarm 16949, remedy: name the same channels in every wait mark); Fanuc_30i-B_Wartung-Wartung_B-64485EN_EN.pdf, p. 778 (PS0160 MISMATCH WAITING M-CODE for differing P values). Web check found no further source.
Differs from the recommendation: yes: a dedicated mismatch ERROR (at detection and at compile) replaces the generic deadlock VM571 for this case.
Confidence: high
Code impact: JobRunner.Waits MarkReleasable (new mismatch diagnostic); job compiler mark check; diagnostics.md.

#### D305 A channel that waits for a finished or never-started channel
Question: VM 3.7 makes 'All channels waiting with no releasable mark' the deadlock ERROR. The architecture 5.4 flowchart ends the job ('job finished') when no channel can run and not all of them wait. Read literally, the job then ends as finished, without a diagnostic, in two cases. In the first, channel 1 has finished and channel 2 waits at SYNC=110 with 1,2. In the second, channel 2 waits for a START_CHANNEL=2 in a block that channel 1 never executed. Either way channel 2 never reaches PROGRAM=END. On main (JobRunner.Run, ReportDeadlock) every job that ends with an unfinished channel is the deadlock ERROR VM571. The message names the finished channels and the START_CHANNEL a channel waits for.
Recommendation: Keep what the code does and write it into VM 3.7, VM 5 and the architecture 5.4 flowchart. When no channel can execute a block and some channel has not finished, that is the deadlock ERROR, whether the other channels wait or have finished. 'All waiting' means 'every channel that has not finished'. A WAIT_CHANNEL on a finished channel is released, as now. The text of VM571 then drops 'every channel waits'. Reason: a channel that can never reach its PROGRAM=END is the hang the deadlock rule exists for, and the message already says what each channel waits for. Alternative: a separate ERROR, 'waits for a channel that has finished or is never started', leaving VM571 for waits among running channels.
Where: VM 3.7 (deadlock sentence), 5; architecture 5.4 (flowchart node 'all waiting?'); docs/spec/generated/diagnostics.md (VM571 row). Code: src/Ncx.Core/Jobs/JobRunner.Waits.cs:75 ReportDeadlock; JobRunner.cs Run; src/Ncx.Core/Model/DiagnosticCodes.Validation.cs:127 (VM571). Answer with D309.

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, corrected 2026-10-26 after the manual audit, not confirmed by the maintainer: the manuals do not settle this. Keeping the ERROR stays the proposal, but as an NCX choice, not because the machines do it: a builder documents a control that lets a lone channel run past its waits. Nakamura says that on its three-unit machines (WTS, NTM 3, NTY 3) the waiting M codes are ignored when one unit runs alone in automatic operation, and the next block is processed. Fanuc offers the same as a switch: the no-wait signal (NOWT for two paths, NMWT for more) makes a path ignore its waiting M codes, so a single path can run without deleting them, and the handle-retrace check of one path of a multi-path system requires the other paths out of MEM mode and that signal set. Neither control raises a diagnostic for a partner that never starts; with the signal off the wait simply holds. The DMG CTX two-channel template puts a common WAITM(0,...) in front of each channel's M30, so a correctly written job does not end with one channel still at a mark. The ERROR remains the stricter reading for a check tool, since it reports the hang the machine shows with waits enabled; the lone-channel behaviour of Nakamura and Fanuc is what the WARNING alternative of D306 would model. The other half of the recommendation is not settled: Siemens WAITE waits for another channel's program end but says nothing about a channel that has already ended. The proposal still agrees with the recommendation, on a weaker reason. Searched: Wartefunktion, M-Code für Warten, Nicht warten, NOWT, NMWT, WAITM, WAITMC, WAITE, Wartemarke together with Reset / Programmende, Kanal im Reset, nicht gestarteter Kanal.
Evidence: Nakamura-Tome Programmierhandbuch Band 1 (4810004ECL-1, 2013), p. 126-127 (wait M codes for three-path machines with P12, P13, P23, P123 or P3, P5, P6, P7 by parameter 8103#1; note: on WTS, NTM 3 and NTY 3 the waiting M codes are ignored in automatic operation of one unit and the next block is processed.); FANUC Series 30i/31i/32i-MODEL B Operator's Manual B-64484EN, p. 1033-1037 (23.2 waiting function for paths; with the waiting ignore signal set, the paths ignore the M code for waiting and execute the next block at once; caution 3: with only one path active the waiting M code need not be deleted, because NOWT or NMWT can ignore it.); FANUC B-64484EN, p. 1268 (manual handle retrace, check of one path in a multi-path system: the paths not checked are put into a mode other than MEM, and the no-wait signal is set if the program contains waiting M codes.); DMG MORI CTX/NTX Schulung Strukturprogrammierung Teil 1 (2016), p. 118-119 (two-channel example X_FUTTER_GAMMA: NN8300: WAITM(0, WAIT_K1, WAIT_K2) and then NN9999: M30; OCR text); DMG MORI CTX/NTX Schulung Strukturprogrammierung Teil 2 (2016), example X_GREIFER_NTX1000 (cited by the earlier answer for the same pattern; listed in the connector, but its text cannot be read there).
Corrected: Replaced "no page describes a control that releases a waiting channel because its partner was never started": Nakamura Band 1 p. 127 says its three-unit machines ignore wait codes when one unit runs alone. The ERROR stays, now as an NCX choice; the Fanuc pages now cite the English B-64484EN and the DMG pattern Teil 1.

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

Keep main. When no channel can execute and some channel has not finished, that is deadlock ERROR VM571, whether the others wait or have finished. A WAIT_CHANNEL on a finished channel is released. VM571's text drops 'every channel waits' and keeps naming what each channel waits for.
Basis: logical (manual-informed)
Source: Nakamura 4810004ECL-1 p. 126-127 and FANUC B-64484EN p. 1033-1037 show that a control can ignore waits (NOWT), but only by an explicit switch. A check tool should report the hang the machine shows with waits enabled.
Differs from the recommendation: no
Confidence: medium
Code impact: none (VM571 text; docs VM 3.7, 5, architecture 5.4).

#### D306 WITH, WAIT_CHANNEL or START_CHANNEL naming a channel the job does not run
Question: Language 4.8 gives WITH, WAIT_CHANNEL and START_CHANNEL channel numbers. VM 3.7 and 5 do not say what a number that matches no [[channel]] of the manifest does. Case: a job of channels 1 and 2 on a machine with [machine] channels = [1, 2, 3], where channel 1 writes SYNC=100 WITH=1,3 or WAIT_CHANNEL=3. That SYNC can never be released and that WAIT_CHANNEL never ends. START_CHANNEL=3 would start a program the job does not hold. On main (JobRunner.ChannelNamed) each one is the ERROR VM851 on its block. The message names the channels of the job, and the job stops.
Recommendation: Keep the ERROR. Add it to the ERROR list of VM 5 and to VM 3.7: 'a WITH, WAIT_CHANNEL or START_CHANNEL naming a channel the job does not run'. Reason: it is the channel counterpart of 'missing jump or call target' (VM 5). Every other outcome either ends in a deadlock or runs something the job does not describe. Alternative: a WARNING, with the word taken as if that channel were not named (WITH without it, no wait, nothing started), so that a job can check a subset of a machine's channels.
Where: VM 3.7, 5; language 4.8. Code: src/Ncx.Core/Jobs/JobRunner.Words.cs:121 ChannelNamed (VM851); docs/spec/generated/diagnostics.md.

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, not confirmed by the maintainer: the manuals do not settle this. Split the case, because the controls treat the two halves differently. A channel number the machine does not have is an error on the control too: the 30i-B raises PS0161 "ILLEGAL P OF WAITING M-CODE" when the P value is negative, is inappropriate for the system configuration, or is a two-path wait in a system with three or more paths — so keeping VM851 as an ERROR is right for a number outside the machine's [machine] channels. A channel the machine has but the job does not run is a situation the control supports: with the "Nicht warten" signal set for channel 2, Fanuc's own three-channel example has the wait M102 P7 (or P123) satisfied by channels 1 and 3 alone, exactly as if the absent channel were not named. For that half the draft's Alternative (WARNING, the word taken as if the channel were not named) is the machine-like answer. Caveats: Fanuc's release of the remaining channels comes from a PLC signal set by the machine builder, not from the program, so NCX would be adding a switch rather than copying a language rule; the page that ties the signal to checking one channel's program belongs to the handle-retrace check function. Nothing was found for Siemens WAITM naming a channel that is configured but not started. Searched: WAITM, WAITE, Wartefunktion für Kanäle, M-Code für Warten, Nicht warten, ILLEGAL P OF WAITING M-CODE, MISMATCH WAITING M-CODE, Systemkonfiguration.
Evidence: Fanuc_30i-B_Wartung-Wartung_B-64485EN_EN.pdf, Appendix A Alarm list, p. 778 (printed 754) (Alarm 0161 "ILLEGAL P OF WAITING M-CODE": <1> when address P is negative, <2> when a P value inappropriate for the system configuration was specified, <3> when a waiting M code without a P command (2-path waiting) was specified in a system having 3 or more paths. Alarm 0160 "MISMATCH WAITING M-CODE" covers mismatching M codes or P values between paths. This is the 30i-B's own alarm, the control the rest of the answer rests on); Fanuc_16-18-21-B_Wartungshandbuch_B-63525EN-02_EN.pdf, alarm list, p. 874 (printed 844) (The older control states the same rule for its three-path T series: alarm 161 "ILLEGAL P OF WAITING M-CODE" fires when the value of address P is negative, is 1, 2, 4 or a value not smaller than 8, or when the value specified in P is not consistent with the system configuration; the remedy is to correct the program); Fanuc_30i-B_Bedienung-Drehen-Fraesen_B-64484EN_EN.pdf, 23.2, p. 1036-1037 (In the worked three-channel example, with the "Nicht warten" signal for channel 2 set, a wait written as M102 P7 (or M102 P123) for all three channels is satisfied by channels 1 and 3 alone: channel 3 then waits only until the machining in channel 1 is finished. Case <3> is the mirror image: channel 2 does not wait, channel 1 still waits for channel 3. The caution adds that with only one channel active the waiting M codes may stay in the program); Fanuc_30i-B_Bedienung-Drehen-Fraesen_B-64484EN_EN.pdf, manual handle retrace, p. 1268 (Checking one channel of a multi-channel system is an intended operation of this check function, and it requires NOWT or NMWT to be set when the program contains a waiting M code). (Citations re-paged to the cnc-manuals connector 2026-10-26.)

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

Split by the machine. A channel number not in [machine] channels stays the ERROR VM851 (the control alarms too: PS0161). A channel the machine has but the job does not run is a WARNING (next free VM85x code, naming the channel and the job's channels), and the word is taken as if that channel were not named: WITH without it, WAIT_CHANNEL does not wait, START_CHANNEL starts nothing. The compiler writes the word unchanged (with the channel) because the program is for the whole machine.
Basis: manual
Source: Fanuc_30i-B_Wartung-Wartung_B-64485EN_EN.pdf, connector p. 778 (PS0161 for a P inappropriate to the system configuration); Fanuc_30i-B_Bedienung-Drehen-Fraesen_B-64484EN_EN.pdf, 23.2, p. 1036-1037 (with "no wait" for a path, M102 P123 is satisfied by the others) and p. 1268 (checking one channel of a multi-channel program is an intended operation).
Differs from the recommendation: yes: ERROR only outside the machine's channels; a WARNING with the channel ignored for a machine channel outside the job.
Confidence: medium
Code impact: JobRunner.Words ChannelNamed (split by [machine] channels, new WARNING); diagnostics.md; VM 3.7/5 text.

#### D307 CHANNEL of the header against the channel of the job manifest
Question: Language 4.1 and 4.14 and VM 2.8 take a program's channel from CHANNEL in its header (default 1). Machine-config 8 and D15 bind a program to the id of its [[channel]]. Controller-mapping 7 says a Siemens program's channel 'is in the job (INIT) or the file name'. No document says which applies when they differ. Case: a [[channel]] with id = 1 whose program header reads CHANNEL=2, for example a path-2 file bound to channel 1 by mistake. On main (JobRunner.CheckHeaderChannel) the channel of the job applies, with the WARNING VM853 on the header. A header without CHANNEL runs on the manifest's channel without a diagnostic, as D223 recommends.
Recommendation: Keep what the code does: the manifest decides, and a header CHANNEL that differs is a WARNING. Write this into language 4.14 and machine-config 8. Reason: the manifest is the one description of the job (D15), and the job compiler already writes each program for the channel of its [[channel]] (JobCompiler.SectionsOnJobChannels). Alternative: an ERROR, because the reader resolved the file for the header's channel: its T words for that channel's holder (D219) and its channel-bound functions (D56, D155).
Where: Language 4.1 (CHANNEL row), 4.14; VM 2.8 (channel.id); machine-config 8; D223. Code: src/Ncx.Core/Jobs/JobRunner.Words.cs:145 CheckHeaderChannel (VM853); src/Ncx.Compilers/JobCompiler.Run.cs SectionsOnJobChannels.

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, not confirmed by the maintainer: the manuals do not settle this. The manuals confirm the first half and leave the severity open. A Siemens part program does not declare a channel: the channel is assigned from outside, by INIT(<channel>,<path>) or by the operator's program selection, and a program can only read the channel it happens to run in ($P_CHANNO, read-only, values 1 to 10). So the manifest deciding is right, and language 4.14 and machine-config 8 can say so. What the manuals leave open is the diagnostic: no Siemens page says what a translator should do when a program's intended channel and its actual channel differ. The maintainer's own DMG GMX start program shows the shop convention is fatal rather than a warning — it opens with IF CHAN_NO <> 1 GOTOF ERROR_CHAN_NO and that label ends in a message, M0 and an endless GOTOB, so the program cannot continue in the wrong channel.
Evidence: Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl-828D_Programmierhandbuch-Arbeitsvorbereitung_DE_2013.pdf, p. 117 (INIT(<Kanal-Nr.>,<Pfadangabe>,<Quittungsmodus>) is the predefined procedure for selecting the NC program that is to be run in the given channel — the channel is a parameter of the selection, not something the program declares. The same page defines START as the procedure that starts the selected programs in the other channels. Verified verbatim.); Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl-828D_Programmierhandbuch-Arbeitsvorbereitung_DE_2013.pdf, p. 211 (Section 2.1: in the second line of a file the target path is given with $PATH=…, and the worked example is %_N_WELLE_MPF followed by ;$PATH=/_N_WKS_DIR/_N_WELLE_WPD. Without a path entry the file lands in /_N_SPF_DIR, the working memory or /_N_MPF_DIR by its extension. Neither line names a channel. (The page does not state that these are the only header directives; that clause of the answer under review is struck.)); Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl_Listenhandbuch-Systemvariable_SW45_DE_2012.pdf, p. 138 (INT $P_CHANNO, "Abfrage der aktuellen Kanalnummer", value 1 to 10, channel-specific; the read/write table gives Read X for the part program and Write "-" — a program can find out its channel but cannot set it. Verified verbatim.); Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl-828D_Funktionshandbuch-Grundfunktionen_DE_2012.pdf, K1, p. 580-581 (Section 8.9.2 "Anwahl und Starten des Teileprogramms": a part program can only be selected while the channel concerned is in the reset state, and the NC instruction START can start program execution in another channel — the binding of program to channel is an operation on the channel, made outside the file. Verified verbatim.); Eigene Notizen: DMG GMX 400 linear, L1001.txt (builder start program, not a manual), p. lines 1-3 and 57-60 (not in the connector) (The channel-1 start program is headed ";OPERATION :STARTPROGRAMM KANAL 1" and its N15 block jumps to ERROR_CHAN_NO when CHAN_NO is not 1. That label issues MSG("$67008") — a message number whose own comment in the file reads "falsche Kanalnummer oder Kanalname" — then M0 and GOTOB back to itself, so a wrong-channel run cannot continue. Verified line by line.). (Citations re-paged to the cnc-manuals connector 2026-10-26.)

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

The manifest decides the channel. A header CHANNEL that differs from it is an ERROR (VM853 raised to ERROR), because the reader resolved T words and channel-bound functions for the header's channel (D219, D56). A header without CHANNEL runs silently on the manifest's channel (D223).
Basis: manual + logical
Source: 840D sl Arbeitsvorbereitung 2013 p. 117 (INIT assigns the channel from outside); system variables p. 138 ($P_CHANNO read-only) (cnc-manuals). The maintainer's DMG start program stops on a wrong channel (M0 plus an endless loop), so the shop convention treats this as fatal.
Differs from the recommendation: yes: ERROR instead of WARNING, as the safer option, since a path-2 program on channel 1 would address the wrong turret.
Confidence: medium
Code impact: JobRunner.CheckHeaderChannel severity; diagnostics.md VM853.

#### D308 Resource state shared by the channels of a job
Question: VM 2 keeps tool state per holder resource (2.3) and spindle state per spindle resource (2.4). VM 2.8 and 3.7 make the resources per job, 'shared by all channels of the job', so a spindle that path 1 starts is running for path 2 as well. The architecture 5.4 flowchart ('load manifest, one VM per channel, shared resources') and implementation 16 P6-01 ('the shared resources') read the same way. But 2.3 puts lastHolder, which OFFSET (VM 3.8 rule 2) and D236 follow, in the per-holder table. Rule 2 also sends a TOOL without a role to default_holder from every channel. Nakamura path 2's TOOL=6 OFFSET=56 would then change the tool of path 1's holder T1 (D219). On main (JobRunner.Add) each channel keeps its own resource state, as a channel program checked alone does. So a path that cuts on a spindle that only the other path started gets the WARNING 'spindle OFF before a LINE' (VM500, VM 5).
Recommendation: Follow VM 2.8. Keep one state per job for every holder (2.3) and every spindle (2.4), which the VM of every channel reads and changes in round order. lastHolder, coolant and functions (2.5) stay per channel, and so does everything in 2.1, 2.2, 2.6 and 2.7, so lastHolder moves out of the 2.3 table. The compiler of each channel program keeps its own state, because every channel file must stand alone. Apply this after D219, whose reading gives path-2 T words the turret's role. D233's recommendation already assumes this reading. Reason: it is what VM 2.8, VM 3.7 ('Resources are per job'), VM 9 level 1 ('conflicts between channels') and the architecture 5.4 flowchart say, and it removes the false VM500 when both turrets turn on one spindle. Alternative: keep the per-channel state as coded, and amend VM 2.8 and architecture 5.4 to 'resource definitions per job, state per channel; conflicts through [shared] (D20)'.
Where: VM 2 (intro), 2.3 (lastHolder row), 2.4, 2.8, 3.7; architecture 5.4 (flowchart node B); implementation 16 P6-01; D219, D233, D236. Code: src/Ncx.Core/Jobs/JobRunner.cs:79 Add; the resource state of src/Ncx.Core/VirtualMachine.

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, not confirmed by the maintainer: the manuals do not settle this. The manuals settle the machine half of the question and leave the NCX half open. A spindle is one physical resource that either channel can command: Fanuc 30i-B §23.4 shows a lathe with one spindle and two tool carriers and says a channel's spindle is normally driven by that channel's own commands, while channel-select signals for the spindle setpoint let one channel's program drive the spindle of any other channel; on the Mori NTX1000 M03/M04/M05 for spindle 1 are standard from HEAD 1 and from HEAD 2 alike. Tool data is the opposite: the tool-compensation memory belongs to the individual channel and reaches the others only as far as parameter 5029 grants, and every Nakamura unit has its own program memory. And real shop programs do not lean on the other channel's spindle state — in the Walter Meier NTY3 examples both turret programs carry their own G97 S2000 M3 and their own M5 — so the VM500 warning of the question does not arise on a program written that way. Whether NCX keeps holder state per job or per channel, and how default_holder and D219 interact, no controller page states.
Evidence: Fanuc_30i-B_Bedienung-Drehen-Fraesen_B-64484EN_EN.pdf, p. 1040 (§23.5) (Section "Spindelsteuerung zwischen Kanälen", with figures for a lathe with one spindle and two tool carriers and for two spindles and two tool carriers: a channel's spindle can in principle be controlled by the commands programmed for that channel, but channel-select signals for the spindle setpoint let one channel's program control the spindle of any other channel. How that is wired is referred to the machine builder's manual); Fanuc_30i-B_Bedienung-Drehen-Fraesen_B-64484EN_EN.pdf, p. 1038–1039 (§23.4) ("Gemeinsamer Speicher für die Kanäle" is a function that gives all channels access to shared data in a defined area. Depending on parameter No. 5029 the tool-compensation memory of the individual channels is made available to the other channels wholly or in part; global macro variables likewise only as far as parameters 6036/6037 set. The figures label the offset pairs and macro variables per channel); Mori-Seiki_NT-NTX-Serie_Programmierung_Programmieranleitung-NTX1000SZM_PX-NT_4-K0DEEN_2011.pdf, p. 233 (M-code list, KOPF 1 / KOPF 2 columns; legend on p. 243) (The M-code list carries one column per head. M03 "Start der Spindel 1 (normal)", M04 and M05 are marked @ (standard) for HEAD 1 and for HEAD 2 alike, so either head may start and stop spindle 1. The *5 footnote beside them is a series restriction (NT3000–NT6000 with self-centering steady rest), not a head restriction); Nakamura-Tome_Fanuc_Programmierung_Programmierhandbuch_DE_2019.pdf, p. 128–130 (Beispiele Arbeitskombinationen NTY3, Beispiel 1 and 2) (Worked NTY3 examples where two turrets turn on the same spindle at once. Both channel programs carry the same number O1000 and each writes its own speed, direction and stop: in example 1 (both at the main spindle) each turret writes G54, G97 S2000 M3 and M5; in example 2 (both at the counter-spindle) the upper-right turret writes G54 … M3 … M5 and the lower-right G59 … M53 … M55. Nothing is left to the other channel's state); Nakamura-Tome_Super-NTJX_Programmierung_Liste-M-G-Codes_DE_2016.pdf, p. 1–2 (M3–M5 on p. 1, M53–M55 on p. 2) (On the NTJX the code names the spindle: M3/M4/M5 turn and stop the main (left) spindle, with the note (*R* = M53/M54/M55) for the right one; the datum is G54 for the left and G59 for the right spindle); Nakamura-Tome_Fanuc_Programmierung_Programmierhandbuch-1_4810004ECL-1_DE_2013.pdf, p. 20–24 (§2-4 Steuerung von Mehrbahn-Maschinen) (For every multi-path series (TW; WT/WY/NTJ/NTJ-100; WTW; WTS/NTM3/NTY3; STW/NTX(W)/NTXL) the programs are held in a separate program memory per unit, and the program of the second unit may be written as though it stood at the first, so the same program can machine identical parts on both sides. On the cycle-start signal the memories run at the same time and drive their own axes). (Citations re-paged to the cnc-manuals connector 2026-10-26.)

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

Follow the recommendation (VM 2.8): spindle state (2.4) and holder state (2.3) are one per job, read and changed by every channel's VM in round order; lastHolder, coolant, functions and everything in 2.1, 2.2, 2.6, 2.7 stay per channel, and lastHolder moves out of the 2.3 table. Tool offsets (OFFSET values) stay per channel, as the control's tool-compensation memory is per channel. Each channel's compiler keeps its own state so every channel file stands alone. Apply after D219 (settled), whose holder-by-channel rule keeps path 2's T words off path 1's holder.
Basis: logical
Source: The manuals confirm a spindle is one physical resource any channel may command (Fanuc_30i-B_Bedienung-Drehen-Fraesen_B-64484EN_EN.pdf p. 1040, Mori NTX1000 p. 233) and that offset memory is per channel (same Fanuc manual p. 1038-1039, parameter 5029). A manufacturer models physical state once; per-channel data (offsets, modal state) per channel. The manual's point that real programs write their own S/M3 does not argue against shared state, it only means the false VM500 rarely shows.
Differs from the recommendation: no (adds that offset values stay per channel)
Confidence: medium
Code impact: JobRunner.Add and VirtualMachine resource state (shared spindle/holder tables per job).

#### D309 Which channels start with a job, and START_CHANNEL of a running or finished channel
Question: Language 4.8 defines START_CHANNEL=2 as 'Start the program of channel 2 (Siemens START)', with NAME selecting the program. The rounds of VM 3.7 and the architecture 5.4 flowchart start every channel of the manifest and never mention START_CHANNEL. No document says which channels wait to be started, or what a START_CHANNEL of a channel that runs or has finished does. Siemens 9 and controller-mapping 7 describe INIT, START and WAITE. Neither says whether a channel-1 program may repeat them to run several programs in channel 2 one after another. On main (JobRunner.StartChannels, StartChannel) a channel waits to be started if a START_CHANNEL names it in any block of any file of the job, whether that block runs or not. Every other channel starts with the job. A START_CHANNEL of a channel that runs or has run starts nothing and gives the WARNING VM852.
Recommendation: Keep what the code does and write it into VM 3.7 and the architecture 5.4 flowchart. A channel that a START_CHANNEL in a file of the job names waits for it, and every other channel starts in the first round. The started channel runs the program that NAME selects, otherwise the program of its [[channel]]. A START_CHANNEL of a channel that runs or has run is the WARNING VM852 and starts nothing. Reason: a channel runs one program per job (machine-config 8, VM854), and the job compiler writes that program as the channel's one file. Alternative: a START_CHANNEL of a finished channel starts it again with the program it names, as a repeated Siemens INIT, START, WAITE sequence would. Every such program must then also be compiled into that channel's files.
Where: Language 4.8 (START_CHANNEL row); VM 3.7; architecture 5.4; siemens 9; controller-mapping 7. Code: src/Ncx.Core/Jobs/JobRunner.cs:154 StartChannels; JobRunner.Words.cs StartChannel (VM852) and ChannelsStartedByWord. Answer with D305.

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, not confirmed by the maintainer: Half of it is confirmed and half of it is not. A channel started from another channel must be in channel state Reset or "interrupted" when the START arrives, so a START_CHANNEL of a channel that is currently running really does start nothing and the WARNING VM852 is right there. But a channel that has reached M30 is back in the Reset state, and the control's pattern is INIT(<channel>,<program>), START(<channel>), WAITE(<channel>) — after M30 both conditions the manuals name (Reset for the selection, Reset or interrupted for the START) hold again, so nothing in them forbids selecting and starting that channel a second time. "A channel runs one program per job" is therefore an NCX restriction, not a Siemens one, and VM 3.7 should say it is ours.
Evidence: Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl-828D_Funktionshandbuch-Grundfunktionen_DE_2012.pdf, K1, p. 581 (Section 8.9.2: program selection is only possible while the channel is in the reset state; via the NC instruction START program execution can be started in another channel, and for that the channel concerned must be in DBX35.7 (Kanalzustand Reset) or DBX35.6 (Kanalzustand unterbrochen). Verified verbatim.); Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl-828D_Funktionshandbuch-Grundfunktionen_DE_2012.pdf, Z1, p. 1874 (Interface signal DB21 DBX35.7 "Kanalzustand Reset" is set to 1 as soon as the channel is in the reset state, that is no machining is active, and to 0 while a part program is being executed, a block search runs, TEACH IN or overstore is active. Verified verbatim.); Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl-828D_Funktionshandbuch-Grundfunktionen_DE_2012.pdf, Z1, p. 1839 (Added in review, because page 1874 alone does not equate program end with the reset state: the description of DB31 DBX60.6 names the condition "die Steuerung ist im Reset-Zustand (Reset-Taste bzw. Programmende)", i.e. program end puts the control into the reset state. Page 1870 adds that DBX35.0 "Programmzustand läuft" goes to 0 when the program end M02/M30 is reached.); Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl-828D_Programmierhandbuch-Arbeitsvorbereitung_DE_2013.pdf, p. 117 and 120 (START is the predefined procedure that starts the selected programs in the other channels (117); example 5 on page 120 has channel 1 do N10 INIT(2,"MPF200","N"), N11 START(2), work, synchronise with WAITM(1,1,2) and WAITM(2,1,2), then N200 WAITE(2) before its own N201 M30 — one INIT/START per channel, no repeat shown. Verified verbatim.); Siemens_Sinumerik-840D-sl_Parameter_Alarme_BS.000503-DE-000-00_DE.pdf, p. 345 (Alarms 16946 and 16947 both explain that the machine datum $MC_DISABLE_PLC_START decides which channel is started by the PLC in general and which channel may only be started from another channel by the part-program command START — but both open with "Dieser Alarm ist nur bei 'Group-Serupro' aktiviert". Verified verbatim.); Siemens_Sinumerik-840D-sl_Parameter_Alarme_BS.000503-DE-000-00_DE.pdf, p. 345-346 (Alarm 16948: a dependent channel, one started indirectly out of the current channel, must be finished ("dh. M30 erreicht haben") before the current channel ends; the remedy is to switch Group-Serupro off or to build in a WAITE. This alarm too is active only under "Group-Serupro", which the answer under review did not say. Verified verbatim.). (Citations re-paged to the cnc-manuals connector 2026-10-26.)

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

Keep the code: a channel named by a START_CHANNEL anywhere in the job's files waits to be started; every other channel starts in the first round; the started channel runs the program NAME selects, else its [[channel]] program. A START_CHANNEL of a running channel is the WARNING VM852 and starts nothing (the control requires Reset or interrupted). A START_CHANNEL of a finished channel also starts nothing, with a WARNING of its own text (or VM852 with a distinct message) stating that the control would restart it but NCX runs one program per channel per job. VM 3.7 states this as an NCX restriction, not a Siemens rule.
Basis: manual
Source: Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl-828D_Funktionshandbuch-Grundfunktionen_DE_2012.pdf, K1 p. 581, Z1 p. 1839, 1874 (START needs Reset/interrupted; program end = Reset); Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl-828D_Programmierhandbuch-Arbeitsvorbereitung_DE_2013.pdf p. 117, 120.
Differs from the recommendation: yes: the finished-channel case gets its own message and is documented as an NCX limit, not as the control's behaviour.
Confidence: medium
Code impact: JobRunner.Words StartChannel (separate message for finished channel); VM 3.7 text.

#### D310 Names of the output files of a job's channels
Question: Implementation 16 (P6-02) names the channel files "O1000, O1000.P-2 per the Nakamura convention from [machine] channels and a [format] key; _C1/_C2 for the STAMA form; %_N_1000_MPF/%_N_2000_MPF for Siemens". Machine-config 2 names no such key, and architecture 10 says only "one NC file per channel" for compile --job. Controller-mapping 7 (CHANNEL row) and fanuc 1 write the Nakamura names without an extension. Rationale B2 (answered), however, names the WY250L files as O1000.NC and O1000.P-2: path 1 with the extension .NC, path 2 without. No document says what happens when two channels would write one file name. Example: two programs of shaft.ncx on a machine without the key, both written as shaft.nc. Main reads [format] channel_files = "path_suffix" | "channel_suffix" | "program_name" and writes the Nakamura files without an extension. Clashing names get _C1 and _C2, while under file_per_program a clashing program name gets _2, _3 (wave-3 question 7, D266).
Recommendation: Adopt main's key in machine-config 2 as optional, with three values. "path_suffix": O plus NUMBER in at least four digits for the first channel of [machine] channels, and O1000.P-n for channel n, without an extension, as controller-mapping 7 and fanuc 1 write them. A program without NUMBER takes the file stem. The maintainer confirms the extension against the machine's memory card, since B2 names O1000.NC. "channel_suffix": the [job] name plus _C<n> plus the controller's extension (STAMA). "program_name": the program NAME plus the extension (the DMG units 1000 and 2000). Without the key, each channel keeps the name its family compiler gives the file of its program, and clashing names get _C<n>. Answer the clash rule together with D266 (wave-3 question 7). Reason: these are the three forms the documents show, an optional key leaves single-channel machines untouched, and a suffix keeps both files instead of overwriting one. The key also fits D223, whose reader takes .P-n with or without an extension. Alternatives: a clash is an ERROR that names both channels and nothing is written; or a template key (channel_file = "O{number}.P-{channel}") replaces the three fixed values.
Where: machine-config 2 ([format] channel_files, values, default); controller-mapping 7 (CHANNEL row points to it); fanuc 1; architecture 10 (compile --job row); implementation 16 P6-02; optionally channel_files in nakamura-ntjx.toml (path_suffix) and dmg-ctx-840d.toml (program_name), in docs/spec/examples/machines and machines/. Code: src/Ncx.Compilers/ChannelOutputNaming.cs:13, src/Ncx.Config/MachineConfigLoader.Identity.cs:131, src/Ncx.Core/Machine/OutputFormat.cs:62, src/Ncx.Core/Machine/ChannelFiles.cs, tests/Ncx.Compilers.Tests/Jobs/ChannelOutputNamingTests.cs; with D266, src/Ncx.Compilers/CompilerBase.Layout.cs:185 (FileNameOf); related D276 (the other [format] keys of the Fanuc compiler).

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, not confirmed by the maintainer: The documented Nakamura convention is O<program number> for the first unit and O<number>.P-n for unit n, with no extension. The memory-card table in Programmierhandbuch 1 §8-5 lists it per machine series and turret — WT, WTW, STS, NTJ, NTX(S), NTJX, NTMX, MX5: upper O△△△△, lower O△△△△.P-2; WTS/NTM3/NTY3 add .P-3; STW/NTX(W)/NTXL likewise — and it states that DNC operation carries the same restrictions. So path_suffix with .P-n and no extension is the builder's own form. What the manuals do not show is that B2's O1000.NC is wrong: that table governs files the control calls from a memory card, no page names the file of a main program kept on a PC or written by a post-processor, and per D223 those were the sample files' actual names. Because Nakamura's own NT NURSE writes the same pair in a second form (O<n>PRG.P-1 / O<n>PRG.P-2, and <n>.PG1 / .PG2 on machines with an 8-digit program number — there with an extension), a template value beside the three fixed ones is the safer shape. Nothing in the library bears on what happens when two channels would write one name.
Evidence: Nakamura-Tome_Fanuc_Programmierung_Programmierhandbuch-1_4810004ECL-1_DE_2013.pdf, p. 153 (§8-5, "LIST Programmdateiname auf der Speicherkarte") (A table of the file name per machine series and turret: SC/TMC/NTX() O△△△△; TW L-unit O△△△△, R-unit O△△△△.P-2; WT, WTW, STS, NTJ, NTX(S), NTJX, NTMX, MX5 upper O△△△△, lower O△△△△.P-2; WTS, NTM3, NTY3 upper L, upper R .P-2, lower .P-3; STW, NTX(W), NTXL upper, lower R .P-2, lower L .P-3. △△△△ is the program number. No extension anywhere. The restrictions below add "DNC-Betrieb mit gleichen Beschränkungen" and that several turrets may call at the same time); Nakamura-Tome_Fanuc_Programmierung_Programmierhandbuch-1_4810004ECL-1_DE_2013.pdf, p. 152 (§8-5 (b) and (2)) (The stored file name has to be assigned to the program number, written as the placeholder O△△△△; the worked example gives the TW L-unit file O1234 and the R-unit file O1234.P-2, and the call example reads a memory-card file named O1000.P-2 from the R-unit program. The page states no digit count and no zero padding); Nakamura-Tome_Fanuc-16-21i_Bedienung_NT-Nurse-Bedienungsanleitung_4800001EBG_DE_2013.pdf, p. 253 (§28-4 Ausgabeformat der Daten) (A second Nakamura naming: on machines without an 8-digit program number the punched main program is O????PRG.P-1 and the per-path data files O????OFS.P-1 and so on, with the note that .P-1, .P-2, .P-3 identify the data of path 1, 2 and 3; on 8-digit machines the forms are ????????.PG1 (PG2, PG3). Here path 1 carries a suffix too, and the 8-digit form carries an extension); Nakamura-Tome_Fanuc_Programmierung_Programmierhandbuch-1_4810004ECL-1_DE_2013.pdf, p. 20–24 (§2-4) (Each unit has its own program memory, so both channel programs may carry the same O number; the Walter Meier NTY3 examples do exactly that (O1000 in every turret program, 2019 handbook pp. 129–131)); Mori-Seiki_NT-NTX-Serie_Programmierung_Programmieranleitung-NTX1000SZM_PX-NT_4-K0DEEN_2011.pdf, p. 283 (§1-24, HINWS. 5) (For a program called from an external I/O device with M198 the called file name must be O plus a 4-digit number (or 7 digits on 8-digit-program-number machines), so "M198 P100;" needs the file O0100 (or O0000100) — the number is padded, not written bare). (Citations re-paged to the cnc-manuals connector 2026-10-26.)

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

Adopt the optional key `[format] channel_files = "path_suffix" | "channel_suffix" | "program_name"`. path_suffix writes O<NUMBER, at least 4 digits> for the first channel and O<NUMBER>.P-n for channel n, with no extension; a program without NUMBER uses the stem. channel_suffix writes <job>_C<n>.<ext> (STAMA). program_name writes NAME.<ext> (DMG). Without the key, each channel keeps its family name. Clashes get _C<n> with a WARNING, the same rule as D266. Set path_suffix in nakamura-ntjx.toml and program_name in dmg-ctx-840d.toml.
Basis: manual
Source: Nakamura 4810004ECL-1 p. 152-153 (§8-5 memory-card names, no extension), NT-Nurse 4800001EBG p. 253 (cnc-manuals). B2's O1000.NC was a PC-side name.
Differs from the recommendation: no
Confidence: medium
Code impact: none beyond docs and two machine files (the key is coded).
