#### D329 Mark range of a SYNC outside the [sync] groups
Question: Machine-config 5 gives [sync] mark_range and an example groups = [{ channels = [1, 2], range = [100, 199] }, { channels = [3, 4], range = [800, 849] }] ("Nakamura WTW: a second wait group between other units"; controller-mapping 7, SYNC row). It does not say which marks a SYNC may use when no group holds all its channels (channels 1 and 3), or when two overlapping groups do. Main takes the range of the first group in file order that holds every participant, otherwise mark_range. It checks each SYNC against that range (CMP710) and picks the range of a generated SYNC the same way.
Recommendation: Keep main and write it into machine-config 5: a SYNC takes the range of the first group whose channels hold all its participants, and every other SYNC takes mark_range. Reason: a group gives its channels a range of their own, which may lie outside mark_range (the WTW's M800 to M849 against M100 to M199), and every other SYNC keeps the machine's general range (Fanuc parameters 8110 and 8111). Alternative: when groups is given, a SYNC that no group holds is an ERROR (the machine has no wait between those units), and overlapping groups are an ERROR when the machine file loads. The maintainer may check the WTW rule in its manual.
Where: machine-config 5 ([sync] groups); controller-mapping 7 (SYNC row). Code: src/Ncx.Compilers/JobCompiler.Marks.cs:16 (CheckMarks, RangeOf).

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, corrected 2026-10-26 after the manual audit, not confirmed by the maintainer: Keep main's rule, and replace the example in machine-config 5 with what the WTW manual says. A Fanuc has two ranges of waiting M codes for the whole control, not one: the normal range from parameter 8110 (minimum) to 8111 (maximum), with 8110 ≤ mark ≤ 8111, and a range of high-speed waiting M codes given by a top number (8114) and a count (8115), which must not overlap the first (M codes in an overlap count as high-speed). Both name the participants with the P word (binary sum or path-number list, chosen by parameter 8103#1), not with the mark number; without P, paths 1 and 2 wait. So a SYNC that no builder group covers takes mark_range, and channels 1 and 3 need no range of their own. A group range need not lie inside the normal range: the WTW's M800–M849 lie inside its 8110..8111 span, form the high-speed range, or are handled by the builder's PLC, and the manuals do not say which. This supports the Recommendation's statement that a group's range may lie outside mark_range. The Nakamura WTW has three builder groups, not two: M100–M199 between the upper and the lower unit of one side, M800–M839 between left-upper↔right-lower and left-lower↔right-upper, M840–M849 between left-upper↔right-upper and left-lower↔right-lower. A group is a set of channel pairs, so the spec's example (channels [1,2] = 100–199, channels [3,4] = 800–849) describes no real machine. Two more points: the Mori NTX1000's control range is M100–M197 (the machine file's [101,197] is a deliberate narrowing for the ESPRIT post, per its own comment, not a transcription error), and on the three-path Nakamura machines one range M100–M199 serves every combination with P12/P13/P23/P123.
Evidence: FANUC 30i-B Operator's Manual (B-64484EN), p. 1033-1034 (§23.2: the range of waiting M codes is set beforehand in parameters 8110 and 8111; format M m (P p), P as a binary sum or a path-number combination chosen by 8103#1 (MWP); without P, paths 1 and 2 wait); p. 1037 (a waiting M code stands in a single block; for single-path operation it need not be deleted, the NOWT/NMWT signal ignores it); p. 1038 (§23.3 waiting M codes of high-speed type: the same format and use of P; their range is set in parameters 8114 and 8115); FANUC 30i-B Parameter Manual (B-64490EN-05), p. 455 (8110/8111 waiting M code range, 2-word, 0 or 100 to 99999999, (8110) ≤ code ≤ (8111), 0 when unused; 8114 top number and 8115 number of high-speed waiting M codes; their range must not overlap the other waiting M codes, overlapping codes count as high-speed); Nakamura-Tome Programmierhandbuch Band 1 (4810004ECL-1), p. 125 (M100 to M199 synchronize the unit programs of the two-path series; a different three-digit code on the other unit raises an alarm and stops both; on the WTW, M100–M199 serve between upper and lower unit and M800–M849 between the R and the L unit), p. 140 (WTW: M800–M839 synchronize left-upper with right-lower and left-lower with right-upper, M840–M849 left-upper with right-upper and left-lower with right-lower) and p. 126-127 (three-path series: the same range M100–M199, participants by a P code, parameter 8103#1; worked example with M100P12, M100P13, M102P23 and M103P123); Nakamura-Tome Programmierhandbuch (Walter Meier, 2019), p. 127 (NTY3: M100–M199 with P12, P13, P23 and P123); Mori Seiki NT/NTX Programmieranleitung NTX1000 SZM (PX-NT_4-K0DEEN), p. 284 and 236 (operation synchronization with M100 to M197 in the HEAD1 and HEAD2 programs, alone in its block; a different number on the other head raises PS0160).
Corrected: dropped "exactly one waiting-M-code range" and "a group range cannot lie outside mark_range"; the control has a second, high-speed range from parameters 8114/8115 that must not overlap the first (B-64490EN-05 p. 455; B-64484EN p. 1038), which strengthens the Recommendation. The German operator's-manual citation is replaced by the English pages.

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

Keep main. A SYNC takes the range of the first group in file order whose channels hold all its participants, and every other SYNC takes mark_range. A group range may lie outside mark_range. Replace the machine-config 5 example with the real WTW pairs: groups of two channels, where the same range may appear in several groups (M800-839 for L-upper/R-lower and L-lower/R-upper, M840-849 for L-upper/R-upper and L-lower/R-lower). Keep the Mori NTX1000 [101,197] narrowing.
Basis: manual
Source: FANUC B-64484EN p. 1033-1038; Parameter B-64490EN-05 p. 455 (8110/8111, 8114/8115); Nakamura ECL-1 p. 125-127, 140 (cnc-manuals).
Differs from the recommendation: no (example corrected)
Confidence: high
Code impact: none (docs example).

#### D330 Assemblies a plugin brings, and a DLL of plugins/ without a plugin class
Question: D106 (answered) gives each plugin a context that shares the Ncx.* assemblies and 'isolates everything else a plugin brings', so a plugin may reference a package. The template has 'no other packages' (code-guidelines 11). Implementation 17 makes every DLL of plugins/ a plugin (P7-01), and ncx plugin build copies 'the DLL' there (P7-02). No document says where the assemblies a plugin brings go. Nor does one say what a DLL among the plugins without a class of the four interfaces is. Case: MyShopRules references a CSV package. Main copies only MyShopRules.dll and its .pdb into plugins/, and the package is not next to them. The plugin then fails with PLG002, or with PLG003 when only a method body uses the package. If the user copies the package into plugins/ by hand, it loads as a plugin of its own and gives the WARNING PLG005. Every run under --strict then exits 1.
Recommendation: Write into implementation 17 and docs/plugins.md: a DLL among the plugins without a plugin class is the WARNING PLG005, as on main. For a plugin whose build output holds no assembly besides its own, build copies the DLL and symbols into plugins/, as on main. For a plugin that brings assemblies, build copies nothing into plugins/. It lists the path of the build output in ncx.toml instead (MyShopRules/bin/ncx/MyShopRules.dll), where the .deps.json and the packages lie and where PluginLoadContext already resolves them. A copy in plugins/ as well would load the plugin a second time without its package: that copy would give a PLG ERROR, and compile would write no NC file (D205). Reason: it is the smallest change for 1.0, whose template brings no package, and nothing is taken for a plugin silently. This needs D238 to keep a list. Alternative: a folder per plugin. build copies its whole output except the Ncx.* assemblies into plugins/<name>/. The loader then loads plugins/<name>/<name>.dll beside the DLLs directly in plugins/, and a DLL that a plugin brings is never taken for a plugin.
Where: Implementation 17 P7-01 (PluginLoader), P7-02 (build); architecture 9 (plugin paragraph); docs/plugins.md; D106, D238. Code: src/Ncx.Plugins/PluginLoader.cs Load (TODO(question) at line 89), Files, PluginLoadContext; src/Ncx.Cli/Commands/PluginBuild.cs CopyIntoPlugins (TODO(question) at line 134), AddLine.

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27: the library does not answer this (searched Cache-wide grep -a -i -r over the text cache for: plug-?in, .dll, assembly/assemblies, dotnet, ".NET". Every hit is PC-side software or a mechanical assembly, none is a managed probing path. ".dll" hits, complete: Fanuc_CNC-Kommunikation_Schulung_DE.pdf (FOCAS2 FWLIBxx.DLL, pages 19-24); Siemens_Sinumerik-840D-sl_Software_Tools_BS.000506-DE-000-00_DE.pdf (alarm 149004 "Missing ComScriptProcessing.dll", page 320); Siemens_Sinumerik840D_Diagnosehandbuch_DE_2005.pdf (alarm 102014, "V24.DLL kann nicht geladen werden"); the Heidenhain TNC 640 and TNC 620 Technische Handbuecher (a simulation DLL setting, JHIOsim.DLL, page 921 in the TNC 640 NC-SW-34059x-11 volume). "Plug-in" hits, complete: Siemens Software Tools (a plug-in of the configuration surface for graphic types, page 57); Unisign_Uniport7000_Service-Anleitung_5189_DE_2011.pdf ("plug-in a USB mouse"); Okuma_Anleitung-Acrobat-Reader-Dokumenten-CD_EN.pdf (an Acrobat Reader plug-in). ".NET" hits of substance: Nakamura-Tome NT-IPS (a ".NET Framework 2.0" requirement of the PC program, page 140) and the Siemens Software Tools WCF interface. "Assembly" is a mechanical assembly throughout (Brother TC installation and maintenance manuals). As NC-side analogues I also searched CUS.DIR, CMA.DIR, Compilezyklen, Compile-Zyklen, Herstellerzyklen and OEM-Zyklen (Siemens 840D/840D sl/ONE/MC, Index, Stama, Burkhardt+Weber MCX 800 HVP, Heidenhain TNC 640 technical manuals): those are NC subprogram/cycle directories and OEM compile cycles on the control, a different mechanism, and settle nothing here). The recommendation above stands for the maintainer. D330 is a question about the .NET host of ncx — where the assemblies a plugin brings are placed so that PluginLoadContext resolves them, and what a DLL in plugins/ without a plugin class is — and no CNC manual in the library describes a managed assembly probing path, a .deps.json or a build output folder. Two near analogues were checked and rejected, so nobody re-searches them. (1) The closest thing the library has to "where do the DLLs a program brings go" is 01_Steuerungen/Fanuc/Allgemein/Schulung/Fanuc_CNC-Kommunikation_Schulung_DE.pdf pages 21 and 24: the FOCAS2 FWLIBxx.DLLs go into Windows\System32 (and 32-bit ones into SysWOW64 on a 64-bit system), and the PC preparation is "Kopie von FWLIBxx.DLL-Dateien ins Zielverzeichnis". That is native Windows DLL placement for a communication library, not a managed assembly probing path and not a folder scanned for plugin classes, so it cannot decide between copying into plugins/ and registering the build-output path. (2) The Siemens CUS.DIR/CMA.DIR/CST.DIR cycle-directory search order (Siemens Arbeitsvorbereitung and High-Level-Language manuals, Stama, Index, Burkhardt+Weber) is the layout the Recommendation's alternative (a folder per plugin) resembles, but it is an NC subprogram search path on the control. Siemens compile cycles (OEM binaries in the NCK) are documented in the library too and are likewise a control-side mechanism.

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

A DLL in plugins/ without a plugin class is WARNING PLG005. When a plugin's build output holds only its own assembly, build copies the DLL and .pdb into plugins/. When the plugin brings assemblies, build copies nothing and adds the build-output path to `[plugins] assemblies` (D238), where PluginLoadContext resolves the .deps.json.
Basis: logical
Source: This is a .NET host question. AssemblyLoadContext/AssemblyDependencyResolver resolves from the .deps.json next to the plugin (https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/tutorials/creating-app-with-plugin-support).
Differs from the recommendation: no
Confidence: high

#### D331 What the plugin commands write on the standard output
Question: Architecture 10 gives the plugin commands the output 'a runnable plugin without knowing dotnet new'. Code-guidelines 11 has ncx plugin check 'list the interfaces it implements', and implementation 17 (risks) has it report the version it was built against. It ends with one line per implemented interface in the order of architecture 9 ('  IProgramRewriter: 1 class'). new names every file it writes, one per line. build names the DLL in plugins/ and the plugin line of ncx.toml. test passes on what dotnet test writes. Diagnostics go to the standard error in the form of D98 (implementation 10, P0-06).
Recommendation: Keep main. Add one sentence to architecture 10's plugin row; docs/plugins.md already shows the forms. Reasons: it is exactly the content the documents ask for, one item per line, which a user reads and a script can take apart. It also tells the user what new and build changed in the working directory. Alternative: new and build write nothing on success, and only check and test write to the standard output.
Where: Architecture 10 (plugin row); code-guidelines 11; implementation 17 P7-02; docs/plugins.md. Code: src/Ncx.Cli/Commands/PluginCheck.cs Listing (TODO(question) at line 71), PluginNew.cs, PluginBuild.cs Run and AddLine.

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27: the library does not answer this (searched Cache-wide grep -a -i -r for Kommandozeile, Befehlszeile, Eingabeaufforderung, Standardausgabe, Konsolenfenster, "command line", "command prompt", "standard output", "console window", plug-in, dotnet, .dll. "standard output" and "console window" have no hits at all. "Kommandozeile" is in eight files: the Heidenhain TNCremoNT manuals (DE 1998 and EN 2002), the Heidenhain TNC 640 Technische Handbuecher and Bedienhandbuch, Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl_Geraetehandbuch-Bedienkomponenten-Vernetzung_DE_2013.pdf and Siemens_Sinumerik-840C_Programmieranleitung_DE_2001.pdf; apart from TNCremoNT these are the control's own service/commissioning shell. "Standardausgabe" has exactly one hit, in Fanuc_PMC_Programmierhandbuch-Kontaktplansprache_B-61863GE-14_DE.pdf page 1439 (not in the connector; the English edition Fanuc_PMC_Ladder-Language-Programming-Manual_B-61863E-14_EN.pdf has the same note on page 1439), and it is the compound "Standardausgabeformat ist 0 (:BINARY)" — the default output format for writing a PMC ladder to a memory card, not a console stream. The two post-processor documents that describe an output format (Hermle Postprozessor-Heidenhain, Grob G750T Postprozessorbeschreibung, and the further Grob, WFL, Mori Seiki and Reiden post documents) state requirements on the NC output a post must produce, never on what such a program prints to a console). The recommendation above stands for the maintainer. D331 asks what ncx plugin new, build, check and test write on the standard output of a PC command line, which no controller or machine-builder manual can say. The one PC command-line tool whose console output the library does document, HEIDENHAIN TNCcmd, prints in the same shape as the Recommendation — a banner line, then one result per line — so nothing in the manuals contradicts it. That is 01_Steuerungen/Heidenhain/Allgemein/Software_Tools/Heidenhain_TNCremoNT_Software-Tools_EN_2002.pdf page 36 (not in the connector; the DE 1998 edition has the same section, Heidenhain_TNCremoNT_Software-Tools_DE_1998.pdf page 34): two worked transcripts of what TNCcmd, a "WIN32 command line client", writes — a version banner, a connecting line, a connection-established line, then one line per result (NC model, NC software version, file names, transmission rate), confirmed in the PDF itself. It is a file-transfer client, not a build or check command, so it cannot fix the text of ncx plugin check; I report it as the nearest analogue, and its form is consistent with the Recommendation rather than against it. The earlier claim that nothing in 01_Steuerungen, 02_Maschinenhersteller or 06_Eigene_Notizen_Projekte describes the console output of a PC-side tool was wrong on this point.

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

Add one sentence to architecture 10's plugin row.
Basis: logical
Source: One item per line is readable by users and scripts. The manuals are silent.
Differs from the recommendation: no

#### D332 Which plugin ncx plugin build and test take without a folder
Question: Architecture 10 gives 'build [<folder>]' and 'test [<folder>]'. Code-guidelines 11's six steps run 'ncx plugin new MyShopRules' and then 'ncx plugin build' without naming the plugin, and P7-02 has new copy the template into ./<name>/. No document says which project is taken without a folder in two cases: when the working directory is itself a plugin folder, and when it holds several plugins that new made. Main (PluginFolder.Find) takes the one project file of the working directory, or else the one subfolder <name>/ that holds <name>.csproj. Several plugins, or none, are exit 2 (CLI553), and the message names the plugins found. In the first case, build writes plugins/ and ncx.toml into the plugin's own folder.
Recommendation: Keep main, and add one sentence to architecture 10's plugin row. Reasons: the six steps work as written, and test runs naturally inside the plugin's folder. With two plugins 'the plugin' has no single meaning, so the command asks instead of guessing (a usage error, D97). Alternative: without a folder, build and test take only the plugin that new made in a subfolder, never the working directory itself. build then always puts plugins/ and ncx.toml beside the NC programs, where compile looks for them.

The Suchpfad and CALLPATH hits are the control's subprogram search path: in Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl-828D_Programmierhandbuch-Grundlagen_DE_2013.pdf "Suchpfad" occurs once, page 411, as the CALLPATH entry of the command list, while the CUS/CMA/CST cycle directories are in the Arbeitsvorbereitung manuals, the High-Level-Language training document, Sinumerik MC and ONE, and the Stama, Index and Burkhardt+Weber books. D332 asks which project ncx plugin build and test take when no folder is named — the working directory itself, or the one subfolder ncx plugin new made — which is a question about the tool's working directory on a PC, not about any control. One near analogue was checked and rejected: Heidenhain_TNCremoNT_Software-Tools_EN_2002.pdf (not in the connector; the same passages are in Heidenhain_TNCremoNT_Software-Tools_DE_1998.pdf, pages 17-18 and 5) documents a working directory for a PC program — page 20 ("the local working directory during program start", the default being My Documents, changeable through the shortcut) and page 7 (the -W<work folder> command-line parameter). #### D333 Replacing frame instructions against a CYCLE800 swivel
Question: siemens 4 says a replacing instruction (TRANS, ROT, SCALE, MIRROR) deletes all earlier programmable-frame instructions, and CYCLE800 is not one of them. Language 4.2 (frame chain), controller-mapping 1 (SHIFT row) and siemens 11 rule 4 cut the NCX chain at its first entry, which also removes a CYCLE800 tilt. Controller-mapping 1 (TILT row) says the compiler keeps a shift before or after the tilt in program order. So the documents answer in two ways whether CYCLE800(...) followed by TRANS X10 keeps the swivel. None says whether a TRANS written before CYCLE800 acts before the rotation. Main: the reader keeps such a TRANS RAW (SiemensChain.TryCut). The compiler assumes the swivel survives. After ROTATE=RESET on the chain TILT, SHIFT, ROTATE, it writes TRANS X.. without writing CYCLE800 again (SiemensFrames.WriteRemoved). It writes ORIGIN=1, SHIFT X=10, TILT B=30 as TRANS X10 and then CYCLE800(...) (checked on main with dmg-ctx-840d). The answer to B1 (D31) calls that order the most common one.
Recommendation: Confirm in the 840D sl manual which frame CYCLE800 writes (a system frame such as $P_TOOLFRAME or $P_WPFRAME, or $P_PFRAME), and where that frame stands in the frame chain. If the swivel is not part of the programmable frame, TRANS, ROT, MIRROR and SCALE cut only the programmable entries. The reader then writes their RESETs where all of them stand after the last CYCLE800 tilt, and keeps the block RAW otherwise, as now. The compiler stays, and language 4.2 says 'the programmable frame' for Siemens. The programmable frame may instead act after the swivel whatever the program order. Then the last clause of controller-mapping 1 (TILT row) does not hold for Siemens: a SHIFT before a tilt is written through _X0 _Y0 _Z0 of CYCLE800 ({x} {y} {z} of TILT_ON, now always 0), not through TRANS. If TRANS does delete the swivel, the reader cuts the whole chain as language 4.2 says. The compiler then writes the tilts again after every TRANS, ROT or MIRROR it writes while a tilt stays. Keep main until the fact is confirmed. The Fanuc and Heidenhain counterparts are D244 and D253.
Where: siemens.md 4, 11 rule 4, 12 rule 4; language 4.2 (frame chain paragraph); controller-mapping 1 (SHIFT, TILT rows); D31 (B1 answer); D244, D253 (counterparts); src/Ncx.Readers/Siemens/SiemensChain.cs TryCut (TODO line 150); src/Ncx.Compilers/Siemens/SiemensFrames.cs WriteRemoved, WriteEntry, WriteTilt.

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, not confirmed by the maintainer: The manual settles both halves, and the second one is a defect on main. CYCLE800 stores the swivel in the system frames (Werkzeugbezug TOOLFRAME, Werkzeugträger PARTFRAME, Werkstückbezug WPFRAME) and "es werden im Schwenkzyklus keine programmierbaren Frames benutzt", so a TRANS, ROT, SCALE or MIRROR after a swivel replaces only the programmable frame and the tilt survives: language 4.2 may say "the programmable frame" for Siemens, the reader may write the RESETs where all of them stand after the last CYCLE800, and the compiler's assumption is right there. The other direction is not: swivelling to a new plane (_ST ones digit 0) deletes the previous swivel frames and the programmed frames, so the TRANS X10 the compiler writes before CYCLE800(...) for ORIGIN=1, SHIFT X=10, TILT B=30 is wiped out on the machine. A shift before a tilt must go into _X0/_Y0/_Z0, the "Bezugspunkt vor der Drehung", or the tilt must be written additive (_ST ones digit 1), where programmable frames active between two swivel cycles are taken into account. The last clause of the controller-mapping 1 TILT row does not hold for Siemens.
Evidence: Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl-828D_Bedienhandbuch-Fraesen_DE_2013.pdf, p. 481 (Section 3.16, "Voraussetzungen vor Aufruf des Schwenkzyklus": before the first swivel call a tool with edge D>0 and the zero offset must be programmed; the cycle recalculates that offset for the machining plane and stores the translational and rotational parts in the system frames Werkzeugbezug (TOOLFRAME), Werkzeugträger (PARTFRAME) and Werkstückbezug (WPFRAME). Then, verbatim: "Es werden im Schwenkzyklus keine programmierbaren Frames benutzt. Die vom Anwender programmierten Frames werden beim additiven Schwenken berücksichtigt. Beim Schwenken auf eine neue Schwenkebene werden die programmierbaren Frames gelöscht (TRANS)."); Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl-828D_Bedienhandbuch-Fraesen_DE_2013.pdf, p. 483 ("Schwenkebene _ST": with "neu", previous swivel frames and programmed frames are deleted and the values entered form the new swivel frame, and every main program should begin with a swivel cycle with plane "neu"; with "additiv" the swivel frame builds on that of the last swivel cycle, and programmable frames active between two swivel cycles (for example AROT, ATRANS) are taken into account in the swivel frame. Verified verbatim.); Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl-828D_Programmierhandbuch-Arbeitsvorbereitung_DE_2013.pdf, 18.1.38, p. 712-713 (Section 3.16.3, parameter list of CYCLE800(_FR,_TC,_ST,_MODE,_X0,_Y0,_Z0,_A,_B,_C,_X1,_Y1,_Z1,_DIR,_FR_I). _ST EINERSTELLE: 0 = neu, 1 = additiv (tens digit = tool tip tracking, hundreds = tool alignment), which is the coding behind the "ones digit" reading; _X0, _Y0, _Z0 = "Bezugspunkt vor der Drehung" and _X1, _Y1, _Z1 = "Nullpunkt nach der Drehung" — the cycle's own place for a shift that has to act before or after the tilt. (The answer under review cited "226-227"; _ST stands on 225 and page 227 carries only the retract modes.)); Siemens_Sinumerik-840D_Programmierhandbuch-Zyklen_DE_2008.pdf, p. 221 (not in the connector) (Deselecting the swivel data set and clearing the swivel frames WPFRAME, PARTFRAME and TOOLFRAME is done by programming CYCLE800() with no arguments; swivelling to the setter's basic position of the kinematics (...,0,0,0,...) aligns the WKS and produces rotations in the swivel frame $P_WPFRAME. Verified verbatim; page 222 is only an input-mask example and is dropped from the citation.); Siemens_Sinumerik840D_Programmierhandbuch-Zyklen_DE_2006.pdf, p. 208 and 212 (printed 3-110 and 3-114) (not in the connector) (The previous edition carries both sentences unchanged — no programmable frames are used in the swivel cycle, and with swivel plane "neu" the previous swivel frames and the programmed frames are deleted — so the rule is not an artefact of one edition. Note that in this manual the printed page numbers are chapter-relative and differ from the PDF pages.). (Citations re-paged to the cnc-manuals connector 2026-10-26.)

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

CYCLE800 writes system frames, not the programmable frame. Reader: TRANS, ROT, SCALE, MIRROR cut only the programmable entries (SHIFT, ROTATE, SCALE, MIRROR) and the tilt survives; the reader writes their RESETs where all of them stand after the last CYCLE800 tilt and keeps the block RAW otherwise (as now). A CYCLE800 with _ST ones digit 0 (new) resets earlier tilts and all programmable entries before its TILT; _X0/_Y0/_Z0 read as a SHIFT before the TILT, _X1/_Y1/_Z1 as a SHIFT after it; ones digit 1 (additive) appends. Compiler: a SHIFT before a tilt is written into _X0/_Y0/_Z0 of CYCLE800 (not as TRANS before it); a SHIFT after the tilt as TRANS after CYCLE800 (survives); ROTATE=RESET etc. after a tilt writes TRANS/ROT without repeating CYCLE800 (as now). A ROTATE, MIRROR or SCALE before a tilt is a compile ERROR (next free CMP code) until a rule for additive swivels is drafted. Language 4.2 says "the programmable frame" for Siemens; the last clause of controller-mapping 1 TILT row is marked "not Siemens".
Basis: manual
Source: Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl-828D_Bedienhandbuch-Fraesen_DE_2013.pdf p. 481, 483 ("keine programmierbaren Frames"; "neu" deletes programmed frames); Siemens_Sinumerik-840Dsl-828D_Programmierhandbuch-Arbeitsvorbereitung_DE_2013.pdf p. 712-713 (_ST, _X0 before rotation, _X1 after). Web: https://Manualslib.com/manual/1327112/Siemens-Sinumerik-840d-Sl.html?page=547 (same "new" swivel-plane text).
Differs from the recommendation: yes: it picks the "swivel is not programmable frame" branch and fixes the compiler's TRANS-before-CYCLE800 output, which the recommendation would have kept.
Confidence: high
Code impact: SiemensFrames.WriteEntry/WriteTilt (shift before tilt into _X0.._Z0, new CMP error); SiemensChain.TryCut (CYCLE800 _ST handling).

#### D338 A formula where Klartext takes a number
Question: Heidenhain 6 says 'Expressions may stand wherever a number stands (L X+Q1 Y-Q2)', but it shows only a signed Q parameter and gives formulas only in the assignment Q1 = Q2 + 3 * SIN Q3. HeidenhainNumbers.SignedValue writes a number or a signed Q parameter and reports anything else as CMP102. So LINE X={$Q1 + 5} F=100, the NCX form of Fanuc X[#1+5.] or Siemens X=R1+5, does not compile for Heidenhain. Nor does a formula in either value of FN 9 to FN 12 (HeidenhainFlow.Condition), or a SETPOS with a formula value (HeidenhainSetpos, which points to this marker). Today heidenhain 6 promises more than the compiler writes.
Recommendation: Confirm from the iTNC 530 manual. Our reading, which is not in the documents: an NC block takes a number or a Q, QL or QR parameter with its sign, never a formula. If this is confirmed, heidenhain 6 reads 'a Q parameter may stand wherever a number stands'. The compiler then writes each formula of a block into a QL parameter, in a block of its own directly before it (QL499 = Q1 + 5, then L X+QL499), using the highest QL numbers that no word of the file names. QL is local to the program (heidenhain 6), so no called program sees it. Heidenhain 8 gets the rule. If the control does take a formula in parentheses, the compiler writes it there instead. Alternative: keep CMP102 in 1.0, as coded, correct heidenhain 6, and add that sentence to heidenhain 8.
Where: heidenhain.md 6 and 8. Code: src/Ncx.Compilers/Heidenhain/HeidenhainNumbers.cs SignedValue (TODO(question) at line 44), HeidenhainFlow.cs Condition, HeidenhainSetpos.cs (the pointer at line 213), HeidenhainFormula.cs.

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, corrected 2026-10-26 after the manual audit, not confirmed by the maintainer: the manuals do not settle this. The manuals document the positive rule but never state the prohibition, so the ERROR stays an NCX decision on documented ground. What they say: instead of a numeric value you put a Q parameter into the machining program ("FN 0: Q10=25", then "L X +Q10", which equals L X +25); FN 0 to FN 5 take exactly two operands to the right of the "="; and every FORMEL example assigns to a Q parameter, never to a coordinate word. No page says a formula in an NC word is rejected, and no counterexample was found in any Heidenhain volume, so heidenhain 6 can read "a Q parameter may stand wherever a number stands", and the compiler can spill each formula into a QL parameter in a block of its own, as the recommendation says. QL is available earlier than the first answer said: the iTNC 530 Klartext manual for NC software 340490-05 (2008) already lists QL0 to QL499, local to one program, and QR0 to QR499, as do the 606420 manuals and the TNC 640. Only the oldest level differs: the DIN/ISO manual for 340490-04 (2007) lists Q0 to Q1999 and QS without QL, and the Klartext manual for 340490-04 cannot be read in the connector, so on that level the spill parameter may have to be a Q. The proposal agrees with the recommendation.
Evidence: HEIDENHAIN iTNC 530 Benutzer-Handbuch Klartext-Dialog (NC-SW 340490-05, 2008), p. 282-283 (9.1 range table: Q0 to Q1999 by use, QL0 to QL499 local within one program, QR0 to QR499 remanent.); same manual, p. 286 (9.2 part families: FN 0 assigns a value to a Q parameter, which then stands in the program instead of the number; example "15 FN 0: Q10=25", "25 L X +Q10", equal to L X +25.); same manual, p. 287 (FN 0 to FN 5 are assignments to a Q parameter; to the right of the "=" two numbers, two Q parameters, or a number and a Q parameter, freely signed.); same manual, p. 316-317 (9.9 entering a formula directly: every example has the form Qn = ...); HEIDENHAIN iTNC 530 Benutzer-Handbuch Klartext-Dialog (NC-SW 606420-01, 2010), p. 289-291 (the same range table with QL and QR) and p. 294 (the FN 0 example); HEIDENHAIN iTNC 530 Benutzer-Handbuch DIN/ISO (NC-SW 340490-04, 2007), p. 529-531 (11.1 range table: Q0 to Q1999 and QS, no QL or QR.); Benutzerhandbuch Klartextprogrammierung (TNC 640), p. 266 (QL 0 to 499 local to one NC program, QR remanent, Q global.); HEIDENHAIN iTNC 530 Benutzer-Handbuch Klartext-Dialog (NC-SW 340490-04, 2007), p. 603-604 and 635-636 (cited by the earlier answer; listed in the connector, but its text cannot be read there).
Corrected: Dropped "QL exists only from 606420; the 340490 manual knows no QL", because Klartext 340490-05 p. 283 lists QL0 to QL499 and QR0 to QR499. The claim holds at most for 340490-04, whose DIN/ISO manual has no QL; the evidence now cites the readable 340490-05 manual instead of the unreadable 340490-04 Klartext manual.

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

heidenhain 6 reads 'a Q parameter may stand wherever a number stands'. The Heidenhain compiler spills each formula of a block into a QL parameter, in a block of its own directly before it (`QL499 = Q1 + 5`, then `L X+QL499`). It uses the highest QL numbers no word of the file names. This applies to motion words, FN 9-12 operands and SETPOS values. CMP102 then remains only where no QL is free. heidenhain 8 gets the rule.
Basis: manual + web
Source: iTNC 530 Klartext 340490-05 p. 282-287, 316-317; TNC 640 p. 266 (QL0-QL499 local) (cnc-manuals). The documented form is a number or a signed Q. A forum post claims `L X (Q1+10)` works (https://en.cncarena.com/heidenhain/forum/thread/8336-parameter-programm/), but no manual confirms it, so it is not relied on.
Differs from the recommendation: no
Confidence: medium
Code impact: HeidenhainNumbers.SignedValue, HeidenhainFlow.Condition and HeidenhainSetpos emit the QL spill.

#### D339 M codes per Fanuc block
Question: Fanuc 1 allows 'up to three M codes per block on 30i (one on older controls)' but does not name the older controls. The dialect of machine-config 1 is free text (30i, 31i-B, 18i-TB and 0i-TD in the machine files). Main writes up to three M codes per block whatever the dialect and moves any further codes into following lines. On a control that takes only one, a block such as SPINDLE=CW COOLANT=ON, written S1000 M3 M8, raises an alarm.
Recommendation: The maintainer confirms this in the Fanuc manuals. Our reading, which is not in the documents: up to three M codes per block is the parameter M3B (No. 3404#7), on the 0i, 16i/18i/21i and 30i series alike. If that is confirmed, add a [format] key m_codes_per_block (1 to 3; 1 when left out, which every control accepts). Fanuc 1 then reads 'up to three M codes per block where the control's parameter allows it (m_codes_per_block), otherwise one'. fanuc-mill-30i.toml sets 3, and the compiler keeps moving the codes beyond the limit into following lines. If the manual instead ties the limit to the series, the compiler takes 3 for 30i/31i/32i and 1 for the others, by dialect and with no key.
Where: fanuc 1; machine-config 2; the Fanuc machine files; src/Ncx.Compilers/Fanuc/FanucFunctions.cs:16 MostMCodes and Add.

ANSWER:
Proposed from the manual library 2026-09-27, not confirmed by the maintainer: The reading is confirmed, but a count alone is not enough. Parameter No. 3404#7 (M3B) sets the number of M codes per block — 0 = one, 1 = up to three — and the same bit with the same wording appears in the 0i-D, the 16i/18i-TB, the 21i-B and the 30i-B manuals; on the 30i-B parameter 11630#5 (M5B) raises it further to five. But the same pages forbid combinations outright: M00, M01, M02, M30, M98, M99 and M198 may never share a block with another M code, nor may an M code that makes the CNC do internal work (the macro-call codes for programs 9001–9009, codes that suppress look-ahead buffering), and a waiting M code must stand in a block of its own — or at least before all the others if it shares one. Builders narrow it further: on the Mori NTX1000 only a listed set of codes may be the second and third M code of a block (M08 is not on that list) and a spindle or tool-spindle rotation code M03/M04/M13/M14 may not share a block with a listed code at all, so the draft's own example S1000 M3 M8 is disallowed there on both counts although three M codes are allowed; the Doosan Puma expressly allows M03 with other codes but not M03 with M04/M05, not M19 with M03/M04/M05/M29/M35, and not the macro-driven codes with anything. So m_codes_per_block needs a companion list of codes that must stand alone (default: the Fanuc seven plus the wait marks), and the compiler must not merge a spindle start with another M code where the builder forbids it.
Evidence: Fanuc_30i-B_Bedienung-Drehen-Fraesen_B-64484EN_EN.pdf, p. 297–298 (§11.1, §11.2) (Normally only one M code per block; depending on bit 7 (M3B) of parameter Nr. 3404 up to three may be programmed, output to the machine at once, which shortens cycle time. Not all M codes may be combined for mechanical reasons — the builder's manual decides. M00, M01, M02, M30, M98, M99 or M198 may not be used together with another M code, and further codes that make the CNC do internal work (calls of programs 9001 to 9009, codes that suppress look-ahead buffering) must each stand in a block of their own. §11.1 adds that the machine processes all M codes except M98, M99, M198 and the subprogram/macro call codes of parameters 6071–6079 and 6080–6089); Fanuc_30i-B_Parameterhandbuch_B-64490EN-05_EN.pdf, p. 194 and 651 (printed p. 182 and 639) (Page 194: parameter 3404 bit 7 M3B, "The number of M codes that can be specified in one block", 0 = One, 1 = Up to three. Page 651: parameter 11630 bit 5 M5B, same subject, 0 = One (up to three when bit 7 (M3B) of parameter No. 3404 is set to 1), 1 = Up to five); Fanuc_0i-D_Bedienung-Drehen-Fraesen_B-64304EN_EN.pdf, p. 169 (§11.2) (The identical rule for the 0i-D: one M code per block normally, up to three when bit 7 (M3B) of parameter Nr. 3404 is 1, the same list of codes that may not be combined (M00, M01, M02, M30, M98, M99, M198), the same exclusion of codes that trigger internal CNC operations, and the same pointer to the builder's manual for the mechanical limits); Fanuc_16-18-TB_Bedienerhandbuch_B-63524EN-01_EN.pdf, p. 161 (ch. 11.2) (Same text for the 16i/18i-TB lathe control: up to three M codes per block when bit 7 (M3B) of parameter Nr. 3404 is 1, with M00, M01, M02, M30, M98, M99 and M198 excluded and the internally-processed codes each in their own block); Fanuc_21i-B_Parameterhandbuch_B-63610EN-01_EN.pdf, p. 151-153 (Parameter 3404 bit 7 M3B on the 21i-B: "The number of M codes that can be specified in one block", 0 = One, 1 = Up to three — the same bit as on the 0i-D, 16i/18i and 30i-B, so the limit is a parameter across the series, not a series property); Fanuc_30i-B_Bedienung-Drehen-Fraesen_B-64484EN_EN.pdf, p. 1037 (§23.2, CAUTION) (A waiting M code must be specified in a block of its own; unlike other M codes it is not output to the PMC; and in a block that does contain several M codes the waiting M code must stand before all the others); Mori-Seiki_NT-NTX-Serie_Programmierung_Programmieranleitung-NTX1000SZM_PX-NT_4-K0DEEN_2011.pdf, p. 252–253 (§1-2 Funktion für mehrere M-Codes) (Up to three M codes in a block, and only the listed codes may serve as multiple-M-code function codes: M10/M11, M210/M211 (chuck clamp/unclamp both spindles), M19/M219 (orientation), M25/M26 (tailstock), M85/M86 (door), M37/M38 (ceiling shutter), M340–M345 (steady rests), M2000–M2020 (multi counter), M2040–M2047 (through-spindle coolant pressure). M08 is not among them. Although the first of two or three codes may be something else, the second and third must be from that list, and a spindle or tool-spindle rotation code (M03, M04, M13, M14) must not be specified in the same block as a multiple-M-code function code); Doosan_PUMA-Baureihe_Bedienungshandbuch_DE_2020.pdf, p. 272 (§1.5 Multi-M-Code-Funktion, printed p. 260; not in the connector: no readable text on that page); alarm list p. 383 (Up to three M codes per block, standard on the machine, with examples that do combine M03 with other codes ("M03 S100 P11 T0101 M169 M260 G00 Z100."). The cautions: M00, M01, M02 and M30 always alone; M03, M04 and M05 not together; M19 not with M03, M04, M05, M29 or M35; macro-driven codes alone, with a named list (M28, M146, M147, M89, M90, M189, M190, M513, M200, M201). The alarm list on p. 383 carries 2399 "ILLEGAL MULTI M CODE"). (Citations re-paged to the cnc-manuals connector 2026-10-26.)

Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

Add [format] keys `m_codes_per_block` (1 to 5; default 1, which every control accepts; 3 needs parameter 3404#7 M3B, 5 needs 11630#5 M5B on 30i-B) and `m_codes_combinable` (optional list; when set, only those codes may be the second and later M code of a block). Regardless of the keys the compiler writes M00, M01, M02, M30, M98, M99, M198, the [sync] wait range and the configured macro-call M codes each in a block of its own, and never puts a spindle code (M3/M4/M5 and the configured spindle codes) in one block with another M code unless m_codes_combinable lists that other code. Generic fanuc machine files keep the default 1; a machine file sets more only from its builder's documentation (Mori NTX1000: 3 with its listed combinable codes). Codes beyond the limit move to following lines, as now.
Basis: manual
Source: Fanuc_30i-B_Bedienung-Drehen-Fraesen_B-64484EN_EN.pdf p. 297-298, 1037; Fanuc_30i-B_Parameterhandbuch_B-64490EN-05_EN.pdf p. 194, 651; Fanuc_0i-D B-64304EN p. 169; Fanuc_21i-B_Parameterhandbuch p. 151-153; Mori NTX1000SZM p. 252-253. Web: Autodesk Fanuc post https://cam.autodesk.com/posts/post.php?name=fanuc writes S..M3 alone and coolant in separate blocks by default (singleLineCoolant: false).
Differs from the recommendation: yes: default 1 also for the generic 30i file (the recommendation set 3), range up to 5, plus the must-stand-alone rule and the combinable list.
Confidence: high
Code impact: FanucFunctions MostMCodes/Add (limit from config, alone-list, spindle rule); [format] schema; Fanuc machine files.

Tenth round, asked 2026-10-01: twenty-five questions found while answering the twelve requests of opencam, the first client of NCXchange, for its release 1 (the request list is `/Users/peterburgener/project_spike/plans/2026-10-01-ncxchange-requests-release1.md`, whose own numbering R1-01 to R1-12 is theirs); the CAM writes one NCX file for every controller, so the controller- and machine-specific part of each request is asked of NCXchange. The entries stand in number order, which is the order of the requests: D347 and D348 for R1-01, D349 and D350 for R1-02, D351 and D352 for R1-03, D353 and D354 for R1-04, D355 and D356 for R1-05, D357 and D358 for R1-06, D359 to D361 for R1-07, D362 for R1-08, D363 to D366 for R1-09, D367 and D368 for R1-10, D369 and D370 for R1-11, and D371 for R1-12, so that the pairs a request asks together stand together and a draft that cites the preceding or the companion one means its neighbour. Four of the twelve requests wait in part on the maintainer's confirmation of a draft that already carries a proposed answer from the manual library: R1-05 and the Siemens `CYCLE_F` of R1-08 on D181, the tolerance half of R1-08 on D151 (its helix half, D268, was settled 2026-10-01), the catalog half of R1-06 on D164, and the first point of R1-09 on D121; R1-07 needs no new rule for the tap itself, which the settled D194 and D256 give, and its three entries are the remainders those answers left. Seven entries are needed before the CAM's NCX writer is built (D347, D349, D350, D355, D362, D363 and D369), sixteen before release 1 ships, and two can wait (D360 and D368). None of the twenty-five is implemented and none has a row in `decisions.md`: they are drafts for the maintainer to answer, and each `Where` names the sections, the data and the code an answer would change. `../implementation/03-open-questions.md` (section "CAM release 1 requests") maps every entry to the task it belongs to and to the request it comes from. One thing to hand out in the answers: several entries each take "the next free" diagnostic code for a rule of their own, so CMP012 (D351, D367), CMP030 (D364, D370), CMP120 (D349, D358, D362), CMP574 (D356, D362) and CFG009 (D348, D357) are each claimed more than once, and the codes have to be allotted where more than one of them is answered yes.

### Tenth round: the release-1 requests of opencam

#### D347 What `ncx --version` prints, and where the number comes from
Question: R1-01 of the opencam request list asks for a version tag the CAM can pin and for `ncx --version` to print it. The tag itself and the binaries CI builds from it are P7-03's scope (17-phase-7, P7-03: binaries "published by CI on a `v*` tag", `tag v1.0.0 on main`), so they need the task, not a decision; and the option is not missing either, because `RootCommand` of System.CommandLine 2.0.12 brings `--version` and `--help` with it (`ncx --help` on main lists both). What no document says is what the line holds. No project and neither `Directory.Build.props` nor `Directory.Packages.props` sets `Version`, so the number is the MSBuild default with the commit the SDK appends to the informational version: main prints `1.0.0+f74559c04a8c548d55d45c9bea04f48118e009e3` (checked 2026-10-01). A build from a tag `v0.1.0` would print the same, so the first half of R1-01's test, "a build from the tag reports the tag", fails whatever tag is pushed. Architecture 10, which F28 made "the one list of the commands and options of `ncx`", lists neither option: its table gives the eight commands and the paragraph after it gives `--strict`, `--machine`, `--skip-blocks`, `--expand-cycles` and `--job`. D74 names only the eight commands. So the two options are a fresh case of the drift F28 closed. D97 gives exit codes for runs that read a file and says nothing about a command line that prints a version and runs nothing (`--version` exits 0 today, checked). The packed tool shows the same gap from the other side: it is `Ncx.Cli` 1.0.0 with authors "Ncx.Cli" and description "Package Description" (`src/Ncx.Cli/obj/Debug/Ncx.Cli.1.0.0.nuspec`, every field an SDK default; the file is a build artifact of an earlier commit, so only the id, authors and description fields are evidence of today's state, and they follow from the csproj, which sets `PackAsTool` and `ToolCommandName` and no package metadata at all), while P7-03 writes `dotnet tool install --global NCXchange.Cli`.
Recommendation: One number, stamped at build from the tag, printed by the option that already exists. `Directory.Build.props` gets `<Version>` holding the version of the next release — the one place that number stands in the repository, next to the single `TargetFramework` it already holds — and the release job passes `-p:Version=${tag#v}`, so a build from `v1.0.0-alpha.1` prints `1.0.0-alpha.1` and the same number goes on the package and on the self-contained binaries; nothing else sets it. Keep System.CommandLine's built-in option instead of writing one: it adds no CLI surface, and it already behaves as D97 needs — it prints, runs nothing and exits 0, with no diagnostic. Say that in the exit-code paragraph of architecture 10, which is the normative text; the settled D97 row is not rewritten for it, and gains the sentence only if the maintainer wants it there, as D165's Where offers for D75. Keep the commit the SDK appends to the informational version, so that a build between two tags cannot claim to be the release and the maintainer can tell a local build from a shipped one; the CAM's CI job asserts the part before `+`, which is exactly the tag. The real alternative is `<IncludeSourceRevisionInInformationalVersion>false</IncludeSourceRevisionInInformationalVersion>`: the line is then the tag and nothing else, the CAM's assertion is a string equality, and the commit lives only in the release notes and in `ncx plugin check`, which 17-phase-7 already has reporting the version a plugin was built against from 1.0 on. Either way `--version` and `--help` go into the architecture 10 table in the same commit (F28), and the package metadata of `Ncx.Cli.csproj` is filled from the same `Version` with the id P7-03 promises, the MIT license of D75 and the repository url (`https://github.com/NC-PB/NCXchange_`), so that the install command in the release notes is true; the `Authors` field is the copyright-holder question of the open draft D165 and is answered there, not twice. This needs no NCX word and no diagnostic code: it is the CLI and the build, not language 4.
Where: architecture 10 (the CLI table and the exit-code paragraph after it: `--version` and `--help`, and that a version or help run prints and exits 0 without a diagnostic, F28); D74 (the root command's two built-in options beside the eight commands); D97 (optionally the row, as D165 offers for D75); D165 (the holder name the package `Authors` takes); `Directory.Build.props` (`<Version>`); `src/Ncx.Cli/Ncx.Cli.csproj` (`PackageId`, `Authors`, `Description`, `PackageLicenseExpression`, `RepositoryUrl`); `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (the publish job, the artifacts, the macOS runner and `contents: write` it lacks today; its `on: push` already fires on a tag); `docs/implementation/17-phase-7-plugins-release.md` P7-03 and `docs/plan/tasks/inbox/P7-03-release-1-0.md` (the version line among the release steps); `docs/implementation/20-schedule.md` 1 (task 35) and 5 (a new row: section 5 has no release ask today — its rows are the remote and CI provider, the decision batches, the corpus and the measured cycle time); tests: `tests/Ncx.Acceptance/Cli/` (a run with `--version` prints the assembly's informational version and exits 0) and the CI release step that asserts the published binary reports the tag.

ANSWER: (Peter, 2026-10-07, drafted by Claude in project_spike) Accept as recommended: one `<Version>` in Directory.Build.props, stamped from the tag by the release job, printed by the built-in `--version`. Keep the commit after `+`; the CAM's CI asserts the part before `+`.

#### D348 The schema version of a machine file and a cycle catalog
Question: opencam bundles one pinned `ncx` together with its catalogs (R1-01 need, opencam D-031 and D-080), so the two must be able to say whether they belong together. Nothing in the data says which version it was written for. machine-config 1 gives `[machine]` its identity keys and no version; section 6 says four catalog files ship with `ncx` and are "user-extendable"; and no file carries a version key — not the eight `machines/*.toml`, not the five `docs/spec/examples/machines/*.toml`, not the four `cycles/*.toml` (checked 2026-10-01). A program file has one: `FILE=BEGIN NCX=1` is the format version and any other value is `PAR022` (language 4.1, `src/Ncx.Core/Parsing/StructurePass.cs` CheckNcxVersion). The configuration that gives a program its meaning has none, so a file written for a newer `ncx` is not merely unchecked by an older build: every key it does not know is `CFG002`, a WARNING "because the schema is a sketch until the compiler exists" (`src/Ncx.Config/DiagnosticCodes.Loading.cs`), which under `--strict` — the mode the CAM runs, R1-09 — sets exit code 1 while naming a key and not a version. Measured: prefixing a root `ncx = 1` to `machines/heidenhain-itnc530.toml` and running `ncx check docs/spec/examples/2.5D_FRAESEN.ncx --machine <that file>` reports `WARNING CFG002: Unknown key ncx; the nearest known table is [sync]` and exits 0, and exits 1 under `--strict`, while the unmodified file exits 0 under `--strict` (2026-10-01). Two further facts shape the answer. The key name `ncx` is not free inside a machine file: every `[[axis]]` and resource table requires `ncx`, "name used in NCX programs" (machine-config 1, `src/Ncx.Config/MachineConfigLoader.Resources.cs` lines 15 and 84), so a root `ncx` would make one file use the name for two different things, and the nearest-key suggestion above shows how it reads. And the other half of R1-01's bundle worry — that a customer folder holding an older `cycles/fanuc.toml` quietly overrides the catalog the CAM pinned, because the project folder wins over the tool's own folder (`src/Ncx.Cli/ProjectFolders.cs`, machine-config 10) — is the open draft D207 and the bundling ask of R1-12, not this question; it is named here only so that it is not answered twice.
Recommendation: Give the two data files the idea the program file already has, and only that. A machine file and a catalog file may carry `ncx_schema = 1` as their first key, the format version of the machine-configuration schema, with exactly the meaning of `NCX=1` in language 4.1: the number of the schema the file is written in, not the release of `ncx` and not the content of the file. The shorter `schema = 1` is free as well and reads cleanly; the bare `ncx` is not, since it already names the NCX name of an axis or a resource. A file without the key is read as version 1, so every file that exists today and every shop's own file keeps working. A file whose version this build does not read is an ERROR under the new code `CFG009`, naming the file and the version: it is the next free code of the CFG loading range CFG001 to CFG099 (CFG001 to CFG008 are taken), from which the catalog loader already draws its generic file codes (`src/Ncx.Config/Cycles/DiagnosticCodes.Cycles.cs` cites CFG001 to CFG004), and it is an ERROR for the reason `PAR022` is one — `ncx` cannot guess what the file means. The key goes into the known root keys of both loaders in the same commit (the lists passed to `ConfigTable.WarnUnknownTables`: `MachineConfigLoader.cs` line 57, `Cycles/CycleCatalogLoader.cs` line 53), or the key the rule introduces is itself a `CFG002` WARNING that fails `--strict`. Add it before the first tag is pushed, and for the opposite reason to the one that first suggests itself: an older binary reading a newer file does not read it "without the check", it reports `CFG002` on the key and fails the CAM's `--strict` run, so every release that ships before the key exists is a build that rejects the files of the releases after it. The number changes only when the schema breaks, so it stays 1 through release 1.0, and the key is a one-line addition to the twelve shipped files (eight machine files, four catalogs) plus the five byte-identical copies under `docs/spec/examples/machines/` — seventeen edits, since those are separate files, not links. Keep the release number out of the data: machine-config 6 makes a catalog the shop's to extend, so `ncx` must not call a shop's own file stale. No NCX word is involved: this is machine-config and `Ncx.Config`.
Where: machine-config 1 (the `[machine]` excerpt and the sentence on `ncx_schema = 1`), 6 (the catalog excerpt) and 10 (the layout); `src/Ncx.Config/DiagnosticCodes.Loading.cs` (CFG009 after CFG008) and `src/Ncx.Config/Cycles/DiagnosticCodes.Cycles.cs` (the range comment); `src/Ncx.Config/MachineConfigLoader.cs` (the root key lists and the `WarnUnknownTables` call at line 57), `src/Ncx.Config/MachineConfigLoader.Identity.cs` and `src/Ncx.Config/Cycles/CycleCatalogLoader.cs` (line 53) — read and check the key; `src/Ncx.Config/ConfigTable.cs` `WarnUnknownTables` (line 688, which reports a root scalar as `CFG002` today); D207 and D156, both open, for the folders and names of the catalogs this key travels with; the data: `machines/*.toml` (8), `cycles/*.toml` (4) and `docs/spec/examples/machines/*.toml` (5 identical copies); tests: `tests/Ncx.Config.Tests/MachineConfigLoaderTests.cs` and `tests/Ncx.Config.Tests/Cycles/CycleCatalogLoaderTests.cs` (a file with `ncx_schema = 2` is CFG009, a file without the key loads as version 1, a file with it reports no CFG002), `tests/Ncx.Config.Tests/Cycles/ShippedCatalogsTests.cs` and `tests/Ncx.Config.Tests/ExampleMachinesTests.cs` (every shipped file carries the key).

ANSWER: (Peter, 2026-10-07, drafted by Claude in project_spike) Accept as recommended: `ncx_schema = 1` as an optional first key of machine files and catalogs, absent means 1, an unknown version is the ERROR CFG009. Add it before the first tag.

#### D349 A word for exact stop and continuous path
Question: Language 4 has no word for the control's path-control mode, the modal switch between stopping in every block and carrying the speed through corners. The documents are silent where they are not contradictory: machine-config 4 gives `[dynamics] path_mode = "continuous" | "exact_stop"` as control behaviour for the runtime estimate (D64), a machine setting a program cannot touch; controller-mapping 1 folds the Fanuc pair `G61.1`/`G64` into the `TOLERANCE` row — D85's own question named that pair — although `G64` is a value of modal group 13 and the `[tolerance]` table of `machines/fanuc-mill-30i.toml:141` writes `G5.1 Q1`/`G5.1 Q0`, the AI contour control, so `TOLERANCE=OFF` leaves group 13 untouched; controller-mapping 9 keeps Siemens `G60`, `G601`, `G64` and `G641`..`G645` with `ADIS` as RAW; fanuc.md 3 lists group 13 (`G61 G62 G63 G64`) and siemens.md 2 group 10 (`G60 G64 G641`..`G645`) as groups NCX reads but writes nothing for; heidenhain.md 2 names no modal form at all. `src/Ncx.Readers/Fanuc/FanucBuilder.cs:320` says it outright: "G61, the cutting mode of group 13, has no NCX word". The one way a program can ask for exact stop today is a machine-specific named function, and exactly one shipped file has it (`machines/doosan-puma-2600sy.toml:223`, a lathe: `EXACT_STOP = { ON = "M159", OFF = "M160" }`; the copy under `docs/spec/examples/machines/` is identical); the name and the M codes differ per machine, so a CAM that writes one NCX file for every controller (opencam D-148) cannot use it. Checked on main: a block `PATH_MODE=EXACT` reports `ERROR PAR010` on all three shipped mills, before any compiler runs. Case: a finishing pass whose corners must stay sharp and a clearing pass that must run continuous cannot be told apart in one NCX file. Worse, a Fanuc source that says `G61` reads as `RAW:FANUC` with that reason and is then an ERROR for any other family (controller-mapping 9, D5), so a shop program with `G61` cannot be compiled for the iTNC 530 at all, although every control in the corpus has the mode.
Recommendation: Add `PATH_MODE` to language 4.1, as the row before `TOLERANCE` (where `TOLERANCE` itself stands, and where the catalog defines it, `src/Ncx.Core/Catalog/FileWords.cs:174`), with the three values `EXACT_STOP` (every block ends at standstill), `CONTINUOUS` (the control carries the speed through corners) and `DEFAULT` (back to the machine file's own `path_mode`). Scope modal; its start value is the machine file's `path_mode` (the companion draft), and the `PROGRAM=END` of virtual machine 4, which sets the words of that row "to the defaults", puts that start value back. Rank 785 in bucket 12 of the canonical order of D90, between `ROTARY_FEED` (780) and `TOLERANCE` (790), so that the words which set how the control runs the path stand together and the coarse switch comes before the tolerance it is measured against; the ranks go in tens precisely so a later word fits between two others without renumbering (`src/Ncx.Core/Catalog/CanonicalRanks.cs` header). The value names are `EXACT_STOP` and `CONTINUOUS`, not the request's `EXACT`, so that the word, the machine key `path_mode = "exact_stop"` and `PathMode.ExactStop` of `src/Ncx.Core/Machine/PathMode.cs` are one vocabulary: a word whose value names differ from the key that gives its default is read wrong in every machine-file comment, and "EXACT" alone does not say what is exact. The third value is what opencam D-148 needs: the CAM cannot know a machine's own mode, so without it the CAM can never hand the mode back, only guess the opposite. Its spelling is a genuine choice, because NCX has no word with a `DEFAULT` value today and the house spelling for "back to the control's default" is `OFF` (`TOLERANCE=OFF`, language 4.1); `DEFAULT` is recommended only because `PATH_MODE=OFF` reads as "no path mode at all", which is not a state any control has. The machine side is two keys in the existing `[transform]` table, named as that table names every option, word then value, beside `ROTARY_PATH_SHORTEST`/`ROTARY_PATH_FULL` and `TCPM_ON`/`TCPM_OFF`: `PATH_MODE_EXACT_STOP` and `PATH_MODE_CONTINUOUS`. They are templates, not an enum, because a Siemens shop writes `G60` and either plain `G64` or a smoothing form (`G642`, `G641 ADIS=0.5`) for the same two states. None of the three shipped mills has a `[transform]` table at all today, so each gets one: `machines/fanuc-mill-30i.toml` with `G61` and `G64`, `machines/siemens-840dsl-mill.toml` with `G60` and `G64`, `machines/heidenhain-itnc530.toml` with both keys empty, because Klartext has no modal switch — the iTNC 530's `M90` is blockwise and needs following-error mode selected, and the TNC 640 has dropped it (the evidence of D286's answer); the header comment on line 5 of each of the three files, which today lists `[transform]` among the tables that "have nothing to configure on this machine", is corrected with them. A key left empty or left out follows the `ROTARY_PATH` reading of that table, "empty = WARNING, kept as written" (machine-config 5, D86), not the `TILT_AXIS_ON` reading, where empty means the target needs the kinematics module and is an ERROR (D82, `CMP107`): the WARNING is the one the compilers already have for a state word without a template, `CMP361` on Fanuc (`FanucOptionNotWritten`, `FanucFrames.Option`) and `CMP533` on Siemens (`SiemensOptionNotWritten`), plus a new Heidenhain code of the same meaning in the `CMP1xx` band (`CMP120` is the next free), since `HeidenhainFrames.WriteMode` carries a built-in M code for every option it writes today and there is none here. Nothing is written and the compile goes on, so `PATH_MODE` never turns a program into an ERROR on a machine that cannot express it, and NCXchange reports what the machine cannot do rather than refusing the file. In the output `PATH_MODE` is written after the tolerance words of its block, so that an explicit mode wins over whatever a tolerance form set — deliberately the reverse of the canonical rank, which orders the NCX text and not the target's blocks, as the compilers reorder for the target everywhere else; on a control where one object carries both (Siemens `CYCLE832` touches group 10, Heidenhain cycle 32 is the only lever) the machine file leaves `PATH_MODE` without a template rather than writing that object twice. Readers: Fanuc `G61` becomes `PATH_MODE=EXACT_STOP` and `G64` `PATH_MODE=CONTINUOUS`, while `G62` (corner override) and `G63` (tapping mode) of the same group stay RAW and `G61.1` stays with `TOLERANCE`, which is the split `FanucBuilder.ReasonFor` already draws at line 318; Siemens `G60` and `G64` become the word, while `G641`..`G645` with `ADIS`/`ADISPOS`, the non-modal `G9` of group 11 and `G601`..`G603` of group 12 stay RAW, because no value of `PATH_MODE` carries a smoothing distance or a block-change criterion; Heidenhain `M90` stays RAW. Alternative 1: no word, and a shop that needs the mode names a `FUNC` in its own machine file, which is what is possible today; it breaks opencam D-148, because the CAM would then write a different NCX file per machine. Alternative 2: two more values of `TOLERANCE_MODE`. That does not fit: `TOLERANCE_MODE` is the control's accuracy-against-speed optimization (cycle 32 `HSC-MODE`, `CYCLE832` technology), which Fanuc has no form for at all, while stop-against-continuous is Fanuc group 13 and Siemens group 10 — two modal groups a control sets independently of each other.
Where: language 4.1 (new row before `TOLERANCE`), 5 rule 6 bucket 12 (`PATH_MODE` between `ROTARY_FEED` and `TOLERANCE`); virtual machine 2.1 (frame table, a row beside rotary path and rotary feed) and 4 (modal summary, the "cylinder, polar, tcpm, rotary path and feed, tolerance" row, whose `PROGRAM=END` reset then means the machine's start value); machine-config 4 (`[dynamics] path_mode` comment: now the start value of the word) and 5 (`[transform]`, the two new keys, with the Siemens and Heidenhain variants in the comment); controller-mapping 1 (new `PATH_MODE` row; the `TOLERANCE` row gives up its `G61`/`G64` pair and keeps `G5.1`, `G5`, `G8` and `G61.1`) and 9 (the Siemens RAW list loses `G60` and `G64` and keeps `G601` and `G641`..`G645` with `ADIS`; `G9` and `G602`/`G603` stand in siemens.md 2, groups 11 and 12, but not in that list today, so naming them there is an addition); controllers/fanuc.md 3 (group 13 row) and 4; controllers/siemens.md 2 (group 10 row) and 3 (Path control bullet); controllers/heidenhain.md 2 (the bullet that lists `M126`/`M127`, `M116`/`M117`); implementation 13 and 15 (decisions needed first). Machine files: a new `[transform]` table in `machines/fanuc-mill-30i.toml`, `machines/siemens-840dsl-mill.toml` and `machines/heidenhain-itnc530.toml` — none of the three has one today — and the header comment on line 5 of each, which lists `[transform]` among the tables with nothing to configure; the two keys in the five machine files that carry `path_mode` and have a `[transform]` table (`dmg-ctx-840d.toml`, `doosan-puma-2600sy.toml`, `millturn1.toml`, `mori-ntx1000-mapps.toml`, `nakamura-ntjx.toml`), each in both of its identical copies, under `machines/` and under `docs/spec/examples/machines/`. #### D350 Whether [dynamics] path_mode is the start value of the programmed mode, and which one the runtime estimate reads
Question: Machine-config 4 gives `[dynamics] path_mode` as control behaviour for the runtime estimate (D64), and virtual machine 8 reads it per corner: "`path_mode = \"exact_stop\"` brakes to zero in every block, `\"continuous\"` carries the speed through corners up to the configured `corner_speed`". Main has exactly one reader of the key, `MachineDynamics.Continuous` (`src/Ncx.Analytics/Runtime/MachineDynamics.cs:40`), and `RuntimeEstimator.CornerSpeed` (line 203) returns 0 whenever it is false. No document says what becomes of the key once a program can write the mode: the companion draft adds `PATH_MODE`, and the request asks that the estimate "use the programmed mode instead of the machine's `path_mode` while it is set", which leaves open whether the key stays a second, independent setting of its own. The sections disagree in effect rather than in words: machine-config 4 presents the key as the machine's behaviour, while virtual machine 2.1 takes the initial value of several modal states "from TOML" (workplane, origin, workpiece holder) and so has a shape ready for a start value that a word then changes — though the nearest neighbours of the new word do not use it, since rotary path, rotary feed and the tolerance triple take fixed initial values there (FULL, DEG_MIN, OFF, none, FINISH). D286 asks only where the path comes to rest while the mode is continuous and answers nothing about where the mode comes from. Case: a square path on `machines/fanuc-mill-30i.toml` (`path_mode = "continuous"`, `corner_speed = 2000`) with `PATH_MODE=EXACT_STOP` written before the finishing pass — the estimate carries 2000 mm/min through every corner of that pass and the report line still reads "path_mode continuous" (`MachineDynamics.ProfileLine`, line 81, asserted in `tests/Ncx.Acceptance/Cli/AnalyzeCommandTests.cs:203`), although the machine stops in each one and the compiled Fanuc file says `G61`.
Recommendation: The machine key is the start value and nothing more. `[dynamics] path_mode` becomes the initial value of the path-control state of virtual machine 2.1, as `workplane` and `origin` take theirs "from TOML"; the state is then the only thing the runtime estimate reads, so `MachineDynamics.Continuous` goes and `RuntimeEstimator.CornerSpeed` asks the snapshot of the motion before the corner, `before.Motion.After`, which the estimator already holds (`PendingMotion.Motion`, `src/Ncx.Analytics/Runtime/PendingMotion.cs`). `PATH_MODE=DEFAULT` puts the start value back, which is why the word needs that third value, and the `PROGRAM=END` of virtual machine 4 puts it back too. A `[dynamics]` without `path_mode` keeps the reading main has today, exact stop, so the start value is exact stop there; a machine file without `[dynamics]` at all leaves the estimate at distance over the commanded feed, where the mode changes nothing, and the report already says so. Where the machine names no template for the mode the program asked for — the recommended `machines/heidenhain-itnc530.toml`, where the compiler writes nothing and reports the new WARNING — the state still rules the estimate and the report says of those corners that the machine cannot express the mode, so the one file does not quietly claim a machine behaviour the compiled program never commands. The report's dynamics line keeps naming the start value, as the file gives it, and where a program changed the mode it says so and counts the corners timed in each mode, so the maintainer still sees every value the estimate used rather than correcting the code (implementation 14, risks). D286's rest points are untouched: they are read against the state instead of against the key, and the `TODO(question)` marker at `RuntimeEstimator.cs:14` stays with D286. Reason: one vocabulary and one place. Two independent settings would let a report say "continuous" of a program that is exact stop throughout, and would make the compiled file and the estimate of the same NCX text disagree about the same machine — and the estimate is the one analytic opencam's own simulation is compared against (R1-06 asks for the control-held values for exactly that reason). Alternative: keep the two apart — the word is for the compilers, the key for the estimate, with a WARNING where a program writes a mode the key contradicts. It is less code and it keeps `[dynamics]` purely descriptive, but it fails the request's test: the runtime of the square path would not rise when the mode switches, and the third value `DEFAULT` of the word would then mean nothing. This draft presupposes the companion draft; answer the two together.
Where: virtual machine 2.1 (the frame table row and its Initial column, "from TOML (`[dynamics] path_mode`, exact stop without it)"), 4 (modal summary, the row that lists rotary path, rotary feed and tolerance) and 8 (the `path_mode` sentence of the runtime estimate); machine-config 4 (`[dynamics] path_mode` comment: the start value of the `PATH_MODE` word, not a setting of its own); implementation 14 (the `RuntimeAnalytic` paragraph) and `docs/architecture/architecture.md` (the Runtime estimate row of section 10, line 1040, and the D64 line of section 13, line 1140). Code: `src/Ncx.Analytics/Runtime/MachineDynamics.cs` (`Continuous` at line 40, documented at 37, and `ProfileLine` at line 81), `src/Ncx.Analytics/Runtime/RuntimeEstimator.cs` (`CornerSpeed` at line 203, `Stop`, and the class marker at line 14 that carries D286), `src/Ncx.Analytics/Runtime/PendingMotion.cs` (the `MotionEvent` the corner is read from), `src/Ncx.Analytics/Runtime/README.md`; `src/Ncx.Core/VirtualMachine/State/FrameState.cs` (the start value from the machine configuration). Tests: `tests/Ncx.Acceptance/Analytics/RuntimeAnalyticTests.cs` (the pair `PathModeExactStop_TwoLinesInARow_BrakeToZeroInTheCorner` at line 77 and `PathModeContinuous_...` at line 90, plus a new test for a square path that switches the mode mid-program and one for the report line at line 457), `tests/Ncx.Acceptance/Cli/AnalyzeCommandTests.cs:203`, `tests/Ncx.Acceptance/Analytics/AnalyticMachines.cs` (the `ExactStop` and continuous dynamics), `tests/Ncx.Config.Tests/MachineConfigLoaderTests.cs:548`. Related D64, D286 and the companion draft.

ANSWER: (Peter, 2026-10-07, drafted by Claude in project_spike) Accept as recommended: `[dynamics] path_mode` is only the start value of the programmed mode, and the runtime estimate reads the state.
