#### D351 A stock word for the blank of the graphic
Question: Language 4 has no word for the blank, and every document that touches it says the same thing: heidenhain 1 and 7 rule 9 keep `BLK FORM 0.1`/`0.2` as `RAW` header information with a WARNING, siemens 3 and 11 rule 8 keep `WORKPIECE(...)` the same way, and controller-mapping 9 lists both among the statements readers keep as `RAW`, with the survey paragraph of 11.1 recording "`BLK FORM` stays `RAW` header information" as the answer of the first word survey. The consequence is that a program NCXchange writes itself carries no blank at all: `HeidenhainCompilerTests.StockDefinition` records the two `BLK FORM` lines as an accepted difference of the compiled program with the grounds "D217 (wave-2 question #81) and heidenhain 7 rule 9: the NCX program holds no BLK FORM", and `RoundTrips.CompileDifferences` uses it for all three Klartext programs, 2.5D_FRAESEN (`Z-20`), BOHREN (`Z-25`) and 3D_FRAESEN (`Z-55`); the Siemens compiler writes no `WORKPIECE(...)`. The example `docs/spec/examples/2.5D_FRAESEN.ncx` says so in its own line 7, "H2/H3 BLK FORM (stock definition) has no NCX word yet". A CAM that writes one NCX file for every controller therefore has no way to say that the blank is a 100 by 100 by 20 box, and the two controls that have a graphic get nothing. Checked by running `ncx check` on a program with the request's own words: `STOCK=BOX` and every `MAX:...` is the ERROR PAR010, unknown key, and the bare `X Y Z` of that block are three PAR012 ERRORs. The names the request offers are not available: `WORKPIECE` is the holder selection of 4.10 (D57, D298) at rank 640, and `CYLINDER` the cylinder-surface transformation of 4.2 (D96) at rank 740. Nothing says which word carries the blank, which value forms it takes, by which words its geometry is given, in which frame its coordinates stand, where it ranks in the canonical order of D90, which axis words the block may carry at all, or what a control without a blank form does.
Recommendation: Adopt `STOCK` as a verb of language 4.2 and leave every control fact in the machine file. The name is free in the catalog (`src/Ncx.Core/Catalog`, `docs/spec/generated/word-catalog.md`) and collides with nothing. Two value forms in release 1, `STOCK=BOX` and `STOCK=CYLINDER`, both given by the same six coordinate words, the bounding box of the solid: the bare absolute axis words `X Y Z` for the corner the solid starts at and the new addressed words `MAX:X MAX:Y MAX:Z` for the opposite one, exactly as an `ARC` carries its end point bare and its centre under `CENTER:`. `STOCK=CYLINDER` is the cylinder inscribed in that box about the tool axis of the active `WORKPLANE`. The coordinates are numbers or expressions in the active units, in the workpiece frame active where the block stands (the frame chain of 4.2), and fixed there: a later `ORIGIN` or `SHIFT` does not move the blank. That is not an NCX invention but what the control does, and the maintainer's library states it: the Siemens blank "is clamped with reference to the coordinate system valid at the time of the blank definition", "is always created in the zero offset that is currently active", and choosing another zero offset afterwards recomputes the coordinate system while the blank's picture stays where it was. The same page requires the datum, and on a swivelling machine a swivel to zero, to stand before the blank definition, so the rule is not only "before the first motion verb" but "after the first `ORIGIN`": `STOCK` stands once per program, in the header, after the first `ORIGIN` and before the first motion verb. Values are rounded to `[format] decimals` like every other value, and NCX always writes the second corner absolute (the iTNC 530 and the TNC 640 accept an incremental MAX point; NCX does not need it). `STOCK` becomes the eleventh verb of 5 rule 1, which is what lets it carry axis words at all under 5 rule 2, and it joins the D117 paragraph of 4.2 beside `SHIFT` and `SETPOS`: absolute axis words only, an incremental word under it the ERROR PAR012. One restriction has to be written down with it, because language 3's KEY rule admits every machine axis word of the D93 form "in a block whose verb takes axis words": `STOCK` carries `X`, `Y`, `Z` and `MAX:X`, `MAX:Y`, `MAX:Z` alone, and any other axis word under it, `A`, `W`, `Z2` or an `I` form, is PAR012 through a new branch of `BlockRules.FrameVerbRefusal`, as `TILT`'s restriction to A, B and C already works. Rank: the shared verb rank 90 of bucket 2 for `STOCK`, and `MAX:X`, `MAX:Y`, `MAX:Z` at 371, 372 and 373 at the end of bucket 5 after the incremental `CENTER` forms. They fit between `CenterIncrementalC` (370) and `R` (380), but they are not steps of ten: the doc comment of `CanonicalRanks` ("The ranks go in steps of ten") and the note of the generated table say so and must be amended, and the alternative is to renumber bucket 5 onward or give the `MAX` family a bucket of its own. Machine key: a new `[stock]` section beside `[retract]` and `[tolerance]`, one template per value form, written in the house style of `[retract]` (`FORM = "line\nline"`). The placeholders are `{axis}` (already defined as the tool axis letter, which `BLK FORM 0.1` names), `{x} {y} {z}`, `{max_x} {max_y} {max_z}` and, computed from the box for the cylinder forms, `{radius}`, `{diameter}`, `{length}` (the extent along the tool axis) and `{dist}` (the offset of the cylinder's near face along that axis). `{diameter}` is a new name because the existing `{d}` of the placeholder list means twice `{r}`, the Siemens `TRACYL` working diameter, which is a different quantity. `machines/heidenhain-itnc530.toml` gets `BOX = "BLK FORM 0.1 {axis} X{x} Y{y} Z{z}\nBLK FORM 0.2 X{max_x} Y{max_y} Z{max_z}"` and no `CYLINDER` template, because the iTNC 530 has only the cuboid: its manual defines "ein quaderförmiges, unbearbeitetes Werkstück" whose sides lie parallel to X, Y and Z, by a MIN and a MAX point, and offers no other shape. `machines/siemens-840dsl-mill.toml` gets a `WORKPIECE(...)` template per shape in the native parameter order with one placeholder per parameter, as the `[transform]` templates are written (D262). `machines/fanuc-mill-30i.toml` gets no `[stock]` section at all. A form the machine file has no template for writes nothing and reports the INFO `CMP012`, the next free code of the compiler framework's template range CMP010-CMP019 in `src/Ncx.Compilers/DiagnosticCodes.cs`; it must not be the ERROR `CMP010` of a missing template, because a control without a graphic is doing nothing wrong, and D98 already has the INFO severity for notes that are neither an error nor a warning. Two more codes of that range: `CMP013`, a WARNING for a stock the machine's own template cannot express, and `CMP014`, a WARNING where a program holds both a `STOCK` and a `RAW:<controller>` blank of the target, in which case the compiler writes the `RAW` text as it stands and skips the `[stock]` template, so that no program ever carries two blanks (that rule is needed the moment `STOCK` exists, whatever the reader direction of the second draft is answered). `CMP013` is needed because the bounding box is not what either control's cylinder form is built from, which the library settles: the TNC 640 writes a cylindrical blank as `BLK FORM CYLINDER Z R50 L105 DIST+5 RI10`, that is rotation axis, radius or diameter, length, an optional `DIST` shift along the axis and an optional inner radius for a hollow cylinder, with no X or Y centre at all, so the cylinder's axis always stands at the active datum's origin; and the Siemens `WORKPIECE(...)` cylinder takes five dimension arguments, not two corners. So a `STOCK=CYLINDER` whose box is not centred on the tool axis through the datum is `CMP013` on such a machine, and nothing is written. Three ERRORs join the frame family of the validation, whose own range is VM420-VM439 inside the validation area VM400-VM599, so VM423 to VM425 are the next free codes after VM422: `VM423` a `STOCK` that does not carry all six coordinate words of its form, `VM424` a `STOCK` with a side of zero or negative extent, or a `STOCK=CYLINDER` whose two sides across the tool axis are not equal so that its footprint is not a circle, and `VM425` a second `STOCK` in one program, a `STOCK` before the first `ORIGIN`, or a `STOCK` after the first motion verb. Reason: the bounding box is the one piece of geometry every blank shape shares, it needs only four new catalog entries, every control value is derived from it by the compiler, and it leaves which blank a control can draw in the machine file, which is where NCX already keeps `[tolerance]`, `[retract]` and `[transform]`. Alternative 1: give `STOCK=CYLINDER` its own words, the rotation axis, `D` or a diameter word, a length and a distance along it, which is exactly what both controls take and needs no derivation and no `CMP013`, at the price of a second set of geometry words and a block shape that differs per value form. Alternative 2: keep `STOCK` a header word of 4.1, where every document already calls the blank header information, and give both corners addressed words, `MIN:X MIN:Y MIN:Z MAX:X MAX:Y MAX:Z`, matching the controls' own MIN and MAX point names, so that 5 rule 1 keeps its ten verbs and 5 rule 2 is untouched, at the price of six new catalog entries and a block that carries coordinates without a verb, which no other block of NCX does.
Where: `docs/spec/ncx-language.md`: a `STOCK` row in 4.2, the D117 axis-word paragraph and the frame-chain paragraph of 4.2, the `IX` row of 4.3, 5 rule 1 (eleven verbs), 5 rule 2, 5 rule 6 buckets 2 and 5, and an example in 6. `docs/spec/ncx-virtual-machine.md` 2.1, 3, 4 and the ERROR list of 5. `docs/spec/machine-config.md`: the placeholder list of the introduction (`{max_x} {max_y} {max_z}`, `{length}`, `{dist}`, `{diameter}` beside the existing `{d}`; D152 is open on unlisted names), a `[stock]` section in 5 beside `[retract]` and `[tolerance]`, and section 11. `docs/spec/controller-mapping.md` 1 (a `STOCK` row) and 9. `docs/controllers/heidenhain.md` 1 and 8, `docs/controllers/siemens.md` 3 and 12, `docs/controllers/fanuc.md`. Machine files: `machines/heidenhain-itnc530.toml`, `machines/siemens-840dsl-mill.toml`, `machines/fanuc-mill-30i.toml` and the five files of `docs/spec/examples/machines/` (`dmg-ctx-840d`, `doosan-puma-2600sy`, `millturn1`, `mori-ntx1000-mapps`, `nakamura-ntjx`). Code: `src/Ncx.Core/Catalog/FrameWords.cs`, `CanonicalRanks.cs` (the new ranks and its step-of-ten comment), `CanonicalOrder.cs`, `WordCheck.cs` and `WordDefinition.cs` (`TakesAxisWords`); `src/Ncx.Core/Parsing/BlockRules.cs` (`s_frameVerbs`, `VerbsWithAxisNames`, `FrameVerbRefusal`, `CheckAxisWords`, whose PAR012 message names the verbs that carry axis words); a new `src/Ncx.Core/Machine/StockTable.cs` beside `ToleranceTable.cs` and `RetractTable.cs`, with its field in `src/Ncx.Core/Machine/MachineConfig.cs`; the Tomlyn loader `src/Ncx.Config/MachineConfigLoader.cs` and `src/Ncx.Config/Templates/` (`TemplateSet.cs`, `Placeholder.cs`, `TemplateValues.cs`); `src/Ncx.Core/VirtualMachine/Validation/FrameValidation.cs`, `src/Ncx.Core/Model/DiagnosticCodes.Validation.cs` for VM423-VM425 and `src/Ncx.Core/VirtualMachine/Validation/DiagnosticTable.cs` for their rows; `src/Ncx.Compilers/DiagnosticCodes.cs` for `CMP012`, `CMP013` and `CMP014`; `src/Ncx.Compilers/Heidenhain/HeidenhainProgramFrame.cs`, `src/Ncx.Compilers/Siemens/SiemensProgramFrame.cs` and `src/Ncx.Compilers/Fanuc/FanucProgramFrame.cs`. Generated: `docs/spec/generated/word-catalog.md` and `docs/spec/generated/diagnostics.md`, written by `WordCatalogTableTests` and `DiagnosticTableTests`; diagnostics.md gains the VM423-VM425 rows only, since it states that the CMP codes of the other projects are not listed there. Tests: `tests/Ncx.Core.Tests/Catalog/WordCatalogTable.cs` and `CanonicalOrderTests.cs` (the note "The ten verbs share one rank"), `WordCheckTests.cs`, the validation tests of `tests/Ncx.Core.Tests`, `tests/Ncx.Compilers.Tests/Heidenhain/HeidenhainProgramFrameTests.cs`, `tests/Ncx.Acceptance/Examples/HeidenhainCompilerTests.cs` (`StockDefinition`, `Differences25DFraesen`, `BohrenDifferences`) and `tests/Ncx.Acceptance/RoundTrips.cs` (`CompileDifferences`). Tasks: P0-03 for the word and its rank, P2-01, P2-02 and P2-04 for the `[stock]` key and its templates, P3-03 for the three CMP codes, P3-04, P3-06 and P5-02 for the writing, P3-07 for the acceptance.

ANSWER: (Peter, 2026-10-07, drafted by Claude in project_spike) Accept as recommended (`STOCK=BOX|CYLINDER` by its bounding box, `[stock]` templates, once per program after the first `ORIGIN` and before the first motion), with one change: CMP013, a cylinder the machine's form cannot express, is an INFO, not a WARNING, because the blank feeds only the control's graphic and a WARNING would fail the CAM's `--strict` runs for a graphic detail. Codes: this draft keeps CMP012 to CMP014; D367 moves to CMP015.

#### D352 Whether the readers read BLK FORM and WORKPIECE() into the stock word
Question: As soon as a `STOCK` word exists, the documents disagree with themselves about the reading direction. heidenhain 7 rule 9, siemens 11 rule 8 and controller-mapping 9 go on saying `RAW`, while D5's ground for `RAW`, "source NCX cannot express", no longer holds for the plain box shape; the survey sentence of controller-mapping 11.1, "`BLK FORM` stays `RAW` header information", was written when the language had no word for it. Reading them in is not a local change. `HeidenhainReaderTests.s_heidenhainReading` expects a WARNING for each of the two `RAW:HEIDENHAIN` blocks and counts them among the thirteen reader differences of the open draft D217; `HeidenhainCompilerTests.StockDefinition`, `Differences25DFraesen` and `BohrenDifferences` carry the absence of the blank as an accepted compile difference, and `RoundTrips.CompileDifferences` uses `StockDefinition` for 3D_FRAESEN as well; and the example 2.5D_FRAESEN.ncx deliberately leaves the blank out so that the file still compiles to Fanuc, because a `RAW` of D5 and D94 compiles only to the controller it names, which is also why `RoundTrips` lets the frozen Fanuc readings stand for the Klartext ones on the Fanuc side. D217's own answer from the manual library supports leaving it out: the blank is needed only for the graphic simulation and its dialogue can be cancelled outright, so "leaving it out of the example changes nothing about the machining". Each side has a gap of its own. Klartext has a third blank form the box cannot hold, the rotationally symmetric blank whose contour stands in a subprogram (`BLK FORM` with `DIM_D`/`DIM_R` and `LBL`), and the TNC 640 cylinder carries an optional inner radius for a hollow cylinder; `WORKPIECE(...)` carries a name, a clamping and a datum that no `STOCK` form holds, and the same Siemens manual writes the call with eleven, twelve and thirteen arguments for the one shape `"BOX"`, so a read-back would silently drop arguments and could not even tell how many to expect. And nothing says what a program compiles to that holds both a `STOCK` word and a `RAW` blank of the target controller, which is exactly what a converted Klartext file plus a hand-added `STOCK` would be; the first draft answers that half with `CMP014`, so this draft decides the reader direction alone.
Recommendation: Release 1 keeps both readers as they are: `BLK FORM` stays `RAW:HEIDENHAIN` and `WORKPIECE(...)` stays `RAW:SIEMENS`, each with its WARNING, and `STOCK` serves the writing direction only. Reason: the request's own test asks only that a box compile to `BLK FORM 0.1`/`0.2` and to `WORKPIECE(...)` and that the Fanuc mill write nothing and report the INFO, so the reading direction buys nothing release 1 needs, while answering it the other way reopens D217's list of thirteen differences, the two frozen `Expected/` readings, the `RoundTrips` matrix and the notes of the example in the same commit. heidenhain 7 rule 9 and siemens 11 rule 8 then gain one clause each: the blank is kept `RAW` although a `STOCK` word exists, because the control's forms carry shapes and arguments the word does not. The reader direction is taken in a later release, when the second half can be stated: a `BLK FORM 0.1 {axis}` and `0.2` pair with no further words, and a `WORKPIECE` whose name, clamping and datum arguments are empty or the control's defaults and whose shape is `"BOX"`, read into `STOCK`; a `BLK FORM CYLINDER` with a `RI`, a `DIM_D`/`LBL` contour blank, a `PIPE` or an `N_CORNER` stay `RAW`, since no `STOCK` form holds them. Alternative: read the plain box in now. It closes the round trip for the one shape that matters, lets the example carry its blank at last and removes two of the thirteen differences of D217, and the price is paid once; it belongs in the same commit as the acceptance lists it changes, not after them, and it needs D217 answered first.
Where: `docs/controllers/heidenhain.md` 1 and 7 rule 9; `docs/controllers/siemens.md` 3 and 11 rule 8; `docs/spec/controller-mapping.md` 1, 9 and the survey paragraph of 11.1; the `RAW` row of `docs/spec/ncx-language.md` 4.1; D5, D94 and the open D217, which this draft must be answered with. #### D353 The path `F` feeds along, on an arc and a helix
Question: Language 4.3 gives `F` as "Feed in the active feed mode" and says of `ARC` only that "A tool-axis word in the same block makes a helix"; VM 2.2 keeps `feed.value` and `feed.mode`, and VM 3.1 adds through D184 that an `ARC` "is interpolated at `F` exactly as a `LINE` is". No section says along which path the feed is measured, so nothing states whether the `F` of a helix feeds the circle in the working plane or the whole path with the tool-axis travel. The CAM has decided it for itself (opencam D-113) and asks NCX to state it (R1-04). Where a document does speak it contradicts the code: the segment bullet of VM 8 reads "the euclidean length (arc length for arcs)", which leaves the tool axis out, while `MotionEvents.LengthOf` adds r times the sweep in the plane to the travel of every other axis that moved (MotionEvents.cs:102, 153), `MotionEvent.Length` documents itself as "the arc length for an arc with the travel of a helix" (MotionEvent.cs:79), and the done task `docs/plan/tasks/done/P1-05-events-with-before-and-after.md`:34 says the same in those words. Implementation 14 (P4-03), `SegmentAnalytic`, its README, its report header and its acceptance test all repeat the VM 8 wording instead. Case: `ARC=CCW IZ=-5 CENTER:X=0 CENTER:Y=0 ANGLE=360 F=600` from X=2 Y=0, one turn of radius 2 and pitch 5. Main reports a segment length of 13.525 mm and an estimated time of 1.4 s (1.3525 s before the report's one decimal, the rounded length over the feed, the built-in default machine having no `[dynamics]`); the circle in the plane alone is 12.566 mm and 1.257 s. The compilers write the feed unchanged for all three shipped mills (`G3 X2. Y0. Z-5. I-2. J0. F600.`, `CP IPA+360 IZ-5 DR+ F600`, `G3 X2 Y0 Z-5 I=AC(0) J=AC(0) F600`), which means one thing on a control that feeds the path and another on a control that feeds the arc; that half of the question is D354. Nothing says either what feeds an `ARC` that moves a linear axis outside the plane which is not the tool axis (a machine axis of D93), although its travel is already part of the length.
Recommendation: State in the `F` row of language 4.3 that `F` is the feed along the path the block's motion describes in the active frame, and in the `ARC` row that for an arc this path is the arc length in the working plane together with the travel of every linear axis the block moves outside it, so that a helix feeds along its three-dimensional path and not along the circle in the plane; `FEED_MODE=PER_REV` measures the same path per revolution of the spindle of D288. Repeat the sentence in VM 3.2 where the helix is defined, and correct the segment bullet of VM 8 to "the arc length with the travel of a helix", so that language, VM 8, the MOTION length, the segment report and the runtime estimate say one thing; implementation 14 (P4-03), `SegmentAnalytic.cs`, its report header, its README and its acceptance test take the same wording. A rotary axis is no part of that path outside the polar and the cylinder plane, where its word is a length (VM 3.1, D102): that keeps the rule inside levels 0 and 1 of VM 9, since the path the tool travels in space while a rotary axis turns is level 2, the kinematics module (VM 9, 10). No new word is needed and none is proposed: `F` keeps its rank in bucket 7 of the canonical order (language 5 rule 6, D90; rank 400 in `generated/word-catalog.md`), the catalog in src/Ncx.Core/Catalog is unchanged, and the rule is a definition, so it needs no diagnostic of its own. Of the two diagnostics it touches, `VM201` for an `ARC` without feed (D184) stays as it is, and the `max_feed` comparison `VM441` is not decided here: D192 is still open and its proposed answer of 2026-09-27 reads the controls as limiting each moving axis's share of the feed (Fanuc parameter 1430, Siemens the axial maxima of the axes taking part, Heidenhain a per-axis `maxWorkFeed`) rather than the path feed, and the helix rule holds under either reading, because it says what the path of an arc is, not what is compared with it. Reason: this is the rule two of the three families state themselves (Heidenhain defines `F` as the speed at which the tool centre moves on its path; Siemens composes the path feed, "im Regelfall", from the velocity components of all geometry axes taking part in the movement, referred to the cutter centre), it is what the length the VM already computes means, and it is the only reading under which one NCX file cuts at the programmed feed on every machine, which is the client's premise (opencam D-148). Alternative: `F` on a helix feeds the circle in the plane, the state a Fanuc control is delivered in on the reading of its manual's first case; then nothing in the VM or the compilers changes for Fanuc, but the Heidenhain and Siemens compilers must scale the feed down instead, and the MOTION length, the segment report and the runtime estimate have to be unpicked from the path they now measure - the same work on two families rather than one, and against those two manuals' own wording.
Where: language 4.3 (the `F` row and one sentence in the `ARC` row); VM 2.2 (`feed.value`), VM 3.2 (the helix sentence) and VM 8 (the segment bullet and the runtime bullet); controllers/differences.md (the Feed row) and controller-mapping 2 (the `F` row); implementation 14 (P4-03, the `SegmentAnalytic` paragraph, line 51); src/Ncx.Core/VirtualMachine/Events/MotionEvents.cs `LengthOf` (line 153) and the plane-length comment at line 102, src/Ncx.Core/VirtualMachine/Events/MotionEvent.cs:79 (the `Length` comment, already right), src/Ncx.Analytics/Runtime/RuntimeEstimator.cs:127 `AddMotion`, src/Ncx.Analytics/Segments/SegmentAnalytic.cs:10, src/Ncx.Analytics/Segments/SegmentAnalytic.Report.cs:15 (the report header the CLI prints) and src/Ncx.Analytics/Segments/README.md; tests/Ncx.Core.Tests/VirtualMachine/Events/MotionEventTests.cs `Motion_Helix_LengthIncludesTheTravelOfTheToolAxis`, tests/Ncx.Acceptance/Analytics/SegmentAnalyticTests.cs:12, and a new case in tests/Ncx.Acceptance/Analytics/RuntimeAnalyticTests.cs for the 13.525 mm turn at F600 (asserted on the estimator or on the segment length, the runtime report printing one decimal); docs/plan/tasks/done/P1-05-events-with-before-and-after.md:34 (the sentence that already states the rule); related D184, D192, D288, D290, D102, D84, D268.

ANSWER: (Peter, 2026-10-07, drafted by Claude in project_spike) Accept as recommended. It matches the CAM's rule (opencam D-096, D-113): `F` on a helix is the feed along the 3D path.

#### D354 The feed a Fanuc control reads on a helix (parameter 1403#5), and what the compiler writes
Question: No document of docs/controllers says along which path a control measures `F` on a helix: fanuc.md 2 gives `F` as the feed per minute or per revolution and fanuc.md 4 gives a helix as "a third axis in the arc block", siemens.md 3 lists `FGROUP(X, Y, Z, A)` and `FGREF[A]=r` among the feed words that controller-mapping 2 keeps `RAW`, and heidenhain.md says nothing of the feed of a `CP IPA`. So the compilers write the NCX feed unchanged, and for the turn of radius 2 and pitch 5 all three shipped mills write F600 (`G3 X2. Y0. Z-5. I-2. J0. F600.`, `CP IPA+360 IZ-5 DR+ F600`, `G3 X2 Y0 Z-5 I=AC(0) J=AC(0) F600`). The families differ, and on Fanuc the difference is one machine's own setting rather than a property of the control: on helical interpolation the 30i measures `F` either along a tangent of the arc in the programmed plane or along the tool path, by bit 5 (HTG) of channel parameter 1403, so the same block cuts at 600 mm/min along the helix on one mill and at 645.750 mm/min on another (600 times 13.524558 over 12.566371, 7.625 percent high), and the runtime estimate of VM 8 is wrong by that factor. Both feeds are modal, which doubles the question: the NCX `F` is modal and the Fanuc `F` is modal, so the rule has to say what the compiler writes on a helix block whose NCX block states no `F`, and what the reader writes for a helix block the source left modal. Siemens has the mirror case: the path feed covers all geometry axes taking part "im Regelfall", but `FGROUP` can drive the infeed axis as a synchronous axis - the manual's own example is a helix with X and Y at the programmed feed and Z synchronous - and after `FGROUP()` the basic state comes from a machine datum; since the reader keeps `FGROUP` `RAW` the compiler can write a program whose `F` means the plane feed without knowing it. Machine-config names no key for any of this, and the reader has the same gap: an `F` read from such a Fanuc source is not the NCX feed, so `ncx convert` does not round-trip.
Recommendation: Add the optional key `helix_feed = "path" | "arc"` to `[format]` (machine-config 2), beside `external_call`, the one key already there that names a control parameter the compiler has to know (parameter 6030) rather than a number format; `[dynamics]` is the other possible home, `path_mode` (D286) being the one other key that is a control behaviour, but only the compiler and the reader need `helix_feed`, because the runtime estimate works on the NCX feed, which D353 defines as the path feed on every machine. `"path"` says the control measures `F` along the whole path of the block, `"arc"` that it measures it along the arc in the working plane. The key is family-independent, so a Siemens machine whose `FGROUP` basic state leaves the infeed axis out of the path-axis group carries `"arc"` too and its compiler scales the same way; a `RAW` `FGROUP(...)` line inside a program stays outside the rule, because `RAW` commits to nothing (D5). Without the key each compiler takes the state its family's manual documents, `"arc"` on Fanuc (parameter 1403#5 = 0, the case the manual explains first; name the parameter in the key's comment of machines/fanuc-mill-30i.toml, whose header already says the file is not verified on a machine, as D100 says of its axis, position and dynamics numbers) and `"path"` on Heidenhain and Siemens. Under `"arc"` the Fanuc compiler writes the `F` of an `ARC` that moves an axis outside the plane scaled by the plane length over the path length, formatted with the `F` decimals of `[format]` like every other feed: F557.491 for the case above. It computes the factor in double from the MOTION event that `FanucArcs` already reads through `MotionOf(write.Step)` - the sweep from `Sweep` and the radius from `From` against `Center`, or from the `R` word on the `R` form, the event carrying no radius of its own - all of them decimals the VM has already rounded to the position decimals, which is finer than the `F` decimals by orders of magnitude. It writes the scaled value on a helix block that states no `F` as well, through the branch of `FanucMotion.AddFeed` that writes the modal feed where the control holds another, and the next `LINE` or `ARC` writes the NCX feed again by itself, because the compiler records what it wrote as the feed the control holds (`FanucBlock.NeedsValueOfTheWalk`, the mechanism D218 uses for the `F` of a cycle block). The Fanuc reader multiplies back by the same factor on such a machine, writing the scaled-back `F` on a helix block the source left modal and the plain `F` again on the next motion, the mirror of the compiler's rule (`FanucMotion.ReadFeed`, `AddModalFeed` and the control and written feed of `FanucCallerState`), so `ncx convert` returns the NCX feed within the rounding. Where the compiler cannot scale, an `F` from an expression that the STATIC walk does not know (VM 1), it writes the `F` as it stands and reports the new WARNING `CMP324` (free in the Fanuc motion range CMP320 to CMP339, of which CMP320 to CMP323 are taken), naming parameter 1403#5 and the feed the control will actually run, so that the setup sheet can show it. Writing a converted value rather than the programmed number has its precedent in D60, where the compiler halves X under `DIAMETER`; design rule 5 ("Numbers untouched") binds the number format, not the value, and its own last sentence hands the number format of the target machine to the compiler. Reason: the difference belongs to a machine's parameter, not to a controller family, so it belongs in the machine file, and only the conversion keeps the premise that one NCX file cuts at the programmed feed on every machine (opencam D-148). Alternative: write the feed unchanged everywhere and report `CMP324` on every helix of a machine whose key says `"arc"`, as R1-10 proposes for the Fanuc tolerance; the NC file then shows the number the programmer wrote and the shop sets the parameter, but every helix of every such program carries a WARNING, the runtime estimate stays wrong by the factor, and `ncx convert` still does not round-trip.
Where: machine-config 2 (`[format]`, the key and its comment); controllers/fanuc.md 2 (the `F` bullet) and 4 (the `G2`/`G3` bullet), controllers/siemens.md 3 (the feed bullet with `FGROUP` and `FGREF`), controllers/heidenhain.md 2, controllers/differences.md (the Feed row), controller-mapping 2 (the `F` row and the `ANGLE` row); machines/fanuc-mill-30i.toml `[format]`, and whether the other machine files of machines/ and docs/spec/examples/machines/ carry the key; src/Ncx.Core/Machine/OutputFormat.cs (a property beside `ExternalCall` at line 69) and src/Ncx.Config/MachineConfigLoader.Identity.cs (the `s_formatKeys` list at lines 20-25 and the read at line 123; its own TODO(question) at line 125 already records that machine-config 2 does not name every key the loader takes, so the key goes into the document, the list and `OutputFormat` together); src/Ncx.Compilers/Fanuc/FanucMotion.cs `AddFeed` (line 346; open-questions row 76 still cites the stale FanucMotion.cs:302 for the same method) and src/Ncx.Compilers/Fanuc/FanucArcs.cs `Add` (line 18, the `R` and the `I J K` form), `WriteTurns` (line 52) and `MotionOf` (line 186) - the Fanuc compiler has no `WriteCentre` or `WriteRadius`, those being `HeidenhainArcs` members; src/Ncx.Compilers/Fanuc/DiagnosticCodes.Fanuc.cs (`CMP324`, declared there alone: docs/spec/generated/diagnostics.md states in its own header that it lists only the Ncx.Core codes and that the CFG, RDR, CMP, ANA, PLG and CLI codes are not listed there, and no document lists the CMP3xx range); src/Ncx.Readers/Fanuc/FanucMotion.cs `ReadArc` (line 366), `ReadFeed` (line 202) and `AddModalFeed` (line 459), src/Ncx.Readers/Fanuc/FanucCallerState.cs (the control and written feed); tests/Ncx.Compilers.Tests/Fanuc/FanucMotionTests.cs beside `Arc_WithASweepBeyond360_IsSplitIntoTurns` (line 45), tests/Ncx.Readers.Tests/Fanuc/FanucMotionTests.cs beside `G3_WithoutJAndWithZ_IsAHelixAboutTheCentre` (line 54), and a round trip in tests/Ncx.Acceptance; related D286, D60, D218, D84, D268, D192, D100.

ANSWER: (Peter, 2026-10-07, drafted by Claude in project_spike) Accept as recommended: `[format] helix_feed = "path"|"arc"`, Fanuc default `"arc"`, the Fanuc compiler scales `F` and the reader scales it back. The scaled `F` is rounded like every other value, half away from zero on its decimal value (R1-09).

#### D355 The plane the first peck counts from
Question: Language 4.7 gives `PECK` as "Peck depth (Q, Q202)" and names no plane it counts from, and the mapping of `PECK` onto `CYCLE83` that R1-05 asks for decides the Siemens reading without a decision. The families count from two different planes. On the 840D sl the first drilling depth is `FDEP` absolute or `FDPR` relative to the reference plane `RFP`, which is `SURFACE`, and with `_DAM` = 0 every further infeed equals it (D181), so `PECK` = `FDPR` makes the first stroke end at `SURFACE` minus `PECK`. On Heidenhain `Q202` is the infeed of cycle 203 below the surface `Q203`, and the settled D163 already counts that way, since `CHIP_BREAK` writes `Q213` = ceil(|Q201| / Q202), the number of infeeds of the depth below the surface; the compiler writes `Q202` = the whole depth below the surface where a block carries no `PECK` (`HeidenhainCycleValues.Infeed`). On Fanuc the `Q` of `G83` and `G73` is cut from the R plane, which is `CLEARANCE`, so the same program's first stroke ends one clearance gap higher; D158's own evidence states the split, that the Fanuc R is Heidenhain's `Q203` plus `Q200` and cannot be recovered from a Fanuc block. The virtual machine is a fourth reading: `CycleRules.Pecks` steps from `CLEARANCE` towards `DEPTH`, and D190, which writes main's model into VM 3.3, says only "splits the feed into steps of `PECK`" and names no plane. The case: `CLEARANCE=2 DEPTH=-10 PECK=5` is the test `CycleCallTests.CycleCall_PeckCycle_FeedsInPecksWithAFullRetract`, whose first peck feeds to Z=-3, while a Siemens `CYCLE83` with `FDPR`=5 and a Heidenhain 203 with `Q202`=5 both cut to -5 when `SURFACE`=0. The CAM writes one NCX file for every controller, and the stroke count, the trace, the runtime estimate and the CAM's own simulation all follow from the plane, so NCX must name it.
Recommendation: Say in the `PECK` row of language 4.7 and in VM 3.3 that `PECK` is the infeed per peck counted from the plane the cutting starts at: `SURFACE` where the block gives one, `CLEARANCE` where it does not. The first peck then ends one `PECK` from that plane in the drilling direction, every further peck one `PECK` deeper, and the last stops at `DEPTH`. Reason: two of the three families can write nothing else, because `FDPR` counts from `RFP` and `Q202` from `Q203` and a constant infeed has no stroke of its own, and the material each stroke cuts then does not depend on `CLEARANCE`, which is an air gap the CAM chooses freely; the settled arithmetic of D163 already counts strokes this way. The `CLEARANCE` fallback has to stand on its own rather than on a claim that every block carries `SURFACE`, because a block without `SURFACE` is an ERROR only on Heidenhain (`CMP104`, "Q203 of cycle 203 has no value"); on Siemens it compiles silently to `CYCLE83(5,,5,-40,...)` with `RFP` empty, and on Fanuc `SURFACE` has no address at all and is carried by a family rule (DrillingFamily.Fanuc.cs `s_fanucRuleWords`; D158). It is also wrong to say that a cycle read from a Fanuc source carries no `SURFACE`: the Fanuc reader writes `SURFACE=0` on every cycle it reads (FanucCycles.cs:909-914), and the open D158 proposes that it write `SURFACE` = R minus a new `[cycles] surface_clearance` instead, so what the fallback reaches, and how often the Fanuc WARNING below fires, is settled by D158 and the two should be answered together. Changes: `CycleRules.Pecks` starts its steps at `SURFACE` and falls back to `CLEARANCE`, and the sentence of D190 reads "steps of `PECK` from `SURFACE`, or from `CLEARANCE` without one", so that the expanded motions and the runtime estimate agree with what the controls cut; the Siemens compiler needs nothing beyond `PECK` = `FDPR`, and the Heidenhain compiler nothing at all. On Fanuc the control keeps its own plane, so the compiler writes `Q` = `PECK` unchanged and reports the shift once, on the block that defines the cycle as `CMP385` is reported (FanucCycles.cs:422), as a new WARNING `CMP387` in the Fanuc cycle range CMP380-CMP399 ("the control cuts the pecks of `CYCLE=PECK` from the R plane, so every stroke before `DEPTH` lies `CLEARANCE` minus `SURFACE` higher"), suppressed where the gap is zero; `DEPTH`, the hole bottom, is unaffected. No new word, no new machine key and no catalog key: both planes already stand on the cycle. First alternative: keep the `CLEARANCE` plane of the VM and of Fanuc and have the Siemens and Heidenhain compilers write `FDPR` = `Q202` = `PECK` minus (`CLEARANCE` minus `SURFACE`). That matches Fanuc's first stroke exactly, but because both controls repeat the first depth it moves every later stroke by the same gap, so it trades one wrong stroke for all of them and needs the WARNING on two families instead of one. Second alternative: let the VM take the plane from the controller family of the machine it runs against, which `convert` and `compile` always have (D77), so that every trace matches its own control and no WARNING is needed. Against it: the same NCX file would then execute differently per machine, which is what the client's single file is meant to rule out, the VM also runs without a machine file (D103), and the CAM's own simulation has no machine to ask.
Where: docs/spec/ncx-language.md 4.7 (the `PECK` row, line 206); docs/spec/ncx-virtual-machine.md 3.3 (the pecking clause of the drilling sequence and of `ExpandCycles`) and 8 Analytics (the runtime-estimate bullet); docs/spec/controller-mapping.md 5 (the `PECK` and `CHIP_BREAK` rows, lines 94-95); cycles/siemens.toml (the `CYCLE83` comment at lines 66-67), cycles/heidenhain.toml (the D163 comment on 203 at lines 61-62), cycles/fanuc.toml (the `G83` and `G73` entries at lines 44-54); src/Ncx.Core/VirtualMachine/CycleRules.cs `Pecks` (line 171) and the TODO(question) of `Drill` that cites D190 (line 144); src/Ncx.Compilers/Heidenhain/HeidenhainCycleValues.cs `Infeed` and the `Q213` rule; src/Ncx.Compilers/Fanuc/FanucCycles.cs with one new constant in src/Ncx.Compilers/Fanuc/DiagnosticCodes.Fanuc.cs (`CMP387`, the next free code of the cycle range, which is used up to CMP386); src/Ncx.Compilers/Siemens/SiemensCycles.cs `Fill`; tests/Ncx.Core.Tests/VirtualMachine/CycleCallTests.cs (`CycleCall_PeckCycle_FeedsInPecksWithAFullRetract` at line 194 and `CycleCall_ChipBreakCycle_FeedsInPecksWithoutLeavingTheHole` at line 210), tests/Ncx.Compilers.Tests/Siemens/SiemensCycleTests.cs, tests/Ncx.Compilers.Tests/Heidenhain/HeidenhainCycleTests.cs (cycle 203) and tests/Ncx.Compilers.Tests/Fanuc/FanucCyclesTests.cs (the new WARNING); related D163 (settled), D158, D181, D190.

ANSWER: (Peter, 2026-10-07, drafted by Claude in project_spike) Accept `SURFACE` as the plane the first peck counts from, with `CLEARANCE` as the fallback, and the VM and D190 changed to match. One change: CMP387 on Fanuc is an INFO, not a WARNING. The CAM always writes `SURFACE` with a clearance gap above it (opencam topic 26), so a WARNING would fire on every Fanuc peck cycle and fail every `--strict` run, while the shift moves only the stroke positions, never the hole bottom. Answer together with D158.

#### D356 A `PECK` or `CHIP_BREAK` without a peck depth on `CYCLE83`
Question: Once D181 is confirmed, `PECK` stands at `FDPR` of `CYCLE83` with `_DAM` = 0 and `FDEP` empty. A `PECK` or `CHIP_BREAK` block that carries no `PECK`, or `PECK` = 0, then leaves both first-depth positions empty: main writes `MCALL CYCLE83(5,0,5,-40,,,,,,,,1)`, and the test that fixes it (`SiemensCycleTests.Peck_WithoutPeckDepth_IsCycle83WithVariOne`) says "without PECK the cycle takes its own infeeds", which no document supports. D181's own general rule says an omitted parameter is zero, and the first drilling depth of `CYCLE83` is programmed through `FDEP` or `FDPR` - the sl Zyklen manual states the first depth is given by one or the other of the two - so a call with neither gives the cycle no first depth at all. Siemens 7 and machine-config 6 say only that a position without a value stays empty and the cycle takes its default, which is the rule that produces this call; D164 keeps that reading for the Siemens reader and says outright that the Siemens compiler still leaves such a position empty. The other two families already have a rule for the same program: the Heidenhain compiler writes `Q202` = the whole depth below the surface, one infeed (`HeidenhainCycleValues.Infeed`, as D164 recommends for the Q parameters no word carries), and the Fanuc compiler writes `G83 G99 Z-40. R5. F100.` without `Q` and reports nothing, the plain drilling cycle. So the one NCX program the CAM may write drills on two controls and may alarm on the third, and nothing reports it. `FDPR` is not the case D164 covers, because after the mapping it is `PECK`'s own position and the block simply omits the word, so the rule has to be stated for the family.
Recommendation: Make it a rule of the Siemens drilling family: for `PECK` and `CHIP_BREAK` the compiler writes `FDPR` = |`DEPTH` - `SURFACE`| where the block carries no `PECK` or `PECK` = 0, the whole depth in one infeed, and |`DEPTH` - `CLEARANCE`| where the block gives no `SURFACE`, so that the rule fits whichever answer D355 receives; `FDEP` stays empty as always. `CLEARANCE` and `DEPTH` are always known, since VM 3.3 requires both and a cycle without them is ERROR `VM251` before the compiler runs. `SURFACE` is not required and today is not reported at all: a Siemens `PECK` without `SURFACE` compiles to `CYCLE83(5,,5,-40,...)` with `RFP` empty and no diagnostic, although `CMP572`'s own description names "the reference plane" among the values it covers (the code raises it only for the retract plane and the drilling axis, SiemensCycles.cs:349 and :381); whether that silence is itself a gap belongs to D188, not here. Reason for the rule: it is the value the Heidenhain compiler already writes at `Q202` in that case (D164), it is the cut the virtual machine executes (D190: a `PECK` above 0 splits the feed, none feeds straight to `DEPTH`), and it keeps the three families drilling the same hole from one NCX file, which is what the client's single file asks of us; the call is then well formed on the control. No new word, no new diagnostic and no catalog key: the rule belongs to the family and is written in the header of cycles/siemens.toml and in the comment of DrillingFamily.Siemens.cs beside the `DEPTH`-from-`DPR` rule, as controller-mapping 5 states the other family rules. Alternative: report it instead, a new ERROR `CMP574` (the next free code of the Siemens cycle range CMP570-CMP589, which is used up to CMP573) saying that `CYCLE=PECK` without `PECK` has no first depth on `CYCLE83`, and leave both positions empty; that is honest about the control but makes a program that compiles on the Fanuc and the Heidenhain mill fail on the Siemens one, which a CAM writing one file for every controller cannot work around. A third form, writing `CYCLE81` for a `PECK` without `PECK` as D177 routes a `DRILL` with a dwell to `CYCLE82`, changes the cycle the program named and loses the chip-break behaviour of `VARI` = 0, and is not recommended.
Where: docs/controllers/siemens.md 7 (the `CYCLE83` row of the cycle table) and 12 rule 5; docs/spec/controller-mapping.md 5 (the `PECK` and `CHIP_BREAK` rows, lines 94-95); cycles/siemens.toml (the `CYCLE83` comment at lines 66-67, which holds the D181 marker today) and src/Ncx.Core/Machine/DrillingFamily.Siemens.cs `SiemensPeckParams` (the TODO(question) at lines 114-115); src/Ncx.Compilers/Siemens/SiemensCycles.cs `Fill` and `ValueOf`; tests/Ncx.Compilers.Tests/Siemens/SiemensCycleTests.cs `Peck_WithoutPeckDepth_IsCycle83WithVariOne` (line 189), which asserts today's two empty positions, plus a `CHIP_BREAK` case and a case without `SURFACE`; row 133 of docs/implementation/03-open-questions.md; related D164, D181, D188, D190.

ANSWER: (Peter, 2026-10-07, drafted by Claude in project_spike) Accept as recommended: a `PECK` or `CHIP_BREAK` without a peck depth writes `FDPR` = the whole depth on `CYCLE83`.

#### D357 The control's cycle distances as machine keys
Question: R1-06 of the opencam release-1 list needs the values the control holds itself for the chip-breaking lift and the peck re-approach, so that the CAM's simulation, the VM trace and the runtime estimate use the same numbers as the machine. No document gives them a place. Machine-config 6 `[cycles]` holds only `catalog`, and `CyclesConfig.cs` and `MachineConfigLoader.Variables.cs` (`s_cyclesKeys`) only that one key; machine-config 4 `[dynamics]` holds `block_time`, `path_mode` and `corner_speed` for the runtime estimate and no cycle value; `[[axis]]` is per axis, and these values are per control; `[retract]` is the `RETRACT` verb of D83. The cycle catalog is the wrong place twice over: it is per controller family, and the effective catalog is the shipped file under the machine's own `[[cycle]]` entries, which only NCXchange resolves, while R1-06 asks for keys the CAM can read itself. The code shows the gap: `CycleRules.Drill` skips the retract between pecks for `CHIP_BREAK` entirely, so an `ExpandCycles` run of `CYCLE=CHIP_BREAK CLEARANCE=2 DEPTH=-20 PECK=5` on the Fanuc mill raises five consecutive feed motions to `DEPTH` with no retract between them (`ncx analyze`: 10 motions, 22 mm rapid, 16.4 s), and `Pecks` returns the exact depths reached, so the same program as `PECK` rapids the whole way back after every peck (18 motions, 122 mm rapid, 17.2 s) with a re-approach of 0; both sit under the `TODO(question)` of D190 at `CycleRules.cs:138-144`, whose manual answer says that 0 is longer than any control's rapid and biases the runtime estimate, and names Fanuc parameters 5115 (G83) and 5114 (G73) without saying where NCXchange is to get them. D164 settles only the value a Heidenhain compiler writes at a signature position, not a fact about the machine. D158, still open, proposes `[cycles] surface_clearance`, the only precedent for a per-machine cycle fact.
Recommendation: Two optional keys in `[cycles]` of the machine file, named after the NCX quantity rather than after any control's parameter, so that one name serves all three families and the CAM reads one key per quantity: `chip_break_lift`, the distance `CHIP_BREAK` lifts before it feeds on (Fanuc parameter 5114, Heidenhain `Q256`, Siemens `CYCLE83` `_VRT`), and `peck_clearance`, the distance above the depth already reached at which `PECK` ends its rapid re-entry and feeds on (Fanuc parameter 5115, Siemens `CYCLE83` `_DIS1`). The first key is `chip_break_lift` and not `chip_break_retract` because the configuration already uses "retract" twice for other things - the `[retract]` table of the `RETRACT` verb (D83) and the NCX word `CYCLE_RETRACT` for the retract plane - while controller-mapping 5 already calls this quantity the lift amount of `_VRT`; `chip_break_retract` is the alternative if the maintainer prefers the Heidenhain wording (`Q256` is "retract for chip breaking" in heidenhain 5). `peck_clearance` follows D158's `surface_clearance` pattern; `peck_reapproach`, D190's own word, is its alternative. Both a decimal in millimetres, as every length of the machine file is (the `[[axis]]` and `[dynamics]` comments write mm and every shipped file has `units_default = "MM"`), independent of `units_default`, and zero or greater. `[cycles]` is the right table because it already means "what this machine does with cycles" and because D158 proposes `surface_clearance` beside it; naming the keys after native parameters, as the request does, has no precedent in machine-config, where even `[format] external_call` names Fanuc parameter 6030 in its comment and not in its key. The VM reads them in `CycleRules.Drill`: between pecks `CHIP_BREAK` lifts by `chip_break_lift` and feeds back instead of feeding straight on, and `PECK` rapids back only to `peck_clearance` above the depth reached, which is D190's correction made concrete and which moves the estimate measurably (the 122 mm of rapid above is what a non-zero key reduces). A key left out means the control family's documented behaviour, not 0: on Siemens an absent `_VRT` is the manual's 1 mm and an absent `_DIS1` the control's own computation; on Heidenhain the peck re-approach is the cycle's own `Q200`, which in NCX words is the distance between `CLEARANCE` and `SURFACE` (heidenhain 5: `CLEARANCE = Q203 + Q200`), so `peck_clearance` is a key a Heidenhain file never needs and `chip_break_lift` is the one it does; on Fanuc both are parameters whose shipped value NCXchange cannot know, so the VM takes 0 and the runtime report names the key it had to default, as it already says that the estimate falls back to distance over feed without `[dynamics]` (VM 8, verbatim: "Without dynamics in the configuration the estimate falls back to distance over feed and says so") - a report line, not a diagnostic, because a machine file that configures nothing is not in error. A negative value: the loader today range-checks no numeric key at all - `block_time`, `corner_speed` and the `[[axis]] rapid`, `max_feed` and `acceleration` are read with a plain `Number(...)` - so either these two keys are read the same way and a negative value is the existing `CFG005` ("a word outside the values its key takes"), which is the consistent answer, or they become the loader's first numeric range check under the next free loading code `CFG009` (CFG001-CFG099, highest in use CFG008). The consistent answer is recommended; the first range check is a decision of its own and should not ride in on this draft. Shipped files: `heidenhain-itnc530.toml` takes `chip_break_lift = 0.6`, the value `BOHREN.h` writes and the value D164 puts in the catalog; `siemens-840dsl-mill.toml` takes 1.0 and no `peck_clearance`; `fanuc-mill-30i.toml` takes both with a comment naming parameters 5114 and 5115, and the D100 sentence in that file's header, which today names only `[[axis]]`, `[positions]`, `[dynamics]` and the spindle limits, gains `[cycles]` so that the two numbers carry the same "plausible for a machine of this class and not verified" note as every other. No new NCX word: the CAM writes one file for every controller, these numbers differ per machine and are not programmable on Fanuc at all, and D164's answer says outright that the chip-break retract has no NCX word. Alternative: one key for both distances. That is wrong on the control the request starts from, where Fanuc keeps two parameters, and wrong in the shop, where the chip-break lift is a chip-clearing nudge of a few tenths and the peck clearance an air-cut saving of a millimetre or more. Second alternative: the keys in `[dynamics]`, which would keep everything the runtime estimate reads in one table, but puts a cycle geometry into a table of control dynamics and hides it from the compiler side that D358 needs.
Where: machine-config 6 (`[cycles]`, the two keys beside `catalog` and D158's `surface_clearance`); ncx-virtual-machine 3.3 (the `ExpandCycles` sentence, together with D190) and 8 (the runtime report naming a key it had to default); src/Ncx.Core/Machine/CyclesConfig.cs; src/Ncx.Config/MachineConfigLoader.Variables.cs (`s_cyclesKeys` and `ReadCycles`, the `[cycles]` read; MachineConfigLoader.cs:108 only calls it) and, only if the maintainer takes the CFG009 branch, src/Ncx.Config/DiagnosticCodes.Loading.cs with tests/Ncx.Config.Tests/DiagnosticCodesTests.cs; src/Ncx.Core/VirtualMachine/CycleRules.cs (`Drill` and `Pecks`, the D190 TODO(question) at lines 138-144 - row 11 of 03-open-questions.md still says :126, which is now the D189 comment, and rows 9 and 10 are stale in the same way); src/Ncx.Analytics/Runtime/RuntimeAnalytic.Report.cs (the fallback note) and RuntimeEstimator.cs; machines/fanuc-mill-30i.toml (including the D100 sentence of its header, line 4), machines/heidenhain-itnc530.toml, machines/siemens-840dsl-mill.toml; tests/Ncx.Core.Tests/VirtualMachine/CycleCallTests.cs (the `ExpandCycles` cases, which is where the request's "VM trace" test belongs, since `ncx trace` shows state variables and not motions), tests/Ncx.Config.Tests/MachineConfigLoaderTests.cs (the `[cycles]` loading cases) and tests/Ncx.Acceptance/Analytics/RuntimeAnalyticTests.cs; related D158, D164, D190.

ANSWER: (Peter, 2026-10-07, drafted by Claude in project_spike) Accept as recommended: `[cycles] chip_break_lift` and `peck_clearance`, absent means the family's behaviour. The CAM's simulation reads the same keys with the same defaults (opencam D-061).

#### D358 One source for a distance the control holds and the compiler writes
Question: If the machine keys of D357 are adopted, the chip-breaking lift stands in two places at once. D164 recommends the catalog key `defaults`, whose shipped Heidenhain value is `Q256 = 0.6`, and `HeidenhainCycleValues.Unmapped` writes that 0.6 from a literal in the compiler today under the D164 marker (verified: a compile writes `Q256=+0,6`); the machine key would carry the same physical distance for the VM, the runtime estimate and the CAM. On Siemens the disagreement is silent rather than doubled: `SiemensCycles` writes only the positions up to the last with a value, so a `CHIP_BREAK` call comes out as `CYCLE83(2,0,2,-20,,,,,,,,0)` with `_VRT` absent, not empty, and the control applies its own 1 mm (D181); a machine key of 0.6 would then describe a machine whose compiled program lifts 1 mm. On Fanuc neither `G73` nor `G83` has an address for it (cycles/fanuc.toml lines 44-54 map only Z, R, Q, P and F), so nothing can be written and the key is a statement about the control's parameters alone. Nothing in machine-config 6, heidenhain 8 rule 7 or siemens 7 and 12 says which of the two numbers is the source, and the `TODO(question)` of cycles/siemens.toml lines 66-67 records that `_VRT`, `_DTD` and `_DIS1` have no NCX word without saying what the compiler does with them.
Recommendation: One source, and it is the machine key: the machine file states what the machine does, and the compiler writes the native parameter from it wherever the native cycle has one. The Heidenhain compiler writes `Q256` from `chip_break_lift`, so `defaults` in cycles/heidenhain.toml keeps only `Q210`, `Q212` and the `Q208` of D164 and drops `Q256`; the Siemens compiler writes `_VRT` from the same key on `CYCLE83` with `VARI=0` and `_DIS1` from `peck_clearance` where that key is set; the Fanuc compiler writes nothing, because the cycle block has no such address, which is also why R1-06 asks for the key in the first place. One cost to weigh, which is why the alternative below is real: `_VRT` is position 15 of the `CYCLE83` signature and `_DIS1` position 17, and `SiemensCycles` writes positions up to the last with a value, so writing `_VRT` turns every `CYCLE83` call into `CYCLE83(2,0,2,-20,,,,,,,,0,,,0.6)` and writing `_DIS1` adds two more commas - every drilling call in every Siemens program gets longer in exchange for a number the control already has right. A machine file that sets neither key keeps the catalog `defaults` value, so no shipped file changes behaviour the day the keys arrive and D164's 0.6 survives as the Heidenhain default. The reason is the request's own: the VM, the compiled program and the CAM's simulation then answer one question with one number, which two places cannot guarantee. D164's reader side is untouched in substance - the reader still takes the named entry only when the unmapped source values equal what the compiler would write - it merely asks the key before the catalog. Two guards: a machine key set while `defaults` also names the same native parameter is a WARNING of the catalog range, `CFG156` (CFG150-CFG199 is the catalog range, CFG150-CFG155 taken), naming both places so the shop removes one; and a `chip_break_lift` the control cannot accept - an iTNC 530's `Q256` input range starts at 0.1, where the TNC 640's starts at 0 - is a WARNING `CMP120`, the next free code of the Heidenhain compiler's range CMP100-CMP299 (highest in use CMP119), naming the range and the value written instead. Alternative: keep the two apart on purpose, the catalog value for what is written and the machine key for what the VM simulates, with a WARNING wherever they differ. That is honest about the two roles, it avoids the ten empty commas on every Siemens call, and it is the answer to give if the maintainer wants `defaults` to stay a pure compiler table; but it leaves the shop two numbers to keep in step and leaves the Siemens case - an absent position against a key - unresolved, since there is no written value to compare.
Where: machine-config 6 (`defaults`, and which value a compiler writes when a machine key gives the same quantity); controllers/heidenhain.md 5 (the `Q256` and `Q208` line), 7 rule 7 and 8 rule 7; controllers/siemens.md 7 and 12 rule 5; controller-mapping 5 (the `PECK` and `CHIP_BREAK` rows, where `_VRT` is called the retract and the lift amount); cycles/heidenhain.toml (the header TODO(question) at lines 23-24 - row 21 of 03-open-questions.md still says :22 - and the `PECK` and `CHIP_BREAK` entries) and cycles/siemens.toml (the TODO at lines 66-67); src/Ncx.Core/Machine/CycleEntry.cs, which needs a string-valued map for `defaults` because `Fixed` is `IReadOnlyDictionary<string, decimal>` and a default may be the literal `MAX`, and src/Ncx.Config/Cycles/CycleCatalogLoader.Entries.cs (`s_entryKeys`, which has no `defaults` today) with the new `CFG156` in src/Ncx.Config/Cycles/DiagnosticCodes.Cycles.cs and tests/Ncx.Config.Tests/Cycles/CycleDiagnosticCodesTests.cs; src/Ncx.Compilers/Heidenhain/HeidenhainCycleValues.cs (`Unmapped`, the `Q256` case at lines 107-121 and its D164 marker) and src/Ncx.Compilers/DiagnosticCodes.Heidenhain.cs (`CMP120`); src/Ncx.Compilers/Siemens/SiemensCycles.cs (the trailing-position rule at line 484); src/Ncx.Readers/Heidenhain/HeidenhainCycles.cs (`WarnUnmapped`); tests/Ncx.Compilers.Tests and the `BOHREN` round trip of tests/Ncx.Acceptance/RoundTrips.cs; related D164, D181, and D357.

ANSWER: (Peter, 2026-10-07, drafted by Claude in project_spike) Accept as recommended: the machine key is the one source, and the compilers write Q256, _VRT and _DIS1 from it. Code: CMP121, because CMP120 goes to D349.

#### D359 The NCX cycle of a Fanuc G84 without its rigid-tapping line, and the Fanuc entry of the floating tap
Question: D256 settles that the rigid-tapping line belongs to CYCLE=TAP and that a G84 the line reaches in none of its three ways "is tapping with a compensating chuck, another machining than the entry names" (controllers/fanuc.md 9 rule 9, docs/controllers/fanuc.md:140; machine-config 6, the `before` bullet, docs/spec/machine-config.md:347; language 4.7.1, docs/spec/ncx-language.md:216). No section names the NCX cycle of that other machining. The name itself exists on two families: cycles/heidenhain.toml:111 gives cycle 206 the name TAP_COMPENSATING, cycles/siemens.toml:110 gives CYCLE840 the same name, and controller-mapping 5's TAP row and controllers/siemens.md 11 (docs/controllers/siemens.md:116) both call CYCLE840 tapping with a compensating chuck; the name itself stands in no specification section, only in the two catalogs. cycles/fanuc.toml has no entry of that name, so D256 defers the answer to D162 ("once the Fanuc catalog has that entry"), and D162's own recommendation accepts the shipped names without adding a Fanuc entry; the gap is row 193 of ../implementation/03-open-questions.md (file line 422) with the marker at src/Ncx.Readers/Fanuc/FanucCycles.cs:639. Measured on main at f74559c: a Fanuc source whose G84 carries no M29 keeps both cycle blocks as RAW:FANUC with the WARNING RDR001 "G84 without the line \"M29 S{rpm}\" in front of it is not the cycle TAP of the catalog but another machining, which NCX cannot name" plus VM400, so a tapped Fanuc program read by ncx convert compiles for no other family; and CYCLE=TAP_COMPENSATING compiled for machines/fanuc-mill-30i.toml is the ERROR CMP380 "no cycle of the catalog of the machine", while the same block compiles to CYCLE840(5,0,5,-20,,,,,,,1.5) on machines/siemens-840dsl-mill.toml and reports the ERROR CMP104 (Q206 of cycle 206 has no value, D164) on machines/heidenhain-itnc530.toml. Three further things no section gives. First, the two Fanuc tappings share one native code: G84 is already the `native` of TAP, machine-config 6 tells two entries of one native apart only by `fixed` native parameters and by whether `params` cover the block's words (the rule D160 settled), and the presence of a `before` line is neither, so CycleCatalog.FindNative and the mill path of FanucCycles.Start (ModalEntry, the first modal entry of the code) would always return TAP, as would LatheEntry on a Fanuc lathe. Second, a machine whose TAP entry sets `before = ""` (the Fanuc parameter 5200 bit 0 case of D256) would carry two entries that both write a bare G84, and machine-config 6 has no key with which a machine file removes an entry (nothing in the document says remove or delete). Third, a new catalog name gets no rule words: CycleCatalog.Override finds no sibling for a name the built-in family does not carry, and DrillingFamily.Fanuc.cs ties s_fanucTapRuleWords to the entry named TAP, so PITCH, SURFACE, SAFE, CYCLE_RETRACT and AXIS would each be the ERROR CMP385 on the new entry (FanucCycles.CheckCarried), which is D157, still open.
Recommendation: Keep the shared name and coin nothing: TAP_COMPENSATING, as the Heidenhain and Siemens catalogs already write it, is the floating tap on every family, which is D162's rule that one name means one cycle in every catalog, so confirming D162 settles the name. No new NCX word is needed, so the word catalog (src/Ncx.Core/Catalog, docs/spec/generated/word-catalog.md) and the canonical order of D90 are untouched; the whole answer is catalog data and two reading rules. Give cycles/fanuc.toml an entry TAP_COMPENSATING with `native = "G84"`, `modal = true`, no `before` key, and the params of TAP (DEPTH = "Z", CLEARANCE = "R", CYCLE_DWELL = "P", CYCLE_F = "F"); PITCH has no address of its own on Fanuc and follows the same feed rule, F = PITCH times the speed, so answer this together with D157 and let its sentence read "an entry whose native is the tapping code" rather than "the TAP entry", or PITCH, SURFACE, SAFE, CYCLE_RETRACT and AXIS all become CMP385 on the new entry. Extend the "two entries of one native" sentence of machine-config 6 so that the `before` line tells entries apart as `fixed` does, which amends the rule D160 settled and should be written as such: of two entries on one native the reader takes the one whose `before` line reaches the block in one of D256's three ways, and the one with no `before` key where it does not; the compiler writes the entry the program names, with its line or without. Where the TAP entry of a machine sets `before = ""`, the control's G84 is always rigid and that machine has no floating tap, and the answer has to say how the compiler refuses CYCLE=TAP_COMPENSATING there, because CMP380 cannot fire by itself once the catalog holds the entry: CMP380 is "a cycle that the Fanuc cycle catalog of the machine does not name" (src/Ncx.Compilers/Fanuc/DiagnosticCodes.Fanuc.cs:132), so without a rule the compiler would write a bare G84 and that machine would tap rigidly under the name of the other machining, silently. State the rule that an entry with no `before` key counts as not in the machine's catalog where the TAP entry of that machine has `before = ""`, which keeps CMP380 of the Fanuc cycle range (CMP380-CMP399) and needs no removal key, with one sentence of machine-config 6 saying why; the alternative is a removal key in machine-config 6, which would serve more cases but is a new key for one machine nobody has yet. The reader then reads a bare G84 as CYCLE=TAP_COMPENSATING instead of RDR001 RAW, so a Fanuc program tapped with a compensating chuck converts and compiles for every family, which is what language 2 rules 1 and 7 ask of one machining, and the CAM's one NCX file can carry both tappings. Align the two existing entries as D162 asks: the feed half is already done (cycles/heidenhain.toml:114 maps CYCLE_F = "Q206" under D178), so only PITCH is left, and D162's own evidence gives the fact - cycle 206 has no pitch parameter and the Fanuc block has no pitch address, while CYCLE840 takes the pitch only in its encoder or ENC=11 forms - so the one word set of the name is DEPTH, CLEARANCE, SURFACE, SAFE, CYCLE_DWELL, CYCLE_F and AXIS, with PITCH written only where the family has a place for it. Alternative: leave cycles/fanuc.toml as it is and keep the reader's RAW with its reason, naming the gap in controllers/fanuc.md 9 rule 9 and in the known limits of the release (P7-03); the Fanuc family then has one tapping NCX can name, every compensating-chuck tap read from a Fanuc file stays RAW, and no NCX program can tap with a compensating chuck on a Fanuc machine.
Where: language 4.7.1 (the D256 sentence, which names the other machining); machine-config 6 (the `before` bullet, the "two entries of one native" rule of the `fixed` bullet, which D160 settled, and the `before = ""` sentence); controller-mapping 5 (the TAP row and a sentence or row for TAP_COMPENSATING on the three families, where the name stands in no section today); controllers/fanuc.md 6 and 9 rule 9 (its last sentence, which names no cycle today); controllers/siemens.md 11 and heidenhain.md 5 (cited). Data: cycles/fanuc.toml (new entry after line 65, and the comment at lines 62-64), cycles/heidenhain.toml:111-116 and cycles/siemens.toml:110-116 (the aligned word set), cycles/fanuc-lathe.toml and its two TAP entries at lines 51-62 if a lathe takes the entry (D160), cycles/README.md (the name list D162 asks for, which has none today), machines/fanuc-mill-30i.toml:134-146. Code: src/Ncx.Core/Machine/CycleCatalog.cs FindNative (lines 75 and 103) and Override (128), src/Ncx.Core/Machine/CycleEntry.cs (RuleWords 96 and Words 126, with D157), src/Ncx.Core/Machine/DrillingFamily.Fanuc.cs (s_fanucTapRuleWords 15, FanucTapBefore 20); src/Ncx.Readers/Fanuc/FanucCycles.cs Start (530), ModalEntry (687), LatheEntry (the lathe path of the same choice, line 566), WithItsBeforeLine (618) and WithoutItsBeforeLine (649, the TODO(question) at line 639); src/Ncx.Compilers/Fanuc/FanucCycles.cs WriteBefore (287) and CheckCarried (136); src/Ncx.Compilers/Fanuc/DiagnosticCodes.Fanuc.cs (CMP380 at 132, CMP385 at 163). Tests: tests/Ncx.Readers.Tests/Fanuc/FanucCycleTests.cs:76 TapWithoutItsRigidTapLine_IsAnotherMachining_KeepsItsBlocksAsRaw (which this answer replaces), a new Fanuc compiler case in tests/Ncx.Compilers.Tests/Fanuc/FanucCyclesTests.cs that CYCLE=TAP_COMPENSATING is a bare G84 and TAP is not, tests/Ncx.Config.Tests/Cycles/ShippedCatalogsTests.cs (one name, one word set across the catalogs). Row 193 of docs/implementation/03-open-questions.md (file line 422). Related: D162, D157, D160, D164, D256.

#### D360 A Fanuc cycle block whose `before` line the reader cannot see: a called section or a jump target
Question: D256's ANSWER requires the rigid-tapping line "immediately before the cycle block" and controllers/fanuc.md 9 rule 9 names the three ways into the mode, none of which a reader can test where the block that runs before the cycle block is none it sees: a G84 that begins a section an M98 or G65 calls, or one a GOTO enters. VM 3.9 (docs/spec/ncx-virtual-machine.md:200) and controller-mapping 6 (docs/spec/controller-mapping.md:112) give the flow a reader follows but no rule for this case, and the Fanuc rule D256 cites names an S word or an axis motion between M29 and G84 as what alarms PS0203, not a call block, so a source may legally write M29 S500 before the M98 whose subprogram begins with the G84 and the mode is then in force at the cycle. Main keeps such a cycle's blocks as RAW with that reason (src/Ncx.Readers/Fanuc/FanucCycles.cs SeesWhatRunsBefore at line 666 and WithoutItsBeforeLine at 649, the TODO(question) at line 642, row 195 of ../implementation/03-open-questions.md, file line 424). Measured on main at f74559c, for M29 S500 / M98 P200 with O0200 beginning G84 G99 Z-20. R5. F750.: the cycle block becomes RAW:FANUC with the WARNING RDR001 "the reader does not see which block runs before this one, so it cannot tell whether the line \"M29 S{rpm}\" of the cycle TAP stands in front of G84 here" plus VM400, and because D256 took RIGID_TAP out of the [func] tables the M29 line itself becomes RPM=500 MFUNC=29 with the WARNING RDR100 "M29 is no code of the controller or of a table of the machine". So a tapping section that is called - the normal shape of a tapped hole pattern - is lost on both sides of the call and the program compiles for no other family, which is the opposite of what D256 was decided for.
Recommendation: Decide it from the flow, as the control does. The mode is in force at a cycle block when the entry's `before` line stands directly before every block that reaches it: directly before each CALL of the section for a cycle block that begins one, directly before every jump to the label for a block a jump enters, and directly before the block in front of it in the file where the flow also runs through it. The reader then reads the cycle as the entry names it, CYCLE=TAP, and the line is not written again as an M function. Where one of the paths reaches the block without the line, the blocks stay RAW with the reason, as main keeps them. Reason: the reader already knows the callers and the jump targets of the file (src/Ncx.Readers/Fanuc/FanucState.cs Calls line 142, JumpTargets 60, BeforeLineOf 82, CycleBeforeRead 89) and the Fanuc compiler already decides a modal value over the paths to a label and over a call (src/Ncx.Compilers/Fanuc/FanucPaths.cs), so the same path test serves here, it needs no new word, no new key and no new diagnostics code, and it never claims a rigid tap the source did not program, which is the risk the RAW workaround was chosen against; a path NCX cannot walk is already a WARNING of its own under D99 (settled, decisions.md:96), and D195, which would extend that to unreachable blocks inside a subprogram, is still open (rationale.md:666), so this answer must not lean on it. Alternative 1: keep RAW always, as main does, with one sentence in controllers/fanuc.md 9 rule 9 and a line in the known limits of the release (P7-03); safe, but it loses every tapped section that is called and leaves its M29 as an unnamed MFUNC. Alternative 2: read such a block as the entry's cycle whenever any path carries the line, with a WARNING naming the paths that do not; that keeps the program portable but can write the line in front of a block the source left floating. Answer it with the question of which NCX cycle a bare G84 is, since both decide what a G84 without a visible line reads as, but the two can be answered apart: this one names no cycle, and under alternative 1 only the other changes.

#### D361 The builder's rigid-tapping line per machine, and a machine whose two paths use two codes
Question: D256 settles that cycles/fanuc.toml gives TAP `before = "M29 S{rpm}"` and that "a machine file overrides it with its builder's code", and machine-config 6's `before` bullet (docs/spec/machine-config.md:347) names the override verbatim, "Mori Seiki `M329 S{rpm}`". No shipped machine file does it: there is no `[[cycle]]` table with the key anywhere in machines/ or docs/spec/examples/machines/ (the only `[[cycle]]` lines in the library are the two commented PECK_MODE examples of doosan-puma-2600sy.toml:233-234), and machines/mori-ntx1000-mapps.toml:244 with its copy docs/spec/examples/machines/mori-ntx1000-mapps.toml:244 still carries `SYNC_TAP = { ON = "M329" }` in [func], the very shape D256 took away from RIGID_TAP on the standard Fanuc mill; controller-mapping 8 (docs/spec/controller-mapping.md:156) still lists "`M329` synchronous tapping" in the Mori column of the Cycle mode switches row. Because the lathe catalog's TAP entries carry no `before` key of their own (cycles/fanuc-lathe.toml has none) they inherit the built-in family's line through CycleEntry.OverriddenBy, so every Fanuc-family machine of the library writes M29. Measured on main at f74559c: CYCLE=TAP SURFACE=0 CLEARANCE=5 DEPTH=-20 PITCH=1.5 compiles for machines/nakamura-ntjx.toml to "M29 S500 / G84 Y-20. R5. F750." and for machines/doosan-puma-2600sy.toml to "N70 M29 S500 / N80 G84 Y-20. R5. F750.", with no diagnostic. So on the Mori Seiki, whose control switches the mode with M329, CYCLE=TAP writes a code that control does not use for rigid tapping, and the right code is reachable only by writing FUNC:SYNC_TAP=ON - the per-machine function R1-07 asks to abolish and D256 abolished for the mill. D256's evidence adds a case no key reaches at all: on the Nakamura "M29 is rigid tapping on the upper path and M429 on the lower path", one machine with two values of one key, and machine-config 6 has no per-channel form for an entry key, although machine-config 5 already gives a function table the key `channel` for exactly this (docs/spec/machine-config.md:216, D56). M429 stands in no file of the repository. Nothing records any of this: no entry of rationale.md names it, docs/implementation/03-open-questions.md has no row for it, and SYNC_TAP appears in no document.
Recommendation: Separate the data from the rule. The data needs no decision, because D256's ANSWER already names the codes from the manuals: give machines/mori-ntx1000-mapps.toml and its copy a `[[cycle]] name = "TAP" before = "M329 S{rpm}"` table and take SYNC_TAP out of [func], exactly as RIGID_TAP left machines/fanuc-mill-30i.toml, with the same kind of comment citing D256; the Doosan and the Nakamura upper path keep the catalog's M29, so their files need nothing beyond the comment they already carry at :215 and :241. controller-mapping 8's Mori column then cites the `before` key instead of listing M329 as a cycle mode switch, as the Fanuc column no longer lists M29, and controllers/fanuc.md 9 rule 9 gains one sentence that the line is the machine's, not the catalog's. What needs an answer is the Nakamura: let the `[[cycle]]` override of machine-config 6 take the key `channel`, which machine-config 5 already defines for a function table (D56), so that the file writes `[[cycle]] name = "TAP" channel = 2 before = "M429 S{rpm}"` beside the channel-less table and the loader picks the table of the compiling channel, falling back to the channel-less one. Reason: the code differs per path as a fact of the control, the machine file is where what differs between machines and their channels stands, the key already exists under that name for functions so nothing new is invented, and a function would bring back exactly what D256 removed. Alternative: no per-channel key, and the lower path's rigid tapping is a stated known limit of the release (P7-03), with a WARNING from the Fanuc compiler where a program taps on a channel whose builder code the file cannot give; simpler, but it keeps writing M29 on a path the control does not accept it on, which is the silent wrong code this draft is about. Either way the answer should say what a compiler does for a Fanuc-family machine whose builder code is unknown, since writing the catalog default is what makes the fault silent today.
Where: machine-config 6 (the `before` bullet and the `[[cycle]]` override, plus the new `channel` key, pointing at the same key of machine-config 5, D56); machine-config 5 (the `channel` key of a function table, cited, docs/spec/machine-config.md:216); controller-mapping 8 (the Cycle mode switches row, docs/spec/controller-mapping.md:156, Mori column); controllers/fanuc.md 9 rule 9 and 10 rule 7 (one sentence that the line is the machine's).
