#### D362 A cycle word the native cycle has no parameter for
Question: Machine-config 6 says what `params`, `signature`, `fixed`, `before` and `for_axis` do and that a native name in `params` the signature does not list is an address word of its own, but it does not say what a compiler writes for an NCX cycle word that the entry maps to no native parameter and that no rule word carries (D157). Language 2 rule 8 is written for the reader - "Source that NCX cannot express is kept as `RAW` with a warning, so nothing disappears silently" - and its own remedy is a WARNING, so it does not settle the compile direction, and the three compilers have answered differently: the Heidenhain compiler writes nothing and reports the WARNING CMP105 (`HeidenhainCycles.WarnUnwritten`), the Siemens compiler the ERROR CMP571 (`SiemensCycles.Fill`) and the Fanuc compiler the ERROR CMP385 (`FanucCycles.CheckCarried`), all three citing rule 8 for the opposite severity. The case is now real on the tapping cycle: `TAP` is rigid tapping on every controller (D194, D256), and D181's answer settles that `CYCLE84` taps with G331/G332 at the speeds SST and SST1 and uses no programmed feed, so `CYCLE_F` stays unmapped on the Siemens `TAP` as it already is on the Heidenhain `TAP`, whose cycle 207 has neither Q206 nor Q211 (D178). `tests/Ncx.Acceptance/Expected/BOHREN.ncx:323` writes `CYCLE=TAP SURFACE=0 CLEARANCE=5 DEPTH=-20 CYCLE_RETRACT=CLEARANCE CYCLE_F=750 CYCLE_DWELL=0 PITCH=1.5`, which is what a CAM writing one file for every controller writes: on `machines/heidenhain-itnc530.toml` it compiles with two CMP105 WARNINGs, on `machines/fanuc-mill-30i.toml` as `M29 S500` plus `G84 ... F750`, and on `machines/siemens-840dsl-mill.toml` it is CMP571 at every `CYCLE_CALL` block and no file is written at all. One NCX file therefore cannot carry a tap. Three things are open here, not one. First, which severity such a word gets. Second, whether a value the control reaches anyway is treated apart from a value that is lost: of the two WARNINGs the Heidenhain tap reports today, `CYCLE_F=750` is derivable (cycle 207 taps from Q239), while `CYCLE_DWELL=0` is derivable from nothing - it is inert, because cycle 207 has no dwell at all and 0 asks for none, and a `CYCLE_DWELL=5` on the same entry would be genuinely lost. So that branch follows from the value, not from `params`, and the compiler's own comment (`HeidenhainCycles.cs` lines 203-205) already lumps the two together. Third, where the diagnostic lands: the Heidenhain WARNING stands once at the `CYCLE` block, while the Siemens ERROR repeats at every `CYCLE_CALL` - `BOHREN` gives five CMP571 for the one `TAP` definition and ten more for the two `CYCLE83` definitions. D279 asks the neighbouring question for a `CYCLE:<controller>=n` block, and its proposed answer states the opposite rule for it ("A cycle word that nothing maps is a CMP ERROR and is never dropped"), so the two have to be answered together.
Recommendation: One rule for the three families, in machine-config 6 after the key list and in controller-mapping 5 under the table, in three branches. A cycle word that the entry maps to no native parameter and that no rule word carries is not written; it is a WARNING where the native cycle reaches the same value itself from another word of the block; it is dropped with no diagnostic where the value is the behaviour the control has anyway (`CYCLE_DWELL=0`, `PECK=0` on a cycle without that motion); and it is the ERROR each compiler reports today where the value is lost. The first branch follows from `params`, so no new catalog key is needed, exactly as D157 derives the rule words: a drilling entry that maps `PITCH` to a native parameter and maps no `CYCLE_F` takes the tapping feed from the pitch itself. That covers the Heidenhain `TAP` (cycle 207 from Q239), the Siemens `TAP` (CYCLE84 from PIT with SST and SST1) and, once D181 takes `CYCLE_F = "F"` off it, the Siemens `TAP_COMPENSATING` (CYCLE840 computes the feed from pitch and speed for every ENC but 1), while the Fanuc `TAP` maps `CYCLE_F` to `F` and is untouched. The second branch cannot be read off `params` and is what keeps the `CYCLE_DWELL=0` of the one CAM file from becoming an ERROR on the iTNC 530: today it is a CMP105 WARNING, so `ncx compile --strict` already exits 1 on every Heidenhain tap of a program that writes the full word set, which is R1-09's "--strict passes on a CAM reference program" test. The codes: the Heidenhain CMP105 keeps its text for the first branch, and the third branch needs a Heidenhain ERROR the compiler does not have - either the generic CMP101, "a word of the block has no Klartext form in the Heidenhain compiler, and nothing is written for it", or, better beside CMP103, CMP104 and CMP105, a cycle code of its own at CMP120, the next free in the Heidenhain range CMP100 to CMP299. The Siemens compiler needs a WARNING of its own beside CMP571 in the cycle range of `DiagnosticCodes.Siemens.cs` (CMP570 to CMP589, of which CMP574 is the next free). The Fanuc CMP385 stays for every other word, and Fanuc needs no WARNING today, because every Fanuc entry that derives a value carries it as a rule word. Every one of these stands once at the `CYCLE` block, as CMP105 does, and not again at each `CYCLE_CALL`, which also takes the Siemens report down from five per definition to one. Each message names the word, the native cycle and where the control takes the value from instead, so the setup sheet can show the feed the control will really tap at. `PECK` of a Siemens `CYCLE83` is untouched and stays CMP571, because nothing maps it and nothing computes it, until D181 maps it to FDPR with `_DAM = 0`. A `CYCLE:<controller>=n` block has no `params` to derive from, so D279's ERROR stands there unchanged; this rule is for catalog and built-in entries only, and that sentence belongs in both drafts, so that answering one does not quietly reverse the other. Reason: the feed of a rigid tap is not the CAM's to give - the control derives it from the pitch and the spindle speed, and NCX already does the same on Fanuc, where a `TAP` without `CYCLE_F` feeds with `PITCH x S` per minute or `PITCH` per revolution (controller-mapping 5, TAP; `FanucCycles.PitchFeed`). So the one NCX file needs only `CYCLE=TAP ... PITCH=1.5`, and where a program carries a `CYCLE_F` anyway, two controls of three cannot use it: that is a WARNING, not a program NCXchange refuses. Alternative: keep one strict rule, make every unmapped cycle word the ERROR that Fanuc and Siemens report, tighten the Heidenhain CMP105 to an ERROR as well, and write into controller-mapping 5 that a `TAP` carries `PITCH` and no `CYCLE_F`. That is the smaller change to the compilers and the stronger guarantee that no feed is quietly ignored, but it rejects a program the Fanuc control runs, gives up a WARNING the Heidenhain compiler already has, and forces a CAM to write a different word set per controller for the tap, which is what opencam's one-file rule rules out - and without the inert branch it breaks the `BOHREN` round trip of `tests/Ncx.Acceptance`, whose tap carries `CYCLE_DWELL=0`, so the inert branch should be kept whatever the other two become.
Where: `docs/spec/machine-config.md` 6 (after the key list, which ends with `for_axis`, not `fixed`); `docs/spec/controller-mapping.md` 5 (the `CYCLE_F`, `CYCLE_DWELL` row and the `TAP` row); `docs/controllers/siemens.md` 7 and 12 rule 5; `docs/controllers/heidenhain.md` 5; `docs/controllers/fanuc.md` 6; `cycles/siemens.toml` (the `TAP` entry and its `TODO(question)` at line 77), `cycles/heidenhain.toml` (the comment at line 70); `src/Ncx.Core/Machine/CycleEntry.cs` (`RuleWords`, `CycleF`, the derived held word), `src/Ncx.Core/Machine/DrillingFamily.Siemens.cs` (`SiemensTapParams`, the marker at lines 125-126); `src/Ncx.Compilers/Siemens/SiemensCycles.cs` `Fill` (the `TODO(question)` at line 306) and `src/Ncx.Compilers/DiagnosticCodes.Siemens.cs` (the new WARNING beside CMP571, CMP574 free); `src/Ncx.Compilers/Heidenhain/HeidenhainCycles.cs` `WarnUnwritten` (line 207) and its comment at lines 203-205, and `src/Ncx.Compilers/DiagnosticCodes.Heidenhain.cs` (the lost-value ERROR: CMP101 or a new CMP120); `src/Ncx.Compilers/Fanuc/FanucCycles.cs` `CheckCarried`; tests: `tests/Ncx.Compilers.Tests/Siemens/SiemensCycleTests.cs`, `tests/Ncx.Compilers.Tests/Heidenhain/HeidenhainCycleTests.cs`, `tests/Ncx.Config.Tests/Cycles/ShippedCatalogsTests.cs` and the `BOHREN` round trip of `tests/Ncx.Acceptance`; related D157, D178, D181, D194, D256, D279.

ANSWER: (Peter, 2026-10-07, drafted by Claude in project_spike) Accept as recommended: derivable value a WARNING, inert value silent, lost value an ERROR; `TAP` needs only `PITCH`. Code for the Heidenhain lost-value ERROR: CMP101 if that code already means exactly this, otherwise CMP122 (CMP120 is D349's, CMP121 D358's).

#### D363 The allowance for rounding to the machine's decimals
Question: Language 2 rule 5 says NCX never rounds and the compiler applies the number format of the target machine; machine-config 2 gives `[format] decimals` per address; and P3-03 made a value with more decimals than its address takes a value rounded half away from zero with the WARNING CMP020 (`NumberFormatter.Format`). No document says that this rounding is the normal case rather than a fault, and nothing bounds how far it may move a point. A CAM that writes every coordinate at one fine resolution, the six decimals of D121, therefore collects a CMP020 on nearly every block of a three-decimal machine file, and `--strict` exits 1 (`ExitCodes.OfRun`) on a file that is correct: a probe of five blocks at six decimals against machines/fanuc-mill-30i.toml gives six warnings and exit 1, and the same file at four decimals gives none. The compilers already disagree about the same value. The program's own `CENTER` word is written through `Format` and warns on Heidenhain (`HeidenhainArcs.WritePole` through `HeidenhainNumbers.Signed`) and on Siemens (`SiemensArcs.WriteCenter` through `Scaled` and `write.Format`), while the Fanuc `I`/`J` is a computed offset through `FanucBlock.FormatComputed` and never warns: the same arc block gives two CMP020 on the Fanuc mill and four on the iTNC 530 and the 840D sl. What is open is the rule, not the arithmetic: whether rounding reports at all, and against what. The client states a budget per operation, a tenth of its path tolerance, and expects NCXchange to report only where the machine's grid cannot hold it. Case: on a three-decimal machine a block whose X, Y and Z each sit on a midpoint (15.0175) writes 15.018 on each axis and moves the programmed point by 0.00087 mm, which is inside a budget of 0.001 mm and outside one of 0.0005 mm; no single value moves by more than 0.0005, so a comparison per value can never see the difference the budget is about.
Recommendation: Rounding a number the program wrote to the decimals of its address is normal, silent compiler behaviour: CMP020 goes, and its number is not reused, as VM904's was not (D118, D98). The program states its allowance in a new modal word `ROUND_LIMIT=0.001`, a number in the active units or an expression, or `OFF`, with the optional address `ROUND_LIMIT:ROTARY=0.01` in degrees for the rotary axes and the angle addresses, exactly as `TOLERANCE` carries `TOLERANCE:ROTARY` (one word with an `AddrRanks` entry, as `FileWords.cs` builds TOLERANCE); `ROUND_LIMIT:ROTARY` without an active `ROUND_LIMIT` is the same ERROR as `TOLERANCE:ROTARY` without `TOLERANCE` (VM 5), raised where `FrameValidation.CheckToleranceWords` raises that one. The quantity checked is the point, not the value: the distance between the tool's programmed point as the block gives it and the point the written file produces, over the linear axes of the block; above the allowance the compiler reports the WARNING CMP023, RoundingBeyondTheLimit, in the CMP020-CMP029 range of the numbers and lines of the output, with the block, the deviation and the address whose decimals caused it. Without `ROUND_LIMIT` nothing is reported for rounding at all. Ranks: `ROUND_LIMIT` 813 and `ROUND_LIMIT:ROTARY` 816, inside the 811-819 gap after `TOLERANCE_MODE` (810) and before `CYCLE` (820), at the end of bucket 12 of language 5 rule 6; `CanonicalRanks.cs` says the ranks go in steps of ten so that a later word fits between two others without renumbering, and two words need the room spaced, so 813 and 816 rather than two adjacent numbers; the alternative, if the maintainer wants the step of ten kept, is 820 and 830 with bucket 13 renumbered from 840 up, one mechanical change to the file and to `docs/spec/generated/word-catalog.md`. Scope modal, state only, read by the compiler, with no control form, so nothing is written through for it (unlike the tolerance row of VM 2, which the compiler does write through) and controller-mapping 1 records the dash beside the `TOLERANCE` row. Reasons: the point is what a tolerance budget is about, a check per value cannot see the worst case, and a WARNING lets the CAM's CI fail under `--strict` exactly where the machine cannot hold the accuracy the operation asked for, which is the client's own contract. Alternative: no word, and CMP020 stays but as an INFO counted once per program, which makes `--strict` usable again and never tells the CAM that the machine is too coarse. Second alternative: compare per value against the limit, simpler and silent in the case above. On the name: D58 (settled 2026-09-11, "chamfers and roundings are expanded by readers; no words for now") floated `CHAMFER=` and `ROUND=` as words to add once hand authoring shows the need, and NCX's prefix convention (`TOLERANCE`/`TOLERANCE_MODE`, `CYCLE`/`CYCLE_F`, `SPINDLE`/`SPINDLE_MODE`) makes `X_Y` read as a modifier of `X`, so `ROUND_LIMIT` would read as the limit of a corner radius; since D58 reserved no spelling, the cheap fix is to call that later word `CORNER=` beside `CHAMFER=` when it is ever added, and keep `ROUND_LIMIT`; otherwise this word is `ROUND_TOLERANCE`.
Where: Language 4.1 (a row after `TOLERANCE_MODE`, where the tolerance words stand), 5 rule 6 bucket 12 (append `ROUND_LIMIT`, `ROUND_LIMIT:ROTARY`), 4.3 (the chamfer sentence, if the later corner word is named `CORNER=`); VM 2 (the state table, the row next to tolerance, line 44) and VM 5 (the ERROR list, next to "`TOLERANCE:ROTARY` or `TOLERANCE_MODE` without an active `TOLERANCE`"); machine-config 2 (one paragraph after the `[format]` block: rounding to the decimals is silent and the allowance is a word of the program); controller-mapping 1 (a row with no control form); D58 (the corner words), D98 and D118 (a retired code is not reused). Code: src/Ncx.Core/Catalog/FileWords.cs (the word, beside TOLERANCE, Section "4.1" - not FrameWords.cs, which does not hold the tolerance words), src/Ncx.Core/Catalog/CanonicalRanks.cs (813, 816), src/Ncx.Core/Catalog/AddrKind.cs and WordCheck.cs (the address kind, as `ToleranceKind`); src/Ncx.Core/VirtualMachine/State/ToleranceState.cs (a RoundLimitState beside it), FrameState.cs, FrameSnapshot.cs, src/Ncx.Core/VirtualMachine/Handlers/FrameHandlers.cs (next to ApplyTolerance, line 215), src/Ncx.Core/VirtualMachine/Validation/FrameValidation.cs (CheckToleranceWords, DiagnosticCodes.ToleranceWordWithoutTolerance); src/Ncx.Compilers/NumberFormatter.cs (the CMP020 branch of Format), src/Ncx.Compilers/DiagnosticCodes.cs (CMP020 retired, CMP023 added), src/Ncx.Compilers/Fanuc/FanucBlock.cs and src/Ncx.Compilers/Siemens/SiemensBlock.cs FormatComputed, src/Ncx.Compilers/Heidenhain/HeidenhainNumbers.cs Signed. Tests: tests/Ncx.Compilers.Tests/NumberFormatterTests.cs (Format_MoreDecimalsThanTheMachineTakes_IsRoundedWithCmp020 and the fits-the-machine case), tests/Ncx.Compilers.Tests/DiagnosticCodesTests.cs, tests/Ncx.Core.Tests/Catalog/WordCatalogTests.cs and CanonicalOrderTests.cs with docs/spec/generated/word-catalog.md (regenerated by tests/Ncx.Core.Tests/Catalog/WordCatalogTableTests.cs, P0-03), tests/Ncx.Core.Tests/Parsing/BlockRulesTests.cs (P0-04), and a new acceptance test under tests/Ncx.Acceptance/Examples that compiles a CAM reference program with `--strict`.

ANSWER: (Peter, 2026-10-07, drafted by Claude in project_spike) Accept as recommended, with the name `ROUND_LIMIT` and the ranks 813 and 816; a later corner word is called `CORNER=`. Rounding to the address's decimals is silent; CMP020 is retired; CMP023 reports a point moved beyond `ROUND_LIMIT`. Ties are rounded half away from zero on the decimal value as written in the NCX (15.0175 becomes 15.018), not on the binary double. The CAM writes `ROUND_LIMIT` per operation as its rounding allowance, 0.1·tol (opencam D-149), and `ROUND_LIMIT:ROTARY` only for programs with rotary axes, which release 1 has none of.

#### D364 The centre of an arc whose end points the machine rounds
Question: The three compilers write an arc's end point and its centre through the number format independently of each other, and two different centres reach them. Where the block carries `CENTER`, Heidenhain and Siemens write the program's own value: `HeidenhainArcs.WritePole` writes CC through `HeidenhainNumbers.Signed`, `SiemensArcs.WriteCenter` writes `I=AC()`/`J=AC()` through `Scaled` and `write.Format`, each rounded to the decimals of the plane address with a CMP020. Fanuc instead writes a computed offset: `FanucArcs.Offset` is `FormatComputed(address, motion.Center - motion.From)`, and `motion.Center` is not the block's exact centre - `MotionEvents` has already rounded it with `Vec3.RoundToDecimal(arc.Arc.Center.X, MotionRules.PositionDecimals(units))`, three decimals in MM and four in INCH whatever the machine takes. For the R and turn forms every family writes that same pre-rounded centre silently (`SiemensArcs.AbsoluteCenterWords`, `HeidenhainArcs.WriteComputedPole`, `FanucArcs.WriteTurns`). Nothing reconciles any of this with the written end point, so the radius the control measures from the written start to the written centre can differ from the one it measures to the written end. Every control checks that difference and alarms: Fanuc against parameter 3410 (PS0020; the parameter page and the alarm are the manual evidence of D139, and D241 cites the same alarm), Heidenhain against circleDeviation (200901, iTNC 530 MP 7431, input range 0.0001 to 0.016 mm, default 0.005 mm), Siemens against MD21000 CIRCLE_ERROR_CONST and MD21010 CIRCLE_ERROR_FACTOR (alarm 14040) - all three cited in D139's answer. Machine-config names no key for any of them, and the key D139 proposes, `[machine] arc_tolerance`, is NCX's own tolerance for resolving an inconsistent CENTER it reads (D36, VM 3.2), not the target control's limit; D139's own answer notes that one number cannot carry the Siemens pair. What is open is whether the compiler may move a centre so that the two radii agree, since a CENTER the program wrote is a number of the program that language 2 rule 5 has the compiler format and not change, and what it reports when it cannot. Case from main, not invented: `ARC=CCW X=15.0175 Y=25.0175 CENTER:X=15.0175 CENTER:Y=15.0175` from X=25.0175 Y=15.0175, exact centre offset (-10, 0), compiles against machines/fanuc-mill-30i.toml to `G3 X15.018 Y25.018 I-10. J0.001` and against the same file at four decimals to `G3 X15.0175 Y25.0175 I-9.9995 J0.0005` - in both the written centre sits 0.0005 to 0.0007 from the programmed one, the two radii differ by 0.001 and 0.0005, and nothing is reported. The same block on the iTNC 530 and the 840D sl writes the centre right, at 15.001 and 15.001, and reports CMP020 twice.
Recommendation: First, the compiler must be given the exact centre: `MotionEvents` keeps the resolved centre at the VM's own precision (six decimals once D121 is confirmed) and not at a figure that imitates a machine's decimals, because a grid search cannot start from a point already quantised to the grid. Then the compiler writes the end point, rounded as every coordinate is, and chooses the centre: among the points of the output grid of the centre's own written form - the absolute CC and `I=AC()`/`J=AC()` on the grid of the plane addresses, the incremental Fanuc `I` and `J` on the grid of the offset from the written start - it takes the one that makes the radius from the written start and the radius to the written end agree best, and among equal candidates the one nearest the exact centre. The search is the nine candidates one step around the rounded centre, which is enough because no better point lies further than one step in either axis. The remaining difference is reported as the WARNING CMP030, ArcRadiusDifferenceBeyondTheMachine, when it exceeds the new key `[machine] arc_radius_tolerance`, a length in millimetres like `rapid`, `max_feed` and `acceleration` (machine-config 4) and like the `arc_tolerance` of D139, converted for an INCH program; without the key the limit is one output step of the centre's address, so a machine file that says nothing reports only where the grid itself cannot do better. Reasons: the control, not NCX, decides whether the file runs, and only the written numbers reach it; moving a written CENTER inside its own rounding step changes no number of the program further than rounding already does, which is why the permission is stated in the specification instead of being left to each compiler. Alternative: leave the centre where plain rounding puts it and only report the difference, which keeps rule 5 untouched but hands the operator an alarm the compiler could have avoided. On the key, the real choice is whether D139's `arc_tolerance` serves both sides: that saves a key but ties NCX's reading tolerance to the target control's alarm limit, and it still cannot carry the Siemens constant and factor, so where a Siemens machine needs both the key takes the form `arc_radius_tolerance = { const = 0.01, factor = 0.001 }`, which is a later decision and not this one.
Where: machine-config 1 (the new `[machine]` key, beside the place D139 puts `arc_tolerance`) and 4 (the unit, as for rapid and acceleration); language 4.3 (one sentence under CENTER: the compiler may place a written centre on the output grid so that the radii agree); VM 3.2 (the stored computed centre keeps the VM's precision, with D121); controllers/fanuc.md 4, heidenhain.md 2, siemens.md 3 (the arc paragraphs); D139, D36, D241, D121. Code: a new shared helper src/Ncx.Compilers/ArcOnTheGrid.cs next to src/Ncx.Compilers/NumberFormatter.cs; src/Ncx.Core/VirtualMachine/Events/MotionEvents.cs (lines 91-98, the centre's stored decimals) and src/Ncx.Core/VirtualMachine/MotionRules.cs PositionDecimals; src/Ncx.Compilers/Fanuc/FanucArcs.cs (CentreOffset, Offset, WriteTurns), src/Ncx.Compilers/Siemens/SiemensArcs.cs (WriteCenter, AbsoluteCenterWords), src/Ncx.Compilers/Heidenhain/HeidenhainArcs.cs (WritePole, WriteComputedPole); src/Ncx.Core/Machine/MachineIdentity.cs and src/Ncx.Config/MachineConfigLoader.Identity.cs for the key, src/Ncx.Config/DefaultMachine.cs; src/Ncx.Compilers/DiagnosticCodes.cs (CMP030, with a new sub-range line for the geometry the compiler resolves). Machine files: machines/*.toml and docs/spec/examples/machines/*.toml. Tests: tests/Ncx.Compilers.Tests/Fanuc/FanucMotionTests.cs, Heidenhain/HeidenhainMotionTests.cs, Siemens/SiemensMotionTests.cs, a new case for the grid search, and tests/Ncx.Config.Tests for the key.

ANSWER: (Peter, 2026-10-07, drafted by Claude in project_spike) Accept as recommended: the VM keeps the resolved centre at its own precision (six decimals, with D121), the compiler picks the best of the nine grid centres, and CMP030 with `[machine] arc_radius_tolerance` reports what remains. This draft keeps CMP030.

#### D365 End points the control computes from the written words
Question: Two of the three compilers write arc forms whose end point in the plane the control works out for itself. D268 settles that a Klartext helix is CC plus CP IPA with the incremental tool-axis travel, and `HeidenhainArcs.WriteHelix` marks the plane axis words as written without writing them (`MarkPlaneWords`), so the iTNC 530 computes the end from the rounded pole, the current radius and the rounded sweep. `SiemensArcs.WriteSweep` writes the centre and `AR=` for a sweep below one turn, and the 840D computes the end from those (controller-mapping 2, ANGLE: `AR=angle` goes with I J K or with the end point). Nothing checks that the point the control reaches is the point the block gave: the pole, the radius and the sweep are each rounded on their own, and the sweep is subject to no decimals limit at all today, because `Format("IPA", ...)` and `Format("ANGLE", ...)` find no key in `[format] decimals` and so write every digit the value has. Neither heidenhain.md 2 and 8 rule 4, nor siemens.md 3 and 12 rule 2, nor controller-mapping 2 says what the compiler owes the end point in such a form. Case from main: a helix of radius 2 about a pole at X10.0005 with the sweep 137.956213 compiles against machines/heidenhain-itnc530.toml to `6 CC X+10,001 Y+10` and `7 CP IPA+137,956213 IZ-5 DR+`, and against machines/siemens-840dsl-mill.toml to `N80 G3 Z=IC(-5) I=AC(10.001) J=AC(10) AR=137.956213`. The pole moved by 0.0005, so the end the control computes lies 0.0005 from the end the NCX block gave while IZ is exact; the sweep is written finer than either control reads; and the next block starts from where the control actually stands, so the error does not cancel.
Recommendation: A compiler that writes a form whose end point the control computes must compute the same point from the words it is about to write and compare it with the end point of the block, rounded to the output decimals. Inside the allowance of `ROUND_LIMIT` — half an output step per axis where the program states none — the form stands. Outside it the compiler first uses the levers it has: more decimals on the angle address where `[format] decimals` allows them, and on Siemens the other legal form, the end point with the centre, which controller-mapping 2 and siemens.md 3 both record as equally valid. Where no form holds the point, it writes the form it has and reports the WARNING CMP031, ComputedEndPointBeyondTheLimit, naming the point the control will reach, the deviation and the words that produce it. On Heidenhain a helix has no second form, since D268 makes CP IPA the only one, so there the lever is the decimals alone and the report is the end of it. Reasons: the control's own arithmetic is what cuts the part, the operator cannot see the deviation in the written numbers, and a computed end is consistent with the words that produced it, so no arc-radius alarm catches it; a report is the least NCXchange owes under the client's rule that NCXchange reports what a machine cannot do. Alternative: give the computed end no check, and accept that a helix whose pole moved by rounding ends up to one output step from the programmed point, with the next block starting from there — which is what main does today and what the probe above shows.
Where: controllers/heidenhain.md 2 and 8 rule 4, siemens.md 3 and 12 rule 2, controller-mapping 2 (the CENTER and ANGLE rows, the paragraph under the table); D268, D84. Code: src/Ncx.Compilers/Heidenhain/HeidenhainArcs.cs (WriteHelix, MarkPlaneWords, the Format("IPA", ...) calls at lines 101 and 295), src/Ncx.Compilers/Siemens/SiemensArcs.cs (WriteSweep, the `AR=` branch at line 80), the check beside the shared helper of the arc-centre draft; src/Ncx.Compilers/DiagnosticCodes.cs (CMP031). Tests: tests/Ncx.Compilers.Tests/Heidenhain/HeidenhainMotionTests.cs (the helix cases), tests/Ncx.Compilers.Tests/Siemens/SiemensMotionTests.cs (the `AR=` cases), and tests/Ncx.Acceptance/RoundTrips.cs for a helix and an `AR=` arc read back within half an output step of the rounded end point.

ANSWER: (Peter, 2026-10-07, drafted by Claude in project_spike) Accept with one change to the target. The compiler checks every end point the control computes and uses its levers (more decimals on the angle address where the machine allows them, on Siemens the end point form) whenever the computed end lies more than half an output step from the rounded end point of the block, as opencam D-149 asks; the report threshold stays `ROUND_LIMIT`. So: aim for half an output step, report CMP031 only beyond `ROUND_LIMIT` (or beyond half a step where the program states none). This draft keeps CMP031.

#### D366 Decimals of the angle addresses the compilers write
Question: `[format] decimals` of machine-config 2 is a table per address, and its example names X, Y, Z, A, C, F and S. The compilers also write angles that are no axis: `HeidenhainArcs` passes the address `IPA` for the polar sweep of CC plus CP (two calls, lines 101 and 295), `SiemensArcs` passes `ANGLE` for `AR=` (line 80). No machine file names either key, so `NumberFormatter.DecimalsOf` returns null, nothing is rounded and nothing is reported — `HeidenhainNumbers.Signed` says so in its own documentation, "any other takes the number as it is". Probe: a sweep of 137.956213 reaches a Klartext block as `CP IPA+137,956213` and a SINUMERIK block as `AR=137.956213`, finer than either control reads, while every coordinate of the same program is written at three. Machine-config 2 also does not say what an address the table leaves out gets: the three shipped mill files declare only three linear axes, so no rotary coordinate can be written against them today, but a five-axis mill file, or the TNC 640 file still to come, would write its A, B or C the same unrounded way, and `MotionRules.PositionDecimals` quantises nothing but the coordinates it stores. D263 settles the defaults of the other `[format]` keys and sets the policy that a key left out takes the value its controller chapter fixes, but it does not touch `decimals`.
Recommendation: One NCX address carries the sweep: `ANGLE`, the NCX word, following P3-03's rule that a family passes the address whose decimals apply (a Fanuc `I` passes `X`). `[format] decimals` gains `ANGLE` in the machine-config 2 example and in the shipped machine files, the Heidenhain compiler passes `ANGLE` where it now passes `IPA`, and a rotary axis keeps its own letter. Without the key the address takes three decimals on every family: that is what heidenhain.md 2 writes in its own example, `CP IPA+737.956 IZ-5.4 DR+`, and what Siemens' default computing resolution of 1000 increments per degree gives (MD10210 INT_INCR_PER_DEG, the manual evidence of D121); so a sweep is always rounded, and its rounding falls under the allowance of the `ROUND_LIMIT` draft instead of being written out in full. Reasons: one address per quantity keeps the machine file short and the compilers already map a native address onto an NCX one; and an angle written finer than the control reads is a number the control rounds itself, out of NCXchange's sight, which defeats the check on the end points the control computes. Alternative, which answers the second half as well: an address that `[format] decimals` does not name takes the decimals of `X`, one rule for every missing key, which also makes a future five-axis file's missing A, B and C safe; it ties an angle to a length, wrong in principle but never wrong by more than the one digit the three families differ by. Second alternative: four decimals on Heidenhain, whose input resolution for rotary axes is 0.0001 degree (D121's evidence), and three on the others, which is the per-family shape D263 chose for the other keys.
Where: machine-config 2 (the `decimals` line of the `[format]` example, and one sentence on an address the table leaves out); language 4.3 (ANGLE, a pointer to the written decimals); controllers/heidenhain.md 2, siemens.md 3; D263 (the sibling policy for the other `[format]` keys), D121 (the VM's own precision and MotionEvents.SweepDecimals). Code: src/Ncx.Compilers/NumberFormatter.cs (DecimalsOf and its documentation), src/Ncx.Compilers/Heidenhain/HeidenhainArcs.cs (the two `Numbers.Format("IPA", ...)` calls at lines 101 and 295), src/Ncx.Compilers/Siemens/SiemensArcs.cs (`write.Format("ANGLE", sweep)` at line 80), src/Ncx.Compilers/Heidenhain/HeidenhainNumbers.cs (the doc comment on Signed). Machine files: machines/heidenhain-itnc530.toml, machines/siemens-840dsl-mill.toml and machines/fanuc-mill-30i.toml (these three have no copy under docs/spec/examples/machines, which holds only the five lathe files). Tests: tests/Ncx.Compilers.Tests/NumberFormatterTests.cs, Heidenhain/HeidenhainMotionTests.cs, Siemens/SiemensMotionTests.cs, tests/Ncx.Acceptance/Examples/ExampleFormatTests.cs.

ANSWER: (Peter, 2026-10-07, drafted by Claude in project_spike) Accept `ANGLE` as the one address of the sweep, with one change to the default. No address is ever written with all its digits: an address the `[format] decimals` table leaves out takes a default, per family as D263 does for the other `[format]` keys. Angle addresses (`ANGLE` and rotary axes): four decimals on Heidenhain (its input resolution of 0.0001°) and three on Siemens and Fanuc. A linear address left out takes the decimals of `X`. Every rounding then falls under `ROUND_LIMIT` (D363) and the end point check (D365).

#### D367 A value of the TOLERANCE words that the machine's form cannot carry (Fanuc G5.1 Q1)
Question: Language 4.1 gives `TOLERANCE` a number in the active units; controller-mapping 1 and fanuc 4 say the Fanuc form is the switch `G5.1 Q1` alone and that the number lives in a control parameter; machine-config 5 ships `[tolerance] ON = "G5.1 Q1"` with no `{tol}`. No section says what the compiler does with the value it was given. On main FanucFrames.WriteTolerance (line 375) sets the `tol` and `rotary` values of the template and renders it; a template that carries neither placeholder ignores them and raises nothing. Run on main: `TOLERANCE=0.005`, `TOLERANCE=0.05` and `TOLERANCE=0.005 TOLERANCE_MODE=FINISH` on machines/fanuc-mill-30i.toml write `G5.1 Q1` three times and no diagnostic, so `ncx compile --strict` exits 0 while the one thing the program says about its tolerance is the one thing the file does not carry, and nothing tells the shop which value to set or where. The same loss hits `TOLERANCE_MODE` (the Fanuc file has no `mode` table) and would hit `TOLERANCE:ROTARY`, so the question is about any value of the TOLERANCE family that the chosen template cannot carry, not about the contour value alone. The rule is not Fanuc's either: I built a Heidenhain file from machines/heidenhain-itnc530.toml with `ON = "CYCL DEF 32.0 TOLERANZ\nCYCL DEF 32.1 T0.01"` and the same program writes its fixed T0.01 three times, also without a word. Two phrasings need splitting as well: controller-mapping 1, machine-config 5 (line 280), the comment of machines/fanuc-mill-30i.toml:142 and the `TOLERANCE` row of language 4.1 all say the value or the option "stays RAW", but nothing becomes a RAW block when writing — RAW keeps native text NCX cannot express (D5), and the reading direction is where `G5.1 Q1` stays RAW (03-open-questions wave 2, row 62). The case: the CAM writes one `TOLERANCE=0.005` for every controller (opencam D-148), and on the Fanuc mill the value vanishes without a word.
Recommendation: No new word and no change to the canonical order: `TOLERANCE` already stands in language 4.1 and in bucket 12 of language 5 rule 6 (D90), and the value already sits in the VM's ToleranceState. Add one optional scalar to `[tolerance]`, lower-case as `mode` is because it is no template: `held_in = "<text>"`, a short phrase naming where the control holds the value. Rule, in the compiler framework and not in a family: when the template the compiler is about to write for a block of the TOLERANCE family carries no placeholder for a value the program set (`{tol}` for `TOLERANCE`, `{rotary}` for `TOLERANCE:ROTARY`, `{mode}` for `TOLERANCE_MODE`), the compiler writes the template as it does today and reports the WARNING CMP012, naming the word as canonical NCX writes it, the value with its active unit, and the `held_in` text; without `held_in` the message says the machine's form carries no value and names no place. The precedent is CMP011, `PreloadDropped`, a WARNING for a word dropped for want of a template, raised in the framework (CompilerBase.Tools.cs:148) and documented in machine-config 5 ("PRELOAD is dropped with a WARNING"): CMP012 is the next code of the same range, CMP010-CMP019, the templates of the machine. Report once per distinct value in a program, not once per block — the precedent is VM 5's "unresolved expression in STATIC mode (counted, reported once)" and D100's "once per run and axis" — because the setup sheet needs every value the program asks for and no more, and a roughing/finishing program that switches between two values would otherwise warn on every switch (main writes the switch again for every TOLERANCE or TOLERANCE_MODE block, verified: three `G5.1 Q1` lines). `TOLERANCE=OFF` carries no value and is never reported. This rule and D151 must share this one code and one wording: D151's proposed answer already reports a dropped `TOLERANCE:ROTARY` on a machine without `ON_ROTARY` as a WARNING, and NCX should not grow two codes for the same loss — D151 decides which template is chosen, CMP012 reports what the chosen one cannot carry. For the shipped Fanuc file the `held_in` text should name the parameter, and the manual gives the facts: on the 30i/31i/32i-B there is no per-program numeric form for the AI-contour-control tolerance, chapter 20.1 names no tolerance at all, and the only parameters that hold a tolerance in the program's input unit belong to nano smoothing — 19581 ("Toleranz für Nanoglätten") and 11682/11683 (the tolerances at smoothing level 1 and level 10), with 11684/11685 the rotary counterparts of nano smoothing 2. Alternatives, in the order I would put them to the maintainer. (1) The severity: INFO instead of WARNING. Under `--strict` a WARNING is exit code 1 (D97), so with a WARNING every CAM program compiled for the Fanuc mill fails `--strict` until the shop has set the parameter — arguably right, because the file alone does not hold the program's tolerance, but it collides with R1-09's ask that `--strict` pass on a CAM reference program, so answer the two together. (2) The channel: the request wants the value where "the setup sheet can show it", and a compiler diagnostic scrolls past in a terminal while the NC file is what reaches the machine. So add, or choose instead, an optional comment the machine file asks for, written beside the switch (`G5.1 Q1 (TOL 0.005 P19581)` or on its own line), with the precedent of R1-11's "a comment where the machine file asks" and of `ncx annotate`; or a "control settings this program needs" line in the `ncx analyze` report. I recommend the diagnostic as the rule, because it reaches CI and `--strict`, and the comment as an option of the machine file. (3) The payload: a numeric key beside the text, `held_value = 0.01`, the value the machine's parameter is actually set to. It costs the maintainer a verified number per machine, but it is the only form that lets NCXchange do what opencam counts on — report that a machine cannot do what the NCX asks — by comparing the programmed tolerance with the one the control holds, and it should be designed with the control-held keys R1-06 asks for (Fanuc 5114/5115, Heidenhain Q256/Q208, Siemens _VRT, D164's pass) so NCX gets one convention for "the control holds this value" instead of two. (4) Prose in the machine file against a fixed compiler sentence plus a bare parameter number (`held_in = "19581"` rendered as "parameter 19581"): weaker, because the place is a parameter on Fanuc, a machine datum on Siemens and a machine-manufacturer setting on Heidenhain, and only free text covers all three.
Where: docs/spec/ncx-language.md 4.1 (the `TOLERANCE` row: a machine whose form carries no value writes the switch and reports the value; and "options it cannot express stay `RAW`" split into the reading direction); docs/spec/controller-mapping.md:27 (TOLERANCE row, Fanuc column: replace "the value stays `RAW`" with "the value is not written and is reported", keeping "stays RAW" for the reading direction); docs/spec/machine-config.md 5 (line 277-280: the new `held_in` key next to `mode`, and the same "stays RAW" phrasing in the line-280 comment); docs/controllers/fanuc.md 4 (line 76, the `G5.1` bullet: no per-program form carries a number, chapter 20.1 names no tolerance, the nano-smoothing parameters 19581 and 11682/11683 and the rotary 11684/11685, and the manual's note that `G05.1`, `G08` and `G05` must stand in a block of their own); machines/fanuc-mill-30i.toml:141-143 (the `[tolerance]` table, its comment, and a `held_in` text marked unverified under D100); machines/heidenhain-itnc530.toml:126-130, machines/siemens-840dsl-mill.toml:132-136, machines/millturn1.toml:238 and docs/spec/examples/machines/millturn1.toml:238 (unchanged, their `ON` carries `{tol}`); src/Ncx.Core/Machine/ToleranceTable.cs (the new property); src/Ncx.Config/MachineConfigLoader.Functions.cs ReadTolerance (line 335) and its `s_toleranceKeys` list, or `WarnUnknownKeys` reports the new key; src/Ncx.Compilers/DiagnosticCodes.cs (CMP012 in the CMP010-CMP019 range, beside CMP011); the shared check in src/Ncx.Compilers/CompilerBase.Templates.cs (as CMP011 sits in CompilerBase.Tools.cs:148), reached from src/Ncx.Compilers/Fanuc/FanucFrames.cs WriteTolerance (line 375), src/Ncx.Compilers/Heidenhain/HeidenhainFrames.cs WriteTolerance (line 155) and src/Ncx.Compilers/Siemens/SiemensFrames.cs WriteTolerance (line 518); a new tests/Ncx.Compilers.Tests/Fanuc/FanucFramesTests.cs test, Tolerance_ValueTheFormCannotCarry_IsAWarningCmp012, asserting the value, the unit and the place in the message and that a second block with the same value adds no second diagnostic (Tolerance_OnAndOff_AreTheToleranceTemplates at line 203 asserts only the body and no ERROR, so it keeps passing); tests/Ncx.Config.Tests for the new key; related D151 (its rotary WARNING becomes this code, answer the two in one pass), D97 (`--strict`), D164 and R1-06 (the control-held values), CMP011 (the precedent).

ANSWER: (Peter, 2026-10-07, drafted by Claude in project_spike) Accept the rule as recommended (one diagnostic per distinct value, raised in the framework, shared with D151's dropped `TOLERANCE:ROTARY`, `held_in` text), plus alternative 3: a numeric `held_value` beside `held_in`, designed together with the control-held keys of D357 and D358. Severity: a WARNING when the held value is unknown or looser than the program's `TOLERANCE`; an INFO when the machine file states a `held_value` at least as tight. A shop that enters its parameter in the machine file then gets a clean `--strict` run, and NCXchange still reports where the machine cannot do what the NCX asks (opencam D-148). The optional comment of alternative 2 is welcome as a machine-file option. Code: CMP015, because D351 keeps CMP012 to CMP014.

#### D368 Fanuc precision level R on G5.1 Q1 as the carrier of the TOLERANCE value
Question: Controller-mapping 1 gives the Fanuc column of `TOLERANCE` as `G5.1 Q1`, `G5 P10000`, `G8 P1`, `G61.1`/`G64`, and fanuc 4 repeats them; neither names the optional `R` word, and no document decides whether NCX should use it. The 30i/31i/32i-B manual gives the format `G05.1 Q1 [R_]`, where R is "Stufe bei Auswahl der Bearbeitungsdaten (1 bis 10)", the precision level of the optional machining-data-selection function, and `G05.1 Q3 Rx` the smoothing level of the machining-quality setting. The level picks a point between a level-1 and a level-10 parameter set, whose two ends are themselves shop-set parameters (for nano smoothing the tolerances 11682 and 11683), so the control fixes no direction: which end is the fine one is a calibration of the machine, not a property of the control. The option is not installed on every machine, and the manual cautions that a level once set stays in force after the mode ends — though parameters 11686 and 11687 hold a default level that a reset or power-on forces when they are 1 to 10, and keep the level when they are 0. The manual also requires `G05.1`, `G08` and `G05` to stand in a block of their own, with no other G code. So the control does have a per-program form — the branch the request asks for first — but it carries a level, not a tolerance in the program's unit. A machine file today can only put a fixed `R` inside `ON`, which would write the same level for every tolerance the program asks for, so the one NCX file the CAM writes (opencam D-148) still cannot steer the control's accuracy on a Fanuc mill.
Recommendation: My recommendation is no: release 1 answers R1-10 with the WARNING of the preceding draft and the Fanuc column stays the switch, which is the request's second branch. What should change now is only the record: fanuc.md and controller-mapping 1 state the `R` form, the level range, the option it needs, the two parameter ends, the default-level parameters and the block-alone rule, so the form is not rediscovered and so the maintainer's no is on the record with its reasons. The alternative, if the maintainer wants the level after all, is an optional band table in `[tolerance]`: `levels = [{ max = 0.005, level = 1 }, { max = 0.02, level = 4 }, { max = 0.05, level = 7 }]`, read in the order written, with a `{level}` placeholder so a machine that has the option can write `ON = "G5.1 Q1 R{level}"`; the compiler fills `{level}` from the first band whose `max` is at or above the programmed value, a value above the last band takes the last level, and in both the out-of-band case and the no-table case the WARNING of the preceding draft still carries the value, because the level is a selection and not the number. The table is read exactly as written, with no assumption that a lower level is finer, since the manual fixes no direction. Where no `levels` table is given nothing changes. For it: this is the only per-program form the control has, and where the shop has calibrated its ten parameter sets it lets the CAM's single tolerance reach a Fanuc mill without a hand-set parameter. Against it: the bands and their direction are a calibration of that machine, its options and its parameter sets; a wrong band is worse than no band, because the program then looks complete and is not; and the level outliving the mode means NCX would be setting control state that `TOLERANCE=OFF` does not undo, which `[tolerance] OFF = "G5.1 Q0"` cannot express — only a machine whose 11687 is set to 1 to 10 undoes it at a reset, which is again a fact about that machine. The shipped machines/fanuc-mill-30i.toml ships without a `levels` table either way, since it is a generic file for a class of machines and not verified on one (D100).
Where: docs/spec/controller-mapping.md:27 (TOLERANCE row, Fanuc column: the `R` level and why NCX does not write it); docs/controllers/fanuc.md 4 (line 76, the `G5.1` bullet: `G5.1 Q1 [R_]` 1 to 10 of the machining-data-selection option, `G5.1 Q3 Rx` of the machining-quality setting, the level-1 and level-10 parameters, 11686/11687 as the default level at reset, that the level survives the mode, and that `G05.1`, `G08` and `G05` must stand alone in a block); only if the band table is adopted: docs/spec/machine-config.md introduction (the `{level}` placeholder, which under D152's proposed closed list must join it) and 5 (`[tolerance] levels`), src/Ncx.Config/Templates/Placeholder.cs (the D152 marker), src/Ncx.Core/Machine/ToleranceTable.cs, src/Ncx.Config/MachineConfigLoader.Functions.cs ReadTolerance (line 335) and `s_toleranceKeys`, src/Ncx.Compilers/Fanuc/FanucFrames.cs WriteTolerance (line 375), a band test in tests/Ncx.Compilers.Tests/Fanuc/FanucFramesTests.cs; machines/fanuc-mill-30i.toml:141-143 (one comment line, no table); related D152 (the placeholder list), D100 (the unverified numbers of that file); depends on the preceding draft, which must be answered first.

ANSWER: (Peter, 2026-10-07, drafted by Claude in project_spike) Accept as recommended: no Fanuc precision level R as a tolerance carrier; document the R form only.

#### D369 Which point of the tool the axis words give, and the word for the tip offset
Question: The specification never says which point of the tool a coordinate belongs to. Language 4.3 defines `X=10.5` as the "Absolute target coordinate", language 4.2 lets `SETPOS` "Declare that the current position has these coordinates", and language 4.7 makes `SURFACE`, `CLEARANCE`, `DEPTH` and `SAFE` "absolute coordinates along the drilling axis" - three places, the same silence; language 2 and VM 2.2 add nothing. Design rule 1 demands one meaning per word, so this is a gap, not a freedom. Every control places its controlled point where the active tool length register was measured to, and a shop measures a bull-nose tool at length minus the corner radius and a ball tool at its centre, so one program text puts the tip at three different depths depending on how the tool was set. opencam's release 1 writes every coordinate as that measured point (its D-151) and asks NCX to say so and to carry the distance from the tip to it, so that the VM, the trace and a simulation can place the tip. The repository has nothing for it, while the specification already promises the tip four times without being able to place it: VM 7 and 10 publish `TOOL_POSE` as the "pose of the tool tip", VM 9 puts "tool tip pose ... runtime of rotary moves" at level 2, language 4.2 says `MOVE=MOVE` positions the rotary axes "while the tool tip stays on the workpiece", and language 4.3 counts `ROTARY_FEED=MM_MIN` "at the tool tip". Language 4.4 holds `PRELOAD`, `TOOL`, `OFFSET` with the addresses `LEN` and `RAD`, and `COMP`; the offsets are register numbers of the control (one `WordDefinition`, `ValueKinds.Integer` with `AddrKind.OffsetKind` and the ranks 450 and 460, `ToolWords.cs`), not lengths. VM 2.3 keeps `spindleTool`, `preloaded`, the three registers and `lastHolder` per holder and no geometry at all. The tool table of D10 and D265 carries `length` and `radius` per tool, but it is an optional file beside the machine file - none of the eight shipped machine files names `tool_table`, no `*.tools.toml` exists, only `kind` is read (`CompilerBase.Tools.cs` `KindOf`), and `ToolTable.LoadText` loads length and radius while nothing uses them - so a program never states it. A search of the specification, the machine files, the catalogs, the code and all 155 open drafts for a gauge, a programmed point or a tip offset finds nothing else; the word "gauge" does not occur in docs/ at all. Run today the request's test has nothing to assert on: a well-formed file with `TOOL=4 GAUGE=1.0` gives `ERROR PAR010` and `ncx trace` then writes no row at all.
Recommendation: State the rule for every axis coordinate, not for 4.3 alone, and name the distance with one new tool word. (1) The rule. In language 4.3, after the paragraph "Axis words require a verb", say that every axis word gives the coordinate of the tool's programmed point - the point the active tool length offset refers to (`OFFSET:LEN`, the Heidenhain `TOOL CALL`) - and that NCX neither shifts nor recomputes it. Repeat the reference in 4.2 for the coordinates `SETPOS` declares and in 4.7 above the cycle table for `SURFACE`, `CLEARANCE`, `DEPTH` and `SAFE`, which the control executes at that same point: a sentence in 4.3 alone leaves the drilling depth undefined, and the depth is where a wrong assumption scraps the part. (2) The word. Add `TIP_OFFSET` to language 4.4: the distance along the tool axis from the tool tip to the programmed point, read in the units active in its block, not negative - 0 for a tool measured at the tip, the corner radius for a bull-nose tool measured at length minus corner radius, the ball radius for a ball tool measured at its centre. Its shape copies `PHASE`, the one word NCX already has of exactly this kind (`SpindleWords.cs`): `ValueKinds.NumberOrExpr`, `Scope.WithPartner` so that it stands only in a block carrying the `TOOL` word, and modal state on the resource as `PHASE` has in VM 2.4. Unlike `PHASE` it takes `AddrKind.Role`, optional, as `TOOL` and `PRELOAD` do, so a second holder's tool can carry its own offset; it is therefore the first `WithPartner` word with an address, which is what makes the partner change below necessary. Rank 435, between `TOOL` (430) and `OFFSET` (440) in bucket 9 of D90 - the free step that the ten-wise ranks of `CanonicalRanks` exist for; bucket 9 then reads `PRELOAD`, `TOOL`, `TIP_OFFSET`, `OFFSET`, `OFFSET:LEN`, `OFFSET:RAD`, `COMP`. Because D90 is settled (2026-09-11), its row in decisions.md gets a Clarified line with the new rank. (3) State. VM 2.3 gains `holder[r].tipOffset`, 0 initially, set by `TIP_OFFSET[:r]` and reset to 0 by every `TOOL` on that holder that carries none, so one tool's offset can never reach the next one silently. The VM never applies it to a position: positions stay the programmed numbers because VM 2.2 sets the position from the executed motion and D54 with VM 9 put the Cartesian tool geometry in the kinematics module. (Not for the reason of design rule 5, which is about rounding and formatting.) Every controller file is therefore byte-identical with and without the word. The tip is derived output only: the kinematics module subtracts `tipOffset` along the active tool axis before it publishes `TOOL_POSE` (VM 10), which makes good on the "pose of the tool tip" VM 7 already promises, and the tool list of VM 8 prints the value per tool beside the offsets it already lists. (4) Output. Compilers write nothing and no reader can produce it, no control having such a word, so the value survives an NCX-to-NCX round trip but not a round trip through a controller file. Alternative the request allows: a `[tool_change] tip_offset_comment` template that writes the value as a comment where the machine file asks for it (the key is free). I recommend nothing written in release 1, the value reaching the setter through the tool list of `ncx analyze`. (5) The name. Not `GAUGE`, as the request proposes: on these controls the gauge line is the spindle face and the gauge length (Einstellmass) is the whole tool length measured from it, so `GAUGE=1.0` reads as a one-millimetre tool, against design rule 6. (6) Diagnostics. A `TIP_OFFSET` in a block without a `TOOL` is the existing ERROR `PAR016`: language 5 rule 5 already lists `PHASE` and `BlockRules.s_partners` already raises it, so one entry `["TIP_OFFSET"] = ["TOOL"]` suffices and this waits on nothing - in particular not on D116, which settles a different set of words (`NAME`, `NUMBER`, `CHANNEL` and the cycle words). What the word does need is the role pairing: `HasAny` tests `block.Has(key)` only, so `TIP_OFFSET:H2` beside `TOOL:H1` would pass, and the partner test must compare the address as well. A negative value, or a `TIP_OFFSET` beside `TOOL=0`, is a new ERROR `VM045`, the next free code after the tool-change band VM040 to VM044 inside VM001-VM199 (block execution, P1-02), with its row in the Tool family of the validation table and so in `generated/diagnostics.md`; `R=0` (VM233) and `ANGLE` not greater than 0 (VM234) are the precedent for a value range being a VM rule rather than a catalog one. Alternatives. A kind instead of a length, `TIP_OFFSET=TIP|CORNER|CENTER`, the distance coming from the tool table's `radius`: rejected, because the table is optional and a measured point is not a kind. No address at all, as `PHASE` has none, which removes the `s_partners` change: rejected, because `TOOL` carries a role and a turn-mill's second holder must be able to carry its own offset. A plain modal word instead of a partner of `TOOL`: shorter to write, but open to a stale value on the next tool. Not an alternative: the machine file, because the coordinates depend on the value and the same NCX file must mean one part in every shop (design rule 1, and the CAM's one-file rule D-148).
Where: docs/spec/ncx-language.md 4.2 (the `SETPOS` row), 4.3 (the sentence on the programmed point), 4.4 (the new row), 4.7 (the sentence above the cycle table), 5 rule 5 and 5 rule 6 bucket 9; docs/spec/ncx-virtual-machine.md 2.3 (the holder row), 3.5 (the tool-change table), 5 (the ERROR list, which already names "PHASE or POINT without their verb or partner"), 6 (trace; the variable name `TIP_OFFSET:H1` follows D197, a trace today naming the holder rows `TOOL:H1` and `OFFSET:LEN:H1`), 7 (the `TOOL_POSE` payload), 8 (the tool list), 10 (the kinematics contract); docs/spec/controller-mapping.md 3 (a row with "not written" in the three controller columns, as the `TOOL` row already carries for Heidenhain); docs/spec/generated/word-catalog.md and docs/spec/generated/diagnostics.md, both regenerated by their tests; the D90 row of docs/decisions/decisions.md gets a Clarified line for the new rank. Code: src/Ncx.Core/Catalog/ToolWords.cs, src/Ncx.Core/Catalog/CanonicalRanks.cs (`TipOffset = 435`, bucket 9 comment), src/Ncx.Core/Parsing/BlockRules.cs (`s_partners` and `HasAny`, which must compare the address), src/Ncx.Core/VirtualMachine/State/HolderState.cs and HolderSnapshot.cs, src/Ncx.Core/VirtualMachine/Handlers/ToolHandlers.cs and src/Ncx.Core/VirtualMachine/ToolChangeRules.cs, src/Ncx.Core/Model/DiagnosticCodes.Vm.cs (`VM045`), src/Ncx.Core/VirtualMachine/Validation/ToolValidation.cs (the new row of the Tool family), src/Ncx.Core/VirtualMachine/Events/StateChanges.cs (the trace variable), src/Ncx.Analytics/ToolList/ToolUse.cs and ToolListAnalytic.Report.cs. Tests: the catalog and generated-table tests of tests/Ncx.Core.Tests (P0-03), the block-rule tests including the role pairing (P0-04), the tool-change and reset tests (P1-02), and a tests/Ncx.Compilers.Tests case that compiles one program with `TIP_OFFSET=0` and with `TIP_OFFSET=1` to identical text on fanuc-mill-30i, heidenhain-itnc530 and siemens-840dsl-mill.

ANSWER: (Peter, 2026-10-07, drafted by Claude in project_spike) Part (1), the rule, accepted: every axis word, the coordinates of `SETPOS` and the cycle heights `SURFACE`, `CLEARANCE`, `DEPTH` and `SAFE` give the tool's programmed point, the point the active length register refers to, and NCX neither shifts nor recomputes them. Not `GAUGE`, agreed. Parts (2) to (6) need a redraft, because opencam changed its model on 2026-10-02 (D-154, D-155; R1-11 rewritten in its request file). A tool has several measurement points, and each operation is written in one of them. Point k of a tool has an axial offset a from the tip (your `TIP_OFFSET`, not negative) and a register radius r, the radius the shop enters for that point (0 for a point on the axis; the control's radius compensation then adds r plus wear). What the CAM needs from NCX: (a) neutral words per section for the point: its number k for the active tool, a and r; valid with `TOOL` and on their own, because the point can change between two operations without a tool change (applied with the next move, which the CAM writes at clearance height); modal per holder, reset to point 1 with a = 0 and r = 0 by a `TOOL` that carries none. (b) The machine file maps tool and k to the control's registers: H and D numbers on Fanuc by a rule or table, `D k` on Siemens, an indexed tool or another tool row on Heidenhain (please check how a TNC handles `TOOL CALL 5.1` when tool 5 is in the spindle). Today `OFFSET:LEN=5` gives `H5` on Fanuc but edge `D5` on Siemens, so register numbers are not neutral; the CAM will write the point words and no `OFFSET:*` numbers, and `OFFSET:*` stays for hand-written programs. (c) The VM keeps positions as programmed, derives the tip by a along the tool axis, and simulates `COMP` with r plus a declared wear (0 by default). (d) Compilers write the registers from the mapping and nothing for a and r except an optional comment where the machine file asks. Names are yours to choose; `POINT` seems taken (VM 5 already names it).

#### D370 The tip offset the shop measured, in the tool table of D10
Question: D10 and D265 settled the optional tool table beside the machine file: `[[tool]]` rows with `number` or `name`, `kind`, `length` and `radius`, an unknown key a WARNING. Only `kind` is read today (`CompilerBase.Tools.cs` `KindOf`); `ToolTable.LoadText` loads `length` and `radius` and nothing uses them, and none of the eight shipped machine files names a `tool_table`. The programmed point of the first draft says which point of the tool the CAM computed its coordinates for; the control puts its controlled point where the shop measured that tool; nothing in the repository compares the two. If the program was written for the corner-radius centre and the setter measured the tool to the tip, every depth is wrong by the corner radius and NCXchange reports nothing: the one failure of the programmed-point model that costs a part, and the one thing a shop-side tool table could catch. Machine-config 1 lists the four `[[tool]]` keys and no measured point (and states no units for `length` and `radius` either), VM 2.3 holds no tool geometry, and R1-11 does not raise the question, so nothing settles whether NCXchange checks this or leaves it to the shop.
Recommendation: Give the `[[tool]]` rows of D265 a fifth key, `tip_offset`, a number with default 0, and let the compiler compare it with the program's `TIP_OFFSET` for that tool. The same sentence of machine-config 1 has to state the units of all three numeric keys, because it states none today: `tip_offset`, `length` and `radius` are read in `units_default`. Where the table describes the tool and the two values differ by more than one output step of the tool axis (`[format] decimals` of that address), a WARNING, a new code `CMP030` opening the band CMP030 to CMP039, "the tool data of the machine (machine-config 1, D10)", inside the compiler-framework range CMP001-CMP099 of `Ncx.Compilers` (P3-03), whose message names the tool, both values and the tool-table file. Where the table does not describe the tool, nothing: D10's warning block at the head of the program already covers missing tool data. A WARNING and not an ERROR, because the shop's table may be older than the program, and because `--strict` already turns every WARNING into exit code 1 (architecture 10, D97) for a shop that wants the check to stop the run. The compiler must not correct the coordinates: VM 2.2 and D54 with VM 9 keep every position the programmed number, and a silent shift would hide a wrongly set tool instead of showing it. Reason for a machine-side key rather than a second program word: the measured point is a fact of the shop's tool, which is what the tool table is for, and only the comparison of the shop's number with the program's says anything. Alternative: no key in release 1, the program's `TIP_OFFSET` appearing per tool in the tool list of `ncx analyze` (first draft) so that the setup sheet carries it and the setter decides; that costs nothing and catches nothing. Rejected alternative: the table as the only source and no program word, which would make the same NCX file mean a different part in two shops.
Where: docs/spec/machine-config.md 1 (the `[[tool]]` example, the sentence on its keys and the units of the three numeric keys); the D265 row of docs/decisions/decisions.md gets a Clarified line. Code: src/Ncx.Config/ToolTable.cs (`s_toolKeys`), src/Ncx.Config/ToolData.cs (the new property), src/Ncx.Compilers/CompilerBase.Tools.cs (the check beside `KindOf`), src/Ncx.Compilers/DiagnosticCodes.cs (the band comment of the CMP ranges and `CMP030`; the CMP codes have no row in docs/spec/generated/diagnostics.md, which holds the Core codes only). Data: a shipped example table machines/fanuc-mill-30i.tools.toml with `tool_table` in machines/fanuc-mill-30i.toml, which names none today. Tests: tests/Ncx.Config.Tests/ToolTableTests.cs for the key and for the unknown-key WARNING of D265, tests/Ncx.Compilers.Tests for the mismatch WARNING, for silence where the table lacks the tool, and for the step at which the WARNING starts.

ANSWER: (Peter, 2026-10-07, drafted by Claude in project_spike) Accept the idea with the new model of D369: tool-table rows per tool and point k, each with `tip_offset` (a) and the register radius (r), compared with the program's values for that point; a WARNING beyond one output step, as recommended, and no correction of coordinates. State the units of all numeric keys, as recommended. Code: CMP032, because CMP030 and CMP031 go to D364 and D365. Redraft together with D369.

#### D371 What a single-file ncx finds of the machine files and catalogs it ships with
Question: Implementation 17 P7-03 publishes ncx as a .NET tool and as "self-contained single-file binaries for `win-x64`, `osx-arm64`, `osx-x64`, `linux-x64` ... on a `v*` tag", and architecture 12 ends at the tagged 1.0. Machine-config 10 lays out a project (`ncx.toml`, `machines/`, `cycles/`, `programs/`, `out/`) and says nothing of an installation. Implementation 12 P2-04, D206 and D207 (both open) give the lookup three places — the folder `ncx.toml` names, then `machines/` or `cycles/` of the working directory, then of "the tool's own folder", which P2-04 and the code comments call the folder that holds the shipped files — and no document says what that folder holds when ncx is one file, nor whether the shipped files travel inside the binary or beside it. The case is the CAM's (opencam D-031): it bundles one pinned ncx with its catalogs and runs it from its own working directory, with no `ncx.toml` and no `machines/` of its own. Measured on main (f74559c): `dotnet publish -r osx-arm64 --self-contained -p:PublishSingleFile=true` writes one 82 MB executable beside loose `machines/` (eight files), `cycles/` (four) and `templates/`, because Ncx.Cli.csproj copies them as `None` items; that folder, run in a temporary working directory, compiles `2.5D_FRAESEN.ncx` for `fanuc-mill-30i`, `heidenhain-itnc530` and `siemens-840dsl-mill` with exit 0. The executable copied away on its own fails three times over, one after the other: `CLI200` on the machine file named by name, exit 2; then, with the machine given by path, `CLI202` on the catalog the machine names, exit 2; and `ncx plugin new` with `CLI552`, exit 2. So all three kinds of shipped file are at stake, not the catalogs alone. With `-p:IncludeAllContentForSelfExtract=true` the one file does run alone and all three work, because the content is extracted at first run into `~/.net/<executable name>/<hash>/`, which the CLI200 message then names as `/Users/<user>/.net/ncx/LaHmWixDanZZ/machines`, a folder the user never made.
Recommendation: Make the shipped set built-in and give the lookup a fourth and last place. Every `.toml` of `machines/` and `cycles/` that the repository ships is embedded in the binary by the same globs that copy it today, and a name that none of the three folders of D206 and D207 holds is taken from the built-in copy of that name; the three folders keep their order, so a shop's own file still wins over the shipped one. The embedding belongs in `src/Ncx.Config/Ncx.Config.csproj` as `EmbeddedResource`, beside the `None` copy that stays in `Ncx.Cli.csproj`, because the reader has to live where the loaders live: `Ncx.Cli` references `Ncx.Config` and not the other way round, so a resource embedded in `Ncx.Cli` is unreachable from `Ncx.Config` without passing an assembly in. A built-in file is named in a diagnostic as `built-in machines/fanuc-mill-30i.toml`, never by a path (D98, which is how `ProjectFolders.NameOf` already names a file the user can find), and the messages of CLI200 and CLI202 (area CLI200-CLI249, the machine of a run, P2-04) end with "and no built-in machine file of that name" and "and no built-in catalog of that name"; no new diagnostic code is needed, and this is no language question, so no word, no canonical rank and no machine key. The release artefact keeps the loose `machines/` and `cycles/` beside the binary as well, so the sketches stay readable and copyable, and publishing stays without trimming (implementation 17, "Risks and open ends"). Two consequences to take up in the answer: the plugin template is not covered, since it is a folder of files a user edits rather than a file the loaders read, so `ncx plugin new` from a lone binary keeps reporting CLI552 — correct behaviour that belongs in the release notes; and a shipped file deleted from the folder beside the binary no longer gives CLI200 but falls back to the built-in copy, so a shop that wants a shipped machine gone has to shadow it with its own file of that name rather than delete it. Reason: NCXchange already carries configuration in code — the built-in default machine of D103 and the built-in drilling family of `DrillingFamily.Catalog(controller)` that a catalog file overrides — so a built-in file is nothing new in kind; the globs leave no second list to maintain and let a test compare each built-in copy with the repository file. Alternative A, which is what main does: no built-in set, and the release notes say the artefact is the folder and not the file — the CAM copies `machines/` and `cycles/` with the binary, or writes its own into the working directory, where the first two places of D206 and D207 find them. It costs no code and keeps the shipped files editable in place, but a binary moved on its own stops finding the shipped mills, which is exactly what the CAM bundles. Alternative B, the cheapest of all and the one that matches R1-12's words most closely: publish with `IncludeAllContentForSelfExtract`, one MSBuild property and no code, after which the single file alone compiles for all three mills and even `ncx plugin new` works, because machines, catalogs and the template are all extracted. Its costs are real but none of them is the diagnostic wording, which is ours to write: a first run that unpacks 82 MB into `~/.net/` per version, a slower cold start, a folder named after the executable that the user never made, and architecture 10 and machine-config would then have to say that the tool's own folder may be an extraction cache. Alternative C, narrower: build in the catalogs only, which are controller facts, and leave the machine files beside the binary, since the front page calls them sketches not verified on a machine. Not settled here, and a question of its own: whether ncx gains a way to write the built-in files out into a project.
Where: Machine-config 10 (a paragraph for the installation beside the project layout) and 6 (`[cycles] catalog`: the built-in copy as the last place); architecture 10 (the `ncx.toml` paragraph and the `--machine` sentence) and 12; implementation 12 P2-04, whose sentence states the three-place order verbatim and gains the fourth; implementation 17 P7-03 and `docs/plan/tasks/inbox/P7-03-release-1-0.md` (what the release artefact contains). Answer with D206 and D207, whose order this extends, and with D156 (the names of the shipped catalogs); cross-reference D317, which gives plugin DLLs their own order without the tool's folder, so that the answer says plainly that the fourth place is for machine files and catalogs alone. Code: `src/Ncx.Cli/ProjectFolders.cs` (the folder order, `FindMachine`, `FindCatalog`, `NameOf`, the `TODO(question)` of D206 at line 71), `src/Ncx.Cli/RunSettings.cs` (`ToolFolder`), `src/Ncx.Cli/RunMachine.cs` (`WithCatalog`, `ReportMachineNotFound`: the two messages and the `TODO(question)` of D207 at line 171), `src/Ncx.Cli/DiagnosticCodes.Project.cs` (the wording of CLI200 and CLI202), `src/Ncx.Cli/Ncx.Cli.csproj` (the `machines/` and `cycles/` globs keep copying) and `src/Ncx.Config/Ncx.Config.csproj` (the same globs as `EmbeddedResource`), a `BuiltInFiles` reader in `src/Ncx.Config` next to `DefaultMachine.cs` (`MachineConfigLoader.LoadText` and `CycleCatalogLoader.LoadText` already take text). Data: `machines/*.toml` and `cycles/*.toml` unchanged. Tests: `tests/Ncx.Acceptance/Cli/ProjectFoldersTests.cs` and `tests/Ncx.Acceptance/Cli/RunMachineTests.cs` (the seven `CycleCatalog_` tests, lines 122 to 224) get the fourth place and the new message; a new test that every built-in copy equals the file of the same name under `Fixture.RepositoryRoot()` (`tests/Fixtures/Fixture.cs:68`, as `tests/Ncx.Config.Tests/Cycles/ShippedCatalogsTests.cs` reads them today); and the P7-03 acceptance that the published executable alone, in a temporary working directory, compiles for the three mills with exit 0.

ANSWER: (Peter, 2026-10-07, drafted by Claude in project_spike) Accept as recommended: the shipped `machines/` and `cycles/` files are built in as the fourth and last place of the lookup, a shop's own file still wins, and the release keeps the loose folders beside the binary. Answer together with D206 and D207.
