### Eleventh round: the measurement points of a tool (opencam D-154 and D-155), asked 2026-10-07

Five drafts that replace parts (2) to (6) of D369 and the form of D370, which the answers of 2026-10-07 sent back for a redraft: opencam changed its model on 2026-10-02, from one gauge offset per tool to several measurement points per tool, each with an axial offset from the tip and a register radius, selected per operation without a tool change (opencam D-154, D-155; R1-11 of the request list, rewritten the same day). Part one of D369 stands as answered and is not repeated here: every axis word, the coordinates of `SETPOS` and the cycle heights give the tool's programmed point, and NCX neither shifts nor recomputes them. The controller facts in these drafts come from the maintainer's manual library with their pages; the one fact the library cannot settle, whether an indexed `TOOL CALL` of the tool already in the spindle runs the change macro on an iTNC 530, is named where it bites.

#### D372 The words for a tool's measurement point
Question: opencam D-154 and D-155 (R1-11, rewritten 2026-10-02) give a tool one or more measurement points, the points the shop measures into the control's registers. Point k has an axial offset a from the tip, which D369's answer calls the tip offset, and a register radius r, the radius the shop enters for that point, 0 for a point on the axis. An operation is written in one point, and the point may change between two operations without a tool change. D369 settled part one on 2026-10-07 (every axis word, the coordinates of `SETPOS` and the cycle heights `SURFACE`, `CLEARANCE`, `DEPTH` and `SAFE` give the tool's programmed point, and NCX neither shifts nor recomputes them) and sent the rest back for this redraft, with the name `GAUGE` refused and the note that `POINT` seems taken. It is: `POINT` is the reference point of `HOME` (language 4.3, rank 730, `src/Ncx.Core/Catalog/MotionWords.cs`), and VM 5 names it in the ERROR of a word without its partner (`PAR016`). What language 4.4 has today is three register numbers and a flag: `OFFSET:LEN`, `OFFSET:RAD`, `OFFSET` (ranks 450, 460, 440) and `COMP` (470), and the holder state of VM 2.3 keeps exactly those three integers (`src/Ncx.Core/VirtualMachine/State/HolderState.cs`). Register numbers are not neutral across controls, which is the reason the CAM cannot write them: `OFFSET:LEN=5` is `H5` on Fanuc (`src/Ncx.Readers/Fanuc/FanucToolWords.cs`), the cutting edge `D5` of the active tool on Siemens (D301, `src/Ncx.Compilers/Siemens/SiemensTools.cs`), and nothing at all on Heidenhain, where `offsets_with_change = true` consumes the words and writes none (`src/Ncx.Compilers/Heidenhain/HeidenhainToolCall.cs`). So nothing in NCX can say which point of a tool a program is written in, and no word carries a or r.
Recommendation: three words in language 4.4, so that the point is named neutrally and its two measured values travel with it. `TOOL_POINT=k` (integer from 1, optional address = holder role as `TOOL` has it, modal per holder, rank 435 between `TOOL` and `OFFSET`, because the point decides which registers the offset words would name); `TIP_OFFSET=a` (number or expression in the active units, not negative, rank 465) and `POINT_RADIUS=r` (number or expression, not negative, rank 467), both modal per holder. The three are valid in a `TOOL` block and in a block of their own, which is what D-155 needs: a point change without a tool change is then a block of its own, and it takes effect as `OFFSET:LEN` does, with the next motion of the tool axis, so the CAM can write it at clearance height. A `TOOL` block that carries none of them resets the holder to point 1 with a = 0 and r = 0, exactly as a `TOOL` consumes a preload today, because a new tool measured elsewhere must not inherit the old tool's point. The default state of a holder is therefore point 1, a = 0, r = 0, which is what every program written before these words says. The ranks break the step of ten of `CanonicalRanks`, as the `MAX` family of D351 does; the comment of that file and the note of the generated table say the step holds, so both are amended, or bucket 9 is renumbered. Validation, in the tool family VM480-VM499 of which only `VM480` is used: `VM481` a point word on a holder that holds no tool, `VM482` a negative `TIP_OFFSET` or `POINT_RADIUS`, `VM483` a `TOOL_POINT` of 0 or less. The names are the one real choice here. The alternative is one word with two addresses, `TOOL_POINT=2` with `TOOL_POINT:LEN=1.0` and `TOOL_POINT:RAD=8`, which mirrors `OFFSET:LEN` and `OFFSET:RAD` and needs one catalog entry instead of three; against it stands that `LEN` and `RAD` under `OFFSET` are register numbers while under `TOOL_POINT` they would be lengths, which reads wrong in the same table. `GAUGE` is out, as answered: on a Fanuc the gauge line is the spindle face and the gauge length is the whole tool length, so `GAUGE=1.0` reads as a one-millimetre tool.
Where: language 4.4 (three rows, the paragraph on what the words mean and when they take effect), 5 rule 6 bucket 9 (the three ranks), 5 rule 4 (a key once per block, with the holder address distinguishing); VM 2.3 (the holder table: point, tip offset and register radius beside the three register numbers), VM 4 (the modal summary row of the tool words), VM 5 (the three new ERRORs); `src/Ncx.Core/Catalog/ToolWords.cs`, `CanonicalRanks.cs` and its step-of-ten comment, `src/Ncx.Core/VirtualMachine/State/HolderState.cs` and `HolderSnapshot.cs`, `src/Ncx.Core/VirtualMachine/Handlers/ToolHandlers.cs`, `src/Ncx.Core/VirtualMachine/Events/StateChanges.cs` (the trace rows), `src/Ncx.Core/VirtualMachine/Validation/ToolValidation.cs` and `src/Ncx.Core/Model/DiagnosticCodes.Validation.cs` (VM481-VM483) with `Validation/DiagnosticTable.cs`; generated `docs/spec/generated/word-catalog.md` and `diagnostics.md`; tests `tests/Ncx.Core.Tests/Catalog/WordCatalogTests.cs` (which reads language 4.4 itself, so word and table land in one commit), `CanonicalOrderTests.cs`, `tests/Ncx.Core.Tests/VirtualMachine/State/HolderStateTests.cs`, `ToolChangeTests.cs`, `Validation/ToolValidationTests.cs`. Tasks: P0-03, P0-04, P0-06, P1-01, P1-02, P1-04, P1-05, all in `done/`. Related D7, D10, D265, D301, D369, D370 and the four drafts below.

ANSWER:
Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

Accept the recommendation: `TOOL_POINT=k` (integer ≥ 1, holder address, modal per holder, rank 435), `TIP_OFFSET=a` (≥ 0, rank 465) and `POINT_RADIUS=r` (≥ 0, rank 467). They are valid in a TOOL block or in a block of their own, and take effect with the next tool-axis motion. A TOOL block without them resets to point 1, a = 0, r = 0. Validation: VM481 (no tool in the holder), VM482 (negative value), VM483 (k ≤ 0). Amend the step-of-ten comment of CanonicalRanks and the generated table note; don't renumber.
Basis: logical
Source: The point has to be named neutrally because the register it selects differs per control (Fanuc H/D, Siemens D edge, Heidenhain index). Resetting on a TOOL change matches what the controls do: Siemens activates the default edge D1 on a tool change (MD20270), and a Klartext TOOL CALL without an index selects the main line. The audit confirmed the draft's facts (manual-audit-2026-10-26 section 4).
Differs from the recommendation: no
Confidence: high
Code impact: Ncx.Core catalog (ToolWords, CanonicalRanks), HolderState, ToolHandlers, ToolValidation (VM481-VM483).

#### D373 How the machine file maps a tool and a point to the control's registers
Question: D-155 asks NCXchange to map tool and point k to each control's registers, and there is no place for it. `[tool_change]` has nine keys (machine-config 3) and none is per point or per edge; `{offset}` stands in the placeholder list of the machine-config introduction without a definition and means `OffsetCombined` in the framework, the turret digits on a Fanuc lathe and the cutting edge on Siemens; `{point}` is used by `[home] point` and is not in the list at all. The three families differ so far that one form cannot serve them, and the manuals say so. Heidenhain: the index is a suffix of the called tool number, `T 5.1`, and selects a whole further table line with its own length, radius and delta columns; at most nine indices per tool (iTNC 530 Klartext 2010, p. 165-166 with MP7262, p. 663; TNC 640 Setup 10/2019, p. 133 and p. 137). Crucially for a point change without a tool change, the TNC 640 Klartext manual (892903-18, 10/2019, p. 123) makes the criterion syntactic: the control changes only the speed when the block carries no tool name, no tool number and the same tool axis, and it runs the tool-change macro when the block carries a tool number — so `TOOL CALL 5.1` while tool 5 stands in the spindle runs the macro, and the manuals name no exception for another index of the same tool; what the macro then does is the machine builder's. For the iTNC 530 the Klartext manual has no such rule, only that a `TOOL CALL` swaps the tool out of the magazine and that the change is machine-dependent (p. 182); its Technisches Handbuch (iTNC530-HSCI, NC-SW 60642x-04, 2014) narrows the fact without settling it. The change macro, named with `TC =` in NCMACRO.SYS, is called during a `TOOL CALL` in place of the T strobe, and without that entry the `TOOL CALL` runs without a macro (p. 1251, p. 1609-1610); MP7480.0 chooses whether the tool number goes out only on a tool-number change (inputs 1, 3, 5) or at every `TOOL CALL` (inputs 2, 4, 6) (p. 1614); number and index are two separate parameters, the index going to the PLC in W266 (p. 1600) and the handbook's macro example reading both and re-sending them as `TOOL CALL Q1 .Q7` (p. 1610-1611); and FN18 ID61 gives the macro the change sequence, value 0 meaning the tool is already in the spindle (p. 1736). No page says whether 5 to 5.1 counts as a tool-number change for MP7480.0, so on that generation whether `TOOL CALL 5.1` with tool 5 in the spindle runs the change macro depends on MP7480.0 and on the builder's macro. Siemens is the opposite: a bare `D` in a motion block switches the offset data set of the tool already active, with the manual's own example `N50 T4 D2` then `N70 G0 Z... D1` (Grundlagen 03/2013, p. 74), an edge carries its own lengths, radius, wear and base dimension (`$TC_DP1`..`$TC_DP25`, Funktionshandbuch Grundfunktionen 07/2012, W1, p. 1596), and how D relates to T is itself one of three machine-data variants (Grundlagen p. 74; MD18105, MD18106, Funktionshandbuch p. 1578). Fanuc has no tool-owned structure: `H` and `D` index a flat per-path pool whose size is parameter 5024, the M-series `T` is only a code and strobe signal to the machine (30i/31i/32i-B Operator's Manual, printed p. 219), and whether `H` and `D` share one table depends on the offset memory type A, B or C (Machining Center volume, printed p. 248-249). Two documented ties exist and are worth having: with tool management, `H99` and `D99` select the registers registered for the tool at the spindle, the 99 being parameter 13265 (printed p. 228-229); and under offset memory A or B the 5-axis cutting-point commands `G43.8` and `G43.9` take length from `H`, radius from `H+n` and corner radius from `H+2n`, n being parameter 11419 and 0 meaning 1, while under memory C they take one `H` for all three when parameter 11269 bit 3 is 1 and `H` plus `D` when it is 0 (printed p. 845, connector p. 877; Parameter Manual B-64490EN p. 630).
Recommendation: a new `[tool_points]` table in the machine file, with one key that says which form the control has and the data that form needs. `form = "indexed_tool"` for Klartext: point 1 is the plain call and point k the index k-1, so point 2 writes `TOOL CALL 5.1`; because that block carries a tool number the TNC 640 runs its change macro, and on an iTNC 530 whether it does depends on MP7480.0 and the builder's macro, so the compiler reports it once per point change with the WARNING `CMP123` (the Heidenhain band's next free code, CMP120 to CMP122 going to D349, D358 and D362), whose text names the change macro and, for an iTNC 530, MP7480.0 and the builder's macro as what decides; a machine whose builder accepts it silences the warning with `point_change = "call"`. `form = "edge"` for Siemens: point k is `D k`, written in the block the point word stands in, and D301's one-register rule is untouched. `form = "registers"` for Fanuc: the registers come from explicit rows, `[[tool_point]] tool = 5, point = 2, length = 12, radius = 12`, and where a shop numbers by a rule the two optional keys `length_register_step` and `radius_register_step` give register = tool + (k-1) times step, the arithmetic the control's own cutting-point command does with parameter 11419 under offset memory A or B; under memory C, where that command takes one `H` or `H` plus `D`, the step keys are the shop's numbering rule and have no counterpart in the control; `managed = true` writes `H99` and `D99` instead, which is the one form that needs no table because the control reads the numbers from the tool in the spindle. A machine file without `[tool_points]` writes nothing for a point other than 1 and reports it once per program as the INFO `CMP016` of the compiler framework's template band, because a control that cannot select a point is doing nothing wrong; a `TOOL_POINT` the table cannot map on a machine that has the form is the ERROR of its family (`CMP341` Fanuc, `CMP514` Siemens, `CMP123` Heidenhain also carrying this case), naming the tool and k, because writing another point's registers would cut with the wrong tool. Nothing is derived from the tool number by NCX itself: the Fanuc manual gives the M-series `T` no relation to `H` and `D` at all, so a rule the shop did not state is a guess at the machine's setup. The loader reads the table with `CFG010`, the next free code of the loading range after D348's `CFG009`, for a form it does not know or a row without its tool. Alternative: keep the mapping out of the machine file and let the CAM write the registers after all, which is what `OFFSET:LEN` and `OFFSET:RAD` already do; that is what D-148 forbids, since the same NCX file then has to differ per control. The iTNC 530 fact (whether an indexed call of the tool in the spindle runs the change macro there too) is narrowed by its Technisches Handbuch but not settled: it depends on MP7480.0 and on the builder's macro, which can see the tool in the spindle through FN18 ID61; so the Klartext form reports on both generations as the TNC 640 rule says, and a builder whose setting and macro leave an index call of the tool in the spindle alone says so with `point_change = "call"`. (Corrected 2026-10-26 after the manual audit: TNC 640 rule cited on p. 123 instead of p. 128 and the iTNC 530 index facts on p. 165-166 and p. 663 instead of p. 173; the cutting-point registers `H`, `H+n`, `H+2n` and so the register-step analogy hold under offset memory A or B only; and the iTNC 530 Technisches Handbuch, which the library does hold, makes the indexed call depend on MP7480.0 and the builder's macro, which the WARNING now names.)
Where: machine-config 3 (the `[tool_change]` neighbourhood and a new `[tool_points]` section), 5 (the table and its keys), the placeholder list of the introduction (`{point}`, which is used by `[home]` and unlisted, and `{offset}`, which needs its definition), 11; controller-mapping 3 (a row for the point words) and the Heidenhain, Siemens and Fanuc columns; controllers/heidenhain.md 4 (the indexed call and the change-macro rule with its page), controllers/siemens.md 5 (the edge), controllers/fanuc.md 5 (the flat pool, the memory types, tool management); `machines/fanuc-mill-30i.toml`, `machines/heidenhain-itnc530.toml`, `machines/siemens-840dsl-mill.toml` and the five files under `docs/spec/examples/machines/`; `src/Ncx.Core/Machine/` (a `ToolPointsTable` beside `ToolChangeConfig`), `src/Ncx.Config/MachineConfigLoader.cs` and `MachineConfigLoader.Functions.cs`, `src/Ncx.Config/DiagnosticCodes.Loading.cs` (`CFG010`); `src/Ncx.Compilers/Heidenhain/HeidenhainToolCall.cs`, `src/Ncx.Compilers/Siemens/SiemensTools.cs`, `src/Ncx.Compilers/Fanuc/FanucToolWords.cs`, `src/Ncx.Compilers/CompilerBase.Tools.cs`, `src/Ncx.Compilers/DiagnosticCodes.cs` (`CMP016`) and the three family files (`CMP123`, `CMP341`, `CMP514`); tests in `tests/Ncx.Config.Tests/MachineConfigLoaderTests.cs` and the three compiler test folders. Tasks: P2-01, P2-02, P2-04, P3-03, P3-04, P3-06 and P5-02. Related D7, D52, D219, D301, D369, D372, D375.

ANSWER:
Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

Accept `[tool_points]` with `form = "indexed_tool" | "edge" | "registers"`, CMP016 (INFO, the machine has no form), CMP123/CMP341/CMP514 (ERROR, a point the form cannot map), CFG010 (loader), and `point_change = "call"`, with five improvements: (1) `indexed_tool`: point k writes index k-1, so k ≤ 10 (at most nine indices). A larger k is CMP123 as an ERROR. (2) `edge`: point k writes `D k` only by default. The control can number edges freely (MD18105, unique D numbers per tool) or flat (MD18102 = 1, D without relation to T). So the form also accepts explicit rows `[[tool_point]] tool = 5, point = 2, edge = 20`, which win over `D k`, and `edge_numbering = "flat"` makes such rows mandatory: without a row, a point is CMP514. (3) `registers`: add the optional `offset_memory = "A" | "B" | "C"`. Under A or B, H and D share one pool, so the loader raises CFG010 when one register number serves as a length for one tool/point and as a radius for another (including length = radius in one row). Under C, the same number for H and D is legal, and so is the common `length = radius` row. When the key is absent, no check is made. (4) `managed = true` (`H99`/`D99`) covers point 1 only, because tool management registers one compensation number per tool. A point k > 1 on a managed machine needs an explicit row, or it is CMP341. (5) The step keys stay as the shop's own numbering rule. The doc says they have a control counterpart (parameter 11419 under `G43.8`/`G43.9`) only under memory A or B. The iTNC 530 fact stays open as the draft says (MP7480.0 and the builder's macro), with the WARNING CMP123 on both Heidenhain generations.
Basis: manual
Source: Fanuc 30i-B B-64484EN-2 p.262-263 (connector) for memories A/B/C (A and B: "D codes and H codes are treated the same"; C: separate memory for D and H); 30i-B B-64484EN p.260 and 0i-F B-64604EN p.183 (H99/D99 select "a compensation number registered as tool management data of a tool attached at a spindle position", with parameter 13265 = 0); 840D sl Funktionshandbuch Grundfunktionen 2012 p.1581 (MD18105, unique D numbers per tool) and p.1590 (MD18102 = 1, D without relation to a tool); 840D sl Programmierung BS.000504 p.451-452 (flat D numbers 1-32000); the Heidenhain facts as cited in the corrected draft (Klartext 892903-18 p.123; iTNC 530 Klartext 2010 p.165-166, p.663; iTNC530-HSCI Technisches Handbuch p.1251, p.1600, p.1609-1614, p.1736).
Differs from the recommendation: yes. It adds explicit edge rows and `edge_numbering` for Siemens, `offset_memory` with a register-collision check for Fanuc, limits `managed` to point 1, and caps the Klartext index at 9.
Confidence: medium (the facts are high; the key shapes are design)
Code impact: Ncx.Core Machine (ToolPointsTable), MachineConfigLoader (CFG010), the three compilers' tool writers.

#### D374 What the virtual machine does with the tip offset and the register radius
Question: D-154 asks that the VM, the trace, the simulation and the verification place the tool tip and apply compensation without the control's tool table, and D369's answer repeats it as part (c). The VM holds none of that today. VM 2.3 and `HolderState` keep three integer register numbers and no geometry; `COMP` is one enum field that no rule reads for anything but the tool-change WARNING and the arc ERROR; `ToolData.Length` and `ToolData.Radius` are loaded from the tool table and read by nothing; and the specification states that the wear table is not the VM's (VM 2.7: `$SYS_WEAR_Z[99]` is UNKNOWN in STATIC mode). At the same time VM 7 promises a `TOOL_POSE` event with the pose of the tool tip, and VM 9 and VM 10 put exactly that in the kinematics module, level 2, "separate module, later", whose task PL-01 is unstarted. So the tip is promised in four places and computable in none, and no decision covers simulating radius compensation at all.
Recommendation: give the VM the two values and the one derivation that needs no kinematics, and leave the rest where VM 9 puts it. The position store keeps what the program wrote, as D369 settled; the tip is a derived value, not a stored one: the VM subtracts the active `TIP_OFFSET` of the holder along the tool axis of the active `WORKPLANE` and reports the result in the MOTION event and, as `TIP:<axis>`, in the trace. That is a shift along one known axis, so it stays inside level 0 and 1 of VM 9; where the tool axis is not a machine axis the shift is unknown and the VM says so once per program instead of guessing, which is the case under `TILT`, `TILT_AXIS` and `TCPM=ON`. The register radius is carried the same way: the VM keeps `POINT_RADIUS` in the holder state, puts it into the MOTION event beside the compensation flag, and the tool-list analytic prints it per tool and point. The VM does not offset the path: the CAM computes the compensated path itself (opencam D-024), so a VM that offset again would show a path neither the CAM nor the control produces; what the VM does is report the radius the control will apply, so that a wrong register in the program is visible. Wear belongs to the shop and not to the program: it is an optional `wear` key per point in the tool table of the draft below, default 0, and the VM adds it to `POINT_RADIUS` only for what it reports, never to a coordinate. No new NCX word for wear, because it changes between two runs of the same program and would make the file machine-specific. Codes: `VM484` for a `TIP_OFFSET` the VM cannot apply because the tool axis is not a machine axis (a WARNING, once per program), in the tool family of the validation. Alternative: hold the tip in the position store and let every motion write the tip, which is what a simulation wants and what the kinematics module of PL-01 will be able to do properly; it contradicts D369's settled part one, which says NCX neither shifts nor recomputes the coordinates, and it would make every position in the trace differ from the program the operator reads.
Where: VM 2.2 and 2.3 (the holder rows and what is derived from them), VM 6 (the trace rows), VM 7 (the MOTION payload, and the `TOOL_POSE` row, which now says which part of it is level 0 and which level 2), VM 8 (the tool list), VM 9 and 10 (the sentence that the tip offset along a known tool axis is not kinematics); language 4.4 (that the VM derives the tip from `TIP_OFFSET` and applies nothing to the coordinates); `src/Ncx.Core/VirtualMachine/State/HolderState.cs`, `src/Ncx.Core/VirtualMachine/MotionRules.cs`, `src/Ncx.Core/VirtualMachine/Events/MotionEvent.cs` and `MotionEvents.cs`, `src/Ncx.Core/VirtualMachine/Events/StateChanges.cs`, `src/Ncx.Core/VirtualMachine/Validation/ToolValidation.cs` (`VM484`), `src/Ncx.Analytics/ToolList/ToolUse.cs`; `docs/spec/generated/diagnostics.md`; tests in `tests/Ncx.Core.Tests/VirtualMachine/` (a tip derived under `WORKPLANE=XY` and under `WORKPLANE=ZX`, and the WARNING under a tilt), `tests/Ncx.Acceptance/Analytics/ToolListAnalyticTests.cs` with its expected file. Tasks: P1-01, P1-02, P1-05, P4-02 and PL-01, which this draft deliberately does not anticipate. Related D10, D24, D37, D51, D369, D372, D376.

ANSWER:
Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

Accept the recommendation. The position store stays as programmed (D369). The VM derives the tip as the programmed point less `TIP_OFFSET` along the tool axis of the active WORKPLANE, and reports it in the MOTION event and as `TIP:<axis>` in the trace. Under TILT, TILT_AXIS or TCPM=ON it reports WARNING VM484 once per program and derives no tip. `POINT_RADIUS` is held per holder and reported beside COMP. The VM never offsets the path. `wear` from the tool table (D376) is added only to the reported radius. TOOL_POSE level 2 stays with PL-01.
Basis: logical
Source: D369 part one (settled) forbids shifting coordinates. The CAM already compensates the path (opencam D-024), and the controls apply the register values themselves, so a second offset in the VM would show a path that neither CAM nor control makes. A shift along one known machine axis needs no kinematics (VM 9 levels 0-1).
Differs from the recommendation: no
Confidence: high
Code impact: Ncx.Core HolderState, MotionRules and MotionEvent, StateChanges, ToolValidation (VM484); Ncx.Analytics ToolUse.

#### D375 What a compiler writes for a measurement point, and what it must not write
Question: D369's answer, part (d), says the compilers write the registers from the mapping and nothing for a and r except an optional comment where the machine file asks. Two things make the "must not" half worth writing down, because both controls that can carry a value in the program carry it additively. On Heidenhain the `DL`, `DR` and `DR2` of a `TOOL CALL` block are deltas added to the table's values, bounded at about 99.999 mm, and they may come from a Q parameter (iTNC 530 Klartext 2010, p. 165 and p. 193: the compensation value is L plus the TOOL CALL delta plus the table delta; TNC 640 Klartext 892903-18, 10/2019, p. 126 and p. 133, where the program's delta comes from the `TOOL CALL` block or from the correction table and the last programmed value acts). On Siemens `TOFFL`, `TOFF` and `TOFFR` modify the effective length and radius without touching the offset memory, are cleared at program end and survive a change of tool or edge, acting on the new one as well (Grundlagen 03/2013, p. 76-78, the last on p. 78), and `DL` selects an additive sum offset of the edge (Arbeitsvorbereitung 03/2013, p. 388; Funktionshandbuch W1 07/2012, p. 1725). Fanuc has no such form at all: a program can only select a register or write one with `G10` or a macro variable, which changes machine state that survives the program (Machining Center volume, printed p. 250-251). So a compiler that wrote a and r as control values next to the register the point already selects would double the offset on two families and change the machine's setup on the third.
Recommendation: a compiler writes the registers of the mapping of the draft above and nothing else. `TIP_OFFSET` and `POINT_RADIUS` are never written as control values, on any family, because the register the point selects already holds them: they are the shop's measurement, and the control applies it. Where a machine file asks for it with `point_comment = true`, the compiler writes one comment line in the control's comment form (`comment_charset`) naming the point, the tip offset and the register radius, so that a setup sheet can be read off the program. A `TOOL_POINT` of 1 with a = 0 and r = 0 writes nothing at all, which keeps every program written before these words byte for byte as it is today. Where the program's `TIP_OFFSET` or `POINT_RADIUS` disagrees with the tool table of the draft below, the framework reports it once, as that draft says; where the machine has no form for a point other than 1, the INFO of the mapping draft stands. The compilers keep their present register behaviour untouched for programs that carry no point words: `G43 H` and `D` where the `OFFSET` words stand on Fanuc, `D` on Siemens, nothing on Heidenhain under `offsets_with_change`. One consequence to state in the Fanuc section: the same register number means one cell under offset memory A or B and two under C, and whether geometry and wear are separate is parameter 8136 bit 6 on the 0i generation; NCX writes the number the machine file gives and derives nothing from it. Alternative: write the deltas where a control takes them (Heidenhain `DL`/`DR`, Siemens `TOFFL`/`TOFFR`) so that a control whose register is empty still cuts correctly. That is what a CAM-written offset would look like, and it is a trap: the value is then applied twice wherever the shop did measure the point, and on Siemens it is cleared at program end while the register is not, and it survives a change of tool or edge, so a value written for one point acts on the next tool too. (Corrected 2026-10-26 after the manual audit: the TNC 640 page says the program's delta comes from the `TOOL CALL` or the correction table and the last programmed value acts, not that the table overwrites it; and the Siemens offsets survive a change of tool or edge, Grundlagen p. 78, which strengthens the trap.)
Where: language 4.4 (the sentence that the point words are not written to the control), controller-mapping 3 (the point row: register per family, nothing for a and r), controllers/heidenhain.md 4 and 8 (the deltas and why they are not used), controllers/siemens.md 5 and 12 (`TOFFL`, `TOFF`, `TOFFR`, `DL`), controllers/fanuc.md 5 and 10 (`G10`, the memory types, parameter 8136 bit 6); machine-config 3 (`point_comment`); `src/Ncx.Compilers/CompilerBase.Tools.cs`, `src/Ncx.Compilers/Fanuc/FanucToolWords.cs`, `src/Ncx.Compilers/Siemens/SiemensTools.cs`, `src/Ncx.Compilers/Heidenhain/HeidenhainToolCall.cs`, `src/Ncx.Compilers/CompilerBase.Layout.cs` (the comment line); tests in the three compiler folders (a point block writes the register and no value; `point_comment` writes one comment; a program without point words compiles byte for byte as before) and `tests/Ncx.Acceptance/RoundTrips.cs`. Tasks: P3-03, P3-04, P3-06, P5-02 and P3-07. Related D5, D7, D301, D369, D372, D373, D376.

ANSWER:
Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

Accept the recommendation, with the wording corrected on 2026-10-26. A compiler writes only the register the D373 mapping gives (Klartext index, Siemens `D`, Fanuc `H`/`D`). It never writes `TIP_OFFSET` or `POINT_RADIUS` as a control value: no `DL`/`DR`/`DR2` in TOOL CALL, no `TOFFL`/`TOFF`/`TOFFR`/`DL=` on Siemens, no `G10` or macro-variable write on Fanuc. `point_comment = true` writes one comment line (point, a, r). Point 1 with a = r = 0 writes nothing, so existing programs compile byte for byte as before. The Fanuc section states that NCX derives nothing from a register number under memory A/B/C or from parameter 8136 bit 6.
Basis: manual
Source: TNC 640 Klartext 892903-18 p.126, p.133 (the program delta comes from TOOL CALL or the correction table, and the last programmed value acts); iTNC 530 Klartext 2010 p.165, p.193; 840D sl Grundlagen 03/2013 p.76-78 (TOFFL/TOFF/TOFFR survive a change of tool or edge and are cleared at program end); 30i-B Machining Center volume printed p.250-251 (G10 changes machine state). Writing the values would double the offset or leak it into the next tool.
Differs from the recommendation: no
Confidence: high
Code impact: CompilerBase.Tools and the three family tool writers (register only, optional comment line).

#### D376 The measurement points of a tool in the tool table of D10
Question: D370's answer of 2026-10-07 accepts the idea with this new model: tool-table rows per tool and point k, each with the tip offset a and the register radius r, compared with the program's values for that point, a WARNING beyond one output step, no correction of coordinates, and the units of every numeric key stated. The table it extends is settled: D265 (2026-10-01) makes it TOML of `[[tool]]` tables with `number` or `name`, `kind`, `length` and `radius`, an unknown key a WARNING, the default kind `ROTARY`. Three facts of the repository have to be said with it. The units of `length` and `radius` are stated nowhere in machine-config 1, which is the gap D370 named. No shipped machine file names a `tool_table` and no `*.tools.toml` exists in the repository, so the table is specified and unexercised. And `ToolData.Length` and `ToolData.Radius` are loaded and read by nothing: the only consumer of the table is `{kind}` in `CompilerBase.Tools.KindOf`. The control's own tables hold the same values per point, which is what the comparison is against: a Klartext index is a table line with its own length and radius (TNC 640 Setup 10/2019, p. 133 and p. 137), a Siemens edge holds lengths, radius, wear and base dimension in `$TC_DP1`..`$TC_DP25` (Funktionshandbuch Grundfunktionen 07/2012, W1, p. 1596), and a Fanuc register pair holds geometry and wear separately only under memory B or C (Machining Center volume, printed p. 248-249).
Recommendation: `[[tool]]` keeps its five keys and gains optional point rows, `[[tool.point]]` with `k` (integer from 1), `tip_offset` (the a of D-154, not negative), `radius` (the register radius r) and the optional `wear` of D374, default 0. Every numeric key of the tool table, the existing `length` and `radius` among them, is in the units of `units_default` of the machine file, stated in machine-config 1 where D370 asks for it. A tool without point rows is a tool with one point, k = 1, a = 0, r = 0, so every table written for D265 keeps its meaning. The compiler compares the program's `TIP_OFFSET` and `POINT_RADIUS` for the active point with the row and reports `CMP033` as a WARNING naming tool, point and both values when they differ by more than one output step of the tool axis, the step being 10 raised to minus the `[format] decimals` of that address (`CMP030` to `CMP032` are taken by D364, D365 and D370); it is silent where the table has no row for that tool or point, and it never corrects a coordinate, because the program is what the CAM computed and a table the shop edits must not move a path. The VM reads the same rows for what D374 reports, so the file is one source for both. A shipped `machines/fanuc-mill-30i.tools.toml` with two tools, one of them with two points, makes the table exercised at last and gives the request's own test its data. Alternative: keep the points out of the tool table and let the machine file's `[tool_points]` rows of D373 carry a and r as well, which puts the register mapping and the measured values in one place; against it stands that the mapping is the machine's and the measurement is the tool's, and a shop re-measures tools far more often than it renumbers registers.
Where: machine-config 1 (the tool-table paragraph, the `[[tool.point]]` rows, the units sentence); `src/Ncx.Config/ToolTable.cs` (`s_toolKeys` and the point rows), `src/Ncx.Config/ToolData.cs`, `src/Ncx.Compilers/CompilerBase.Tools.cs` (the comparison), `src/Ncx.Compilers/DiagnosticCodes.cs` (`CMP033`), `src/Ncx.Core/VirtualMachine/` where D374 reads the wear; the new `machines/fanuc-mill-30i.tools.toml` and the `tool_table` key of `machines/fanuc-mill-30i.toml`; tests `tests/Ncx.Config.Tests/ToolTableTests.cs` (the rows, the unknown-key WARNING, a tool without rows), `tests/Ncx.Compilers.Tests/ToolTableWarningTests.cs` and a new case for `CMP033`, `tests/Ncx.Acceptance/Examples/FanucCompilerTests.cs`. Tasks: P2-01, P2-04, P3-03 and P1-01. Related D10, D265, D369, D370, D372, D374.

ANSWER:
Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

Accept the recommendation. `[[tool]]` gains optional `[[tool.point]]` rows: `k` (≥ 1), `tip_offset` (≥ 0), `radius` and `wear` (default 0). Every numeric key of the tool table, including `length` and `radius`, is in the machine file's `units_default`, stated in machine-config 1. A tool without rows is point 1 with a = r = 0. The compiler raises WARNING CMP032 (the code Peter gave in D370) when the program's `TIP_OFFSET` or `POINT_RADIUS` differs from the row by more than one output step (10^-decimals of the tool-axis address). It is silent when no row exists and never corrects a coordinate. The VM reads the same rows (D374). Ship `machines/fanuc-mill-30i.tools.toml` with two tools, one with two points.
Basis: logical
Source: The measurement belongs to the tool and the register mapping to the machine (D373), and a shop re-measures far more often than it renumbers. The control tables hold one length and radius per point in the same way: a Klartext index line (TNC 640 Setup 10/2019 p.133, p.137), a Siemens edge `$TC_DP1..25` (Funktionshandbuch 2012 p.1596), and a Fanuc register under memory B/C (B-64484EN-2 p.262-263).
Differs from the recommendation: no
Confidence: high
Code impact: Ncx.Config ToolTable/ToolData (point rows), CompilerBase.Tools (CMP032), the new tools.toml and the `tool_table` key of fanuc-mill-30i.toml.

### Twelfth round: corrections from the manual audit, asked 2026-10-26

On 2026-10-26 the decision record was audited against the manual connector cnc-manuals, about 1300 control and machine manuals (summary `manual-audit-2026-10-26.md`, detailed reports in `manual-audit-2026-10-26/`). Of the answers given on 2026-10-07, two do not hold against the manuals (summary, section 2). D361 rests on a wrong fact: the Nakamura code it takes for rigid tapping on the lower path, `M429`, is the work-counter increment. D190's change 2 holds for TAP on every family, but not for REAM on every control. The two drafts below correct them. D377 replaces the lower-path table of D361 and gives NCX a rule for a channel that has no rigid tapping. D378 lets REAM's feed-out plane differ per machine. D361 and D190 stay recorded above as they were answered: their Question, Recommendation, Where and ANSWER are not edited, and these drafts change them only once answered. Every controller fact below names the connector's document and page. These drafts were checked again in the connector on 2026-10-26, and that check found one fact the audit did not have: the Heidenhain generations differ on REAM too (D378).

#### D377 A channel without rigid tapping, in place of D361's lower-path M429 table
Question: D361's ANSWER (Peter, 2026-10-07: "Accept as recommended") rests on a fact from D256's evidence, that on the Nakamura "M29 is rigid tapping on the upper path and M429 on the lower path". From it the answer takes two things: a `[[cycle]] name = "TAP" channel = 2 before = "M429 S{rpm}"` table in machines/nakamura-ntjx.toml beside the channel-less one, and the key `channel` for the `[[cycle]]` override of machine-config 6, which the answer borrows from the function tables of machine-config 5 (D56) for this one case. The manual audit of 2026-10-26 (summary section 2, report 13) found the fact wrong, and the connector confirms it. `M429` is "work counter data increment": the M-code table of the Nakamura Programming Manual-1 4810004EDG-1 (Super NTJX, 2015) lists it on p.79 and p.98, and p.148-149 item (35) says that a value on the hardware work counter increases by one, once PMC parameter D109 is set to 2. The WY-250L manual 4810004EEE (2020) gives M429 the same row (p.79, p.99). The rigid-tapping chapter of 4810004EDG-1 (p.310-312) has one mode code, `M29`, for the spindle and for the rotary tool, started "using the M29 command instead of M3" with the spindle stopped. Its M-code table 17-4 (p.311-312) lists M29, M86, M94, M792-M795, M41 and M98 P9000, and no lower-path code. The notes on p.312 restrict the mode per turret: "With WTW/WTS, the spindle rigid tapping is valid only for the upper turret", and "With STW/STS, the spindle rigid tapping is valid only for the upper turret and the lower turret of the R-unit". The German Nakamura Programmierhandbuch (Allgemein, 2019) gives the same per-spindle rule for the WT machines: on the main spindle rigid tapping works only with the upper turret, and on the back spindle only with the lower turret (p.77-78). Its M-code list for rigid tapping (p.77) adds `M494`, the lower milling spindle's reversal for a tapping cycle, beside `M94` for the upper one. No connector manual shows another rigid-tapping code for the lower path. Nothing of D361 is applied yet: `s_entryKeys` of src/Ncx.Config/Cycles/CycleCatalogLoader.Entries.cs:9-14 has no `channel`, and M429 stands in no file outside docs/decisions. So no code needs undoing, but the answer cannot be applied as given, for three reasons. First, the table would write a wrong code. Under it, CYCLE=TAP on the lower path would increment the work counter and then run a `G84` without the mode, that is tapping with a compensating chuck (D256, D359), with the solid holder the CAM chose for a rigid tap. Second, the `channel` key loses the only case D361 gave it. Third, NCX still has no rule for a channel whose path cannot tap rigidly at all, and the Nakamura notes show this is a real case: a WTW or WTS lower turret. Today CYCLE=TAP compiles on every channel of every Fanuc-family machine to the catalog's `M29 S{rpm}` line (CycleEntry.OverriddenBy inherits it, and D361 measured it on machines/nakamura-ntjx.toml), so on such a turret NCX writes a mode the builder says is not valid there, with no diagnostic. The other families give the same picture. On every control, whether a spindle taps rigidly is a property of that spindle or path, set by the builder. Where it cannot, the control offers only tapping with a compensating chuck, a different cycle with a different holder, and never turns one into the other. Fanuc: parameter 5200, whose bit 0 decides whether rigid tapping needs the M code of parameter 5210, is of data type "Bit path" (30i-A Parameterhandbuch B-63950EN-03 p.339). A two-path lathe can tap rigidly with the spindle of the other path only when bit 4 (SPR) of parameter 3703 is set, or by an address P on the M29 S block under multi-spindle control (0i-D Connection Manual B-64303EN-1/02 p.882). Heidenhain: cycle 207 needs a machine and TNC prepared by the builder and works only on machines with a controlled spindle (TNC 620 Zyklen 679295-12 p.101), and with a unipolar spindle tapping is possible only with a compensating chuck (TNC 640 Technisches Handbuch 892899-18 p.2272). Cycle 206 begins with "Längenausgleichsfutter einwechseln", load the length-compensating chuck (iTNC 530 Lotse Klartext 340490-04 p.55). Siemens: ISO `G84` can be used only where the drilling spindle can switch to position-controlled operation (840D sl/828D Programmierhandbuch ISO-Fräsen 2012 p.103), and `CYCLE840` is the separate cycle for tapping with a compensating chuck (Bedienhandbuch Drehen 2013 p.297). The Mori Seiki half of D361 is not affected: the connector shows `M329 G84` and `M329 G88` as its synchronized tapping cycles (NT-NTX Programmieranleitung NTX1000SZM PX-NT 4-K0DEEN 2011 p.467, p.470).
Recommendation: Correct the data, and give the `channel` key the case it really has. The data: drop the channel-2 M429 table from D361's answer. machines/nakamura-ntjx.toml and its copy keep the catalog's `M29 S{rpm}` on both paths. The comment at :241 then cites this draft and the p.312 notes: M29 is the only Nakamura rigid-tapping code the manuals give; whether the NTJX taps rigidly on the lower path is not in any connector manual and is to be confirmed on the machine; and where it does not, the file adds the table below for channel 2. The Mori Seiki half of D361 (`M329 S{rpm}` as `before`, SYNC_TAP out of [func]) and the controller-mapping 8 and fanuc.md 9 sentences stand as answered. The rule: keep `channel` on a `[[cycle]]` override as D361 accepted it, with its lookup unchanged. The loader keeps both the table of a channel and the channel-less table, and a compiler takes the table of the channel it compiles, falling back to the channel-less one. The override also gets one new key, `available`, a boolean whose default is `true`. `[[cycle]] name = "TAP" channel = 2 available = false` says that the machine has no form of TAP on channel 2. Where a cycle's entry is unavailable on the channel being compiled, the compiler reports an ERROR and writes nothing for the cycle. The code is CMP004, the next free code of the compiler framework's range for what a machine takes at all (CMP001-CMP009 in src/Ncx.Compilers/DiagnosticCodes.cs; CMP001-CMP003 are taken). It is a framework code because the override is the same on every family; CMP380 of the Fanuc range means that a catalog does not name the cycle at all, and that is not the case here. The ERROR names the cycle and the channel. The compiler writes no substitute. It does not write the catalog's line, a mode the builder says is not valid on that path, and it does not write a bare `G84`, which is TAP_COMPENSATING (D359), the other machining with the other holder. The program then either taps on a channel that can, or names TAP_COMPENSATING where the shop puts a compensating chuck on that turret. That choice is the CAM's, because only the CAM knows the holder. `available = false` without `channel` removes the cycle from the whole machine, for example TAP on a Heidenhain without a controlled spindle. In a catalog file, `channel` and `available` mean nothing, because a catalog serves every machine of its family. There they are the WARNING CFG157, the next free code of the catalog range (CFG150-CFG199 in src/Ncx.Config/Cycles/DiagnosticCodes.Cycles.cs; CFG150-CFG155 are taken and CFG156 is D358's), and the entry is loaded as if they were absent. D359's rule stays as answered: an entry without a `before` key counts as absent where the machine's TAP has `before = ""`. `available` could express that case later, but this draft does not change D359. Reason: the fact the manuals give is not a second code but a path with no rigid tapping, so the machine file must be able to say so. It says it with the key D361 already accepted plus one boolean. The compiler then refuses to write a silent wrong code, which is the fault D256 and D361 set out to remove. Alternative 1: compile CYCLE=TAP on such a channel as TAP_COMPENSATING with a WARNING. The program then runs, but with the solid holder the CAM chose for a rigid tap, under a cycle that does not keep feed and spindle in step (our reading of the three families' pages above). That is the silent substitution D256 took away. Alternative 2: no key. The release names "rigid tapping on a path without it" as a known limit (P7-03), and the compiler goes on writing the catalog's M29 on every channel, as main does. Not proposed: on the WT machines the restriction depends on the spindle the turret works on, not only on the channel (Programmierhandbuch 2019 p.77-78). That would need a key `workpiece = "MAIN"` or `"SUB"` on the override as well ([workpiece], D57). No shipped machine file is a WT, so the draft leaves it for the machine that needs it.
Where: machine-config 6 (the `before` bullet, the `channel` key D361 adds, the new `available` key and the CFG157 sentence); machine-config 5 (the `channel` key of a function table, D56, cited); controllers/fanuc.md 9 rule 9 and 10 rule 7 (one sentence: a channel without the mode is CMP004, not the catalog's line); language 4.7.1 (the D256 sentence on the other machining, cited). Data: machines/nakamura-ntjx.toml:241 and docs/spec/examples/machines/nakamura-ntjx.toml (no channel-2 M429 table; the comment above); cycles/fanuc.toml:62-64 (the override comment names `channel` and `available`). Code: src/Ncx.Config/Cycles/CycleCatalogLoader.Entries.cs (`s_entryKeys` at line 9, `channel` and `available`); src/Ncx.Config/Cycles/DiagnosticCodes.Cycles.cs (CFG157); src/Ncx.Core/Machine/CycleEntry.cs (OverriddenBy at 236, the two keys); src/Ncx.Core/Machine/CycleCatalog.cs (Override at 128, Find at 30 and 50, the per-channel pick) and MachineConfig.cs (CycleEntries at 152); src/Ncx.Compilers/DiagnosticCodes.cs (CMP004) and the cycle writers that look an entry up: src/Ncx.Compilers/Fanuc/FanucCycles.cs (WriteBefore at 287 and the entry lookup in front of it), src/Ncx.Compilers/Heidenhain/HeidenhainCycles.cs, src/Ncx.Compilers/Siemens/SiemensCycles.cs. Tests: tests/Ncx.Config.Tests/Cycles/MachineCycleEntriesTests.cs (a channel table, an unavailable entry, the fallback) and CycleDiagnosticCodesTests.cs; tests/Ncx.Compilers.Tests/Fanuc/FanucCyclesTests.cs (CYCLE=TAP on an unavailable channel is CMP004 and writes neither M29 nor G84; on the other channel it writes M29 S); tests/Ncx.Compilers.Tests/DiagnosticCodesTests.cs. Row 211 of docs/implementation/03-open-questions.md (D361) and the new row for this draft. Related: D361, D256, D359, D56, D57, D162.

ANSWER:
Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

Accept the recommendation as drafted. Drop the channel-2 `M429` table. Both paths of machines/nakamura-ntjx.toml (and its spec copy) keep the catalog's `M29 S{rpm}`, and the comment at :241 cites D377 and 4810004EDG-1 p.312. The `[[cycle]]` override keeps `channel` (lookup: the table for the compiled channel first, then the channel-less one) and gains `available` (bool, default true). If a cycle is `available = false` on the channel being compiled, or on the whole machine when `channel` is absent, the compiler reports ERROR CMP004, which names the cycle and the channel. It writes nothing for that cycle: no `M29` line and no bare `G84`/TAP_COMPENSATING substitute. In a catalog file, `channel` and `available` raise WARNING CFG157 and the loader ignores them. D359 is unchanged. The Mori Seiki half of D361 (`M329 S{rpm}`) stands as answered.
Basis: manual
Source: Nakamura Super NTJX Programming Manual-1 4810004EDG-1 p.79, p.148-149 (M429 is the work counter), p.310-312 (M29 is the only rigid-tapping code; WTW/WTS allow spindle rigid tapping on the upper turret only); WY-250L 4810004EEE p.79, p.99; Nakamura Programmierhandbuch Allgemein 2019 p.77-78; Fanuc parameter 5200 is a path parameter (30i-A Parameterhandbuch B-63950EN-03 p.339). I checked that CMP004 and CFG157 are still free on main: src/Ncx.Compilers/DiagnosticCodes.cs uses CMP001-CMP003, and DiagnosticCodes.Cycles.cs uses CFG150-CFG155, with CFG156 going to D358.
Differs from the recommendation: no
Confidence: high
Code impact: Ncx.Config (cycle loader keys `channel` and `available`, CFG157), Ncx.Core CycleCatalog (per-channel pick), compilers (CMP004 in the cycle writers), plus the Nakamura machine-file comment.

#### D378 The plane REAM feeds out to, per machine, in place of D190's change 2 for REAM
Question: D190's ANSWER (Peter, 2026-10-07) accepted change 2: TAP and REAM feed out only to CLEARANCE, and under CYCLE_RETRACT=SAFE the rest of the way to SAFE is a rapid. The manual evidence under that answer says that Siemens CYCLE84 and CYCLE85 retract at the thread or RFF feed to the reference plane and then go to the retract plane with G0. For that it cites the 2008 Zyklen manual (p.73), whose CYCLE85 pages the connector cannot read: only the index of the 840D Programmierhandbuch Zyklen 2008 is extracted, and it places CYCLE85 at printed page 72. The manual audit of 2026-10-26 (summary section 2, report 08) found that change 2 holds for TAP everywhere and for REAM on Heidenhain and Fanuc, but not for CYCLE85 on an 840D sl. The connector confirms the Siemens part and adds a Heidenhain part. Siemens 840D sl: in the reaming sequence, step 4 is "Rückzug auf Rückzugsebene mit programmierten Rückzugsvorschub FR", that is retract to the retract plane at the programmed retract feed FR. The Bedienhandbuch Fräsen 2013 says so on p.308 and the Bedienhandbuch Drehen 2013 on p.287, and cycles/siemens.toml maps the retract plane RTP to SAFE. CYCLE84, by contrast, retracts to the safety clearance and then goes to the retract plane with G0 (Fräsen 2013 p.316), so TAP holds. Fanuc: table 5.1 (a) gives G85 and G89 the retraction "Feed", and the six operations end with "Retraction to point R level" and "Rapid traverse up to the initial point" (30i-B Bedienung Fräsen B-64484EN-2 p.56-57; G85 on p.76). On the lathe, G85 and G89 return from point Z to point R at double the cutting feedrate, and at the cutting feedrate itself in the Series 15-T format (30i-B Bedienung Drehen B-64484EN-1 p.299; 0i-F Plus Bedienung Drehen B-64694EN-1 p.294). The Nakamura G85 works like G84 without the spindle reversal (Programmierhandbuch 2019 p.78). So the Fanuc target is R on mill and lathe; only the lathe's retract speed differs, and that concerns change 1, not change 2. Heidenhain differs by generation, which the audit did not find. On the iTNC 530 and the older TNC 620, cycle 201 moves "im Vorschub F zurück auf den Sicherheits-Abstand", back to the safety clearance at feed F, and from there with FMAX to the 2nd safety clearance (iTNC 530 Zyklen 670 388-12 p.81; TNC 620 Zyklen 679295-12 p.69). On the TNC 640 and the TNC 128, step 4 reads that the control moves the tool at feed F back to the safety clearance or to the 2nd safety clearance, Q204 acting only when it is programmed larger than Q200. The FMAX step is gone (TNC 640 Zyklen 892905-18, NC-SW 34059x-10, p.90; TNC 128 Programmierung Klartext 819494-15 p.323). Our reading is that the newer controls feed out all the way to Q204, as the 840D sl does. TAP is unchanged on the TNC 640: cycles 206 and 207 retract to the safety clearance and go with FMAX to the 2nd one (p.133, p.136). So the plane REAM feeds out to is not a constant of a controller family. It differs between Siemens and the other two, and within Heidenhain between the generations that share cycles/heidenhain.toml. So neither a catalog entry nor a rule per `controller` can carry it. On main, src/Ncx.Core/VirtualMachine/CycleRules.cs:164 still rapids REAM out to the retract plane and feeds TAP all the way to it (the D190 TODO(question) at lines 138-144). `[cycles]` reads only `catalog` (src/Ncx.Config/MachineConfigLoader.Variables.cs:8); D357's two keys are not applied yet. The difference is the feed time over SAFE minus CLEARANCE on every reamed hole, in the runtime estimate and in the CAM's simulation, which reads the same rules (opencam D-061).
Recommendation: A third optional key in `[cycles]` of the machine file, beside D357's `chip_break_lift` and `peck_clearance`: `ream_feed_out`, with the value `"CLEARANCE"` or `"SAFE"`. It is the plane up to which REAM feeds out at CYCLE_F (D190 change 1) before the rest of the retract is a rapid. It acts only under CYCLE_RETRACT=SAFE; under CLEARANCE, REAM feeds out to CLEARANCE and stops, as change 2 says. An absent key means the documented behaviour of the control family, as D357's answer set for its keys: CLEARANCE on Fanuc and Heidenhain, SAFE on Siemens. So no shipped machine file needs the key. The three Siemens files (siemens-840dsl-mill, millturn1, dmg-ctx-840d) get SAFE from their family, heidenhain-itnc530.toml and the four Fanuc files get CLEARANCE, and a future TNC 640 or TNC 128 file writes `ream_feed_out = "SAFE"`. The values are the NCX words of the two planes, and the key is named after the NCX quantity like D357's keys. It avoids "retract" for the reason D357 gave: the configuration already uses that word for the `[retract]` table and for CYCLE_RETRACT. Any other value is the existing ERROR CFG005 (ValueNotAllowed in src/Ncx.Config/DiagnosticCodes.Loading.cs), so no new code is needed. TAP keeps change 2 on every family and gets no key, since every manual above agrees on it. The VM reads the key in CycleRules.Drill when it writes the D190 sequence into VM 3.3. The CAM's simulation reads the same key with the same default, as D190's answer requires. The compilers write nothing from the key, because no native parameter selects the plane: CYCLE85's RFF and Heidenhain's Q208 are feeds, not targets. Not in this draft: the Fanuc lathe's G85 and G89 return at double the cutting feed. That is a speed, not a target, so it belongs to change 1. The estimate keeps CYCLE_F there unless the maintainer extends change 1. Reason: the motion differs per machine, not per family, so the machine file is where it can be stated, in the table that D357 already made "what this machine does with cycles", with a default that reproduces the manuals of each family. Alternative 1: accept the difference. Keep change 2 for REAM on every machine, and name the 840D sl CYCLE85 and the newer Heidenhain cycle 201 in VM 3.3 as known deviations. That needs no key and no code, but on those machines the estimate is short by the feed time over SAFE minus CLEARANCE per reamed hole, and the CAM shows a rapid where the machine feeds. Alternative 2: a rule in code keyed on `controller` and `dialect` (Siemens SAFE, TNC 640 SAFE, the rest CLEARANCE). That needs no key either, but it ties a motion rule to dialect strings that no section lists for the TNC 640 or TNC 128, and a machine whose builder changed the cycle could not say so.
Where: machine-config 6 (`[cycles]`, the new key beside `catalog` and D357's `chip_break_lift` and `peck_clearance`); ncx-virtual-machine 3.3 (the D190 sequence and the ExpandCycles sentence: REAM feeds out to the key's plane) and 8 (the runtime estimate); controllers/siemens.md 7 (the CYCLE85 row: the retract at RFF to the retract plane, cited) and heidenhain.md 5 (cycle 201: the two generations, cited); cycles/siemens.toml:85 (the RFF comment) and cycles/heidenhain.toml:73 (the REAM entry, a comment on the generations). Code: src/Ncx.Core/Machine/CyclesConfig.cs (the key, beside D357's); src/Ncx.Config/MachineConfigLoader.Variables.cs (`s_cyclesKeys` at line 8 and ReadCycles); src/Ncx.Core/VirtualMachine/CycleRules.cs (Drill: line 164 and the TODO(question) at lines 138-144, answered together with D190 and D357); src/Ncx.Analytics/Runtime/RuntimeEstimator.cs. Tests: tests/Ncx.Core.Tests/VirtualMachine/CycleCallTests.cs (ExpandCycles: REAM on a Siemens machine feeds to SAFE, on a Fanuc and a Heidenhain machine feeds to CLEARANCE and rapids on, the key overrides both, TAP feeds to CLEARANCE everywhere); tests/Ncx.Config.Tests/MachineConfigLoaderTests.cs (the key, and CFG005 for another value); tests/Ncx.Acceptance/Analytics/RuntimeAnalyticTests.cs. Row 11 of docs/implementation/03-open-questions.md (D190) and the new row for this draft. Related: D190, D357, D164, D160, D178.

ANSWER:
Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

Accept the recommendation. Add an optional `[cycles] ream_feed_out = "CLEARANCE" | "SAFE"` beside D357's `chip_break_lift` and `peck_clearance`. It applies only under CYCLE_RETRACT=SAFE: REAM feeds at CYCLE_F up to that plane, and the rest of the retract is a rapid. Under CLEARANCE it feeds to CLEARANCE and stops. When the key is absent, the family default applies: CLEARANCE on Fanuc and Heidenhain, SAFE on Siemens. A future TNC 640 or TNC 128 machine file writes `"SAFE"`. Any other value raises ERROR CFG005. TAP keeps change 2 on every family and gets no key. Only the VM (CycleRules.Drill), the runtime estimate and the CAM simulation read the key; compilers write nothing from it. The Fanuc lathe's double-feed G85/G89 return stays outside this decision (it belongs to change 1).
Basis: manual
Source: 840D sl Bedienhandbuch Fräsen 2013 p.308 and Drehen 2013 p.287 (CYCLE85 retracts at FR to the retract plane); Fräsen 2013 p.316 (CYCLE84 goes to SC, then G0); 30i-B B-64484EN-2 p.56-57, p.76; iTNC 530 Zyklen 670388-12 p.81 and TNC 620 679295-12 p.69 (feed to Q200, then FMAX); TNC 640 Zyklen 892905-18 p.90 and TNC 128 819494-15 p.323 (feed to Q204).
Differs from the recommendation: no
Confidence: high
Code impact: Ncx.Core CyclesConfig and CycleRules.Drill (line 164 and the D190 TODO), MachineConfigLoader `s_cyclesKeys`, RuntimeEstimator.

Questions that came up on 2026-10-26 while coding the decisions D256, D344 and D346 (rows 1 to 4 of "Manual audit 2026-10-26" in `docs/implementation/03-open-questions.md` and three more from the reviews), and two follow-ups of the manual audit to answers of 2026-10-07 that keep the maintainer's answer and correct a fact under it. #### D379 SLOT on SINUMERIK 840D sl (follow-up to D162)
Question: D162's answer (Peter, 2026-10-07) maps the catalog name SLOT to the Siemens SLOT1. The manual audit (manual-audit-2026-10-26.md section 2) found that on the 840D sl SLOT1 is a longitudinal slot ("Längsnut"), not the slots-on-a-circle cycle of the older packages. What does the Siemens SLOT entry map to, and what does the reader do with the older form?
Recommendation: none; the question went straight to the delegated decision.
Where: cycles/siemens.toml (SLOT, CIRC_SLOT); Siemens reader cycle table; D162

ANSWER:
Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

Peter's answer to D162 stands: one name means one cycle with one word set. The follow-up corrects only the fact his answer assumed. On the 840D sl (Operate cycles), `SLOT1` is "Längsnut", a single straight slot. Its `NUM` must be 1, `RAD` and `INDA` are reserved, and several slots are made by `MCALL` with a position pattern. So SLOT1 is Heidenhain 253's counterpart. The "slots on a pitch circle" meaning belongs only to the older 840D SLOT1. (1) cycles/README.md defines SLOT as "one straight slot at the call position" and names 253 and the sl `SLOT1` as its natives. CIRC_SLOT names 254 and the sl `SLOT2`, the latter only with `NUM` = 1, because SLOT2's `NUM` counts circular slots on a circle. (2) cycles/siemens.toml gets a `SLOT` entry, native `SLOT1`, with the full sl signature (31 positions: RTP … _AMODE). It maps the same six words as 253: SAFE=RTP, SURFACE=RFP, CLEARANCE=SDIS (absolute_from_surface), DEPTH=_DP, PECK=_MID, CYCLE_F=FFD (the infeed feed, as Q206 is). (3) The compiler writes `NUM`=1, `RAD` and `INDA` empty, the `_DMODE` thousands digit 1 ("Funktionserweiterung SLOT1"), the `_AMODE` ones digit 2 (Z1 absolute), and `_CPA`/`_CPO` = the call position. (4) The reader converts a SLOT1 to SLOT only in the sl form: `_DMODE` thousands digit 1, `NUM` empty/0/1, `RAD` and `INDA` empty or 0, and `_CPA`/`_CPO` equal to the current plane position or supplied by an MCALL pattern. Any other SLOT1, the older pattern form included, stays native as CYCLE:SIEMENS (D94). The same rule applies to SLOT2 with `NUM` > 1. (5) The geometry positions (length, width, angle, reference point: 253's Q218, Q219, Q374, Q367 against LENG, WID, STA1 and the `_GMODE` thousands digit) get NCX words in both catalogs together or in neither. This decision maps none of them, because the order of Q367 against `_GMODE` has not been checked.
Basis: manual
Source: 840D sl NC-Programmierung SW4.92 (2019) p.1052-1055 (SLOT1 "Längsnut": NUM "Anzahl der Nuten = 1", RAD/INDA "reserviert", _DMODE thousands digit 1 "Funktionserweiterung SLOT1", _AMODE ones digit 0 compat/1 inc/2 abs; the note on p.1055 says NUM/RAD/INDA are no longer shown and that several slots are made by MCALL plus a position pattern; SLOT2 p.1055 has NUM, RAD, INDA); 840D sl Bedienhandbuch Fräsen 2013 p.359 and Drehen 2013 p.408 ("Mit dem Zyklus Längsnut … eine beliebige Längsnut fräsen"); 840D sl Programmierung BS.000504 p.719-720. The old meaning: 840D Zyklen 2004 (Index edition) p.122-123.
Differs from the recommendation: yes. The D162 draft and the manual-library note treated SLOT1 as a pattern and left Siemens without a SLOT. Peter's answer now gets a Siemens entry with the version gate above.
Confidence: medium (the sl facts are high; the call-position and MCALL handling in (4) is logical)
Code impact: cycles/siemens.toml (new SLOT entry, CIRC_SLOT/SLOT2 NUM gate), cycles/README.md, the Siemens reader's catalog match (version and NUM gate).

#### D380 The `_AMODE` ones digit of CYCLE830 (correction to D181)
Question: D181's answer (Peter, 2026-10-07) takes the CYCLE81 to CYCLE86 meaning of the `_AMODE` ones digit for CYCLE830. The manual audit found that CYCLE830 inverts it. Which value does the compiler write, and how does the reader take an omitted or 0 value?
Recommendation: none; the question went straight to the delegated decision.
Where: cycles/siemens.toml (DEEP_HOLE); Siemens compiler and reader cycle tables; D181

ANSWER:
Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

Peter's answer stands. One fact is corrected. In `CYCLE830` (position 38, `_AMODE`), the ones digit sets the depth `_DP` as 0 = incremental and 1 = absolute. This is the reverse of CYCLE81 to CYCLE86, where 0 = compatibility (DP/DPR), 1 = incremental, 2 = absolute. Because an omitted parameter is 0, a CYCLE830 without `_AMODE` has an incremental `_DP`. Reader: if the ones digit is 1, DEPTH = `_DP`. If it is 0 (or `_AMODE` is omitted), DEPTH = RFP less |`_DP`|, counted away from the retract plane. This is the same rule as DPR (D334), with Z0 as the reference, as for every Z1 (ink) of the sl cycles. Compiler: always writes `_AMODE` with ones digit 1 and DEPTH absolute. The other digits are 0 unless a mapped word sets them. The ten-thousands digit is FDEP abs/inc with 0 = incremental, coded the same reversed way. Also correct the shipped DEEP_HOLE entry of cycles/siemens.toml to the full 41-position signature. Its `CYCLE_F = "F"` becomes `CYCLE_F = "S_FB"` (position 18, "Bohrvorschub"), as the D181 manual note already said. The TODO(question) at lines 106-107 is then answered.
Basis: manual
Source: 840D sl NC-Programmierung SW4.92 (2019) p.1119-1123 (CYCLE830 signature; p.1120 _DP "abs/ink (siehe _AMODE EINER)"; p.1122-1123 _AMODE ones digit "0 = inkrementell, 1 = absolut"; ten-thousands digit the same for FDEP). The CYCLE81 contrast is in 840D sl Programmierung BS.000504 p.752-753 (_AMODE ones digit "0 = Kompatibilität aus Programmierung DP/DPR, 1 = inkrementell"). The rule that an omitted parameter is 0: Zyklen 01/2008 p.18.
Differs from the recommendation: no (the recommendation left the mode to the manual; this supplies it)
Confidence: high for the coding; medium that the incremental reference is RFP
Code impact: cycles/siemens.toml DEEP_HOLE entry, and the Siemens drilling reader/compiler (DrillingFamily.Siemens.cs) for the CYCLE830 depth mode.

#### D381 RET in a SINUMERIK subprogram declared SAVE
Question: 840D sl NC-Programmierung SW4.92 p.523 says RET is used in a subprogram without SAVE, while Siemens's own DISPLOF examples end `PROC ... SAVE DISPLOF` with RET (SW4.94 EN p.508). D344's code took the conservative reading: JUMP=END in a SAVE subprogram is the ERROR CMP597. May RET, plain or parameterized, stand in a SAVE subprogram?
Recommendation: none; the question went straight to the delegated decision.
Where: src/Ncx.Compilers/Siemens/SiemensFlow.cs WriteJumpToEndInSubprogram; DiagnosticCodes.Siemens.cs CMP597; 03-open-questions "Manual audit 2026-10-26" row 1

ANSWER:
Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

RET is allowed in a `SAVE` subprogram, plain and parameterized. The compiler writes `RET("<end label>",,$P_STACK)` for `JUMP=END` in a `SAVE` subprogram exactly as in any other subprogram, and drops the ERROR CMP597 path from `WriteJumpToEndInSubprogram`. Retire CMP597 (keep the code number reserved, do not reuse it). The plain subprogram end stays `M17`, as today. Remove both TODO(question) markers.
Basis: manual
Source: The p.523 sentence is about the G64 effect of RET. The 840D/810D Arbeitsvorbereitung 2006 p.92 says, after "RET ... wenn ein G64-Bahnsteuerbetrieb ... nicht unterbrochen werden soll": "Voraussetzung dafür ist, dass das Unterprogramm kein SAVE-Attribut besitzt". The HLL training 2010 p.357 (4.5) says the same. So SAVE takes away RET's continuous-path benefit; it does not forbid RET. Siemens's own examples use `PROC ... SAVE DISPLOF ... RET`: SW4.92 p.518, SW4.94 EN p.508, the ISO-Dialekt guide `PROC CYCLE328 SAVE DISPLOF ... N99 RET` (https://www.scribd.com/document/376074812/PGM-pdf). For parameterized RET, 840D sl NC-Programmierung SW4.92 p.526 (connector p.526, "Randbedingungen") says a return over several levels evaluates the SAVE of each level. That only makes sense if a SAVE level can be left by RET. The failure case is also safe: if a control rejected RET there, it would raise an interpreter alarm and would not move wrongly.
Differs from the recommendation: yes: the conservative reading (ERROR CMP597) is replaced by allowing RET.
Confidence: medium
Code impact: Siemens compiler: `SiemensFlow.WriteJumpToEndInSubprogram` loses the `DeclaresSave` branch; `DiagnosticCodes.Siemens.cs` CMP597 is retired; the tests for CMP597 are inverted.

#### D382 Rounding of SINUMERIK DIV with a negative operand
Question: D346 writes DIV as INT(a / b). No manual shows a negative operand: does DIV truncate towards zero or round towards minus infinity? The code keeps such a block RAW (RDR506) unless both operands are number literals of 0 or more.
Recommendation: none; the question went straight to the delegated decision.
Where: src/Ncx.Readers/Siemens/SiemensExpression.cs; RDR506; 03-open-questions "Manual audit 2026-10-26" row 2

ANSWER:
Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

Keep today's behaviour. A `DIV` stays `RAW` with WARNING RDR506 unless both operands are number literals ≥ 0. Add one safe widening: also convert `DIV` when both operands are integer-valued literals (either sign) and the divisor divides the dividend exactly (e.g. `-8 DIV 2 = -4`). Both rounding rules give the same result there. The Siemens compiler still writes no `DIV`.
Basis: logical (web and manuals checked, nothing found)
Source: Two web searches (Siemens support/forum, "-7 DIV 2", German and English) found no statement or example with a negative operand. The manuals give only non-negative cases: SW4.94 EN p.442, ONE SW6.14 p.440, and BS.000504 p.73-74 (connector), all with `7 DIV 4.1 = 1` and `7 MOD 4.1 = 2.9`. MOD's sign rule for negatives is not documented either, so the identity a = (a DIV b)·b + a MOD b settles nothing. Truncating and flooring differ by one only when the quotient is not exact, so the exact case is safe. Every other case stays a visible RAW and is not a guess.
Differs from the recommendation: no (adds the exact-quotient widening only)
Confidence: high (that the rounding stays undecided); medium (the widening)
Code impact: `SiemensExpression.cs:174`: accept literal operands with an exact integer quotient; the TODO stays for the general case.

#### D383 M6, T, G43, G44, G49 between the Fanuc M29 S line and G84
Question: D256 reads G84 as rigid tapping when the M29 S line stands in an earlier block. Do a tool change, a T word or a length offset between the line and G84 cancel the mode or raise an alarm? The code stops the walk unseen and keeps the G84 RAW.
Recommendation: none; the question went straight to the delegated decision.
Where: src/Ncx.Readers/Fanuc/FanucReader.cs MarkBeforeLines; 03-open-questions "Manual audit 2026-10-26" row 3

ANSWER:
Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

Keep today's behaviour. The walk back from the G84 ends unseen at a block with `M6`, a `T` word, `G43`, `G44` or `G49`, so the cycle stays `RAW` with the "does not see" reason. The control does not cancel the mode on its own for these blocks. The manual does not raise an alarm for them either. Whether they work depends on the machine. Change the TODO(question) to a plain comment that cites this decision.
Basis: manual + logical
Source: B-64484EN-2 p.104 (connector p.104, "M29"): an S command or an axis movement between M29 and G84 raises PS0203. The 0i-D Connection Manual B-64303EN-1 p.899 (note 4) says the same. Tool changes (M6, T) are handled by the PMC ladder or by a macro the machine builder writes (B-64484EN-2 p.85-86 programs them with Z moves, e.g. `G49 Z250.0 T15 M6`), and such a macro moves the Z axis or orients the spindle. Whether G43/G44 with no axis word moves at once depends on a parameter. Any of these then raises PS0203 or drops the PMC rigid mode (B-64303EN-1 p.927-928, 10.13.16.8). A RAW block is the safe reading. CAM posts put `M29 S` directly before the cycle, so real programs rarely hit this.
Differs from the recommendation: no
Confidence: medium
Code impact: none (marker text only, `FanucReader.cs:861`)

#### D384 `G0 Z10. M29 S500` before G84
Question: A group-01 code in the same block as M29 S: does the M29 hold for the G84 that follows? The code keeps the G84 RAW with its own reason.
Recommendation: none; the question went straight to the delegated decision.
Where: src/Ncx.Readers/Fanuc/FanucReader.cs; FanucState.BeforeLineWithACancel; 03-open-questions "Manual audit 2026-10-26" row 4

ANSWER:
Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

Keep `RAW` with the reason `BeforeLineWithACancel`. Add the cited facts to the reason text: the manuals state the group-01 cancel only after tapping (B-64303EN-1 p.927), and the one builder example of a move in the M29 block has no G code (Mori NTX1000SZM p.281-282). A modal move in the M29 block with no G code (`Z10. M29 S500`) stays a valid place for the line, as today.
Basis: logical
Source: One web search for `G00 ... M29 S` in one block found only separate-block practice (e.g. https://www.emastercam.com/forums/topic/23663-rigid-tapping-on-fanuc/). The PS0203 rule only covers what stands between M29 and G84 (B-64484EN-2 p.104). The cancel by a group-01 code is a PMC sequence on the falling ENB edge (B-64303EN-1 p.927-928). Whether an explicit G00 in the M29 block starts that sequence is decided by the builder's ladder, not the CNC. If the reader guesses wrong, it reads rigid tapping as floating-chuck tapping or the other way round, which breaks the tap. RAW shows the problem to the user at no real cost, because removing the redundant `G0` makes the program readable.
Differs from the recommendation: no
Confidence: medium
Code impact: none beyond the reason text and marker (`FanucReader.cs:869`)

#### D385 M3, M4, M5 between the Fanuc M29 S line and G84
Question: B-64484EN-2 p.104 forbids only S and axis motion between M29 and G84. Do spindle M codes there keep the rigid mode? The code passes over them and reads TAP.
Recommendation: none; the question went straight to the delegated decision.
Where: src/Ncx.Readers/Fanuc/FanucReader.cs HidesWhatRunsBefore

ANSWER:
Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

Treat `M3`, `M4`, `M5` and `M19` (spindle orientation) between the M29 S line and the G84 like the blocks of Q3. The walk ends unseen and the cycle stays `RAW` with a reason that names the spindle code ("a spindle command between M29 and G84 is handled by the machine's PMC and may raise an alarm or drop the rigid mode"). The reader no longer passes over them and reads TAP. A spindle code before the M29 line (the usual `S500 M3` / `M29 S500` / `G84`) is unaffected.
Basis: manual + web
Source: In rigid mode the PMC holds the spindle. It enters rigid mode from M29 with the spindle stopped and leaves it on the ENB edge, and a spindle M code at that moment "may" cause "an error ... in the PMC" (B-64303EN-1 p.898, p.927-928 CAUTION 1-2, connector p.928). B-64484EN-2 p.103-105 has no rule that allows spindle M codes between M29 and G84. Shop reports disagree and depend on the machine: "All the machines I have that use S*** M29 will alarm out if M03 is active", and others report SP0740 "spindle ... not stopped" (https://www.emastercam.com/forums/topic/96166-fanuc-g682-with-rigid-tapping/page/2/, https://www.emastercam.com/forums/topic/23663-rigid-tapping-on-fanuc/). Because it depends on the PMC, the reader must not claim TAP.
Differs from the recommendation: yes: today these blocks are passed over and the G84 reads as TAP; now the cycle stays RAW.
Confidence: medium
Code impact: Fanuc reader: `HidesWhatRunsBefore` (or the walk in `MarkBeforeLines`) also stops unseen at M3/M4/M5/M19, with a reason of its own; add tests.
