#### D386 A group-01 code in the Fanuc G84 block after M29 S
Question: B-64484EN-2 p.105 says a group-01 code in the G84 block cancels G84. `M29 S500 / G0 X10. G84 ...` reads TAP on main. What does the reader do?
Recommendation: none; the question went straight to the delegated decision.
Where: src/Ncx.Readers/Fanuc/FanucCycles.cs; FanucReader.cs

ANSWER:
Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

A block with a group-01 code (`G0`..`G3`) and a drilling canned-cycle code is not a cycle. The control executes the group-01 code, and the cycle is cancelled as by `G80`. The reader keeps the block `RAW` with a WARNING whose reason cites B-64484EN-2 p.105: "a group-01 code in the G84 block cancels G84; the control moves with the block's axis words, the hole-bottom Z included". It does not read TAP and does not write a RAPID guess, because the control's handling of R, Q, P and K words in a G0 block is not documented. After the block the reader's state is: motion = the block's group-01 code, no cycle (`CYCLE=OFF` where one was active), and R and Z cleared. The following X/Y-only blocks are therefore plain moves. The rigid-tapping line before it gets no TAP mark. This applies to every Fanuc drilling cycle code (G73, G74, G76, G81-G89), mill and lathe, not only G84.
Basis: manual
Source: B-64484EN-2 p.105 (connector p.105, "Cancel"): "Do not specify a G code of the 01 group ... and G84 in a single block. Otherwise, G84 will be canceled". The same is said for G89 on p.84 and on the lathe in B-64484EN-1 p.309. 16/18-MB B-63534EN-02 p.62 (connector p.62), G-code note 5: a group-01 code in a canned cycle sets the G80 state, and "the G codes in group 01 are not affected by a G code specifying a canned cycle". This is consistent with the settled D247 (a group-01 code ends a canned cycle and is never written in one block with a cycle code). RAW instead of a RAPID because a rapid to the hole-bottom Z is a crash the user must see.
Differs from the recommendation: yes: today on main this block reads TAP; now RAW with a WARNING, and the cycle ends.
Confidence: high
Code impact: Fanuc reader `FanucCycles` (`Ends`/cycle start): a block with both a group-01 code and a drilling-cycle code goes RAW + WARNING and ends the cycle; `MarkBeforeLines` treats it as a cancel.

#### D387 A literal F in a SINUMERIK MCALL position block
Question: After `MCALL CYCLE81(...)`, a position block `X10 Y10 F200`: is that F the cycle's feed, the path feed of the next blocks, or both? The reader keeps the old cycle feed.
Recommendation: none; the question went straight to the delegated decision.
Where: src/Ncx.Readers/Siemens/SiemensCycles.cs; P5-01 task log

ANSWER:
Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (Peter, 2026-10-27: most of these cases never appear in a program, he knows no more than the manuals and has no machine to test on; so a short web research first, and failing that the most logical approach, as if we were the control manufacturer).

The F is both the cycle's feed and the path feed. It is the modal F at the moment the modal cycle runs, so `CYCLE81`..`CYCLE83` drill this hole and every later hole of the modal range with it, and it is also the modal feed of the following blocks. The reader writes the `CYCLE` block again with `CYCLE_F=200` (all other words unchanged) directly before this `CYCLE_CALL`, as D254 (3) does for the Heidenhain pattern. It keeps `ControlFeed = 200` as today, so the next feed motion writes `F=200`. A cycle with its own feed parameter (`CYCLE85` `FFR`, `CYCLE84`) ignores the F for the cycle and takes only the path-feed half. A non-literal F keeps the existing RAW rule.
Basis: manual
Source: The Index 840D Zyklen LY4401.10092 (2004) p.51 and p.54-55 (connector) give the CYCLE81/82 sequence: "Fahren auf Endbohrtiefe mit dem im aufrufenden Programm programmierten Vorschub (G1)". p.89 says "dem vor Zyklusaufruf programmierten Vorschub". The modal call runs after the position block, so the block's F is the one programmed before the call. The settled D259 already relies on an F in a block under MCALL firing the modal cycle. D29 keeps `CYCLE_F` and the motion `F` as separate words, which is why both are written.
Differs from the recommendation: yes: today only the path feed is updated and the cycle keeps the `CYCLE_F` captured at the MCALL, so the call drills with the old feed.
Confidence: high
Code impact: Siemens reader: `SiemensCycles.CallAt` re-emits the `CYCLE` block with the new `CYCLE_F` (for entries with `CycleF == "F"`) before the `CYCLE_CALL`; tests in `SiemensCycleTests`.

#### D388 Resolutions for the code wave of the 2026-10-27 decisions
Question: Planning the code wave (`.worktrees/codewave/PLAN.md`, 2026-10-27) found contradictions between decisions, codes taken twice, and names the decisions leave open. Which way does each go?
Recommendation: none; the points went straight to the delegated decision.
Where: the rows named below in decisions.md; machine-config 5 and 6; language 4.13; the controller documents the keys touch.

ANSWER:
Decided 2026-10-27 by Claude on the maintainer's delegation (see the head of this section), by the most logical approach: keep what main and the frozen expected files already do where a later row only restates it, and give every new name the form of its neighbours.

(1) D157 against D226: D226 stands. The Heidenhain compiler writes Q204 = Q200 for CLEARANCE, as main and the BOHREN expected file do; D157's "Q204=0" is corrected. (2) D167: the ranks of @SAVE and @RESTORE are 1140 and 1150, as main has them; 1130 is MESSAGE (D326). (3) D257: CMP300 is retired and its number reserved; the WARNING that names a generated O number is CMP310. (4) D264 against D278: D278 is the more specific rule. A Fanuc contour section that D278 inlines into G70-G76 is never written as an O program, and language 4.13 names this exception to "every SUB is written at least once". (5) D373: CMP123 stays the WARNING; the ERROR is CMP124. (6) D191 takes VM426; VM423 stays with D351. (7) D308 against D372: TOOL_POINT, TIP_OFFSET and POINT_RADIUS select and size registers, so they are offset state and stay per channel, like the offsets D308 keeps per channel. (8) D306: a job of more than one channel compiled without a machine file is a CLI ERROR that says a multi-channel job needs a machine file, instead of VM851 on the built-in default machine. (9) D314: `start_mark` in machines/nakamura-ntjx.toml (and its copy) becomes 198, the mark the manual and the builder template use; the acceptance output follows. (10) A new optional `[[axis]]` key `frames_in_diameter = false|true` (default false) says whether frame offsets and actual-value variables of a diameter axis are diameters (Siemens MD20360); D125, D216 and D240 read it. (11) D278's type II pocketing is the `[cycles]` key `contour_type_ii = false|true` (default false); D279's peck rigid tapping is `[cycles]` key `peck_rigid_tapping = false|true` (default false). (12) D213: the Heidenhain compiler takes its loop counters from the `[format]` key `counter_registers` (a first and last Q or QL number); a repeat that needs a counter on a machine without the key is an ERROR, never a guessed register. Siemens needs no counter: it writes its native loop. (13) D316: the library file is `<job name>_LIB` with the family's extension; on Heidenhain each uncalled SUB becomes its own program, called with CALL PGM. (14) D339: the Mori list of combinable M codes is taken from the manual connector; until a page names it, the key exists without a shipped list. (15) Any other name or code a package needs that no decision gives, for example D367's comment key, D263's CFG code (reuse CFG005), the Siemens signatures of D181, D379 and D380 (from the manual connector), D387's re-emitted cycle block, the decimals of D121's analytics reports: the package picks it in the form of its neighbours and adds a "Gap closed 2026-10-27 (delegated)" note to the decisions.md row. (16) D299's corpus form is out of reach (the corpus is outside the repository) and is not applied. (17) D347's package Authors waits for D165.

### Fifteenth round: the open TODO(question) markers, decided 2026-10-30

An inventory of 2026-10-30 found 57 TODO(question) markers in the repository: 15 already settled by decisions (only their comments change) and 42 in 32 question groups. Each group was decided on the maintainer's delegation of 2026-10-27 (short web search, else the approach a control manufacturer would choose; RAW or a diagnostic over a silent guess). New key and code names follow their neighbours; Heidenhain cycle 27 ships in release 1; Siemens G973 stays RAW (D424). Source: `.worktrees/openitems/decisions-open.md` and `inventory.md`.

#### D394 Heidenhain cycle 27 for CYLINDER
Markers: src/Ncx.Compilers/Heidenhain/HeidenhainFrames.cs:62   Row: CAM-234
Decision: The Heidenhain compiler writes a CYLINDER section (`CYLINDER=r` .. `CYLINDER=OFF`) as `CYCL DEF 14 KONTUR` + `CYCL DEF 27 ZYLINDER-MANTEL` + `CYCL CALL` **only** when the section has the shape the cycle executes itself: (1) positioning moves above the start point, (2) one feed motion along the radial axis to a constant depth (the plunge), (3) a chain of LINE/ARC in the cylinder plane at that constant radial position, (4) a retract along the radial axis. Several passes with the same contour at increasing depth are allowed and set Q10. The contour of (3) becomes a contour subprogram `LBL n` .. `LBL 0`. It takes its label from the D271 allocation, uses X for the circumference and Y along the axis on the TNC 640 (the machine's rotary letter on the iTNC 530, D146), puts both coordinates in its first block, and uses L/CC+C/CR only. COMP=LEFT/RIGHT becomes RL/RR in the first block. Q values: Q1 = depth − r (negative); Q3 = 0; Q6 = plunge start radius − r, which must be > the tool radius (else CMP101); Q10 = depth step (= |Q1| for one pass); Q11 = F of the plunge; Q12 = F of the contour, and a contour with more than one F is CMP101; Q16 = r; Q17 = 1 (mm, because the NCX C word is a length on the circumference, D102). Anything else stays CMP101 and writes nothing, as it does now. This includes COMP=OFF (the manual describes a contour that the cycle offsets), a contour with a RAPID, a varying radius, or a CHF/RND that NCX has already expanded. The reader keeps a source `CYCL DEF 27` native (`CYCLE:HEIDENHAIN=27`, D94) and does not expand it.
Basis: manual + logical
Source: TNC640 Zyklen 892905-18 (doc `Heidenhain_TNC640_Zyklen_892905-18_NC-SW-34059x-10_DE_2019.pdf`) p.333-335: the contour is described in a subprogram set by cycle 14, always in X/Y, with L, CHF, CR, RND, CT; the cycle positions, mills at each infeed Q10 down to Q1, and retracts to Q6; "the set-up clearance must be greater than the tool radius"; the NC example lists Q1, Q3, Q6, Q10, Q11, Q12, Q16, Q17. The shape test is logical: the cycle does its own infeed, so only an NCX section that already has that infeed can map to it without changing the toolpath.
Confidence: medium (the parameters come from the manual; the shape matcher is our own rule)
Code impact: HeidenhainFrames.RefuseCylinder → new HeidenhainCylinder writer; HeidenhainLabels (allocation); CMP101 keeps the fallback; tests with a TNC 640 and an iTNC 530 machine.

#### D395 Heidenhain: where M0/M1 of STOP stand
Markers: src/Ncx.Compilers/Heidenhain/HeidenhainFunctions.cs:32 (refs :76, tests/.../HeidenhainFunctionTests.cs:57)   Row: W3-33
Decision: Keep the code. STOP writes M0/M1 after the motion (in a block of its own, or in the L block itself, where it also acts at the block end). The half of D252's compiler sentence that puts STOP in the block before the L is withdrawn. A note under D252 records that STOP follows the VM order. D252's own evidence lists M0 and M1 as functions that act at the block end, so this placement stops where the NCX block stops.

Confidence: high
Code impact: comment only in HeidenhainFunctions; decisions.md D252 note; the two refs.

#### D396 Klartext F and S with a formula or a signed parameter
Markers: src/Ncx.Compilers/Heidenhain/HeidenhainParameters.cs:134 (ref HeidenhainMotionTests.cs:222)   Row: none (the remainder D338 names)
Decision: Extend D338 to F and S. A formula, or a parameter with a sign, in F or S is spilled into the highest free QL in a block of its own directly before the block, which then writes `F QLn` / `S QLn`, as D338 does for coordinates. CMP102 stays only where no QL is free. A literal negative F or S is not new here: it is already a VM error.
Basis: logical (D338 + heidenhain 6: "a Q parameter may stand wherever a number stands")
Source: D338 spills coordinates the same way; F and S accept a Q parameter, so they accept the spilled QL.
Confidence: high
Code impact: HeidenhainParameters, the D338 spill helper; HeidenhainMotionTests (CMP102 → spill).

#### D397 Target of the FN 18 SYSREAD block
Markers: src/Ncx.Compilers/Heidenhain/HeidenhainFormula.cs:186, machines/heidenhain-itnc530.toml:165   Row: none (W1-10 / D182)
Decision: A `$SYS_` name read in a block is assigned to the highest free QL of the D338 pool, in `FN 18: SYSREAD QLn = ID.. NR.. IDX..`, in a block of its own directly before the block that uses it, one QL per distinct name in the block. QL is local to the program, so the read cannot clobber a user Q. When no QL is free, the result is CMP102. This unblocks the FN 18 ID270/ID240 route of D320.
Basis: logical
Source: D182 fixes the id and the separate block; D338 already reserves the highest free QL for compiler temporaries, so one pool keeps the allocation predictable.
Confidence: high
Code impact: HeidenhainFormula ($SYS_ no longer refused), the shared QL allocator, heidenhain-itnc530.toml comment, D320 follow-up in HeidenhainSetpos.

#### D398 Replacing Klartext transform with others after it (7-10-7)
Markers: src/Ncx.Compilers/Heidenhain/HeidenhainChain.cs:135, src/Ncx.Compilers/Heidenhain/HeidenhainSetpos.cs:108, :278 (refs in HeidenhainFrameTests, HeidenhainSetposTests)   Row: W3-19, W3-40, W3-43
Decision: Final as coded. A cycle 7/8/10/11/26/19/PLANE that would replace an entry with others after it in the chain is CMP106. A RESET that removes a transform the SETPOS cycle 7 follows is CMP114. The compiler never writes either case. This is the end state, not a waiting state, so the comment cites D253(a) and this decision instead of "open". Revisit only with a machine test.

No page says whether a redefined cycle 7 acts in place or at the end of the chain. With no evidence either way, the control maker reports the case rather than guessing.

#### D399 REPEAT without TIMES, compiler form
Markers: src/Ncx.Compilers/Heidenhain/HeidenhainFlow.cs:252, src/Ncx.Compilers/Siemens/SiemensFlow.cs:253 (refs HeidenhainFlowTests.cs:92, :107, assertion :156)   Row: W3-29, W3-139
Decision: Heidenhain writes `CALL LBL n REP 1`. Without REP it would be a subprogram call, which is a different construct. Siemens writes `REPEAT start end` with no P, which is the form D212 names as equal to "once more". Fanuc keeps its counter form.
Basis: logical
Source: D212 ("a REPEAT without TIMES runs the blocks once more, as a Sinumerik REPEAT without P"); on Klartext a program-section repeat is `CALL LBL n REP k`, and a CALL LBL without REP is a subprogram call.
Confidence: high
Code impact: comments only; HeidenhainFlowTests.cs:156 asserts that the marker exists and is replaced by an assertion of the written text.

#### D403 Decimals of numbers a reader computes
Markers: src/Ncx.Readers/Fanuc/FanucNumbers.cs:31, src/Ncx.Readers/Heidenhain/HeidenhainNumbers.cs:34, src/Ncx.Readers/Fanuc/FanucCycles.cs:1173   Row: none (W1-46 / D121 for the VM)
Decision: Extend D121 to the readers. A value a reader computes (polar point, tangential arc centre, chamfer or rounding point, spatial angle, pitch F/S) is rounded to 6 decimals, half away from zero, and trailing zeros are dropped. The rule "as many as the source words, at least three" goes. The compiler's `[format]` decimals alone decide the digits written to the control.
Basis: logical
Source: D121 already fixes 6 decimals for every VM-computed value so that computed and written points compare equal. Using one precision in reader and VM removes a second rule. Six decimals is below every control resolution.
Confidence: high
Code impact: FanucNumbers, HeidenhainNumbers (one shared helper), FanucCycles:1173 (comment only); expected NCX files with computed values may gain digits.

#### D404 Fanuc ATAN range (parameter 6004#0 NAT)
Markers: src/Ncx.Compilers/Fanuc/FanucExpressions.cs:238, src/Ncx.Readers/Fanuc/FanucExpression.cs:294   Row: W3-60, W1-86
Decision: New optional machine key `[variables] atan_nat` (bool, default `false` = the factory setting: ATAN gives 0..360). With `false`, the reader reads `ATAN[y]/[x]` as `(ATAN2(y, x) + 360) MOD 360`, and the compiler writes NCX `ATAN2(y, x)` as `[ATAN[y]/[x] - 360*FIX[ATAN[y]/[x]/180]]`, which maps 0..360 to -180..180. Exactly 180 becomes -180, the same direction. With `true`, both write the plain form. Fanuc ASIN follows the same bit (270..0..90 under 0) and gets the same treatment where ASIN is mapped.
Basis: manual
Source: 30i-B Parameterhandbuch B-64490EN-05 p.340-341, parameter 6004 #0 NAT: "0: the result of ATAN is 0 to 360.0 … 1: −180.0 to 0 to 180.0" (the same in 30i-A B-63950EN-03 p.383).
Confidence: high (behaviour), medium (key name)
Code impact: machine-config 7 + loader key, FanucExpressions.Call, FanucExpression reader, D119 note; tests for both settings.

#### D405 Fanuc HOME of an axis with no incremental letter (G28 B in system A)
Markers: src/Ncx.Compilers/Fanuc/FanucFrames.cs:519, tests/Ncx.Acceptance/Jobs/NakamuraJobCompileTests.cs:26 (refs :126, README.md:5)   Row: W3-65, W3-175
Decision: The compiler writes HOME of such an axis as `G28 B<v>`, where v is a known position that makes the intermediate move zero or the one NCX asked for. (a) A `RAPID B=v` directly before `HOME B`, with nothing between, folds into `G28 Bv`; this is the reader's own D243 reading of `G28 B0`, so the round trip is exact. (b) Otherwise, if the VM knows the current B, the compiler writes `G28 B<current>` (an intermediate point equal to the current position means no intermediate motion). (c) If B is unknown, CMP321 stays an ERROR. It never writes G91, which is not the incremental code in system A. The Nakamura test drops its incremental-letter patch.
Basis: logical (from D243 and the system A address rules)
Source: D243: an absolute word of G28 is the intermediate point, reached at rapid; an address with no incremental twin is always absolute. Writing the point the axis already stands at is what a programmer does on the control.
Confidence: medium-high
Code impact: FanucFrames.WriteHome, a look-back at the previous RAPID, CMP321 narrowed to the unknown case; nakamura-ntjx test.

#### D409 Other words of G70..G76 and the two-block form
Markers: cycles/fanuc-lathe.toml:140, src/Ncx.Readers/Fanuc/FanucCycles.cs:256   Row: W1-18 (D175 remainder)
Decision: No new NCX words. The catalog entries get the remaining addresses as catalog parameters with descriptive names (D114 provisional form, kept in source order). The two-block form is one catalog cycle whose parameters carry a block suffix: G71/G72 `DEPTH_OF_CUT`=U (or W on G72) and `RETRACT`=R of block 1, then `ALLOWANCE_X`=U and `ALLOWANCE_Z`=W of block 2 with P/Q as the contour; G73 `RELIEF_X`=U, `RELIEF_Z`=W, `DIVISIONS`=R / `ALLOWANCE_X`, `ALLOWANCE_Z`; G74/G75 `RETURN`=R (block 1), `STEP_X`=P, `STEP_Z`=Q, `ESCAPE`=R (block 2); G76 `THREAD_DATA`=P (mmrraa), `MIN_DEPTH`=Q, `FINISH_ALLOWANCE`=R (block 1), `TAPER`=R, `HEIGHT`=P, `FIRST_DEPTH`=Q, `PITCH`=F (block 2). The compiler writes the two blocks in the control's order. The one-block (Series 15) form stays RAW. Until the catalog lands, the current RAW + WARNING stays.
Basis: manual + logical
Source: Fanuc lathe manuals give the two-block formats (e.g. 0i-D Bedienerhandbuch-Drehen B-64304EN-1-01 p.82-88, G70-G75 description, G74/G75 "cutting by Δi, return by e, escape Δd"). Native parameters, not NCX words, keep NCX free of Fanuc-only semantics (D114, D94).
Confidence: medium (parameter names are ours)
Code impact: cycles/fanuc-lathe.toml, the reader's two-block join (FanucCycles), FanucCycles compiler writer, ShippedCatalogsTests.

#### D420 Does a RAW builder cycle change the Siemens frame?
Markers: src/Ncx.Compilers/Siemens/SiemensFrames.cs:270   Row: none
Decision: Split by what the RAW line is. A RAW line that is MSG, STOPRE, a comment, G4, or an instruction the reader already classifies as frame-neutral leaves the frame known (as now). A RAW subprogram or builder-cycle call (a name with or without parentheses that is not a known frame-neutral instruction) makes the frame unknown, as D343 does for the modal call. The compiler then writes the full frame (ORIGIN, TRANS…, CYCLE800) before the next motion.
Basis: logical
Source: D343 treats a RAW call as able to change channel state; frames are channel state. Exempting the known neutral lines avoids writing frames after every MSG.

#### D421 Siemens datum (G54..G599, G500) and the CYCLE800 swivel
Markers: src/Ncx.Readers/Siemens/SiemensFrames.cs:44   Row: W3-189
Decision: The datum leaves the swivel standing. CYCLE800 writes system frames (D333), and a settable frame is a separate component of the total frame (D340(3)). The reader writes, after the ORIGIN, the programmable entries (as now) and also the standing TILT with MOVE=STAY, the same reading D253(d) gives Heidenhain cycle 247. The Siemens compiler writes nothing for a TILT MOVE=STAY right after an ORIGIN when it equals the swivel the control still holds, so the round trip is unchanged.
Basis: manual + decision
Source: Sinumerik 840D sl Programming Manual NC Programming (2020) p.144 and p.305-306: a settable work offset is a settable frame, separate from the programmable and system frame components; D333 (2026-10-27): CYCLE800 writes system frames.
Confidence: medium-high
Code impact: SiemensFrames reader (ORIGIN path), SiemensFrames compiler (skip identical STAY tilt), tests.

#### D422 Position block while an unknown modal call is armed
Markers: src/Ncx.Readers/Siemens/SiemensMotion.cs:232   Row: none (D259 remainder)
Decision: Extend D259. From a RAW `MCALL` (or an MCALL of a subprogram the reader cannot expand) to the MCALL alone that disarms it, within the unit, every block stays RAW, found by the same look-ahead. Without a closing MCALL in the unit, the range runs to the end of the unit. Reading the positions as plain motions would let a compiler insert F/S/plane blocks between them, which fire the modal call (D259).
Basis: logical
Source: D259's own argument (S or F with G0/G1 calls the modal subprogram).
Confidence: medium-high
Code impact: SiemensMotion / SiemensCycles look-ahead; expected files of sources with a subprogram MCALL.

## Answered (ninth round, 2026-10-01; settled in `decisions.md`)

Eighty-four questions of the sixth, seventh and eighth rounds, answered from the maintainer's manual library and settled on 2026-10-01. Each draft was researched by one agent and checked by a second, who re-opened every manual page the answer cites and struck or corrected whatever the page did not carry; the Evidence line of each entry names the manual and the page, so any reader can do the same. Of the answers that came back, the maintainer let exactly one group be applied without reviewing each entry: those whose manual-confirmed answer agrees with the draft's own recommendation and rests on a page the verifier gave high confidence. Those are the entries below, each carrying the line "Settled 2026-10-01" and a row in `decisions.md`. Everything else stays in "Still open" above and still waits for the maintainer: the drafts whose manual-confirmed answer contradicts the recommendation, the drafts whose manual pages only inform the question without settling it, and the drafts the library does not cover at all. The headings below keep each entry's round and urgency, so an entry can still be found where it stood.

### Sixth round: needed now (phase 1 behaviour)

#### D117 Axis words under SHIFT, TILT, TILT_AXIS and SETPOS
Question: Language 5 rule 2 says 'SHIFT, TILT, TILT_AXIS and SETPOS carry their own axis words'. The 4.2 rows give SHIFT and SETPOS 'axis words', TILT 'spatial angles A, B, C' and TILT_AXIS 'rotary axis angles', and the D82 rationale says 'NCX `TILT` takes spatial angles only'. For the incremental forms (SHIFT IX=5, SETPOS IC=0), 4.3 defines IX only as a target: 'current position plus the value'. The only document that touches them is controller-mapping 2. Its IX row lists the Fanuc system A addresses U W 'also in `G28 U0 W0` and `G52 U2.75 W1.25`', which reads as SHIFT IX=2.75 IZ=1.25 without saying what such a shift means. On main the parser accepts every axis-naming word under all four verbs, TILT X=1 included. VirtualMachine.ApplyShift, ApplyTilt and ApplySetpos then skip the incremental words silently.
Recommendation: The allowed words per verb: TILT carries A, B and C only; TILT_AXIS carries A, B, C and machine axis words of the D93 form, and the VM reports an ERROR when such an axis is not rotary; SHIFT and SETPOS carry every absolute axis word. An incremental form under any of the four is the PAR012 ERROR. Reasons: a SHIFT is already relative to the frame it stands in (D31), so SHIFT IX adds nothing that SHIFT X lacks, and SETPOS declares a coordinate, so a reader folds a source increment itself. The Fanuc G52 U W of controller-mapping 2 becomes either a SHIFT appended without RESET or a RESET plus SHIFT, depending on the Fanuc meaning, which P3-02 confirms. The IX row then drops G52 from its list, and the SHIFT row says how the reader folds it. Alternative: allow SETPOS IX as 'declared = current + value' (a shift by minus the value), if the maintainer confirms that Fanuc system A has G50 U W.
Where: language 4.2, 4.3 (IX row), 5 rule 2; VM 3.4, 5; controller-mapping 2 (IX row) and 1 (SHIFT row); P3-02; src/Ncx.Core/Parsing/BlockRules.cs CheckAxisWords (TODO(question)); src/Ncx.Core/VirtualMachine/VirtualMachine.cs ApplyFrameVerb, ApplyShift, ApplyTilt, ApplySetpos (TODO(question) above ApplyFrameVerb).

ANSWER:
As recommended, confirmed from the manual library: The Fanuc facts hold, with one correction to the reasoning. G52's value is the origin of the local coordinate system stated in the workpiece coordinate system, a new G52 is programmed by naming the new origin the same way (which is why fanuc 9 rule 6 writes SHIFT=RESET first), and motion blocks immediately after a G52 block must be absolute. But `G52 U2.75 W1.25` is real Fanuc, not an impossible form: the Nakamura manuals of the corpus — the source of the controller-mapping 2 example — print exactly it and say the local origin lies offset from the active G54..G59 by the value given with U/W *or* X/Z, cancelled by `G52 U0. W0.`; so in a G52 block U and W are the lathe spelling of the same absolute local origin, not an increment, and that is why the IX row should drop G52 — while the Fanuc reader's general "U W means incremental" rule (fanuc 9 rule 1) needs a G52 exception written next to it. The maintainer's alternative is confirmed as a fact but is not needed: system A does have `G50 U(u) W(w)`, the coordinate-system shift under which the current tool position becomes (x+u, z+w), so a reader folds it into an absolute SETPOS. TILT needs no axis words either: `G68.2 X Y Z I J K` carries the origin of the tilted system in X Y Z (0 for the three basic axes when omitted) and only I J K as the Euler angles, so the reader splits that block into SHIFT plus TILT.
Evidence: FANUC Series 30i/31i/32i-MODEL B Betriebshandbuch Drehen/Fräsen (B-64484GE/02), p. PDF 216-217 (printed 182-183, §7.3) (G52 IP_ sets a local coordinate system whose origin is the position IP_ given in the workpiece coordinate system; the local system is changed by commanding G52 with the new origin, again in the workpiece coordinate system, and cleared by putting its origin on the workpiece origin. Caution 6 on the next page requires motion commands immediately after a G52 block to be in absolute mode); Nakamura-Tome Programmierhandbuch (Walter Meier, Fanuc 0iTF/31iB/32iA), p. PDF 53 (printed 49, G52) (The G52 page writes `G52 U2.75 W1.25` and `G52 U5.3 W3.5` as the ordinary spellings, says the origin of the local system lies offset from the active G54..G59 by the value given with U/W or X/Z, that the shift may be made in one axis only, and that the local system is cleared with `G52 U0. W0.` or `X0. Z0.`. It repeats that the next block after G52 must be a motion with absolute coordinates, and that G50 overwrites active G52 values. The Super NTJX and WY-series manuals carry the same wording); FANUC Series 16i/18i-TB Benutzerhandbuch (B-63524GE/01), p. PDF 130-131 (printed 107-108, §7.3) (The same wording for a lathe control: the origin of each local system is given with IP_ in the workpiece coordinate system, moving the local system means commanding G52 with the new origin in that system, and warning 4 says motion right after a G52 block must be absolute); FANUC Series 16i/18i/21i/160i/180i/210is-B Beschreibungen (B-63522GE/02), p. PDF 123 (printed 98, §7.2, Verschiebung des Werkstück-Koordinatensystems, Serie T) (The shift of the workpiece coordinate system on series T is given as `(G91) G92X(u)Z(w);` and, in G-code system A, as `G50U(u)W(w);`. The command creates a new coordinate system in which the current coordinate value (x, z) of a point on the tool becomes (x+u, z+w)); FANUC Series 30i/31i/32i-MODEL B Betriebshandbuch Drehen/Fräsen (B-64484GE/02), p. PDF 203 (printed 169) and PDF 207 (printed 173), §7.2 (Page 203 gives the format for setting a workpiece coordinate system: `(G90) G92 IP_` on series M, `G50 IP_` on series T. Page 207 adds, marked T, that when IP is an incremental value the workpiece coordinate system is defined so that the current tool position equals the incremental value plus the coordinates of the previous tool position, and calls this a coordinate-system shift); FANUC Series 30i/31i/32i-MODEL B Betriebshandbuch Drehen/Fräsen (B-64484GE/02), p. PDF 868 (printed 834, §22.6) (Format of the tilted working plane command: `G68.2 X x0 Y y0 Z z0 I J K`, where X, Y, Z are the origin of the specific coordinate system (taken as 0 for the three basic axes when not written) and I, J, K are the Euler angles that orient it. G69 cancels on M, G69.1 on T, and G53.1 must stand in the block after the G68.2 block); Haas VF-Serie Schulungsheft Bearbeitungszentren V1.3, p. PDF 4 (G-Code-Liste) (The G-code table of this Fanuc-style control gives G52 as setting a local coordinate system with X, Y, Z and marks the command "nur absolut"; the cancel form is G52 X0 Y0 Z0).
Settled 2026-10-01: the maintainer let the manual-confirmed answers that agree with their recommendation be applied without reviewing each one.

#### D118 Number of arguments of each function (language 4.12)
Question: Language 4.12 lists seventeen functions under one syntax, function "(" expr { "," expr } ")". It defines only degrees, INT and ROUND. It does not say how many arguments each function takes: is SIN(1, 2) valid, or MIN(3)? It also does not say whether a wrong count is a parse ERROR or is found only when INTERPRETED mode evaluates the expression. STATIC mode, which convert, check and compile use, does not evaluate expressions (VM 1). Today the expression parser accepts one or more arguments (P0-05) and the evaluator reports VM904 (P4-01a). So format, check and compile pass SIN(1, 2), and only analyze stops on it.
Recommendation: ATAN2 takes two arguments, MIN and MAX two or more, every other function one (ROUND has no decimals argument). A wrong count is a PAR ERROR of the expression parser, like an unknown function (PAR107), so format, convert, check and compile all report it. Code changes: the count check moves from Evaluator.ArgumentCountFits (VM904) into ExprParser.ParseCall, with a new code from PAR111 on, and MIN and MAX then require two arguments. Alternatives: MIN and MAX also take one argument (as implemented); the check stays at evaluation, so only analyze reports it (as implemented).
Where: language 4.12 (paragraph after the grammar); src/Ncx.Core/Expressions/ExprParser.cs ParseCall (TODO(question) at line 307); src/Ncx.Core/Expressions/Evaluator.Functions.cs ArgumentCountFits; src/Ncx.Core/Model/DiagnosticCodes.Expressions.cs (new PAR code), DiagnosticCodes.Evaluation.cs (VM904).

ANSWER:
As recommended, confirmed from the manual library: Keep the recommendation on arity: ATAN2 takes two arguments and every other function one. The controls state this where it matters — Siemens writes ATAN2(,) with a comma and explains it as the angle of the sum of two perpendicular vectors, Fanuc's macro table gives one argument in brackets for every function except ATAN (one-argument and two-argument forms) and POW[#j,#k], and Heidenhain's FN 6 and FN 7 take one value while FN 8 LEN and FN 13 ANG take two. "MIN and MAX two or more" goes beyond the controls: Siemens' MINVAL and MAXVAL compare exactly two variables and neither Fanuc nor Heidenhain has the function at all. The manuals do not settle whether a wrong count is a parse ERROR or an evaluation ERROR; Fanuc's PS1131 is a program alarm raised when the block runs, and the manual gives the missing bracket, not the argument count, as its cause. Two corrections to an earlier draft. First, the Siemens table's empty brackets do not state arity — BOUND() is written the same way and takes three arguments — so the one-argument reading of SIN, COS and the rest rests on their ordinary meaning and on the worked examples, not on the notation. Second, PS1131 is not evidence for the proposed parser-level treatment: it is a program alarm raised when the block is prepared for execution, closer to NCX's INTERPRETED evaluation than to a static parse, and the manual attributes it to the missing bracket. Nothing in the library supports or refutes MIN and MAX with more than two arguments; if the maintainer wants the controls' own arity, it is exactly two. Fanuc's POW and PRM show that a control can have a two-argument function other than ATAN2, but NCX 4.12 has neither.
Evidence: SINUMERIK 840D sl NC-Programmierung, Programmierhandbuch 06/2019, p. 448-449 (The Rechenfunktionen table writes SIN(), COS(), TAN(), ASIN(), ACOS(), SQRT(), ABS(), POT(), TRUNC(), ROUND(), LN(), EXP(), MINVAL(), MAXVAL(), BOUND() with an empty pair of brackets and ATAN2(,) with a comma. The empty brackets are notation only and do not state arity — BOUND() in the same list takes three arguments — but ATAN2 is singled out by the comma, and the glosses give MINVAL and MAXVAL as the smaller and the larger value "zweier Variablen". Page 449: ATAN2 computes from two perpendicular vectors the angle of the sum vector, over four quadrants (-180° to +180°), the reference always being the second value.); SINUMERIK 840D sl NC-Programmierung, Programmierhandbuch 06/2019, p. 431-432 (Section 3.1.1.15: MINVAL and MAXVAL compare the values of two variables. The syntax block gives <Kleinerer Wert>=MINVAL(<Variable1>,<Variable2>) and <Größerer Wert>=MAXVAL(<Variable1>,<Variable2>) — exactly two operands — next to <Rückgabewert>=<BOUND>(<Minimum>,<Maximum>,<Prüfvariable>), which takes three.); FANUC Series 30i/31i/32i-MODEL B, Betriebshandbuch (Drehen/Fräsen), B-64484GE/02, p. 489-490 (printed 455-456) (Table 16.4(a) of the custom-macro chapter lists SIN[#j], COS[#j], TAN[#j], ASIN[#j], ACOS[#j], SQRT[#j], ABS[#j], BIN[#j], BCD[#j], ROUND[#j], FIX[#j], FUP[#j], LN[#j], EXP[#j], ADP[#j] with one argument; POW[#j,#k] and PRM[#j,#k] with two; and ATAN in a one-argument form ATAN[#j] and two two-argument forms ATAN[#j]/[#k] and ATAN[#j,#k], the table itself naming them "ein Argument" and "zwei Argumente". Page 490 adds that #100 = ATAN[1]/10 is taken as the two-argument form but raises alarm PS1131 "because the X coordinate is not bracketed".); FANUC Series 30i/31i/32i-MODEL B, Betriebshandbuch (Drehen/Fräsen), B-64484GE/02, p. 2404 (Anhang H, alarm index) (1131 "ÖFFNENDE KLAMMER FEHLT": the custom-macro statement contains fewer left brackets ([) than right ones (]). 1132 is the mirror case. The alarm is about bracket balance, not about how many arguments a function was given.); HEIDENHAIN TNC 640, Benutzerhandbuch Klartextprogrammierung, 10/2019, p. 275 (Section 9.4 Winkelfunktionen: FN 6 SIN and FN 7 COS take one value; FN 8 WURZEL AUS QUADRATSUMME forms a length from two values ("FN 8: Q10 = +5 LEN +4"); FN 13 WINKEL determines an angle by arctan from the opposite and the adjacent side, also two values. A grep of the whole manual finds no MIN or MAX among the Q-parameter functions, and none in the Fanuc macro table either.).
Settled 2026-10-01: the maintainer let the manual-confirmed answers that agree with their recommendation be applied without reviewing each one.

#### D119 Values of ATAN2 and FRAC (language 4.12)
Question: Language 4.12 names ATAN2 and FRAC but does not define them. For ATAN2 it gives no argument order, no range and no value at (0, 0). Controller-mapping 6 and siemens.md 8 list Siemens ATAN2() without its order, and fanuc.md 7 and heidenhain.md 6 list only ATAN. For FRAC it gives no value for a negative number: is FRAC(-2.7) -0.7 or 0.3? Each function comes from one control, FRAC from Heidenhain (heidenhain.md 6, controller-mapping 6) and ATAN2 from Siemens. The readers of those controls pass them through, so NCX must mean what the control means. 4.12 also has no rule for a function without a real result: 'Division by zero is an ERROR' is its only rule of that kind.
Recommendation: ATAN2(y, x) is the angle of the point (x, y) from +X in degrees, above -180 and up to 180. That is the C library convention, and it should be Siemens ATAN2's too (P5-01 confirms against the manual). Fanuc's two-argument ATAN[y]/[x] is not listed in fanuc.md 7. It gives 0 to 360 degrees unless a parameter selects -180 to 180 (to be confirmed against the Fanuc manual), so the Fanuc reader (P3-02) and the Fanuc compiler (P3-06) convert the range. FRAC(x) = x - INT(x) keeps the sign of x, so that INT(x) + FRAC(x) = x with the truncating INT of 4.12; P3-05 confirms that the TNC's FRAC does the same. 4.12 should state once that a function without a real result is an ERROR, in line with 'Division by zero is an ERROR': ATAN2(0, 0), SQRT(-1), LN(0), ASIN(2), TAN(90) (VM905 today). Code changes: none; ArcTangent2 and FRAC stay as implemented. Alternatives: ATAN2(0, 0) = 0, as in the C library; ATAN2 from 0 up to 360, as Fanuc gives it by default; FRAC = x - floor(x), always from 0 up to 1.
Where: language 4.12 (paragraph after the grammar); src/Ncx.Core/Expressions/Evaluator.Functions.cs ArcTangent2 and EvaluateCall (FRAC), both TODO(question); controllers fanuc.md 7, heidenhain.md 6, siemens.md 8 (the control conventions, once confirmed).

ANSWER:
As recommended, confirmed from the manual library: ATAN2(y, x) is the angle of the point (x, y) from +X in degrees over -180 to 180, as Siemens defines it ("Basis für den Winkelbezug ist immer der 2. Wert", four quadrants, ATAN2(30,-80) = 159.444 degrees), so ArcTangent2 stays as implemented. Fanuc's two-argument ATAN[y]/[x] has the same argument order but gives 0 to 360 degrees by default and -180 to 180 only when bit 0 (NAT) of parameter 6004 is 1, so the Fanuc reader and compiler convert the range — and because the program does not carry that bit, the machine file has to say which range the control uses. FRAC(x) = x - INT(x) keeps the sign of x: the TNC's own words are FRAC "Vorkommastellen abschneiden" beside INT "Nachkommastellen abschneiden", and the TNC 640 states that INT does not round but only cuts the decimals. Add the sentence that a function without a real result is an ERROR: Fanuc raises PS0119 "Argumentwert außer Bereich" for ASIN/ACOS outside -1..1, for LN of zero or less and for an EXP overflow.
Evidence: SINUMERIK High Level Language, Trainingsdokumentation (2010), p. 241 (Verified. ATAN2 computes the angle of the sum of two perpendicular vectors, result in four quadrants, "Basis für den Winkelbezug ist immer der 2. Wert in positiver Richtung"; the worked examples give ATAN2(30.5, 80.1) = 20.8455 degrees and ATAN2(30, -80) = 159.444 degrees, both of which reproduce atan2(y, x) exactly); SINUMERIK 840D sl Programmierhandbuch NC-Programmierung, 06/2019 (SW 4.92), p. 449 (Verified. Same definition in the current manual, the range written as four quadrants between -180 and +180 degrees, the angle referred to the second argument); FANUC Series 30i/31i/32i-MODEL B Betriebshandbuch (B-64484GE/02), p. PDF 490 (printed 456), custom macro arithmetic (Verified. ATAN[#j,#k] is equivalent to ATAN[#j]/[#k] and returns the arctangent of the point (#k, #j) in the X-Y plane; with bit 0 (NAT) of parameter 6004 = 0 the result is 0 to 360 degrees (ATAN[-1]/[-1] = 225.0), with NAT = 1 it is -180 to 180 (-135.0). The same page gives PS0119 for ASIN/ACOS outside -1..1, for LN of an argument at or below zero and for an EXP overflow, and notes the one-argument ATAN returns the principal value -90 to 90); FANUC Series 30i/31i/32i-MODEL B Betriebshandbuch (B-64484GE/02), p. PDF 2117 (printed 2083), parameter 6004 (Verified. Bit 0 (NAT) of parameter 6004 selects the result range of the two-argument ATAN (0 to 360,0, or -180,0 to 180,0) and of ASIN (270,0 to 90,0, or -90,0 to 90,0). No default is stated); HEIDENHAIN TNC 640 Benutzerhandbuch Klartextprogrammierung (NC-SW 34059x-10, 10/2019), p. 325 and 348 (Verified. The function list defines FRAC as "Vorkommastellen einer Zahl abschneiden / Fraktionieren" beside INT "Nachkommastellen abschneiden"; p. 325 adds "Die Funktion INT rundet nicht, sondern schneidet nur die Nachkommastellen ab", and the p. 348 example rounds by adding 0,5 to a positive and subtracting 0,5 from a negative number via SGN, which only works if INT truncates toward zero).
Settled 2026-10-01: the maintainer let the manual-confirmed answers that agree with their recommendation be applied without reviewing each one.

#### D122 Full circle and zero radius in the CENTER form of ARC
Question: For the CENTER form, VM 3.2 says "Start = end is a full circle" right after the tolerance check of |start - center| against |end - center| (D36). It does not say whether start = end means exactly equal or equal within that tolerance. Nor does it say what a center on the start point (radius 0) is. The tolerance check lets such an arc through when the end lies within the tolerance of the start, and language 4.3 forbids only R=0. Two examples. From 10/0, ARC=CCW X=10 Y=0.004 CENTER:X=0 CENTER:Y=0 is either a full circle (the end is 0.004 from the start, under 0.01 mm) or an arc of 0.023 degrees. From 0/0, ARC=CW X=0.005 Y=0 CENTER:X=0 CENTER:Y=0 has radius 0.
Recommendation: Compare exactly, as the code does: start = end means equal plane coordinates as stored (at the precision of D121). An end near the start resolves to the short arc or the near-full turn that the direction gives. Reason: the arc tolerance (0.01 mm) is larger than the chord of the short arcs in CAM output, and a control cuts those as short arcs at its own resolution. A center on the start point (radius 0) becomes an ERROR in VM 5 next to "inconsistent center", as R=0 already is (language 4.3). Alternative: compare within the arc tolerance. That also reads a full circle whose end a reader rounded as a full circle, but it turns every arc with a chord under 0.01 mm into a full turn.
Where: VM 3.2 and 5; language 4.3 (CENTER rows). Code: src/Ncx.Core/Geometry/ArcResolver.cs ResolveCenterForm (TODO line 39, SameInPlane, plus a new ArcError for radius 0); the P1-04 diagnostics table.

ANSWER:
As recommended, confirmed from the manual library: Compare exactly, as the recommendation says. Heidenhain states the rule outright: for a full circle you program the same coordinates for the end point as for the start point, and the arc tolerance (machine parameter circleDeviation, max. 0.016 mm) is only the permitted deviation of start and end from the circular path, never a snap to a full turn. Fanuc and Siemens reach the full circle by a different route, leaving the end-point words out, so the three controls do not agree on the form; none of them turns a near-coincident end point into a full turn. The R form keeps its ERROR, and all three controls back it: with R and an end point coinciding with the start Fanuc gives an arc of 0° and the tool stands still, Siemens raises alarm 14040 Kreisendpunktfehler because the circle's position is then undetermined, and Heidenhain needs two blocks for a full circle with CR. For radius 0 the manuals give support rather than a rule — Heidenhain names 0.016 mm as the smallest circle the control can traverse. No manual states what a centre lying on the start point (radius 0) does; the Heidenhain 0.016 mm smallest-circle figure is the nearest thing and supports making it an ERROR. All three arc tolerances found — Fanuc parameter 3410, Heidenhain circleDeviation, Siemens MD21000/MD21010 — are radius-consistency checks between start and end, and none is used to decide between a short arc and a full turn, which is the point the draft turns on. I struck the earlier claim that Fanuc's and Siemens' omitted end point is "the same case" as NCX's start = end: the two controls reach the full circle by omitting words, Heidenhain by repeating the start coordinates, and the equivalence is an NCX reading, not a manual statement.
Evidence: HEIDENHAIN TNC 640, Benutzerhandbuch Klartextprogrammierung, 10/2019, p. 159 (Circular path C about the centre CC: "Vollkreis — Programmieren Sie für den Endpunkt die gleichen Koordinaten wie für den Startpunkt." Start and end must lie on the circular path; the maximum input tolerance is 0.016 mm, set in machine parameter circleDeviation (no. 200901); the smallest circle the control can traverse is 0.016 mm.); HEIDENHAIN TNC 640, Benutzerhandbuch Klartextprogrammierung, 10/2019, p. 160 (Circular path CR with a fixed radius: "Für einen Vollkreis programmieren Sie zwei Kreissätze hintereinander", the end of the first half circle being the start of the second. The radius form cannot make a full circle in one block.); FANUC Series 30i/31i/32i-MODEL B, Betriebshandbuch (Drehen/Fräsen), B-64484GE/02, p. 84 (printed 50) ("Befehl für einen Kreis": when Xp, Yp and Zp are omitted (end point equals start point) and the centre is given with I, J, K, a 360° arc results — G02 I_ ;. If the same words are omitted, the end coincides with the start and R is used instead, an arc of 0° results and the tool stands still (G02 R_ ;). If the difference between the radius at the start point and the radius at the end point exceeds the value allowed in parameter no. 3410, alarm PS0020 is raised.); SINUMERIK 840D sl NC-Programmierung, Programmierhandbuch 06/2019, p. 193, 195, 197 (For G2/G3 with centre and end point (2.9.6.2): "Wird der Kreis ohne Endpunkt programmiert, entsteht ein Vollkreis." The variants with radius CR= (2.9.6.3, p. 195) and with aperture angle AR= (2.9.6.4, p. 197) each carry the sentence "Vollkreise (Verfahrwinkel 360°) können mit dieser Variante nicht programmiert werden." The Stama Programmieranleitung for the 840D (2004, cache p. 46) repeats the radius restriction for a machine builder.); SINUMERIK 840D sl, SINAMICS S120 Alarme, Diagnosehandbuch, 08/2018, 6FC5398-6BP40-6AA2, p. 216 (Alarm 14040 "Kreisendpunktfehler", first listed cause: "Bei der Radiusprogrammierung sind Start- und Endpunkt identisch, weshalb die Lage des Kreises nicht durch Start- oder Endpunkt bestimmt ist." The other causes are radius-consistency limits: the difference of the radii at start and end must stay under MD21000 $MC_CIRCLE_ERROR_CONST or under the programmed radius times MD21010 $MC_CIRCLE_ERROR_FACTOR.).
Settled 2026-10-01: the maintainer let the manual-confirmed answers that agree with their recommendation be applied without reviewing each one.

#### D127 How long 'directly after a HOME' lasts for SETPOS
Question: D101 (clarified 2026-09-12), the SETPOS row of language 4.2, and VM 3.4 and 5 accept SETPOS on an axis unknown in every frame "directly after a HOME of that axis that found no reference point". None of them says whether other blocks may stand between the two. POLAR_FACE has none (HOME C, SETPOS C=0), but a reader may produce HOME C, COOLANT=OFF, SETPOS C=0. Does the permission hold for the next block only, or until something touches the axis? The code keeps it until a block names the axis (VirtualMachine.cs ResetBlockScope); HOME C, COOLANT=OFF, SETPOS C=0 is accepted and leaves C known in the workpiece frame at 0.
Recommendation: The permission lasts until the next block that names the axis (a motion, HOME or SETPOS with it), as the code does. A block that switches the spindle owning the axis to SPINDLE mode also ends it, because the axis then turns as a spindle and no longer stands at the reference HOME found. VM 3.8 rule 4 already makes SETPOS C an ERROR while the spindle is in SPINDLE mode (VM011 in the code), but without this rule a switch back to AXIS mode before the SETPOS would keep the permission. Blocks that do not touch the axis leave it where HOME left it, unknown in every frame, so the exception means the same after them, and a reader need not keep G28 H0 and G50 C0 adjacent. Alternative: the next block only; any block between makes the SETPOS the ERROR of VM 5.
Where: D101 log line; language 4.2 SETPOS row; VM 3.4 and 5. Code: src/Ncx.Core/VirtualMachine/VirtualMachine.cs ResetBlockScope (TODO line 524), the _homedWithoutReference set used by HomeRules, and the SPINDLE_MODE handler.

ANSWER:
As recommended, confirmed from the manual library: Do not require adjacency: the controls scope the permission to the C-axis session, not to the next block. Fanuc states the condition twice and both times it is a session, not a block: to use the function that establishes the Cs-axis coordinate the reference point must have been approached at least once since power-on, and under parameter 3700 bit 0 the count restarts when the serial spindle is switched into Cs contour-axis mode ('since switching into Cs mode ... at least once'), with alarm PS0303 otherwise. The Nakamura examples bear this out: the idiom is M91, G28 H0, G50 C0 adjacent, but the same program writes a second G50 C0 many blocks later after probing and a G00 C#500, and another example puts the reference return inside a called subprogram (M98 P9000) with G50 C0 in the caller. So the recommendation's two rules both hold — more than the next block, and a switch back to spindle mode ends it — though Fanuc's own scope is wider than the code's rule: it runs to the end of the AXIS-mode session, not only to the next block that names the axis. Caveats: Two gaps remain. (1) The manuals' scope is wider than the recommendation's: Fanuc ties the permission to the whole Cs-mode session, not to 'the next block that names the axis', so a manual-shaped rule would keep the permission alive across an intervening RAPID C= as well. The recommendation's narrower rule is an NCX choice the manuals do not contradict but also do not support. (2) The manual cases are reference returns that succeeded. NCX's case is a HOME on an axis with no reference point in the configuration. The nearest control counterpart is parameter 3700 bit 2 (CNM): a Cs-axis command while the zero point is not established raises PS0224 'Referenzfahren nicht beendet' unless the bit suppresses it for a zero-travel command — a control refuses where NCX accepts with a WARNING (D100) and then a SETPOS (D101). That is a difference of purpose (control versus checker), not a contradiction, but it is closer to NCX's case than the earlier reading allowed. The 'machine position stays unknown' half is already settled by D101 and is not what this draft asks.
Evidence: Parameterhandbuch FANUC 30i/31i/32i-MODEL B (B-64490GE/03), p. 225 (PDF page; printed 213, section 4.23) (Parameter 3700, bit 0 (CRF): with the function active, commanding G00 on a Cs contour-control axis without the axis having approached the reference point at least once 'seit dem Umschalten der seriellen Spindel' into Cs contour-axis mode raises alarm PS0303; bit 1 (NRF) likewise counts from that switch; bit 2 (CNM) decides whether a Cs-axis command with the zero point not established raises PS0224. The reference state is scoped to the Cs-mode session, never to the preceding block.); Betriebshandbuch Drehen/Fräsen 30i/31i/32i-B (B-64484GE/02), p. 1136 (PDF page; printed 1102) (Closing note of the section 'Programm-Neustart für die Cs-Bahnsteuerungsachse': to use the function that establishes the Cs-axis coordinate, the reference point of the Cs contour axis must have been approached at least once after power-on. The condition is 'since power-on', not 'in the previous block'. It is stated of that named function in the program-restart context, not of G50 in general.); Nakamura-Tome, NT Nurse / NT Work Navigator Bedienungsanleitung (Fanuc 16/21i), p. 303 (PDF page; printed 3-2-22) (Worked example: G28 U0 W0, M91 (C-Achsen-Anschluss), G28 H0 (C-Achsen-Nullpunktrückstellung), G50 C0 (Initialisierung der C-Achsen-Koordinate) stand adjacent; the same program then probes twice, computes #500=[#501+#502]/2, moves with G00 C#500 and writes G50 C0 a second time as 'Einstellung des Bearbeitungs-Bezugspunkts', with many blocks between it and any reference return.); Nakamura-Tome, NT Nurse / NT Work Navigator Bedienungsanleitung (Fanuc 16/21i), p. 292 (PDF page; printed 3-2-11) (Under '(2) Für C-Achsen-Befehl' of the machining-reference-point-shift function: G50 re-sets the C coordinate to the programmed value at the position the axis currently stands, with the examples G50 C0 and G50 C12,5 ('C0° wird für die aktuelle Position der C-Achse eingestellt'). No reference return is named as a precondition — an argument from silence, and the passage is about that one function, not about G50 generally.); Nakamura-Tome, NT Nurse / NT Work Navigator Bedienungsanleitung (Fanuc 16/21i), p. 215 (PDF page; printed 2-23-8) (Program example for the involute cycle G362: the C-axis connection is made by 'M98 P9000; C-Achsen-Anschluss' and the next block is G50 C0, so a subprogram call and its return stand between the coordinate setting and the reference return. The page itself does not say what P9000 contains.); Nakamura-Tome, Präzisionsdrehzentrum Programmierhandbuch (1/2), Fanuc, p. 226 (PDF page; printed 14-1) (Names the contents of O9000, the subprogram called as M98 P9000 in place of M91: 'O9000 / M91; / M27; / G28 *H / M28; / M99;'. This is where the reference return that the NT NURSE example hides inside the call actually sits.); Muratec, Programming Manual (TE0001E-08), p. 166 and 168 (PDF pages; printed 5-38 and 5-40) (Two sample programs show the common adjacent form: 'M68; G28 H0; G50 C-90.;' before cylindrical interpolation, and 'G28 H0: G50 X170. Z104. C22.5;' before polar interpolation — the idiom the NCX POLAR_FACE example mirrors, without any statement making adjacency a rule.).
Settled 2026-10-01: the maintainer let the manual-confirmed answers that agree with their recommendation be applied without reviewing each one.

#### D131 Words covered by the C= check of VM 3.8 rule 4
Question: VM 3.8 rule 4 and VM 5 make "C= on a spindle in SPINDLE mode" an ERROR, and language 4.5 says that in AXIS mode "its axis is driven with C=". None of them names the verbs. Language 5 rule 2 gives SHIFT, TILT_AXIS and SETPOS axis words of their own and HOME bare axis names. VM 3.4 lets TILT_AXIS with MOVE=TURN or MOVE put the rotary axes at their angles. The code checks C and IC under RAPID, LINE, ARC, CYCLE_CALL and SETPOS only. HOME C (a bare word, skipped), SHIFT C= and TILT_AXIS C= pass in SPINDLE mode. The words of HOME and TILT_AXIS still resolve through rule 3 (VirtualMachine.ResolveAxisWords skips only TILT), so their C is the workpiece holder's axis: on the default machine, the C of MAIN. The C of TILT is a spatial angle and never resolves to the spindle.
Recommendation: The rule covers every word that moves the spindle's axis or declares its position. That means C and IC under RAPID, LINE, ARC, CYCLE_CALL and SETPOS (as coded), plus the bare C of HOME and the C of TILT_AXIS with MOVE=TURN or MOVE=MOVE. It does not cover SHIFT (a chain entry, nothing moves) or TILT_AXIS with MOVE=STAY. Reason: 'driven with C=' in language 4.5 is about positioning the axis, and HOME and a moving TILT_AXIS position it (VM 3.4). POLAR_FACE stays clean, because its HOME C and SETPOS C=0 come after SPINDLE_MODE:MAIN=AXIS. Code change: add HOME and TILT_AXIS with MOVE to CheckSpindleAxisWords. Side effect: on the default machine C belongs to MAIN (D103). A mill program checked without a machine file that writes HOME C, or TILT_AXIS with C and MOVE=TURN, then gets this ERROR, as its RAPID C= and LINE C= already do. Alternative: keep the coded set and read 'C=' literally, since HOME's C has no value. That is the smallest change.
Where: VM 3.8 rule 4; VM 5 ERROR list; language 4.5 (SPINDLE_MODE row); src/Ncx.Core/VirtualMachine/ResourceResolver.cs CheckSpindleAxisWords.

ANSWER:
As recommended, confirmed from the manual library: Cover the bare C of HOME as well as the C and IC of RAPID, LINE, ARC, CYCLE_CALL and SETPOS. The Nakamura programming manual states the rule outright: after M91 (C-axis selection) a C-axis program must always follow, and putting such a block in an earlier block — still in spindle mode — or in the same block as M91 prevents normal operation; its right/wrong table names G28 H0 (the C-axis reference return) and G0 H-10. as exactly those C-axis blocks, and marks G00H-10. before M91 and G28H0M91 in one block as wrong. Monforts shows the same order on another builder (M5, then M21, then G28 C0). Fanuc's own alarm for the violation is PS0197 'C-ACHS-BEFEHL IM SPINDEL-MODUS'. The SETPOS half follows from the NT NURSE ordering M91, G28 H0, G50 C0, which puts the coordinate-setting block inside C-axis mode too. Caveats: The manuals settle HOME and, through the M91 / G28 H0 / G50 C0 order, SETPOS. They say nothing about TILT_AXIS with MOVE=TURN/MOVE on a work-spindle C axis, and nothing about a frame word such as SHIFT C=; that part of the recommendation rests on the NCX model alone. Fanuc's alarm text speaks of a movement along the Cs axis, which would not by itself cover a SETPOS that moves nothing — it is the Nakamura ordering rule plus the NT NURSE example that cover it. One observation on the other half of VM 3.8 rule 4, which this draft does not ask about: Monforts does not treat a spindle word in C-axis mode as an error at all — with M21 active, S, M3, M4 and M5 simply refer to the tool spindle instead of the main spindle.
Evidence: Nakamura-Tome, Präzisionsdrehzentrum Programmierhandbuch (1/2), Fanuc, p. 227 (PDF page; printed 14-2) ('Nach Anwahl des C-Achsen-Modus über den Befehl M91 muss stets ein Programm für die C-Achse eingefügt werden. Wird dieses Programm in einem vorherigen Satz (also noch im Spindelmodus) eingefügt oder in den gleichen Satz wie der Befehl M91, kann der normale Betrieb nicht ausgeführt werden.' The right/wrong table gives the correct order as M91, then G28H0, then G0H-10., and marks G00H-10. before M91 and G28H0M91 in one block as wrong.); Nakamura-Tome, Präzisionsdrehzentrum Programmierhandbuch (1/2), Fanuc, p. 226 (PDF page; printed 14-1) (Section 14-1 C-Achsen-Anschluss: M91 selects the C axis instead of the spindle and 'muss separat in einem eigenen Satz programmiert werden'; M41 switches back to spindle selection.); Nakamura-Tome, NT Nurse / NT Work Navigator Bedienungsanleitung (Fanuc 16/21i), p. 303 (PDF page; printed 3-2-22) (The worked example orders the blocks M91 (C-Achsen-Anschluss), G28 H0 (C-Achsen-Nullpunktrückstellung), G50 C0 (Initialisierung der C-Achsen-Koordinate): the coordinate-setting block stands inside C-axis mode, after the switch, which is what the SETPOS half of the rule needs.); Betriebshandbuch Drehen/Fräsen 30i/31i/32i-B (B-64484GE/02), Anhang H, p. 2391 (PDF page; printed 2357, alarm list) (Alarm 0197 'C-ACHS-BEFEHL IM SPINDEL-MODUS': 'Bewegung entlang der Cs-Achse befohlen, aber das Schaltsignal für Cs-Bahnsteuerung ist ausgeschaltet.' This is the control's version of the VM 3.8 rule 4 ERROR.); Monforts, Angetriebene Werkzeuge mit C-Achse über Hauptantrieb (Fanuc 16T/18iT/21iT), p. 5 (PDF page; printed Seite 3) (Program-structure example and its notes: N100 M5 stops the main spindle, N110 M21 selects C-axis mode ('M21 löscht M22'), and only then does N120 G28 C0 'Referenzieren der Rundachse C'. The reference return of the C axis is a C-axis-mode operation. Page 4 adds that with M21 active the spindle words S, M3, M4, M5 refer to the tool spindle.).
Settled 2026-10-01: the maintainer let the manual-confirmed answers that agree with their recommendation be applied without reviewing each one.

#### D133 Bare SKIP under a switch list
Question: Language 4.1 writes a bare SKIP for the plain block skip and SKIP=n for switch n. VM 3.6 introduces the list form skip_blocks = [1, 3] 'for numbered switches', and D53 says only that SKIP blocks run by default. Nothing says whether a list skips a bare SKIP, and the controllers differ. In controller-mapping 1 (row SKIP), Siemens '/' is the same as '/0', a level of its own beside '/1'..'/9'. On Fanuc, '/' and '/1' are one switch (Fanuc manual, not in the documents). Case: --skip-blocks 1 (P1-07) on a Fanuc program whose /M99 was read as SKIP JUMP=START. The code executes the block, while the machine with switch 1 on skips it. Also, no value of the option skips the bare SKIP blocks alone.
Recommendation: A bare SKIP is the first switch and has the number 0 in the run option. skip_blocks = [0, 3] (--skip-blocks 0,3) skips the bare SKIP blocks and SKIP=3. A list without 0 leaves the bare ones running, and all skips every SKIP block. This keeps the code's reading of the list and follows the Siemens numbering that controller-mapping 1 already gives. It needs SkipBlocks to count a bare SKIP as 0, and the P1-07 option to accept 0. The Fanuc reader then reads '/1' as a bare SKIP, because the control treats the two as one switch, and '/2'..'/9' as SKIP=2..9. For a Fanuc operator, the switch of '/' is therefore 0 in --skip-blocks, which the P1-07 help text says. Alternative: a bare SKIP counts as switch 1 (the Fanuc reading), so [1] skips both. The VM would then treat Siemens '/' and '/1', which are two levels on the control, as one switch.
Where: VM 3.6 (skip_blocks sentence), VM 2.2 (row skip), language 4.1 (row SKIP), controller-mapping 1 (row SKIP, Fanuc '/1'); src/Ncx.Core/VirtualMachine/SkipBlocks.cs Skips and OnSwitches (TODO at 59-62); implementation 11 and P1-07 (`--skip-blocks <none|all|1,3>`, which P1-07 enters into architecture 10 per F28).

ANSWER:
As recommended, confirmed from the manual library: The Fanuc reading in the recommendation is right and can now be written as fact instead of as a guess: on Fanuc `/` and `/1` are one switch — the table of input signal against start code gives BDT1 the codes "/ oder /1", and the 1 in /1 may be omitted, being required only when a block carries several skips (`/1 /3 /5` is right, `//3` is wrong). Siemens numbers one lower: `/` and `/0` are both the first skip level and `/1` is the second, with at most one level per block and ten levels in all. So the Fanuc reader reads `/1` as a bare SKIP and `/2`..`/9` as SKIP=2..9, the bare SKIP is switch 0 in `--skip-blocks`, and the P1-07 help text says that a Fanuc operator's switch 1 is 0 there.
Evidence: FANUC Series 30i/31i/32i-MODEL B Betriebshandbuch Drehen/Fräsen (B-64484GE/02), p. PDF 331 (printed 297, §13, Wahlweise Satzausblendung) (With /n (n = 1 to 9) at the head of a block and the matching signal BDT1..BDT9 at 1, everything from /n to the end of block is ignored. The table of input signal against start code gives BDT1 the codes "/ oder /1" and BDT2..BDT9 the codes /2../9. The examples mark //3 wrong and /1 /3 right); FANUC Series 30i/31i/32i-MODEL B Betriebshandbuch Drehen/Fräsen (B-64484GE/02), p. PDF 332 (printed 298) (Note 1 states that the 1 in /1 may be left out, but is needed when a block specifies more than one optional block skip. Case 4 below shows /1 /3 /5 on one block, which is ignored when any one of the matching signals is set to 1); SINUMERIK 840D sl / 828D Programmierhandbuch Grundlagen (03/2013), p. PDF 40 (§2.2, Ausblendebenen) (Blocks may be assigned up to ten skip levels, written as a slash plus the level number, and only one level per block. The example list gives / and /0 as the first skip level, /1 as the second, /2 as the third, up to /9 as the tenth).
Settled 2026-10-01: the maintainer let the manual-confirmed answers that agree with their recommendation be applied without reviewing each one.

### Sixth round: needed before the readers and compilers (phase 3)

#### D144 The form of n in `CYCLE:<controller>=n`
Question: The CYCLE row of language 4.7 gives the addressed form as 'the native cycle number of that family' and shows only CYCLE:HEIDENHAIN=251; D45 writes CYCLE:CONTROLLER=n. The catalogs write the native cycle as text: machine-config 6 writes native = 251 for Heidenhain and native = "G71" for Fanuc; cycles/siemens.toml writes native = "CYCLE81"; controller-mapping 5 names Siemens cycles that are not a prefix plus a cycle number (LONGHOLE, POCKET3, HOLES1) and Fanuc-family cycles with a decimal point (Mori Seiki G83.5, G87.5). The CYCLE entry on main takes only an integer after a controller address (CycleWords.cs, AddressedValueKinds). CYCLE:FANUC=G71 and CYCLE:SIEMENS=CYCLE952 are therefore value ERRORs (PAR153). CYCLE:FANUC=71 never finds the entry "G71", because CycleCatalog.FindNative compares text.
Recommendation: n is the native cycle exactly as the family's catalog writes `native`: an integer for Heidenhain (251); an identifier for Siemens (CYCLE952, LONGHOLE) and Fanuc (G71); a string where the native is neither, as with the dotted Fanuc-family codes (CYCLE:FANUC="G83.5"). The CYCLE word with an address then takes an integer, an identifier or a string. FindNative stays a text comparison, using the string's content. The 4.7 row reads: 'the native cycle of that family as its cycle catalog writes it (CYCLE:HEIDENHAIN=251, CYCLE:FANUC=G71, CYCLE:SIEMENS=CYCLE952)'. Alternative: the number alone (71, 952), with the readers and compilers restoring the family prefix. That fails for Siemens names that are not a prefix plus a number (LONGHOLE, POCKET3, HOLES1). This settles n only. In a Fanuc native block, the Fanuc parameters F, R, X and Z are catalog words, not native parameters, because D94 takes only the keys the catalog does not know. Siemens signature names with a leading underscore (_AXN, _VRT) are not NCX keys (language 3). The parameters of a native Fanuc or Siemens cycle therefore need a question of their own before P3-06 and P5-02.
Where: language 4.7 (CYCLE row), 4.7.1; D45, D94; machine-config 6; controller-mapping 5; src/Ncx.Core/Catalog/CycleWords.cs (CYCLE AddressedValueKinds); src/Ncx.Core/Machine/CycleCatalog.cs (TODO(question) above PassesThrough, FindNative); docs/spec/generated/word-catalog.md (CYCLE row).

ANSWER:
As recommended, confirmed from the manual library: Keep the recommendation and drop the "number alone" alternative: in the Fanuc family the native cycle code is not a number. The Mori Seiki NTX1000 G-code list carries G83.5, G83.6, G87.5, G87.6 (and G80.4/G81.4) beside the plain G83/G87, so dotted native codes are real and need the string form, `CYCLE:FANUC="G83.5"`. A bare number would also be ambiguous inside Fanuc itself: in G-code system C the outside roughing cycle is G73 while the token G71 means millimetre input, and within systems A and B G71 stands for the turning roughing cycle in group 00 and for the "Zeilenschleifzyklus" in group 01 — only the family catalog's `native` text, read against the machine's `gcode_system`, identifies the cycle. On the Siemens side the overview of cycles likewise lists HOLES1, HOLES2, LONGHOLE, SLOT1, POCKET1..POCKET4 beside the CYCLExx names, which no prefix-plus-number scheme covers.
Evidence: Mori Seiki NT/NTX-Serie Programmieranleitung NTX1000 SZM (PX-NT_4-K0DEEN), p. PDF 80 (§2-1 G-Code-Liste) (The machine's G-code list has, in the group-10 hole-cycle block beside G80 and the plain G83/G87, the codes G83.5 and G87.5 for high-speed deep-hole drilling on the face and the side and G83.6/G87.6 for the deep-hole variants; G80.4 and G81.4 for hobbing synchronisation stand on the same page as options); FANUC Series 30i/31i/32i-MODEL B Betriebshandbuch Drehen (B-64484GE-1/02), p. PDF 30 (printed 14, G-Code-Liste, Tabelle 2 (a)) (The three-column list of G-code systems A/B/C shows G71 in systems A and B as "Materialabnahme beim Drehen (außen)" in group 00 while system C uses G73 for it, and further down the same page G71 in systems A and B is the "Zeilenschleifzyklus" of group 01 (G72 in system C)); FANUC Series 30i/31i/32i-MODEL B Betriebshandbuch Drehen (B-64484GE-1/02), p. PDF 27 (printed 11, G-Code-Liste, Tabelle 2 (a)) (In the same list, G20/G21 for inch and millimetre input in systems A and B are G70/G71 in system C, so the token G71 means millimetre input on a system C machine); SINUMERIK 840D sl / 840D / 840Di sl Zyklen, Programmierhandbuch (01/2008), p. PDF 12 (§1.1 Überblick über die Zyklen) (The overview of cycles lists the hole-pattern cycles HOLES1, HOLES2 and CYCLE801 and the milling cycles CYCLE90, LONGHOLE, SLOT1, SLOT2, POCKET1 to POCKET4, CYCLE71, CYCLE72 and further — names that are not a common prefix plus a cycle number).
Settled 2026-10-01: the maintainer let the manual-confirmed answers that agree with their recommendation be applied without reviewing each one.

#### D147 Which of A, B, C resolve to the workpiece holder's axis
Question: VM 3.8 rule 3, language 4.3 (X row) and language 4.10 (WORKPIECE row: "ORIGIN, SHIFT and A B C refer to it") let each of A, B and C name the rotary axis of the current workpiece holder. Machine-config 4 gives only a work spindle an axis ("the C axis this spindle becomes in AXIS mode"). Read literally, B on mori-ntx1000-mapps.toml and dmg-ctx-840d.toml (the tool spindle swivel B1) resolves to C1 or C4 while the main spindle holds the part, and to C2 or C3 after WORKPIECE=SUB. On doosan-puma-2600sy.toml and nakamura-ntjx.toml B is the linear sub spindle slide B1, so the slide moves of a transfer, made while MAIN holds the part, would go to C1. On the Mori Seiki, A (the linear sub spindle slide A1) resolves to C2 after WORKPIECE=SUB. The code resolves only the name whose letter the holder's axis carries (C to C2); A and B resolve by NCX name.
Recommendation: Keep what the code does. The standard name whose letter the holder's rotary axis carries (its NCX name without the digits: C2 gives C, so in practice C) resolves to that axis. Every other name resolves through [[axis]] by NCX name. Reason: the literal reading breaks every A or B program on the four mill-turn example files that have such an axis. Also, millturn1.toml, doosan-puma-2600sy.toml and nakamura-ntjx.toml already comment that a program's C is the holder's axis. Writing the rule as 'C resolves to the holder's axis' is equivalent in every documented case.
Where: VM 3.8 rule 3; language 4.3 (X row) and 4.10 (WORKPIECE row); src/Ncx.Core/Machine/MachineConfig.cs ResolveAxis(ncxName, workpieceHolder) TODO.

ANSWER:
As recommended, confirmed from the manual library: Keep what the code does; the literal reading of VM 3.8 rule 3 would break real programs on every mill-turn in the library. B is always something else: the tool-spindle index angle on the Mori NTX, the tool carrier's swivel B1 on the DMG CTX/GMX (-30 to 210 degrees, only on machines that have a B1 axis), the counter-spindle slide on the Doosan Puma 2600SY (830 mm of travel on the L750 bed, measured from main to counter spindle head) and the linear NC sub spindle on Nakamura; A is the Mori's headstock-2 / workpiece-ejector slide, which takes a Z coordinate. And the holder's own axis is rarely plain C — the Doosan has C1 and C2, the DMG has C3 for the counter and C4 for the main spindle through L705 and L707 — while a Hermle table carries both a C and an A axis, so "the holder's rotary axis" is not even unique on a mill. Resolve to the holder's axis by that axis, and let every other name go through [[axis]].
Evidence: MORI SEIKI NT/NTX-Serie, Programmieranleitung NTX1000 SZM (PX-NT_4-K0DEEN, 2011), p. 74-76 (Achsensteuerung und Bewegungsrichtung); PDF page = printed page (The axis list: X gives diametral dimensions, Z longitudinal, Y the direction perpendicular to both, C the spindle index angle for milling, B the tool-spindle index angle with B0 at the zero-return position, and BW the index angle of the workpiece ejector and spindle 2 on the NTX1000 series. Page 76 adds the note that in cutting off, spindle 2 moves in the Z direction to take the part over, and that on the NT-SZ series this movement is made along the A axis.); MORI SEIKI NT/NTX-Serie, Programmieranleitung NTX1000 SZM (PX-NT_4-K0DEEN, 2011), p. 566 (sections 4-1 and 4-2); PDF page = printed page (Moving the workpiece ejector / headstock 2 is the A axis, and `G00 A_` takes the target Z coordinate the unit travels to, as an absolute command — a linear slide, not a rotary axis of a holder. Section 4-2 separately gives BW as an index of the same unit, rotation range 0 to 225, with four M-code-selected positions.); DOOSAN PUMA 2600 LSY II, Benutzerhandbuch Spezifikation und Wartung (2020), p. printed 046 (PDF 56, section 3 Zuordnung der Achsen); printed 76 (PDF 86); printed 190 (PDF 200); printed 232 (PDF 242) (The axis assignment diagram of the P2600SY II names Z, C1, C2, Y, X and B. The specification table gives the B axis a travel of 830 mm on the L750 bed with a rapid of 30 m/min, the travel table's note 3 says the B travel is measured between the main spindle head and the counter spindle head, and the lubrication chapter's item is "B-Achsenführungsbahn (Gegenspindel oder Servo-Reitstock)". The two work spindles' rotary axes are C1 and C2.); Nakamura-Tome NT NURSE Bedienungsanleitung (4800001EBG, 2013), p. printed 2-26—1 (PDF 242), section 26-1 (The arbitrary-axis torque-limit function G359 lists its available axes as "Z-Achse und B-Achse (NC-Zusatzspindel)", and `G359 Z__ B__` takes a limit value of 1 to 255 for each, exactly as for Z — B is a linear slide on this machine.); Nakamura-Tome Programmierhandbuch (DE 2019, agent handbook), p. printed 129 ff. (PDF 133-139), chapter "Nakamura B-Achsen Schwenkrevolvermaschinen NTJ100"; the linear B on PDF 24 (The M-code list speaks of "die lineare B-Achse rechts", while the separate NTJ100 chapter treats B as a swivel: "B: Winkel der B-Achse (-90 ≤ B ≤ 90)", with the machine swivelling the B axis automatically when the cycle is called. The same letter is a slide on one Nakamura and an angle on another.); DMG MORI CTX / GMX, Technik und Programmierung Sinumerik 840D sl V2.1 (2015), p. printed 2-15 to 2-22 (PDF 29-36) for the C axes; printed 2-24 (PDF 38) and PDF 100-102 and 119 for B1 (L701/L702 switch tool spindle 1 into and out of C-axis mode as the C1 axis, L703/L704 tool spindle 2 as C2, L705/L706 the counter spindle as C3 and L707/L708 the main spindle as C4. Separately, the tool-change-point cycle's order parameter offers "5 = Wechselpunkt wird in B1 angefahren (nur Maschinen mit B1-Achse)", and the cycle parameter tables give ANG - B1 a range of -30 / 210 degrees with the meaning "Winkel der B1-Achse für den Tool-Carrier" / "Werkzeugausrichtung".); Hermle M-Funktionen C 400 / C 12 / C 22 / C 32 / C 42 / C 52 / C 60 (2015), p. printed 233 (PDF 3) (M25 and M26 release and clamp the C axis, M27 and M28 the A axis, the latter marked "nur MT-Maschinen" and present in only two of the four machine-group columns. On a Hermle swivel-rotary table the workpiece carrier therefore has two rotary axes.).
