#### D148 Start values of a callee's V1..V33
Question: VM 3.6 says a CALL 'pushes return pc and the local variables V1..V33, assigns ARG words to the callee's locals'. The variables row of VM 4 has 'V1..V33 per call' and 'SUB=END and RETURN restore locals'. Neither says whether the callee's V1..V33 start unassigned or as a copy of the caller's. The two Fanuc calls differ. G65 opens a new level whose #1..#33 are vacant except the letter arguments (fanuc 7: '#1..#33 are local to a macro call level'). M98 opens no new level, and the subprogram reads and writes the caller's #1..#33 (Fanuc manual, not in the documents). Case: a caller sets VAR:V1=5 and CALL=100, and the subprogram reads {$V1}. In INTERPRETED mode, an unassigned start makes that read the D38 ERROR, and a copy reads 5. STATIC mode evaluates no expression, so there only the variables in the subprogram's snapshots and trace rows differ.
Recommendation: The callee's V1..V33 start unassigned, apart from the ARG values, and SUB=END and RETURN restore the caller's. The code already does this. Reasons: V1..V33 exist in NCX for the G65 letter arguments (language 4.9, last paragraph; fanuc 7). VM 3.6 already restores the caller's locals at the return, which is how G65 behaves and not M98, because under M98 the caller sees what the subprogram wrote. A copy would let an M98 subprogram read the caller's values, but its writes would still be lost at the return, so a copy does not make M98 work either. D38 then reports a read of a local the caller did not pass. Consequence for the Fanuc reader (P3-02): if an M98 subprogram reads the caller's #1..#33, the reader passes them as ARG:Vn={$Vn} on the CALL. If it writes them back for the caller, it is not a plain CALL and the reader reports it. Alternative: the callee's V1..V33 start as a copy of the caller's. M98 reads then work, but a G65 macro sees caller values where the control has vacant ones.
Where: VM 3.6 (CALL sentence), VM 4 (row variables), language 4.9 (last paragraph), fanuc 7; src/Ncx.Core/VirtualMachine/State/VariableStore.cs PushLocals (TODO at 169-170); P4-01 (ARG into the callee's locals); Fanuc reader M98/G65 rule (P3-02).

ANSWER:
As recommended, confirmed from the manual library: Keep the recommendation and the code as it stands: a callee's V1..V33 start unassigned apart from the ARG values, and SUB=END and RETURN restore the caller's. Fanuc states both halves outright — a local variable that received no argument starts as <Null> (vacant) and may then be used freely, and a macro call raises the local-variable level (levels 0 to 5, the main program being 0), the previous level's values being stored in the CNC and restored when M99 lowers the level again. The difference the draft turns on is written down as well: the list of differences between a macro call and a subprogram call ends with the point that a macro call changes the local-variable level while a subprogram call does not — so an M98 subprogram shares the caller's #1..#33 for reading and for writing, and the reader consequence stands: an M98 subprogram that reads them needs ARG:Vn={$Vn} on the CALL, and one that writes them back for the caller is not a plain CALL.
Evidence: FANUC Series 30i/31i/32i-MODEL B Betriebshandbuch Drehen/Fräsen (B-64484GE/02), p. PDF 427 (printed 393, §16.1, Lokale Variable #1-#33) (A local variable belongs to one macro call, so the #i a macro uses at one time is a different one from the #i at another time, and a nested macro cannot damage the caller's locals. Locals carry the arguments, and the initial state of a local that received no argument is <Null>, the variable then being free to use); FANUC Series 30i/31i/32i-MODEL B Betriebshandbuch Drehen/Fräsen (B-64484GE/02), p. PDF 505 (printed 471, §16.9 Beschränkungen) (Among the listed differences between a macro call (G66, G66.1, Ggg, Mmm) and a subprogram call (M98, Mmm, Ttt): only a macro call can take arguments, and the last bullet says a macro call changes the level of local variables while a subprogram call does not, cross-referring to "Ebenen lokaler Variablen" in the G65 subsection); FANUC Series 30i/31i/32i-MODEL B Betriebshandbuch Drehen/Fräsen (B-64484GE/02), p. PDF 511 (printed 477, §16.9.1, Ebenen lokaler Variablen) (Local variables have levels 0 to 5; the main program is level 0, every macro call raises the level by one and the previous level's values are stored in the CNC, and executing M99 in the macro returns to the caller, lowers the level by one and restores the stored values. The figure shows an independent #1..#33 per level).
Settled 2026-10-01: the maintainer let the manual-confirmed answers that agree with their recommendation be applied without reviewing each one.

#### D153 Padded placeholders against numbers of another width
Question: The machine-config introduction says only 'A format suffix pads numbers: {tool:02} writes 04'. It does not say how a reader matches a source without the leading zero, or what a number wider than the width writes. Fanuc address values carry no significant leading zeros, so a lathe source may write T101 for T0101 (tool 1, offset 01). Please confirm: fanuc.md 5 and controller-mapping 3 show only zero-padded forms (T0404, T0100, T001001). P2-02 already lets an unpadded placeholder read leading zeros (M{mark} matches M0106, D105). Main reads exactly the width, so T101 does not match T{tool:02}{offset:02} and becomes RAW; and it renders a wider number in full, so tool 123 writes T12301, which does not match back.
Recommendation: Read the digits of one address as one number that the placeholders split from the right: a padded placeholder that begins a run of digits reads one or more digits; a padded placeholder that follows digits (a literal digit or another placeholder) reads exactly its width. So T101 reads as tool 1, offset 1, and G340 T101. A2. reads like G340 T0101. A02. T12301 reads as tool 123, offset 1. #11{index:03} still needs exactly three digits after 11. Render pads and never truncates, as on main. A number wider than its width is written in full where it begins the run. Where it follows digits (offset 123 in T{tool:02}{offset:02}, index 1234 in #11{index:03}), it is a CFG ERROR on the block, because the text would read back as other numbers. This keeps every rendered text matching back. Alternative: treat the width as the machine's fixed field. Read exactly the width, as on main, so T101 becomes RAW with a WARNING, and make every wider number a CFG ERROR at render.
Where: machine-config introduction (the format suffix sentence); src/Ncx.Config/Templates/TemplatePattern.cs GroupOf (TODO(question)); Placeholder.Write and Template.Render (the new ERROR); DiagnosticCodes.Templates.cs; tests/Ncx.Config.Tests/Templates/TemplateMatchesTests.cs and TemplateRenderTests.cs.

ANSWER:
As recommended, confirmed from the manual library: Take the recommendation: read the digits of one address as one number that the placeholders split from the right. That is what the control does — Fanuc defines the wear-offset number as the last one, two or three digits of the T code (parameter 5028, with bit 1 (LGN) of parameter 5002 deciding whether the leading digits also carry the geometry number), and the total digit count is only a maximum, 1 to 8 by parameter 3032. Real programs write the unpadded form: Doosan's own Fanuc-30-series manual programs `T202 ... T200` for tool 2 with offset 02 and then the offset cancel, and states that only the lower two digits call the tool offset (`T0021` = offset 21). `#11{index:03}` keeps its exactly-three-digits rule, because there the index is a compensation number 1..999 inside a fixed variable number (#10001-#10999, #11001-#11999) and 1000 has nowhere to go.
Evidence: FANUC Series 30i/31i/32i-MODEL B Betriebshandbuch Drehen (B-64484GE-1/02), p. PDF 149 (printed 133, §5.1.2 T-Code für Werkzeugkorrektur) (The table defines the T code as a tool selection part plus an offset part taken from the end: the wear offset number is specified with the last digit, the last two digits or the last three digits according to parameter 5028, and bit 1 (LGN) of parameter 5002 decides whether the leading digits also carry the geometry offset. Footnote 1 says the maximum number of digits of a T code is set by parameter 3032 (1 to 8); footnote 2 that with 5028 = 0 the number of offset digits follows the number of offsets available (1-9 → last digit, 10-99 → last two, 100-999 → last three)); Doosan NC Programming for Turning Centers, Fanuc 30 Series, p. PDF 19 (printed 13, §3.14) (The page explains that a tool may be commanded with different offsets (T0101, T0121) and that an offset alone can be commanded without a tool number, giving T0021 as offset 21; on a gang-type lathe the upper two digits are never used and only the lower two digits are used for calling the tool offset); Doosan NC Programming for Turning Centers, Fanuc 30 Series, p. PDF 73 (printed 67, G74 example) (The worked peck-drilling program writes the three-digit form: it starts with N100 T202 M8 and ends with G0 G40 X10. Z10. T200, that is tool 2 with offset 02 and then the same tool with the offset cancelled); Nakamura-Tome NT-IPS Bedienungsanleitung (4800554EAG), p. PDF 27 (printed 4-17) (The load-display page tells the operator to enter the T code with as many digits as the selected T-code type has (four-digit or six-digit) and heads its example "Zur Festlegung von T101 oder T0101", treating the padded and the unpadded spelling as the same T code. It is an entry screen rule, not a statement about program text); FANUC Series 30i/31i/32i-MODEL B Betriebshandbuch Drehen/Fräsen (B-64484GE/02), p. PDF 433 (printed 399, §16.2) (The tool-compensation variables #10001-#10999 and #11001-#11999 are the named [#_OFSW[n]] / [#_OFSG[n]] with the index n running from 1 to 999, so the index occupies exactly the last three digits of the variable number).
Settled 2026-10-01: the maintainer let the manual-confirmed answers that agree with their recommendation be applied without reviewing each one.

#### D160 Fanuc lathe drilling: a lathe catalog and an axis key
Question: Controller-mapping 5 (AXIS), fanuc 6 and language 4.7 (AXIS, D59) give lathe drilling as G83/G84/G85 along Z and G87/G88/G89 along X. The built-in Fanuc family (DrillingFamily.Fanuc.cs) and cycles/fanuc.toml carry the mill codes. fanuc.toml also holds the lathe turning entries (G90/G92/G94, G70..G76), and fanuc-mill-30i.toml names that file. On a lathe G73, G74 and G76 are turning cycles and G87..G89 drill along X. On a mill the same numbers are chip breaking, left-hand tapping, fine boring and back boring, and G90/G92/G94 are not cycles at all. Phase 3 P3-02 (FanucCycles) reads "G73..G89 into CYCLE=" and sets AXIS=X for G87..G89 without naming the machine kind. Machine-config 6 gives an entry one `native` and no key that selects it by AXIS, so DRILL cannot be G83 under AXIS=Z and G87 under AXIS=X (POLAR_FACE.ncx writes DRILL AXIS=X as G87). `fixed` compares values only, so no key tells a lathe G83 without Q (DRILL) from one with Q (PECK). No document says which NCX cycle a lathe G85/G89 is.
Recommendation: (1) Ship cycles/fanuc-lathe.toml, named by `[cycles] catalog` in the Fanuc lathe files and written in system A numbers (see D174). fanuc.toml keeps the mill codes, and its turning entries move to the lathe file. A machine file still overrides per machine (the Doosan PECK_MODE rules). (2) Add an optional entry key `for_axis = "X"`: the entry maps its cycle only under that AXIS, and the entry without the key maps the default axis. The reader sets AXIS from the entry it matched, and the compiler looks up name plus AXIS. Override and the duplicate check go by name plus for_axis. (3) Of two entries on one native, the reader takes the first in catalog order whose params cover the words of the block. Machine-config 6 says so next to `fixed`. (4) Lathe entries: DRILL = G83/G87 without Q; PECK = G83/G87 with Q, listed after DRILL so that (3) picks it when Q stands; TAP = G84/G88; REAM = G85/G89 (feed in and feed out, the motion of mill G85; to be confirmed against the lathe manual). CHIP_BREAK stays per machine, since a parameter or a builder M code selects it (Doosan M292). Reason: D59 keeps one family with AXIS, D76 keeps catalogs as data, and `[cycles] catalog` already names a file per machine. Alternative: lathe entries in each lathe machine file, as the code has it now. That needs no new file but makes three copies, and still needs the axis key and rule (3).
Where: machine-config 6 (entry keys, `fixed`, shipped catalogs) and 10 (cycles/ layout); controller-mapping 5 (AXIS row); fanuc 6; 13-phase-3-readers-compilers.md P3-02 (FanucCycles) and the P3-02 task; cycles/fanuc.toml lines 76-80 and 83-158; new cycles/fanuc-lathe.toml; src/Ncx.Core/Machine/CycleEntry.cs and CycleCatalog.cs (Find, FindNative, Override); src/Ncx.Config/Cycles/CycleCatalogLoader.Entries.cs; tests/Ncx.Config.Tests/Cycles/ShippedCatalogsTests.cs (the turning and G71 tests); in docs/spec/examples/machines/, the [machine] tables of nakamura-ntjx and mori-ntx1000-mapps (neither has a [cycles] table yet) and the [cycles] table of doosan-puma-2600sy.

ANSWER:
As recommended, confirmed from the manual library: Ship the lathe catalog as recommended, with the lathe drilling group corrected: a Fanuc lathe's canned-cycle group holds only G80, G83/G84/G85 (drilling axis Z, positioning axes X and C) and G87/G88/G89 (drilling axis X, positioning axes Z and C). G86 does not appear anywhere in the lathe G-code list, and G81 and G82 appear in it only as FS15-T and FS15 format codes, not as cycles of this group. All six cycles accept P, a dwell at the hole bottom. DRILL = G83/G87 without Q (without Q the control runs a plain drilling cycle and retracts from the bottom in rapid), PECK = G83/G87 with Q, TAP = G84/G88, REAM = G85/G89, which feeds in, dwells and feeds back out at twice the cutting feedrate. A lathe G83 with Q does not say by itself whether it breaks chips or fully retracts — bit 2 (RTR) of parameter 5101 decides — so CHIP_BREAK per machine is right, and G83.5/G87.5 (high-speed, small retract) and G83.6/G87.6 (full retract) are the clean explicit lathe codes for the two behaviours.
Evidence: Betriebshandbuch Drehen 30i/31i/32i-B (B-64484GE-1/02), p. 92 (printed 76) (Table 4.3 (a) lists the lathe canned cycles: G80 end, G83 and G87 cutting feed / intermittent with a dwell at the bottom and rapid retract, G84 and G88 with a spindle reversal, G85 and G89 cutting feed in, dwell, cutting feed out. Nothing else is in the table); Betriebshandbuch Drehen 30i/31i/32i-B (B-64484GE-1/02), p. 93 (printed 77) (Table 4.3 (b): for G83, G84, G85 the positioning axes are X and C and the drilling axis is Z; for G87, G88, G89 they are Z and C with X as the drilling axis. The text adds that the two triples are otherwise identical in function); Betriebshandbuch Drehen 30i/31i/32i-B (B-64484GE-1/02), p. 96 and 98 (printed 80 and 82) (Format G83 X(U) C(H) Z(W) R P Q F K M (and G87 with X and Z exchanged); Q is the depth of cut per infeed, P the dwell at the bottom. Page 98 states that without Q a normal drilling cycle is performed and the tool is retracted from the bottom in rapid. Page 96 also says bit 2 (RTR) of parameter 5101 picks the high-speed peck or the full-retract peck, and that G83.5/G87.5 and G83.6/G87.6 name the two without the parameter); Betriebshandbuch Drehen 30i/31i/32i-B (B-64484GE-1/02), p. 100 (printed 84) (Format G85 X(U) C(H) Z(W) R P F K M and G89 with X and Z exchanged; the explanation says the tool cuts from R to Z and returns from Z to R at twice the cutting feedrate); Betriebshandbuch Drehen 30i/31i/32i-B (B-64484GE-1/02), p. 30 (printed 14) (The lathe G-code list gives G81 as "Punktbohren (FS15-T-Format)" and G82 as "Senkbohren (FS15-Format)"; G86 does not occur in the list at all (a grep of the whole volume finds no G86). G73, G74, G75, G76 stand in group 00 as the pattern-repeat, Z-peck, OD/ID boring and multiple thread cycles, so the mill meanings of those numbers do not exist on the lathe); Präzisionsdrehzentrum Programmierhandbuch (1/2), Nakamura-Tome 4810004ECL-1, p. 238 (printed 14-13) (Table 14-1, the builder's own cycle table, repeats it for the NT family: G83/G84/G85 on the Z axis, G87/G88/G89 on the X axis, G85/G89 as "Aufbohren" with a dwell and a feed retract, and a footnote that in G83 and G87 the axis feed is cutting feed or peck feed depending on whether a Q command is programmed).
Settled 2026-10-01: the maintainer let the manual-confirmed answers that agree with their recommendation be applied without reviewing each one.

#### D161 NCX names of Fanuc G92 and G76
Question: Language 4.7.1 lists the turning cycles next to their counterparts on the other controls: ROUGH_TURN, ROUGH_FACE, FINISH, GROOVE and THREAD for Fanuc G70..G76, Siemens CYCLE95/CYCLE93/CYCLE97 and Heidenhain 81x. That list reads THREAD as G76, next to the Siemens thread cycle CYCLE97. The specification gives no NCX name to G92 or G94, and none of COMPOUND_THREAD, FACE or TURN_ID appears in it. The phase file P2-03, and cycles/fanuc.toml after it, give THREAD to G92 and COMPOUND_THREAD to G76. Where a phase file and the specification disagree, the specification wins (implementation/README.md line 41). A CYCLE=THREAD read from a Siemens CYCLE97 would compile to one G92 pass as the catalog stands.
Recommendation: Follow the specification. THREAD = G76, the thread cycle that cuts every pass in one call, as Siemens CYCLE97 does, and COMPOUND_THREAD is dropped. G92 cuts one pass per block, like TURN_OD (G90) and FACE (G94), and gets a name of its own: THREAD_PASS. Language 4.7.1 names TURN_OD, THREAD_PASS and FACE for G90/G92/G94. Reason: a program that writes CYCLE=THREAD then means the whole thread on every controller. Alternative: amend the list of language 4.7.1 to THREAD = G92 and COMPOUND_THREAD = G76, as the code has it.
Where: language 4.7.1; controller-mapping 5 (turning cycles row); 12-phase-2-configuration.md P2-03 (plan text); cycles/fanuc.toml lines 107-117 and 150-156; tests/Ncx.Config.Tests/Cycles/ShippedCatalogsTests.cs (THREAD and COMPOUND_THREAD rows).

ANSWER:
As recommended, confirmed from the manual library: Follow the specification: THREAD = G76, THREAD_PASS = G92, and COMPOUND_THREAD is dropped. The manual makes the two plainly different in kind: G92 is the modal "Gewindeschneidzyklus" that cuts one pass in four moves and comes back to the start point, so a following block with a new X repeats it, exactly like G90 and G94; G76 is the one-shot (group 00) "Zyklus für Mehrfach-Gewindeschneiden" that cuts the whole thread from the thread height k with an automatic infeed that decreases from the first cut Δd and is clamped at Δdmin, plus a finish allowance d and m finishing repeats. That is the same job as Siemens CYCLE97, whose infeed is likewise automatic with NRC roughing and NID spring cuts, so a CYCLE=THREAD read from CYCLE97 must compile to G76 and not to one G92 pass.
Evidence: Betriebshandbuch Drehen 30i/31i/32i-B (B-64484GE-1/02), p. 40 and 41 (printed 24 and 25) (Section 4.1.2 "Gewindeschneidzyklus (G92)": G92 X(U) Z(W) F Q, F being the thread pitch (L); the cycle runs four operations, cutting one pass, and the fourth brings the tool back to the start point A. It is cancelled only by a group 01 code other than G90, G92, G94); Betriebshandbuch Drehen 30i/31i/32i-B (B-64484GE-1/02), p. 84 and 85 (printed 68 and 69) (Section 4.2.7: the two-block G76 carries m finishing repeats, chamfer r and tool angle a packed into P, the minimum cut Δdmin in Q and the finish allowance d in R, and in the second block the thread height k, the first cut Δd and the lead F; figure 4.2.7 (b) shows passes 1, 2, 3 … n cut down to the thread height with Δd·√n infeeds. Page 30 puts G76 in group 00, i.e. one-shot); Programmierhandbuch Zyklen SINUMERIK 840D sl/840D/840Di sl, p. 351 and 352 (CYCLE97 makes a complete cylindrical or tapered thread, single or multi-start; the infeed happens automatically, with a choice of constant depth per cut or constant chip section, and the parameters include thread depth TDEP, finish allowance FAL, number of roughing cuts NRC, number of spring cuts NID and number of starts NUMT).
Settled 2026-10-01: the maintainer let the manual-confirmed answers that agree with their recommendation be applied without reviewing each one.

#### D163 Heidenhain 200 and 203: which Q values select the NCX cycle
Question: controller-mapping 5 maps DRILL and DRILL_DWELL to CYCL DEF 200 (DRILL_DWELL 'with Q211'), PECK to 203 'with retract' and CHIP_BREAK to 203 'with Q256'. The example pair contradicts the Q256 reading. BOHREN.h writes Q256=0,6 in all three 203 blocks and differs only in Q213: Q213=24 where BOHREN.fanuc.nc has G73, Q213=0 where it has G83, and Q213=3 where the Fanuc source writes single G0/G1 moves. machine-config 6 'fixed' can express only equality. The code takes the first entry (DRILL, PECK) for every 200 and 203 (CycleCatalog.FindNative).
Recommendation: Cycle 200: Q211=0 reads as DRILL, any other Q211 as DRILL_DWELL with CYCLE_DWELL=Q211. Both compile with Q211 = CYCLE_DWELL, or 0 when there is none. Cycle 203: Q213=0 reads as PECK (full retract after every infeed, language 4.7 'deep hole, full retract', G83). A Q213 of at least the number of infeeds, ceil(|Q201|/Q202), reads as CHIP_BREAK (G73). Any Q213 in between is the mixed form, which has no NCX cycle; it is read natively as CYCLE:HEIDENHAIN=203 (D94). The compiler writes Q213=0 for PECK and the number of infeeds for CHIP_BREAK. These are rules of the Heidenhain reader and compiler (heidenhain 7 and 8 rule 7), not fixed values. controller-mapping 5 then reads '203 with Q213=0' and '203 with Q213 at least the number of infeeds'. Two consequences for phase 3. First, BOHREN.h's Q213=24 compiles back as 19, so the P3-04 comparison must allow it. Second, the Q213=3 section needs an exception in both acceptance lines whatever is decided here. BOHREN.fanuc.nc writes that section as single G0/G1 moves, so the two sources cannot give the same BOHREN.ncx (P3-05). And Expected/BOHREN.ncx, which comes from the Fanuc source, cannot compile back to CYCL DEF 203 Q213=3 (P3-04). Alternative: every Q213>0 is CHIP_BREAK, and the mixed form gets a WARNING.
Where: controller-mapping 5 (DRILL_DWELL, PECK, CHIP_BREAK rows); heidenhain.md 7 rule 7, 8 rule 7; cycles/heidenhain.toml (200 and 203 entries); src/Ncx.Core/Machine/DrillingFamily.Heidenhain.cs; CycleCatalog.FindNative; 13-phase-3 P3-04 and P3-05 acceptance.

ANSWER:
As recommended, confirmed from the manual library: Cycle 200: Q211 is the dwell at the hole bottom, a time in seconds with range from 0, so Q211=0 reads as DRILL and any other value as DRILL_DWELL with CYCLE_DWELL=Q211, and the compiler writes Q211=0 when there is none. Cycle 203: Q213 is "Anzahl Spanbrüche vor Rückzug", the number of chip breaks before the control retracts from the hole, so Q213=0 is the manual's "ohne Spanbruch" case — a full retract to Q200 after every infeed, which is G83 and NCX PECK — and a Q213 the drilling never reaches, at least ceil(|Q201|/Q202) infeeds, never produces a full retract, which is G73 and CHIP_BREAK; anything in between is the mixed form and stays CYCLE:HEIDENHAIN=203. Q256 cannot be the discriminator: it stands in every 203 block (iTNC input range from 0.1) and does nothing when Q213=0, so the controller-mapping 5 row "203 with Q256" is wrong and should read "203 with Q213=0" and "203 with Q213 at least the number of infeeds". BOHREN.h says the same in its own comments: Q213=24 is headed SPANBRECHEN, Q213=0 ENTSPANEN, Q213=3 SPANBRECHEN + ENTSPANEN.
Evidence: HEIDENHAIN TNC 640 Benutzerhandbuch Zyklenprogrammierung (NC-SW 34059x-10, 10/2019), p. 96, 97, 98 and 100-101 (cycle 203) — the original citation omitted 98 (Corrected: the cycle is described in three behaviours, not two — ohne Spanbruch ohne Abnahmebetrag (p. 96), mit Spanbruch ohne Abnahmebetrag (p. 97), mit Spanbruch mit Abnahmebetrag (p. 98). Without chip break the tool is pulled out to the clearance Q200 after every infeed (p. 96 step 5). With chip break it is pulled back only by Q256 and the control keeps feeding "bis die ANZ. SPANBRUECHE Q213 erreicht ist, oder bis die Bohrung die gewünschte TIEFE Q201 hat"; when Q213 is reached first it retracts at Q208 to Q200 (pp. 97 and 98, step 5). Q213 is "Anzahl Spanbrüche vor Rückzug" (p. 100)); HEIDENHAIN iTNC 530 Benutzer-Handbuch Zyklenprogrammierung (NC-SW 340490-07, 2011), p. 87 and 90 (cycle 203) (Verified. Step 3 of the sequence: "Falls Spanbruch eingegeben, fährt die TNC das Werkzeug um den eingegebenen Rückzugswert zurück. Wenn Sie ohne Spanbruch arbeiten, dann fährt die TNC das Werkzeug mit dem Vorschub Rückzug auf den Sicherheits-Abstand zurück." Step 6 adds that the tool dwells at the hole bottom "falls eingegeben". Q213 is the number of chip breaks before the control pulls the tool out, range 0 to 99999; Q256 is the retract at a chip break, range from 0,1); HEIDENHAIN iTNC 530 Benutzer-Handbuch Zyklenprogrammierung (NC-SW 340490-07, 2011), p. 80 (cycle 200 parameters) (Corrected. Q211 is "Verweilzeit unten", the time in seconds the tool dwells at the hole bottom, input range 0 to 3600 — so zero is no dwell. The original citation also claimed the cycle-200 sequence on p. 79 dwells at the bottom "falls eingegeben"; it does not mention a bottom dwell at all, and the "falls eingegeben" there belongs to the dwell at the clearance. The "falls eingegeben" wording for the bottom dwell is on p. 87 (cycle 203, step 6) and in the TNC 640 at p. 98 step 9); SINUMERIK 840D sl / 840D / 840Di sl Zyklen, Programmierhandbuch 01/2008, p. 51 (CYCLE83 parameter table) (Verified verbatim. "Bearbeitungsart VARI integer, Werte: 0: Spänebrechen, 1: Entspänen" — the same pair of behaviours NCX calls CHIP_BREAK and PECK); FANUC Series 30i/31i/32i-MODEL B Bedienungshandbuch Fräsen (B-64484GE-2/02), p. PDF 66 (printed 50) for G73, PDF 75 (printed 59) for G83 (Verified with one softening. G73 feeds intermittently, "ein kleinerer Wert für den Rückzug" is possible, the retract amount d is set in parameter 5114 and "Das Werkzeug wird im Eilgang zurückgezogen". For G83 the text states only that from the second peck the tool rapids to a point d before the previous end point (parameter 5115); that it first returns all the way to the R point is shown in the cycle figure rather than said in words).
Settled 2026-10-01: the maintainer let the manual-confirmed answers that agree with their recommendation be applied without reviewing each one.

### Sixth round: later

#### D168 AND and OR evaluate both operands (language 4.12)
Question: Language 4.12 gives AND and OR their precedence and says 'Comparisons yield 1 or 0'. It does not say whether the right operand is evaluated when the left one already decides the value. Expressions have no side effects, so the answer only decides which evaluation ERRORs appear. These are a division by zero, an unassigned variable or a string where a number is required (VM 5), an unknown SYS_ read (VM 2.7, 3.6), and a function without a real result. With Q2 = 0, IF={$Q2 != 0 AND $Q1 / $Q2 > 1} gives either 0 or the division-by-zero ERROR.
Recommendation: No short-circuit, as implemented in Evaluator.EvaluateBinary: both operands are evaluated left to right, and the first ERROR stops the run. Reason: every other operator works that way. The documents do not say that Fanuc (AND OR XOR, fanuc.md 7) or Siemens (siemens.md 8) skip the right operand, so NCX should not accept a guard that the target control may still alarm on. A guard is written as two blocks. Alternative: short-circuit, so that a guard fits in one IF.
Where: language 4.12 (after 'Comparisons yield 1 or 0'); src/Ncx.Core/Expressions/Evaluator.cs EvaluateBinary (TODO(question)).

ANSWER:
As recommended, confirmed from the manual library: No short-circuit: both operands are evaluated left to right, as Evaluator.EvaluateBinary does, and the first ERROR stops the run. The manuals confirm the recommendation's stated reason. On Fanuc, AND/OR/XOR are not boolean connectives at all but 32-bit bitwise operations sitting in the ordinary arithmetic precedence table (AND with multiplication/division, OR/XOR with addition/subtraction), so both operands must be computed before the operator can be applied, and a complex conditional expression is defined as an AND, OR or XOR over the results of several complete simple comparisons. Siemens defines AND/OR/NOT/XOR as operators over truth values and says nothing about skipping an operand; its only remark on order is that parentheses can fix the processing order of all operators and so depart from the normal priority rules. A guard therefore stays two blocks, and {$Q2 != 0 AND $Q1 / $Q2 > 1} with Q2 = 0 is the division-by-zero ERROR. Caveats: Heidenhain contributes nothing either way: FN 9 to FN 12 each take one comparison, and the only AND/OR in the TNC 640 Klartext manual is in the WHERE clause of an SQL statement (p. 310), not in a jump condition. No manual in the library uses the words short-circuit, and a whole-cache search for a statement that an operand may go unevaluated found only electrical short circuits. The Fanuc case is decisive only by inference: a bitwise operator cannot skip an operand.
Evidence: FANUC Series 30i/31i/32i-MODEL B, Betriebshandbuch Drehen/Fräsen, B-64484GE/02, p. 489 (PDF page; printed 455; ch. 16 Kundenmakro, Tabelle 16.4 (a)) (The table of arithmetic and logical operations lists #i=#j OR #k and #i=#j XOR #k under addition/subtraction and #i=#j AND #k under multiplication/division, each described as a 32-bit bitwise operation.); FANUC Series 30i/31i/32i-MODEL B, Betriebshandbuch Drehen/Fräsen, B-64484GE/02, p. 493 (PDF page; printed 459) (The operator priority list has three levels: functions, then multiplication and division together with AND, then addition and subtraction together with OR and XOR - the logical operators rank as arithmetic ones.); FANUC Series 30i/31i/32i-MODEL B, Betriebshandbuch Drehen/Fräsen, B-64484GE/02, p. 501 (PDF page; printed 467; 16.8.3 Bedingte Verzweigung) (A complex conditional expression performs an AND, OR or XOR operation on the results (true or false) of several simple conditional expressions, i.e. the parts are evaluated first and then combined.); SINUMERIK 840D sl/828D Programmierhandbuch Arbeitsvorbereitung (03/2013), p. 71-72 (section 1.4) (AND, OR, NOT, XOR are listed as logical operators over BOOL values (0 is FALSE, non-zero TRUE for CHAR/INT/REAL), with B_AND/B_OR/B_XOR as a separate bitwise set; the only note on order says parentheses can set the processing order of all operators and so depart from the normal priority rules.); TNC 640 Benutzerhandbuch Klartextprogrammierung, 892903-18 (NC-SW 34059x-10, 10/2019), p. 310 (section 9.7, SQL-Anweisungen) (The only place the manual gives a logical AND and OR is the table of WHERE conditions of an SQL statement, for linking several conditions - the jump functions FN 9 to FN 12 on p. 279 take one comparison each.).
Settled 2026-10-01: the maintainer let the manual-confirmed answers that agree with their recommendation be applied without reviewing each one.

#### D171 Where syncPartner and syncPhase stand
Question: VM 2.4 gives every spindle the fields syncPartner and syncPhase (set by SPINDLE_SYNC and PHASE) but does not say whether both coupled spindles carry them or only one. Language 4.5 says "the second follows the first", and VM 3.8 rule 5 warns on "RPM:b and SPINDLE:b while synchronized", so rule 5 must know which spindle is b. Case: after SPINDLE_SYNC=MAIN,SUB PHASE=90, do ncx trace, the Before/After snapshots (SpindleSnapshot) and @SAVE show the partner on SUB only, or on both spindles?
Recommendation: Keep what the code does (SpindleHandlers.ApplySpindleSync). The fields stand on the following spindle only: it names the leading spindle and carries the phase, and the leader keeps none. Reason: with the two documented fields, this is the only form that tells rule 5 which spindle is b. Alternative: both spindles carry each other as partner, and VM 2.4 gains a third field (leading or following), so that a listener also sees the coupling from the leader.
Where: VM 2.4 (spindle table row); architecture 5 SpindleState (one sentence); src/Ncx.Core/VirtualMachine/Handlers/SpindleHandlers.cs ApplySpindleSync TODO.

ANSWER:
As recommended, confirmed from the manual library: Keep what SpindleHandlers.ApplySpindleSync does: syncPartner and syncPhase stand on the following spindle only, naming the leading spindle and carrying the phase, and the leader keeps none. Siemens names the pair leading spindle (LS) and following spindle (FS), writes the coupling as COUPON(<FS>,<LS>,<POSFS>) with the FS mandatory and the LS an optional parameter that may be omitted, and reads the state and the angular offset per follower ($AA_COUP_ACT[<FS>], $AA_COUP_OFFS[<FS>] = current angular offset of the following to the leading spindle). Nakamura commands the sync from the second spindle's side as well: on a two-spindle machine M96/M97 switch speed synchronization on and off at the right unit and M92 switches phase synchronization on at the right unit, while the leading (left) spindle keeps its own M3/M4 and S. Caveats: Bearing on VM 3.8 rule 5 rather than on D171 itself: Nakamura's alarm list makes 'both units given a rotation direction' a machine alarm (A11.0), which is stricter than NCX's WARNING, while Siemens' COUPONC deliberately takes over a previously programmed M3/M4 S of the follower and adopts a differential speed at once — so a WARNING, not an ERROR, is the right compromise. Also note that Siemens writes the pair follower-first, the reverse of the NCX order SPINDLE_SYNC=MAIN,SUB. On Nakamura, M92's primary meaning is tailstock quill pressure; the phase-synchronization meaning applies only on a double-spindle or MATA-BEI machine, and M93 then sets the synchronization position.
Evidence: SINUMERIK 840D sl Programmierhandbuch Arbeitsvorbereitung, BS.000504 (08/2018), p. 594 (section 13.5 Synchronspindel) (In synchronous mode there is one leading spindle (LS) and one following spindle (FS); the following spindle follows the movements of the leading spindle while the coupling is active.); SINUMERIK 840D sl Programmierhandbuch Arbeitsvorbereitung, BS.000504 (08/2018), p. 595-597 (section 13.5.1) (The syntax is COUPON(<FS>,<LS>,<POSFS>), COUPOF(<FS>,<LS>,...) and so on; <FS> is the following spindle while <LS>, the leading spindle, is listed under 'Optionale Parameter' and may be omitted. POSFS is the angular offset between leading and following spindle (in COUPOF/COUPOFS the switch-off position of the follower). COUPONC takes over a preceding M3 S.../M4 S... of the follower and adopts a differential speed immediately.); SINUMERIK 840D sl Programmierhandbuch Arbeitsvorbereitung, BS.000504 (08/2018), p. 603-604 (section 13.5) (The coupling state is read bit-coded as $AA_COUP_ACT[<FS>] for a following spindle, and the current angular offset of the following spindle to the leading spindle as $AA_COUP_OFFS[<FS>] ($VA_COUP_OFFS for the actual value); the control keeps both on the follower.); Nakamura-Tome Programmierhandbuch Band 1 (Fanuc), 4810004ECL-1, p. 123-124 (ch. 7 Zusatzfunktion, items 77, 78, 81, 82) (On a double-spindle or MATA-BEI machine M92 switches spindle phase synchronization on for the right unit and M93 sets the synchronization position; M96 switches spindle speed synchronization on at the right unit and M97 switches it off at the right unit.); Nakamura-Tome Liste der Warn- und Alarmmeldungen (Fanuc), 4830001EEJ, p. 78 (alarm A11.0) (Alarm A11.0 fires when both the L and the R unit were programmed with a spindle direction in a synchronization program; the remedy names M96 for the R side and M03/M04 for the L side.).
Settled 2026-10-01: the maintainer let the manual-confirmed answers that agree with their recommendation be applied without reviewing each one.

#### D173 Variable map of a Siemens machine
Question: Language 4.9 says the compiler maps variable names back through the machine configuration. Machine-config 7 shows `[variables] map` for Fanuc only (`Q = "#1"`: prefix plus number, so Q1 becomes #101, and QR1 #501). That works only if the number is padded to two digits ("#1" plus 1 gives #101), which the section does not say. P5-02 says 'R and DEF variables from [variables]' without giving a form. How do the Heidenhain names of PATTERN_LOOP (`Q1`, `Q2`) compile for siemens-840dsl-mill.toml, which has no map?
Recommendation: Write each `map` entry as a template of the variable's number, with `{index}` as `[system_variables]` already uses it. For Siemens, `map = { Q = "R{index}" }` turns Q1 into R1 (siemens.md 8). The Fanuc entries of machine-config 7 and fanuc-mill-30i.toml become `Q = "#1{index:02}"` and `QR = "#5{index:02}"`, which write Q1 -> #101 and QR1 -> #501 as machine-config 7 has them, and `QL = "#{index}"`. A name no entry covers is an ERROR at compile time that names the variable; this includes QS strings, which no R parameter holds. Names read from a Siemens source (`R5`, DEF names) are written as they are. Reason: the bare prefix works only with the unstated two-digit padding, so `Q = "R"` under the same rule writes `R01`, not the `R1` a Siemens programmer writes; a template states the width. Alternative: keep the bare prefix, state the two-digit rule and write R01 (to be confirmed on the control). Or declare unmapped names with `DEF REAL` at the program start, which needs the Sinumerik naming rules confirmed first.
Where: machine-config 7; controllers/siemens.md 8, 12; machines/siemens-840dsl-mill.toml:145; machines/fanuc-mill-30i.toml:145 (map); docs/spec/examples/machines/millturn1.toml; P5-02 (SiemensFlow).

ANSWER:
As recommended, confirmed from the manual library: Write the map as a template with {index}: for Siemens map = { Q = "R{index}" }, which gives R1. The manual settles the padding question as far as a manual can: the R parameter number is <n> of type INT with range 0 to MD28050 minus one, written R<n> or R[<expression>], and every worked assignment is R0, R[1], R3, R7, R10 — never R00 or R01. It also settles the QS case: R parameters are defined as a field of data type REAL, so no string fits one, and an unmapped QS name therefore cannot be written as an R parameter. Note for the loader that global R parameters are a different address, written only with brackets as RG[<n>], with the name settable through MD15800 and the count from MD18156, and that in synchronous actions the channel R parameters take a $ prefix ($R10).
Evidence: SINUMERIK 840D sl NC-Programmierung, Programmierhandbuch 06/2019 (CNC-SW 4.92), p. 398-399 (Channel-specific arithmetic parameters are predefined user variables named R, "definiert als Feld vom Datentyp REAL"; besides the field-index spelling R[10] the spelling without an index, R10, is allowed for historical reasons, and in synchronous actions the $ prefix is added ($R10). <n> is of type INT with range 0 to MAX_INDEX = MD28050 $MN_MM_NUM_R_PARAM minus 1, and the examples assign R0=3.5678, R[1]=-37.3, R3=-7, R7=SIN(25.3) and read R10, with no leading zeros anywhere.); SINUMERIK 840D sl NC-Programmierung, Programmierhandbuch 06/2019 (CNC-SW 4.92), p. 400-401 (Global arithmetic parameters are a separate address, written RG[<n>] or RG[<expression>] for writing and R...=RG[<n>] for reading; the default name RG is settable through MD15800 $MN_R_PARAM_NCK_NAME and their count comes from MD18156. They cannot be used in synchronous actions or technology cycles.); SINUMERIK 840D sl/840D/840Di sl Zyklen, Programmierhandbuch 01/2008, p. 18 (Cycles may be supplied from predefined variables such as R parameters, and the example writes them as N10 R1=5 R2=0.1 R3=1 R4=0 in a single block; the text warns that R parameters are predefined as type real and that type compatibility with the target parameter must be watched.).
Settled 2026-10-01: the maintainer let the manual-confirmed answers that agree with their recommendation be applied without reviewing each one.

### Sixth round: controller and machine facts to confirm

#### D174 Fanuc G-code systems B and C: cycle numbers
Question: Fanuc 3 gives the simple turning cycles as G77/G78/G79 in system B and G20/G21/G24 in system C, with G70/G71 as inch and metric in C (group 06 row). Fanuc 6 also writes "G77/G78/G79 in B" only. Controller-mapping 5 (turning cycles row) and language 4.7.1 write "G77, G78, G79 in B and C". They also give G70..G76 as the multiple repetitive cycles without naming a system, although G70/G71 are the units in C. By controllers/README.md line 14 the mapping is the specification and the controller files are background ("fix the background"). As the documents stand, system C therefore writes G77/G78/G79 and fanuc 3 is wrong. The Fanuc lathe manuals, which are not among the documents, give system C its own numbers. Machine-config 6 has no key that ties an entry to a system: cycles/fanuc.toml holds system A only, and GcodeSystem.cs documents C as "as B".
Recommendation: The maintainer confirms the system C table from the Fanuc lathe manual. Our reading of it: G20/G21/G24 for the simple cycles, G70/G71 for inch and metric, and G72..G78 for the cycles that system A numbers G70..G76. If that is confirmed, the specification is corrected despite the precedence of controllers/README.md, because the controller decides: controller-mapping 5 and language 4.7.1 read "G77/G78/G79 in B, G20/G21/G24 in C" and give the system C numbers of the multiple repetitive cycles, and controller-mapping 1 (UNITS) adds G70/G71 for system C; fanuc 3 and 6 carry the full system C table; catalog entries stay in system A numbers, and the Fanuc reader and compiler translate by gcode_system with those tables (fanuc 3: "the readers select their tables by it"). No catalog key is added, and machine-config 6 says so in one sentence. This is what cycles/fanuc.toml does now. If it is not confirmed, fanuc 3 and 6 are fixed to match the mapping. Alternative: one catalog file per system.
Where: fanuc 3 (system paragraph, group 06 row) and 6; controllers/README.md (precedence); controller-mapping 1 (UNITS row) and 5 (turning cycles row); language 4.7.1; machine-config 1 (gcode_system) and 6; cycles/fanuc.toml lines 83-91; src/Ncx.Core/Machine/GcodeSystem.cs (summary of C); P3-02 FanucModalGroups and P3-06.

ANSWER:
As recommended, confirmed from the manual library: Confirmed, exactly as the recommendation reads it. Table 2 (a) of the Fanuc lathe manual gives, per system A / B / C: the simple turning cycles G90, G92, G94 = G77, G78, G79 = G20, G21, G24; the units of group 06 G20, G21 = G20, G21 = G70, G71; and the multiple repetitive cycles G70..G76 = G70..G76 = G72..G78 (G70→G72 finish, G71→G73 rough OD, G72→G74 rough face, G73→G75 pattern repeat, G74→G76, G75→G77, G76→G78). The system is picked with bits 6 (GSB) and 7 (GSC) of parameter 3401. So fanuc 3 is right and controller-mapping 5 / language 4.7.1 ("G77, G78, G79 in B and C") is wrong and gets corrected despite the precedence of controllers/README.md. The same table also gives G50 in A as G92 in B and C, and G98/G99 (feed per minute / per revolution) in A as G94/G95 in B and C. The drilling cycles G80..G89 carry the same numbers in all three systems, so the AXIS rule of D160 is system-independent.
Evidence: Betriebshandbuch Drehen 30i/31i/32i-B (B-64484GE-1/02), p. 30 (printed 14) (The group 00 rows read G70/G70/G72, G71/G71/G73, G72/G72/G74, G73/G73/G75, G74/G74/G76, G75/G75/G77, G76/G76/G78; the group 01 rows read G90/G77/G20, G92/G78/G21, G94/G79/G24; the group 05 feed rows read G98/G94/G94 and G99/G95/G95. The drilling rows G80 to G89 carry the same number in all three columns); Betriebshandbuch Drehen 30i/31i/32i-B (B-64484GE-1/02), p. 27 and 28 (printed 11 and 12) (The group 06 units row on page 27 reads G20/G20/G70 (inch) and G21/G21/G71 (mm). The last row of page 28 reads G50/G92/G92, "Koordinatensystem-Bestimmung oder maximale Spindeldrehzahlbegrenzung"); Betriebshandbuch Drehen 30i/31i/32i-B (B-64484GE-1/02), p. 26 (printed 10) (The lathe system has three G-code systems A, B and C, selected with bit 6 (GSB) and bit 7 (GSC) of parameter 3401; B and C need the corresponding option, and the manual otherwise assumes system A); FANUC 0i-D Bedienerhandbuch Drehen (B-64304GE-1), p. 34 and 35 (The same three-column G-code list for the 0i-D: G70/G70/G72 … G76/G76/G78, G90/G77/G20, G92/G78/G21, G94/G79/G24 and G98/G94/G94, G99/G95/G95); Bedienungshandbuch Serien 16i/18i/160i/180i-TB (B-63524GE-01), p. 64 (The 16i/18i-TB G-code list carries the identical A/B/C columns, including G70/G70/G72, G76/G76/G78 and G90/G77/G20).
Settled 2026-10-01: the maintainer let the manual-confirmed answers that agree with their recommendation be applied without reviewing each one.

#### D175 Words of the Fanuc turning cycles
Question: Fanuc 6 describes only P and Q of G70..G76, and the repeat words X, Z and R of G90/G92/G94. No document gives the meaning of R on G90/G92/G94 (the taper), of F on G92 and G76 (the lead), or of the other words of G71..G76 (depth of cut, retract, allowances, thread data). Language 4.7 has PITCH only "for TAP". Its CYCLE_CALL row reads a Fanuc X/Z/R block under G90/G92/G94 as a call, although a CYCLE_CALL carries axis words only. The Fanuc lathe manuals also write G71..G76 in two blocks on 16i/18i/0i/30i. The first block carries: on G71, U (depth of cut) and R (retract); on G72, W and R; on G73, U and W (relief) and R (divisions); on G74 and G75, R (retract); on G76, P, Q and R (thread data). The second block carries P and Q with the allowances U and W and the F, or on G74..G76 the end point and the infeeds. The single params map per entry of machine-config 6 cannot express that.
Recommendation: The maintainer confirms the address tables from the Fanuc lathe manual, and fanuc 6 carries them. Then PITCH = F on G92 and G76, extending the PITCH row of language 4.7 to thread cycles. F is the lead, which equals the pitch only on a single-start thread; a multi-start thread (lead = starts x pitch, with the start shifted in Z or given by Q on newer controls) stays RAW until a decision. A catalog word TAPER takes R of G90/G92/G94, a radius value (D60). A repeat block with a new R is then a new CYCLE block, since a new CYCLE replaces all parameters (language 4.7). The CYCLE_CALL row of language 4.7 and the turning cycles row of controller-mapping 5 then say "an X/Z block" and name the R case. The other words of G71..G76 and the two-block form follow in a later catalog decision. Until then the Fanuc reader keeps any turning-cycle block with a word its entry does not map as RAW with a WARNING (D5), so nothing is lost, and cycles/fanuc.toml stays as it is. Alternative: keep all Fanuc multiple repetitive cycles RAW in 1.0 and ship only the entry names.
Where: fanuc 6; language 4.7 (PITCH and CYCLE_CALL rows) and 4.7.1; controller-mapping 5 (turning cycles row); machine-config 6 (two-block form, later); cycles/fanuc.toml lines 92, 94-117 and 119-122; P3-02 FanucCycles and P3-06.

ANSWER:
As recommended, confirmed from the manual library: Confirmed, and the address tables can go into fanuc 6 as read. R on G90/G92/G94 is the taper ("Verjüngung"), entered as a radius value, and X(U), Z(W) and R are modal data shared by all three cycles, so an omitted word repeats the previous one. F on G92 and on G76 is the thread lead ("Gewindesteigung", the L of the figure), so PITCH = F on both is right; a multi-start thread is made by shifting the thread start angle with Q (0.001 degree steps, not modal) on G32/G34/G92, and with G76 it must be written in the FS15 format — so keeping multi-start RAW for now is sound. The two-block form is real and the meaning of the letters switches with the block: G71/G72 first block U or W = depth of cut Δd and R = retract e, second block P/Q with the allowances U(Δu)/W(Δw) and F, S, T; G73 first block U(Δi)/W(Δk) relief and R(d) number of divisions; G74/G75 first block R(e) return amount, second block X(U)/Z(W), P(Δi), Q(Δk), R(Δd) and F; G76 as in D161. The manual itself warns for G71, G73, G74 and G76 that the same address means different things depending on which other words stand.
Evidence: Betriebshandbuch Drehen 30i/31i/32i-B (B-64484GE-1/02), p. 39, 40 and 48 (printed 23, 24 and 32) (G90 X(U) Z(W) R F and G94 X(U) Z(W) R F: R is the taper ("Verjüngung"), and a note says to enter a radius value for R; page 40's table 4.1.1.2 (a) shows its sign together with the end point deciding which of four tool paths is cut); Betriebshandbuch Drehen 30i/31i/32i-B (B-64484GE-1/02), p. 53 (printed 37) (Under "Modal": X(U), Z(W) and R are modal data shared by G90, G92 and G94, so if no new value is given the previous one applies; the example repeats the cycle with only the X word); Betriebshandbuch Drehen 30i/31i/32i-B (B-64484GE-1/02), p. 35 and 36 (printed 19 and 20) (Section 3.3: Q shifts the thread start angle (0.001 degree increments, 0 to 360000, not modal, taken as 0 if absent) so that multi-start threads can be cut; it is available on G32, G34, G76 and G92, and for a multi-start thread the G76 command must always be given in the FS15 format. The worked example cuts a two-start thread with F4.0 and Q0 / Q180000); Betriebshandbuch Drehen 30i/31i/32i-B (B-64484GE-1/02), p. 56 and 57 (printed 40 and 41) (G71 is written as two blocks: G71 U(Δd) R(e) with the depth of cut and the retract amount, then G71 P(ns) Q(nf) U(Δu) W(Δw) F S T with the contour block range and the finishing allowances. Note 1 says that although Δd and Δu use the same address, their meaning depends on whether P and Q are present); Betriebshandbuch Drehen 30i/31i/32i-B (B-64484GE-1/02), p. 73, 80, 81 and 82 (printed 57, 64, 65 and 66) (G73 first block W(Δk) U(Δi) R(d): the two relief distances and the number of divisions. G74 and G75 first block R(e) return amount, second block X(U) Z(W) P(Δi) Q(Δk) R(Δd) F. Note 1 on page 81 says e and Δd share an address and are told apart by whether an axis word is given); Betriebshandbuch Drehen 30i/31i/32i-B (B-64484GE-1/02), p. 84 and 86 (printed 68 and 70) (G76 second block X(U) Z(W) R(i) taper, P(k) thread height, Q(Δd) first cut, F(L) thread lead; note 1 on page 86 says the meaning of the data at P, Q and R is decided by the presence of X(U) and Z(W), and note 3 that the values at P, Q and R are modal).
Settled 2026-10-01: the maintainer let the manual-confirmed answers that agree with their recommendation be applied without reviewing each one.

#### D176 Fanuc G74..G76 take no contour range
Question: Several documents say P and Q of every cycle G70..G76 name the contour block range: fanuc 6, controller-mapping 5 (turning cycles row), language 4.7.1 (with the CONTOUR row of 4.7), the D65 row, and the D65 line of architecture 13. cycles/fanuc.toml on main follows them for G75 (GROOVE) and G76 (COMPOUND_THREAD). The Fanuc lathe manuals, which are not among the documents, give that meaning only to G70..G73. They use P and Q of G74 and G75 for the infeed steps, and of G76 for the thread data. A phase 3 reader would therefore turn a groove's infeed into a contour SUB section. G73 (pattern repeat, a contour cycle) and G74 have no NCX name, and on a mill their numbers are CHIP_BREAK and left-hand tapping.
Recommendation: If the manual confirms: the documents read "G70..G73 name the contour with P and Q; G74 (face grooving, peck drilling), G75 (OD grooving) and G76 (compound thread) take P and Q as infeed and thread data"; D65 gets a Clarified line that its range is the contour cycles G70..G73, and the representation (a SUB section named by CONTOUR=name) stays; `contour` is removed from the G75 and G76 entries; G73 gets a catalog entry with contour (PATTERN_REPEAT, fanuc 6's wording) and G74 one without (FACE_GROOVE). Both go into the lathe catalog of D160, which removes the clash with the mill numbers. Their other words follow D175. Alternative: the documents stand, and contour stays on G75/G76 as on main.
Where: fanuc 6; controller-mapping 5 (turning cycles row); language 4.7 (CONTOUR row) and 4.7.1; decisions.md D65 row and rationale.md D65 (Clarified line); architecture 13 (the D65 line); 12-phase-2-configuration.md P2-03 ("G70..G76 with Contour"); cycles/fanuc.toml lines 119-124 and 144-158; tests/Ncx.Config.Tests/Cycles/ShippedCatalogsTests.cs (GROOVE, COMPOUND_THREAD rows); the P2-03 task log.

ANSWER:
As recommended, confirmed from the manual library: Confirmed, and the documents are wrong as they stand. Only G70, G71, G72 and G73 use P and Q as the block-number range ns..nf of the finishing contour. On G74 and G75 the second block's P is Δi and Q is Δk, the step in the second and the first plane axis; on G76 the first block's P packs m (finishing repeats), r (chamfer) and a (tool angle) and Q is Δdmin, while the second block's P is the thread height k and Q the first cut Δd. So `contour` comes off the G75 and G76 entries, D65 gets its Clarified line limiting the contour range to G70..G73, and G73 gets a catalog entry with a contour while G74 gets one without.
Evidence: Betriebshandbuch Drehen 30i/31i/32i-B (B-64484GE-1/02), p. 56, 73 and 76 (printed 40, 57 and 60) (For G71, G73 and G70 the manual defines ns as the block number of the first block and nf as the block number of the last block of the finishing-contour program, given at P and Q); Betriebshandbuch Drehen 30i/31i/32i-B (B-64484GE-1/02), p. 80 (printed 64) (G74 format: G74 R(e); G74 X(U) Z(W) P(Δi) Q(Δk) R(Δd) F(f). Δi is the travel in the second plane axis, Δk the depth of cut in the first plane axis, Δd the tool relief at the cut bottom. No block numbers appear anywhere in the cycle); Betriebshandbuch Drehen 30i/31i/32i-B (B-64484GE-1/02), p. 82 (printed 66) (G75 is G74 with the two plane axes exchanged: P(Δi) is the depth of cut in the second plane axis and Q(Δk) the travel in the first, and the cycle serves grooving during OD machining and parting off when Z(W) and Q are omitted); Betriebshandbuch Drehen 30i/31i/32i-B (B-64484GE-1/02), p. 84 and 86 (printed 68 and 70) (G76 P(m)(r)(a) Q(Δdmin) R(d); G76 X(U) Z(W) R(i) P(k) Q(Δd) F(L): P in the first block is the three-part number m, r, a, in the second block the thread height; Q is the minimum cut and then the first cut. Note 1 adds that what P, Q and R mean is decided by whether X(U) and Z(W) are present).
Settled 2026-10-01: the maintainer let the manual-confirmed answers that agree with their recommendation be applied without reviewing each one.

#### D178 Q parameter lists of the Heidenhain catalog cycles
Question: heidenhain.md 5 gives the meanings of Q200 to Q204, Q206 to Q208, Q210, Q211, Q239, Q256 and Q257 (not Q205 or Q209). BOHREN.h gives the orders of cycles 200, 201, 203 and 207. No document gives the parameters and orders of 202, 204 to 206, 208, 209, 240, 241 and 251 to 257. Yet P3-05 reads 200 to 209, 240 and 241, and P3-04 writes CYCL DEF 'with the Q parameters in the control's order' (heidenhain 8 rule 7). Two statements look wrong. heidenhain 5 calls Q207 'tapping feed' without naming a cycle, and it gives Q239 as the pitch of 207 only. So the feed of 206 and the pitch of 209 are unmapped.
Recommendation: Copy the lists from the iTNC 530 cycle programming manual (controller-mapping 10) into heidenhain.md 5, one line per cycle, and into the catalog signatures. While doing it, check this reading of the Heidenhain manuals, which is not in the documents: Q207 is the milling feed of 251 to 257; 206 takes its feed from Q206; 209 takes its pitch from Q239, as 207 does. heidenhain 5 would then read 'Q207 milling feed (251 to 257)' and 'Q239 pitch (207, 209)'. Until the lists are in, compiling a Heidenhain entry without a signature is a CMP ERROR, and the reader reads its cycle natively as CYCLE:HEIDENHAIN=n (D94).

As recommended, confirmed from the manual library: Copy the orders from the iTNC 530 cycle manual; the NC-example block of each cycle gives the order the control writes. Verified block for block against the manual: 200 = Q200 Q201 Q206 Q202 Q210 Q203 Q204 Q211; 201 = Q200 Q201 Q206 Q211 Q208 Q203 Q204; 202 = Q200 Q201 Q206 Q211 Q208 Q203 Q204 Q214 Q336; 203 = Q200 Q201 Q206 Q202 Q210 Q203 Q204 Q212 Q213 Q205 Q211 Q208 Q256; 204 = Q200 Q249 Q250 Q251 Q252 Q253 Q254 Q255 Q203 Q204 Q214 Q336; 205 = Q200 Q201 Q206 Q202 Q203 Q204 Q212 Q205 Q258 Q259 Q257 Q256 Q211 Q379 Q253; 206 = Q200 Q201 Q206 Q211 Q203 Q204; 207 = Q200 Q201 Q239 Q203 Q204; 208 = Q200 Q201 Q206 Q334 Q203 Q204 Q335 Q342 Q351; 209 = Q200 Q201 Q239 Q203 Q204 Q257 Q256 Q336 Q403; 240 = Q200 Q343 Q201 Q344 Q206 Q211 Q203 Q204; 241 = Q200 Q201 Q206 Q211 Q203 Q204 Q379 Q253 Q208 Q426 Q427 Q428 Q429 Q430 Q435; 251 = Q215 Q218 Q219 Q220 Q368 Q224 Q367 Q207 Q351 Q201 Q202 Q369 Q206 Q338 Q200 Q203 Q204 Q370 Q366 Q385; 252 = Q215 Q223 Q368 Q207 Q351 Q201 Q202 Q369 Q206 Q338 Q200 Q203 Q204 Q370 Q366 Q385; 253 = Q215 Q218 Q219 Q368 Q374 Q367 Q207 Q351 Q201 Q202 Q369 Q206 Q338 Q200 Q203 Q204 Q366 Q385; 254 = Q215 Q219 Q368 Q375 Q367 Q216 Q217 Q376 Q248 Q378 Q377 Q207 Q351 Q201 Q202 Q369 Q206 Q338 Q200 Q203 Q204 Q366 Q385; 256 = Q218 Q424 Q219 Q425 Q220 Q368 Q224 Q367 Q207 Q351 Q201 Q202 Q206 Q200 Q203 Q204 Q370; 257 = Q223 Q222 Q368 Q207 Q351 Q201 Q202 Q206 Q200 Q203 Q204 Q370. The draft's reading is right and heidenhain.md 5 is wrong: Q207 is the milling feed ("VORSCHUB FRAESEN") on every cycle that carries it, never a tapping feed; 206 takes its plunge feed from Q206 and 209 its pitch from Q239, as 207 does. The correction should be wider than the draft proposes: Q207 also carries the milling feed of 213, 225, 230, 231, 232, 262 to 265, 267 and 275, and Q239 is also the pitch of the thread-milling cycles 262 to 265 and 267, so heidenhain 5 should read "Q207 milling feed (the milling cycles, 251 to 257 among them)" and "Q239 pitch (207, 209 and the thread-milling cycles)".

None of the three carries a Q207); HEIDENHAIN iTNC 530, Benutzer-Handbuch Zyklenprogrammierung (670 388-12, NC-SW 340490-07), p. 149, 153, 158, 163, 167, 171 (The pocket, slot and stud cycles 251, 252, 253, 254, 256 and 257 each carry Q207 with the parameter text "Vorschub Fräsen" and the comment "VORSCHUB FRAESEN", the travel speed of the tool while milling; the plunge feed beside it is Q206, "Vorschub Tiefenzustellung"); HEIDENHAIN iTNC 530, Benutzer-Handbuch Zyklenprogrammierung (670 388-12, NC-SW 340490-07), p. 123, 214, 264, 268, 273, 318, 456 (The same "Vorschub Fräsen Q207" stands in the thread-milling cycle 262 (beside "Gewindesteigung Q239"), in 275, 230, 231, 232 and in 225 GRAVIEREN (Q207=750 ;VORSCHUB FRAESEN), which the draft's list leaves out. Cycle 213 ZAPFEN SCHLICHTEN carries Q207 too, but only in the programming example on page 456; this manual has no cycle-213 section); HEIDENHAIN iTNC 530, Benutzer-Handbuch Zyklenprogrammierung (670 388-12, NC-SW 340490-07), p. 82 (The parameter list of cycle 201 explains Q208 "Vorschub Rückzug" as the speed at which the tool leaves the hole, and says the reaming feed applies when Q208 is entered as 0).

#### D180 TOOL CALL S without a tool number on the iTNC 530
Question: heidenhain.md 4 says that `TOOL CALL S2000` without a tool number changes only the speed "on newer controls". Controller-mapping 3 says it is "allowed on newer TNCs". Neither says whether the iTNC 530 is one of those controls, although it is the control of the example machine and of the three .h samples. heidenhain.md 8 has no rule for an RPM without a TOOL. Rule 3 folds only the RPM of the TOOL block or the block after it into the TOOL CALL. Every other RPM is therefore written with the [spindle.TOOL] RPM template of heidenhain-itnc530.toml. Does the iTNC 530 accept `TOOL CALL S2000`, only `TOOL CALL Z S2000`, or does a speed change have to repeat the tool number?
Recommendation: If the maintainer's iTNC 530 or its manual accepts the bare form, keep `RPM = "TOOL CALL S{rpm}"`, as the file has. Then replace "on newer controls" in heidenhain.md 4 and controller-mapping 3 with the names of the controls that accept it. If only the form with the axis works, the template becomes `TOOL CALL {axis} S{rpm}`. If a speed change needs the tool number, the template becomes `TOOL CALL {tool} {axis} S{rpm}`. Both placeholders already have values in every template (machine-config introduction). But that form calls the active tool again: it may run the builder's tool-change macro, and it resets the DL/DR deltas of the original call. heidenhain.md 8 then needs a sentence about it after rule 3.
Where: machines/heidenhain-itnc530.toml [spindle.TOOL] RPM (TODO at line 112); heidenhain.md 4 and 8; controller-mapping 3 (reader-rules paragraph); P3-04 HeidenhainToolCall. The reader (P3-05) reads `TOOL CALL S` alone whatever the answer (controller-mapping 3). No example program changes RPM without a TOOL, so the P3-04 acceptance does not depend on the answer.

ANSWER:
As recommended, confirmed from the manual library: The iTNC 530 accepts the bare form, so `RPM = "TOOL CALL S{rpm}"` in heidenhain-itnc530.toml stays as it is: the manual's keying procedure for a programmed speed change skips both the tool-number prompt and the spindle-axis prompt with NO ENT and enters only S. "On newer controls" in heidenhain.md 4 and "allowed on newer TNCs" in controller-mapping 3 become "on the iTNC 530 and the TNC 640". Add to heidenhain.md 8 after rule 3: the compiler never repeats the tool number for a speed change, because a TOOL CALL that carries a tool number (or a changed tool-axis direction) runs the machine's tool-change macro and may swap in a sister tool, while a TOOL CALL with neither a tool name nor a tool number, and either no tool axis or the same tool axis as the previous TOOL CALL, changes only the speed — a case list the library prints for the TNC 640 only.
Evidence: HEIDENHAIN iTNC 530, Benutzer-Handbuch Klartext-Programmierung (NC-SW 340490-04), p. 197 (Section 5.1, "Spindeldrehzahl S / Programmierte Änderung": the speed can be changed with a TOOL CALL block in which exclusively the new speed is entered. The keying sequence skips the tool-number prompt and the spindle-axis prompt with NO ENT and enters only S, which is exactly the block `TOOL CALL S<rpm>`); HEIDENHAIN TNC 640, Benutzerhandbuch Klartextprogrammierung (892903-18, NC-SW 34059x-10), p. 123 (Same procedure, and then an explicit list: the control changes only the speed for a TOOL CALL block without tool name, tool number and tool axis, and for one without tool name and number but with the same tool axis as the previous TOOL CALL. It runs the tool-change macro, possibly swapping in a sister tool, for a TOOL CALL with a tool number, with a tool name, or without either but with a changed tool-axis direction).
Settled 2026-10-01: the maintainer let the manual-confirmed answers that agree with their recommendation be applied without reviewing each one.

#### D182 FN 18 ids of the iTNC 530 for SYS_ names
Question: Machine-config 7 maps SYS_ names to 'FN 18 ids' on Heidenhain. heidenhain.md 6 names `FN 18: SYSREAD` (positions, tool data) but gives no ids, so heidenhain-itnc530.toml has no `[system_variables]`. Which SYSREAD ID, NR and IDX return the workpiece position and the machine position of each axis, and a wear register, on the iTNC 530? heidenhain.md 6 lists FN 18 among the FN statements (like `FN 0: Q5 = +10`), not among the functions a formula may use (`SIN COS ... EXP`). Is a read therefore written as its own FN 18 block, into a spare Q parameter, before the block that uses it?
Recommendation: Leave the table out until the ids are taken from the iTNC 530 manual (the FN 18 chapter). Until then a `$SYS_` read compiled for Heidenhain is unmapped (VM 3.6) and cannot be written. Once the ids are known, each entry holds the SYSREAD arguments (`SYS_POS_X = "ID.. NR.. IDX.."`), and the compiler writes `FN 18: SYSREAD Qn = ...` in a block before the use. No example or source reads a system variable, so nothing is waiting on this.
Where: machine-config 7; controllers/heidenhain.md 6; machines/heidenhain-itnc530.toml:139; P3-04 (HeidenhainFlow).

ANSWER:
As recommended, confirmed from the manual library: Fill `[system_variables]` from the FN 18 table of the iTNC 530 manual. The position in the active coordinate system is `ID270 NR1 IDX<axis>`, the nominal position in the REF system is `ID240 NR1 IDX<axis>`, with the axis index 1=X, 2=Y, 3=Z, 4=A, 5=B, 6=C, 7=U, 8=V, 9=W — so `SYS_POS_X = "ID270 NR1 IDX1"` and `SYS_MPOS_X = "ID240 NR1 IDX1"`. The wear registers are the delta columns of the tool table: `ID50 NR4 IDX<tool>` is the length oversize DL and `ID50 NR5 IDX<tool>` the radius oversize DR, and without an index they return the data of the active tool; `ID200 NR1`/`NR2` give the active tool radius and length including the delta values. A read is its own block, `FN 18: SYSREAD Qn = ID.. NR.. IDX..`, written before the block that uses Qn, exactly as the recommendation supposes.
Evidence: HEIDENHAIN iTNC 530, Benutzer-Handbuch Klartext-Programmierung (NC-SW 340490-04), p. 623 (Section 11.8 opens FN 18: system data are read and stored in Q parameters, and the datum is selected by a group number (ID), a number and, where needed, an index); HEIDENHAIN iTNC 530, Benutzer-Handbuch Klartext-Programmierung (NC-SW 340490-04), p. 627, 628 (The table rows "Soll-Position im REF-System, 240" and "Aktuelle Position im aktiven Koordinatensystem, 270" both use number 1 and an index that runs X, Y, Z, A, B, C, U, V, W; group 270's ninth index, W, continues on page 628); HEIDENHAIN iTNC 530, Benutzer-Handbuch Klartext-Programmierung (NC-SW 340490-04), p. 624, 625 (Group 50 reads the tool table with the tool number as the index: numbers 1, 2 and 3 are length, radius and R2, and 4, 5 and 6 the oversizes DL, DR and DR2. The line closing the group says "Ohne Index: Daten des aktiven Werkzeugs"); HEIDENHAIN iTNC 530, Benutzer-Handbuch Klartext-Programmierung (NC-SW 340490-04), p. 626, 629 (Group 200 "Aktive Werkzeug-Korrektur" returns the tool radius and the tool length, each "incl. Delta-Werte". The worked example on page 629 is a single NC block, `55 FN 18: SYSREAD Q25 = ID210 NR4 IDX3`, which shows that the read stands in a block of its own and assigns into a Q parameter).
Settled 2026-10-01: the maintainer let the manual-confirmed answers that agree with their recommendation be applied without reviewing each one.

### Seventh round: needed now

#### D184 ARC without feed
Question: VM 3.1 ('LINE with feed.value none: ERROR') and the VM 5 ERROR list ('LINE without feed') name only LINE. VM 3.9 and VM 5 suppress that rule in a subprogram nothing calls (D99). Language 4.3 writes 'at the active feed' only in the LINE row, and its ARC row says only 'Circular interpolation'. But ARC is G2/G3 (the direction paragraph of 4.3), which the control runs at the programmed feed just as it runs G1. VM 8 also times every motion except RAPID and HOME at the commanded feed. Case: a program whose first feed motion, from X=0 Y=0, is ARC=CW X=20 Y=0 CENTER:X=10 CENTER:Y=0 with no F set. On main only LINE is checked (MotionRules.MoveStraight, VM201), so this ARC gets no diagnostic, and VM 8 has no feed to time it with.
Recommendation: Make ARC without feed the ERROR VM201, the same as LINE, with the same D99 suppression. An arc is interpolated at F exactly as a line is, and neither the control nor VM 8 can run it without one. CYCLE_CALL stays outside the rule, because its feed is CYCLE_F and never F (D29). Code: move the feed test of MoveStraight into a helper that ArcRules.Execute also calls, and change the VM201 text to 'LINE or ARC without feed'. VM 3.1 (or 3.2), the VM 5 ERROR list and the suppression lists of VM 3.9 and VM 5 then name ARC. None of the five examples changes: every ARC in 2.5D_FRAESEN and POLAR_FACE follows an F. Alternative: LINE only, as coded.
Where: VM 3.1 (the feed sentence) or 3.2; VM 3.9 and VM 5 (ERROR list, suppression list); implementation 11 P1-03; src/Ncx.Core/VirtualMachine/MotionRules.cs MoveStraight (TODO(question) at line 80) and ArcRules.Execute; docs/spec/generated/diagnostics.md (VM201 row).

ANSWER:
As recommended, confirmed from the manual library: Make ARC without feed the ERROR VM201 exactly as LINE, with the same D99 suppression, and reword VM201 to 'LINE or ARC without feed'. Fanuc treats G01, G02 and G03 alike: a cutting-feed block whose F value is 0 — which is what a program that has set no F yet has — triggers alarm PS0011 'VORSCHUB NULL (SOLLWERT)', and the parameter that can suppress it names 'ein Satz (G01, G02, G03, etc.)' in one breath; the manual also states that the feedrate of circular interpolation is the F code, controlled as the tangential speed along the arc. Siemens is not silent either: alarm 10860 'Kein Vorschub programmiert' fires for a traverse block with no programmed traverse speed, with no restriction to straight lines, and the remedy is to program a feed value matching the interpolation type. Mazak, in inverse-time mode where F is not modal, gives the G01 and the G02/G03 programming format side by side, each with F, and alarms 816 VORSCHUB NULL if the F is omitted. CYCLE_CALL stays outside the rule (its feed is CYCLE_F, D29). Caveats: The Fanuc and Mazak evidence is about a commanded F of zero or a missing F, which is the state of the F register before any F has been programmed — that step is my inference, not a sentence in either manual. Siemens' 10860 covers a traverse block generally but its listed causes are all feed-type changes (G94 to G95 and so on), not a program that never set F. Heidenhain gives no comparable alarm text in the pages I read; it only makes F modal over all path functions and offers F in the arc block's dialogue just as in the straight-line block.
Evidence: FANUC Series 30i/31i/32i-MODEL B, Betriebshandbuch Drehen/Fräsen, B-64484GE/02, p. 2021 (PDF page; printed 1987; parameter no. 1404 bit 7, FC0) (If a block (G01, G02, G03, etc.) occurs in automatic mode whose feedrate command F is 0, setting 0 raises alarm PS0011 'VORS. NULL (SOLLW.)'; setting 1 suppresses the alarm and runs the block.); FANUC Series 30i/31i/32i-MODEL B, Betriebshandbuch Drehen/Fräsen, B-64484GE/02, p. 85 (PDF page; printed 51; section 4.4 Kreisinterpolation) (The feedrate of circular interpolation equals the speed given by the F code, and the tangential feedrate along the arc is controlled to match it - an arc is interpolated at F exactly as a line is.); SINUMERIK 840D sl Diagnosehandbuch / Parameter, Alarme, BS.000503 (08/2018), p. 152 (alarm 10860) (Alarm 10860 'Kein Vorschub programmiert': no traverse speed is programmed for the displayed traverse block; the remedy is to program a feed value according to the interpolation type (G93, G94/G97, G95, G96). The alarm text names no particular path function.); FANUC Series 0i-D Bedienerhandbuch Drehen/Fräsen, B-64304GE/01, p. 1424 (PDF page; alarm list) (Alarm 0011 'VORSCHUB NULL (SOLLW)': the cutting feedrate programmed with the F code is 0.); Nakamura-Tome Liste der Warn- und Alarmmeldungen (Fanuc), 4830001EEJ, p. 282 (ch. 20, alarm 0011) (The shop's own machine carries the same alarm: 0011 FEED ZERO (COMMAND) - the feed programmed by F code was set to 0.); Mazatrol Matrix 2 Programmieranleitung EIA/ISO, H740PB6043G, p. 125 (section 7-13, Umkehrzeit-Vorschub G93) (The programming format is given twice, 'Geradeninterpolation: G93 G01 Xx1 Yy1 Ff1' and 'Kreisinterpolation: G93 G02 Xx1 Yy1 Rr1 Ff1'; since F is not modal in G93 it must be set in every block, and omitting an F code raises alarm 816 VORSCHUB NULL.); TNC 640 Benutzerhandbuch Klartextprogrammierung, 892903-18 (NC-SW 34059x-10, 10/2019), p. 159-160 (Kreisbahn C, Kreisbahn CR) (The dialogue of a circular block asks for direction of rotation DR, feed F and miscellaneous function M, the same feed entry as a straight-line block - the arc is an ordinary feed move.).
Settled 2026-10-01: the maintainer let the manual-confirmed answers that agree with their recommendation be applied without reviewing each one.

#### D187 Position after the call of a catalog cycle
Question: VM 3.3 gives the full sequence only for the built-in drilling family. For a `CYCLE:<controller>=n` cycle it gives only the position: the call moves the plane axes to its axis words, the drilling axis is unknown afterwards, and ExpandCycles raises no MOTION events (D94). No sentence covers a catalog name outside the family, such as CYCLE=RECT_POCKET (language 4.7.1) or the TURN_OD and ROUGH_TURN blocks the Fanuc reader writes. Main calls them like the native form (CycleRules.Call, PositionTheHoleOnly). That fits a pocket called at its centre, but not the Fanuc turning cycles. After CYCLE_CALL X=50 Z=-70 of TURN_OD (G90 X50. Z-70.), main holds X50 Z-70. The control, however, brings the tool back to its start point after G90, G92, G94 and G70 to G76 (Fanuc lathe manual, not in the documents). So a later IX counts from a point the tool never stands at. The Fanuc reader's source-side position does the same (FanucCycles.Call through FanucMotion.Move): a repeat block U-10. is counted from the previous end point, where the control counts it from the start point. Main also makes the drilling axis unknown after every such call. For a turning cycle under WORKPLANE=ZX that axis is Y, which nakamura-ntjx, doosan-puma-2600sy and mori-ntx1000-mapps all have, so a later IY is VM202.
Recommendation: Extend the D94 sentence of VM 3.3 to every cycle outside the built-in family, as main does, with one exception. After a call of a Fanuc turning cycle, no axis moves and none becomes unknown, because the tool returns to its start point and a turning cycle has no drilling axis. This covers TURN_OD, FACE and the thread pass of G92 (names per D161), and the one-shot cycles of G70 to G76. Two rules follow for the modal ones. First, an axis a CYCLE_CALL leaves out reads as the current position (language 4.7). That is now the start point, while the control keeps the previous end point. So the Fanuc reader writes both end-point words, X and Z, on every CYCLE_CALL of a simple turning cycle, with U and W counted from the start point, and the Fanuc compiler may drop a word that equals the previous call's. Second, the reader's source-side position follows the same rule (FanucCycles.Call). Siemens and Heidenhain turning cycles keep the D94 rule until their end positions are confirmed. Reason: the VM knows no sequence outside the family (D94). For a positioned cycle the call point is where it ends, but the words of a turning cycle are the end point of one pass. Alternative: every axis the call names becomes unknown after any cycle outside the family. That is always safe, but an IX after a Heidenhain pocket then becomes VM202.
Where: VM 3.3 (the D94 sentence); language 4.7 (CYCLE_CALL row) and 4.7.1; controller-mapping 5 (turning cycles row); src/Ncx.Core/VirtualMachine/CycleRules.cs Call (TODO(question) at lines 52-55) and PositionTheHoleOnly; src/Ncx.Readers/Fanuc/FanucCycles.cs Call and ReadTurning (FanucMotion.Move for a turning cycle); related: D161, D175.

ANSWER:
As recommended, confirmed from the manual library: Confirmed for the cycles the exception has to cover, and main is wrong. The manual states the return to the start point outright for exactly the cycles at issue: operation 4 of G90, G92 and G94 is a move back to the start point A; note 3 of G73 says the tool returns to point A after the cycle; G70 returns in rapid to the cycle start point, with a paragraph of its own; and the G76 tool-path table runs four legs 1(R), 2(F), 3(R), 4(R) around a closed path back to A. So after the call of a Fanuc simple turning cycle no axis has moved and none becomes unknown — the D94 sentence gets exactly the exception the recommendation proposes for TURN_OD, THREAD_PASS and FACE, and for G70, G73 and G76. The manual's own repeat example makes the consequence explicit: N030 G90 U-8.0 W-66.0 F0.4 followed by U-16.0, U-24.0, U-32.0 cuts four progressively deeper passes, which only works because every incremental U is counted from the same start point A, not from the previous end point. X(U), Z(W) and R are modal data shared by G90/G92/G94, so an omitted word repeats the previous value — which is why the reader must write both end-point words on every CYCLE_CALL.
Evidence: Betriebshandbuch Drehen 30i/31i/32i-B (B-64484GE-1/02), p. 38, 41 and 47 (printed 22, 25 and 31) (For G90, G92 and G94 the four operations are listed and the fourth reads: move to the start coordinate of the remaining plane axis — "das Werkzeug kehrt zum Startpunkt (A) zurück" (rapid for G90 and G94, rapid for G92's legs 3 and 4)); Betriebshandbuch Drehen 30i/31i/32i-B (B-64484GE-1/02), p. 53 (printed 37) (X(U), Z(W) and R are modal data shared by G90, G92 and G94, and the example N030 G90 U-8.0 W-66.0 F0.4 / N031 U-16.0 / N032 U-24.0 / N033 U-32.0 repeats the cycle with only the X-axis travel changed); Betriebshandbuch Drehen 30i/31i/32i-B (B-64484GE-1/02), p. 74, 76 and 77 (printed 58, 60 and 61) (Note 3 of G73: after the cycle operation the tool returns to point A. For G70 the text says the tool returns in rapid to the start point after the cycle, and a separate paragraph "Rückkehr zum Zyklusstartpunkt" repeats it and warns that the return is always non-linear positioning); Betriebshandbuch Drehen 30i/31i/32i-B (B-64484GE-1/02), p. 87 (printed 71) (Table 4.2.7 (a) for G76 draws the four tool paths as legs 1(R), 2(F), 3(R), 4(R) forming a closed loop, matching figure 4.2.7 (a) on page 85 where the loop starts and ends at A); Betriebshandbuch Drehen 30i/31i/32i-B (B-64484GE-1/02), p. 61, 63 and 72 (printed 45, 47 and 56) (For G71 type II: after the last cut the tool returns to the start point given in G71, and after the roughing passes along the first plane axis it returns temporarily to the cycle start point; page 72 says the same for G72 type II. These are mid-cycle returns — no sentence was found stating where G71 type I, G72 type I, G74 or G75 leave the tool).
Settled 2026-10-01: the maintainer let the manual-confirmed answers that agree with their recommendation be applied without reviewing each one.
