#### D222 A datum inside a [workpiece] template
Question: Machine-config 5 writes [workpiece] MAIN = "G54 M428" and says 'the datum may be part of the template'. nakamura-ntjx.toml does the same, and millturn1.toml writes datums only (MAIN = "G54", SUB = "G55"). Controller-mapping 4 (WORKPIECE row) says Nakamura writes M428 'together with that spindle's datum'. The WY sample writes the two apart (N100M428, then G54G18 two blocks later) and together only once (G54G18M428, path 1 line 93). No document says how a reader matches a template split over blocks, or whether WORKPIECE also sets the datum. The reader takes the template's M code alone as WORKPIECE and reads G54 as ORIGIN where it stands (FanucBuilder.WorkpieceOf). POLAR_FACE line 7 writes G54 M428 as ORIGIN=1 WORKPIECE=MAIN. On the compile side, rendering the template writes G54 at every WORKPIECE=MAIN, whatever ORIGIN the program has. On millturn1, it writes G55 twice for MILLTURN_TRANSFER's WORKPIECE=SUB followed by ORIGIN=2.
Recommendation: A [workpiece] template holds the selection code only; the datum is ORIGIN. nakamura-ntjx.toml gets MAIN = "M428" and SUB = "M427", as the Mori Seiki, Doosan and DMG files already write theirs. millturn1.toml's control has no selection code, so the file leaves MAIN and SUB out; WORKPIECE then writes nothing there, and a reader takes it from the chuck rule that its [func_meta] already names (D40). SUB_frame stays (D104). The reader matches the whole template, in whatever block the code stands, and reads G54..G59 as ORIGIN where the source writes them (controller-mapping 1), which is what it does now. The compiler writes ORIGIN=1 WORKPIECE=MAIN of one block as G54 M428 on one line. Machine-config 5 drops 'the datum may be part of the template' and says that WORKPIECE writes nothing without a template. Reason: WORKPIECE then never changes the datum behind the VM's ORIGIN, and the reader code stays as it is. Also, on millturn1 the templates G54 and G55 are ORIGIN=1 and ORIGIN=2 as well (controller-mapping 1, Siemens column), so a reader that matches them cannot tell WORKPIECE from ORIGIN. Alternative: keep the datum in the template. The reader matches only the template's codes other than the datum (as coded), and the compiler writes the template's datum only where the block's ORIGIN is that datum.
Where: machine-config 5 ([workpiece] example and its comment); controller-mapping 4 (WORKPIECE row) and 8 ('Which spindle the slide works on' row, 'written with the datum'); docs/spec/examples/machines/nakamura-ntjx.toml:209-210, millturn1.toml:201-202 and its [func_meta] comment at line 219 ('[workpiece] has the native codes'); src/Ncx.Readers/Fanuc/FanucBuilder.cs WorkpieceOf (TODO(question) at line 199); the WORKPIECE template in P3-03, P3-06 and P5-02.

ANSWER:
As recommended, confirmed from the manual library: Take the recommendation: a [workpiece] template holds the selection code only, the datum stays ORIGIN. Nakamura documents M427/M428 as the modal "Wahl des Bearbeitungsmodus" for the R and L spindle, to be entered at the start of the program and issued implicitly by M41/M91 and M441/M491; no datum is part of it, and the Walter Meier NTJX sheet names M428 plainly as machining at the main spindle and M427 at the sub spindle while listing G54..G59 separately as coordinate systems 1 to 6. The manual's own two-turret example bears this out: the datum G59 stands once in the program header and is never rewritten when M428 and M427 switch the side. Mori Seiki's M303/M304 and Doosan's M34/M134 are the same kind of code, written in their own block. So nakamura-ntjx.toml gets MAIN = "M428" and SUB = "M427", and machine-config 5 drops "the datum may be part of the template". This contradicts the present wording of controller-mapping 4 and 8 ("written together with that spindle's datum", "G54 M428"): I found no manual page that requires the two on one line, so the pairing in the WY sample is a shop habit. Note also that the manuals settle only the machine fact (the selection code carries no datum and is modal); the rest of the recommendation — how the reader matches a template split over blocks, millturn1 leaving MAIN/SUB out, the compiler writing ORIGIN and WORKPIECE on one line — is NCX design that no manual touches.
Evidence: Nakamura-Tome Programmierhandbuch Band 1 (4810004ECL-1), p. 133 (Section (34) describes M427/M428 as the choice of machining mode for the R and L spindle, to be given at the start of the program, modal, with neither spindle selected at power-on; on the Super NTJ, NTJ-100, WT and WY series M428 is issued automatically with M41/M91 and M427 with M441/M491. No datum is mentioned.); Nakamura-Tome Programmierhandbuch Band 2 (4810004ECL-2), p. 69-70 (In the WT150 two-turret example "G59;" stands alone in the program header of both turret programs, while M428 and M427 appear later on ordinary rapid blocks ("N4 G0 Z-100. M428", "N6 G0 Z100. M427") and once on a block of their own ("M428;" after M130/M131); the datum is never repeated with them.); Liste M- und G-Codes Nakamura NTJX (Walter Meier/KOST), p. 1, 3, 5 (The head of the sheet gives the datums as a shop convention ("NULLPUNKT LINKE SPINDEL = G54", "NULLPUNKT RECHTE SPINDEL = G59"), page 3 lists "M427 = BEARBEITUNG AN DER SUBSPINDEL" and "M428 = BEARBEITUNG AN DER HAUPTSPINDEL", and page 5 lists G54..G59 plainly as coordinate systems 1 to 6.); Mori Seiki NT/NTX Programmieranleitung NTX1000SZM (PX-NT_4-K0DEEN), p. 285 (M303/M304 designate which control system performs the cutting at which spindle (they decide where the spindle feedback signal is returned) and the selection remains until the power is switched off; nothing about a datum.); Mori Seiki NT/NTX Programmieranleitung NTX1000SZM (PX-NT_4-K0DEEN), p. 145 (The G43 example writes "G54;" as its own block at the head and M303 several blocks later, directly after the G361 tool change (O0001; N1; G54; T1001; G330; G361 B0 D1.; M303;) — selection code and datum in separate blocks.); M-Funktionen Puma 2600SY, p. 2, 3 ("M34 DREHMODUS LINKS" and "M134 DREHMODUS RECHTS" are listed on their own, with no datum attached.).
Settled 2026-10-01: the maintainer let the manual-confirmed answers that agree with their recommendation be applied without reviewing each one.

#### D226 Heidenhain Q204 that does not lift above the set-up clearance
Question: Controller-mapping 5 gives the Heidenhain CYCLE_RETRACT as 'with or without Q204' and SAFE = Q203 + Q204. heidenhain.md 5 calls Q204 the retract height after the cycle, and heidenhain 8 rule 7 writes Q204 only for CYCLE_RETRACT=SAFE. Language 4.7 defines CYCLE_RETRACT as 'where the tool ends after each hole' and makes SAFE optional. None of them says how a Q204 reads when it does not put the tool above CLEARANCE: Q204 equal to Q200, Q204=0, or 0 < Q204 < Q200. None says either which Q204 the compiler writes for CYCLE_RETRACT=CLEARANCE. The concrete case is BOHREN.h. All six definitions have Q200=5 Q204=5, where BOHREN.fanuc.nc writes G99 R5. 13-phase-3 P3-05 leaves the choice to the task log with a note in controller-mapping 5, which 00-method 1.6 does not allow. Today HeidenhainCycles.AddRetract writes SAFE=Q203+Q204 CYCLE_RETRACT=SAFE whenever Q204 stands. So every BOHREN cycle is a listed difference of the P3-05 acceptance, while Expected/BOHREN.ncx keeps the Fanuc CYCLE_RETRACT=CLEARANCE. P3-04 needs the other direction: Expected/BOHREN.ncx must compile to a program equivalent to BOHREN.h, Q204=5 included.
Recommendation: The reader: a Q204 from 0 up to Q200 reads as CYCLE_RETRACT=CLEARANCE without SAFE. A Q204 above Q200 reads as SAFE=Q203+Q204 CYCLE_RETRACT=SAFE. The compiler: for CYCLE_RETRACT=CLEARANCE the Heidenhain compiler writes Q204 equal to Q200 (CLEARANCE minus SURFACE). This is one sentence in heidenhain 8 rule 7, next to 'CYCLE_RETRACT=SAFE becomes Q204'. Reasons: the words then say where the tool ends, as language 4.7 defines them, and one motion gets one text from both controllers (language 2 rules 1 and 7). The BOHREN cycles read as the Fanuc source does, so Expected/BOHREN.ncx stays as frozen and the SAFE entries leave the list of differing blocks. The rest of that list stays: CYCLE_F=565.487, CYCLE_DWELL=0, the CYCLE_F and CYCLE_DWELL of the TAP block, and D163. Expected/BOHREN.ncx compiles back to Q204=5, as BOHREN.h writes it, so P3-04 needs no exception for it. Q204=Q200 also ends at the set-up clearance, whatever the control does with a Q204 below Q200. To confirm on the iTNC 530: the tool ends at the set-up clearance when Q204 is 0 or below Q200. If it does not, only a Q204 equal to Q200 reads as CLEARANCE. Alternative: keep Q204 as SAFE always, as coded. Controller-mapping 5 then says the two readers write this motion in two forms, and the list of differing blocks keeps the entries. The Heidenhain compiler then still needs a Q204 for CYCLE_RETRACT=CLEARANCE, which heidenhain 8 rule 7 does not give.
Where: controller-mapping 5 (CYCLE_RETRACT row); heidenhain.md 7 rule 7 and 8 rule 7; 13-phase-3 P3-05 acceptance sentence (drop the deferral to the task log) and the first item of 'Risks and open ends'; src/Ncx.Readers/Heidenhain/HeidenhainCycles.cs AddRetract (TODO(question) at line 401); tests/Ncx.Acceptance/Examples/HeidenhainReaderTests.cs s_bohrenReading; P3-04 HeidenhainCycles.

ANSWER:
As recommended, confirmed from the manual library: The recommendation holds, and the manual supplies the exact threshold: Q204 takes effect only when it is programmed larger than Q200. So a Q204 from 0 up to and including Q200 reads as CYCLE_RETRACT=CLEARANCE without SAFE, and a Q204 greater than Q200 reads as SAFE=Q203+Q204 with CYCLE_RETRACT=SAFE; for CYCLE_RETRACT=CLEARANCE the Heidenhain compiler writes Q204 equal to Q200 (CLEARANCE minus SURFACE). BOHREN.h's Q200=5 Q204=5 therefore ends the tool at the set-up clearance, exactly where the Fanuc G99 R5. leaves it, so Expected/BOHREN.ncx stays as frozen and the SAFE entries leave the list of differing blocks.
Evidence: Heidenhain TNC 640 — Benutzerhandbuch Zyklenprogrammierung (892905-18, 10/2019), p. 87 (Cycle 200, last step of the cycle sequence: from the hole bottom the tool goes at FMAX to the safety clearance or to the 2nd safety clearance, and then the decisive sentence — the 2nd safety clearance Q204 "wirkt erst, wenn dieser größer programmiert ist als der Sicherheitsabstand Q200". Verified); Heidenhain TNC 640 — Benutzerhandbuch Zyklenprogrammierung (892905-18, 10/2019), p. 96 (The same sentence for cycle 203, the universal drilling cycle BOHREN.h uses. A grep over the whole book puts it on pages 87, 90, 92, 96, 97, 98, 102, 106, 114 and 125 — ten cycles, not the eight the earlier pass listed (page 106 was missing from it)); Heidenhain TNC 640 — User's Manual Cycle Programming (892905-28, 10/2019, English), p. printed 102 (and the cycle 200 / cycle 204 pages) (The English edition of the same manual says it in English: the 2nd set-up clearance Q204 "will only come into effect if its value is greater than the set-up clearance Q200". Not a translation artefact of one German sentence); Heidenhain TNC 128 — Benutzerhandbuch Klartextprogrammierung (819494-15, NC-SW 771841-07, 2018), p. 321, 323, 325, 338 (A second control family carries the identical rule for its drilling cycles, which shows it is Heidenhain's general behaviour for Q204 and not a TNC 640 peculiarity); Heidenhain iTNC 530 — Benutzer-Handbuch Zyklenprogrammierung (670 388-12, NC-SW 340490-07, 2011), p. 79 (Cycle 200 on the older control: the last step is "auf Sicherheits-Abstand oder – falls eingegeben – auf den 2. Sicherheits-Abstand". The retract goes to Q200 unless a 2nd clearance was entered; no threshold is given. Verified); Heidenhain iTNC 530 — Benutzer-Handbuch Zyklenprogrammierung (670 388-12, NC-SW 340490-07, 2011), p. 80 (Q204 is defined as the spindle-axis coordinate at which no collision between tool and workpiece or clamping device can occur, incremental, input range 0 to 99999.9999, alternatively PREDEF — a clearance height, not an obligatory motion. Verified); Heidenhain iTNC 530 — Benutzer-Handbuch Zyklenprogrammierung (670 388-12, NC-SW 340490-07, 2011), p. 59 (In the GLOBAL DEF list the 2nd set-up clearance is "Position, auf die die TNC das Werkzeug am Ende eines Bearbeitungsschrittes positioniert", at which height the next position in the plane is approached — which is what language 4.7's CYCLE_RETRACT describes. Verified).
Settled 2026-10-01: the maintainer let the manual-confirmed answers that agree with their recommendation be applied without reviewing each one.

#### D227 Where the Klartext reader writes CYCLE=OFF
Question: heidenhain.md 5, controller-mapping 5 (CYCLE=OFF row) and 13-phase-3 P3-05 have the reader emit CYCLE=OFF 'before the next non-cycle motion'. Their reason: Klartext has no cancel word, and the definition stays until the next CYCL DEF. A positioning between the definition and its first call (CYCL DEF 200, L Z+5 R0 FMAX, CYCL CALL) is such a motion. Read literally, the cycle is off at its first call. That CYCLE_CALL is then an ERROR (VM 5) unless the reader writes the definition a second time, which no document says. HeidenhainReader.Write writes CYCLE=OFF before the first non-cycle motion after a call. HeidenhainCycles.Call writes the definition again before a call made while NCX has the cycle off. A TOOL CALL while NCX has the cycle on writes no CYCLE=OFF. VM 4 ends the cycle at TOOL with a WARNING, so check raises the VM 5 WARNING 'TOOL while a cycle is active' on a source the control runs as written.
Recommendation: Keep the code's reading and close its gap at the tool change. CYCLE=OFF stands before the first motion after a call of the cycle, and before a TOOL CALL while NCX has the cycle on. A call made while NCX has the cycle off writes the definition again. heidenhain 5, the CYCLE=OFF row of controller-mapping 5 and P3-05 say so. Reasons: the definition stays next to its calls, and CYCLE=OFF stands where BOHREN.fanuc.nc writes G80 (both BOHREN readings give CYCLE_CALL X=90, CYCLE=OFF, RAPID Z=5). No definition is written twice for the common positioning before the first call. A tool change raises no WARNING the source does not deserve, whether or not the cycle was called. ReadCall already turns the NCX cycle off, so the next call writes the definition again. Code: HeidenhainToolCall.ReadCall writes CYCLE=OFF before the TOOL block while the cycle is on. Alternative: the literal reading, CYCLE=OFF before every non-cycle motion and the definition again before every call that follows one.
Where: heidenhain.md 5; controller-mapping 5 (CYCLE=OFF row); 13-phase-3 P3-05 (HeidenhainCycles item); src/Ncx.Readers/Heidenhain/HeidenhainReader.cs Write (TODO(question) at line 383); HeidenhainToolCall.cs ReadCall; HeidenhainCycles.cs Call.

ANSWER:
As recommended, confirmed from the manual library: Keep the code's reading; the literal reading is wrong on the control. A positioning block between a CYCL DEF and its first call does not end the definition — it is the shape of Heidenhain's own worked examples (CYCL DEF 200, L X+10 Y+10 R0 FMAX M3, CYCL CALL), and CYCL CALL and M99 always execute "den zuletzt definierten Bearbeitungszyklus". So CYCLE=OFF stands before the first non-cycle motion after a call of the cycle, not before every non-cycle motion, and no definition is written twice for the usual pre-positioning.
Evidence: Heidenhain TNC 640 — Benutzerhandbuch Zyklenprogrammierung (892905-18, 10/2019), p. 127 (Worked example "Beispiel: Bohrzyklen": block 5 defines cycle 200, block 6 is a plain positioning motion L X+10 Y+10 R0 FMAX M3, block 7 is the bare CYCL CALL. The non-cycle motion between definition and first call is the documented, normal form and leaves the cycle active. Verified); Heidenhain iTNC 530 — Benutzer-Handbuch Zyklenprogrammierung (670 388-12, NC-SW 340490-07, 2011), p. 80 (The cycle 200 example on the older control does the same: CYCL DEF 200 in block 11, L X+30 Y+20 FMAX M3 in block 12, CYCL CALL in block 13, L X+80 Y+50 FMAX M99 in block 14. Verified); Heidenhain iTNC 530 — Benutzer-Handbuch Zyklenprogrammierung (670 388-12, NC-SW 340490-07, 2011), p. 53 (The prerequisites before any cycle call, in order: BLK FORM, tool call, spindle direction M3/M4, cycle definition. The tool call comes before the definition, and nothing says a later tool call undoes one. The TNC 640 repeats the list on page 64. Verified); Heidenhain iTNC 530 — Benutzer-Handbuch Zyklenprogrammierung (670 388-12, NC-SW 340490-07, 2011), p. 55 (To cancel the modal M89 cycle call you program M99 in the positioning block, a CYCL CALL POS block, or a new cycle with CYCL DEF. A tool change is not one of the ways. The TNC 640 repeats the list on page 66. Verified); Heidenhain iTNC 530 — Benutzer-Handbuch Zyklenprogrammierung (670 388-12, NC-SW 340490-07, 2011), p. 278 (For the coordinate-transformation cycles the book states the modal model outright: effective from the definition, "so lange, bis sie rückgesetzt oder neu definiert wird". The machining cycles have no cancel word at all, which is why the NCX reader has to place CYCLE=OFF itself. Verified).
Settled 2026-10-01: the maintainer let the manual-confirmed answers that agree with their recommendation be applied without reviewing each one.

#### D228 The MB of a PLANE, and PLANE RESET with TURN or MOVE
Question: Language 4.2 defines MOVE=TURN as positioning the rotary axes with the 'tool retracted first'. heidenhain.md 3 has TURN position them 'with the retract from MB' (MB MAX, MB 50, MB 0). Controller-mapping 1 (TILT row) writes the Siemens _FR retract of CYCLE800 as a RETRACT block in front of the TILT. The Heidenhain move template of machine-config 5 ([transform] move, TURN = "TURN FMAX") writes no MB. So it is open whether MB is a RETRACT in front of the tilt or part of MOVE=TURN. PLANE RESET TURN or MOVE, which turns the axes back, has no NCX form: TILT=RESET only removes the entry, and MOVE needs TILT or TILT_AXIS (language 5 rule 5, VM 5). Today HeidenhainPlane.Options writes MB MAX as RETRACT and MB n as RETRACT=n in front of the tilt, and MB 0 as nothing. It keeps MB with STAY RAW, and keeps PLANE RESET with TURN, MOVE or MB RAW.
Recommendation: Keep the code's reading. The MB of a PLANE is a RETRACT in front of the tilt, as the Siemens _FR is. In the MOVE=TURN row of language 4.2, 'tool retracted first' becomes: 'a retract before the positioning is a RETRACT block in front of the tilt (Heidenhain MB, Siemens _FR)'. The Heidenhain compiler writes that RETRACT through [retract] (M140 MB) before the PLANE. PLANE RESET with TURN or MOVE stays RAW in 1.0, named in heidenhain 7 rule 6. Reasons: the move template already writes TURN without MB, one retract word then serves both controllers, and the RETRACT block moves the tool axis before the axes turn (VM 3.1a). Alternative: MB as an option of MOVE=TURN. That needs a retract-length word on TILT and changes the Siemens _FR reading. For the reset, the alternative is a new form TILT=RESET MOVE=TURN.
Where: language 4.2 (MOVE row); controller-mapping 1 (TILT and MOVE rows); heidenhain.md 3, 7 rule 6; machine-config 5 ([transform] move); src/Ncx.Readers/Heidenhain/HeidenhainPlane.cs Options (TODO(question) at line 99); P3-04 HeidenhainFrames.

ANSWER:
As recommended, confirmed from the manual library: Keep the code's reading — the manual says it in as many words. MB is a retract path in the active tool-axis direction, incremental from the current tool position, which the control travels to before the swivel; MB MAX goes to just short of the software limit switch. That is precisely NCX RETRACT (bare, to the axis limit) and RETRACT=n, written as a block in front of the TILT, as the Siemens _FR is. MB belongs to TURN only — MOVE takes ABST/DIST and F instead — so language 4.2's "tool retracted first" should become the draft's wording. PLANE RESET with TURN or MOVE is a documented block (25 PLANE RESET MOVE ABST50 F1000) that positions the swivel axes back into their basic position, a real motion that TILT=RESET alone does not express, so keeping it RAW in 1.0 with a note in heidenhain 7 rule 6 is right.
Evidence: Heidenhain iTNC 530 — Benutzer-Handbuch HEIDENHAIN-Klartext-Dialog (NC-SW 606420-01, 2010), p. 463 (MB is defined as the "Rückzugsweg, wirkt inkremental von der aktuellen Werkzeug-Position in der aktiven Werkzeug-Achsrichtung, den die TNC vor dem Einschwenkvorgang anfährt"; MB MAX moves the tool to just short of the software limit switch. A retract, before the tilt, in the tool axis only. Verified); Heidenhain iTNC 530 — Benutzer-Handbuch HEIDENHAIN-Klartext-Dialog (NC-SW 606420-01, 2010), p. 462 (MOVE swivels with a compensating motion in the linear axes so the relative position of workpiece and tool does not change, and then needs ABST and F; TURN swivels without any compensating motion and then needs MB and F; STAY leaves the positioning to a separate block. The retract is an option of TURN, not the meaning of TURN. Verified); Heidenhain TNC 640 — Benutzerhandbuch Klartextprogrammierung (892903-18, 10/2019), p. 430 (Identical MB definition on the TNC 640: retract path, incremental from the current tool position in the active tool-axis direction, travelled before the swivel, MB MAX to just short of the limit switch. Page 429 keeps the MOVE/TURN/STAY split but requires only F for TURN. Verified); Heidenhain iTNC 530 — Benutzer-Handbuch HEIDENHAIN-Klartext-Dialog (NC-SW 606420-01, 2010), p. 448 (PLANE RESET: the dialog asks whether the control should move the swivel axes automatically into their basic position (MOVE or TURN) or not (STAY); the example block is 25 PLANE RESET MOVE ABST50 F1000. PLANE RESET fully resets the active PLANE function or an active cycle 19 (angle 0, function inactive). Verified); Heidenhain TNC 640 — Benutzerhandbuch Klartextprogrammierung (892903-18, 10/2019), p. 413 (The same on the TNC 640, with the example 25 PLANE RESET MOVE DIST50 F1000: MOVE or TURN positions the swivel axes into their basic position, STAY does not. Verified).
Settled 2026-10-01: the maintainer let the manual-confirmed answers that agree with their recommendation be applied without reviewing each one.

### Seventh round: controller and machine facts to confirm

#### D241 Fanuc arc with a centre word left out
Question: Fanuc 4 describes G2/G3 'with the end point and I J K ... or R (...; a full circle needs I J)', but not an arc whose I, J or K of the plane is left out. VM 3.2 requires both plane axes of CENTER. Case: G0 X10. Y0 Z0, then G3 X10. Y0 Z-5. I-10. without J. Main takes the left-out word as 0 (FanucMotion.ReadArc) and writes ARC=CCW X=10 Y=0 Z=-5 CENTER:X=0 CENTER:Y=0 (test G3_WithoutJAndWithZ_IsAHelixAboutTheCentre).
Recommendation: Confirm in the Fanuc 30i manual (circular interpolation). Our reading of the manual, which is not in the documents: 'I0, J0 and K0 can be omitted', so a left-out centre word is 0, as main does. If that is confirmed, fanuc 4 adds the sentence, the paragraph under controller-mapping 2 says the reader writes the 0, and the TODO(question) becomes a comment. If the manual makes such an arc an alarm, the reader keeps it RAW with a WARNING (D5).
Where: controllers/fanuc.md 4 (G2/G3 bullet); controller-mapping 2 (paragraph under the table); src/Ncx.Readers/Fanuc/FanucMotion.cs ReadArc (TODO(question) at line 398); tests/Ncx.Readers.Tests/Fanuc/FanucMotionTests.cs G3_WithoutJAndWithZ_IsAHelixAboutTheCentre.

ANSWER:
As recommended, confirmed from the manual library: A left-out I, J or K of the plane is 0, so main is right. The circular-interpolation section, after explaining that I, J and K are the signed vector from the start point to the arc centre and are always incremental regardless of G90/G91, states plainly that I0, J0 and K0 may be omitted, so `G3 X10. Y0 Z-5. I-10.` in G17 is an arc about the centre offset (-10, 0) from the start point, i.e. CENTER:X=0 CENTER:Y=0 as the reader writes it. The only alarm named for the centre form is PS0020 when the start and end radii differ by more than parameter 3410, so such a block is not an alarm. Add the sentence to fanuc 4, note the reader's 0 under controller-mapping 2, and turn the TODO(question) into a comment.
Evidence: Fanuc Series 30i/31i/32i-B Betriebshandbuch Drehen/Fräsen B-64484GE/02, p. PDF 84 (printed p. 50), section 4.4 (I, J and K give the arc centre for the Xp, Yp and Zp axes as a signed vector component from the start point, always incremental regardless of G90/G91; the text then says "I0, J0 und K0 können entfallen", and the only alarm named is PS0020 when the start and end radii differ by more than parameter 3410); Fanuc Series 30i/31i/32i-B Operator's Manual B-64484EN, p. PDF 79 (The English twin of the same paragraph reads "I0, J0, and K0 can be omitted").

#### D242 Fanuc group 01 before the first G0 to G3, and the rate of G53
Question: Fanuc 3 says one code per group is active 'until another G of the same group appears', but does not say which group 01 code is active at the start, which is a control parameter. Language 4.3 needs a verb on every block with axis words. Both Nakamura paths reach G53X#528 (path 1 line 20, path 2 line 28) before any G0 to G3. Fanuc 4, 9 rule 3 and controller-mapping 1 (FRAME=MACHINE) give G53 as 'machine coordinates for that block' but not its rate. So under an active G1, main reads a G53 block as LINE ... FRAME=MACHINE with the modal F. Main writes RAPID before any group 01 code (FanucMotion.VerbOf, test AxisWords_BeforeAnyMotionCode_AreRapid) and the active group 01 verb on a G53 block. In a subprogram whose callers leave group 01 open, a G53 block therefore stays RAW (FanucMotion.UnknownFact).
Recommendation: Confirm in the Fanuc 30i manual. Our reading, which is not in the documents: group 01 powers on and resets to G00 unless parameter 3402#0 selects G01, and a G53 block moves at rapid traverse whatever group 01 holds. If that is confirmed, fanuc 3 says group 01 starts at G0, and the reader keeps RAPID without a machine key. Fanuc 4, 9 rule 3 and the controller-mapping 1 FRAME=MACHINE row say that G53 moves at rapid. The reader then writes RAPID on every G53 block and leaves group 01 as it was for the blocks after it (FanucMotion.ReadMotion when block.MachineFrame). A G53 block then no longer depends on the code of group 01, so it need not stay RAW in a subprogram whose callers leave that code open. The Fanuc compiler (P3-06) reports a LINE or ARC with FRAME=MACHINE (for example Heidenhain L X.. F.. M91) as an ERROR, because G53 would move it at rapid. No acceptance output changes: every G53 of the Nakamura pair stands under G0 or before any group 01 code, and the mill sources have none. Alternative: a [machine] key for the start code of group 01, for machines set to G01.
Where: controllers/fanuc.md 3 (modality paragraph), 4 (G53 bullet), 9 rules 1 and 3; controller-mapping 1 (FRAME=MACHINE row); src/Ncx.Readers/Fanuc/FanucMotion.cs VerbOf (TODO(question) at line 336), ReadMotion and UnknownFact; tests/Ncx.Readers.Tests/Fanuc/FanucMotionTests.cs AxisWords_BeforeAnyMotionCode_AreRapid and FanucFrameTests.cs G53_IsFrameMachineOnItsBlock; P3-06 FanucFrames.

ANSWER:
As recommended, confirmed from the manual library: Both halves are confirmed. Group 01 comes up and resets to G00 unless parameter 3402 bit 0 (G01) selects G01, so the reader's RAPID before any group-01 code stands without a machine key. G53 always moves at rapid traverse ("verfährt die Maschine im Eilgang an diese Position"), is a one-shot code effective only in its own block, and wants an absolute value — an incremental value makes the G53 ignored — so the reader writes RAPID on every G53 block, leaves group 01 untouched for the blocks after it, and a G53 block no longer depends on the caller's group 01. The Fanuc feed variant is the separate G53.2, which is the code that needs a modal G00/G01 (alarm PS5372 otherwise).
Evidence: Fanuc Series 30i/31i/32i-B Parameterhandbuch B-64490GE/03, p. PDF 202 (printed p. 190) (Parameter 3402 bit 0 (G01) sets the initial mode at power-on and after reset: 0 gives the G00 positioning mode, 1 the G01 linear-interpolation mode); Fanuc Series 30i/31i/32i-B Betriebshandbuch Drehen/Fräsen B-64484GE/02, p. PDF 66 (printed p. 32) (In the clear state set at power-on or reset the modal G codes go to the marked states, and sub-item (4) of the explanation says the user selects G00 or G01 through bit 0 (G01) of parameter 3402); Fanuc Series 30i/31i/32i-B Betriebshandbuch Drehen/Fräsen B-64484GE/02, p. PDF 200-201 (printed pp. 166-167), section 7.1 (When a position in the machine coordinate system is commanded the machine travels there "im Eilgang"; G53 is a one-shot code valid only in the block in which it stands, must be given an absolute value, and is ignored if an incremental value is given. The next page introduces G53.2 as the separate machine-coordinate positioning at a feedrate, which alarms PS5372 if the modal group-01 code is anything but G00/G01); Fanuc Series 30i/31i/32i-B Betriebshandbuch Drehen/Fräsen B-64484GE/02, p. PDF 77 (printed p. 43) (Supporting only: in the G00 section the cases where positioning is not linear even though linear positioning is selected are listed as the moves between reference and intermediate points with G28, and G53. This shows G53 is handled with the rapid modes; it does not by itself state the rate); Nakamura-Tome Programmierhandbuch (Walter Meier), Fanuc 0iTF/31iB/32iA, p. PDF 20 (G list) and pp. 53-54 (The builder's G list calls G53 positioning in machine coordinates "Bewegung im Eilgang", and the detail page repeats that G53 positioning is possible only at rapid and in absolute coordinates, that G53 is block-wise only ("G53 ist nur Satzweise wirksam"), and that it may be written with variables such as G53 X#548 Z#549).
Settled 2026-10-01: the maintainer let the manual-confirmed answers that agree with their recommendation be applied without reviewing each one.

#### D243 Fanuc G28 and G30 with an absolute word
Question: Fanuc 4 explains G91 G28 Z0 ('the 0 is an incremental distance of zero on the way to the reference point') and says 'G28 with a real distance moves to the intermediate point first'. Controller-mapping 1 (HOME) reads G28 U0 W0, 'G28 X0 Y0 Z0 with G91', G28 H0 and 'G28 B0 for a sub spindle slide' as HOME. No document says what an absolute word of G28 or G30 means: a word under G90, or a system A address without an incremental letter, such as B in G28 B0 and G28 U0 B0 (Nakamura path 2, lines 29, 119, 141 and 174). Case: G90 G28 Z0 with the tool at Z50. Main treats a 0 as no intermediate point in either mode, and any other value as one (FanucFrames.ReadHome; tests G28_WithADistance_MovesToTheIntermediatePointFirst, G28U0W0_OnSystemA_BecomesHomeXZ).
Recommendation: Confirm in the Fanuc 30i manual (reference position return). Our reading, which is not in the documents: the words of G28 and G30 are the intermediate position, and the axes reach that position at rapid before the return. A word is absolute under G90 or on an address that is always absolute, and incremental under G91 or when written with U W H V. If that is confirmed, only an incremental 0 means no intermediate move, and an absolute word, 0 included, writes a RAPID to it first. So G90 G28 Z0 is RAPID Z=0 then HOME Z, and G28 U0 B0 is RAPID B=0 then HOME X B. Fanuc 4, 9 rule 3 and the controller-mapping 1 HOME row say so, and ReadHome tests the 0 on incremental words only. Nakamura path 2 then gains a RAPID B=0 before each of its four G28 blocks. No expected file holds them, but P3-07 checks the pair. The mill examples keep their reading, because N380/N390 of 2.5D_FRAESEN and the returns of BOHREN and 3D_FRAESEN stand under G91. There the Fanuc reader still writes HOME Z and HOME X Y, where the Heidenhain reader writes RAPID Z=0 FRAME=MACHINE and RAPID X=0 Y=0 FRAME=MACHINE (2.5D_FRAESEN note 4, an M6 difference of its own). Alternative: keep main's rule and state in fanuc 4 that the reader drops the intermediate point at an absolute 0. The NCX then differs from the machine wherever the axis stands away from that 0.
Where: controllers/fanuc.md 4 (G28 bullet), 9 rule 3; controller-mapping 1 (HOME row); src/Ncx.Readers/Fanuc/FanucFrames.cs ReadHome (TODO(question) at line 113); tests/Ncx.Readers.Tests/Fanuc/FanucFrameTests.cs (the G28 tests); docs/spec/examples/sources/NAKAMURA_WY250L_O1000.path2.nc lines 29, 119, 141, 174.

ANSWER:
As recommended, confirmed from the manual library: Confirmed: the words of G28 and G30 are the intermediate point, given in the absolute coordinate system and usable in absolute or incremental programming, and the axes reach it at rapid before the return. So `G90 G28 Z0` is RAPID Z=0 then HOME Z, and only an incremental zero (`G28 U0 W0`, `G28 H0`) means no intermediate move; Mori Seiki warns about exactly this and tells the programmer to use an incremental form because an absolute `G28 X0 Y0 Z0` first drives to the workpiece zero. An address that has no incremental twin is always absolute: under G-code system A only axes named X, Y, Z or C get U, V, W and H, so a `G28 B0` is an absolute B intermediate point and gains a RAPID B=0 before the HOME — the same case Mori Seiki flags for its A axis, where it prescribes G330 instead of `G28 A0`.
Evidence: Fanuc Series 30i/31i/32i-B Betriebshandbuch Drehen/Fräsen B-64484GE/02, p. PDF 193 (printed p. 159), section 6.1 (The format gives G28 IP_ with IP_ as the intermediate-point command in the absolute coordinate system, usable in absolute or incremental programming; positioning at the intermediate and the reference point is at rapid on all axes, and the intermediate coordinates are stored for the axes named in the block, the previous values being used for the others); Mori Seiki NT/NTX Programmieranleitung NTX1000SZM, PX-NT 4-K0DEEN, p. PDF 124 (section 2-18, CAUTION 1 and 2) (To return from the present position, use an incremental command such as G28 U0 V0 W0; with an absolute command such as G28 X0 Y0 Z0 the axes first move to the workpiece zero point before returning to the machine zero, which may cause interference. Caution 2 adds that G28 A0 likewise takes the A axis (tailstock/headstock 2/workpiece discharge) to the machine zero via the workpiece zero, so G330 should be used instead; the word list notes that the value after X, Y, Z is the coordinate of the intermediate point); Fanuc Series 30i/31i/32i-B Parameterhandbuch B-64490GE/03, p. PDF 62 (printed p. 50), parameter 1020 (In a lathe system with G-code system A, a command written with U, V, W or H is the incremental form only for an axis whose name 1 is X, Y, Z or C; an axis named B therefore has no incremental address); Fanuc Series 30i/31i/32i-B Betriebshandbuch Drehen/Fräsen B-64484GE/02, p. PDF 67 (printed p. 33), note 8 (With G-code system A, absolute or incremental programming is not selected by G90/G91 but by the address word pairs X/U, Z/W, C/H, Y/V); Nakamura-Tome Programmierhandbuch (Walter Meier), Fanuc 0iTF/31iB/32iA, p. PDF 111 (The two-channel header example writes G28 U0, G28 W0 for the incremental axes and G28 B0 on the lower turret, i.e. exactly the mixed form the draft asks about).
Settled 2026-10-01: the maintainer let the manual-confirmed answers that agree with their recommendation be applied without reviewing each one.

#### D246 The words of Fanuc G68.1 and its NCX form
Question: D82 lists G68.1 among the source forms of TILT_AXIS, and so does the TILT_AXIS row of language 4.2 ('Fanuc G68.1/G53.1 sequences'). Controller-mapping 1 (TILT_AXIS row) reads 'G68.1 (3D conversion by axis angles, corpus: 23 lines) with G53.1, else RAW'. Controller-mapping 11 lists G68.1 and G53.1 under 'a tilted plane by rotary axis angles', and differences.md reads 'G68.1 by axis angles'. Fanuc 4, however, says that G68.1 'rotates the coordinate system about an axis (3D coordinate conversion, on Mazak and Mori Seiki)', and TILT_AXIS takes the positions of the machine's rotary axes (language 4.2). No document gives the words of G68.1, so the reader cannot compute axis angles from G68.1 X0 Y0 Z0 I0 J0 K1 R30. Main keeps every G68.1 RAW (FanucTilt.Read, test G681_IsKeptAsRaw).
Recommendation: The maintainer confirms the format from the Mori Seiki NTX programming manual and the 23 corpus lines. Our reading of the Fanuc manuals, which is not in the documents: G68.1 X Y Z I J K R is the 3D coordinate conversion of the lathe G-code systems, whose G68/G69 are the double-turret functions (fanuc 3, group 16). It is a rotation by R about the axis I J K through X Y Z, cancelled by G69.1 (40 corpus lines), and it names no rotary axis position. If that is confirmed, G68.1 stays RAW in 1.0, as main does and as the 'else RAW' of controller-mapping 1 allows. The TILT_AXIS row of language 4.2 drops 'Fanuc G68.1/G53.1 sequences' (this is specification text). The TILT_AXIS row of controller-mapping 1 and differences.md drop G68.1, controller-mapping 11 takes G68.1 out of the axis-angle list, and fanuc 4 stays. D82 gets a Clarified line that G68.1 is not one of its source forms (the TILT_AXIS word is unchanged), and the 'G68.1 as TILT_AXIS' of P3-02 goes. P3-06 then writes no G68.1 for TILT_AXIS. Alternative: read a G68.1 about an axis through the origin as TILT with the spatial angles of that rotation, computed as the reader already does for G68.2 P0, and read G69.1 as TILT=RESET. If the manual does show rotary axis words on G68.1, it is TILT_AXIS with those words, as D82 says.
Where: decisions.md D82 row and rationale.md D82 (Clarified line); language 4.2 (TILT_AXIS row); controller-mapping 1 (TILT_AXIS and TILT rows) and 11 (the paragraph on the words of D81 to D86); controllers/differences.md (rotation row); controllers/fanuc.md 4; controllers/sample-corpus.md (G68.1/G53.1 among the words of D81 to D86); 13-phase-3-readers-compilers.md P3-02 (FanucFrames bullet) and P3-06; src/Ncx.Readers/Fanuc/FanucTilt.cs Read (TODO(question) at line 30); tests/Ncx.Readers.Tests/Fanuc/FanucFrameTests.cs G681_IsKeptAsRaw.

ANSWER:
As recommended, confirmed from the manual library: Confirmed: G68.1 is the lathe form of the G68 coordinate rotation, not an axis-angle tilt. Without I J K it is a plane rotation `G68.1 G17 X_ Y_ Rα` about a centre; with them it is `G68.1 Xp Yp Zp I J K R`, a rotation by R about the axis direction I J K through the centre Xp Yp Zp, cancelled by G69.1 (group 17 on lathes, where G68/G69 are the double-turret mirror or balance mode instead). The Mori Seiki NTX1000 manual gives exactly that block and says the operator writes R as 90 plus the B-axis angle — the rotary axis position appears nowhere in the block. So G68.1 stays RAW in 1.0, and the specification drops it from TILT_AXIS as the recommendation says; note that this needs a Clarified line on the already recorded decision D82, which lists G68.1 among the source forms of TILT_AXIS.
Evidence: Fanuc Series 30i/31i-A Programmierung, Kapitelauszug "4 PROGRAM FORMAT" (G68/G68.1/G68.2/G68.3), p. printed p. 91 (the file's only page; image-only, read by rendering it with ghostscript) (The program-format table lists "Coordinate system rotation, Three-dimensional coordinate conversion (G68, G69), (G68.1, G69.1)" and gives, for the machining-centre system, G68 with G17 X Y / G18 Z X / G19 Y Z and R α, cancelled by G69, and for the lathe system the identical form on G68.1, cancelled by G69.1. G68.2 is listed separately with X Y Z as the feature-system origin and I J K as Euler angles); Fanuc Series 30i/31i/32i-B Betriebshandbuch Drehen/Fräsen B-64484GE/02, p. PDF 347 (printed p. 313), section 14.2 (The lathe format is G68.1 Xp Yp Zp I J K R with Xp Yp Zp the centre of rotation in absolute coordinates, I J K the direction of the rotation axis and R the angle, ended by G69.1; the machining-centre twin is the same on G68/G69); Fanuc Series 30i/31i/32i-B Betriebshandbuch Drehen/Fräsen B-64484GE/02, p. PDF 74 (printed p. 40), table 3.2 (b) (In the lathe G-code list G68.1 and G69.1 are group 17, coordinate-system rotation start/end or three-dimensional coordinate conversion on/off, while G68/G69 are group 04, mirror image for a double turret or balanced-machining mode); Fanuc Series 16i/18i-TB Benutzerhandbuch B-63524GE/01, p. PDF 238 (the statement); the two-G68.1 worked example is on PDF 241 (Three-dimensional and two-dimensional coordinate conversion use the same codes G68.1 and G69.1; a block with I, J and K is the three-dimensional command, one without them the two-dimensional one, and the workpiece coordinates are held in #5041 to #5048. The example on p. 241 chains two G68.1 blocks, the second measured in the system the first created); Mori Seiki NT/NTX Programmieranleitung NTX1000SZM, PX-NT 4-K0DEEN, p. PDF 175-177 (section 2-35) (G68.1 X_ Y_ Z_ I_ J_ K_ R_ is the 3D coordinate conversion, cancelled by G69.1: X Y Z are the coordinates of the centre of rotation as absolute values, I J K name the axis of rotation (I=X, J=Y, K=Z; on the NT series "I0 J1 K0" for the Y axis) and R is the rotation angle, specified as "90 + B-Achsenwinkel". The command must be nested with G43/G49 in one of two prescribed orders, pattern 2 for turning); Nakamura-Tome Programmierhandbuch (Walter Meier), Fanuc 0iTF/31iB/32iA, p. PDF 20-21 (The Nakamura G list gives G68/G69 as simultaneous (balance) machining on and off in group 04, and puts the three-dimensional coordinate conversion on the builder cycles G358 (swivel-turret series) and G368/G369 (milling-spindle series)).
Settled 2026-10-01: the maintainer let the manual-confirmed answers that agree with their recommendation be applied without reviewing each one.

#### D247 G0 to G3 as the end of a Fanuc mill canned cycle
Question: fanuc 6 says G80 cancels a canned cycle, '(or a G0/G1 on some controls)'. fanuc 3 puts the mill cycles in group 09 and G0..G3 in group 01. Its rule 'one value per group is active until another G of the same group appears' reads as if a G0 left the cycle active. fanuc 9 rule 5 and controller-mapping 5 (CYCLE=OFF row) name G80 only. Case: G0 X50. while a G81 is active. Does the block move, or does it drill at X50? Main ends the cycle at any G0 to G3 on a mill: it writes CYCLE=OFF and the block moves (FanucCycles.Ends, EndsEveryCycle).
Recommendation: Confirm from the Fanuc 30i machining-center manual that a group 01 code (G0, G1, G2, G3) cancels a canned cycle as G80 does. That is our reading of the manual, not something in the documents. If confirmed, fanuc 6 and 9 rule 5 read 'G80 or any G0 to G3 cancels', controller-mapping 5 adds it to the CYCLE=OFF row, and main stays as it is. If a control of the corpus keeps the cycle through G0/G1, a machine key ([cycles] motion_cancels = false) selects that behaviour, with today's behaviour as the default. No acceptance source depends on it: BOHREN writes G80 before every G0.
Where: fanuc 3 (group 09 row), 6, 9 rule 5; controller-mapping 5 (CYCLE=OFF row); src/Ncx.Readers/Fanuc/FanucCycles.cs Ends (TODO(question) at lines 362-363) and EndsEveryCycle; machine-config 6 only if the key is needed.

ANSWER:
As recommended, confirmed from the manual library: Confirmed, and the corpus machine's own manual says it too: any group 01 code (G0, G1, G2, G3) ends a Fanuc canned cycle and leaves the same state as G80, on the mill and on the lathe, so `G0 X50.` under an active G81 is a rapid to X50 and drills nothing. Main stays as it is: fanuc 6 and fanuc 9 rule 5 read "G80 or any G0 to G3 cancels", controller-mapping 5 adds the group 01 codes to the CYCLE=OFF row, and no [cycles] motion_cancels key is needed. Two things the manuals add that the answer should carry: a group 01 code and a cycle G code in one block are a documented hazard (the mill manual forbids it and drops the cycle code; the Nakamura says the outcome depends on which of the two stands first in the block), and a group 01 cancel is not identical to G80 in what it keeps — G80 also clears the point R and point Z levels, while after a group 01 cancel the Nakamura keeps the R value and the initial-point coordinates.
Evidence: Fanuc Series 30i/31i/32i-B, Betriebshandbuch Drehen und Fräsen, B-64484GE/02, p. 67 (printed 33), note 5 of the Erläuterung to chapter 3 (A group 01 G code given inside a drilling canned cycle deletes the cycle and produces the same state as programming G80; conversely the canned-cycle G codes have no effect on the group 01 codes. The notes stand in chapter 3 before section 3.1 (machining-centre list) and section 3.2 (lathe list), so they hold for both; only note 8 is marked T); Fanuc Series 30i/31i/32i-B, Bedienung Fräsen, B-64484GE-2/02, p. 65 (printed 49), section "Beenden" of the canned-cycle overview (To end canned cycles "muss G80 oder ein G-Code der Gruppe 01 verwendet werden", and G00, G01, G02, G03 are then listed by name); Fanuc Series 30i/31i/32i-B, Betriebshandbuch Drehen, B-64484GE-1/02, p. 94 (printed 78), section "Beenden" (The same sentence for the lathe canned cycles, with G00, G01, G02, G03 listed as examples of group 01); Fanuc Series 0i-D, Bedienung Drehen, B-64304GE-1/02, p. 104 (printed 84) (Identical wording on the older 0i-D, so the rule is not a 30i peculiarity); Fanuc Series 30i/31i/32i-B, Bedienung Fräsen, B-64484GE-2/02, p. 73 (printed 57), G81 "Beenden" (A group 01 code (G00 to G03) and G81 must not be specified in the same block, otherwise G81 is deleted. The identical sentence is repeated on pages 67, 69, 71, 74, 76, 83, 85, 86, 88, 90 and 92 for G73, G74, G76, G82 to G89); Nakamura-Tome Programming Manual (WY-250L), 4810004EEE, 2020, p. 283 and 288 (chapter 14-7) (The corpus machine's own manual: "The drilling cycle mode is canceled by a G80 command or a G code in group 01." Page 288 adds that the cancellation happens when the group 01 code is read, and that when a group 01 code and a cycle-calling G code stand in one block the result depends on which is written first — cycle first: the cycle runs; group 01 first: the axes position in that mode, R is ignored and F is only stored); Nakamura-Tome Programmierhandbuch (Walter Meier, 2019), Fanuc 0iTF/31iB/32iA, p. 72 ("Mit den G-Funktionen der Gruppe 01 (G00, G01, G02, G03 usw.) wird der Bohrzyklus ebenfalls gelöscht, aber die Werte der Zyklus-Variabel "R" und die Koordinaten des Ausgangspunktes bleiben erhalten." So the two cancels differ in what modal data survives).
Settled 2026-10-01: the maintainer let the manual-confirmed answers that agree with their recommendation be applied without reviewing each one.

#### D251 Feed of TOOL CALL and F AUTO
Question: heidenhain.md 4 lists the F of TOOL CALL 4 Z S1592 F500 as 'optionally the feed' without saying what it does. heidenhain.md 2 gives F AUTO as 'the feed of the tool table', a value that no NCX word and no machine key holds. Today HeidenhainMotion.ReadFeed keeps an L with F AUTO RAW, and HeidenhainToolCall.ReadCall keeps a TOOL CALL with F RAW. DL and DR need no answer: language 4.4 has no delta word, so RAW with a WARNING is D5, as coded.
Recommendation: The maintainer confirms from the iTNC 530 user manual (TOOL CALL, feed rate F, F AUTO). Our reading, not in the documents: F AUTO recalls the F of the last TOOL CALL, and that F is also the modal feed until the next F. If so, the reader writes `F=<value>` in the TOOL block (F is a modal word, language 4.3) and keeps the value. It reads F AUTO as `F=<that value>`, and keeps the block RAW only where no TOOL CALL F is known. The Heidenhain compiler folds an F of the TOOL block into the TOOL CALL (heidenhain 8 rule 3), and heidenhain 2 and 4 are corrected. Alternative: keep both RAW, as coded.
Where: heidenhain.md 2, 4, 8 rule 3; src/Ncx.Readers/Heidenhain/HeidenhainMotion.cs ReadFeed (TODO(question) at line 183) and HeidenhainToolCall.cs ReadCall (TODO(question) at line 35); P3-04 HeidenhainToolCall.

ANSWER:
As recommended, confirmed from the manual library: Confirmed, and heidenhain.md 2 is wrong and must be corrected. The F of a TOOL CALL is the ordinary modal feed: "F wirkt solange, bis Sie in einem Positioniersatz oder in einem TOOL CALL-Satz einen neuen Vorschub programmieren". F AUTO (written FAUTO) is not the feed of the tool table — it is the feed from the TOOL CALL block. So the reader writes F=<value> in the TOOL block, keeps the value, reads an L with F AUTO as F=<that value>, and keeps a block RAW only where no TOOL CALL feed is known; the compiler folds an F of the TOOL block back into the TOOL CALL.
Evidence: Heidenhain iTNC 530 — Benutzer-Handbuch HEIDENHAIN-Klartext-Dialog (NC-SW 606420-01, 2010), p. 205 (In the worked dialog for a straight-line block the feed choice is: enter a value, press FMAX for rapid, or press FAUTO to travel "mit Vorschub ..., der im TOOL CALL-Satz definiert ist". Verified); Heidenhain iTNC 530 — Benutzer-Handbuch HEIDENHAIN-Klartext-Dialog (NC-SW 606420-01, 2010), p. 180 (In the TOOL CALL description: the feed F may be entered directly or computed by the control from the cutting-data tables (softkey F AUTOM. BERECHNEN), and "F wirkt solange, bis Sie in einem Positioniersatz oder in einem TOOL CALL-Satz einen neuen Vorschub programmieren". The TOOL CALL feed is the modal feed. Verified); Heidenhain iTNC 530 — Benutzer-Handbuch HEIDENHAIN-Klartext-Dialog (NC-SW 606420-01, 2010), p. 462 (In the PLANE positioning section, as an alternative to a numeric F the swivel motion can run with FMAX or with "FAUTO (Vorschub aus TOOL CALL-Satz)" — the same definition spelled out in one parenthesis. Verified); Heidenhain TNC 640 — Benutzerhandbuch Klartextprogrammierung (892903-18, 10/2019), p. 429 (The TNC 640 repeats the parenthesis: FAUTO is the feed from the TOOL CALL block. Verified. Page 143 of the same manual carries the line-block dialog with "mit dem Vorschub verfahren, der im TOOL CALL-Satz definiert ist: Softkey F AUTO drücken" — there the word is spelled with a space, which is why a search for FAUTO alone misses it); Heidenhain iTNC 530 — Benutzer-Handbuch HEIDENHAIN-Klartext-Dialog (NC-SW 606420-01, 2010), p. 162 (Duration of effect of F: a feed programmed as a number holds until a block programs a new one; F MAX holds only for its own block, after which the last numeric feed applies again. F may be entered in the TOOL CALL block and in every positioning block. The modal model the reader needs. Verified); Heidenhain TNC 640 — Benutzerhandbuch Zyklenprogrammierung (892905-18, 10/2019), p. 89 (Cycle 200's parameter Q206 accepts a number "alternativ FAUTO, FU" — FAUTO appears as a cycle parameter value too, with the same meaning. Verified).
Settled 2026-10-01: the maintainer let the manual-confirmed answers that agree with their recommendation be applied without reviewing each one.

#### D252 When the M functions of a Klartext block act
Question: heidenhain.md 2 allows up to two M functions at the end of an L block and does not say when they act. Language 5 rule 3 makes every state word of an NCX motion block act before its motion. fanuc.md 1 says the same only for S and M3 in a Fanuc motion block. HeidenhainFunctions writes every M function of a positioning block into the NCX block of the motion. No TODO(question) marks this; only the P3-05 log records it. On the TNC, each M function acts either at the block start or at the block end. If M5 and M9 act at the end, L Z+100 R0 FMAX M5 reads as SPINDLE=OFF before the retract. That is a different program: it stops the spindle with the tool still in the cut. The Heidenhain compiler faces the same question in the other direction. No example source writes an M function other than M91 or M99 on an L block, so the acceptance files do not show it.
Recommendation: The maintainer confirms the iTNC 530 manual's table of which M functions act at the block start and which at the block end, and heidenhain.md 2 carries it. Our reading, not in the documents: M3, M4, M8, M13 and M14 act at the block start. M0, M1, M2, M5, M9 and M30 act at the block end. The rest act as the table says. The reader writes the word of a function that acts at the block end in a block of its own directly after the motion. It keeps the others in the motion block, and language 5 rule 3 stays. A builder function from the machine's tables stays in the motion block. The Heidenhain compiler writes a word whose M function acts at the block end (SPINDLE=OFF, COOLANT=OFF, STOP) in a block before the L. That is one sentence in heidenhain 8.
Where: heidenhain.md 2 (the table), 7 (a reader rule), 8 (a compiler rule); src/Ncx.Readers/Heidenhain/HeidenhainFunctions.cs Read and ReadCode (a TODO(question) belongs there); the P3-05 log (it names HeidenhainMotion); P3-04.

ANSWER:
As recommended, confirmed from the manual library: Confirmed, and the manual carries the whole table. The general rule is stated outright: some auxiliary functions become effective at the start of a positioning block and others at the end, regardless of the order in which they stand in the block. The list is: block start M3, M4, M8, M13, M14; block end M0, M1, M2, M5, M6, M9, M30. So L Z+100 R0 FMAX M5 does stop the spindle at the end of the retract, the reader writes the word of a block-end function in a block of its own directly after the motion, and the Heidenhain compiler writes SPINDLE=OFF, COOLANT=OFF and STOP into a block before the L. Add M6 to the block-end list of the draft's reading.
Evidence: Heidenhain TNC 640 — Benutzerhandbuch Klartextprogrammierung (892903-18, 10/2019), p. 225 (The overview table "M | Wirkung | Wirkung am Satz - Anfang | Ende". I re-extracted the page with a layout-preserving extraction: marks in the Anfang column for M3, M4, M8, M13, M14; marks in the Ende column for M0, M1, M2, M5, M6, M9, M30. Verified); Heidenhain iTNC 530 — Benutzer-Handbuch HEIDENHAIN-Klartext-Dialog (NC-SW 606420-01, 2010), p. 352 (The rule the draft needs, stated plainly: "Beachten Sie, dass einige Zusatz-Funktionen zu Beginn eines Positionier-Satzes wirksam werden, andere am Ende, unabhängig von der Reihenfolge, in der sie im jeweiligen NC-Satz stehen." Up to two M functions may stand at the end of a positioning block or in a block of their own, and the machine manufacturer may release functions not described in the book. Verified); Heidenhain iTNC 530 — Benutzer-Handbuch HEIDENHAIN-Klartext-Dialog (NC-SW 606420-01, 2010), p. 353 (The same overview table for the iTNC 530. Read from a rendering of the page, not from the text layer: Anfang for M3, M4, M8, M13, M14; Ende for M0, M1, M2, M5, M6, M9, M30 — row for row the same assignment as the TNC 640); Heidenhain iTNC 530 — Benutzer-Handbuch HEIDENHAIN-Klartext-Dialog (NC-SW 606420-01, 2010), p. 355 (Example of the per-function statements the same manual gives for everything outside the overview table: "M91 und M92 werden wirksam am Satz-Anfang." I checked the others named: page 356 "M104 wird wirksam am Satz-Ende", page 368 "M140 wird wirksam am Satz-Anfang", page 480 "M128 wird wirksam am Satz-Anfang, M129 am Satz-Ende". All verified).
Settled 2026-10-01: the maintainer let the manual-confirmed answers that agree with their recommendation be applied without reviewing each one.

#### D254 Klartext LBL the main flow runs through, CC with one axis, PATTERN DEF surface
Question: (1) heidenhain.md 1 puts subprograms after the M30. heidenhain 7 rule 3 and controller-mapping 6 make an LBL n ... LBL 0 that CALL LBL calls without REP a SUB section. None says what such a section is when the main flow also runs through it: one that stands before the M30, or one in a program without M30 (tolerated, heidenhain 1). None says what an LBL is that CALL LBL calls and that REP or an FN jump also uses. (2) heidenhain 2 gives CC with both plane axes, incremental, or alone (the current position), but not with one axis. (3) heidenhain 5 writes PATTERN DEF points with a tool-axis coordinate, POS1 (X+25 Y+33.5 Z+0), without saying what it means. Today HeidenhainLabels.DecideSubs makes such an LBL no subprogram and keeps its CALL LBL RAW. HeidenhainArcs.ReadPole leaves the pole unknown and keeps the arcs about it RAW. HeidenhainCycles.PointOf keeps the pattern RAW unless the coordinate is 0.
Recommendation: The maintainer confirms from the iTNC 530 manual. Our reading, not in the documents, point by point. (1) The control runs a section that the flow reaches as ordinary blocks and passes over its LBL 0. The reader then writes the section as a SUB, and a CALL=n where the section stood, which runs the same blocks in the same order (language 4.13, D89). An LBL also used by REP or an FN jump stays as coded. (2) The coordinate that CC leaves out is the last programmed position of that axis, as for L. The pole is unknown only where that position is unknown. (3) The tool-axis coordinate of a point is added to the Q203 of the cycle. The reader writes the CYCLE block again before that point's CYCLE_CALL, with SURFACE, CLEARANCE, DEPTH and SAFE shifted by it. It writes the block back where the next point differs (language 4.7: a new CYCLE replaces all parameters). heidenhain 1, 2, 5 and 7 record the facts. Until then the code stays RAW.
Where: heidenhain.md 1, 2, 5, 7 rules 3, 5, 7; controller-mapping 6 (paragraph after the table); src/Ncx.Readers/Heidenhain/HeidenhainLabels.cs DecideSubs (TODO(question) at line 213), HeidenhainArcs.cs ReadPole and PoleOf (TODO(question) at line 64), HeidenhainCycles.cs PointOf (TODO(question) at line 500).

ANSWER:
As recommended, confirmed from the manual library: Point by point. (1) Confirmed in as many words: "Wenn Unterprogramme im Bearbeitungs-Programm vor dem Satz mit M2 oder M30 stehen, dann werden sie ohne Aufruf mindestens einmal abgearbeitet" — a labelled section standing before the M2/M30 is run at least once as ordinary blocks, over and above its calls; the manual's own instruction is to put subprograms after the M2/M30 block. So the reader may write such a section as a SUB with a CALL=n where it stood, which runs the same blocks in the same order. (2) Not settled: the manuals describe CC with both plane coordinates, CC with no coordinate at all (it takes over the last programmed position) and an incremental CC coordinate (relative to the last programmed tool position), but never CC with exactly one axis word. (3) Confirmed: "Wenn Sie eine Werkstückoberfläche in Z ungleich 0 definieren, dann wirkt dieser Wert zusätzlich zur Werkstückoberfläche Q203, die Sie im Bearbeitungszyklus definiert haben" — the point's tool-axis coordinate is added to the cycle's Q203, in POS and in ROW, PAT, FRAME and the circle patterns alike.
Evidence: Heidenhain iTNC 530 — Benutzer-Handbuch HEIDENHAIN-Klartext-Dialog (NC-SW 606420-01, 2010), p. 273 (Programming notes for subprograms: program them at the end of the main program, behind the block with M2 or M30; and if subprograms stand in the program before the M2/M30 block, they are worked through at least once without being called. Calling and falling through are separate things and both happen. Verified); Heidenhain TNC 640 — Benutzerhandbuch Klartextprogrammierung (892903-18, 10/2019), p. 247 (The same two notes word for word on the TNC 640, plus the working principle: the control runs to a CALL LBL, works the called section to LBL 0, and then continues with the block after the call. Verified); Heidenhain iTNC 530 — Benutzer-Handbuch HEIDENHAIN-Klartext-Dialog (NC-SW 606420-01, 2010), p. 218 (The circle centre CC: enter the rectangular coordinates of the centre in the working plane, or take over the last programmed position by entering no coordinates at all, or take over the actual position. An incremental centre coordinate always refers to the last programmed tool position. The centre stays fixed until a new one is programmed and is also the pole for polar coordinates. Nothing about a CC carrying only one of the two axes. Verified); Heidenhain TNC 640 — Benutzerhandbuch Klartextprogrammierung (892903-18, 10/2019), p. 158 (The TNC 640's CC section is the same text with the same three entry cases and the same incremental rule; the one-axis case is absent here too. Verified. The TNC 426/430 manual (page 169) and the TNC 310 manual carry the same text, so four generations agree in saying nothing about it); Heidenhain iTNC 530 — Benutzer-Handbuch Zyklenprogrammierung (670 388-12, NC-SW 340490-07, 2011), p. 64 (Defining single machining positions in PATTERN DEF: the third field is the workpiece-surface coordinate in Z at which machining starts, and if you define a surface in Z other than 0 this value acts in addition to the workpiece surface Q203 defined in the machining cycle. Up to nine positions; the example is POS1 (X+25 Y+33,5 Z+0). Verified); Heidenhain TNC 640 — Benutzerhandbuch Zyklenprogrammierung (892905-18, 10/2019), p. 75 (The same sentence on the TNC 640, and on the same page again for the row pattern: a Z other than 0 acts in addition to the cycle's Q203. POS1 must be absolute; POS2 to POS9 may be absolute and/or incremental. Verified); Heidenhain TNC 640 — Benutzerhandbuch Zyklenprogrammierung (892905-18, 10/2019), p. 74 (Two further PATTERN DEF rules: between the start points the control retracts to the safe height, which is the greater of the spindle-axis coordinate at the cycle call and Q204; and if the coordinate surface in the PATTERN DEF is greater than the one in the cycle, the safety clearance and the 2nd safety clearance are computed on the PATTERN DEF surface. Page 73 warns that PATTERN DEF computes in X and Y and is to be used with tool axis Z only. Verified).
Settled 2026-10-01: the maintainer let the manual-confirmed answers that agree with their recommendation be applied without reviewing each one.

#### D255 Klartext CHF and RND: size, feed, and the incremental line after them
Question: D58 and language 4.3 have readers expand chamfers and roundings into LINE and ARC blocks. heidenhain.md 2 says only 'CHF 2 chamfer and RND 4 rounding between two motion blocks', and that the F of an L stays. Three facts decide the expansion. (1) Is the CHF length the distance along each line from the corner point, or the length of the chamfer line itself? Siemens has both: CHR is the leg and CHF the chamfer line (siemens 3). FanucCorners takes the Fanuc ,C as the leg, which fanuc 4 does not define either. (2) Does an F in a CHF or RND block feed only the corner, or also the lines after it? The Siemens FRC is blockwise and is folded into the expanded blocks (controller-mapping 2, F row). (3) Does an IX in the line after the corner count from the corner point that the line before programs, or from the end of the corner? Today HeidenhainCorners takes (1) the distance along each line and (3) the corner point, as FanucCorners does. It keeps a CHF or RND with its own F RAW and leaves the lines about it unshortened. Since RR-P3-05 it also counts a CC alone or by IX and IY, and a polar coordinate that takes the current position, from the corner point, and it expands an RND next to an arc; a chamfer next to an arc stays RAW under a marker of its own (HeidenhainCorners.cs line 231), which is not part of this round.
Recommendation: The maintainer confirms from the iTNC 530 manual (chamfer CHF, corner rounding RND). Our reading, not in the documents, point by point. (1) The chamfer side length is measured from the corner point along each line, as coded. (2) An F in a CHF or RND block feeds that block only, and the earlier feed applies again after it. The reader writes F on the expanded chamfer line or rounding arc. It writes the earlier F again on the next line, unless that line has its own. It keeps the corner RAW only where the earlier feed is unknown. (3) An incremental coordinate counts from the last programmed position, which is the corner point, as coded. heidenhain.md 2 records the three facts.
Where: heidenhain.md 2; src/Ncx.Readers/Heidenhain/HeidenhainCorners.cs BetweenLines (TODO(question) at line 360), Size (at line 540), CurrentPosition and FromCornerEnd (at line 118); tests/Ncx.Readers.Tests/Heidenhain/HeidenhainCornerTests.cs.

ANSWER:
As recommended, confirmed from the manual library: All three facts are settled by the manual, and all three confirm the code as written. (1) The chamfer value is the distance along each line from the corner point: the figure beside the CHF text, in the iTNC 530 and in the TNC 640 manual alike, dimensions the example CHF 12 twice — 12 along the line before the corner and 12 along the line after it (the chamfer line itself measures 17.1 there). (2) A feed programmed in a CHF or RND block acts only in that block, and the feed programmed before it is valid again afterwards. (3) An incremental coordinate counts from the last programmed tool position, which is the corner: in the same example (L X+40 IY+5 / CHF 12 F250 / L IX+5 Y+0) the figure dimensions the end point as 40 + 5 = X45, so the IX counts from the corner the chamfer cut away, not from the chamfer's end. Two further manual facts for heidenhain.md 2: a contour may not begin with a CHF block, and the chamfer shortens both the line before and the line after it (errors 354/355/356 'Fase zu groß').
Evidence: iTNC 530 Benutzer-Handbuch Klartext-Dialog-Programmierung, NC-SW 340490-04 (2007), p. 251 (figure) (The figure beside 'Fase CHF zwischen zwei Geraden einfügen' draws the example contour and dimensions the chamfer twice with the value 12: once between the extension line through the chamfer's start and the extension line through the corner, measured along the line before it, and once between the corner and the chamfer's end, measured along the line after it. Reconstructing the example numerically (corner at X40 Y35, the two line directions) puts the chamfer's ends at (28.09, 33.51) and (41.70, 23.12), which is exactly where the figure draws them, and makes the chamfer line 17.1 long. So the input is the leg, the distance along each line from the corner); iTNC 530 Benutzer-Handbuch Klartext-Dialog-Programmierung, NC-SW 340490-04 (2007), p. 251 (figure, lower dimension chain) (The same figure dimensions the contour end point of the example block 10 L IX+5 Y+0 with a chain 40 then 5 on the X axis, i.e. X45. The 40 ends on the extension line through the corner (X40) that the chamfer cut away, so the incremental IX+5 is counted from the programmed corner, not from the chamfer's end at X41.7. That is point (3), shown outright); iTNC 530 Benutzer-Handbuch Klartext-Dialog-Programmierung, NC-SW 340490-04 (2007), p. 251 (text) (CHF between two straight lines. Input 'Fasen-Abschnitt: Länge der Fase', plus an optional feed that acts 'nur im CHF-Satz'; a note repeats that the feed programmed in the CHF block applies to that block alone and that the feed programmed before it is valid again afterwards. Two further notes: do not begin a contour with a CHF block, and the corner point cut away by the chamfer is not approached. Example: 7 L X+0 Y+30 RL F300 M3 / 8 L X+40 IY+5 / 9 CHF 12 F250 / 10 L IX+5 Y+0); iTNC 530 Benutzer-Handbuch Klartext-Dialog-Programmierung, NC-SW 340490-04 (2007), p. 252 (RND rounds a corner with an arc tangential to the element before and after it; the input is the rounding radius plus an optional feed that acts only in the RND block, with the same note that the earlier feed applies again afterwards, and that the corner point is not approached); iTNC 530 Benutzer-Handbuch Klartext-Dialog-Programmierung, NC-SW 340490-04 (2007), p. 113 (Incremental coordinates refer to the last programmed position of the tool, which serves as an imaginary relative datum; the same sentence is repeated for incremental polar coordinates); iTNC 530 Benutzer-Handbuch Klartext-Dialog-Programmierung, NC-SW 340490-04 (2007), p. 253 (CC with no coordinates takes the last programmed position, and an incrementally entered circle-centre coordinate always refers to the last programmed tool position. This is the rule RR-P3-05 relies on, stated outright); iTNC 530 NC-Fehlermeldungen (2003), p. 85-86 (Errors 354 and 355, both 'Fase zu groß': the chamfer cannot be inserted because the straight line before, respectively after, the chamfer is too short; error 356 adds the case where the chamfer's start or end point no longer lies on a neighbouring contour element. Errors 351 to 353 on the same pages add that a chamfer may only stand between blocks with the same radius compensation and only in the working plane); TNC 640 User's Manual Klartext Programming, 892903-28, NC-SW 34059x-10 (2019, English), p. 156 (and overview 154) (The English text of the same input is 'Chamfer side length: Length of the chamfer', as ambiguous as the German, and the overview table on page 154 lists 'Chamfer side length'. The figure on page 156 is the identical drawing to the iTNC 530's: the same example, the same two dimensions of 12 along the line before and the line after the corner, the same 40 + 5 chain to the end point. Both control families therefore define the value the same way); Hermle CNC-Seminar Grundkurs iTNC 530, p. 13 (drawing), 15 (program) (The exercise drawing on page 13 dimensions the top-right corner of the part '10 x 45°', with the dimension arrows measuring the vertical leg from the corner down to where the chamfer meets the vertical face; the program on page 15 writes that corner as L X+180 / CHF 10 / L Y+20. So a drawing chamfer '10 x 45°' is programmed CHF 10, which corroborates the leg reading in shop practice).
Settled 2026-10-01: the maintainer let the manual-confirmed answers that agree with their recommendation be applied without reviewing each one.

### Eighth round: needed now

#### D256 Fanuc M29 before G84: part of CYCLE=TAP or a machine function
Question: Three documents treat NCX TAP as rigid tapping. Controller-mapping 5 maps CYCLE=TAP to Fanuc 'G84 (M29 rigid)'. It maps TAP to Heidenhain CYCL DEF 207, which heidenhain 5 calls rigid; tapping with a compensating chuck is the catalog cycle TAP_COMPENSATING (D162). Fanuc 6 says 'M29 S before it makes it rigid'. No rule in fanuc 9 or 10 says how M29 is read or written. The rigid-tapping code is not the same on every Fanuc machine. Controller-mapping 8 (Cycle mode switches) lists M329 synchronous tapping on the Mori Seiki and M35 rigid tapping on the Biglia. The comment of the TAP entry in cycles/fanuc.toml calls M29 'a function of the machine file (a pre rule of an overriding entry, machine-config 5a)'. That is the mechanism language 4.7.1 gives a builder's mode code before a cycle (Doosan M291 before G83). fanuc-mill-30i.toml:135 maps M29 as the [func] function RIGID_TAP, so BOHREN.fanuc.nc N3100 'M29 S500' reads as 'RPM=500 FUNC:RIGID_TAP=ON' (Expected/BOHREN.ncx:323). heidenhain-itnc530.toml has no such function, so compiling Expected/BOHREN.ncx for the iTNC 530 reports the ERROR VM006. Both HeidenhainCompilerTests (line 69) and RoundTrips take the block out before compiling (WithoutRigidTap). HeidenhainReaderTests lists the block as a difference, because BOHREN.h has none.
Recommendation: Treat the rigid-tapping line directly before a G84 as part of CYCLE=TAP, which is rigid tapping on every family. Take that line from the catalog, not from code in the reader. Controller-mapping 8 shows that the code belongs to the builder (M29 on the standard Fanuc, M329 on the Mori Seiki, M35 on the Biglia), and machine-config keeps what differs between machines in the machine file. Add an optional catalog entry key to machine-config 6, `before = "M29 S{rpm}"`. It is a native line that the compiler writes directly before the cycle block and that the reader folds into the cycle when it finds it there. cycles/fanuc.toml gives it to TAP. A machine file overrides it key by key (D140) with its builder's code. Where a parameter makes G84 rigid without any code, the machine file sets it to "" (our reading of the Fanuc manual, not in the documents). The Fanuc reader writes RPM=n only where n differs from the running speed. fanuc 9 and 10 each get one rule. RIGID_TAP ON leaves [func] in fanuc-mill-30i.toml and in both copies of nakamura-ntjx.toml. Both copies of doosan-puma-2600sy.toml keep REVERSE_ON and REVERSE_OFF under a name of their own. Line 323 leaves Expected/BOHREN.ncx, which removes both acceptance exceptions. Reasons: one tapping gets one text from both sources (language 2 rules 1 and 7), a program read from Fanuc compiles for every family, the template writes the S that M29 needs in its block, and the builder codes of controller-mapping 8 need no change to the reader. As a consequence, on a machine whose TAP entry names such a line, a G84 without it is tapping with a compensating chuck. That becomes TAP_COMPENSATING once the Fanuc catalog has that entry (D162). Alternative: the mechanism that language 4.7.1 and machine-config 5a give a mode code before a cycle, which the TAP comment in cycles/fanuc.toml names. The TAP entry carries pre = ["FUNC:RIGID_TAP=ON"], and the reader folds it back. That keeps the function and needs no new key, but it depends on D204 and D231 and cannot write the S that M29 needs in its block.
Where: controllers/fanuc.md 6, 9, 10; controller-mapping 5 (TAP row, unchanged) and 8 (Cycle mode switches row, cited); language 4.7.1 (mode code sentence); machine-config 6 (new entry key) and 5a; cycles/fanuc.toml TAP entry (comment at line 61); machines/fanuc-mill-30i.toml:135, machines/nakamura-ntjx.toml:239, docs/spec/examples/machines/nakamura-ntjx.toml:239, machines/doosan-puma-2600sy.toml:213, docs/spec/examples/machines/doosan-puma-2600sy.toml:213; src/Ncx.Core/Machine/CycleEntry.cs and src/Ncx.Config/Cycles/CycleCatalogLoader.Entries.cs (s_entryKeys); src/Ncx.Readers/Fanuc/FanucFunction.cs and FanucCycles.cs; src/Ncx.Compilers/Fanuc/FanucCycles.cs and FanucLine.cs; tests/Ncx.Acceptance/Expected/BOHREN.ncx:323; tests/Ncx.Acceptance/Examples/HeidenhainCompilerTests.cs:69 (WithoutRigidTap), tests/Ncx.Acceptance/RoundTrips.cs:169, tests/Ncx.Acceptance/Examples/HeidenhainReaderTests.cs:71; the M29 tests of FanucCyclesTests, FanucToolWordsTests and FanucBuilderTests, and the test machines in FanucRead.cs and FanucCompile.cs.

ANSWER:
As recommended, confirmed from the manual library: Treat the rigid-tapping line as part of CYCLE=TAP with a catalog key `before = "M29 S{rpm}"`, as recommended; the manuals back every part of it. Fanuc gives three ways into the mode — M29 S before the tapping block, M29 S in the same block, or G84/G88 alone when parameter 5200 bit 0 is set, which is the documented `before = ""` case — and an S word or an axis motion between M29 and G84 raises alarm PS0203, so the line must stand immediately before the cycle block. The consequence the draft predicts is spelled out by the builder: Doosan writes that a G84/G88 cycle without the M29 code runs as normal (compensating-chuck) tapping. On Nakamura the spindle is started with M29 S instead of M3/M4 and M29 may only be given with the spindle stopped, so the template must always carry its own S.
Evidence: Fanuc Series 30i/31i/32i-B, Bedienung Fräsen, B-64484GE-2/02, p. 109 (printed 93), "Modus Gewindebohren ohne Ausgleichsfutter" (Three ways to enter rigid tapping: M29 S***** before a tapping command, M29 S***** in the same block as the tapping command, or G84 as the rigid-tapping code with parameter 5200 bit 0 set to 1); Fanuc Series 30i/31i/32i-B, Bedienung Fräsen, B-64484GE-2/02, p. 111 (printed 95), "- M29" and the worked example (An S command and an axis-motion command between M29 and G84 produce alarm PS0203; M29 inside a running tapping cycle produces PS0204. The example is `M29 S1000;` followed by `G84 Z-100.0 R-20.0 F1000;`, with the pitch equal to feed divided by speed under G94 and equal to the feed under G95); Fanuc Series 30i/31i/32i-B, Betriebshandbuch Drehen, B-64484GE-1/02, p. 113 (printed 97) and 116 (printed 100) (The same three entries for the lathe, naming G84 and G88, and the example `M29 S1000;` before `G84 Z-100.0 R-20.0 F1000;` under G98 and `F1.0` under G99); Doosan Puma MX/TT, Programming Manual Turning-Milling, MXTTPGE68, p. 116 (printed 115), section 9.2 (M29 is the rigid-tapping M code; it "must be used before commanding G-code"; "M29 S**** : spindle speed in rigid tapping is set by S-code. Single command in a block"; it must be executed in G97 and G98 mode and alarms in G96; and "G84(G88) cycle that don't use the M29 code will be activated with normal tapping"); Nakamura-Tome Precision Turning Center Programmierhandbuch 1, 4810004ECL-1, p. 294 to 296, chapter 17 STARRES GEWINDEBOHREN (The programmed sequence is M29 S1000, then G84 or G88 with Z/X, R, F and P, then G80. "Die Spindeldrehzahl mit dem Befehl M29 anstelle des Befehls M3 programmieren. Hierbei wird M3 oder M4 nicht benötigt." M29 may only be programmed with the spindle (or milling axis) stopped. On the MATA-BEI sub spindle M29 replaces M53, and M53/M54 are then not needed. The M-code table of 17-4 lists M29, M86, M94, M792/M793, M794/M795); Nakamura-Tome Programmierhandbuch (Walter Meier, 2019), p. 23 (M-code list) and 76 (M29 is rigid tapping on the upper path and M429 on the lower path. Page 76: "Beim Gewindeschneiden ohne Ausgleichsfutter wird die Spindel mit M29 S.... gestartet. Die Funktionen M03 / M04 / M88 / M89 / M488 oder M489 dürfen nicht verwendet werden"; the cycle must be cleared with G80 before moving to the change point; M29 only with the spindle stopped); Mori Seiki NT/NTX-Serie, Programmieranleitung NT-NTX (2017), p. 246 (M-code list, referring to 476); section titles on 21; examples on 291 and 304 (Page 246: "M329 Modus für Spindel-Synchrongewindebohren aktiviert". The chapter title reads "M329 G84 (G84.2) Zyklus zum Flächen-Synchrongewindebohren, M329 G88 (G84.2) Zyklus zum Seiten-Synchrongewindebohren", and the worked programs write `M329 S400;` and `M329 S300;` before the cycle — the same before-the-cycle shape with the builder's own code).
Settled 2026-10-01: the maintainer let the manual-confirmed answers that agree with their recommendation be applied without reviewing each one.
