#### D300 G961 for the G96 of a VC template
Question: Machine-config 5 gives each spindle a VC template, G96 S{value} on millturn1 and dmg-ctx-840d, which D154 recommends reading as CSS=ON VC={value}. G96 switches G95 on (siemens 5). G961 is the constant surface speed with feed per minute (controller-mapping 4, CSS row), and a G94 in a later block would switch the surface speed off, since both are in group 15 (siemens 2). So CSS=ON under FEED_MODE=PER_MIN cannot be written with the template as it stands. No document lets a compiler change the code a template writes; architecture 6 has one template string serve both directions. Main writes a template's G96 or G961 as the code for the feed type the block leaves, and a FEED_MODE change under the surface speed as G96 or G961 alone.
Recommendation: Allow it, as coded, and say so in siemens 12 rule 3 and in the VC comment of machine-config 5. On Siemens the compiler writes a spindle template's group-15 code as the code for the feed type the block leaves: G96 or G961. Once D342 confirms the G97 fact, the same rule gives G97 or G971. Reasons: on this control the feed type and the surface speed are one code, which the program's FEED_MODE decides and no template can know; architecture 8 leaves to the compiler how the machine writes a word; and the reader reads G961 natively, so the round trip holds. Alternative: an optional VC_PER_MIN state in [spindle.ROLE] (G961 S{value}), written under PER_MIN, with an ERROR on a machine that lacks it. Templates then stay verbatim, at the cost of one more key per spindle.
Where: siemens.md 12 rule 3; machine-config 5 ([spindle.ROLE] VC); controller-mapping 4 (CSS row); D154 (VC as CSS=ON VC); src/Ncx.Compilers/Siemens/SiemensSpindles.cs AddToMain (TODO at 298); src/Ncx.Compilers/Siemens/SiemensMotion.cs WriteFeedType, SurfaceSpeedCode; related D342.

ANSWER:
As recommended, confirmed from the manual library: Confirmed, so allow it as coded: on this control G96 is the constant surface speed with feed type G95 (it switches G95 on by itself), G961 the same surface speed with G94, and G97/G971 switch it off with G95/G94 respectively — all of them in G group 15 together with G93/G94/G95, so a later G94 or G95 switches the surface speed off on its own. The Siemens compiler may therefore write a spindle template's group-15 code as the code for the feed type the block leaves (G96 or G961, G97 or G971), and writing the code alone under an unchanged VC is legal because the S value is only required on the first selection. Worth recording in siemens 12 rule 3: the control also has G962 and G972, constant surface speed on/off with feed type G94 or G95, which leave the feed type untouched and are the exact form for a CSS change that must not decide a FEED_MODE.
Evidence: Programmierhandbuch Grundlagen SINUMERIK 840D sl/828D, 03/2013, p. 93 (Section 6.3, Bedeutung: G96 = constant surface speed with feed type G95 ON, and it switches G95 on automatically (a new F is needed if G95 was not active); G961 = the same with feed type G94; G962 = with G94 or G95; G97/G971/G972 switch it off with G95 / G94 / either; G973 switches it off without activating the speed limit. Closing note: on first selection of G96/G961/G962 an S must be given, on re-selection it is optional. Verified verbatim.); Programmierhandbuch Grundlagen SINUMERIK 840D sl/828D, 03/2013, p. 83 ("Interpretation des S-Werts": outside G331/G332 the reading of S depends on G function group 15 (Vorschubtyp) — under G96, G961 or G962 the S value is a constant cutting speed in m/min, in every other case a speed in rev/min. Verified verbatim.); Programmierhandbuch Grundlagen SINUMERIK 840D sl/828D, 03/2013, p. 95 ("Konstante Schnittgeschwindigkeit ausschalten": G96/G961 can also be switched off with G94 or G95, and the last programmed S then counts as a speed again; after G97/G971 the last speed set under G96/G961 is kept if no new one is given; and G97 may be programmed without a preceding G96, in which case it acts like G95 with LIMS available.); Programmierhandbuch Grundlagen SINUMERIK 840D sl/828D, 03/2013, p. 500-501 (Added in review, because no cited page carried the group membership: table 16-14 "Gruppe 15: Vorschubtyp" lists G93, G94, G95, G96, G97, G931, G961, G971, G942, G952, G962, G972 and G973 as the thirteen members of group 15, every one of them modal.).
Settled 2026-10-01: the maintainer let the manual-confirmed answers that agree with their recommendation be applied without reviewing each one.

#### D301 One Siemens D for OFFSET:LEN and OFFSET:RAD
Question: Controller-mapping 3 gives the Siemens D as the cutting edge, with length and radius in one register, which language 4.4 calls OFFSET. MILLTURN_TRANSFER settles equal registers: OFFSET:LEN=3 OFFSET:RAD=3 is 'T3 D3'. No document says how the compiler writes an OFFSET:LEN and an OFFSET:RAD that differ, as a program read from Fanuc can carry them. Main writes the length register, or the radius register where the length is 0, with a WARNING where both are set and differ. Case 1: G43 H1 with G41 D21 (OFFSET:LEN=1, OFFSET:RAD=21) writes D1, so the contour is cut with the radius of edge 1. Case 2: G49 after G40 (OFFSET:LEN=0, OFFSET:RAD still set) writes or keeps D21, so the control keeps a tool length that NCX cancelled. A later G53 retract does not clear it. The corpus writes D0 there (controller-mapping 1, FRAME=MACHINE), but a program read from Fanuc has no OFFSET word in that block, and the compiler writes a D only from OFFSET words.
Recommendation: Keep main's rule and add one case. Equal registers, or a single set register, give that D. Two different registers give the length register with the WARNING, as on main. A block that sets OFFSET:LEN=0 writes D0, because on this control a D always carries the length (main keeps the radius register there). Where COMP is still LEFT or RIGHT after that block, D0 also drops the radius, and the compiler reports a WARNING. Write this in the Siemens cell of the OFFSET:LEN, OFFSET:RAD row of controller-mapping 3. Alternative: an ERROR where a block leaves two different non-zero registers, since the output then cuts with another edge's radius or length.
Where: controller-mapping 3 (OFFSET:LEN, OFFSET:RAD row, Siemens cell); controller-mapping 1 (FRAME=MACHINE); language 4.4 (OFFSET rows); siemens.md 5, 12 rule 3; src/Ncx.Compilers/Siemens/SiemensTools.cs EdgeOf, WriteOffset, ReportTwoRegisters (TODO at 72).

ANSWER:
As recommended, confirmed from the manual library: Confirmed, keep main's rule and add the D0 case. On this control one D activates one correction data record of the active tool — the tool-length data among them — and D0 deactivates that record, so a D0 drops the length and the radius together; a radius offset still needs G41/G42 on top. Two different registers therefore cannot be written in one block at all (TOFFL/TOFF/TOFFR only add an offset to the active record and cannot fetch another edge's values), so writing the length register with the WARNING is right, and the harm the WARNING names is real: the correction record may be changed while compensation is active and a changed tool radius takes effect from the very block the new D stands in.
Evidence: Programmierhandbuch Grundlagen SINUMERIK 840D sl/828D, 03/2013, p. 73 (Section 5.6: calling the D number activates the correction data of one cutting edge, "u. a. die Daten für die Werkzeuglängenkorrektur"; with D0 programmed the tool's corrections are ineffective; a tool radius compensation must additionally be switched on with G41/G42. The Bedeutung table gives D0 as the command to deactivate the correction record of the active tool, value range 0 to 32000. Verified verbatim.); Programmierhandbuch Grundlagen SINUMERIK 840D sl/828D, 03/2013, p. 74 (Continues the same Bedeutung table with G41/G42/G40 and then "Art der D-Programmierung": machine data decide whether the D number is the cutting edge number (1 to max. 12), a freely assigned number, or an absolute number 1 to 32000 with no reference to T. (The answer under review cited this page for the D0 command, which in this edition stands on page 73.)); Programmierhandbuch Grundlagen SINUMERIK 840D sl/828D, 03/2013, p. 265 (Section 10.1, "Wechsel des Werkzeugkorrekturdatensatzes (D…)": the correction record may be changed while compensation is running, and a changed tool radius applies from the block in which the new D number stands. Verified verbatim.); Programmierhandbuch Grundlagen SINUMERIK 840D sl/828D, 03/2013, p. 76 (Section 5.8: TOFFL/TOFF modify the effective tool length and TOFFR the effective radius without changing the correction data held in the correction store, and the offsets are cleared at program end — an offset on the active record, not a way to select a second one. Verified verbatim.); Diagnosehandbuch Sinumerik 840D sl/840D/840Di/810D (DA), 08/2005, p. 196 (Alarm 14090 "unzulaessige D-Nummer": every active tool automatically has one parameter set of 25 correction values, each tool may have nine sets D1 to D9 (D1 the default); changing the D number makes the new parameter set effective, and D0 serves to deselect the correction values. Verified verbatim.); Diagnosehandbuch Sinumerik 840D sl/840D/840Di/810D (DA), 08/2005, p. 116-117 (Alarm 10750: the cutter radius compensation is computed when G41 or G42 is programmed, from parameter P6 (geometry) and P15 (wear) "des aktiven Korrekturdatensatzes Dx" — the radius always comes from the record the active D selected. Verified verbatim.).
Settled 2026-10-01: the maintainer let the manual-confirmed answers that agree with their recommendation be applied without reviewing each one.

#### D312 Words bound to every channel that several channel programs write
Question: Machine-config 5 (channels = "all") and VM 3.8 rule 2a want the word "in every channel program behind a wait". D56 has the job compiler duplicate it and insert the SYNC it needs, and VM 3.7 pairs marks in execution order. Three cases are open. (a) Every channel program already writes the word between the same two marks, as a Mori Seiki job read from its sources does (machine-builders.md: M35 and M34 "written in both programs after a wait code"). Main leaves the words as they stand. (b) Two channels write such words between the same two marks, or both before every mark, e.g. M96 in channel 1 and M70 in channel 2 between M110 and M111. Placing every copy directly after the mark made each program command the other channel's word first, so the paths commanded M70 and M96 at the same wait. Main reports CMP705 on the second channel's words. (c) D56 binds the table, so main duplicates every state of [spindle_sync], M36 too, and a single-file compile reports CMP701 on M36. The comment of mori-ntx1000-mapps.toml (docs/spec/examples/machines and machines/) says instead "M36 in either one".
Recommendation: (a) Keep main. A word that every channel program of the job writes, with the same canonical text, between the same two marks already stands behind that wait and is not duplicated. (b) Keep the ERROR CMP705. An automatic order does exist: take the manifest's channel order, keep each channel's own words in place behind their generated SYNC, put the copies of an earlier channel's words directly after the mark, and put those of a later channel after the channel's own last such word. The generated SYNCs then pair. But that order is one the author did not write, it makes a channel wait for another in the middle of the section, and the case is rare. One SYNC that the author writes between the two words states the order. Write (a) and (b) into VM 3.8 rule 2a. (c) is a machine fact. If the NTX accepts M36 from one path alone, machine-config 5 needs a way to bind only some states of a table (for example ON and PHASE), and D198's open states key is a model for it. Otherwise the comment of the example file drops "M36 in either one". Reason: (a) lets a Mori Seiki job read from its sources write M34 and M35 back without extra waits. M36 depends on (c). Alternative for (b): the automatic order above, written into VM 3.8 rule 2a.
Where: VM 3.8 rule 2a; machine-config 5 (channels = "all"); mori-ntx1000-mapps.toml [spindle_sync] comment (docs/spec/examples/machines and machines/). Code: src/Ncx.Compilers/JobCompiler.Binding.cs:121 (Duplicate, StandsInEveryChannel) and :163 (DuplicatedByAnotherChannel, CMP705); src/Ncx.Compilers/ChannelBinding.cs (BoundTableOf, per table); tests/Ncx.Compilers.Tests/Jobs/JobBindingTests.cs.

ANSWER:
As recommended, confirmed from the manual library: The manuals settle (a) and (c) and back the ERROR in (b). (a) Keep main: Mori Seiki requires the same synchronized-operation M code (M34, M35) in both the tool-spindle and the turret-2 program, with the program-execution synchronization M code in the block immediately preceding it, and the worked transfer program writes M100 then M34 in both columns — words that every channel already writes between the same two marks must be left as they stand. (c) The example file's comment is right and machine-config 5 needs a way to bind only some states of a table: Mori Seiki says plainly that M36 is to be specified in either the tool-spindle or the turret-2 program and that it is not necessary to specify it in both, and its transfer example writes M36 in one path only; Nakamura says the same for its pair — M442 and M443 go in the upper or the lower turret program, entering them in both is superfluous, and M443 must not be programmed on the opposite turret side. (b) Keep CMP705: since the machine wants the bound word in the block immediately after the wait, only one channel's word can hold that place, so an order NCX invents would break the rule and the author has to write the SYNC. One detail of an earlier draft is wrong: in the transfer example M36 stands in the turret-2 column, not the tool-spindle column (the columns are at x=31 and x=297 in the PDF, and M36 is at x=297; the page header says left is the tool spindle, right turret 2). That does not change the finding — the code appears in one program only. Mori's notes 4 and 5 are marked "(NT-SZ, NT-SZM)" and note 1 restricts M34/M35/M36 to the NT-S, NT-SZ and NT-SZM series; they are printed in the NTX1000SZM manual and repeated unchanged in the 2017 NT/NTX revision. Finally, the claim that this makes D56 wrong in general is too strong: D56 says the compiler moves or duplicates according to the configuration, so a code that belongs in one program simply must not be configured channels = "all". What the Nakamura and Mori pages show is that such codes exist and that the configuration must be able to say so — which is exactly what (c) asks for.
Evidence: Mori Seiki NT/NTX Programmieranleitung NTX1000SZM (PX-NT_4-K0DEEN), p. 539 (Note 4 of section 2-1 requires the same synchronized-operation calling M code (M34, M35) in both the tool-spindle and the turret-2 side programs, and requires the program-execution synchronization M code in the block immediately preceding the one that carries it.); Mori Seiki NT/NTX Programmieranleitung NTX1000SZM (PX-NT_4-K0DEEN), p. 540 (Note 5 states that M36 is to be specified in either the tool-spindle or the turret-2 program when cancelling the synchronized operation of both spindles, and that it is not necessary to specify this M code in both programs.); Mori Seiki NT/NTX Programmieranleitung NTX1000SZM (PX-NT_4-K0DEEN), p. 547-548 (The two-program transfer example prints M100 then M34 in both columns and M101, M102, M103, M104 and M105 in both, whereas M36 appears once only, in the turret-2 column, between the marks M104 and M105 — the on codes duplicated, the off code in one path.); Mori Seiki NT/NTX Programmieranleitung NT/NTX (2017 revision), p. 556-557 (The later revision repeats both notes unchanged: the same M34/M35 in both programs behind a program-synchronization code, and M36 in either program only.); Nakamura-Tome Programmierhandbuch Band 1 (4810004ECL-1), p. 302, 304 (Chapter 19 says the back-milling M code must be entered behind a wait M code in the machining program, that M443 must not be programmed on the opposite turret side and must also stand behind a wait code on the turret side that gave M442; the closing line of example 2 states that M442 and M443 are to be given in the upper or the lower turret program and that entering them in both is superfluous.); Nakamura-Tome Programmierhandbuch Band 1 (4810004ECL-1), p. 303-304 (Both examples put M442 directly after the wait mark M100 in one turret program only, with M101 in both, and M443 after a wait mark in the same program (after M101 in example 1, after M102 in example 2).).
Settled 2026-10-01: the maintainer let the manual-confirmed answers that agree with their recommendation be applied without reviewing each one.

### Eighth round: later

#### D321 WORKPLANE change without a TOOL on Heidenhain
Question: Controller-mapping 1 (WORKPLANE row) and heidenhain 8 rule 3 give the Klartext working plane only as the tool-axis letter of TOOL CALL, taken from the WORKPLANE of the TOOL block or of its following block. Language 4.2 lets WORKPLANE change in any block, and the Fanuc and Siemens readers write it wherever the source switches the plane, for example a G18 before an arc in XZ. HeidenhainToolCall.CheckWorkplane reports CMP110 when a WORKPLANE in a block without TOOL changes the tool axis of the last TOOL CALL. A WORKPLANE in the following block of a TOOL block (HeidenhainToolCall.FollowingBlock) is folded into that call and is not reported. The Heidenhain reader never writes WORKPLANE without TOOL (heidenhain 7 rule 2).
Recommendation: Keep the ERROR, as coded, and state it in heidenhain 8 rule 3: a WORKPLANE that changes the tool axis of the last TOOL CALL needs a TOOL in its own block, or must stand in the following block of a TOOL block (the rule of D275). Reason: the only other Klartext form in the documents is a TOOL CALL, with the new axis, of the tool already in the spindle. That re-calls the tool, which may run the builder's change macro and resets DL and DR (the cost D180 describes for a speed change). Whether the iTNC 530 accepts a TOOL CALL without a tool number is D180's open fact. Alternative: once D180 confirms what a re-call does, write TOOL CALL {tool} {axis} S{rpm} for the tool in the spindle through the change template. Answer together with D180.
Where: heidenhain.md 8 rule 3; controller-mapping 1 (WORKPLANE row). Code: src/Ncx.Compilers/Heidenhain/HeidenhainToolCall.cs CheckWorkplane (TODO(question) at line 137) and WriteChange. Related: D180, D275.

ANSWER:
As recommended, confirmed from the manual library: Keep the ERROR, as coded, and state it in heidenhain 8 rule 3: a WORKPLANE that changes the tool axis of the last TOOL CALL needs a TOOL in its own block, or must stand in the following block of a TOOL block (D275). Both Klartext manuals say it outright - "the principal plane is to be defined at the tool call TOOL CALL by fixing the spindle axis" - and there is no other Klartext block that sets it; DIN/ISO mode says the same and writes the plane code inside the tool call (T1 G17 S2000 = "tool call, tool axis Z"). D180's open fact is settled with it: a TOOL CALL without tool name and number is accepted and changes only the speed when the tool axis is absent or unchanged, but the same block with a changed tool-axis direction runs the tool-change macro, so the re-call form exists and costs a tool change.
Evidence: Benutzer-Handbuch HEIDENHAIN-Klartext-Dialog (iTNC 530, NC-SW 340490-04), p. 239 (In the path-function basics: arcs are programmed in the principal planes, and "Die Hauptebene ist beim Werkzeug-Aufruf TOOL CALL mit dem Festlegen der Spindelachse zu definieren", with the table spindle axis Z -> XY, Y -> ZX, X -> YZ. Circles outside that plane need the tilt function or Q parameters); Benutzerhandbuch Klartextprogrammierung (TNC 640), p. 141 (The same sentence on the TNC 640: the principal plane is to be defined at the tool call TOOL CALL by fixing the spindle axis, with the same Z/Y/X table); Benutzerhandbuch Klartextprogrammierung (TNC 640), p. 128 (Two lists. The control changes only the speed for a TOOL CALL without name, number and tool axis, or without name and number but with the same tool axis as the previous TOOL CALL. It runs the tool-change macro, and may change in a replacement tool, for a TOOL CALL with a number, with a name, or without name or number but with a changed tool-axis direction); Benutzer-Handbuch HEIDENHAIN-Klartext-Dialog (iTNC 530, NC-SW 340490-04), p. 197 (To change the spindle speed alone you program a TOOL CALL and pass the tool-number dialog and the "Spindelachse parallel X/Y/Z" dialog with NO ENT. So a TOOL CALL without a tool number is a documented iTNC 530 form, and the tool axis is one of the fields it can leave out); Benutzer-Handbuch HEIDENHAIN-Klartext-Dialog (iTNC 530, NC-SW 340490-04), p. 211 (The tool axis is a field of the TOOL CALL dialog ("Spindelachse parallel X/Y/Z: Werkzeugachse eingeben"), between the tool number and the speed); Benutzer-Handbuch DIN/ISO-Programmierung (iTNC 530, NC-SW 340490-04), p. 226 (The same statement in ISO mode: circles are programmed in the principal planes, and the principal plane "ist beim Werkzeug-Aufruf mit dem Festlegen der Spindelachse zu definieren", with the table Z (G17) -> XY, Y (G18) -> ZX, X (G19) -> YZ); Benutzer-Handbuch DIN/ISO-Programmierung (iTNC 530, NC-SW 340490-04), p. 103 (Example block "N20 T1 G17 S2000" annotated "tool call: tool axis Z, spindle speed 2000"; page 432 has "N20 T1 G18 S2000" annotated "tool call, tool axis Y". Throughout the manual G17..G19 appear only inside a T call or inside the G30 blank-form block, never as a plane change of their own).
Settled 2026-10-01: the maintainer let the manual-confirmed answers that agree with their recommendation be applied without reviewing each one.

#### D322 Fanuc code of an external CALL: M98 or M198
Question: Language 4.9 calls an external program by file name (CALL="O9010"). Fanuc 1 has a program in its own file called with M98 and says 'M198 calls a program from external memory'. Controller-mapping 6 (CALL, TIMES row) lists M198 as the external program call of the Mori Seiki. The Fanuc reader reads M198 P9010, and an M98 P9010 whose program is not in the file, alike as CALL="O9010" (FanucMacro.ReadCalls, Target, External). The Fanuc compiler writes every external CALL as M98 P (FanucFlow.WriteCall). The Siemens compiler writes the same CALL as EXTCALL, the Siemens call from external memory (SiemensFlow). Case: a Mori Seiki source with M198 P9010 converts and compiles back for mori-ntx1000-mapps.toml as M98 P9010, which fails when O9010 is not in the control's memory. D215 settles only the file that the VM opens, not the code that calls it.
Recommendation: Keep M98 as the default, since fanuc 1 calls a program in its own file with M98. Add an optional [format] key, for example external_call = "M198": the code that the Fanuc compiler writes in place of M98 for a CALL of a program outside the file, and that the reader reads as CALL. mori-ntx1000-mapps.toml gets it once the maintainer confirms where the called programs of that machine stand. Reason: where a called program is stored is a fact of the machine, not of the NCX program, and an M198 source then survives the round trip. Alternative: always M98. Controller-mapping 6 then says that M198 reads as CALL 'the same as M98 for NCX', as it already says for the Nakamura M200, and an M198 source compiles back as M98.
Where: language 4.9 (CALL row); controller-mapping 6 (CALL, TIMES row); controllers fanuc.md 1 (subprogram bullet); machine-config 2 ([format]); machines/mori-ntx1000-mapps.toml and docs/spec/examples/machines/mori-ntx1000-mapps.toml; src/Ncx.Compilers/Fanuc/FanucFlow.cs WriteCall (TODO(question) at line 194); src/Ncx.Readers/Fanuc/FanucMacro.cs ReadCalls and External; D215.

ANSWER:
As recommended, confirmed from the manual library: Add the key, and treat the code as a machine fact rather than a family default: on Fanuc the M code that calls an external subprogram sits in parameter No. 6030, M198 is only the factory setting, and if a code other than M198 is set there, M198 is executed as an ordinary M code. That is exactly why Nakamura's memory-card setup sets 6030 = 200 and calls with M200 P<repeats><number>, and why M198 on a Nakamura is a builder function inside the M100–M199 range rather than a call — the NTJX header template uses it as the turret rendezvous ("SYNCHRONISATION MIT *U*" / "*O*") and the WY template as the bar-end query. So the key should carry the whole call template, not just a code — Fanuc's own FS16-compatible form is M198 P<repeats><4-digit number> — and the reader may read M198 as CALL only when the machine file says so, never on a machine whose wait range covers 198. mori-ntx1000-mapps.toml gets M198: the NTX1000 M-code list has it (as an option) as the subprogram call in the external I/O device.
Evidence: Fanuc Series 30i/31i/32i-B Betriebshandbuch Drehen/Fräsen (B-64484GE/02), p. 1108–1109 (§4.5 Externer Unterprogrammaufruf (M198), printed p. 1074–1075) (Format M198 Pxxxxxxxx Lyyyyyyyy, or M198 <file name> L, plus an FS16-compatible form M198 Pxxxx yyyy (repeat count then 4-digit program number). The explanation adds that an external subprogram can also be called with an M code set in parameter No. 6030, and that if a code other than M198 is set there, M198 is executed as a normal M code. A program in USB memory cannot be called this way); Nakamura-Tome Programmierhandbuch Band 1 (4810004ECL-1), p. 152 (§8-5 Aufruf eines Unterprogramms von Speicherkarte) (The setup list for the memory-card call names the parameters to confirm for every turret head — Nr. 0020 = 4, Nr. 0138.7 = 1, Nr. 3404.2 = 1, Nr. 6030 = 200 — and the call itself is written M200 P<repeat count><program number>; omitting the count runs the program once); Nakamura-Tome Liste M- und G-Codes NTJX (Walter Meier/KOST, 2016), p. 2 (The NTJX code list: M98 subprogram call, M99 subprogram end, M100 bis M199 Wartefunktionen, M200 "PROGRAMM AUFRUF AB SPEICHERKARTE (USB-STICK)". M198 has no call meaning on this machine; it falls inside the wait range); Nakamura-Tome Programmieranleitung NC-Wort/Adresse, Super NTJX (Fanuc 18i-TB, Walter Meier 2009), p. 19–20 (A real NTJX program header ends with M198 carrying the comment "SYNCHRONISATION MIT *U*" in the upper turret program and "SYNCHRONISATION MIT *O*" in the lower — M198 used as the rendezvous between the two turrets. The WY-series template of the same author (WY manual p. 21) writes M198 with the comment "** STANGEN-END ABFRAGE **"); Mori Seiki NT/NTX Programmieranleitung NTX1000 SZM (PX-NT_4-K0DEEN), p. 236 (M-code list) and 283 (§1-24) (The list has M98 as the subprogram call and M198 (option, ^^) as "Unterprogrammaufruf im externen E/A-Gerät"; M100–M197 are the operation synchronization and M200 the chip conveyor. Page 283 adds that the main program is stored in NC memory, that M198 cannot be executed in DNC operation, that it is not available on the cabinet RS232C interface, that a program on an external device may not call another with M198, and that the called file must be named O plus four (or seven) digits).
Settled 2026-10-01: the maintainer let the manual-confirmed answers that agree with their recommendation be applied without reviewing each one.

#### D326 A MESSAGE word for Siemens MSG
Question: Controller-mapping 1 (COMMENT, SECTION row), 6 (macros row), 9 and 11.1 keep MSG("text") and MSG() as RAW:SIEMENS until a message word exists, and 11.1 names MESSAGE="..." as the candidate. Implementation 15 expects this draft before phase 5 closes. The corpus writes MSG before every operation (273 lines in 47 of the 62 .mpf files). So almost every Siemens program read today carries RAW blocks, and each is an ERROR when compiled for another family (controller-mapping 9), although a message moves nothing.
Recommendation: Add MESSAGE="text" to language 4.1 next to COMMENT and SECTION. It is a block word, an operator message shown at run time, and MESSAGE="" clears it (MSG()). The VM executes nothing for it. The Siemens reader writes MSG("text") as MESSAGE="text"; an MSG built from an expression (<<) stays RAW. The Siemens compiler writes MSG("text"). A compiler without a message form writes the text as a comment, as SECTION is written on the controls without * - (language 4.1). Reason: the text survives every conversion and comes back as MSG on Siemens. Alternative: read MSG as COMMENT="text" and add no word. The message then comes back to Siemens as a comment that the screen no longer shows.
Where: language 4.1 (new row) and 5 rule 6 (rank next to COMMENT, SECTION); controller-mapping 1 (COMMENT, SECTION row), 6 (macros row), 9, 11.1; controllers/siemens.md 11 rule 8, 12; implementation 15 (decisions list, exit checklist). Code: src/Ncx.Readers/Siemens/SiemensRaw.cs Statements (TODO at 70); the word catalog in src/Ncx.Core/Catalog and docs/spec/generated/word-catalog.md; the compilers (P3-04, P3-06, P5-02).

ANSWER:
As recommended, confirmed from the manual library: Add MESSAGE="text" as recommended; every Siemens fact the draft needs holds. MSG("<text>") outputs an arbitrary string from the part program as an operator message, MSG() without a text clears the current one, and without clearing the display stays until the next message arrives — so MESSAGE="" is the right clear form and the word is modal, not block-scoped. Two details belong in the language 4.1 row: the text is at most 124 characters, shown in two lines of 62; and MSG takes an optional second argument, MSG("text",1), which forces a main-run block of its own and interrupts continuous-path mode, so an MSG carrying that argument — like one built with the concatenation operator << — has no MESSAGE form and stays RAW.
Evidence: Programmierhandbuch Grundlagen SINUMERIK 840D sl/828D, 03/2013, p. 367 (Section 14.1 "Meldung ausgeben (MSG)": syntax MSG("<Meldungstext>"[,<Ausführung>]) and MSG(); the text is any string, maximum 124 characters displayed in two lines of 62, and may carry variables through the operator <<; <Ausführung> 0 (default) writes no main-run block of its own and does not break continuous path, 1 creates its own main-run block and interrupts it; MSG() without a text clears the current message, and without clearing, the display stays until the next message arrives. Verified verbatim.); Programmierhandbuch Grundlagen SINUMERIK 840D sl/828D, 03/2013, p. 368 (Examples: N20 MSG("Bearbeitung Teil 1") with the note that the message is only output with N30 and continuous path is kept; N410 MSG("Bearbeitung Teil 2",1) with the note that continuous path is interrupted; N900 MSG() to clear; and MSG("Position der X-Achse"<<R12<<"prüfen") for a message built from a variable. Verified verbatim.); Programmierhandbuch Grundlagen SINUMERIK 840D sl/828D, 03/2013, p. 440 (Statement list: the MSG row gives type P (predefined procedure), meaning "Programmierbare Meldungen", effect column "m" (modal), programmable in the part program, not in synchronous actions, described on page 367. Verified verbatim.).
Settled 2026-10-01: the maintainer let the manual-confirmed answers that agree with their recommendation be applied without reviewing each one.

#### D327 Place and name of a Siemens REPEAT range lowered to a SUB
Question: The REPEAT + TIMES row of controller-mapping 6 reads REPEAT start end P=k as 'a block range, lowered to a SUB'. The reader does the same for REPEATB and for REPEAT label P= with ENDLABEL when the range does not end right before the repeat. The row does not say whether the range leaves its place, with the SUB called there and at the repeat, or stays where it stands with the SUB a copy. Nor does it say how the SUB is named. Since the P5-01 review fixes, the structure pass leaves the blocks in place, copies them into a SUB named REPEAT_<first>_<last> (REPEAT_<label> for REPEATB) behind the program, and writes CALL=REPEAT_START_END TIMES=k. A range with a jump, a call, an end or a nested repeat stays RAW. The open D254 (1) recommends the other form for a Klartext LBL section that the flow runs through: the section becomes a SUB, called where it stood.
Recommendation: Keep the copy and the name, as coded, and say so in the REPEAT + TIMES row. Reason: the blocks are read where the control first runs them, with the state they have there, and the SUB needs to agree only with the state of its repeats (D225), so fewer blocks stay RAW. REPEAT_<first label>_<last label>, made unique in the file, tells where the range comes from. Answer D254 (1) the same way, or record why the Klartext section differs. Alternative: move the range into the SUB and call it where it stood as well, as D254 (1) recommends. Every block then stands once in the file, but the in-place pass becomes one more call whose state the SUB must agree with.
Where: controller-mapping 6 (REPEAT + TIMES row); controllers/siemens.md 11 rule 6; D254 (1). Code: src/Ncx.Readers/StructurePass.Repeats.cs FindRepeats (TODO at 26), StructurePass.Contours.cs NewSectionName; src/Ncx.Readers/Siemens/SiemensFlow.cs ReadRepeat; tests/Ncx.Readers.Tests/Siemens/SiemensFlowTests.cs RepeatOfARange_BecomesASubSectionAndItsCall.

ANSWER:
As recommended, confirmed from the manual library: Keep the copy and the place, as coded. On the control the marked range stays where it stands and is executed there first, and the REPEAT then runs it again: the manual's own example drills the hole positions in place with the centre drill and repeats the same ranges later, after the drill and the tap have been changed in — exactly the state difference the copy form is built for. The control also occupies one subprogram level per repetition and shows it as a subprogram level of its own, which is what the lowering to a SUB models. The RAW cases are the control's own limits: an M17 or RET inside a repetition aborts it and the program continues after the REPEAT line, and mixing jumps with repetitions makes the blocks be processed purely sequentially.
Evidence: Programmierhandbuch Arbeitsvorbereitung SINUMERIK 840D sl/828D, 03/2013, p. 102-104 (Section 1.11 gives the four forms (REPEATB line, label to REPEAT, label to label, label to ENDLABEL); the line carrying the label may stand before or after the REPEAT/REPEATB (searched towards the program start first); P is the address for the repetition count, "Der zu wiederholende Programmteil wird <n> mal wiederholt", without P=<n> it is repeated exactly once, and after the last repetition the program continues with the line following the REPEAT/REPEATB line. Verified verbatim.); Programmierhandbuch Arbeitsvorbereitung SINUMERIK 840D sl/828D, 03/2013, p. 106-107 (Example 5: N10 ZENTRIERBOHRER(), then the ranges POS_1 (N20-N70 ENDLABEL) and POS_2 (N80-N120 ENDLABEL) of hole positions are run where they stand, then N130 BOHRER() and N140 GEWINDE(6) change the tool and N150 REPEAT POS_1 runs the same blocks again, followed by N160 BOHRER(), N170 GEWINDE(8) and N180 REPEAT POS_2 — the range is executed in place and repeated with a different state. Example 4 on page 106 is the P=3 / P=2 case whose comments read "dreimal aus" / "zweimal aus".); Programmierhandbuch Arbeitsvorbereitung SINUMERIK 840D sl/828D, 03/2013, p. 107 ("Weitere Informationen": repetitions may be nested and each call occupies one subprogram level; the repetition is shown as a subprogram level of its own in the current program display; an M17 or RET during a repetition aborts it and the program continues with the block after the REPEAT line; control structures and repetitions may be combined but should not overlap; mixing jumps with repetitions makes the blocks be processed purely sequentially. Verified verbatim.); Programmierhandbuch Arbeitsvorbereitung SINUMERIK 840D sl/828D, 03/2013, p. 108 (Closing note of section 1.11, after the jump example: "Die REPEAT-Anweisung sollte hinter den Verfahrsätzen stehen." Verified verbatim. (The answer under review carried a first evidence entry with the Grundlagen path and the page "see the Arbeitsvorbereitung entry below"; it cites nothing and is struck.)).
Settled 2026-10-01: the maintainer let the manual-confirmed answers that agree with their recommendation be applied without reviewing each one.

### Eighth round: controller and machine facts to confirm

#### D334 Sign of DPR and SDIS in the SINUMERIK drilling cycles
Question: Controller-mapping 5 (CYCLE81 cell; the DEPTH, CLEARANCE row) and the header of cycles/siemens.toml give DEPTH = RFP + DPR and CLEARANCE = RFP + SDIS ('unsigned, added to RFP'). The reader computes them that way (SiemensCycles.CycleReading.Relative). As far as we know, the SINUMERIK cycles take DPR without a sign as the depth below RFP, and the cycle drills away from RTP. If so, CYCLE81(10,0,2,,15) drills to Z-15 and main reads it as DEPTH=15. The same direction question applies to SDIS where RTP lies below RFP; the compiler then writes a negative SDIS (CycleEntry.ToNative).
Recommendation: Confirm this in the 840D sl manual 3.25, together with D181. If confirmed, DEPTH = RFP - DPR and CLEARANCE = RFP + SDIS where RTP lies above RFP, with both signs reversed where it lies below. The reader keeps the call RAW where RTP and RFP are not both numbers and the direction is needed. The compiler writes DP as now and writes SDIS as the distance |CLEARANCE - SURFACE|, with an ERROR where CLEARANCE and SAFE lie on opposite sides of SURFACE. Controller-mapping 5, siemens 7 and the header of the catalog say so. Alternative, if the manual shows a signed DPR: keep main and remove the marker.
Where: controller-mapping 5 (CYCLE81 cell; DEPTH, CLEARANCE row); siemens.md 7 (CYCLE81 row); cycles/siemens.toml header; src/Ncx.Readers/Siemens/SiemensCycles.cs CycleReading.Relative (TODO line 369) and the absolute_from_surface sum; src/Ncx.Compilers/Siemens/SiemensCycles.cs ValueOf; src/Ncx.Core/Machine/CycleEntry.cs ToNative.

ANSWER:
As recommended, confirmed from the manual library: Confirmed, so take the recommendation. SDIS and DPR are both entered without a sign; DPR is the final drilling depth relative to the reference plane and the cycle works the resulting depth out itself from where the reference and retract planes lie, while the safety distance moves the reference plane forward in a direction the cycle determines automatically. The cycle assumes the retract plane lies before the reference plane, that is farther from the depth; identical planes, or a retract plane behind the reference plane, give error 61101 "Referenzebene falsch definiert" and the cycle does not run. So DEPTH = RFP − DPR and CLEARANCE = RFP + SDIS where RTP lies above RFP, with both signs reversed where it lies below; the reader keeps the call RAW where RTP and RFP are not both numbers, and the compiler writes SDIS as |CLEARANCE − SURFACE| with the ERROR where CLEARANCE and SAFE lie on opposite sides of SURFACE. The manual's own example proves the arithmetic: CYCLE81(110,100,2,,65) is the same hole as CYCLE81(110,100,2,35).
Evidence: Programmierhandbuch Zyklen SINUMERIK 840D sl/840D/840Di sl, 01/2008, p. 44 (Section 2.1.3, parameter table of CYCLE81 (RTP, RFP, SDIS, DP, DPR): RTP Rückzugsebene (absolut), RFP Referenzebene (absolut), SDIS Sicherheitsabstand "ohne Vorzeichen einzugeben", DP Endbohrtiefe (absolut), DPR Endbohrtiefe relativ zur Referenzebene, likewise "ohne Vorzeichen einzugeben". Verified verbatim.); Programmierhandbuch Zyklen SINUMERIK 840D sl/840D/840Di sl, 01/2008, p. 46 ("RFP und RTP": the cycle assumes the retract plane lies before the reference plane, so its distance to the final depth is the larger one; with identical values for reference and retract plane a relative depth entry is not admissible and error 61101 "Referenzebene falsch definiert" is issued without running the cycle, and the same error appears when the retract plane lies after the reference plane. Verified verbatim.); Programmierhandbuch Zyklen SINUMERIK 840D sl/840D/840Di sl, 01/2008, p. 47 ("SDIS": the safety distance acts with respect to the reference plane, which is moved forward by that amount, and the direction in which it acts is determined automatically by the cycle. "DP und DPR": the final depth may be given absolutely (DP) or relative to the reference plane (DPR), and on a relative entry the cycle computes the resulting depth itself from the positions of the reference and retract planes; if both are given the depth is derived from DPR. Verified verbatim.); Programmierhandbuch Zyklen SINUMERIK 840D sl/840D/840Di sl, 01/2008, p. 45 (Worked example with the drilling axis Z: N40 CYCLE81(110,100,2,35) drills to the absolute depth 35 from RFP 100 with SDIS 2; N60 CYCLE81(110,102,,35) reaches the same start plane without SDIS by raising RFP to 102; N90 CYCLE81(110,100,2,,65) drills the same hole relatively, i.e. 100 − 65 = 35. Verified verbatim.).
Settled 2026-10-01: the maintainer let the manual-confirmed answers that agree with their recommendation be applied without reviewing each one.

#### D335 CYCLE800 angle modes against TILT
Question: Language 4.2 defines TILT as rotations about X, Y and Z of the frame where the word stands, in that order, and names 'CYCLE800 with spatial angles' as its Siemens form. Controller-mapping 1 (TILT row) and siemens 4 give only the _MODE codes: axis-wise with the order in bits 5..0 (27 = Z Y X, 57 = X Y Z in controller-mapping 1), 01 spatial, 10 projection. Controller-mapping 11 calls modes 27 and 39 'TILT with the angles in the order the mode gives'. The TILT_ON examples (machine-config 5, millturn1.toml, dmg-ctx-840d.toml) write TILT as mode 57. So the documents name three different modes as the form of TILT. No document says whether the axis-wise rotations turn about the fixed axes or about the ones already rotated. None says whether _A, _B, _C are the angles about X, Y, Z or about the first, second and third axis of the order. Nor do they say what the spatial and projection angles are, or whether the reader converts. Main writes TILT unchanged for mode 57, for mode 01 and for any order with at most one non-zero angle, and keeps the rest RAW (SiemensTilt.Entry). Suppose the axis-wise rotations build on each other and _A, _B, _C turn about X, Y, Z. Then mode 27 (Z, Y', X'') is TILT and 57 is not. CYCLE800(0,"TC1",0,57,0,0,0,30,45,0,0,0,0,-1,,1) is then read as a different plane from the one it means, and TILT A=30 B=45 is compiled as one.
Recommendation: Confirm the following from the 840D sl manual (CYCLE800, swivel plane): the rotation sense of each mode, what _A, _B and _C name, and the definitions of the solid and projection angles. Then the TILT_ON examples use the mode that equals TILT, and the TILT row of language 4.2 names that mode instead of 'CYCLE800 with spatial angles'. The reader converts every other axis-wise order, and the solid and projection angles, into TILT's A, B, C through the rotation matrix, as FanucTilt.SpatialAngles converts the Euler angles of G68.2 (computed angles keep at least three decimals). This matches what controller-mapping 1 already says for the other Heidenhain PLANE forms ('converted or RAW'). Reason: one plane is one TILT, whatever convention the source uses. Alternative: keep RAW every mode except the one that equals TILT, and keep the one-angle exception only if _A, _B, _C prove to be the angles about X, Y, Z.
Where: language 4.2 (TILT row); controller-mapping 1 (TILT row), 11 (CYCLE800 sentence); siemens.md 4; machine-config 5 ([transform] TILT_ON comment); machines/millturn1.toml:228, machines/dmg-ctx-840d.toml:282 and their copies in docs/spec/examples/machines; src/Ncx.Readers/Siemens/SiemensTilt.cs Entry (TODO line 149); src/Ncx.Compilers/Siemens/SiemensFrames.cs WriteTilt; precedent src/Ncx.Readers/Fanuc/FanucTilt.cs SpatialAngles.

ANSWER:
As recommended, confirmed from the manual library: The axis-wise CYCLE800 rotations build on each other (each turns about the already rotated axis) and the order is the one the _MODE bit pairs give; _A, _B and _C are the first, second and third rotation angle of that order, not the angles about X, Y and Z. No page says that last part in words - the parameter table calls all three plainly "Achswinkel" - but it is the only reading under which the two worked CYCLE800 calls in the library come out right, and it is what the figure's "Drehwinkel 1 / 2 / 3" labels name. Mode 27 is therefore intrinsic Z, Y', X'' and is exactly NCX `TILT`, with `A` = _C, `B` = _B, `C` = _A (Heidenhain PLANE SPATIAL is the same rotation: SPA, SPB, SPC about the unrotated X, Y, Z, i.e. intrinsic Z, Y', X''). Mode 57 (intrinsic X, Y', Z'') is the reverse convention and is not TILT unless at most one angle is non-zero, and the Siemens 'Raumwinkel' mode (bits 7..6 = 01) is not TILT either: it is only two angles, Z by _A then Y' by _B, which is `TILT A=0 B=_B C=_A`. So the TILT_ON templates must write mode 27 with the angles reversed, `CYCLE800(1,"TC1",0,27,0,0,0,{c},{b},{a},0,0,0,{dir},100,1)`, the reader must convert every other axis-wise order and the projection angles through the rotation matrix, and main's mode-57 pass-through, its mode-01 pass-through and its one-angle exception all go (the exception is safe only for an order that starts with X: under mode 27 with only _A non-zero main writes `TILT A=_A` where the plane is `TILT C=_A`).
Evidence: SINUMERIK 840D sl / 840D / 840Di sl – Zyklen, Programmierhandbuch 01/2008, p. 217-218 (Swivelling can be axis-wise, by projection angles, by spatial angles or with the rotary axes direct. Axis-wise means turning about the single axes of the coordinate system one after another, and each rotation 'setzt auf die vorherige auf' (builds on the previous one); the order of the axes is freely selectable. With spatial angles the control turns first about Z and then about Y, the second rotation building on the first.); SINUMERIK 840D sl / 840D / 840Di sl – Zyklen, Programmierhandbuch 01/2008, p. 225-226 (Gives the call CYCLE800(_FR, _TC, _ST, _MODE, _X0, _Y0, _Z0, _A, _B, _C, _X1, _Y1, _Z1, _DIR, _FR_I), says _MODE is decimal but coded binary, and gives the worked coding 'Drehung achsweise zyx, Binär 00011011, Dezimal 27'. It adds that bits 0 to 5 have no meaning for the spatial-angle mode, and that in that mode _A is the angle in the XY plane about Z and _B the angle in space about Y.); INDEX / SINUMERIK 840D/840Di/810D/FM-NC – Programmieranleitung Zyklen (PGZ), Ausgabe 10.04, p. 218 (printed 3-218) (The same _MODE figure with a readable text layer: bits 7 and 6 are 00 axis-wise swivel angles (A, B, C), 01 spatial angles (A, B), 10 projection angles (A, B, C). Bits 1-0 belong to 'Drehwinkel 1', bits 3-2 to 'Drehwinkel 2', bits 5-4 to 'Drehwinkel 3', and each pair says 01 rotation about the 1st axis, 10 about the 2nd, 11 about the 3rd. The same page carries the 27 = 'achsweise zyx' example, which is what fixes bits 1-0 as the first rotation: 27 = 00011011 gives 11 there, the 3rd axis, Z.); HELLER HF-Baureihe, Programmieranleitung PA.000105-DE-01 (840D sl), 2019, p. 128 (Gives one and the same swivelled plane two ways. Under the heading '1. Möglichkeit: Rotation um X-90 Grad' it writes CYCLE800(0,"H",100000,54,0,0,0,0,-90,0,0,0,0,-1,,1), where _B carries the -90; mode 54 assigns the second rotation angle to the first axis, X. The second way, headed 'Rundachsen direkt programmieren', is CYCLE800(0,"H",100000,192,0,0,0,-90,0,0,...), which fixes bits 7 and 6 = 11 as the rotary-axes mode. The same page's four 'Winkelfläche bei B0/B90/B180/B270' calls, also mode 54, carry 0/90/180/-90 in _A, the first rotation of the order, which is about Y.); SINUMERIK – Handbuch Formenbau von 3- bis 5-Achs-Simultanfräsen, p. 125 (A five-axis finishing program calls CYCLE800(0,"TABLE",100000,27,0,0,0,288.079,0,-10.196,0,0,0,-1,0,1) at N7 and then positions the machine at N16 with A-10.196 C=DC(+288.079). So under mode 27 the first angle _A is the rotation about Z (the C axis) and the third angle _C the rotation about X (the A axis).); SINUMERIK 840D sl/828D – Bedienhandbuch Fräsen, 03/2013, p. 484 and 488 (The Operate screen form for the swivel cycle. Page 484 repeats the four modes and the sentence that in the axis-wise mode each rotation builds on the previous, order freely selectable. Page 488 lists the input fields: 'Achsreihenfolge' with the six values XYZ, XZY, YXZ, YZX, ZXY, ZYX, and then three angles labelled 'Drehung um X', 'Drehung um Y', 'Drehung um Z'. The screen names the angles by axis, not by their place in the order.); HEIDENHAIN TNC 640 – Benutzerhandbuch Klartextprogrammierung, 10/2019, p. 414-415 (PLANE SPATIAL defines the plane by up to three rotations in the unswivelled workpiece system, swivel order A-B-C: SPA about the unrotated X, SPB about the unrotated Y, SPC about the unrotated Z. The identical view in the other direction is order C-B-A: about the unrotated Z, then about the swivelled Y, then about the swivelled X.).
Settled 2026-10-01: the maintainer let the manual-confirmed answers that agree with their recommendation be applied without reviewing each one.

#### D336 Comparison words of FN 10 and FN 11
Question: Heidenhain 6 writes FN 9 as IF +Q1 EQU +Q3 GOTO LBL 5 and names FN 10 (unequal), FN 11 (greater) and FN 12 (less) without their words. Only the comment in PATTERN_LOOP.ncx shows LT for FN 12. HeidenhainFlow.Condition writes FN 10: IF a NE b and FN 11: IF a GT b. The reader takes the comparison from the FN number and ignores the word (Ncx.Readers HeidenhainFlow.ReadJump), so only the compiled text depends on the answer.
Recommendation: Confirm from the iTNC 530 manual (jumps with FN 9 to FN 12). Our reading, which is not in the documents: FN 10: IF +a NE +b GOTO LBL n and FN 11: IF +a GT +b GOTO LBL n, as coded. Heidenhain 6 then gives all four forms, and the marker becomes a comment. If the manual shows other words, only the strings in Condition change.
Where: heidenhain.md 6. Code: src/Ncx.Compilers/Heidenhain/HeidenhainFlow.cs Condition (TODO(question) at line 190).

ANSWER:
As recommended, confirmed from the manual library: The words are as coded: FN 9 EQU, FN 10 NE, FN 11 GT, FN 12 LT, with the sign written on both values - FN 10: IF +10 NE -Q5 GOTO LBL 10, FN 11: IF+Q1 GT+10 GOTO LBL 5, FN 12: IF+Q5 LT+0 GOTO LBL "ANYNAME". Heidenhain 6 then gives all four forms and the marker in HeidenhainFlow.Condition becomes a comment.
Evidence: Benutzer-Handbuch HEIDENHAIN-Klartext-Dialog (iTNC 530, NC-SW 340490-04), p. 609 (Section 11.6 lists the four jump softkeys with one example block each: FN 9 WENN GLEICH with EQU, FN 10 WENN UNGLEICH with NE, FN 11 WENN GROESSER with GT, FN 12 WENN KLEINER with LT, each of the form IF <value> <word> <value> GOTO LBL <label>. The page also glosses the abbreviations and gives an unconditional jump as FN 9: IF+10 EQU+10 GOTO LBL1); Benutzer-Handbuch HEIDENHAIN-Klartext-Dialog (iTNC 530, NC-SW 606420-01), p. 301 (The same four rows on the newest iTNC 530 software level, with the abbreviation list (EQU, NE, GT, LT, GOTO) and with the jump address also allowed as a label name or a QS parameter); Benutzer-Handbuch HEIDENHAIN-Klartext-Dialog (iTNC 530, NC-SW 340490-04), p. 662 (A worked Q-parameter example program (KUGEL) using the words in real blocks: "FN 11: IF +Q24 GT +Q5 GOTO LBL 2", "FN 12: IF +Q28 LT +Q9 GOTO LBL 1", "FN 9: IF +Q28 EQU +Q9 GOTO LBL 1").
Settled 2026-10-01: the maintainer let the manual-confirmed answers that agree with their recommendation be applied without reviewing each one.

#### D337 Feed per minute at the start of a Klartext program
Question: The compiler's target state starts unknown in every program (P3-03), so the FEED_MODE=PER_MIN of the complete header (D34) is written as M137. Neither 2.5D_FRAESEN.h nor BOHREN.h writes it, and the P3-04 acceptance lists it as an exception (HeidenhainCompilerTests). Heidenhain 2 lists M136/M137 only as feed per revolution and does not say what is active when a program starts. 2.5D_FRAESEN.h switches M136 on at block 27 and ends without M137, which suggests that the control does not carry M136 into the next program.
Recommendation: Confirm from the iTNC 530 manual (M136) or on the control. Our reading, which is not in the documents: M137 cancels M136, and so does selecting a program in a program run mode, so every program starts with feed per minute. If this is confirmed, heidenhain 2 says so. The compiler then starts a program's target state with feed per minute (M137) known, so the header writes nothing and the M137 exception leaves the P3-04 acceptance. FEED_MODE=PER_REV still writes M136. If it is not confirmed, the compiler keeps writing M137 in the header, which does no harm, and P3-04 lists it as a header difference. Answer together with D283, the same question for the Fanuc units code.
Where: heidenhain.md 2. Code: src/Ncx.Compilers/Heidenhain/HeidenhainFunctions.cs WriteFeedMode (TODO(question) at line 94) and the start of the target state in HeidenhainCompiler; tests/Ncx.Acceptance/Examples/HeidenhainCompilerTests.cs (the M137 exception, lines 30-38); related D283.

ANSWER:
As recommended, confirmed from the manual library: Every Klartext program starts with feed per minute. The general rule for the M functions is that a function which is not effective block by block must be cancelled in a later block with a separate M function "or it is cancelled automatically by the TNC at program end", and the control additionally resets the modal program information when a new program is selected and on M2, M30 or END PGM, so M136 never carries into the next program. The compiler therefore starts a program's target state with feed per minute (M137) known, the header writes nothing, and the M137 exception leaves the P3-04 acceptance; FEED_MODE=PER_REV still writes M136. Heidenhain 2 says so.
Evidence: Benutzer-Handbuch HEIDENHAIN-Klartext-Dialog (iTNC 530, NC-SW 340490-04), p. 302 (Basics of the M functions: functions act from the block in which they are called; a function that is not effective block by block must be cancelled in a later block with a separate M function, "oder sie wird automatisch von der TNC am Programm-Ende aufgehoben"); Benutzer-Handbuch HEIDENHAIN-Klartext-Dialog (iTNC 530, NC-SW 340490-04), p. 320 (Under M142, "Standardverhalten": the control resets the modal program information when a new program is selected, when M2, M30 or the END PGM block is executed (depending on machine parameter 7300), and when a cycle is redefined with its base values); Benutzer-Handbuch HEIDENHAIN-Klartext-Dialog (iTNC 530, NC-SW 340490-04), p. 313 (M136: the default behaviour is the programmed feed F in mm/min; with M136 the feed is in millimetres per spindle revolution. It takes effect at block start, and "M136 heben Sie auf, indem Sie M137 programmieren"); Benutzerhandbuch Klartextprogrammierung (TNC 640), p. 224 (The same basic rule for the TNC 640: a modal additional function must be cancelled with a separate M function in a later NC block, or the control cancels it automatically at program end. Page 232 repeats that the default behaviour without M136 is feed in mm/min and that M137 cancels M136).
Settled 2026-10-01: the maintainer let the manual-confirmed answers that agree with their recommendation be applied without reviewing each one.

#### D340 SINUMERIK counterparts of D241, D242 and D244
Question: The Siemens reader follows the workarounds of three Fanuc entries that the documents do not settle for Sinumerik. (1) siemens 3 gives G2/G3 with I J K, but not an arc whose centre word of the plane is left out. SiemensArcs.AddCenter takes such a word as 0 from the start point, as D241 describes for Fanuc. (2) siemens 2 does not say which code of group 1 is active before the first G0 to G3. SiemensMotion writes RAPID for axis words before any of them (MotionCode ?? "G0"), as in D242. (3) siemens 4 separates the settable frame (G54..G57, G505..G599, G500, group 8) from the programmable frame (TRANS, ROT, MIRROR, SCALE, their A forms, G58, G59, group 3). It does not say whether selecting a datum ends the programmable frame. SiemensFrames.ReadOrigin writes ORIGIN, which empties the NCX chain (language 4.2, D31), and does not write the programmable frame again. Case: TRANS X10, G55, G0 X0. NCX stands at X0 of datum 2, while the control stands at X10 if the frame stays.
Recommendation: Confirm from the 840D sl programming manual; each point then follows its Fanuc entry. (1) If a centre word of 0 may be left out, siemens 3 says so and the reader stays as it is. If it is an alarm, such an arc stays RAW with a WARNING (D5). (2) If group 1 starts at G0, siemens 2 says so and RAPID stays. If machine data sets the start code, the [machine] key that D242 names as its alternative serves both families. (3) Our reading, not in the documents: the programmable frame is independent of the settable frame and survives G54..G599 and G500 (they are separate groups in siemens 2). If that is confirmed, the reader writes the entries of the programmable frame again after ORIGIN, the pattern D244 (a) recommends for the Fanuc G52, and siemens 4 says so. The Siemens compiler needs no change: WriteChain already writes TRANS alone where an ORIGIN empties the chain, and writes a rewritten entry again after the G54..G599, which is right under either reading. Answer together with D241, D242 and D244 so that both readers keep one rule.
Where: controllers/siemens.md 2, 3 (arcs), 4; controller-mapping 1 (ORIGIN row). Code: src/Ncx.Readers/Siemens/SiemensArcs.cs AddCenter and CenterValue (TODO at 131); SiemensMotion.cs (TODO at 236, the G0 default of MotionCode); SiemensFrames.cs ReadOrigin (TODO at 41) and SiemensChain; src/Ncx.Compilers/Siemens/SiemensFrames.cs WriteChain and WriteRemoved (no change, point 3). Related: D241, D242, D244.

ANSWER:
As recommended, confirmed from the manual library: (1) The reader stays as it is: an interpolation parameter I, J or K whose value is 0 may be left out, but the belonging second centre word must be given in every case, so siemens 3 gets that sentence and a G2/G3 that writes neither centre word of its plane stays RAW. (2) The manuals contradict main: the Siemens standard reset value of G group 1 is G1, not G0, and it is settable per machine with MD20150 $MC_GCODE_RESET_VALUES, so the language default becomes LINE and the [machine] key of D242 carries the builder's value for both families - this is the second branch the recommendation already allows for. (3) Confirmed as our reading has it: the programmable frame is a separate factor of the total frame ($P_IFRAME and $P_PFRAME are different components of $P_ACTFRAME) and is deleted only by a bare TRANS/ROT/SCALE/MIRROR, while G500 switches off the settable frames alone; so TRANS survives G54..G599 and G500, and the reader writes the programmable-frame entries again after the ORIGIN, as D244 (a) does for the Fanuc G52.
Evidence: SINUMERIK 840D sl/828D – Grundlagen, Programmierhandbuch 03/2013, p. 197 (Under circular interpolation with centre and end point: I, J, K are by default incremental from the arc start point, and an interpolation parameter I, J, K with the value 0 'kann entfallen', while 'der zugehörige zweite Parameter muss in jedem Fall angegeben werden'.); SINUMERIK 840D sl/828D – Grundlagen, Programmierhandbuch 03/2013, p. 494-495, legend 517 (The table of G group 1 (modal motion commands) carries exactly one mark in the whole group, on the G1 row, in the STD column; MD20150 is '+' (configurable) on every row. The legend on 517 says that when no function of a modal group is programmed the standard setting takes effect, that it is changeable through MD20150 $MC_GCODE_RESET_VALUES, and that SAG is the Siemens AG standard setting, MH the machine builder's.); SINUMERIK 840D sl – NC programming, Programming Manual 10/2020, p. 1290 (The English table of G group 1 in the newest edition carries the same single mark: 'G1 Linear interpolation' has an x in the first STD sub-column, SAG, and MD20150 is configurable for every row of the group.); SINUMERIK ONE – NC-Programmierung, Programmierhandbuch 10/2020 (SW 6.14), p. 1294 (The G group 1 table of the ONE manual, whose extraction keeps the two STD sub-columns apart: of the twenty-one rows only 'G1 Linearinterpolation' carries a mark, and it stands in SAG, not in MH.); SINUMERIK 840D sl/828D – Grundlagen, Programmierhandbuch 03/2013, p. 321 and 354 (A replacing frame instruction deletes all earlier programmed frame instructions, and its reference is the last called settable zero offset (G54...G57, G505...G599). Deselecting frames: G500 is the modal switch-off of all settable frames only, while 'TRANS/ROT/SCALE/MIRROR ohne Achsangabe bewirkt ein Löschen der programmierbaren Frames'; G53/G153/SUPA only suppress them block-wise.); SINUMERIK 840D sl/828D – Arbeitsvorbereitung, Programmierhandbuch 03/2013, p. 297 (also 275) (The current total frame $P_ACTFRAME is the chain $P_PARTFRAME : $P_SETFRAME : $P_EXTFRAME : $P_ACTBFRAME : $P_IFRAME : $P_TOOLFRAME : $P_WPFRAME : $P_TRAFRAME : $P_PFRAME : $P_CYCFRAME, and it is recomputed whenever one component changes. The settable frame and the programmable frame are separate components of that chain.).
Settled 2026-10-01: the maintainer let the manual-confirmed answers that agree with their recommendation be applied without reviewing each one.

#### D341 Signatures of CYCLE801 and CYCLE802
Question: siemens 7 and controller-mapping 5 (catalog cycles and repeats rows) name CYCLE801 (grid or frame) and CYCLE802 (free positions) as patterns that 'expand into CYCLE_CALL blocks', and implementation 15 P5-01 plans that expansion. Only HOLES1 and HOLES2 have their leading parameters in siemens 7. Main keeps both RAW with a WARNING (SiemensCycles.Read), so a pattern of an 840D sl program converts to no NCX calls.
Recommendation: Take the full sl signatures of CYCLE801 and CYCLE802 from the 840D sl manual 3.25 (controller-mapping 10) into siemens 7. Record the meaning of each parameter and the default of an empty position. The reader then expands them into CYCLE_CALL blocks, as SiemensPatterns does for HOLES1 and HOLES2. The compiler needs nothing new, since it writes MCALL and one position block per call. This fits naturally with the answer to D181. Until then the pattern stays RAW, with its modal cycle kept beside it as D259 proposes.
Where: siemens.md 7 (patterns row); controller-mapping 5 (catalog cycles, repeats rows); implementation 15 P5-01; src/Ncx.Readers/Siemens/SiemensCycles.cs Read (TODO line 51); src/Ncx.Readers/Siemens/SiemensPatterns.cs; related D181, D259.

ANSWER:
As recommended, confirmed from the manual library: The full sl signatures are in the 840D sl programming manual, chapter 3.25 'Zyklen extern programmieren': CYCLE801(_SPCA, _SPCO, _STA, _DIS1, _DIS2, _NUM1, _NUM2, _VARI, _UMODE, _ANG1, _ANG2, _HIDE, _NSP, _DMODE) with reference point X0/Y0 absolute, base angle, column and row spacing, column and row count, _VARI ones digit 0 = grid and 1 = frame, two shear angles, and _HIDE a string of suppressed position numbers such as "1,3"; and CYCLE802(_XA, _YA, _X0, _Y0 ... _X8, _Y8, _VARI, _UMODE, _DMODE, S_ABA, S_AB0 ... S_AB8) with at most nine positions, _XA/_YA/S_ABA nine-digit codes with 1 = absolute and 2 = incremental per position (the first programmed position is always absolute). On the empty position the manual says only that unneeded X1/Y1/A1 to X8/Y8/A8 may be left out, while _XA, _YA and S_ABA must be given in full for all nine. One catch for the expansion: the pattern cycles choose the order themselves from the position reached before the call, so a fixed sequence of CYCLE_CALL blocks does not reproduce the machine's path.
Evidence: SINUMERIK 840D sl – NC-Programmierung, Programmierhandbuch 06/2019 (SW 4.92), p. 1114-1116 (Section 3.25.1.35 gives CYCLE801 with fourteen parameters and a table of each: X0/Y0 the absolute reference point of the grid or frame in the 1st and 2nd axis, a0 the base rotation angle to the 1st axis, L1/L2 the column and row spacing without sign, N1/N2 the counts, _VARI ones digit 0 grid / 1 frame, _UMODE and _NSP reserved, aX/aY the shear angles of the rows and of the columns, _HIDE a string of up to 198 characters listing the position numbers not to be machined (example "1,3"), _DMODE ones digit the plane G17/G18/G19.); SINUMERIK 840D sl – NC-Programmierung, Programmierhandbuch 06/2019 (SW 4.92), p. 1116-1119 (Section 3.25.1.36 gives CYCLE802 with thirty-three parameters: _XA and _YA are nine-digit decimals, one digit per position, 1 = absolute and 2 = incremental with the first programmed position always absolute; then nine X/Y pairs; then _VARI (spindle clamping and the rotary-axis combinations, marked 'nur für Aufruf aus Jobshop'), _UMODE, _DMODE, and S_ABA plus nine rotary-axis positions. A closing note says unneeded positions X1/Y1/A1 to X8/Y8/A8 may be omitted, but the alternative codes must be given completely for all nine.); SINUMERIK 840D sl / 840D / 840Di sl – Zyklen, Programmierhandbuch 01/2008, p. 98-99 (The classic CYCLE801 is a seven-parameter grid, CYCLE801(_SPCA, _SPCO, _STA, _DIS1, _DIS2, _NUM1, _NUM2), called after a modal MCALL of the drilling cycle (example N15 MCALL CYCLE82(...), N20 CYCLE801(30,20,0,10,15,5,3)). Its 'Ablauf' says the cycle fixes the order of the holes internally to keep the idle paths short, and that the starting position is decided from the last position reached in the plane before the call, one of the four corner positions.); SINUMERIK 840D sl / 840D / 840Di sl – Zyklen, Programmierhandbuch 01/2008, p. 92-94 (HOLES1(SPCA, SPCO, STA1, FDIS, DBH, NUM) is the row pattern, and its 'Ablauf' on page 94 says the cycle decides from the actual position of the plane axes and the row geometry whether it works the row from the first or from the last hole, then approaches the positions one after another at rapid. The worked example calls the same HOLES1 twice and comments that the first call starts at hole 1 and the second at hole 5.).
Settled 2026-10-01: the maintainer let the manual-confirmed answers that agree with their recommendation be applied without reviewing each one.

#### D342 Feed type after G97, G971, G972 and G973
Question: Siemens 2 puts G93 to G97, G961, G962 and G971 to G973 into one group 15, feed type and constant surface speed. Siemens 5 and controller-mapping 4 (CSS row) give the feed type of G96 (it switches G95 on) and of G961 (per minute). They call G97, G971 and G972 only 'off' and G973 'off without limit'. Main reads G971 as per minute and lets G97 and G972 keep the feed type, both in the reader (FEED_MODE) and in the compiler's target state. Case: G961 S200 F500, then later G97 S1000 G1 X10. If G97 selects the feed type of G95, the reader's FEED_MODE=PER_MIN is wrong. The compiler has the same problem: under PER_MIN it writes the CSS_OFF template G97 of millturn1 and dmg-ctx-840d, and the control would then feed per revolution. The CLX post also writes G94 G97 S3600 M3, two codes of group 15 in one block (machine-builders 2).
Recommendation: Take the feed type of each code from the 840D sl programming manual (controller-mapping 10) into siemens 5 and the CSS row. To confirm there: G97 switches off with the feed type of G95, G971 with that of G94, G972 keeps G94 or G95, and G973 acts as G97 without the speed limit; also which code wins in G94 G97 S3600 M3. If this is confirmed, the reader writes FEED_MODE where G97 or G973 changes it, as it already does for G96 after G94. The compiler then records G95 after a template's G97, and writes G971 where the block leaves feed per minute (the rule of D300). Until then main's reading stays.
Where: siemens.md 2 (group 15), 5; controller-mapping 4 (CSS row); machine-builders 2 (CLX post); src/Ncx.Readers/Siemens/SiemensSpindles.cs ReadSurfaceSpeed (TODO at 187); src/Ncx.Compilers/Siemens/SiemensMotion.cs FeedTypeSwitched (TODO at 148); related D300.

ANSWER:
As recommended, confirmed from the manual library: Every point of the recommendation is confirmed, so main's reading is wrong and changes: G97 switches the constant surface speed off and selects the feed type of G95 (the manual adds that G97 may be programmed without a preceding G96 and then 'wirkt wie G95'), G971 switches it off with the feed type of G94, G972 switches it off keeping G94 or G95, and G973 is G97 without the speed limit, that is feed per revolution and no LIMS. The reader therefore writes FEED_MODE=PER_REV on G97 and G973 as it already does on G96, and the compiler records G95 after a template's G97 and writes G971 where the block is to keep feed per minute (D300). For `G94 G97 S3600 M3` the control raises alarm 12060 and the documented evaluation is that the last function of the group takes effect, so that block is feed per revolution and the CLX post's G94 in it is ignored.
Evidence: SINUMERIK 840D sl/828D – Grundlagen, Programmierhandbuch 03/2013, p. 93 (Section 6.3 lists the meanings: G96 constant surface speed with feed type G95 ON (G95 is switched on automatically), G961 with feed type G94 ON, G962 with G94 or G95 ON, G97 'Konstante Schnittgeschwindigkeit ausschalten mit Vorschubtyp G95', G971 off with feed type G94, G972 off with feed type G94 or G95, G973 off without activating the spindle speed limit.); SINUMERIK 840D sl/828D – Grundlagen, Programmierhandbuch 03/2013, p. 95-96 (Switching the constant surface speed off: after G97/G971 the S value counts as rev/min again, and G96/G961 may also be switched off with G94 or G95. It then states that G97 may be programmed without a preceding G96 and that the function then acts like G95, with LIMS additionally programmable. LIMS is effective only under G96, G961 and G97 and does not act under G971; G973 switches off without a speed limit.); SINUMERIK 840D sl/828D – Grundlagen, Programmierhandbuch 03/2013, p. 500-501 (The table of G group 15 (feed type) marks G94 as the Siemens standard setting and describes G973 as 'Umdrehungsvorschub ohne Spindeldrehzahlbegrenzung (G97 ohne LIMS für ISO-Modus)', which names G973's feed type outright as feed per revolution.); SINUMERIK 840D sl – Diagnosehandbuch (Alarme), 08/2018, p. 168 (Alarm 12060 'gleiche G-Gruppe mehrmals programmiert': only one G function per group may be programmed. The alarm applies to the non-syntax-determining groups (5 to n, which includes group 15) and the explanation says that if several functions of one group are called in an NC block, 'so wirkt die jeweils letzte einer Gruppe (die vorherigen werden ignoriert)'.).
Settled 2026-10-01: the maintainer let the manual-confirmed answers that agree with their recommendation be applied without reviewing each one.

#### D343 Modal call after a RAW line that calls a subprogram
Question: siemens 7 says MCALL makes a call modal until MCALL alone ends it, and siemens 11 rule 8 keeps builder cycles and other unknown calls RAW. No document says whether a subprogram that a RAW line calls can return with a modal call still armed. The Siemens compiler ends the modal call before every RAW, writing MCALL alone where one may be armed. After the RAW it forgets the G groups, feed, D, SETMS, datum and DIAMON (SiemensCompiler.WriteRaw). It forgets the modal call only after a RAW that names MCALL (SiemensCycles.AfterRaw). If the MCALL of a builder cycle survives its RET, the next RAPID after a RAW builder call is written without MCALL alone, and the control drills there. It drills there even where the source wrote MCALL alone after the builder call: the reader turns that MCALL alone into CYCLE=OFF, and the compiler writes nothing for it, because its state says no call is armed.
Recommendation: Confirm in the 840D sl manual whether an MCALL programmed in a subprogram stays active in the caller after RET or M17. If it ends with the subprogram, keep main. If it survives, the modal call becomes unknown after every RAW, as the G groups already are, so that MCALL alone precedes the next motion. The cost is one MCALL line after each MSG or STOPRE that a motion follows. Alternative, whatever the fact: make it unknown after every RAW now, which is always safe. Answer together with D259, which touches the same rule of the compiler.
Where: siemens.md 7, 11 rule 8; src/Ncx.Compilers/Siemens/SiemensCycles.cs AfterRaw (TODO line 152), EndModalCall; src/Ncx.Compilers/Siemens/SiemensCompiler.cs WriteRaw; related D259.

ANSWER:
As recommended, confirmed from the manual library: The modal call survives the return: the manual says the modal subprogram is called after every path-motion block from the MCALL on, 'Auch über Programmebenen hinweg', and that in one program run only the last MCALL acts and the current one replaces the active one - it is one channel state, not something scoped to a program level. Nothing ends it but another MCALL or a bare MCALL, and a bare MCALL programmed in a level that a multi-level return skips is lost while the modal subprogram stays active. So take the recommendation's second branch: the modal call becomes unknown after every RAW, like the G groups, and the compiler writes MCALL alone before the next motion.
Evidence: SINUMERIK 840D sl – NC-Programmierung, Programmierhandbuch 06/2019 (SW 4.92), p. 539-541 (Section 3.2.3.4: with MCALL the named subprogram is not called at once; from that point in the part program it is called automatically after every traversing block with path motion, 'Auch über Programmebenen hinweg'. A note adds that in one program run only the last MCALL acts and the current one replaces the active one. A warning lists the two cases where it is called without path motion (S or F under G0/G1; G0/G1 alone or with other G commands), and the boundary conditions say no modal subprogram calls are executed in an ASUP. Example 2 arms MCALL L70 in the main program and then calls L80, whose motion blocks trigger L70.); SINUMERIK 840D sl – NC-Programmierung, Programmierhandbuch 06/2019 (SW 4.92), p. 527 (Example 1 of the parameterised return: from program level 3 (an ASUP) N19100 RET("N10900", ,$P_STACK) returns into the main program, and the target block N10900 is followed by N10910 MCALL commented 'Modalen Unterprogrammaufruf ausschalten' and by N10920 restoring the other modal settings.); SINUMERIK 840D sl/828D – Arbeitsvorbereitung, Programmierhandbuch 03/2013, p. 181 (Boundary conditions of the multi-level return: the SAVE statements of the individual levels are evaluated, and if a modal subprogram is active and the deselect command MCALL is programmed in one of the skipped subprograms, 'bleibt das modale Unterprogramm weiterhin aktiv'. A warning follows that the programmer must make sure the right modal settings continue after such a return.); SINUMERIK 840D sl/828D – Arbeitsvorbereitung, Programmierhandbuch 03/2013, p. 166 (Section 1.24.2.4: the SAVE attribute saves the modal G functions active before the subprogram call and reactivates them after the subprogram end. Only modal G functions are named.).
Settled 2026-10-01: the maintainer let the manual-confirmed answers that agree with their recommendation be applied without reviewing each one.
